structured_extraction.program_description: The Allegany County Local Development Council distributes funding to county non-profits and municipalities from slot machine revenues generated by Rocky Gap Casino. A sub-committee of the 15-member Local Development Council reviews submitted requests and makes spending recommendations to the Allegany County Commissioners. Grants are awarded for capital-related projects only; operating expenses are not eligible.

Funds may only be used for capital-related items and cannot be used for operating expenses or ongoing operational costs. Award amounts are determined by the Local Development Council based on submitted requests and sub-committee recommendations. Funds are disbursed within approximately six weeks of award announcement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Watershed Restoration Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Anne Arundel County Watershed Restoration Grant Program annually funds on-the-ground watershed restoration projects designed to reduce stormwater runoff into local waterways, treat and filter pollutants from impervious surfaces, and engage residents in protecting local rivers and streams. The program also supports cost-effective reforestation and greening efforts that increase protected forested land, improve water and air quality, increase and protect habitat and tree cover, and reduce flooding and erosion. Administered in partnership with the Chesapeake Bay Trust, the program awards grants to 501(c) nonprofit organizations based in Anne Arundel County or the City of Annapolis, including local watershed groups, community associations, homeowners' associations, service and civic groups, youth groups, and faith-based organizations.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program anticipates $1,000,000 available for awards in Anne Arundel County and $300,000 available for awards in the City of Annapolis. Individual funding requests generally will not exceed $300,000. Requests larger than $300,000 require prior approval from the Chesapeake Bay Trust. Matching or leveraged resources are not required but are viewed favorably in applications. Applicants may count resources already invested in project design and permitting phases, including previously received awards, as matching funds. Projects are categorized as Category 1 (small-scale, disturbance footprint less than 5,000 square feet or disturbing less than 100 cubic yards of earth) or Category 2 (large-scale, disturbance footprint greater than 5,000 square feet or disturbing more than 100 cubic yards of earth). Applicants must provide sound technical designs and project budgets demonstrating cost-effective stormwater treatment or accomplishment of metrics helping the County and City meet water quality and runoff reduction goals.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: RFPs typically open in the Fall and close in the Spring. Interested applicants should check the Chesapeake Bay Trust website for the current year's specific application deadline.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Katie Mullen (Grants Manager), Anne Arundel County; Sarah T. Koser (Senior Program Officer, Chesapeake Bay Trust)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified 501(c) non-profit organizations based in Anne Arundel County or the City of Annapolis, including local watershed groups, community associations, homeowners' associations, service and civic groups, youth groups, and faith-based organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Watershed restoration projects that reduce stormwater runoff and pollutants through best management practices (BMPs) such as stream restoration, living shorelines, bioretention, rain gardens, stormwater retrofits, impervious surface removal, and habitat creation. Projects must accomplish on-the-ground restoration that treats rainwater runoff from impervious surfaces or demonstrates accomplishment of metrics helping the County and City meet water quality and runoff reduction goals. Also supports cost-effective reforestation and greening efforts to increase protected forested land and improve water and air quality.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Anne Arundel County, including the City of Annapolis. At least one partner in the application must represent a stakeholder group based in Anne Arundel County (including the City of Annapolis). Non-profit organizations may propose projects on non-profit property, private property, City of Annapolis-owned property, or public school properties, provided the landowner supports the project. Projects that are most competitive will have single landowners, complete landowner support for full maintenance agreements with Anne Arundel County DPW, sufficient site access away from buildings and infrastructure, fairly gentle slopes (less than 8%), no right-of-way or utility conflicts, and no downstream infrastructure concerns.
requirements_list: Must be a certified 501(c) nonprofit organization
Must be based in Anne Arundel County or the City of Annapolis
Applications must include at least one partner representing a stakeholder group based in Anne Arundel County (including the City of Annapolis)
Projects must be located in Anne Arundel County (including the City of Annapolis)
Project must reduce stormwater flowing into local waterways
Project must treat and filter pollutants from impervious surfaces
Project must engage residents in restoration and protection efforts
Applicants must provide sound technical designs and project budgets
Projects must demonstrate cost-effective stormwater treatment or accomplish metrics meeting local water quality and runoff reduction improvement goals
Landowner support must be assured and documented in the application
Individual funding requests generally will not exceed $300,000
Matching or leveraged resources are not required but are viewed favorably; applicants may count resources already invested in project design and permitting phases as matching funds

Projects categorized as Category 1 (disturbance footprint less than 5,000 sq ft or less than 100 cubic yards earth disturbance) or Category 2 (disturbance footprint greater than 5,000 sq ft or more than 100 cubic yards earth disturbance)
Project sites on multiple properties require all landowners to sign grading permit applications and every design revision submittal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests for Proposals (RFPs) are solicited annually by the Chesapeake Bay Trust, typically opening in the Fall and closing in the Spring. Interested applicants should contact the Chesapeake Bay Trust or Anne Arundel County Watershed Protection and Restoration Program staff to discuss potential project sites before applying. Applicants must visit the Chesapeake Bay Trust website application page to access the current year's RFP and submit applications according to the guidelines and deadlines specified in that RFP. The Guidelines for Selecting the Right Project Site document should be used to evaluate project sites and determine competitiveness. Applicants should provide all required BMP data forms, design plans, technical reports, GIS files (if applicable), drainage area maps, and any applicable environmental assessment data. Projects are reviewed and selected based on technical merit, cost-effectiveness, alignment with water quality goals, and quality of partnerships and landowner support.

structured_extraction.program_description: Property owners who revitalize their properties in designated Commercial Revitalization Areas can receive a property tax credit for up to five years. The credit equals the incremental increase in real property tax assessment resulting from improvements of at least $100,000. The tax credit can be extended for an additional five years for investments of at least $10,000,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying property owners receive a property tax credit for up to five years equal to the incremental increase in real property tax assessment. The tax credit can be extended for an additional five years for investments of at least $10,000,000. Properties must be located in one of nine designated Commercial Revitalization Areas, undergo improvements of at least $100,000, and be certified by the Office of Planning and Zoning as qualified. Qualifying improvements may include full site redevelopment, demolition and redevelopment, new facades, landscaping and signage, lighting, replacing pavement with green spaces, or other measures that improve the physical appearance and aesthetics of the property and increase its economic viability. The owner must apply to the County Office of Finance for the revitalization credit within 120 days after receiving the notice of assessment from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A place-based model designed to engage local communities and provide wrap-around services and support to families living in high-need areas. The program aims to reduce poverty and the number of children in out-of-home placements by bringing together diverse stakeholders including local agencies, community organizations, residents, faith leaders, businesses, and service providers to create collaborative support systems that address family wellness and stability. The program operates in four designated Communities of Hope geographic areas in Anne Arundel County: Brooklyn Park (North County), West County (Severn/Meade), Annapolis, and South County. Each area implements a two-generation, place-based approach with shared priorities including improving access to community resources, increasing safe spaces for children and youth, reducing health disparities, promoting economic stability, addressing basic needs, and interrupting violence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides wrap-around services and community support through a collaborative network of stakeholders. It coordinates resources and services among local agencies, community organizations, faith leaders, and business owners to support families living in high-need communities. Each Community of Hope area implements shared priorities and strategies focused on: coordinating support systems for youth based on trusted relationships; providing enhanced pathways to economic opportunity; implementing evidence-based practices for prevention, intervention, and re-entry; utilizing placed-based and two-generation approaches; developing and implementing programming focused on interrupting and reducing violence; increasing collaboration and braiding funding between youth and family-serving agencies; embedding trauma-informed approaches; increasing agency capacity through leadership development and program measurement; addressing systemic barriers including racism and inequality; creating safe, vibrant public spaces; expanding bilingual services; and reducing barriers to accessing services and actualizing goals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families living in high-need communities in Anne Arundel County and community organizations, faith leaders, and service providers serving those areas. The program particularly focuses on residents of public and subsidized housing communities, youth and families experiencing economic instability, and communities disproportionately impacted by youth violence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program coordinates services and support to address family wellness and stability, reduce poverty, and reduce the number of children in out-of-home placements. Specific focus areas include: coordinating support to meet basic needs; providing job training and vocational programs; offering affordable quality childcare options; improving access to medical care including prenatal care and substance use services; providing mental health resources and services; supporting youth development and employment readiness; increasing safe recreational and educational programming; improving housing affordability and livability; expanding food access and healthy food options; providing transportation assistance; and creating safe spaces for learning and community engagement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program operates in four designated Communities of Hope geographic areas in Anne Arundel County: Brooklyn Park (North County), West County (Severn/Meade), Annapolis, and South County. These areas were identified based on concentration of negative social and health indicators including poverty rates, food deserts, health disparities, youth violence, and other social determinants of health.
requirements_list: Organizations must be located in or serving one of the four designated Communities of Hope areas (Brooklyn Park, West County, Annapolis, or South County)
Organizations should be willing to participate in collaborative networks and braid funding and resources with other service providers
Commitment to embedding trauma-informed approaches in service delivery
Willingness to adopt and implement evidence-based practices
Participation in data collection and program measurement activities
Commitment to addressing systemic barriers including racism and inequality
Organizations should prioritize bilingual services and cultural competency
Focus on two-generation and place-based approaches
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals and organizations can contact the Community of Hope Director to become a partner in the program. Potential partners can connect through established communication channels and partner networks in their designated area (Annapolis, Brooklyn Park, West County, or South County). The program utilizes a collaborative model where organizations are invited to participate in coordinated systems of care rather than a traditional grant application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program supporting cultural festivals, parades, and other celebrations that help foster community belonging, local identity, and quality of life while providing economic and social benefits to Anne Arundel County residents and visitors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding supports cultural festivals, parades, and community celebration events in Anne Arundel County. Grants are provided to eligible non-profit organizations that demonstrate how their event will foster community belonging, provide local identity enhancement, and improve quality of life while generating economic and social benefits for county residents and visitors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based non-profit organizations seeking to host cultural festivals, parades, and community celebrations in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting festivals, cultural events, parades, and celebrations that provide economic and social benefits to the community and foster community belonging and local identity.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County
requirements_list: Must be a community-based festival, cultural event, parade, or celebration
Must be organized by a non-profit organization
Must provide economic and social benefits to the community
Must foster community belonging and local identity
Must improve quality of life for Anne Arundel County residents and visitors
Must meet all eligibility criteria outlined in the program guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through an online Google Form during the designated application window (July 14, 2025 - August 11, 2025). The form titled 'Community Building Mini Grant (CBMG) Supporting Cultural Festivals, Events, and Activations' collects organization information, event details, and demonstration of how the event meets program criteria regarding community benefits and impact.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Reinvestment and Repair Commission (CRRC) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The CRRC Grant Program provides funding from a special revenue fund supported by sales tax revenue from recreational cannabis sales. Grants support community-based initiatives intended to benefit low-income communities in Anne Arundel County, with priority given to organizations serving residents in Disproportionately Impacted Areas (DIAs). Eligible projects address strategic priorities including mental health and substance abuse services, education and youth enrichment, housing and homelessness prevention, and workforce development and employment training. The program is administered by the Anne Arundel County Development Services (ACDS) under the direction of the Community Reinvestment and Repair Commission.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded from the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund (CRRF), which is funded by a portion of sales tax revenue from adult-use recreational cannabis sales. Grant awards in Fiscal Year 2026 ranged from $24,060 to $180,000, with a total allocation of $1,691,200 distributed across 41 funded organizations. Award amounts are determined based on the nature and scope of the proposed project and the CRRC's recommendations. The specific grant amounts and award terms vary by project. Applications for Local Fiscal Year 2027 launched on January 14, 2026 with a deadline of February 25, 2026 at noon. Grant funds must be used to support community-based initiatives addressing one or more of four strategic priorities: Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services, Education and Youth Enrichment and After School Activities, Housing and Homelessness Prevention Services, or Workforce Development and Employment Training.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maggie Staudenmaier, Grants Associate; Elizabeth Harig-Blaine
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based non-profit organizations serving low-income communities in Anne Arundel County, particularly those in Disproportionately Impacted Areas (DIAs) identified by the Maryland Office of Social Equity or the ten priority zip codes identified by the Anne Arundel County CRRC.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grants must support community-based initiatives that address one or more of the following strategic priorities: Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services; Education, Youth Enrichment, and After School Activities; Housing and Homelessness Prevention Services; or Workforce Development and Employment Training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County. Priority is given to organizations serving residents in Disproportionately Impacted Areas (DIAs). The Anne Arundel County CRRC has identified ten priority zip codes: 21060, 21061, 21113, 21122, 21144, 21225, 21401, 21403, 20724, and 20755. Eight additional DIAs in Anne Arundel County are identified by the Maryland Office of Social Equity based on cannabis charge data exceeding 150% of the 10-year state mean (21060, 21061, 21113, 21122, 21144, 21225, 21401, 21403).
requirements_list: Applicant must be a community-based non-profit organization
Project or initiative must be intended to benefit low-income communities

Project must address one or more of the four strategic priorities: Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services, Education and Youth Enrichment and After School Activities, Housing and Homelessness Prevention Services, or Workforce Development and Employment Training
Priority given to organizations serving residents in Disproportionately Impacted Areas (DIAs)
Applications must be submitted online through the Neighborly Portal at portal.neighborlysoftware.com/acds/Participant
Free Neighborly account registration is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications for Local Fiscal Year 2027 launched on Wednesday, January 14, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. with a deadline of February 25, 2026 at noon. Applications must be submitted online through the Neighborly Portal at portal.neighborlysoftware.com/acds/Participant. Free Neighborly account registration is required. Application training sessions were offered on January 16, 22, 26, 28, and 29, 2026 at various locations and times. Questions about the application should be directed to Maggie Staudenmaier at mstaudenmaier@acdsinc.org. Complete funding award information for FY2026 is available on the ACDS website.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Anne Arundel County Executive's Office offers grants to eligible non-profit organizations to help them continue operating and increase the impact of existing programs, pilot new programs, undertake one-time projects that improve and enrich the lives of Anne Arundel County residents and communities, or build organizational capacity. Grant proposals should align with the County Executive's priorities: providing services to underserved populations, addressing community health and well-being, promoting equity and inclusion, and helping eliminate the opportunity gap in education. Collaborative projects are preferred.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $2 million in total funding anticipated for FY2027. Grant applications should be for no less than $15,000, with awards typically ranging from $15,000 to $50,000. Grants support program and project costs including staff, supplies, travel, equipment, and proportional administrative overhead (not to exceed 5% of total grant award). One-time projects and small equipment purchases are eligible. Capacity building support is also available as a category of funding to allow non-profits to operate more efficiently and effectively, including strategic planning, governance, professional development, technology improvements, and systems innovation. Collaborative projects are preferred but not required. Funding is based on availability of funds in the County's annual budget and is contingent on approval of the FY 2027 budget. Funding period is July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations serving Anne Arundel County residents and communities that are tax-exempt under section 501(c)(3), in good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessment & Taxation, provide direct services to Anne Arundel County residents, have an established and active Board of Directors, and have filed IRS Form 990 and/or audited financials.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program and project support including staff costs, supplies, travel, equipment, and proportional administrative overhead (not to exceed 5% of total grant award); one-time projects; small equipment purchases; capacity building support such as strategic planning, governance, professional development, technology improvements, and systems innovation; services to underserved populations; health and well-being initiatives; equity and inclusion programs; education opportunity gap reduction. Grant funds must be used for activities that benefit Anne Arundel County residents and communities and must align with at least one County Executive priority.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Applicant organizations must provide direct service to Anne Arundel County residents and communities.
requirements_list: Must be a non-profit organization with 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status
Must be in good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessment & Taxation (SDAT)
Must provide direct service to Anne Arundel County residents
Must have an established and active Board of Directors
Must have filed IRS Form 990 and/or audited financials in most recent fiscal year (FY25)

Must meet ACDS insurance requirements including Comprehensive General Liability ($1,000,000 per occurrence, $2,000,000 general aggregate), Auto Liability ($1,000,000 combined single limit as applicable), and Workers' Compensation as applicable
Must be able to comply with all terms, conditions, and certifications of the required grant agreement
If applying with a Fiscal Sponsor, must have a Letter of Partnership signed by both organizations
If faith-based organization, must adhere to Guidelines on Funding Faith-Based Organizations & Related Activities
Must submit Letter of Support from an agency, organization, community leader, or other entity demonstrating support and indicating need for the program or project
Must have copy of Articles of Incorporation
Must have copy of Organization's By-Laws
Must provide Board of Directors/Trustees list with names and terms of office
Must provide copy of Federal tax-exempt IRS determination letter
Must provide good standing status from SDAT
Must provide Job Descriptions for each staff position requesting County funds
Must have written Conflict of Interest policy and procedures
Must submit completed Form W-9 (signed within the last year)
Grant applications should be for no less than $15,000
Projects or programs must benefit Anne Arundel County residents and communities

Proposals should align with at least one County Executive priority: services to underserved populations, community health and well-being, promoting equity and inclusion, or eliminating the opportunity gap in education
Collaborative projects preferred but not required
Do not begin incurring expenses until a fully executed written agreement with ACDS has been signed by all parties
Grantees must follow ACDS-approved procurement process and must not procure equipment or construction work prior to award
Grantees receiving County funds over $100,000 must carry Directors and Officers Insurance of not less than $1,000,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications opened January 7, 2026. Applicants complete the online application through the ACDS Neighborly Portal at https://portal.neighborlysoftware.com/acds/participant (Google Chrome is recommended). A training session was held January 9, 2026 at 2:00 p.m. via Zoom with a recording available on the CSG Program webpage. Applications must be submitted through the Neighborly portal no later than 12:00 p.m. on Wednesday, February 18, 2026, with all supporting documents included. Initial screening for basic eligibility and compliance is conducted by ACDS staff, then applications are reviewed by a panel of County agency representatives. The County Agency Panel makes final recommendations for award and funding amount to the County Executive's Office, and the County Executive makes final decisions. Applicants will be notified of award in writing by July 1, 2026. Awardees must enter into a grant agreement with Arundel Community Development Services, Inc. (ACDS), which will define responsibilities and payment schedule. Awardees will be required to attend an information session with ACDS staff and must submit all required grant documents including an Insurance Certificate naming ACDS as additional insured and board resolution confirming authorized signatory. Grantees must follow ACDS invoicing procedures on a reimbursement basis, submit progress reports and final report once project/program is complete, and schedule a monitoring visit with ACDS staff.

structured_extraction.program_name: County Agricultural and Woodland District Agreements
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides property tax credits to eligible landowners who establish a 10-year District Agreement on their land to preserve agriculture and woodland resources. Landowners agree to protective covenants in exchange for a credit against their annual County Property Tax bill.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners receive an Agricultural Tax Credit applied to the County Real Estate Tax portion of their Real Property Tax Bill. The credit is available for the term of the 10-year District Agreement. Landowners are only invoiced for State property taxes, County fees, and charges. The amount of the credit is not specified on this page.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted anytime, but the County encourages applications be made by March 31 if a tax credit is sought for the following fiscal year tax bill.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with eligible agricultural or woodland property in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit is applied to reduce County Real Estate Tax liability. The program is designed to encourage preservation of agriculture and woodland resources and promote good land stewardship practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be within Rural Agricultural (RA) or Residential Low Density (RLD) zoning districts and outside existing or planned Water and Sewer categories 1, 2, and 3 in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: For Agricultural Districts: land (in whole or in part) must consist of at least 50 contiguous acres devoted to agriculture, or multiple contiguous properties under different ownership with each property at least 10 acres and totaling at least 50 acres
Property must meet certain USDA Soil Capability Classes criteria
Must have an active Soil and Water Conservation Plan in place
For Woodland Districts: at least 10 contiguous acres of woodlands required; 10-acre minimum per landowner when adding to existing district
Must have a Forest Management Plan for woodland districts
Must be in appropriate zoning districts (RA or RLD)
Must be outside existing or planned Water and Sewer categories 1, 2, and 3
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners submit an application anytime, preferably by March 31 for the following fiscal year. The Agricultural and Woodland Preservation Staff can help determine if your property qualifies and assist in preparing the application. Upon approval, the landowner enters into a District Agreement which is recorded in the County Land Records.

structured_extraction.program_description: A transportation assistance program that provides on-demand rides at approximately 50% of normal cost to qualified older adults and individuals with disabilities in Anne Arundel County. Professional drivers operate appropriately equipped vehicles and offer door-to-door service with same-day availability upon at least two hours notice, helping eligible residents travel throughout the county and beyond.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rides are provided at approximately 50% of normal taxi fares through a county match subsidy. Participants purchase vouchers monthly, with a maximum of $150.00 in total voucher value available per month. The pricing structure ranges from purchasing $5.00 in vouchers (worth $10.00 in rides) up to $75.00 in vouchers (worth $150.00 in rides), effectively doubling the value of purchased vouchers. Service includes professional drivers operating equipped cars, vans, or SUVs with door-to-door service within Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line. Airport trips are excluded. Same-day service is available with at least two hours notice. Vouchers can be used for trips with Rides-On-Demand service providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents aged 55 and older, or residents aged 18 and older with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation services for trips within Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line, excluding airport trips. Vouchers are purchased and used to pay for on-demand rides.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line. Airport trips are excluded.
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County resident with a current Maryland State driver's license or Maryland State Issued ID from the Motor Vehicle Administration showing an Anne Arundel County address
Must be 55 years of age or older, or 18 years of age or older with a disability

For persons aged 18 or older with a disability, must provide a copy of SSI or SSDI most recent award letter or disability verification form completed by a physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, or program director of a qualified social agency
Must complete ETA Application Form
Must complete ETA Liability Form
Must complete ETA Order Form for Rides-On-Demand with payment by check or money order
Must agree to adhere to all requirements set forth by Rides-On-Demand service providers and Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, submit the completed ETA Application Form, ETA Liability Form, ETA Disability Verification Form (if applicable), proof of Anne Arundel County residency, and disability verification (if applicable aged 18-54) by mail to Easy Travel Access (ETA) Program, Department of Aging and Disabilities, 2666 Riva Road, Suite 400, Annapolis, MD 21401. To establish eligibility and make initial purchase, complete and mail the ETA Order Form for Rides-On-Demand with payment by check or money order. Payment can be made in person during walk-in hours (8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.) at one of two locations, or by mail. Once eligibility is established, participants may call the Rides-On-Demand reservations number to schedule rides. For subsequent months, reorders only require the Order Form and payment (up to $150.00 in voucher value per month). Participants are personally responsible for scheduling their own trips and paying for all trips scheduled.

structured_extraction.program_name: Easy Travel Access (ETA) Taxi Voucher Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A transportation assistance program that provides discounted taxi vouchers to help older adults and individuals with disabilities pay for taxi fares with participating cab companies in Anne Arundel County. Participants purchase discounted voucher books that can be used for transportation to run errands, visit polling places, pick up groceries, or go shopping throughout Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants purchase taxi voucher books at a discounted rate. Each book costs $5.00 and has a value of $10.00. Approved residents may purchase up to 15 books per month (maximum $150.00 monthly value), providing a county match of up to $75 per month. For example, three books cost $15.00 but have a total value of $30.00. Vouchers can be used with participating cab companies listed on the books and may not be used for tips. Payment must be made by check or money order payable to Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents aged 55 and older, or residents aged 18 to 54 with verifiable transportation disabilities that preclude the ability to use public transportation services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Taxi fares for errands, visiting polling places, grocery shopping, and shopping within Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County residents only. Proof of residency required with current Maryland State driver's license or Maryland State Issued ID from the Motor Vehicle Administration showing an Anne Arundel County address.
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County resident with a current Maryland State driver's license or Maryland State Issued ID from the Motor Vehicle Administration showing an Anne Arundel County address
Must be 55 years of age or older, or 18 to 54 years of age with a verifiable transportation disability that precludes the ability to use public transportation services

For persons aged 18 to 54 with a disability, must provide disability verification completed by a physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, or program director of a qualified social agency. Verification must explain how the disability prevents use of public transportation and indicate whether the disability is permanent or temporary.
Must complete ETA Application and Liability Form
Must complete ETA Order Form for Taxi Voucher
Must sign liability waiver agreeing to indemnify and hold harmless the Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities ETA Program
Payment must be submitted by check or money order payable to Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, visit one of two locations in person during walk-in hours (8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.) or mail completed forms to 2666 Riva Road, Suite 400, Annapolis, MD 21401. Submit the completed ETA Application, Liability Form, proof of Anne Arundel County residency, disability verification if applicable (completed by a health care provider), and completed Order Form with payment by check or money order. Once eligibility is established and the application is approved, reorders only require the Order Form and payment. Participants may purchase up to $150.00 in vouchers per month.

structured_extraction.program_description: A multi-departmental Anne Arundel County program that provides free emergent marsh grasses to county residents for planting in marsh areas as part of qualifying living shoreline or other tidal improvement projects. The program supplies appropriate native marsh grass species (Spartina alterniflora or Spartina patens) based on site conditions determined through a county field visit and evaluation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free emergent marsh grasses (Spartina alterniflora or Spartina patens) at no cost to qualifying county residents for planting in tidal or living shoreline projects. The number of plants is calculated by multiplying the length of area to be planted by the width and dividing by the correct spacing for the plant type. County personnel conduct a field visit to evaluate site conditions and determine appropriate plant species and spacing. Plant types are determined by position on the shore with respect to tides and salinity. Applicants can request plant descriptions and recommended spacing from the Forestry Section.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Forestry Section, Department of Inspections and Permits
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents with qualifying living shoreline or other tidal projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting of emergent marsh grasses in marsh areas as part of living shoreline or tidal improvement projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Anne Arundel County
Must have a qualifying living shoreline or other tidal project
Must be planting in marsh areas
County field visit and site evaluation required
Plantings can be on private property or community association property with authorization
Any additional work along the shoreline requires proper permits prior to beginning work
Cutting or clearing of vegetation (including tree limbs) within 100 feet of tidal waters is prohibited without an approved Vegetation Management Plan (VMP)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Forestry Section at (410) 222-7441 or forestry@aacounty.org to apply. County personnel recommend scheduling a field visit prior to application submittal to assist with initial project planning. Complete the Emergent (Marsh) Grasses Application form and submit it to: Inspections and Permits, Forestry Section, 2664 Riva Road, MS 6201, Annapolis, MD 21401. Include a description of the project or copies of relevant permit applications if plantings are part of a more extensive project. County personnel will conduct a field visit to evaluate site conditions and determine appropriate plant species and spacing. The number of plants needed is calculated based on the area dimensions and recommended plant spacing for the species type.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Anne Arundel County Fire Department provides free smoke alarms and installation services to seniors and those who cannot financially afford smoke alarms.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free smoke alarms and professional installation services provided at no charge to eligible residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors and individuals who cannot financially afford smoke alarms in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Smoke alarms and installation services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a senior or unable to financially afford smoke alarms
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-222-8303 or email fdpubed@aacounty.org to inquire about the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 2027 Laurel Race Course Impact Fund Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants for nonprofit and community organizations to provide services and facilities that benefit communities within three miles of the Laurel Race Course, funded through revenues generated by the Laurel Race Course. The program supports community impact projects in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $10,000 to $50,000, with a minimum request amount of $10,000. The amount available varies each year depending on revenues from the Laurel Race Course (last year awarded $455,000 total). Funding can be used to purchase equipment and related supplies, make small capital improvements such as renovation, remodeling, or restoration/beautification of buildings or public community spaces, expand existing services, or pilot test new programs. Awards are paid on a reimbursement basis (except some capital projects), with ACDS striving to make payment within 30 days of receipt of a complete invoice.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, December 17, 2025 at 12:00pm; FY28 process will begin in December 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) status serving communities within three miles of the Laurel Race Course in Anne Arundel County. Applications from organizations outside the three-mile radius will be considered if they demonstrate significant impacts for those who live and work within the three-mile area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of equipment and related supplies, small capital improvements such as renovation, remodeling, or restoration/beautification of buildings or public community spaces, expansion of existing services, or pilot testing of new programs that benefit communities within three miles of the Laurel Race Course.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant organization must be located in Anne Arundel County within 3 miles of the Laurel Race Course. Applications from organizations outside the three-mile radius will be considered if they demonstrate significant impacts for those who live and work within the three-mile area.
requirements_list: Applicant must have 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) nonprofit status
Organization must be located in Anne Arundel County within 3 miles of the Laurel Race Course, or demonstrate significant impacts for communities within the three-mile radius
Minimum grant request of $10,000
Program/project must be responsive to specific problems or needs of communities in Anne Arundel County within three miles of the Laurel Race Course
Demonstrated need for the program/project
Organizational capacity and previous grant management experience required
Community support for the project
Completeness and clarity of grant application form

Once funded, grantee must maintain comprehensive general liability insurance ($2 million general aggregate, $1 million per occurrence), auto insurance ($1 million combined single limit), and workers compensation
Grantee must execute grant agreement before expending any funds
Do not start spending funds until under contract and after speaking with grant administrator
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through ACDS's Neighborly Portal at https://portal.neighborlysoftware.com/acds/participant. Applications are due Wednesday, December 17, 2025 at 12:00pm. Selected applicants are invited to present to the LRCIF Advisory Committee at meetings in March (Wednesday, March 4 & March 11, 2026 at 6:30 pm, virtual). A public comment period follows from January 8 - January 22, 2026. The LRCIF Advisory Committee makes final grant award recommendations to the County Executive. The FY 2027 budget is approved by County Council in June 2026, and applicants are notified of award decisions. Grantees meet final requirements and execute award agreements in summer 2026. FY 2027 awards are for grant terms of July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027. Grantees are required to submit biannual reports (at mid-year and year-end) with unduplicated data, undergo financial review, and participate in monitoring visits. All invoicing is completed through the Neighborly portal.

structured_extraction.program_name: Fall 2025 Professional Development Cohort Program - Fundraising & Sustainability 2.0
structured_extraction.program_description: A recurring cohort-based training program administered by the Anne Arundel County Nonprofit Center that helps 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations diversify their revenue sources, develop or update resource development plans, and strengthen long-term organizational sustainability. The program has been offered in multiple iterations, including a foundational Fundraising & Sustainability cohort and an advanced 'Fundraising & Sustainability 2.0' cohort for organizations with prior cohort experience or baseline fundraising knowledge. The advanced cohort consists of five group sessions held every other week over approximately two months, featuring expert facilitation, peer learning, networking, one-on-one consulting, and lifetime access to resource materials and templates. Earlier cohort versions ran approximately three months with four in-person sessions and online coaching for teams of two to three people from up to ten organizations. Topics covered include case development, organizational storytelling, strategic prospecting, grant development, and diversified fundraising planning.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Five group training sessions held every other week from October 8, 2025 through December 3, 2025, from 2:00 p.m. to 4:30 p.m. at the Nonprofit Center in Crownsville, Maryland. Up to three team members per organization can attend. The program includes expert facilitation by Lili Leonard of Black Dog Philanthropic, peer learning, networking, one-on-one consulting time on a project of the organization's choice, and lifetime access to resource materials, examples, and templates. Cost is $75 for organizations with budgets under $500,000 and $150 for organizations with budgets over $500,000. Earlier cohort iterations were free and included four in-person sessions plus online coaching over three months.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Fall 2025 cohort is now full; Spring 2026 cohort planned
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit leaders and teams from 501(c)(3) organizations located in and serving residents of Anne Arundel County who seek to diversify revenue sources and improve financial sustainability. The advanced cohort is intended for those who have completed a previous Fundraising & Sustainability cohort or who have baseline knowledge of fundraising concepts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and professional development in fundraising and sustainability strategies, including case development, organizational storytelling, strategic prospecting, grant development, diversified fundraising planning, and development or updating of a resource development plan.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Any 501(c)(3) nonprofit located in and serving residents of Anne Arundel County with administrative offices located in Anne Arundel County. At least 75 percent of the population served must reside in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: 501(c)(3) status for at least one year
In good standing with the State of Maryland
At least 75 percent of population served reside in Anne Arundel County

structured_extraction.program_description: The County funds design-build-maintain contracts with private firms to construct cost-effective stormwater Best Management Practices on privately owned properties. structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County reimburses private firms for design-build-maintain contracts that construct stormwater Best Management Practices. Award amounts vary by project; for example, recent awards ranged from $363,000 to $3,000,000. Full payment is made upon completion and County verification of the project's water quality benefits, typically within one year of construction. Ongoing maintenance payments may be released annually for up to 5 years after project completion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Solicitations conventionally open in late September to early October timeframe annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private firms that work with landowners to design and build stormwater Best Management Practices
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design, construction, and maintenance of stormwater Best Management Practices such as living shorelines, stream restoration, wetland enhancement, and regenerative stormwater conveyance on private properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only sites on private property within Anne Arundel County's Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) geography that do not conflict with existing projects underway are eligible
requirements_list: Project must be on private property within Anne Arundel County's MS4 geography
Project must not conflict with existing projects underway
Project must be construction-ready ("turnkey")
Project must generate verifiable water quality credits
Competitive proposals are prioritized based on technical merit, implementation likelihood, and cost-effectiveness metrics relating to the County's cost per equivalent impervious acre treated
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Search for the Request for Proposals on the Purchasing Office's Bid Opportunities webpage using the search term "full delivery of turnkey water quality improvements". structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps non-profits, homeowners associations, private landowners, and other organizations enhance the habitat and ecological balance of natural areas. The program supports activities such as pruning for vegetation health and safety, non-commercial timber stand improvement, and removal of invasive non-native vegetation with replanting of native species. Plans are required for removal of more than 5,000 square feet of existing natural vegetation in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area, Forest Conservation Easements, or Bog Protection Areas.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides planning guidance and approval for habitat enhancement activities. Applicants must complete and submit a Habitat Enhancement Plan to the Forestry Program for review before work may begin. The program offers two-year approval for compliant plans. All required state and federal permits must be obtained prior to Forestry approval. The approved plan or an available copy must be posted onsite during work performance for inspection purposes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profits, homeowners associations, private landowners, and other organizations seeking to enhance natural habitats and ecological balance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Activities may include pruning for the health and safety of vegetation, non-commercial timber stand improvement, and removal of non-native invasive vegetation with replanting of native species. Activities cannot include clearing of vegetation for development or work in preparation of a development application.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, specifically in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area, Forest Conservation Easements, or Bog Protection Areas for projects involving removal of greater than 5,000 square feet of existing natural vegetation.
requirements_list: Removal of greater than 5,000 square feet of existing natural vegetation in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area, Forest Conservation Easements, or Bog Protection Areas
All required state and federal permits must be obtained prior to Forestry approval
Approved plan or available copy must be posted onsite when work is being performed for inspection purposes
Activities cannot include clearing of vegetation for development or work in preparation of a development application
Scaled site plan required with dimensions drawn at specific ratio (1" = 20', 1" = 40', or 1" = 50' maximum)
Limit of Disturbance (LOD) and on-site location of vegetation to be removed must be clearly marked
Description of existing conditions and proposed work required, including size of disturbed area, eradication methods, replanting work, and timeline
Management plan required to ensure maintenance and management of areas (short term and long term)
Erosion and sediment controls are required and maintained
Submittal package must include cover letter, completed application, scaled site plan, work description, timeline, and management plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, contact the Forestry Office at (410) 222-7441 or forestry@aacounty.org to schedule an on-site proposal review. Prepare a complete submittal package including: a cover letter with contact information, completed Habitat Enhancement Plan Application with tax account number, scaled site plan showing Limit of Disturbance and environmental zones, description of existing conditions and proposed work with eradication methods and replanting details, timeline for invasive plant eradication, and long-term management plan. Submit the package (as a .pdf if emailing) to the Department of Inspections & Permits, Permit Center Reception Desk, 1st Floor, 2664 Riva Road, Annapolis, MD 21401 or email to forestry@aacounty.org. Obtain all required state and federal permits before Forestry approval. Approval is granted for two years unless otherwise noted. Post the approved plan or an available copy onsite during work performance for inspection purposes.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rural Legacy Area Program (Anne Arundel County)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program created by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that preserves large contiguous tracts of land while protecting natural resources, agriculture, forestry, and environmental resources. The program supports a sustainable land base for natural resource-based industries by acquiring easements and extinguishing development rights, with a major focus on increased stream buffer protection through required buffers. In Anne Arundel County, the program focuses on the Anne Arundel South Rural Legacy Area, creating greenways, preserving scenic views, and protecting historic and natural resources.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Purchases development rights from landowners via an Easement Valuation System (EVS) formula that awards points for development potential, presence of agriculture and woodland resources, and protection of natural resources on a property. Recent easement offers range from $8,000 to $10,000 per acre with cash at settlement. As of November 30, 2024, 17,059 acres (46%) of the Anne Arundel South Rural Legacy Area have been protected, including 1,830 acres permanently preserved through easements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with property located in a designated rural legacy area in Maryland, particularly those in Anne Arundel County's Anne Arundel South Rural Legacy Area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preservation of large contiguous tracts of land through purchase of development rights to create greenways, preserve scenic views, protect historic and natural resources, support agriculture and forestry, and establish required stream buffer protection.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated rural legacy areas in Maryland. In Anne Arundel County, the Anne Arundel South Rural Legacy Area encompasses 37,381 acres covering the area south of Central Avenue, extending west to east between the Patuxent and Rhode Rivers.
requirements_list: Property must be located in a designated rural legacy area
100 foot grass and forest buffers required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners in eligible rural legacy areas submit applications to participate in the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Management Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Residential and commercial property owners in Anne Arundel County may receive a credit towards their County real property taxes for the recent installation of qualified stormwater management practices. The credit is applied to County real property taxes only and becomes effective in the taxable year following approval. Eligible improvements must be from the Department of Public Works' approved devices list and pass a County inspection prior to credit approval.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The tax credit is 10% of the cost of materials and installation for making qualified improvements, not to exceed a total of $10,000 over the five-year life of the credit. The credit is applied to County real property taxes only and becomes effective in the taxable year following approval. The credit becomes effective beginning in the taxable year following approval and continues for four succeeding taxable years (five taxable years total), provided the property continues to meet all requirements. Improvements must remain in working condition and be regularly maintained. Failure to maintain improvements entitles the County to pursue a refund of the credit plus a penalty equal to 200% of the credit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 45 days of completion of qualifying improvements
structured_extraction.contact_name: Bureau of Watershed Protection and Restoration
structured_extraction.contact_phone: (410) 222-4240; (410) 222-1748 for property tax credit questions; (410) 222-7536 for qualified device questions
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential and commercial property owners in Anne Arundel County who have recently installed qualified stormwater management practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit applies to the cost of materials and installation of qualified stormwater management practices from the approved devices list, including but not limited to rain barrels/cisterns, rain gardens, removal of impervious coverage, swales, dry wells, landscape infiltration, permeable pavers, infiltration trenches, sand filters, green roofs, bioretention, constructed wetlands, regenerative step pool storm conveyance, wet ponds, retrofitted wet ponds with CMAC systems, and living shorelines.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must have recently installed qualified stormwater management practices from the Department of Public Works approved devices list
Application must be submitted within 45 days of completion of qualifying improvements
The credit cannot be combined with other tax credits
The qualified improvements cannot be installed as a requirement in any State or local law
The practice(s) must pass an inspection by County staff (Department of Public Works) prior to credit approval
Improvements must remain in working condition and be regularly maintained for the duration the credit is applied to the tax bill
Property owner must be current on all taxes owed to Anne Arundel County

Applicant must provide all required documentation with application submission, including receipts, invoices, photographs (before, during, and after if available), detailed plans as required for the specific device type, and soil type documentation as applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Stormwater Management Tax Credit Application Form. The application form requires property owner information, property address, parcel ID, type of qualified device(s) being claimed, date of completion, total cost of improvements, and copies of all receipts and paid invoices. Based on the type of qualified device selected, applicants must include required documentation which may include permits, photographs showing affected areas and improvements, detailed plans, and soil type documentation (specific requirements vary by device type per the List of Qualified Devices). Submit the completed application with all required documentation by email to taxcredits@aacounty.org or by mail to Anne Arundel County Office of Finance, Attn: Tax Credits, PO Box 427, Annapolis, MD 21404-0427. If mailing the application less than 14 days before the deadline, use a traceable form of delivery. The Department of Public Works will review and certify whether the property qualifies. Written notification will be sent upon approval or denial. If approved, the credit becomes effective in the taxable year following approval and appears on the real property tax bill for five consecutive taxable years (provided maintenance requirements are met).

structured_extraction.program_name: Video Lottery Terminal Grants – Video Lottery Facility Local Development Council (FY 2027)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Local Development Council (LDC) provides competitive grants to nonprofit and community organizations funded by revenues generated by Maryland Live! Casino video lottery terminals. Grants support local development and community initiatives for residents and communities within a three-mile radius of Live! Casino at Arundel Mills in Anne Arundel County. Eligible uses include community development and beautification, activities and services for children, youth, and vulnerable populations, workforce and skills development, infrastructure improvements, facilities, public safety, sanitation, economic and community development including housing, and other public services and improvements. Both capital and non-capital grant opportunities are available, including a standard Community Grant process and invitation-only grants for council-identified priorities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Community grants available on a competitive basis with award amounts ranging from a minimum of $1,000 to a maximum of $40,000. A limited number of grants may be awarded in excess of the $40,000 maximum. Invitation-only grants allow the Local Development Council to invite nonprofit organizations to apply for funding outside the standard Community Grant process to meet identified needs or council priorities. Both capital and non-capital grant opportunities are available. Capital grants fund equipment, supplies, and capital improvements (renovation, remodeling, restoration, or new construction of buildings). Non-capital grants build organizational capacity, increase impact, and support operational efficiency. Funding for organizations is limited to three consecutive grant cycles, after which the organization becomes ineligible for the following one grant cycle, except upon LDC finding that extraordinary circumstances justify a waiver.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and community associations serving residents within a three-mile radius of Live! Casino at Arundel Mills in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community development and beautification; activities and services for children, youth, and vulnerable populations; workforce and skills development; infrastructure improvements; facilities; public safety; sanitation; economic and community development including housing; and other public services and improvements. Both capital projects (equipment, supplies, renovation, remodeling, restoration, or new construction of buildings) and non-capital projects (capacity building, operational efficiency) are eligible. Projects should address important community needs without duplicating existing services and should serve a large number of residents or target special needs populations within the three-mile radius of the casino.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Communities and residents within a three-mile radius of Live! Casino at Arundel Mills in Anne Arundel County
requirements_list: Nonprofit organization or community association registered and in good standing
Serves residents within three-mile radius of Live! Casino at Arundel Mills
Demonstrates important community need without duplication of services
Project designed to meet identified community need
Organization has appropriate experience, capabilities, and financial viability
Provides evidence of community support and collaboration
Budget is reasonable and leverages other funding sources
Application contains all requested information with sufficient depth and clarity

For non-capital grants over $15,000: evidence of Commercial General Liability Insurance, Business Automobile Liability Insurance, Workers' Compensation Insurance, and Directors and Officers Liability Insurance

For capital grants regardless of funding amount: evidence of Commercial General Liability Insurance, Business Automobile Liability Insurance, Workers' Compensation Insurance, and Directors and Officers Liability Insurance with minimum coverage limits ($1,000,000 general liability, $1,000,000 automobile liability, $500,000 workers' compensation per accident/employee/disease, $1,000,000 directors and officers)
Certificate of Liability Insurance must name Anne Arundel County, Maryland, its servants, agents and employees as additional insureds
Compliance with Community Grant Guidelines

For non-capital grants up to $15,000: good standing status required but insurance certificate not required; for non-capital grants over $15,000: both good standing status and insurance certificate required
Award amounts between $1,000 and $40,000 for standard community grants
Limited funding availability for three consecutive grant cycles, with ineligibility for one cycle thereafter unless waiver granted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through an online platform (Neighborly) at portal.neighborlysoftware.com/acds/Participant. Applicants must review the Community Grant Guidelines before applying. Training videos and slides are provided to guide applicants through the application process. Standard proposal elements should include: cover letter, executive summary, need statement, project description (goals and objectives using SMART method: Specific, Measurable, Attainable, Relevant, Time Bound), methodology, detailed budget with justification narrative, and evaluation and reporting plan. The Local Development Council, composed of volunteers with diverse backgrounds, reviews applications and advises on grant awards. Applicants may be invited to present their proposal to the LDC (recommended limit: 10 minutes presentation with 5 minutes for questions). Applications should be compelling but concise, avoid industry jargon, explain any technical terminology or acronyms, and provide clear information on how the proposed project will address an identified need for the target population rather than organizational needs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee (WPRF) Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Property owners in Anne Arundel County can reduce their Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee (WPRF, also known as stormwater fee) assessments by up to 50% by implementing and maintaining proactive and sustainable stormwater control practices on their property. Property owners may enter into a Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement with the County outlining their maintenance responsibilities and allowing County inspections. The credit is calculated based on the amount of impervious surface treated and the rainfall depth managed by the installed practices.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reduces annual WPRF assessments by a percentage between 0% and 50% depending on the amount of impervious surface treated and rainfall treated. Multi-family, non-residential, and residential properties can receive up to 50% credit if the entire impervious surface area is treated with practices controlling at least 1 inch of rainfall. Partial credit is available if only a portion of impervious surface is treated or if practices control less than 1 inch of rainfall. The credit is calculated using the formula: (Treated Impervious ÷ Site's Total Impervious) x Treatment Value x Maximum Allowable Credit, where Maximum Allowable Credit is 50% and Treatment Value is 100% if at least 1 inch of rainfall is treated, or the percentage of 1 inch if less than 1 inch is treated. Non-residential properties with NPDES permits can receive 50% credit if the entire property is covered under the permit, or partial credit if only a portion is covered. Marina properties can receive up to 25% credit for NPDES permit compliance and up to 25% credit for Clean Marina Initiative certification, for a combined maximum of 50%. Property owners may enter into a Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement with the County to formalize maintenance responsibilities. Credits are valid for 3-year periods and continue in perpetuity provided practices are in good working condition and the property owner maintains compliance with the agreement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Anne Arundel County with stormwater management practices on their properties, including residential, multi-family, non-residential, marina, and NPDES-permitted properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credits are applied against the annual Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee (WPRF) to reduce the fee owed by the property owner. Property owners implement stormwater runoff controls to qualify for the credit. Eligible stormwater best management practices (BMPs) include permeable pavement, green roofs, rain gardens, bioretention facilities, bio-swales, cisterns, rain barrels, sheet flow to buffer areas, dry wells, infiltration systems, filtration systems, wetland systems, and wet ponds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Credits are available to multi-family, non-residential, and residential property owners, as well as agricultural properties (classified as residential if in residential zone with permanent dwelling with occupancy permit, otherwise classified as non-residential), NPDES-permitted properties, and marina properties.
requirements_list: Property must be located in Anne Arundel County
Stormwater management practices must be privately owned and maintained
Practices must be located on land with the same owner as the parcel seeking credit
Practices must have passed a recent inspection by County staff to verify proper design, construction, and maintenance
Practices must provide water quality treatment of at least 1 inch of rainfall for full credit, or proportional credit for less than 1 inch

Practices must be designed, approved, constructed, and maintained in accordance with County Standards, Stormwater Management Practices and Procedures Manual, and/or 2000 Maryland Stormwater Design Manual, Volumes I and II, and Supplements
Practices must be covered under an Inspection and Maintenance Agreement for Private Stormwater Management or a Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement
For multi-family, non-residential, and residential properties seeking full 50% credit, the entire impervious surface area or equivalent area must be treated with at least 1 inch of rainfall treated
For non-residential properties with NPDES permit, the entire property must be covered under the NPDES permit for full credit; partial credit available if only portion is covered
Marina properties must be regulated through an NPDES permit with stormwater management controls and/or certified by Maryland Department of Natural Resources as a Clean Marina
Application must be received or postmarked by October 1 of the taxable year (applications after this date will be processed but credit will not start until the following taxable year)

Applicant must submit photographs of practices and drainage areas, site plan or sketch showing property layout and practice locations, and copies of grading permit plans, stormwater management report, and installation documentation if applicable
Stormwater management practices must not be under an existing Inspection and Maintenance Agreement for Private Stormwater Management (for agreement-based pathway)
All owners listed on the property deed must sign the Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement

If the property is transferred to new owners, a new agreement must be entered into to continue the credit. An Inspection and Maintenance Agreement stays with the land and remains enforceable; a Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement does not transfer and new owner must enter into new agreement within specified timeframe or credit will be revoked
Must use proactive and sustainable stormwater runoff controls
For NPDES-permitted and Clean Marina properties, must maintain current permit or certification status to continue credit
Property owner must maintain and repair practices to ensure functioning as designed and must maintain inspection and maintenance records
County reserves right to inspect stormwater practices at any time; inspections occur at minimum once every three years for properties under Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application online through www.aarivers.org or by paper form. Paper applications must be received or postmarked by October 1 of the taxable year to receive credit in that taxable year; applications received after October 1 will be processed but credit will not start until the following taxable year. Required documentation includes: photographs of practices and drainage areas, site plan or sketch showing property layout and practice location, and copies of grading permit plans, stormwater management report, and installation documentation if applicable. For properties under an Inspection and Maintenance Agreement, attach a copy of the recorded agreement retrieved from Anne Arundel County Circuit Court Land Records or mdlandrec.net. For properties without such an agreement, indicate willingness to enter into a Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement during the application process. If needed, the County will provide an unsigned draft agreement specific to the property; all owners listed on the deed must sign and return it by mail. County staff will review the completed application and issue a written decision within 90 days of receipt. Prior to credit approval, the stormwater practice must pass a County inspection. If approved, necessary adjustments will be made to the billed fee and refund checks will be mailed separately from the decision letter. If payment has been made and a credit is thereafter granted, a refund will be issued for the current taxable year and the credit will be applied going forward. If payment has not been made before a credit is granted, the bill for the current taxable year will be adjusted and reissued. Credits are initially valid for a 3-year period and renew for 3-year intervals in perpetuity provided practices are in good working condition and functioning as designed and the applicant abides by the agreement. A renewal application is NOT required; the County will conduct functional verification prior to the end of each 3-year period. Property owner is responsible for continued maintenance and repair of practices and providing access to County for inspections. Failure to maintain practices in compliance with approved plans and agreements will result in loss of credit; property owner will be notified and given opportunity for corrective action before revocation.
