structured_extraction.program_description: A citywide public financing program administered by Baltimore City that uses Tax Increment Financing (TIF) bond proceeds to support affordable housing development by funding grants for hard construction costs to rehabilitate vacant buildings and public infrastructure improvements. The program targets vacant structures citywide—including properties with Vacant Building Notices—rather than specific geographic areas, making it available throughout Baltimore City across approximately 3,900–4,000 eligible properties. It is a historic first-of-its-kind citywide affordable housing TIF, unlike previous TIF districts focused on harbor neighborhoods, and forms a key part of Mayor Scott's $3 billion vacant housing elimination initiative. Grants are provided with no repayment requirement and are intended to close appraisal gaps, increase homeownership and rental opportunities for low- and moderate-income households, and support small, emerging, and minority developers. The program prioritizes legacy residents, women and minority-owned businesses, and small and emerging developers. The first series of TIF Bonds totaling $28.8 million closed on December 23, 2025, with up to $150 million planned over the life of the program.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TIF bond proceeds are provided as grants with no repayment requirement. The first series of bonds totaling $28.8 million closed on December 23, 2025. The initial round has approximately $15–18 million available for grant awards; up to $150 million is planned over the program's lifetime. An estimated $3 million is allocated specifically to legacy residents, small and emerging developers, minority developers, current TIF District residents, business owners, and individuals renovating family-owned homes. There is no maximum amount of TIF funds that can be requested or number of properties for which funds can be requested. Average award is anticipated at approximately $100,000 per project. Grant amounts are determined based on property size, condition, end use (rental or homeownership), affordability level, appraisal gap, construction budget, project description, financing ability, and capacity to complete. TIF funds are provided on a reimbursement basis only. Applicants must fund construction upfront and submit reimbursement requests with documentation. Funds are disbursed via reimbursement in up to 4 draws: two draws totaling up to 90% of approved construction costs during construction, one draw upon receipt of Use and Occupancy permit, and one final draw when the property is occupied. Reimbursement requests require third-party inspector approval, City review, and Verification Agent approval. Applicants must provide proof of eligible cost completion and executed construction contracts.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 3, 2025 (first round, now closed); subsequent rounds anticipated. Submissions accepted through Neighborly Platform online portal.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, developers, nonprofits, limited liability companies, individual residents, legacy residents, small and emerging developers, women and minority-owned businesses, community development organizations, business owners, and individuals seeking to rehabilitate vacant properties in Baltimore City into affordable housing for rental or homeownership. Applicants include: organizations with executed Land Disposition Agreements (LDAs), developers in DHCD's Developer Registry, legacy residents living in the TIF District, current TIF District residents, small and emerging developers (with 3 or fewer years of experience or 5 or fewer completed projects), for-profit and nonprofit affordable housing developers, and individuals purchasing or currently owning TIF-eligible properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hard construction costs to redevelop vacant buildings for residential use (rental or homeownership), including excavation, demolition, grading, site improvements, building structure/shell repair, foundations, framing, floor and roof structure, roof cover, ceiling, building service equipment (electrical, plumbing, HVAC, fire protection, alarm systems, elevators, computer and network cabling, telecommunications cabling), interior and exterior finishes, floor coverings, stationary equipment, and other building fixed equipment. Public infrastructure improvements required for city-sponsored homeownership development projects, including streets, curbs, gutters, sidewalks, lighting, landscaping, roads, water and utilities. Funds can be used to close appraisal gaps and create or preserve affordability. Funds CANNOT be used for architectural and engineering services (except as specified for design costs), site development, landscaping (except in infrastructure improvements), utilities installation (except in infrastructure improvements), permitting costs, financing costs (e.g., interest, points), property acquisition, work already completed, or costs incurred before Grant Agreement execution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Citywide Baltimore City. Eligible properties must be located within the City-Wide Affordable Housing TIF District (established under City Council Bill 24-0595 / Ordinance 24-443), which includes approximately 3,991 vacant properties eligible for redevelopment out of 8,587 total TIF properties when the district was established in December 2024. Properties must have been issued a Vacant Building Notice (VBN), or meet other eligibility criteria including: eligible for Judicial In Rem Foreclosure, acquired using ARPA or other City funds, City-owned vacant building, or needed for a development project. Applicants can verify eligibility using the City's searchable GIS/interactive map at https://baltimoredhcd.maps.arcgis.com/apps/webappviewer/index.html?id=07c3067e80574982a813349a11fd9986 (properties marked with a green dot are eligible). The district covers non-contiguous neighborhoods including Auchentoroly-Parkwood, Broadway East, Darley Park, Druid Heights, East Baltimore Midway, Harlem Park, Mondawmin, Oliver, Park Heights, Penn-North, Poppleton, Upton, Walbrook, and Coldstream Homestead Montebello, among others across East and West Baltimore.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the online Neighborly Platform (https://portal.neighborlysoftware.com/baltimoremd/Participant). This is a multi-step process: (1) Threshold Review and Scoring: DHCD staff conducts internal administrative and financial review to ensure all application requirements are met, verifying eligibility, confirming completeness, and checking for discrepancies. Applications with 3 or fewer Threshold Review inaccuracies are given opportunity to cure. ALL SUBMISSIONS MUST MEET THRESHOLD REVIEW to be considered for award. (2) Applications determined to have met Threshold Criteria are scored on: Financing and Ability to Spend TIF Funds (40 points maximum for LDA & Developer Registry applications only—based on executed Letters of Commitment, award letters, evidence of personal funds, and sufficient financing for project completion); Scheduling (25 points maximum for LDA & Developer Registry applications only—based on feasibility of completing project within 12 months with realistic benchmarks); Applicant Capacity (25 points maximum for LDA & Developer Registry applications only—based on prior experience, team readiness, and team members' experience renovating Baltimore single-family residential properties); and Site Control (10 points maximum for LDA & Developer Registry applications only—based on demonstrated ability to have title within 30 days of Grant Agreement execution). Funding requests that are part of LDA or Developer Registry will be evaluated based on meeting Threshold Requirements and will NOT be scored. Applications requesting funds for privately owned properties will be evaluated for Threshold Requirements AND will be scored. Applications submitted by Legacy Residents living within TIF District will be evaluated for Threshold Requirements and will NOT be subject to scoring. Other considerations include affordability level, support from Baltimore Vacancy Reduction Initiative (BVRI), whole-block outcomes, and community support and alignment with community plans. (3) Conditional Award Letters: Applicants recommended for award receive letter requesting detailed project budgets for review by City's Bond Counsel and TIF Verification Agent, executed construction contracts, and financial information confirming TIF Funds are needed to bridge appraisal gap or promote affordability. (4) Execution of Grant Agreement: Following review and approval, City and awardee execute Grant Agreement (form agreement previously approved by Board of Estimates; cannot be revised). Awardees must accept award by signing and returning Award Letter within 5 calendar days of receipt and execute Grant Agreement no more than 30 days after receiving Award Letter. (5) Project Implementation and Disbursement: Grantees implement projects and provide quarterly progress reports to ensure completion within 12-month term and TIF Funds disbursed prior to end of term. To receive reimbursement, grantees submit requisition forms with: documentation of completed work, third-party inspector approval, actual costs, and executed construction contracts. Reimbursement requires inspection and approval by third-party inspector, review by City, and review and approval by Verification Agent. Funds disbursed in up to 4 draws: two draws up to 90% of approved construction costs during construction, one draw upon receipt of Use and Occupancy permit, one final draw when property is occupied. Contact AHTIF@baltimorecity.gov for technical assistance or info@neighborlysoftware.com for Neighborly platform technical assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A fund created by Baltimore City voters to increase affordable housing for very-low and low-income households in Baltimore City. The fund supports both rental and for-sale affordable housing, requiring that all revenue be used to help those with incomes at or below 50 percent of the Area Median Income, with at least half of the funds reserved for those with incomes at or below 30 percent of the Area Median Income (approximately $27,000 or less for a family of four as of 2018). Annual city allocations scale from $2 million in FY2020 to $7 million annually from FY2023 onward.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Trust Fund provides financial assistance for affordable housing development and preservation. Annual city allocations are: FY2020 $2 million, FY2021 $3.5 million, FY2022 $5 million, and FY2023 and subsequent years $7 million annually. Funds are allocated according to approved spending priorities designed to maximize effectiveness, with specific funding amounts and terms detailed in individual Notices of Funding. The fund is administered through the Affordable Housing Trust Fund Commission, which makes recommendations to DHCD regarding fund expenditures and operation. The Commission includes representatives from housing, community development, lending, social services, homeless services, fair housing advocacy, nonprofit development, and homebuilding sectors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Very-low and low-income households in Baltimore City seeking rental or for-sale affordable housing, particularly those earning at or below 50 percent of Area Median Income, with priority for those at or below 30 percent of Area Median Income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting rental and for-sale affordable housing development and preservation for households with incomes at or below 50 percent of Area Median Income, with at least half directed to those at or below 30 percent of Area Median Income.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only.
requirements_list: Household income must be at or below 50 percent of Area Median Income
At least half of funds directed to households at or below 30 percent of Area Median Income (approximately $27,000 or less for a family of four as of 2018)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants apply through the Neighborly Application Portal. Applications are reviewed by the Affordable Housing Trust Fund Commission, an advisory body that makes recommendations to DHCD regarding fund expenditures and operation. The Commission includes 13 members representing diverse stakeholder groups including housing professionals, lenders, DHCD staff, residents at various income levels, homebuilders, fair housing advocates, and social service providers. Details on current funding opportunities and application requirements are available through Notices of Funding published by the Trust Fund.

structured_extraction.program_name: Affordable Housing Trust Fund - Community Land Trust Homeownership NOFA
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development administers the Affordable Housing Trust Fund to support homeownership projects sponsored by Community Land Trusts. The program promotes equitable community development in historically disinvested areas of Baltimore City by funding single family homeownership initiatives through three strategies: Acquisition & Rehab, Buyers Choice/Buyer-Initiated, and Innovation. The most recent round (August 2024) makes up to $8.1 million available, with qualified applicants able to request up to $1,000,000 per project. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis through June 30, 2025.
list_of_prioritized_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $8.1 million in grant funds available from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund for homeownership projects. Qualified applicants can request up to $1,000,000 per project. Per-unit maximums: $75,000 for units restricted to persons with incomes at or below 50% of AMI, and $120,000 per unit for units restricted to persons with incomes at or below 30% of AMI. Funds can support up to 50% of Total Development Cost (TDC) for 50% AMI units, or up to 66% of TDC for 30% AMI units. Up to 25% of total award can be used for predevelopment and/or acquisition costs, and up to 20% can be used for operating costs directly related to project implementation. Eligible uses include permits, surveys, legal fees, property consultant fees, market feasibility analysis, architectural/engineering costs, environmental assessment, construction, acquisition and stabilization of non-City owned properties, carrying costs, financing and lender fees, consultant fees, landscaping, project management staff, and infrastructure/utilities for single family, condos, and co-op projects. For Buyers Choice projects, funds can provide direct subsidy to assist eligible buyers. Awards are notified within 90 days of application submission. All grants are reimbursable upon submission of invoice or payment receipt.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Land Trusts (CLTs) sponsoring homeownership projects in Baltimore City, particularly those focused on single family homeownership in communities with long-term and historical disinvestment. Applicants must be organized or managed by a nonprofit organization exempt from taxation under §501(c)(2), (3), or (4) of the Internal Revenue Code, or demonstrate equivalent nonprofit management structure.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Homeownership projects sponsored by Community Land Trusts using one of three strategies: (1) Acquisition & Rehab - acquiring homes or vacant land and rehabilitating for sale to eligible first-time homebuyers; (2) Buyers Choice/Buyer-Initiated - allowing eligible buyers to identify and purchase housing in target areas with funding to lower first mortgage requirements; (3) Innovation - other creative homeownership strategies. Funds support single family, condo, and co-op housing projects in communities with long-term and historical disinvestment, restricted to households earning 50% or less of Area Median Income (AMI), with preference for households at 30% AMI or below.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Projects must be located within Baltimore City. DHCD reserves the right to ensure funded projects include geographic representation across the city and support a range of eligible organizations.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted electronically on a rolling basis starting August 23, 2024 through June 30, 2025 via the Neighborly Portal at portal.neighborlysoftware.com/BALTIMOREMD. Applicants must submit one complete electronic PDF copy of application using Application Checklist as Table of Contents, including all attachments and Threshold Requirements, plus one Excel Spreadsheet copy of development budget. Applications meeting Threshold Review requirements are scored by AHTF Staff based on project feasibility (70 points maximum), community engagement and participation (40 points maximum), and achieving equity (15 points maximum), with opportunities for up to 30 bonus points. Minimum score of 120 out of 155 points required for consideration. AHTF Staff provides recommendations to Housing Commissioner for final award decisions. Notification of awards occurs within 90 days of application submission. Incomplete, denied, or threshold-non-compliant submissions cannot resubmit until 60 days after notice. Pre-Proposal Conference resources from prior rounds available on DHCD website; no new conference held for rolling NOFA. Questions submitted in writing to DHCD.AHTFNOFA@baltimorecity.gov. Responses posted on DHCD website. Threshold requirements include: Authorization to Submit signed within 30 days; completed application form; IRS Determination Letter; Certification of Compliance; Owned Property Disclosure; Commitment to Comply; Local Hire Certification; organizational documents including Corporate Resolution/Board approval; By-Laws; Evidence of Good Standing with State of Maryland; Board of Directors list with titles and affiliations; organizational chart showing board structure; copy of Ground Lease or Deed Restriction; Stewardship Standards; Memorandum of Understanding between land trust and developer; progress reports for existing awardees; commitment letters for all funding sources; most recent 990 Tax Return (nonprofits with annual budgets $500,000+) or Audited Financial Statement (budgets $500,000+) or Financial Statement from certified accounting firm (budgets $200,000-$500,000) or annual budget (budgets under $200,000); estimated rehab budget and template; site plans for new projects and remodels. Following submission deadline, DHCD posts summary of submissions including applicant name, project, location, units, total development cost, and funds requested. After award notification, DHCD conducts underwriting meeting to review fund availability and draw-down process. Board of Estimates must approve Funding Agreement before funds made available. Quarterly reports required after Board of Estimates approval. Reimbursement-based grants require invoice or payment receipt submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Health Department certifies entities to serve as Air Monitoring Contractors for commercial solid waste incinerators in the city. Certified contractors design, install, operate, and maintain continuous emissions monitoring systems, report emissions data, manage public dissemination of data, and conduct periodic inspections.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Health Department provides certification to qualified entities, enabling them to be hired by regulated commercial solid waste incinerators within Baltimore City to perform air emissions monitoring and reporting services. Certified contractors design, install, operate, and maintain continuous emissions monitoring systems (CEMS) for specified air pollutants including dioxins/furans, CO2, CO, HCl, HF, NOx, SO2, PM, VOCs, PAHs, and heavy metals (arsenic, cadmium, chromium VI, lead, manganese, mercury, nickel, selenium, zinc). Contractors must report daily emissions data to the Health Department, display and archive historical and real-time emissions data on a public website with graphical representation, conduct unannounced inspections of CEMS equipment at least four times per calendar year, and develop software capable of capturing and disseminating CEMS and stack test data.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single contractors, contractors with subcontractors, and partnerships of co-applicants capable of providing comprehensive air monitoring services for commercial solid waste incinerators in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification enables contractors to provide design, installation, operation, and maintenance of continuous emissions monitoring systems for commercial solid waste incinerators, as well as public data dissemination, archival, and periodic inspections.

Fayette Street, Baltimore, MD 21202. The application must include corporate name(s), officer/owner names and titles, business address, contact information, email address(es), proof of compliance with Maryland Workers' Compensation requirements, and a Statement of Capacity indicating the entity's ability to fulfill all obligations under the Baltimore Clean Air Act. Applications may be mailed or provided in person. The application fee must be submitted with the application, made payable to 'Director of Finance.'

structured_extraction.program_description: The Alley Gating and Alley Greening Programs allow Baltimore City residents to gate and green public alleys to create quiet, safe spaces and green oases in their neighborhoods. Alley Gating involves installing locked gates to limit access and eliminate vehicular traffic, noise, littering, and loitering. Alley Greening goes further by making alleys impassible to vehicles through landscaping and alterations. The program is administered by the Department of Transportation's Land Conveyance Section.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program facilitates the gating and greening of alleys by providing administrative support, technical guidance, and coordination with city agencies and utilities. The program does not provide direct financial assistance for gate construction or greening improvements; applicants must raise funds to purchase gates and pay for installations. Applicants must also submit a $250 processing fee payable to the Director of Finance. For Alley Gating, the city issues a Lease Agreement typically for a 5-year term that automatically renews for four additional 5-year terms. For Alley Greening, applicants must follow the Developer's Agreement process and obtain an engineered drawing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents, property owners, neighborhood associations, and non-profit entities interested in gating and greening public alleys in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Applicants must raise funds to purchase and install gates for Alley Gating projects. For Alley Greening, funds are needed for engineered drawings, alterations to make alleys impassible to vehicles, landscaping, and installation of green infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Public alleys in Baltimore City where adjacent structures are mostly residential and the gating and/or greening will promote public health, safety, or welfare. Baltimore City has approximately 600 miles of alleys.
requirements_list: Alley must be in an area where adjacent structures are mostly residential
Gating and/or greening must promote public health, safety, or welfare
For Alley Gating: Obtain written consent from owners of at least 75% of affected properties (excluding abandoned properties)
For Alley Greening: Obtain written consent from 100% of abutting property owners
Applicants must be a Neighborhood Association or Non-Profit Entity (for lease execution)
Submit Alley Gating Application with digital images and marked-up City Block Plat
Applicants must raise funds to purchase the gate or pay for greening improvements
Submit $250 processing fee payable to Director of Finance
For Alley Greening: Submit engineered drawing and follow Developer's Agreement process
For historic neighborhoods: Obtain approval from Baltimore City Commission for Historic and Architectural Preservation (CHAP)
Approval required from Police Commissioner and Fire Marshal
Gates must include three lock boxes (Knox box for Fire Department, BGE box, and utility/city/police box)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Contact the Land Conveyance Section at 410-396-4283 or alley.gating@baltimorecity.gov to discuss feasibility and obtain necessary forms. Step 2: Submit Alley Gating Application with digital images and marked-up City Block Plat to Land Conveyance Section (Councilman Harry S Cummings Building, LL 401 E. Fayette Street, Baltimore City, MD 21202). Step 3: Land Conveyance Section distributes application to utilities and city agencies for review; approval from Police Commissioner and Fire Marshal is required. Step 4: Obtain written consent from at least 75% of abutting property owners (100% for Alley Greening) using consent forms provided by Land Conveyance Section. For abandoned properties, an affidavit may be submitted. Step 5: Mail or email copies of consents, $250 processing fee check, and all required documents to Land Conveyance Section. Step 6: Land Conveyance Section contacts applicant with public hearing date, time, and location. Step 7: Applicant is responsible for mailing notice to all abutting property owners at least 10 days before hearing and posting notices at each end of the alley (minimum 11" x 14"). Step 8: Attend public hearing with original signed consents and required documents; Land Conveyance Section prepares affidavit for applicant to execute. Step 9: Director issues written decision within 30 days of hearing. Step 10: If approved, Land Conveyance Section prepares Lease Agreement (typically 5-year term with automatic renewal for four additional 5-year terms); applicant executes and returns three copies to Land Conveyance Section for approval by City Law Department, Director, Mayor's Office, and Board of Estimates. Step 11: After Board of Estimates approval, obtain necessary permits from HCD Permit Office (417 E. Fayette Street, First Floor, Baltimore, MD 21202); for historic neighborhoods, obtain CHAP approval. Step 12: Once permits approved, applicant or contractor may construct/install gates with three required lock boxes. For Alley Greening: Follow same steps but require 100% property owner consent and submit engineered drawing; follow Developer's Agreement process and contact DOT Transportation Engineering and Construction Division (410-396-6946) to schedule Change of Grade Hearing if applicable.

structured_extraction.program_description: An out-of-school job training program for young adults aged 18-24 that provides certification training in customer service, pharmacy, childcare, and nursing assistant roles.

Must be aged 18-24

structured_extraction.program_description: The Mayor's Office of Employment Development provides employers with $2,500 per apprentice to support apprenticeship programs. MOED helps employers recruit Baltimore City residents for apprenticeship opportunities and provides or connects apprentices to support services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers receive $2,500 per apprentice to pay for training, wages, or support services. Employers must provide at least 2,000 hours per year of on-the-job training, training at the worksite under highly skilled industry experts, and at least 144 hours of related instruction per year of the apprenticeship. MOED also helps with recruiting Baltimore City residents and connecting apprentices to support services.

Training must occur at the worksite under the direction of highly skilled industry experts
Employers must provide at least 144 hours of related instruction per year of the apprenticeship
Apprentices must be Baltimore City residents
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers interested in learning more about MOED's apprenticeship subsidies or creating an apprenticeship program should email apprenticeships@baltimorecity.gov

structured_extraction.program_description: The Mayor's Office of Employment Development connects jobseekers with paid apprenticeship opportunities across Baltimore City in industries including healthcare, plumbing, HVAC, construction, technology, transportation, and telecommunications. Apprentices build skills through personalized instruction from industry experts while earning wages.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Apprentices receive at least 2,000 hours per year of on-the-job training at the worksite under the direction of skilled industry experts (journeyworkers), plus at least 144 hours of related classroom instruction per year. Participants are paid while training and receive scheduled pay increases tied to skills and service. Apprentices earn credentials to boost career opportunities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Jobseekers over 18 years old who live in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid apprenticeship training in healthcare, plumbing, HVAC, construction, technology, transportation, telecommunications, and related industries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Applicants must live in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years or older
Must be a Baltimore City resident
Pre-apprenticeship support available including resume building and skills assessments
Only 100 new apprenticeships available for paid training and wages
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the Apprenticeship Form online and the office will reach out via email shortly. Pre-apprenticeship support is available, including resume building, skills assessment, and more. Find out more and apply by emailing apprenticeships@baltimorecity.gov or calling 410-396-1910.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funding support for artists in Baltimore through the Creative Baltimore Fund, administered by Create Baltimore.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Artist grants providing funding to support artists in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Artists in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To support artists through funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: SNAP participants in Baltimore City can earn produce benefit coupons and delivery discounts by purchasing groceries through Amazon Fresh using their SNAP/EBT cards. For every $5 spent in SNAP funds at Amazon Fresh, participants receive a $30 produce benefit coupon to buy fresh or frozen fruits and vegetables, plus a $20 delivery promotion coupon.
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants earn a $30 produce benefit coupon valid for 60 days after spending $5 in SNAP/EBT funds at Amazon Fresh. Additionally, they receive a $20 delivery promotion coupon applied toward delivery fees. Participants can receive one produce benefit coupon and one delivery benefit coupon each month. The produce benefit coupons can be used to purchase SNAP/EBT eligible fresh or frozen fruits and vegetables with no added salt, sugar, or fat.
structured_extraction.program_audience: SNAP/EBT participants who live in Baltimore City and have a Baltimore City zip code
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Produce benefit coupons can be used to purchase SNAP/EBT eligible fresh or frozen fruits and vegetables with no added salt, sugar, or fat. Delivery coupons can be applied toward Amazon Fresh delivery fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Amazon account must have a Baltimore City zip code to qualify. Program is available to Baltimore City residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a SNAP/EBT participant
Must have a Baltimore City zip code
Must create an Amazon account (Prime account not required)
Must add SNAP/EBT card to Amazon Wallet using a Baltimore City address as the default address
Must spend at least $5 in SNAP funds at Amazon Fresh each month to qualify for that month's benefit coupons
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Create or log in to an Amazon account with a Baltimore City zip code. Add your SNAP/EBT card to your Amazon Wallet using your Baltimore City address. Spend at least $5 in SNAP funds at Amazon Fresh each month. After your order is delivered, the $30 benefit coupon and $20 delivery coupon will appear in your Benefits Balance section. Redeem your benefit coupon within 60 days.

structured_extraction.program_name: B'more Fresh: Online SNAP Produce Incentive
structured_extraction.program_description: B'more Fresh is an online SNAP incentive program administered by Baltimore City that provides SNAP participants with monthly produce vouchers to purchase fresh and frozen fruits and vegetables from approved online retailers including Amazon, Giant, and Safeway. After spending a minimum of $5 on SNAP-eligible items through online shopping, eligible participants receive a $30 monthly e-incentive for produce purchases. The program is funded by a $3.6 million American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) investment and is designed to address digital equity and food access inequities in Baltimore City, enabling home delivery of groceries. The Safeway-specific component additionally provides three $10 digital deals and one free grocery delivery per month to qualifying participants. The program is currently funded through December 2026.
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: After spending a minimum of $5 on SNAP-eligible items through online shopping with participating retailers (Amazon, Giant, or Safeway), eligible participants receive a $30 monthly e-incentive that can be used to purchase fresh and frozen fruits and vegetables online. At Safeway specifically, participants who spend $5 or more using their SNAP EBT card each month receive three $10 digital deals (total $30 value) for online produce purchases plus one free grocery delivery per month. Digital deals are automatically loaded to the participant's Safeway for U account on the first day of the following month. The program is funded by a $3.6 million ARPA investment and runs through December 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents enrolled in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) who shop for groceries online through approved retailers including Amazon, Giant, and Safeway.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of fresh and frozen fruits and vegetables (with no added salt, sugar, or fat for Safeway digital deals) from approved online retailers including Amazon, Giant, and Safeway. Orders must be placed online for curbside pick-up or home delivery in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Orders must be placed online for curbside pick-up or delivery in Baltimore City. For the Safeway component, purchases must be made at Baltimore City Safeway locations.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City resident receiving SNAP benefits
Must have a valid SNAP EBT card on file at the time of purchase
Must spend a minimum of $5 on SNAP-eligible items through online shopping to receive the monthly $30 e-incentive
Must shop at one of the participating retailers: Amazon, Giant, or Safeway
Orders must be placed online for curbside pick-up or delivery in Baltimore City
For Safeway component: must have or create a free Safeway for U account
For Safeway component: must enter phone number at checkout pin pad or with online order
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: SNAP participants automatically qualify and can begin earning vouchers by spending $5 on SNAP-eligible items when shopping online with participating retailers (Amazon, Giant, or Safeway). After each qualifying purchase, a $30 produce voucher or e-incentive is added to the online account. For the Safeway component, participants must sign up for a free Safeway for U account at Safeway.com or in-store, use their SNAP EBT card to spend at least $5 at a Baltimore City Safeway location, and enter their phone number at the pin pad during checkout or with their online order. Digital deals will be automatically loaded to the Safeway for U account on the first day of the following month. Visit https://www.baltimorecity.gov/bmorefresh for full enrollment information.

structured_extraction.program_description: An innovative initiative to reduce infant mortality in Baltimore City through programs emphasizing policy change, service improvements, community mobilization, and behavior change.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The initiative provides services and support focused on reducing infant mortality through policy development, service improvements, community engagement, and behavior change programs.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services focused on improving birth outcomes and reducing infant mortality.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore Gas and Electric offers a special needs program for older adults and other customers who require power to run life-support equipment in their homes during emergencies and cold weather events.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Special program providing priority protection of power service for customers with life-support equipment needs during emergencies and extreme cold events.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults and other BGE customers who require power to operate life-support medical equipment in their homes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Priority electrical service protection for homes with life-support equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: BGE service territory customers in Baltimore City area.
requirements_list: Require power to run life-support equipment in home
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact BGE's special needs hotline at 1-877-213-2610 during emergency events or visit their Special Needs Customers webpage for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Fire Department provides free smoke alarms to residents of Baltimore City. Firefighters will install 10-year lithium, tamper-resistant smoke alarms on each level of the home, typically within two hours of the request.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free smoke alarms and installation to eligible residents. The alarms are 10-year lithium, tamper-resistant models that are installed on each level of the home, typically within two hours of request.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Baltimore City, including those who are deaf or hard of hearing
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free smoke alarms and professional installation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Baltimore City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To request free smoke alarms, residents should call 311. The request is routed to the Baltimore City Fire Department. Residents who are deaf or hard of hearing can contact the Office of the Fire Marshal directly at (410) 396-5752.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore City Community Action Partnership Energy Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Community Action Partnership provides subsidies to help low-income residents pay their heating bills during winter months, reducing vulnerability to hypothermia and cold-related health problems. The program also helps residents manage their energy bills and prevent service disconnections by offering assistance with utility costs and energy efficiency improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial subsidies to assist low-income residents with heating bills during winter months, as well as support for energy efficiency improvements to help reduce household energy costs. Applicants can check their application status or obtain an application through the online portal at myohepstatus.org.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income residents of Baltimore City who need help paying heating and utility bills.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of heating bills, utility bills, and home energy efficiency improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City residents only.
requirements_list: Low-income household
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals can apply online through the status portal at myohepstatus.org, by calling 410-396-5555, or by dialing 311. Older adults can receive assistance completing and mailing applications through the Baltimore City Office of Aging & CARE Services at 410-396-CARE (2273).

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides financial assistance to employees of Baltimore City and quasi-City agencies to help them buy homes in the city. Eligible employees receive a one-time incentive to reduce closing costs and support their down payment. The incentive is provided as a five-year forgivable loan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible employees receive $5,000 in assistance provided as a five-year forgivable loan to help reduce closing costs and support down payments. Employees must have been employed with the City or a quasi-City agency for at least six months to qualify. All incentives require homeownership counseling from a City-approved homeownership counseling agency within one year before writing an offer on a home, and a minimum $1,000 investment from the home buyer's own funds towards the purchase of the property.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Funding is planned each year based on the City's fiscal calendar (July 1 to June 30). Incentives are given out on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employees of Baltimore City and quasi-City agencies who have been employed for at least six months and are interested in buying a home in Baltimore.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The assistance can be used to reduce closing costs and support down payments when buying a home in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: This program is available to homebuyers purchasing property in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be employed by Baltimore City or a quasi-City agency
Must have been employed for at least six months
Must complete a homeownership class from a City-approved homeownership counseling agency within one year before writing an offer on a home
Must contribute at least $1,000 of your own funds towards the purchase of the property
Settlement date must be at least 30 days after submitting application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register your account and submit an application through the Applicant Portal at https://portal.neighborlysoftware.com/baltimoremd/Participant. Create a user name (using your email address) and password during registration. The email address you choose will be used for system notifications, so it is recommended to use your work email address. Your housing counselor and lender must complete the online application. Allow at least 30 days between application submission and settlement date for processing. Checks typically take 10 to 15 business days to be sent after approval. The system will automatically log you out after thirty minutes of inactivity.

structured_extraction.program_description: A public campaign financing program that provides matching funds from the City to eligible candidates running for City elective office. The program aims to reduce the influence of large contributions and encourage small donations from residents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides matching City funds to candidates who meet eligibility requirements. Candidates must receive qualifying contributions of up to $150 each from City residents. Matching fund amounts vary by office: Mayor requires at least 500 qualifying contributions totaling $40,000; Council President and Comptroller each require at least 250 qualifying contributions totaling $15,000; and City Council candidates require at least 150 qualifying contributions totaling $5,000. For every qualifying contribution received, the City provides matching funds at a specified rate.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by election cycle; candidates must apply for certification during the designated filing period for their race
structured_extraction.program_audience: Candidates who are City residents running for Mayor, Comptroller, City Council President, or City Council seats in contested primary and/or general elections.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Campaign financing for eligible candidates for City elective office.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Candidates must be residents of Baltimore City and running for City elective office in Baltimore.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City resident
Must be running for Mayor, Comptroller, City Council President, or City Council
Must be running in a contested primary and/or general election
Must be certified for public funding by the State Board of Elections
Mayor candidates must receive at least 500 qualifying contributions (up to $150 each) totaling $40,000 from City residents
Council President candidates must receive at least 250 qualifying contributions (up to $150 each) totaling $15,000 from City residents
Comptroller candidates must receive at least 250 qualifying contributions (up to $150 each) totaling $15,000 from City residents
City Council candidates must receive at least 150 qualifying contributions (up to $150 each) totaling $5,000 from City residents
Must comply with campaign finance reporting requirements
Contributions must come from individual Baltimore City residents
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Candidates must apply for certification with the State Board of Elections during the designated filing period for their election. The Fair Election Fund is overseen by the City's Department of Finance in consultation with the Fair Election Fund Commission and State Board of Elections. Once certified, candidates who meet the threshold requirements receive matching funds based on qualifying small-dollar contributions received from City residents.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore City Family Caregiver Application / National Family Caregiver Support Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A support program administered by Baltimore City's Office of Aging & CARE Services that provides free resources, training, and supportive services to help family caregivers provide care while maintaining their own well-being. Services include information and referral, personal assistance, counseling and education, support groups, respite care guidance, and limited financial grants for in-home services and caregiving supplies. The program is funded through the National Family Caregiver Support Program and serves caregivers of older adults, individuals with Alzheimer's or related dementias, and grandparents or relatives caring for children or adults with disabilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers non-emergency financial grants of $300 to $600 per person annually to pay for respite services, in-home services, or to reimburse caregivers for out-of-pocket expenses. Funds may be paid directly to the caregiver or care recipient. The program also provides free training, counseling, support groups, and referral services. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis and are subject to the availability of funds. Processing time is up to 90 days.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis - applications accepted year-round on first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.contact_name: Linda Stewart, Jazmine Adams, Jose Jimenez
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family caregivers who are 18 years or older caring for older adults age 60 or older, individuals with Alzheimer's or related dementias, grandparents or relatives age 55 or older caring for children 18 and under, and relatives age 55 or older caring for adults with disabilities. All applicants must be Baltimore City residents or caregivers of Baltimore City residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used to hire providers for respite services, pay for in-home services, purchase consumable caregiving supplies, and reimburse caregivers for out-of-pocket expenses related to caregiving.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The care recipient must be a Baltimore City resident. The caregiver and care recipient do not need to live in the same household, but if they live separately, the distance cannot exceed 25 miles.
requirements_list: Complete all application forms and submit to the Office of Aging & CARE Services
Care recipient must need help with at least 2 activities of daily living (for adults 60 and older or disabled adults)
Medical verification required from care recipient's doctor or medical practitioner (for adults 60 and older and disabled adults ages 19-59)
For grandparent or relative caregivers of children, must demonstrate guardianship, custody, or kinship care and be 55 years or older
Caregiver must be 18 years or older for adults 60 and older, or 55 years or older for grandparent/relative caregivers and caregivers for disabled adults
If caregiver and care recipient live separately, a notarized letter must be provided naming the primary caregiver
Copy of Maryland State ID or other photo ID verifying age
Copy of unaltered Social Security card for both caregiver and care recipient
Copies of receipts, invoices, or bills justifying the grant request
W-9 form completed before processing and disbursement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the National Family Caregiver Support Program at 410-396-1337 to request an application package. Complete all forms in the application packet including the Family Caregiver Grant Request form. Include supporting documents such as copies of receipts and invoices. Provide medical verification from the care recipient's doctor using the Medical Status Verification Form. Submit ID verification, Social Security card copies, and a completed W-9 form. Return the completed packet to the Office of Aging & CARE Services as soon as possible. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis subject to fund availability. Processing time is up to 90 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Financial Empowerment Center offers free professional one-on-one financial counseling and coaching to all Baltimore City residents regardless of income level. Services are delivered in person or remotely and cover managing finances, paying down debt, increasing savings, establishing and building credit, accessing safe and affordable banking products, and legacy planning education. Counselors are professionally trained and certified, and a minimum of 3-5 sessions is recommended.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free professional financial counseling and coaching delivered through one-on-one sessions (in-person or remote). Services include credit building and repair, banking guidance, debt reduction strategies, savings planning, and legacy planning education. A minimum of 3-5 sessions is recommended. Counselors are professionally trained and certified. Available to all Baltimore City residents regardless of income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All Baltimore City residents regardless of income who seek professional financial guidance, counseling, credit repair assistance, and financial coaching.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counseling services support credit building and repair, debt management, banking access, savings goal planning, and legacy planning education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City residents only.
requirements_list: Baltimore City resident
No income requirement
No specific eligibility restrictions stated
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New clients complete an online referral form to make an appointment. Existing clients schedule appointments through the FEC portal using an email address. Alternatively, contact the Financial Empowerment Center directly by phone or visit the program website to access free counseling services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore City Housing Department LIGHT Program
structured_extraction.program_description: LIGHT (Baltimore City) helps residents get free or low-cost services to make their homes safer, healthier, and more comfortable. LIGHT Coordinators talk with residents to find out what they need and connect them with programs that can help, including home repairs, energy efficiency improvements, energy savings, high water bill remediation, and lead hazard removal. The program also assists with addressing high water bills and other housing-related problems through coordination with housing counselors and Community Action Centers.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: LIGHT Coordinators provide free assessment and coordination services to connect Baltimore City residents with home repair, energy efficiency, lead hazard reduction, and water bill assistance programs. Services include weatherization (attic insulation, air sealing, weather stripping, heating system maintenance, pipe wrapping, light bulbs), lead-based paint remediation for eligible homeowners and renters with pregnant women or children under 6 (door/window treatment, floor treatment, paint removal and stabilization, heating system maintenance), and housing rehabilitation repairs addressing emergencies, code violations, and health/safety issues (roof repair, water/sewer line repair, water heater replacement, electrical repair, accessibility modifications, plumbing repair). Some programs provide assistance as grants, while others offer forgivable loans (forgiven after 5 years if resident remains primary occupant) or deferred loans (due when property is sold, paid from sale proceeds). Services are free or low-cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents who need help making their homes safer, healthier, and more comfortable, including homeowners and renters with housing repair needs related to water bills, energy efficiency, lead hazards, accessibility, and emergency repairs. Priority consideration for households with pregnant women or children under age 6 for lead remediation services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free or low-cost services to improve home safety, health, and comfort including weatherization/energy efficiency improvements (attic insulation, air sealing, weather stripping, heating system maintenance, pipe wrapping, efficient light bulbs), lead hazard removal and remediation (particularly for homes with pregnant women or children under 6), home repairs addressing emergencies and code violations (roof repair, water/sewer line repair, water heater replacement, electrical repair, plumbing repair), disability accessibility modifications, and remediation of high water bills and other housing-related problems
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only
requirements_list: Household income limits based on family size (ranging from $66,300 for 1-person household to $124,950 for 8-person household, plus $13,450 for each additional person)
For lead remediation: home must be pre-1978 construction with chipping/peeling paint, AND pregnant woman or child under age 6 must be part of core household

For homeowners: deed must be in applicant's name (other deed holders may be present if they do not live in home), current on mortgage payments (if applicable), current on ground rent (if applicable), current on property taxes, have homeowner's insurance, no outstanding judgments, no bankruptcy in last 7 years, no active foreclosure efforts, no ownership of other properties
For renters: must have landlord contact information available
Homes must be occupied as primary residence at time of application
Some programs have waiting lists
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the LIGHT Intake & Assessment Unit to submit a pre-application: (1) Call (410) 396-3023, (2) Email dhcd.light@baltimorecity.gov, (3) Visit the online Application Portal at portal.neighborlysoftware.com/BALTIMOREMD/participant, or (4) Mail pre-application form to 417 East Fayette Street, Suite 1125, Baltimore, MD 21202. Alternatively, apply through a housing counselor or Community Action Center. The pre-application collects general information about household composition, income, property details, and repair concerns to determine which programs applicant may be eligible for. If potentially eligible for specific programs, LIGHT will request full application and supporting documents (photos, contractor estimates, violation notices, etc.). Full applications are submitted to individual programs for eligibility review. LIGHT Coordinators will conduct needs assessment and help coordinate with and connect residents to appropriate programs and services. Some programs have waiting lists.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that creates a coordinated apprenticeship pipeline connecting city agencies, contractors, and unions to provide career pathways and pre-apprenticeship training to young people.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program establishes a coordinated, citywide apprenticeship ecosystem under the Department of Human Resources. It connects city agencies, contractors, and unions into a single pipeline, aligns capital contracts with apprenticeship utilization goals, and creates clear entry points through pre-apprenticeship and training programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City young people seeking apprenticeship and career training opportunities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-apprenticeship training and apprenticeship placement
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only
requirements_list: Baltimore City resident
Interest in apprenticeship or career training
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals can access apprenticeship opportunities through the coordinated program under the Department of Human Resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: A mandate requiring businesses and contractors awarded city contracts to hire Baltimore City residents. The program provides free recruitment services, pre-screening, interview space, and tax credits to help employers meet a 51% local hiring goal for new hires on city-funded contracts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses awarded city contracts over $300,000 or participating in city-subsidized projects over $5,000,000 receive free recruitment services from MOED, including job posting for seven days, pre-screening of candidates, and interview space. Employers also receive tax credits. The primary obligation is to hire 51% Baltimore City residents for all new positions on the contract. An Employ Baltimore Executive Order applies to contracts between $50,000.01 and $300,000.00 with different requirements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - applies to all contracts awarded after 2018
structured_extraction.program_audience: Vendors, contractors, and subcontractors who are awarded city contracts worth more than $300,000 or participate in city-subsidized projects over $5,000,000. Businesses with collective bargaining agreements may request waivers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Businesses use the recruitment services and support to meet local hiring requirements on city-funded projects and contracts. Positions must be filled with Baltimore City residents at a 51% rate for new hires.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applies to all businesses with city contracts awarded by Baltimore City. The law applies to contracts awarded after 2018 and renewals or extensions of those contracts.
requirements_list: Meet with MOED within 2 weeks after contract award to complete an Employment Analysis
Complete employment analysis projecting workforce needs including total employees, workers required for the project, subcontractor workers, and recruitment needs
Post new jobs with MOED for a period of seven days only
Utilize MOED's recruitment services for new hires
Achieve a goal of 51% of all new hires being Baltimore City residents
Submit monthly employment reports with information on current workers, new workers, and Baltimore City residents working on the project

Add all new hires to vendor profile in B2Gnow system with required information including address, SSN (last four digits), position, referral source, education level, benefits offered, hours per week, and application date
Positions must be posted with MOED unless vendor has approved waiver (e.g., collective bargaining agreement positions)
Professional service contracts are not exempt from the law; only emergency service contracts and some contracts funded by federal grants are exempt
All positions necessary to complete the contract throughout its duration are applicable to the law
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: After a city contract is awarded, the contracting agency submits a Vendor Contact Form to MOED. MOED contacts the vendor and the Employment Analysis must be completed within two weeks of the contract award date. The vendor meets with MOED Employer Services staff to discuss staffing needs and learn about available free services. When hiring, the vendor sends job postings to MOED through the B2Gnow system, which pre-screens applicants and provides recruitment services. New hires must be added to the vendor profile with required information and assigned to contracts. The vendor then submits monthly employment reports (generated by the first business day of each month) showing compliance with local hiring requirements, including number of workers, Baltimore City residents hired, new hires, positions posted with MOED, and other employment data. Reports are not required after the contract end date.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides rental assistance and eviction prevention services to help residents pay rent and avoid losing their housing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Offers financial assistance with rent payments and eviction prevention services to help residents maintain stable housing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents who need help paying rent or preventing eviction.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rent payments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Housing & Community Development or visit the provided website to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City TB Program provides free tuberculosis services including case management, testing, treatment, and referrals for individuals with active TB disease, presumptive TB, or latent TB infection. The program offers nurse case management, expert medical TB management, TB medications, directly observed therapy, contact investigations, and referrals to outside services as needed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: All TB services are offered free of charge, including: nurse case management; expert medical TB management with lab work and imaging; TB medications for latent TB infection (9 months Isoniazid, 4 months Rifampin, or 12 weeks Isoniazid/Rifapentine); directly observed therapy for active TB; diagnostic testing including chest X-rays, sputum AFB smear, and sputum mycobacterial culture; skin tests (PPD) and QuantiFERON Plus testing; contact investigations; and referrals to outside services as needed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with active TB disease, presumptive TB, or latent TB infection, including those without insurance, recent immigrants, refugees, asylum seekers, and individuals experiencing barriers to TB care.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: TB consultation services, case management, diagnostic testing including chest X-rays and QuantiFERON Plus, TB medications for latent TB infection and active TB treatment (Isoniazid, Rifampin, Pyrazinamide, Ethambutol), directly observed therapy, contact investigations, and referrals to other services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Referral required for active TB disease (microbiologically or clinically confirmed). Microbiologic diagnosis required; cases must be discussed with TB clinician prior to referral if diagnosis not confirmed.
Referral required for presumptive TB (individuals being evaluated for active TB disease)

For latent TB infection: diagnosed LTBI without insurance, barriers to TB evaluation, high-risk status (HIV, immunocompromised, history of incarceration or homelessness, recent immigration from TB endemic country, or contact to active TB case), or inability to access LTBI services elsewhere
Clinical provider must be identified for future evaluation and care; patients with incomplete diagnostic evaluations will be returned
For active TB referrals, relevant radiology and lab reports and narrative notes should be submitted with referral form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the TB Referral Form (for active TB, presumptive TB, or latent TB cases). 2. Submit form by faxing to 410-396-9403 along with relevant radiology and lab reports and any narrative notes that would aid in evaluation. 3. Alternatively, complete the form electronically through the Qualtrics TB referral online portal. 4. For TB consultation services or to discuss cases with a TB clinician, call 410-396-9413 or 410-396-9414. 5. Appointments are required; walk-ins are not accepted. 6. Note: BCHD provides no responsibility for evaluation of fungal disease, malignancy, or conditions other than TB. Diagnostic testing at BCHD is limited to chest X-rays, sputum AFB smear, and sputum mycobacterial culture; other testing such as CT scans, bronchoscopy, or tissue biopsy should be completed before referral.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Water Access Program allows site stewards of community open space (both City and privately owned) in Baltimore City to access water for their sites during the growing season at a flat rate. The program supports community gardens and urban agriculture by providing subsidized water access from March 1st through November 1st each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: The BuyIntoBmore Fixed Pricing Program is a sales program for City-owned vacant buildings and lots in Baltimore City, administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). The program streamlines and simplifies property transfers at fixed prices to promote transparency in pricing and reduce the number of vacant properties. Priority is given to homeowners planning to live in properties as their primary residence, followed by community land trusts, nonprofits, and for-profit developers. Properties are priced based on property type and purchaser category, ranging from $1 to $3,000. The program aims to make property acquisition more accessible to eligible applicants and supports new construction, rehabilitation, green space conversion, and side yard development.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program facilitates the purchase of City-owned vacant buildings and lots at fixed prices. Homebuyers can purchase residential properties for $1 if they plan to live there as a primary residence and have $90,000 available for renovations. Community Land Trusts pay $1 for either property type (buildings or lots), provided they are registered Affordable Housing Land Trusts compliant with Maryland law. Nonprofits with 50 or fewer employees can purchase vacant buildings for $1,000 or vacant lots for $500. Larger nonprofits (51+ employees) and for-profit developers pay $3,000 for buildings or $1,000 for lots. All purchasers must obtain a use and occupancy permit within 12 months of settlement. Homeowners must maintain the property as their primary residence for a minimum of 5 years after permit issuance. If a property is sold within the 6-year period following settlement, homeowners must pay a pro-rated portion of $3,000 based on the year of sale. Properties assessed at less than the fixed price will be sold at assessed value. Properties assessed at $100,000 or more are subject to valuation review; if valued below $100,000, they remain eligible under fixed pricing; if valued at $100,000 or more, they are not eligible for fixed pricing. All properties must be developed for residential, residential mixed-use, or eligible green space (including side yards). Side yard properties can be sold in Housing Market Typology categories A-J if the applicant owns the adjacent property as their primary residence with confirmed use and occupancy. A maximum of 12 properties can be applied for at any given time. Applicants must pay a $100 application fee, which is credited to settlement if approved or refunded if rejected. All sales are subject to a Land Disposition Agreement and its compliance terms.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; Phase One priority period ended June 20, 2024 (originally April 1 - July 1, 2024 for homeowners). Applications now accepted on a rolling basis beginning July 1, 2024 for all applicant types.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents seeking to purchase and rehabilitate vacant City-owned properties as primary residences, community land trusts, non-profit organizations (including 501(c)(3) organizations), and for-profit developers interested in acquiring and restoring vacant properties in Baltimore City. Priority given to current Baltimore City residents planning to restore and reside in homes they purchase as their primary residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and renovation of vacant City-owned residential buildings and lots. Permitted uses include new construction, rehabilitation, green space conversion, and side yard development of vacant lots and buildings. For side yards, the applicant must own the adjacent property as their primary residence. Funds must be used for property acquisition and rehabilitation to bring properties to code. Applicants must demonstrate available funding of at least $90,000 per property for rehabilitation purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Properties must be located within Baltimore City's Housing Market Typology categories E-J, with the exception of side yard properties which can be located in categories A-J provided the applicant owns and resides in the adjacent property with confirmed use and occupancy. Properties are selected based on community-based block-level planning and whole-block redevelopment strategies. Not all properties in eligible typologies are available; selection is based on agency strategy work to achieve whole-block outcomes.
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner, nonprofit, community land trust, or for-profit developer
Homeowners must plan to restore and reside in the property as their primary residence to receive the $1 pricing tier
Proof of available funding of at least $90,000 to complete renovations per property applied for
No unpaid federal or state liens or court orders related to money owed to government
For homeowners: commitment to maintain property as primary residence for minimum 5 years after use and occupancy permit issuance
For nonprofits: must be 501(c)(3) organizations registered with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation

For Community Land Trusts: must be registered Affordable Housing Land Trusts with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation and in compliance with Maryland affordable housing land trust laws (Maryland Annotated Code Real Property Article 14-501 et seq.)
Use and occupancy permit must be obtained within 12 months from date of settlement
Application fee of $100 (credited to settlement if approved, refunded if rejected)
Property history review including vacant property status and prior rehabilitation work

If applicant owns vacant building inventory, Vacant Building Notice must be less than two years old; if older than two years, application may be rejected; if less than two years old, there must be active/open permits or application may be rejected
No open or pending criminal cases that might impede ability to complete the project
For applicable entities: must be in good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
For-profit developers must comply with project specifications

Maximum of 12 properties per application; applicants can apply for additional properties as they obtain use and occupancy permits on previously purchased properties, not to exceed 12 properties at any given time
Applicants should not submit multiple applications under different entities
If property is assessed for less than fixed price, property will be sold for assessed value
For homeowners who sell within the 6-year period (12 months to obtain permit + 5 years primary residence), a pro-rated portion of $3,000 must be paid based on year of sale

Properties assessed at $100,000 or more are subject to internal review and valuation; if true value is less than $100,000, property remains eligible; if true value is $100,000 or greater, property is not eligible for fixed pricing
For side yard applicants: must own adjacent property as owner-occupant; adjacent property must have valid use and occupancy permit
All purchasers must comply with Land Disposition Agreement terms and obtain proper permits within 90 days of conveyance
All purchasers must begin construction within 30 days of obtaining all required permits
Commercial liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence required prior to entering property
Homestead tax credit application and maintenance required for homeowner applicants during 5-year residency period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Buy Into Bmore interactive map portal at https://buyintobmore.baltimorecity.gov/. One user-friendly application form has been created for the purchase of both vacant buildings and vacant lots, used for all purchaser types (homeowners, nonprofits, and for-profit developers). DHCD reviews applications on a rolling basis and renders award or rejection decisions within two weeks of receipt. Applicants who do not pass vetting are given five business days to remedy issues. If multiple qualified applications are received for the same property, applications are reviewed in order of submission (first-come-first-served). Once an applicant successfully passes the vetting process, the property is awarded and removed from the BuyIntoBmore site. If unable to remedy vetting issues, the property is re-offered on the BuyIntoBmore site. Once approved, the sale is finalized through a formal Board of Estimates (BoE) approval process. DHCD maintains a standing, recurring item on the BoE agenda titled 'Fixed Pricing Policy Dispositions.' Once BoE approval is received, settlement must occur within 45 days. At time of award, the City abates all municipally imposed liens and charges within 10 days. Purchasers must then sign the Land Disposition Agreement, arrange title company/closing, and complete settlement. After settlement, purchasers have 12 months to obtain use and occupancy permits and complete all construction and rehabilitation work. DHCD monitors compliance throughout the contract period and can take action including property reacquisition or receivership if use and occupancy permit is not obtained within the contract period.
