structured_extraction.program_name: CFY 2027 Transportation Services Request for Proposals
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant opportunity for organizations to deliver free transportation services to individuals and families experiencing homelessness in Baltimore City. The transportation connects homeless individuals and families to shelters and other homeless services program locations within the Baltimore Continuum of Care, prioritizing assistance based on vulnerability and severity of service needs. The program covers both the winter shelter period (October 15th through March 31st) and non-winter shelter period (April 1st through October 14th). Providers must establish and maintain transportation vehicles that are wheelchair accessible, provide real-time communication systems for dispatch and drivers, maintain comprehensive records and data tracking systems, and ensure staff receive mandatory training including customer service, cultural competency, mental health first aid, trauma informed care, non-violent crisis intervention, CPR/First Aid, and critical incident reporting.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding awarded through a Request for Proposals process to provide free transportation services to individuals and families experiencing homelessness. Providers must operate wheelchair-accessible vehicles (minimum 2-3 vehicles during non-Code Blue weather, minimum 4 vehicles during Code Blue Extreme Cold Alerts with 2 replacement vehicles in each case) with regular operating hours of 5:45 am to 9:00 am and 4:00 pm to 7:00 pm seven days a week during non-winter season (April 1 to October 14), and 5:45 am to 10:00 pm and 4:00 pm to 11:00 pm seven days a week during winter season (October 15 to March 31). Transportation connects clients to designated shelter and homeless service program locations within the Baltimore Continuum of Care. Services must be provided free of charge and with a non-discrimination approach. Providers are responsible for all operational costs including vehicle procurement/leasing, fuel, maintenance, staff salaries and benefits, supplies, equipment, communications devices, training, insurance, and administrative costs (capped at 10% of total budget). Monthly reporting to MOHS includes financial expenditure reports, vehicle mileage and maintenance logs, and incident documentation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations and city agencies providing transportation or homeless services in Baltimore City, seeking to deliver free transportation services to individuals and families experiencing homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding is used to provide free transportation services to individuals and families experiencing homelessness to connect them to shelters and other homeless services program locations within the Baltimore Continuum of Care. Funds cover all operational costs including vehicle procurement/leasing, fuel, maintenance, personnel costs (salaries and fringe benefits), staff training, insurance, equipment, communications systems, supplies, and administrative costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services must be provided within Baltimore Continuum of Care areas in Baltimore City only. Required service locations include routine shelter pick-ups at Pinderhughes School (1200 N. Fremont St.), Manna House (435 E. 25th St.), WHRC (620 Fallsway), Sarah's Hope (1114 N. Mount Ave.), Monument St Shelter (4601 E. Monument St.), Project PLASE (3549 Old Frederick Rd.), My Sister's Place (17 W. Franklin Ave.), Beans and Bread (402 S Bond St.), and community pick-ups at Division of Vital Records (6764B Reisterstown Rd.), Birth and Death Records (4201 Patterson Ave.), DSS Broadway (200 North Broadway), DSS Penn (2500 Pennsylvania Ave.), DSS Biddle (2919 E Biddle St), and Social Security Office (1010 Park Ave.).
requirements_list: Must be a registered nonprofit 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization or another city agency
Must be in Good Standing with the State of Maryland
Must have two years of most recent independent audits (financial statements are not accepted)
Must agree to participate in Baltimore Continuum of Care (BCOC) meetings and be part of the collaborative body if granted an award
Must establish and enforce a code of conduct for transportation staff when interacting with clients
Must adhere to MOHS conduct policy regarding incidents on vehicles including altercations, injuries, illnesses, accidents, and vehicle damage
Must establish real-time communication systems (two-way radios or cell phones) between dispatchers and drivers
Must assist disabled clients with moving personal belongings during transportation
Must establish a data tracking system to track total number of riders by location daily, number of calls received, and maintain driver's logs
Must provide monthly reports to MOHS including financial expenditure reports, vehicle mileage and maintenance logs, and shuttle incidents
Must develop and maintain a financial tracking system that tracks expenditures by line item category including personnel, services, administrative fees, and operating costs
Must maintain all original invoices and receipts in a secure location

Must develop and maintain comprehensive records including signed agreements, RFP proposals, program budgets, personnel lists, job descriptions, organizational charts, financial reports, Certificate of Occupancy, business license, fiscal controls certification, lease agreements, insurance policies, and workplace policies
Must develop and submit standard operating procedures, policy documents, training plans, and monitoring plans subject to MOHS approval
Must develop and submit a vehicle maintenance plan including routine maintenance, minor repairs, major repairs, and fueling
Must adhere to all federal, State, and local regulations
Must conduct criminal background checks for all employees and maintain records for at least three years after employment termination
Must ensure transportation services comply with a schedule determined by MOHS and coordinate services during winter season under the Winter Shelter Plan
Must ensure scheduled and unscheduled transportation is accessible in accordance with federal, State, and local disability rules, laws, and regulations
Must provide all necessary supplies and equipment including 2-way radios, mobile devices, cell phone stipends for managers and family drivers, and cleaning products
Must store all data and reports electronically in an approved database system
Must utilize company owned and/or leased vehicles to perform transportation services
Must establish and maintain appropriate liability insurance limits as required by law
Must park and maintain all vehicles at its own facility

Must collaborate with MOHS in devising a training plan for transportation staff including customer service training, cultural competency and sensitivity training, mental health first aid training, trauma informed care training, non-violent crisis intervention training, CPR First Aid Bloodborne Pathogens Training, and Critical Incident Reporting
Must cooperate with MOHS and any successor Provider to enable smooth transition of property, equipment, activities, and records if award expires or is terminated

Must have a conflict of interest policy in place prohibiting employees, officers, agents, and volunteers from participating in decision-making regarding procurement if they have direct financial interest

If a primary religious organization, must provide services free from religious influences and cannot discriminate based on religion, require religious service attendance as condition of receiving shelter, or engage in religious proselytizing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit a proposal including the Shelter Transportation Application form and a Budget Proposal through the Request for Proposals process by the stated deadline of Friday, March 27, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. Proposals must address all components outlined in the Request for Proposals and provide comprehensive narratives on planned services, staffing, and organizational capacity. A separate application must be submitted for each service location or program being bid. Applicants must also complete a Conflict of Interest Questionnaire disclosing any conflicts with City employees, consultants, or City Council members. Proposals are reviewed by a committee comprised of MOHS staff, a Local Emergency Coordination (LEC) member, a Continuum of Care (CoC) Board Leadership member, and a Community Liaison member using a point system for scoring. MOHS has historically hosted a Pre-Bidder's presentation and facility tours to provide information about the application process and allow prospective providers to tour facilities. Successful applicants will be notified and enter into a formal Agreement with the City of Baltimore for grant award execution.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Casino Local Impact Funds Program distributes state gaming revenues to benefit communities surrounding Maryland casinos. In Baltimore, funds support infrastructure investments, facilities, public safety, sanitation, economic and community development including housing, and other public services and investments in the South Baltimore Gateway area centered on the Horseshoe Casino.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program allocates Casino Local Impact Grant funds annually through spending plans developed in consultation with the Local Development Council, City agencies, community partners, and neighborhood associations. Funds are distributed to support infrastructure investments, facilities, public safety, sanitation, economic and community development including housing, and other public services aligned with the nine South Baltimore Gateway Master Plan goals. Beginning in fiscal year 2018, at least 50% of local impact grants in Baltimore City are distributed directly to the South Baltimore Gateway Community Impact District Management Authority. Fund amounts vary annually based on video lottery terminal revenues, with distributions calculated as 82% to jurisdictions with video lottery facilities based on gross revenues, and a portion (18% for operations through fiscal year 2032) dedicated to Baltimore City for the South Baltimore Gateway area.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Communities and organizations in the South Baltimore Gateway area surrounding the Horseshoe Casino, including residents of immediate proximity communities, businesses, institutions, and nonprofit organizations serving the area
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure improvements, facilities, public safety, sanitation, economic and community development including housing, and other public services and improvements aligned with the South Baltimore Gateway Master Plan goals: Transportation Connectivity, Environmental Sustainability, Safety, Community Development and Revitalization, Economic Growth, Education, Health and Wellness, Quality of Life, and Infrastructure. Funds may support capital projects benefiting economic and community development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program serves the South Baltimore Gateway, a geographic area designated to benefit from this funding source and centered on the Horseshoe Casino. This includes communities in immediate proximity to the video lottery facility and any census blockgroup identified by Baltimore City as being located partly or entirely within 1 mile of the Horseshoe Casino. Local impact grants from video lottery facilities are used for improvements primarily in communities in immediate proximity to the facilities.
requirements_list: Multiyear expenditure plan must be developed by Baltimore City in consultation with the Local Development Council before any fund expenditure
Plan must be submitted to the Local Development Council for review and comment before adoption
Baltimore City must hold a public hearing on the plan for expenditure of allocated funds
Quarterly reports on fund distribution must be provided to the Legislative Policy Committee
Beginning in fiscal year 2018, at least 50% of local impact grants in Baltimore City must be distributed directly to the South Baltimore Gateway Community Impact District Management Authority
Funds must be used for improvements in communities in immediate proximity to the Horseshoe Casino video lottery facility
At least 75% of certain allocations must be consistent with the Park Heights Master Plan or adopted neighborhood priorities
Funds cannot be used for purposes outside those specified in State Government Article § 9-1A-31(b)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Casino Local Impact Funds Program does not involve a traditional application process by external parties. Instead, Baltimore City Department of Planning develops annual spending plans in consultation with the Local Development Council, which consists of community representatives, business leaders, legislators, and video lottery facility representatives. The Local Development Council advises the Mayor on priorities and community needs. Final funding decisions and allocations are determined through the City budget approval process by the Mayor and City Council. The South Baltimore Gateway Community Impact District Management Authority receives at least 50% of allocated funds directly beginning in fiscal year 2018. Community input is gathered through the Local Development Council consultation process and public hearings held by the City on proposed spending plans.
