structured_extraction.program_description: The program works to reduce lead poisoning in Baltimore City through primary prevention services, lead testing, home visits and case management, advocacy, and enforcement of the city's lead laws. It includes preventative home visits for low-income pregnant women and families with children under age 6, Healthy Homes Gatherings for community education, point-of-care blood lead testing, case management for families with lead-poisoned children, and legal enforcement against properties with lead violations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides primary prevention services including preventative home visits to assess lead hazards and provide referrals to legal and financial resources. Community health workers conduct these visits with low-income pregnant women and families with children under age 6. The program also offers Healthy Homes Gatherings for community education, point-of-care blood lead testing at health fairs and events, case management services for families with children who have elevated blood lead levels, education to healthcare providers, and enforcement action against properties with lead violations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children ages 1 to 6, particularly low-income families in neighborhoods with high lead poisoning rates, and pregnant women.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides home assessment services, referrals to legal and financial resources to address lead hazards, education, prevention supplies, blood lead testing, case management, and advocacy services to reduce childhood lead poisoning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program serves the City of Baltimore.
requirements_list: Families with children under age 6 or pregnant women
Low-income status for prevention home visit services
Children ages 1-2 must be tested for lead as mandated by state and Baltimore City Health Code
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families can contact the program directly or be referred through healthcare providers and partner organizations. For prevention services, community health workers identify and reach out to eligible families. For case management services, contact is initiated based on lab results from the Maryland Department of Health showing blood lead levels at or above 5 micrograms per deciliter. Families are offered telephonic or in-person education and case management services.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Baltimore Lead Hazard Reduction and Healthy Homes Program (EBL-targeted)
structured_extraction.program_description: A multi-year program providing comprehensive lead hazard control measures and healthy homes interventions to assist low to moderate income households with children under age six who have elevated blood lead levels and live in dwellings built before 1978 in Baltimore City. The program includes lead risk assessments, lead hazard reduction activities such as window replacement and paint stabilization, healthy homes assessments and interventions, outreach and education, and post-remediation home visits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $4,100,000 total HUD grant (MDLHD0608-25) consisting of $3,600,000 in Lead-Based Paint Hazard Control Grant funding and $500,000 in Healthy Homes Supplemental grant funding. The grant covers the period from April 1, 2026 to April 1, 2030 (48 months). Local match funds of $1,516,000 are also associated with the grant activities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 13, 2026 (for public comments on Environmental Review Record)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low to moderate income households in Baltimore City with children under age six who have elevated blood lead levels and reside in dwellings constructed prior to 1978
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead-based paint risk assessments, lead hazard reduction activities including window replacement and paint abatement, dust wipe clearance testing, healthy homes housing rating system assessments, healthy homes interventions, outreach and education sessions, home visits for post-remediation education, and lead education and guidance for families with elevated blood lead levels
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Baltimore, Maryland - specifically targeting dwellings constructed prior to 1978 where eligible households reside
requirements_list: Household income must be low to moderate
Must have children under age six
Children must have elevated blood lead levels (EBLL) of 5ug/dL and above
Dwelling must have been constructed prior to 1978
Must reside in the City of Baltimore
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The City of Baltimore will submit a request to HUD for the release of funds on or about April 14, 2026. Public comments on the Environmental Review Record may be submitted by April 13, 2026. The program implementation will occur from April 1, 2026 to April 1, 2030.

structured_extraction.program_description: A multi-agency workforce development and community cleanup initiative that hires under and unemployed residents to clean and maintain community spaces including vacant lots, alleys, sidewalks, and tree pits. The program provides holistic support including trauma-informed counseling, rental assistance, expungement services, GED programs, driver's license training, resume writing, interview coaching, and leadership training to help participants stabilize their lives and advance their careers.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Clean Corps hires under and unemployed residents and provides wages for cleanup and maintenance work. The program also offers workforce development support including trauma-informed counseling, rental assistance, expungement services, GED programs, certified driver's license training, resume writing, interview coaching, conflict resolution training, and leadership training.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maddy Silberger-Franek (East side neighborhoods); Lamar West (West and South neighborhoods)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Under and unemployed residents of Baltimore City, particularly those living in the 42 underinvested neighborhoods served by the program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment and wages for community cleanup and maintenance work; workforce development and support services including counseling, training, and assistance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program operates in 42 underinvested neighborhoods across Baltimore City
requirements_list: Must be an under or unemployed resident
Must live in or be served by one of the 42 targeted neighborhoods
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can contact Clean Corps directly through email or phone to inquire about employment and participation opportunities

structured_extraction.program_description: A 12-week, paid, in-person leadership course that helps residents and local leaders build skills in community development, violence prevention, environmental design, and neighborhood improvement to strengthen public safety and lead community revitalization in their neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive a 12-week paid in-person leadership course running from May 18, 2026 through August 7, 2026. The program includes hands-on training in community leadership and organizing, environmental design, public safety strategy, violence prevention, storytelling, grant writing, project planning, and data-informed problem solving. Participants also have the opportunity to design and implement grant-funded neighborhood improvement projects within their own communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Aspiring community leaders and small business owners in Baltimore's Northern District who are passionate about community change and committed to turning ideas into action.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants gain practical skills and hands-on experience in community leadership, environmental design, neighborhood improvement, public safety strategy, violence prevention, storytelling, grant writing, project planning, and data-informed problem solving. Participants design and implement grant-funded neighborhood improvement projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to Baltimore City's Northern District. Applicants must be located in the Northern District.
requirements_list: Located in Baltimore City's Northern District
Interested in community development, violence prevention, and neighborhood improvement
Ready to engage in a 12-week in-person course from May 18 through August 7, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants submit an online application through the provided form. The application deadline is May 3, 2026. Information sessions are available in-person on April 16, 2026 and virtually on April 29, 2026 to learn more about the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A funding opportunity providing operating funds through a Notice of Funding Availability. The Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development is making up to $1,020,000 in operating funds available to eligible applicants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $1,020,000 in operating funds available through a Notice of Funding Availability for eligible organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations eligible to receive operating funds from the city
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs for eligible organizations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit applications by April 24, 2026 through the Notice of Funding Availability process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A training program that educates volunteers on how to prepare for hazards and cope with emergencies. CERT courses and drills cover basic disaster prevention, preparation, and response skills, including fire safety, light search and rescue, team organization, communications, and emergency medical procedures. Members can volunteer with Baltimore City Office of Emergency Management to support outreach, emergency response, and recovery operations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-person CERT training courses covering disaster prevention, preparation, and response skills. Members meet quarterly throughout the year for trainings and informational sessions with in-person and hybrid meeting options. No financial assistance is provided; the program offers volunteer training and opportunities to support community emergency response and recovery operations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents and workers in Baltimore City who are at least 18 years old and want to learn emergency response skills and volunteer in their community.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable; this is a training program, not a financial assistance program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must live or work in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be at least 18 years of age
Must live or work in Baltimore City
Must register for a FEMA SID
Must complete an in-person CERT training course covering CERT and the Incident Command System (ICS) and Introduction to Community Emergency Response Team
Must support one OEM-sponsored preparedness and outreach event per year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for a FEMA SID through the DHS website. Enroll in and complete an in-person CERT training course. Attend quarterly trainings and informational sessions throughout the year. Support at least one OEM-sponsored preparedness and outreach event per year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Land Trust - Homeownership NOFA - Round 5
structured_extraction.program_description: The Affordable Housing Trust Fund provides grants to support homeownership projects sponsored by Community Land Trusts. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis through June 30, 2026 or until all funds are allocated.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $8,000,000 total funding available from Affordable Housing Trust Fund to support Community Land Trust homeownership projects. Qualified applicants can request up to $2,000,000 per project. Trust funds can be used to fund up to 50% of a project's Total Development Cost or a maximum of $2,000,000 per project, whichever is less. Maximum request per unit is $75,000 for households earning 50% AMI, adjusted for family size, and $120,000 for fewer than 10 units or $150,000 for 10+ units at 30% AMI, adjusted for family size. Up to 25% of total award can be used for predevelopment and/or acquisition costs (combined). Up to 10% of award can be used for operating costs directly related to project implementation including staff costs. Eligible uses include acquisition and stabilization of non-City owned properties, architectural and engineering, environmental assessment, market and financial feasibility analysis, construction, financing and lender fees, legal fees, consultant fees, project management staff, infrastructure, utilities, single family units, condos, co-operative buildings, demolition, and customary landscaping. Applications accepted on rolling basis through June 30, 2026 or until all funds allocated.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 30, 2026 or until all funds allocated (rolling basis); 90 days from application submission for notification of awards
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Land Trusts developing homeownership projects in Baltimore City for affordable housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support homeownership projects sponsored by Community Land Trusts for households at or below 50 percent of Area Median Income, with at least half serving households at or below 30 percent of Area Median Income. Eligible uses include acquisition and stabilization of non-City owned properties, architectural and engineering, environmental assessment and testing, market and financial feasibility analysis, construction, financing and lender fees, legal fees, consultant fees, project management staff, infrastructure and utilities, single family units, condos, co-operative buildings, demolition, and customary landscaping including parking, infrastructure and utilities. Mixed-use buildings that include ground floor retail are eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Community Land Trust
Projects must serve households at or below 50 percent of Area Median Income
At least half of units must serve households at or below 30 percent of Area Median Income
Request up to $2,000,000 per project
Registration as an Affordable Housing Land Trust with Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Compliance with State's Affordable Housing Land Trust Laws (Section 14 of Maryland Real Property Article)
By-Laws establishing terms for board of directors, officers, stewardship, conflicts of interest, ownership, open membership criteria, resale limitations and dissolution
Tri-partite board of directors (one-third community members, one-third land trust residents, one-third local stakeholders) or equivalent structure
Established Stewardship Standards including administrative manual and electronic information tracking system
Sample rental lease documentation
Site control at time of submission and title within 12 months of executing Funding Agreement
All units must restrict leasing and occupancy for at least 30 years to households at or below 50% AMI
Commitment to comply with City's MBE/WBE requirements (27% for minority-owned contractors, 10% for women-owned contractors)
Local Hiring Plan detailing community resident job access and recruitment of individuals with barriers to employment
Compliance with City Prevailing Wage Rates for construction contracts exceeding $5,000
Compliance with City Green Construction Law (Part XI of Baltimore City Building, Fire and Related Codes)
At least 5% of units must fully comply with UFAS requirements for persons with mobility impairments
At least 2% of units must fully comply with UFAS requirements for persons with hearing or vision impairments
Not more than 3 active existing construction/subsidy awards from Affordable Housing Trust Fund
Demonstration of capacity to complete and occupy projects within 2 years of executing Funding Agreement
All threshold requirements must be met including Authorization to Submit, Certification of Compliance, Owned Property Disclosure, and Financial and organizational disclosures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications available August 22, 2025. Pre-proposal conference scheduled for August 27, 2025 at 1:00 PM. Additional pre-proposal conference held December 10, 2025, 5:00 p.m. to 6:30 p.m. EST via Teams (Teams Meeting ID: 276 399 613 061 0, Passcode: ya3bc9KP, or dial +1 667-228-6519, Conference ID: 343 585 104#). Questions must be submitted electronically to DHCD.AHTFNOFA@baltimorecity.gov through December 12, 2025, with responses posted by December 22, 2025. Applications submitted via Neighborly Portal on rolling basis. Submission deadline January 9, 2026. DHCD will provide threshold review notification and post updated summary on website. Applications meeting all Threshold criteria will be scored and evaluated according to project feasibility (70 points maximum), community engagement and participation (25 points maximum), and achieving equity (25 points maximum), with up to 70 bonus points available. Minimum score of 105 out of 120 points required for consideration. Review and scoring conducted January 20 - March 17, 2026. Notification of awards expected week of April 13, 2026. Applications reviewed by interagency panel of City representatives with final discretion on funding decisions by Housing Commissioner. Final deadline June 30, 2026 or until all funds allocated.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Land Trusts - Homeownership & Rental NOFAs (2022)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development issued two Notices of Funding Availability for the Affordable Housing Trust Fund Community Land Trusts Program to support equitable community development and meet demand for affordable housing in historically disinvested communities. The program includes separate funding tracks for homeownership and rental projects sponsored by Community Land Trusts.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund to support Community Land Trust homeownership and rental projects. Rental track: up to $1.5 million total available; applicants can request up to $750,000 per project with awards ranging up to $750,000. Homeownership track: up to $4.0 million total available; applicants can request up to $1,000,000 per project. Both tracks require funds to serve households earning 50% or less of Area Median Income (AMI). Funds can cover up to 50% of Total Development Cost (TDC) for units at 50% AMI or up to 66% TDC for units at 30% AMI. Up to 25% of award can be advanced for predevelopment and acquisition costs combined; up to 20% can be used for operating costs directly related to project implementation. Eligible uses include acquisition, architectural/engineering, environmental assessment, market analysis, construction, carrying costs, financing fees, legal fees, consultant fees, landscaping, project management, and infrastructure/utilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Land Trusts sponsoring homeownership and rental housing projects in Baltimore City serving low- and very-low income households
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Homeownership and rental housing projects in historically disinvested communities. Eligible uses include: acquisition and stabilization of non-City-owned properties, architectural and engineering services, environmental assessment and testing, market and financial feasibility analysis, construction, carrying costs, financing and lender fees, legal fees for CLT-required documents, consultant fees, landscaping, project management staff, and infrastructure/utilities. For homeownership: single family homes, condos, and co-operative buildings. For rental: new construction and preservation of existing rental units. Ineligible uses: City-owned property acquisition, temporary/shelter housing, staff not directly related to projects, general organizational operating costs, relocation, loan repayment, community gardens/urban agriculture, religious projects, commercial/economic development, and NOFA submission preparation costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City, with focus on historically disinvested communities and areas consistent with community or neighborhood revitalization plans. Projects must demonstrate location in underserved communities.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Community Land Trust registered with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Compliance with State Affordable Housing Land Trust Laws (Annotated Code of Maryland Real Property Article, Section 14)
Organization must be managed by a nonprofit exempt from taxation under 501(c)(2), (3), or (4) of the Internal Revenue Code, or be a legally organized business entity managed by a nonprofit
By-laws establishing terms for board of directors, officers, stewardship, conflicts of interest, ownership, open membership criteria, resale limitations, and dissolution

Tri-partite board of directors comprised of one-third community members, one-third land trust residents (when available), and one-third local stakeholders and experts, or equivalent structure balancing community control with expertise

Established Stewardship Standards including administrative manual, electronic information tracking system, sales and loan closing procedures, maintenance and repair funds, and resale value documentation
Sample rental lease (for rental track) or warranty deed (for homeownership track)
Ground Lease protecting affordability based on National CLT 2011 Ground Lease model
Capacity to undertake and complete projects in no more than two (2) years from executing a Funding Agreement, including site control

Demonstrated site control at time of submission and title within 12 months of Funding Agreement execution (can include deed, executed contract, option to purchase, Land Disposition Agreement, Vacants to Value approval, Receivership/Tax Sale Foreclosure documentation, or other documentation deemed sufficient by DHCD)
Committed sources of funding from all participating funding sources (must submit commitment letters or letters of intent)
Established infrastructure to support tenants/residents and manage compliance and day-to-day management of units (rental) or post-purchase stewardship (homeownership)
Partnership with experienced developer (for rental track) with at least five (5) completed development projects
Memorandum of Understanding between developer and Community Land Trust
Experienced management team with documented experience managing similar properties (rental track)
IRS Determination Letter
Certification of Compliance
Owned Property Disclosure
Commitment to Comply certification
Local Hire Certification
Corporate Resolution and Board of Directors approval (nonprofit applicants)
Evidence of Good Standing with State of Maryland for all parties
List of Board of Directors with titles and affiliations (nonprofit applicants)
Organizational chart showing board structure, total seats, and roles/responsibilities of all partners

Most recent 990 Tax Return (nonprofit applicants) or financial statements based on annual budget: Audited Financial Statement if $500,000+; Certified accounting firm statement if $200,000-$500,000; Annual budget if less than $200,000
Site plans for new projects and remodels
Local Hiring Plan for projects with 15 or more units detailing community resident access to jobs, training for individuals with barriers to employment, and apprenticeship participation
Compliance with City Prevailing Wage Law for construction contracts over $5,000
Compliance with City Green Building Law
Affordable pricing methodology demonstrating how resale formula (homeownership) or rental formula (rental) keeps units affordable over time
Projects must meet all applicable Zoning and Development requirements with documentation of pre-development meeting with Department of Planning
For rental track: Experienced Development Team with sufficient capacity; for homeownership track: Experienced Development Team and demonstrated experience selling and managing CLT properties
Market analysis or feasibility study demonstrating housing needs and that project can meet City, State, and private lenders' underwriting criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications submitted electronically through Neighborly application portal only. Applicants submit: (1) one complete application using Application Checklist as table of contents with all attachments and Threshold Requirements in PDF format, and (2) one development budget as Excel spreadsheet. Applications due by 4:00 PM EST on 09/02/2022 (deadline now closed; applications accepted only during open periods). Pre-Proposal Conference held on 7/27/2022 (rental) and 7/28/2022 (homeownership) from 5:00-6:30 PM EST via video conference to review NOFA, application requirements, evaluation and award process, and answer questions. Written questions submitted by 7/29/2022 (rental) or 8/01/2022 (homeownership); answers posted on DHCD website by 8/15/2022. Threshold Review first determines organizational, financial, and compliance eligibility. Applications meeting Threshold criteria scored by interagency review panel on: Project Feasibility (70 points maximum), Community Engagement & Participation (40 points maximum), and Achieving Equity (15 points maximum), plus up to 20 bonus points. Minimum score of 102 out of 125 points required for consideration. Review panel submits recommendations to Deputy Commissioner for Development, then Housing Commissioner for final award determination. All awardees notified by phone and in writing. Non-awardees may request written 30-minute debriefing. Final list of reviewed applications, scores, rankings, and awards posted on DHCD website. Following award, DHCD conducts underwriting including appraisals, market feasibility studies, environmental assessments; DHCD takes security interest in project.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Land Trusts - Operating Costs NOFA (Affordable Housing Trust Fund)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development provides grants from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund to support Community Land Trust operating costs. These funds provide operational and capacity building support for Community Land Trust organizations that provide affordable housing to low and very low income households. Up to $500,000 is available, with applications accepted on a recurring basis through a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $500,000 available per NOFA cycle from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund to support Community Land Trust operating costs. Eligible applicants can request a maximum of $100,000 per Community Land Trust entity. Funds support operating, predevelopment, personnel, and capacity building costs directly related to Community Land Trust operations and projects creating affordable units for residents with area median income (AMI) of 50% and below. Eligible uses include: market and financial feasibility analysis, carrying costs, financing and lender fees, legal fees associated with closing and financing, project management staff, and general organizational operating costs such as rent, utilities, salaries, and operating supplies. Funds cannot be used for acquisition of City-owned properties, construction costs, relocation, loan repayment, community gardens, religious projects, commercial development, or NOFA submission preparation costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Submission deadline 10/06/2023 by 4:00 PM EST (for 2023 NOFA cycle); rolling application cycles occur periodically
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Land Trust organizations providing affordable housing to low and very low income households in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs, predevelopment costs, personnel costs, and capacity building support directly related to Community Land Trust operations. Eligible uses include market and financial feasibility analysis, carrying costs, financing and lender fees, legal fees for closing and financing, project management staff, and general organizational operating costs such as rent, utilities, salaries, and operating supplies for Community Land Trusts creating affordable units for residents at 50% AMI or below.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Community Land Trust entity organized or managed by a nonprofit exempt from taxation under IRC § 501(c)(2), (3), or (4)
Must be registered as an Affordable Housing Land Trust with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must comply with Section 14 of the Annotated Code of Maryland Real Property Article
Must have bylaws establishing board terms, officers, stewardship, conflicts of interest, ownership, open membership criteria, resale limitations, and dissolution provisions

Must have a tri-partite board of directors comprised of one-third community members, one-third land trust residents (when available), and one-third local stakeholders and experts, or equivalent structure
Must have been in operation as a land trust for a minimum of 2 years
Must show proof of 5 or more affordable units built and/or in process of being built under the land trust model for residents at 50% AMI or below
Must have active projects/activities/partnerships with DHCD in the past 24 months and/or provide essential statewide/regional advocacy in affordable housing or fair housing
Must be in good standing with DHCD with no outstanding fees, reports, or loan payments
Must have no unresolved compliance issues
Must not be on federal or state debarred list
Only one application per organization permitted
Request cannot exceed maximum of $100,000 per Community Land Trust entity
Must demonstrate organizational capacity to manage a Community Land Trust
Must demonstrate ability to leverage other sources of funds for operating costs
Must have established infrastructure to support employees and manage daily operations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted electronically through the Neighborly Portal. The process includes: (1) NOFA Guidelines and Application released on 8/29/2023; (2) Pre-Proposal Conference held 9/06/2023 from 2-3:30 PM EST to review requirements and answer questions; (3) Written questions accepted through 9/08/2023, with answers posted on DHCD website; (4) Submission deadline 10/06/2023 by 4:00 PM EST (late submissions not accepted); (5) Threshold Review by DHCD staff to determine eligibility; (6) Applications meeting threshold reviewed and ranked by AHTF staff; (7) Staff recommendations provided to Deputy Commissioner for Development, then to Housing Commissioner for final award determination; (8) Award notification by phone and in writing; (9) Awardees scheduled for underwriting meeting to review fund availability, security interest requirements, and draw-down procedures; (10) Funds available upon Board of Estimates approval of Funding Agreement; (11) Annual report due by December 30 summarizing fund use and outcomes. Applicants must submit one complete electronic PDF copy of application with all attachments and required documents, plus one Excel spreadsheet copy of operating budget.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Department of Transportation offers community groups the opportunity to create fun and creative projects in public spaces like streets, sidewalks, and alleys. These projects can improve neighborhood aesthetics, help slow down traffic, and provide more space for people to walk and gather. The community group pursuing the project must pay for it.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program facilitates community-led projects in public spaces through design approval and permitting. Communities design and fund their own projects. The program provides approval processes, technical guidance, and facilitation. Project types include: Paint in the Right-of-Way (artistic painting on streets, sidewalks, alleys), Landscape Plantings (trees, flowers, plants), Planters and Barriers (for traffic calming), Signage (community name signs, historic site signs, educational signs), Parklets (small public spaces in parking spots), and Special Projects (plazas, public art, creative lighting). For parklets and special projects, organizations must provide commercial liability insurance of $1 million per occurrence and $2 million in aggregate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community groups, neighborhood associations, local businesses, nonprofits, school parent groups, and any organization interested in creating placemaking projects in Baltimore City public spaces.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds may be used for community-led placemaking projects including artistic painting, landscape plantings, planters and barriers, signage, parklets (small public spaces in parking spots), and special projects such as plazas, public art installations, and creative lighting in public spaces like streets, sidewalks, and alleys.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Baltimore City public spaces maintained by the Department of Transportation, including streets, sidewalks, and alleys.
requirements_list: Design rendering required
Project location(s) must be specified
Materials to be used must be listed

Letters of support or signed petitions from adjacent occupants: for parklets and mid-block projects, petition must include 60% of block occupants; for intersections, petition must include 60% of occupants of three properties in each direction
Proof of property owner support from properties directly abutting the project
Proof that organization is in good standing with the State of Maryland
Commercial liability insurance of $1 million per occurrence and $2 million in aggregate required for parklets and special projects
Maintenance plan for the project required
Paint must be pre-approved by DOT for Paint in the Right-of-Way projects
For landscape plantings, must contact Miss Utility before digging to ensure underground pipes or wires are not damaged
All designs subject to DOT approval
Projects cannot contain obscene, vulgar, or violent messages
Projects cannot block walkways or violate Americans with Disabilities Act requirements
Projects cannot introduce roadway safety hazards or block sight distance
Projects cannot require unreasonable maintenance from DOT
Projects cannot cause damage to DOT assets or public utilities
Projects cannot include harmful or poisonous plants
Paint designs cannot incorporate words or political messages
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Community groups submit project designs and documents through the Community Based Programs Application portal. The application must include design rendering, project location, materials list, letters of support from adjacent occupants, property owner support, proof of good standing with Maryland, liability insurance (for parklets and special projects), and maintenance plan. For projects that include new traffic calming elements, communities can either submit a traffic calming request to 311 for DOT approval or hire a contractor to install traffic calming elements (with DOT approval of engineering drawings and installation details) prior to submitting the Community-Led Placemaking Application. Once approved, the community group receives a written agreement outlining what has been approved, project timeline, maintenance responsibilities, and any special rules.

structured_extraction.program_name: Complementary CBO Project - Caregiver Services Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program funding community-based organizations to support caregiver-related programs including respite care, support groups, and resources for aging adults or veterans. The goal is to increase awareness and access to services for family caregivers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $10,000 grants awarded to community-based organizations to support caregiver services programs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Call for proposals launches in early March
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations serving family caregivers, aging adults, disabled individuals, and veterans in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Respite care, support groups, resources, and programs for aging adults, disabled individuals, and veterans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Must be a community-based organization
Program must relate to caregiver services
Program may include respite care, support groups, and resources for aging adults or veterans
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call for proposals will be launched in early March 2026. Community-based organizations submit proposals for caregiver-related programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: An annual competitive grant opportunity administered by the Mayor's Office of Homeless Services (MOHS) in Baltimore City that provides funding to qualified non-profit organizations and local government agencies to support efforts to end homelessness and serve vulnerable populations. The program awards funding to organizations providing services to individuals and families who are at-risk of homelessness, currently homeless, low-income and living with HIV or AIDS, or at risk of crises including those with behavioral health needs. Organizations submit one application and can be considered for multiple eligible funding sources simultaneously. The CFA has been offered annually for fiscal years 2021 through 2027, with funding sourced from federal, state, and local streams including HUD Emergency Solutions Grant (ESG), HUD Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS/HIV (HOPWA), State of Maryland Homeless Solutions Program (HSP), Baltimore City Department of Social Services (DSS), Maryland Department of Health State Special Funds (SSF), Baltimore City General Funds, and the Baltimore City Opioid Restitution Fund.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants funded through multiple sources including: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development Emergency Solutions Grant (ESG), State of Maryland Homeless Solutions Program (HSP), Baltimore City Department of Social Services (DSS), U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS/HIV (HOPWA), Maryland Department of Health State Special Funds (SSF), Baltimore City General Funds, and Baltimore City Opioid Restitution Fund. Awards cover a 12-month performance period (July 1 through June 30 of the funded fiscal year). Programs submit one application and may be considered for multiple eligible funding sources. The most recent cycle (FY 2026) had a performance period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026. The FY 2027 cycle has a deadline of March 20, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, March 20, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. (FY 2027 cycle); prior cycles: FY 2026 deadline was March 21, 2025 at 5:00 p.m. EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified non-profit organizations and local government agencies providing services to individuals and families who are at-risk of homelessness, currently homeless, low-income and living with HIV or AIDS, or at risk of crises including those with behavioral health needs in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services for individuals and families at-risk of homelessness, currently homeless, low-income and living with HIV or AIDS, or at risk of crises including those with behavioral health needs. Eligible project types include: emergency shelter, drop-in and day center services, transitional housing, street outreach, comprehensive street outreach, rapid re-housing, permanent supportive housing, housing stabilization and homelessness prevention, eviction prevention, housing and services for people with HIV/AIDS, and coordinated entry systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified non-profit organization or local government agency

Must provide services to eligible populations: individuals and families at-risk of homelessness, currently homeless, low-income with HIV/AIDS, or at risk of crises including those with behavioral health needs
Both new and renewal project proposals are eligible
Application must be submitted electronically via the Neighborly portal (recent cycles) or by email to HSPApplications@baltimorecity.gov (earlier cycles)
An authorized individual at the agency must upload and certify all application materials
Two points of contact must be added to Neighborly account (FY 2026+)
Budget workbook appropriate to service category must be included
Submit by stated deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should obtain the Request for Proposals and review all guidance materials. For recent cycles (FY 2026+), applicants create an account in the Neighborly portal well before the deadline and review all application questions listed there. An authorized individual at the agency completes all application materials, uploads them to Neighborly, and certifies and submits the application; the system sends an automated confirmation upon receipt. For earlier cycles, completed new or renewal project application templates and appropriate budget workbooks were submitted via email to HSPApplications@baltimorecity.gov. A Bidder's Conference (webinar) is held prior to each deadline to assist applicants. Applications are reviewed for threshold/eligibility and evaluated by panel. Conditional awards are announced approximately one month after the deadline, followed by contract development, with contracts beginning July 1 of the funded fiscal year, subject to grant fund availability and approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Continuum of Care (CoC) Builds Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal funding opportunity to address homelessness by adding new permanent supportive housing units through new construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation. The program provides one-time awards to qualified collaborative applicants to develop housing with integrated supportive services and property management for individuals and families experiencing homelessness where at least one household member has a disability.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $175 million in total federal funding is available through this NOFO to support new permanent supportive housing units. Of this total, approximately $110 million is reserved for Continuum of Care coalitions in states with populations exceeding 2.5 million people, which includes the Baltimore City Continuum of Care (MD-501). Approximately $65 million is available for CoCs in states with populations fewer than 2.5 million. Funding supports property acquisition, new construction, rehabilitation, and integrated supportive services and property management. Awards range from $1,000,000 to $10,000,000 per project. Applicants may request up to 20% of total funds for project-based rental assistance, operating costs, or supportive services. Up to 10% of the total budget may be used for project administrative costs. All funded projects must provide a 25% match of the awarded grant amount (excluding leasing funds) with cash or in-kind resources. Grant terms may be two, three, four, or five years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, October 18, 2024 at 3:00 pm EST (HUD submission deadline: November 21, 2024 at 11:59 pm)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Homeless Services (MOHS)
structured_extraction.program_audience: CoC-designated Collaborative Applicants (one applicant per CoC only) including developers, property managers, and service providers able to work together to create permanent supportive housing with integrated services for individuals and families experiencing homelessness where at least one household member has a disability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To develop new permanent supportive housing units through new construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation; to provide supportive services (such as case management, life skills, health care, mental health services, substance use treatment, employment assistance, legal services, and other eligible services per 24 CFR 578.53); to provide property management services; and to cover operating costs (maintenance, repairs, property tax, insurance, utilities, security, furniture, equipment) and project administration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City Continuum of Care (MD-501). HUD will review CoCBuilds project applications only from the CoC-designated Collaborative Applicant. Each CoC may submit only one CoCBuilds application.
requirements_list: CoC-designated Collaborative Applicant status required from HUD
Only one CoCBuilds application permitted per CoC
Must include a developer, property manager, and service provider through either memoranda of understanding (MOUs) between organizations or within a single organization
Proposals must address creation of new permanent supportive housing units
Must demonstrate capacity to provide both supportive services and property management
Project must serve individuals and families experiencing homelessness where at least one household member has a disability
Must demonstrate experience managing at least four properties similar to the proposed project
Must provide proof of site control prior to execution of grant agreement
Must complete environmental review before awarded funds can be drawn
Must meet timeliness standards outlined in 24 CFR 578.85 for new construction and rehabilitation projects
Projects must be ready for occupancy within 36 months of award
Must leverage non-CoC funded housing resources for at least 50% of the amount requested OR provide subsidies for at least 25% of proposed units
Must demonstrate coordination with healthcare organizations, housing providers, and social service providers
Must use CoC's coordinated entry process for referring individuals and families to units
Must provide 25% match of awarded grant amount (excluding leasing funds) with cash or in-kind resources
Must comply with Section 3 of the Housing and Urban Development Act of 1968 for employment and training opportunities
Maximum 20% of award may be used for non-capital costs (rental assistance, operating costs, supportive services)
Maximum 10% of award may be used for project administrative costs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit written proposals in response to the RFP released August 30, 2024. A Technical Assistance Bidder's Conference was held September 12, 2024. Questions could be submitted by September 20, 2024, with RFP Q&A Addendum released September 27, 2024. Proposals are due October 18, 2024 by 3:00 pm EST via email to BaltimorePSH@lesardevelopment.com in PDF format with all required supporting documents. All forms and application documents must be submitted via Grants.gov (additional details provided via MOHS website). Internal review and scoring occurs October 21-25, 2024. Review, scoring, and recommendations by the Resource Allocation Committee (RAC) occur October 28 - November 4, 2024. Selection panel discussion and interviews occur October 28 - November 1, 2024. The CoC Board approves recommendations November 1-4, 2024. Final award notices are issued November 11-15, 2024. MOHS then submits the selected application to HUD via grants.gov by November 18, 2024, with the HUD deadline of November 21, 2024 at 11:59 pm.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Continuum of Care (CoC) Program is a federal competitive grant program administered by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) that promotes community-wide commitment to ending homelessness. It provides annual funding to nonprofit providers and state and local governments to quickly rehouse homeless individuals and families while minimizing trauma and dislocation, promote access to mainstream programs, and optimize self-sufficiency among people experiencing homelessness. The program aims to make homelessness rare and brief, establish coordinated entry systems, advance racial equity, and apply a Housing First approach. In Baltimore City, more than 75% of CoC funding supports Permanent Supportive Housing programs that combine long-term housing subsidies with supportive services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive federal grant funding awarded annually through a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) process. In Baltimore City, over 75% of CoC funding supports Permanent Supportive Housing programs that combine long-term housing subsidies with supportive services. Funds can be used for permanent housing, supportive services only, and HMIS (Homeless Management Information System). Local areas typically have 60 to 75 days to apply once HUD announces the NOFA. Renewal, new, expansion, and YHDP renewal/replacement project applications are reviewed by a Resource Allocation Committee and approved by the CoC Board before submission to HUD.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies annually; typically 60 to 75 days after HUD announces the nationwide competition. For FY 2022: August 19, 2022 at 5:00 pm (renewal applications); August 29, 2022 at 5:00 pm (new, YHDP renewal/replacement, and expansion applications).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit providers and state and local government agencies working to end homelessness, including those providing permanent housing, supportive services, and homeless management information systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permanent housing, supportive services, Homeless Management Information System (HMIS), efforts to quickly rehouse homeless individuals and families, access to mainstream programs, and promoting self-sufficiency among people experiencing homelessness.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City participates in the nationwide CoC program; funded projects serve Baltimore City residents.
requirements_list: Eligible applicants must be nonprofit providers or state and local governments
Programs must use a Housing First approach to help people get housing quickly
Programs must use a Coordinated Entry system that is easy to access, fair to everyone, and lets people choose the help that works best for them
Programs must treat everyone fairly and equally and recognize and fix racial inequalities
Programs must use data and proven methods to determine which programs work best and spend money wisely
Programs must help people connect to public benefits and work with employers to create job opportunities
Make homelessness rare and short by responding in a clear and organized way
Applicants must submit all required materials including supporting documentation and match documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: HUD announces funding availability through a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA). Baltimore City holds a local competition to select renewal, new, expansion, and YHDP renewal/replacement project applications that match HUD funding priorities and community needs. Applicants submit applications by the specified deadlines via email to HSP Applications (HSPApplications@baltimorecity.gov) with all required supporting documentation and match documentation. The Resource Allocation Committee reviews applications and the CoC Board approves final rankings before submitting the consolidated application to HUD.

structured_extraction.program_name: Coordinated Access Navigator Sites / Coordinated Access System
structured_extraction.program_description: Coordinated Access Navigators are trained to help individuals and families currently experiencing homelessness in Baltimore City gather information needed to complete housing applications and determine eligibility for housing programs. Multiple organizations serve different populations including people experiencing homelessness generally, homeless youth, people with HIV/AIDS, and veterans. Navigators connect clients with appropriate resources and housing assistance through the Coordinated Access System.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Trained Coordinated Access Navigators help individuals and families experiencing homelessness gather necessary information for housing applications, assess eligibility for housing programs, and connect them with appropriate resources and housing assistance. Multiple partner organizations serve different populations: People Encouraging People (anyone experiencing homelessness), Springboard Community Services (primarily youth ages 18-24), MOHS HOPWA Program (people with HIV/AIDS), New Vision House of Hope (veterans), and The Baltimore Station (veterans).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families currently experiencing homelessness in Baltimore City, including general population, youth ages 18-24, people with HIV/AIDS, and veterans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assessment and navigation services to determine housing program eligibility, housing application assistance, and connection to appropriate housing resources and support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City; services provided through multiple partner organizations at various locations throughout the city.
requirements_list: Currently experiencing homelessness
Must be experiencing homelessness
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call one of the Coordinated Access Navigator Sites to schedule an appointment or visit walk-in locations for assistance. Organizations serve different populations: People Encouraging People (anyone experiencing homelessness), Springboard Community Services (primarily youth ages 18-24), MOHS HOPWA Program (people with HIV/AIDS), New Vision House of Hope (veterans), or The Baltimore Station (veterans). Contact a Coordinated Access Navigator for further assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that reduces economic damage to Baltimore City and its businesses following a major emergency or catastrophic event by allowing pre-credentialed critical business employees rapid access to their facilities through a secure identification card recognized by the Baltimore Police Department. This helps businesses quickly assess damage, maintain IT systems, meet regulatory obligations, and secure vital records and data.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Pre-event credentialing program that issues secure identification cards to critical business employees, allowing them to access restricted areas and their work sites following a declared disaster or serious emergency.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore-based businesses of all types and sizes that employ critical personnel needing access to facilities during emergencies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to business facilities and work sites to assess damage, maintain core IT systems, meet regulatory obligations, and secure or remove vital records and data following a major emergency or catastrophic event.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Employees must be designated as critical business personnel
Must obtain pre-event credentialing before a disaster occurs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses should visit www.ceas.com to learn more about the credentialing process and enroll critical employees in the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Baltimore provides capital support to cultural organizations for eligible capital improvements to their facilities through General Obligation bonds awarded every two years. The program aims to support organizations that promote arts and culture in Baltimore City and contribute to the City's unique identity.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: General Obligation bonds are awarded to support capital improvements at cultural institutions. A total of $1 million per fiscal year is available for FY 2026 and FY 2027. Individual awards will not exceed $200,000 over two years. Typical awards range between $50,000 to $100,000 over a two-year period. Funds are provided on a reimbursement basis. FY 2026 funds become available July 1, 2025, and FY 2027 funds become available July 1, 2026. Expenses cannot be incurred until after final approval of the budget by City Council.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered non-profit museums, galleries, theaters, and other arts and cultural venues within designated arts and entertainment districts in Baltimore City that promote arts and culture and contribute to the City's unique identity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements to cultural facilities including physical betterments and improvements such as building systems (roof, HVAC, windows, etc.), interior and exterior renovations, fire protection systems, ADA accessibility improvements, plaza or entrance upgrades for accessibility, elevator replacements, museum or exhibit expansions, and equipment needed in connection with such improvements. Minimum project cost is $50,000 and projects should have a minimum 15-year service life.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must have a physical location in Baltimore City. Cultural venues located within designated arts and entertainment districts (see Maryland State Arts Council website to search by address) are eligible to apply.
requirements_list: Must be a registered non-profit in good standing with the State Department of Assessment and Taxation
Must have a physical location in Baltimore City
Must either own the facility or have a minimum fifteen-year lease with primary responsibility for capital improvements
Facility must be open to the general public
Project cost must be at least $50,000
Projects should have a minimum 15-year service life
Projects cannot be repair or maintenance in nature costing less than $100,000 or of an emergency nature
Cannot include vehicular equipment or salaries except those properly capitalized as part of project cost
Cannot include operating support, relocation, or repayment of existing loans or liens
Cannot include projects that support specific religious or other affiliations, or that support political actions, causes, advocacy, or parties
Requests should not exceed $200,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted by April 30, 2025. Information sessions are held on March 6, 2025 at 10:00 am and March 18, 2025 at 2:00 pm via WebEx to explain the program. The Department of Planning conducts an inter-agency review of applications in May 2025. Organizations are notified of awards on June 23, 2025. Awards are contingent on approval of the FY 2026 and FY 2027 capital budgets by City Council. If awarded, grant agreements must be signed by the grantee, Department of Planning, and Law Department and approved by the Board of Estimates. Funds are provided on a reimbursement basis, with invoices submitted to the Department of Planning and processed by the Department of Finance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Customized Training is a business-driven, employer-focused training strategy that helps job seekers with little or no skills in a specific industry gain occupational skills tailored to employer needs. MOED reimburses businesses up to 50 percent of training costs for training new employees in hard-to-fill or newly created positions. The program benefits both employers seeking skilled workers and job seekers looking to enter a specific industry.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MOED reimburses businesses up to 50 percent of training costs, which may include wages, tools, uniforms, and training courses. Businesses must commit to hiring trainees who successfully complete the program. Training positions must be full-time permanent positions with wages of $10 per hour or higher. Training can be provided by the employer or through WIOA Eligible Training Providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers in all industries looking to train new employees for hard-to-fill or newly created positions, and job seekers with little or no skills in a specific industry seeking employment
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training costs including wages, tools, uniforms, and training courses for new employees in hard-to-fill or newly created positions, as well as job training tailored to specific industry needs for job seekers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Training positions must be full-time permanent positions
Wages must be $10 per hour or higher
Businesses must commit to hiring trainees who successfully complete training
Training can be provided by the employer or through WIOA Eligible Training Providers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers complete the Customized Training/OJT Business Application. MOED provides marketing, recruitment, and pre-screening of applicants through career center services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Department of Housing and Community Development Weatherization Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development offers weatherization and energy efficiency services to help low-income households reduce energy expenses and stay warm during extreme cold weather. The program performs a full energy assessment and installs energy-conservation materials, products, and measures in residents' homes to lower utility bills and improve overall energy efficiency.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant-funded assistance and subsidy providing a full energy usage assessment and installation of energy-conservation materials, products, and measures in eligible residents' homes to reduce energy expenses and lower utility bills. Assistance may be provided as a grant or as a forgivable or deferred loan. A forgivable loan is forgiven after five years if you live in your home as your primary residence during that time. A deferred loan is due back to the City when you sell your home and is paid from the profit of the sale.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income homeowners and renters in Baltimore City with incomes at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Level seeking to reduce energy expenses and improve home energy efficiency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy conservation materials and products including weatherization repairs and energy-efficiency improvements to homes to reduce utility bills. May address energy efficiency, HVAC, electrical, plumbing, roof, water line, sewer line, lead paint hazard reduction, disability accessibility modifications, and other home repair concerns.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City residents with incomes at or below 200 percent of the Federal Poverty Level.
requirements_list: Income at or below 200% of Federal Poverty Level
Owner of a home or renter receiving reduced rent through HUD or subsidized housing
Property deed in applicant's name (for homeowners)
Current on mortgage payments if applicable (for homeowners)
Current on ground rent payments if applicable (for homeowners)
Current on property taxes (for homeowners)
No outstanding judgments against household members
No bankruptcy declared by household members in the last seven years
No foreclosure efforts on property
Homeowner's insurance required (for homeowners)
Home built before 1978 may require lead-based paint assessment if chipping and peeling paint present or pregnant women or children under age 6 reside in home
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a pre-application form either online at https://portal.neighborlysoftware.com/BALTIMOREMD/participant or by mail to LIGHT Intake and Assessment Unit, 417 East Fayette Street, Suite 1125, Baltimore, MD 21202. The pre-application will be used to determine which home repair programs you may be eligible for. If eligible for a particular program, applicants will be requested to submit a full application with supporting documents. The program will then review and determine final eligibility. Some programs have waiting lists. Applicants may be asked if they are open to considering forgivable or deferred loans if grants are not available. Contact the Department of Housing and Community Development at (410) 396-3023 or dhcd.light@baltimorecity.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program created to help people and organizations fix up vacant homes. The program gives money to groups, non-profits, and homeowners who are making major repairs to empty houses, including those with a Vacant Building Notice. Homes must be in special areas of the city where the program focuses on improving neighborhoods.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides money to help pay for the full cost of fixing up vacant homes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People, organizations, non-profits, and homeowners in Baltimore City working to repair vacant homes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Major repairs and rehabilitation of vacant homes, including those with Vacant Building Notices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Special focus areas within Baltimore City where the program concentrates on improving neighborhoods.
requirements_list: Home must be vacant
Located in designated program focus areas

structured_extraction.program_description: The fund provides grants to Baltimore-based nonprofit organizations working in close partnership with communities to address the digital divide through education, outreach, planning, and implementation activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three types of grants are available: Education and Outreach grants ($5,000–$10,000) to fund community-based activities raising awareness of the digital divide and supporting programming to address it; Planning grants (up to $50,000) to support development of neighborhood digital inclusion plans; and Implementation grants (up to $75,000) to support communities in putting digital inclusion plans into action.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore-based nonprofit organizations working in close partnership with communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based activities to raise awareness of the digital divide, support programming to address the digital divide, build capacity, develop neighborhood digital inclusion plans, and implement digital inclusion plans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization based in Baltimore
Must work in close partnership with communities

structured_extraction.program_description: Digital Learning Labs offer computer courseware covering Microsoft application software tutorials as well as IC3 courseware and certification. The IC3 certification provides an internationally recognized credential that increases a job seeker's technical knowledge and skills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Digital Learning Labs provide free or subsidized access to computer courseware including Microsoft applications tutorials and IC3 certification courses to help job seekers gain technical skills and internationally recognized credentials.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers seeking to develop computer and technical skills
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Computer skills training and IC3 certification

structured_extraction.program_description: An emergency response fund established by the Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs and the Baltimore Civic Fund to provide direct monetary support to families who lost loved ones in the Key Bridge collapse, as well as families of survivors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct monetary support to families of victims and survivors of the Key Bridge collapse. Funding is disbursed to families in conjunction with case management efforts to alleviate financial burden and provide resources as they work through the situation. To date, the fund has raised more than $450,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families of victims and survivors of the Key Bridge collapse
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct financial support to alleviate burden and provide resources to families
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City and surrounding region
requirements_list: Lost a loved one or family member in the Key Bridge collapse
OR are a family of a survivor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Baltimore Civic Fund through http://www.baltimorecivicfund.org/key-bridge-response-fund

structured_extraction.program_description: A joint program between the Maryland Department of Health and the Baltimore City Fire Department that enables first responders to leave naloxone with patients and their support systems during overdose-related 911 calls in Baltimore City. The program ensures life-saving resources are available whether or not the patient goes to the hospital, distributing naloxone at no cost to those most likely to need it in emergencies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: First responders distribute naloxone directly to patients and their support systems during overdose-related 911 emergency calls at no cost to the recipient, leaving the medication with them whether or not the patient is transported to the hospital.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents experiencing opioid overdose and their support systems who contact 911 for emergency services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Naloxone distributed by first responders for immediate overdose reversal and left behind for future emergency use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only, available through 911 emergency response.
requirements_list: Receives naloxone during overdose-related 911 call response
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Naloxone is automatically offered and left with patients and their support systems by first responders during overdose-related 911 calls; no separate application is required.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that provides funding to operate emergency homeless shelter sites offering dignified residential settings and services to help people experiencing homelessness transition back to housing stability within Baltimore City's Continuum of Care. The program funds three separate shelter sites: one for single men and women, one for single women and families, and one for families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding to operate three emergency homeless shelter sites within Baltimore City for fiscal year 2021 (July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021): (1) Single Men/Single Women at 620 Fallsway (175 single adult male beds, 75 single adult female beds, plus 15 overflow beds each); (2) Single Women/Families at 1200 N. Fremont Avenue (70 single adult female beds, 8 family beds, plus 60 female/50 male/40 family overflow beds); (3) Families at privately-owned location to be determined (150 family beds). Funding comes from a combination of federal sources (HUD Emergency Solutions Grant), state sources (Maryland State Homelessness Solutions Program, Department of Social Services Shelter Program), and local General Fund appropriations. Awards are based on applicant's proposed service model, budget, fidelity to best practices, and organizational capacity. Applicants must provide a minimum 10% match through cash, in-kind services, or donated materials. Provider will be reimbursed monthly for expenses.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Wade Carver, Angela D. McCauley, Jay Wilson
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations and Baltimore City agencies operating or seeking to operate emergency homeless shelter services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating emergency homeless shelter sites that provide residential settings and supportive services to help people experiencing homelessness transition to housing stability. Permitted uses include day-to-day shelter operations (maintenance, certified food services, janitorial services, shelter monitoring), case management, complaint response and monitoring, data collection and entry, linkage to community support services, and other supportive services consistent with Housing First principles and trauma-informed care practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Three specific shelter sites: 620 Fallsway (single men and women), 1200 N. Fremont Avenue (single women and families), and a privately-owned site to be determined (families). Provider must maintain an office within Baltimore City of sufficient size to support management of homeless services network and provide space for staff trainings, meetings, and files.
requirements_list: Be a registered 501(c)(3) non-stock non-profit organization with the State of Maryland and the United States Internal Revenue Service (IRS), or be another City agency
Certify good standing with the State of Maryland
Submit two years of most recent independent audits (A-133 or independent financial audit; financial statements alone not accepted)
Agree to participate in Baltimore Continuum of Care meetings and maintain active, up-to-date membership, regular attendance, and participation in at least one Continuum committee or workgroup
Submit Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws
Submit current Certificate of Good Standing from State of Maryland
Submit Federal Tax Exemption Determination Letter
Submit List of Board of Directors
Submit Project Organizational Chart with name, title, email, and phone for each staff position
Submit Match and Leveraging Documents
Provide minimum 10% match through cash, in-kind services, or donated materials

Carry or be willing to obtain Professional Liability/Errors and Omissions Insurance (minimum $3 million), Worker's Compensation Coverage, General Commercial Liability Insurance (minimum $3 million), Business Automobile Liability Insurance (minimum $1 million), Fidelity Coverage, and Cyber Liability Insurance (minimum $1 million)
Implement criminal and financial background checks for all new hires and current employees
Ensure all staff have tuberculosis testing
Develop code of conduct policy approved by MOHS
If applicable, designate at least one staff member as McKinney-Vento liaison for educational rights of homeless students
Designate at least one staff member as equity liaison trained in cultural responsiveness
Ensure case management services available in clients' foreign languages without service interruption
Comply with Local Hiring requirements if contract exceeds $300,000 (51% of new hires must be Baltimore City residents); comply with Employ Baltimore if contract between $50,001-$300,001
Submit staffing plan to MOHS within 30 days of award
Submit training plan within 30 days of award describing trainings to be provided, schedule, and providers
Submit recordkeeping system within 30 days of award complying with OMB Super Circular A200
Operate according to Housing First Principles
Provide trauma-informed, professional service delivery
Maintain zero discrimination on basis of religion in employment and service provision if organization is primarily religious in nature
Report unusual incidents to MOHS within 2 hours or next business day
Report incidents resulting in bodily injury or substantial property damage within 24 hours
Report deaths or missing children under 18 to police and City within 2 hours, provide police report copy within 30 days
Submit monthly summary reports with client numbers and services provided
Report client grievances within 24 hours of submission
Submit final annual report within 30 days of performance period end
Provide monthly employment reports if Local Hiring requirements apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit a complete proposal in PDF format to mohs.hsp.application@baltimorecity.gov by the deadline. Submissions must include: (1) Emergency Homeless Shelter Grant Application form; (2) Comprehensive Project Budget using provided template; (3) Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws; (4) Current Certificate of Good Standing from State of Maryland; (5) Federal Tax Exemption Determination Letter; (6) List of Board of Directors; (7) Project Organizational Chart with staff names, titles, emails, and phones; (8) Match and Leveraging Documents; and (9) Most recent A-133 or independent financial audit. Applicants may apply for one, a combination of, or all three shelter projects (each considered separately). A pre-proposal conference was held March 24, 2020. Facility tours were offered April 1-2, 2020. Questions submitted by April 1, 2020 deadline were addressed in published FAQs. Late or hand-delivered submissions are not accepted. MOHS reviewed proposals July 13-31, 2020 and announced award recipients August 7, 2020. The review committee scores proposals based on service model quality, budget feasibility, fidelity to best practices, and organizational capacity. The City reserves the right to change scope of services, service quantity, and requirements during the agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program assists Baltimore City homeowners and renters whose homes are facing foreclosure or eviction due to economic hardship. Funding allocation includes: $10.7 million for rapid rehousing and homelessness prevention services; remaining funds support emergency shelter operations, street outreach services, data management systems, and program administration and oversight. Funding is distributed to pre-selected nonprofit providers serving Baltimore City residents experiencing or at risk of homelessness.
