structured_extraction.program_name: Expedited Reimbursement Program for Sewage Backups
structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides reimbursement to Baltimore City residential property owners and tenants for reasonable, documented cleanup, disinfection, and disposal services costs resulting from sewage backups caused by capacity-related wet weather events in the sanitary sewer collection system. The program is established under the Modified Consent Decree and reimburses up to $5,000 per dwelling unit per event. Sewage backup events prior to April 6, 2018 are not eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimburses up to $5,000 per dwelling unit, per event for reasonable, documented cleanup, disinfection, and disposal services costs resulting from sewage backups caused by capacity-related wet weather events (at least 1/4 inch of precipitation within 24 hours causing sewer lines to surcharge or overflow). Insurance deductibles paid are also eligible if demonstrably linked to cleanup and disinfection costs. Reimbursement eligibility is based on requirements set forth in Appendix E of the Modified Consent Decree. Final determinations are issued within 60 days of receiving all necessary information and documentation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be received within 90 days after the backup.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residential customers (homeowners or tenants) whose properties have experienced sewage backups caused by capacity-related wet weather events in the sanitary sewer collection system.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cleanup, disinfection, and disposal services costs related to sewage backups, including any insurance deductible paid if demonstrably linked to cleanup and disinfection.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City residential properties only. Sewage backup events prior to April 6, 2018 are not eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City residential customer (homeowner or tenant)
Sewage backup must be caused by a capacity-related wet weather event (at least 1/4 inch of precipitation within 24 hours causing sewer lines to surcharge or overflow)
Applications must be received within 90 days after the backup

If property is insured against backups, must receive final determination from insurance company before the application can be processed; insurance company documentation may be provided up to 30 days after receipt from the insurer
All documentation from the insurance company must be included with the application, including proof of any insurance deductible paid
Documentation of all cleanup, disinfection and disposal expenses required
If tenant, must provide signed lease
If filing on behalf of owner or tenant, must include written proof of power of attorney
Backup must be the result of surcharging in the collection system caused by wet weather events
Reimbursement is per dwelling unit, per occurrence
Sewage backup must originate from Baltimore's sanitary sewer collection system (not from private laterals or property-owned systems)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the program website or submit a completed application by email, certified U.S. Mail, or commercial delivery to the Baltimore City Department of Public Works, Bureau of Water and Wastewater. Residents can call 410-396-3500 to have an application mailed or to inquire about the program. Applications must be filed within 90 days of the sewage backup incident. If insured, applicants must obtain a final written determination from their insurance company and include all documentation with the application (insurance documentation may be provided up to 30 days after receipt from the insurer). Submit all required documentation with the application. The program processes applications within 60 days of receiving all necessary information and documentation. If the application is eligible with all qualifying expenses documented, the applicant receives a Release for Signature. The signed release must be returned before a check is processed.

Projects must meet HUD Continuum of Care program requirements

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 2022 CoC Unsheltered Special NOFO Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal funding opportunity from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) that supports communities in implementing coordinated approaches to reduce unsheltered homelessness and improve services, health outcomes, and housing stability among vulnerable unsheltered individuals and families. The program promotes Housing First and public health principles, encouraging partnerships between health and housing agencies to leverage mainstream resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HUD awards federal grant funding to eligible communities through a competitive application process. Nonprofit service providers and state and local governments can apply for funding to quickly rehouse homeless individuals and families, provide supportive services, minimize trauma and dislocation caused by homelessness, promote access to mainstream housing and healthcare programs, and optimize self-sufficiency. Funding supports coordinated entry systems, rapid rehousing programs, permanent supportive housing, transitional housing with services, and prevention/diversion programs. Projects must align with Housing First principles and emphasize partnerships between health and housing agencies to leverage existing mainstream resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit service providers, state agencies, and local government agencies within the Baltimore City Continuum of Care seeking to reduce unsheltered homelessness and improve housing stability for vulnerable individuals and families. Primary focus on organizations already engaged in homeless services or housing provision.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports efforts to quickly rehouse homeless individuals and families, minimize trauma and dislocation caused by homelessness, promote access to mainstream programs and services, optimize self-sufficiency among people experiencing homelessness, implement coordinated entry systems, provide rapid rehousing assistance, support permanent supportive housing and transitional housing with services, and fund prevention and diversion programs. Resources can support salaries for case managers, housing search assistance, security deposits, rental assistance, utility payments, and other supportive services aligned with Housing First principles.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City and the Baltimore City Continuum of Care (CoC) area, which includes Baltimore City and surrounding jurisdictions participating in the coordinated regional homeless response system.
requirements_list: Applicants must be nonprofit providers, state agencies, or local government agencies registered and in good standing
Organizations must demonstrate experience in homeless services or housing provision
Projects must partner with both health and housing agencies to coordinate services
All projects must adopt Housing First principles and prioritize rapid rehousing
Projects should leverage and coordinate with mainstream housing, healthcare, and social service resources
Organizations must participate in the Continuum of Care coordinated entry system
Applications must include all required materials and supporting documentation as specified in the RFP Guidelines
Match documentation and funding commitment letters must be submitted with application
Organizations must comply with HUD regulations and requirements for grant recipients
Ability to execute project activities according to HUD timelines and requirements
Organizations should demonstrate capacity to serve vulnerable populations experiencing homelessness
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The FY 2022 CoC Unsheltered Special NOFO competition follows a structured local selection process. First, eligible applicants must attend a Bidder's Conference held by the Baltimore City Homeless Services Program to receive detailed information about program requirements, submission procedures, and scoring criteria. Organizations then submit complete project applications by the deadline including the new project application forms, consolidated application components, program narratives, budgets, organizational documentation, and evidence of health/housing partnerships. Submitted applications are reviewed and scored by the Resource Allocation Committee using established evaluation criteria assessing project feasibility, organizational capacity, Housing First alignment, and potential impact. The Resource Allocation Committee ranks all projects and selects those recommended for inclusion in Baltimore City's Continuum of Care application to HUD. HUD then conducts federal review of the consolidated CoC application. Applicants are notified in writing of acceptance or rejection of their projects. Selected projects are incorporated into the city's final CoC application submitted to HUD for federal funding decisions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program administered by Baltimore City's Mayor's Office of Homeless Services that provides funding to qualified organizations offering services to individuals and families who are at-risk of homelessness, currently homeless, or living with HIV or AIDS. Organizations submit one application and can be considered for multiple eligible funding sources. The program covers service categories including emergency shelter, transitional housing, housing and services for people with HIV/AIDS, housing stabilization and homelessness prevention, rapid re-housing, street outreach, and permanent supportive housing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants drawn from six funding sources: (1) U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development Emergency Solutions Grant (ESG) - approximately $1,895,820 available; (2) State of Maryland Homeless Solutions Program (HSP) - approximately $3,297,802 available; (3) Baltimore City Department of Social Services (DSS) - approximately $314,128 available; (4) U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS/HIV (HOPWA) - approximately $7,238,355 available; (5) Maryland Department of Health State Special Funds (SSF) - approximately $690,249 available; and (6) Baltimore City General Funds - approximately $9,000,000 available. Grant term runs July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025. Programs may receive funding for emergency shelter, transitional housing, housing stabilization, homelessness prevention, rapid re-housing, street outreach, and permanent supportive housing. Exact funding amounts are estimates only and subject to availability. MOHS will assign the most appropriate funding source to each approved project according to the project's proposed activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified non-profit organizations providing services to individuals and families who are: (1) at-risk of homelessness, (2) currently homeless, and/or (3) low-income and living with HIV or AIDS.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services for individuals and families who are at-risk of homelessness, currently homeless, or living with HIV or AIDS. Eligible activities and costs include: street outreach (engagement, case management, emergency services, transportation); emergency shelter (operations, essential services, food, transportation, vouchers); rapid re-housing (housing identification, rental and financial assistance, case management); housing stabilization and homelessness prevention (time-limited assistance, relocation services); housing and services for people with HIV/AIDS (short-term rent/mortgage/utility assistance, support services, permanent housing placement); and support services for permanent supportive housing (case management linking residents to supportive services, job training, health care, budgeting, treatment).

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 2025 Continuum of Care (CoC) NOFO Program Competition
structured_extraction.program_description: The Continuum of Care program promotes a community-wide commitment to ending homelessness. It provides funding to nonprofit providers and state and local governments to quickly rehouse individuals and families experiencing homelessness while minimizing the impacts of trauma and dislocation. The program also promotes self-sufficiency and access to mainstream programs by individuals and families experiencing homelessness. The FY 2025 competition includes significant changes from prior years, including new HUD policy priorities focused on ending street homelessness, prioritizing treatment and recovery, advancing public safety, promoting self-sufficiency, improving outcomes, and minimizing trauma.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive funding is provided to nonprofit providers and state and local governments to support rapid rehousing, transitional housing, permanent supportive housing, and supportive services only projects for individuals and families experiencing homelessness. FY 2025 available funding totals approximately $42.8 million, including: $31.8 million in Annual Renewal Demand (ARD) for renewal projects; $6.4 million in CoC Bonus Project funding; $3.1 million in Domestic Violence Bonus Project funding; and $1.5 million for CoC Planning Grants. The program accepts both new and renewal project proposals through a competitive application process. Permanent housing projects (PSH, RRH, Joint TH-RRH) are capped at 30% of ARD ($9.5 million). Tier 1 projects are capped at 30% of ARD. New Transitional Housing projects and Supportive Services Only projects are strongly encouraged. All applications must be submitted through the Neighborly portal and are evaluated by the Resource Allocation Committee and CoC Board according to HUD scoring and ranking methodology.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit providers and state and local governments seeking to provide homelessness services and housing support in Baltimore City. Applicants must have authorized individuals who can certify and submit applications through the Neighborly portal.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports rapid rehousing of individuals and families experiencing homelessness, trauma-informed services, self-sufficiency programs, access to mainstream support programs, permanent supportive housing for elderly individuals and those with disabilities, transitional housing with 40 hours per week of supportive services, and supportive services only projects including street outreach, coordinated entry, and standalone services. All or majority of projects must require participation in supportive services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City

Must submit complete application materials via Neighborly portal by December 12, 2025 at 5:00 pm EST

Add two points of contact for organization

Projects must not operate drug injection sites, distribute drug paraphernalia, or permit illicit drug use or distribution

Transitional housing providers must provide minimum 40 hours per week of supportive services
All or majority of projects must require program participants to participate in supportive services per formal lease agreement or supportive service agreement
Project applicants must be able to begin assistance within 12 months of conditional award (24 months for sponsor-based and project-based rental assistance)
Projects must demonstrate matching funds requirement (25 percent of awarded grant amount minus leasing funds)
Renewal PSH projects will be prioritized; RRH and TH-RRH projects very unlikely to receive funding
Renewal Joint TH-RRH projects must include alternative funding source to support RRH program
New applications for PSH and RRH only considered for CoC Bonus and DV Bonus funds (extremely competitive)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants create an account and log into the Neighborly portal to submit applications. The application release date was November 19, 2025. A Bidder's Conference was held on November 21, 2025 from 11:00 am to 12:30 pm EST (webinar recorded and shared). FAQs from the Bidder's Conference were posted on November 28, 2025. An authorized individual at the applicant organization uploads all completed application materials including supporting documentation to Neighborly once ready for submission. The authorized individual certifies and submits the application by the December 12, 2025 deadline at 5:00 pm EST. Neighborly sends an automated message confirming receipt of submission. On December 14, 2025, the Resource Allocation Committee receives an overview of renewal project performance data and overview of new project applications that have passed threshold. On December 17, 2025, the RAC meets to review renewal project applications and scores and to discuss new projects being considered. On December 23, 2025, final project ranking is sent to the CoC Board for review and posted via Member365, with notification to applicants of project ranking at least 15 days prior to HUD application submission. Applications are reviewed by the Resource Allocation Committee and CoC Board according to scoring and ranking methodology established in the competition guidelines. The CoC application is posted for public comment on January 8, 2026, and the final consolidated CoC application is submitted to HUD on January 13, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps eligible first-time homebuyers purchase homes in Baltimore City by providing financial assistance to reduce down payments, lower loan balances, and buy down interest rates.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible first-time homebuyers at or below 80% of the area median income can receive up to 50% of their down payment as a grant, GAP funding (calculated as the difference between 30% of annual household income and the annual mortgage payment), up to 2.5% of the sales price for interest rate buydown or other incentives, and up to 50% of closing costs covered. An additional $5,000 bonus is available in certain circumstances. Funds are provided as grants that do not need to be repaid if the homeowner stays in the home for five years. Funds are available on a first-come, first-served basis. For FY25, household income limits range from $72,950 for a 1-person household to $137,550 for an 8-person household (80% of Area Median Income). Example: A household earning $85,000 annually with a $1,800 monthly mortgage payment and $10,000 in closing costs may receive approximately $10,125 in total incentives. Note: Buyers cannot receive cash at the settlement table and funds cannot be used to pay realtor fees.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Funding is planned each year based on the City's fiscal calendar (July 1 to June 30). Incentives are given out on a first-come, first-served basis. New incentives are available until funding has been exhausted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers in Baltimore City who are at or below 80% of the area median income and interested in purchasing a home.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The assistance can be used to reduce down payment requirements, reduce loan balances, lower interest rates on mortgages, and cover up to 50% of closing costs. Funds cannot be used to pay realtor fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: This program is available to homebuyers purchasing property in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be a first-time homebuyer

Household income must be at or below 80% of the area median income (FY25 limits: 1 person $72,950; 2 persons $83,400; 3 persons $93,800; 4 persons $104,200; 5 persons $112,550; 6 persons $120,900; 7 persons $129,250; 8 persons $137,550)
Must complete a homeownership class from a City-approved homeownership counseling agency within one year before attempting to buy
Must contribute at least $1,000 of your own money towards the house
Settlement date must be at least 30 days after submitting application
Cannot receive 2.5% interest rate buydown if receiving funds from the Maryland Mortgage Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register your account and submit an application through the Applicant Portal at https://portal.neighborlysoftware.com/baltimoremd/Participant. To register: Click the Register link and create a username (email address) and password. The system will send a validation email; check spam/bulk mail if not received within 2 minutes. Once registered, log in with your email and password. Your housing counselor and lender must complete the online application. Provide the Title Company's Employer Identification Number (EIN) in section H (Closing Information) of the application. Allow at least 30 days between application submission and settlement date for processing. Checks typically take 10 to 15 business days to be sent after approval. Use the FTHIP Incentives Calculator at https://cityservices.baltimorecity.gov/fthip to estimate your benefit by entering applicant name, household annual income, loan amount, monthly mortgage payment, and down payment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A workforce development and training center that prepares Baltimore City residents for careers in the automotive and fleet industries. Participants gain hands-on experience and classroom instruction in preventive maintenance, diagnostics, welding, fabrication, CDL prep, safety, hybrid and diesel technology, and workplace readiness. The program serves high school students, recent graduates, career changers, and young adults looking to enter skilled trades.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive hands-on training and classroom instruction in automotive repair, welding, CDL preparation, and related skilled trades. The program runs Monday through Friday from 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM for approximately six months (July 2026 through January 2027) at 4910 Park Heights Avenue.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students in automotive programs, recent high school graduates, young adults ages 18-24 looking to enter the workforce, career changers, individuals interested in skilled trades, and young people not currently in school or employment who would benefit from structure and skill-building.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides training in preventive maintenance and diagnostics, welding and fabrication, CDL prep and safety, hybrid and diesel technology, professionalism and workplace readiness.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Applicants must be Baltimore City residents.
requirements_list: Be between 18 and 24 years old at time of application
Be a Baltimore City resident
Demonstrate interest in automotive technology or mechanical trades
Be currently enrolled in a high school or GED program OR be a recent high school graduate
Submit academic records (latest report card or transcript)
Submit recommendation letter from a teacher, mentor, or employer
Submit personal statement or interest essay
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a completed application with academic records, a recommendation letter, and a personal statement. The application window for the third cohort opened March 1, 2026 and closed March 31, 2026. Decision letters are issued April 27 through May 1, 2026. Classes begin July 7, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Flexible Fund for Diversion and Rapid Resolution
structured_extraction.program_description: A program funded through the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) that provides flexible funding to help prevent homelessness and rapidly resolve housing crises for people at risk of or experiencing homelessness in Baltimore City. The program supports both diversion services (helping people avoid entering shelter) and rapid resolution assistance (quickly resolving housing crises). $2.3 million was committed through the Mayor's Office of Homeless Services, with community listening sessions held to gather feedback on implementation. As of May 31, 2024, all funding has been used and the program is no longer accepting applications.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $2.3 million committed to provide flexible funding for diversion services (helping people avoid entering shelter) and rapid resolution assistance (quickly resolving housing crises). Financial assistance covers housing-related expenses to prevent homelessness. As of May 31, 2024, all funding has been used and the program is no longer accepting applications.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: As of May 31, 2024, all funding has been used and the program is no longer accepting applications
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Flexible emergency assistance with housing-related expenses to prevent homelessness or rapidly resolve housing crises, including diversion services and rapid resolution support
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: At risk of homelessness
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Program launched in 2023 through the Mayor's Office of Homeless Services. As of May 31, 2024, all funding has been used and the program is no longer accepting applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Baltimore issues General Obligation Bonds (GO Bonds) every two years to fund capital projects. These borrowed funds support housing and neighborhood revitalization, school renovations and improvements, economic development, park and recreation center improvements, and key city institutions and cultural attractions. The bonds are backed by the city's full faith and credit and taxing authority.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: GO Bonds are borrowed funds issued by the City of Baltimore to finance capital projects. The city must obtain voter approval through a ballot referendum every two years to issue these bonds. The bonds are repaid over time using the city's taxing authority. The 2024 loan authorization approved up to $250 million total over fiscal years 2026 and 2027, allocated across four categories: Affordable Housing (up to $20 million), Schools (up to $55 million), Community and Economic Development (up to $50 million), and Public Infrastructure (up to $125 million).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: November 2024 ballot (2024 authorization for fiscal years 2026-2027); next round begins fall 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Baltimore government for funding capital improvement projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for capital projects including: housing acquisition, preservation, production, demolition and rental assistance; school renovations and improvements; community and economic development including neighborhood revitalization and blight elimination; and public infrastructure improvements to parks, recreation centers, libraries, streets, bridges, courthouses, police stations, fire stations, and information technology systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only
requirements_list: Projects must be capital improvement projects
Voter approval through ballot referendum required
Affordable Housing funds limited to housing-related activities
Schools funds for systemic improvements and school building renovations
Community and Economic Development funds for neighborhood revitalization and private investment incentives
Public Infrastructure funds for government facilities and infrastructure
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The process begins with the Planning Commission in the fall prior to a general election year. After Planning Commission approval, the bond issue categories are approved by the Board of Finance, Board of Estimates, City Delegation to the Maryland General Assembly, and City Council before being placed on the general election ballot for voter approval. Specific projects funded by the bonds are determined through the regular annual capital improvement program planning process.

structured_extraction.program_name: HOPWA-CV (Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS - Coronavirus)

Provides short-term rent, mortgage, and utility assistance to prevent homelessness, supportive services including food and medications, hotel or motel leasing for isolation and quarantine, and administrative oversight.

Funds are allocated by jurisdiction with Baltimore City receiving the largest portion.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll County, and Queen Anne's County in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be HOPWA eligible (person with AIDS or family member)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit written comments regarding proposed activities to Lakeysha Vaughn, Program Compliance Supervisor at the Mayor's Office of Homeless Services by the deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Hardship Exemption and Alternative Compliance Program for Tax-Exempt Organizations
structured_extraction.program_description: A program allowing eligible tax-exempt organizations in Baltimore City to apply for an exemption or reduction from stormwater fees by submitting an alternative compliance plan that outlines stormwater runoff and pollution reduction practices. The program provides flexibility to protect the environment and reduce burden on the City's municipal separate storm sewer system while alleviating financial hardship for qualifying organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible tax-exempt organizations receive an exemption from or reduction of their stormwater fee by implementing an approved alternative compliance plan that demonstrates how they will reduce stormwater runoff and pollution. Organizations may reduce their annual stormwater fee or receive a full exemption upon approval of their alternative compliance plan. The fee reduction or exemption remains active as long as the organization maintains its tax-exempt status, continues to document implementation of the approved alternative compliance plan, and meets all eligibility requirements through annual recertification.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling; applications accepted year-round. Organizations must recertify eligibility annually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tax-exempt charitable and nonprofit organizations in Baltimore City experiencing financial hardship due to stormwater remediation fees
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption or reduction of stormwater fees for organizations implementing environmental protection and stormwater reduction practices as outlined in an alternative compliance plan, including pollution prevention measures, stormwater management best practices, and activities that reduce demand on the City's drainage system.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only
requirements_list: Organization must be tax-exempt under IRS Section 501(c)(3) or (d)
Total annual stormwater remediation fee must exceed 0.75% of total annual revenue (including any discounts or credits previously received)
Total annual revenue must not exceed $1,000,000
Organization must own the property or provide a copy of current landlord/tenant lease agreement showing responsibility for stormwater remediation fee charges
Organization must submit a written alternative compliance plan to the Department for review and approval
Organization must initiate implementation of the approved alternative compliance plan within one year of receiving approval
Organization must recertify eligibility on an annual basis and document implementation of the approved alternative compliance plan
Failure to recertify or document implementation results in removal from the hardship exemption program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible organizations must download and complete the Hardship Exemption and Alternative Compliance Program Plan form, which requires documentation of tax-exempt status, financial hardship, property ownership or lease agreement, and a detailed alternative compliance plan. The form and required supporting materials should be submitted to the Bureau of Water and Wastewater at 200 Holliday Street, Room 404, Baltimore, MD 21202, or via email to publicworks@baltimorecity.gov (with 'STORMWATER CREDIT APPLICATION' in the subject line). Applications are reviewed within 30 days of receipt of a complete application package. Upon approval, the organization must begin implementing the alternative compliance plan within one year. Annual recertification is required, with renewal applications due at least 30 days before the end of the credit period. Organizations must maintain proper documentation of their approved alternative compliance plan implementation to retain exemption status.

structured_extraction.program_name: Hardship Water Bill Discount / Hardship Exemption Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Exempts eligible low-income Baltimore City residents from paying the Chesapeake Bay Restoration Fee and the Stormwater Remediation Fee on their water and sewer bills. The program is designed to assist homeowners and tenants who meet income or assistance-based eligibility criteria, and the exemption must be renewed annually.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible applicants are exempted from paying the Chesapeake Bay Restoration Fee and the Stormwater Remediation Fee on their water and sewer bills. The exemption must be reapplied for annually to maintain the benefit. Applicants must meet at least two of the following conditions: (A) Receiving energy assistance subsidy; (B) Receiving public assistance - Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or food stamps and medical assistance; (C) Receiving veterans, social security or social security disability benefits; or (D) Meeting gross income criteria based on household size (current year standards apply, adjusted annually per U.S. Poverty Guidelines).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual application required; no specific deadline stated - applications accepted on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.contact_name: Baltimore City Department of Public Works, Bureau of Water and Wastewater, Customer Support and Services Division
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City homeowners and tenants who receive water and sewer bills directly from the city and meet income or assistance-based eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program exempts qualified applicants from two specific utility fees on their water and sewer bills: the Chesapeake Bay Restoration Fee and the Stormwater Remediation Fee.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Applicants must be City of Baltimore residents who receive water and sewer bills directly from the city.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Baltimore City resident receiving water and sewer bill directly from the city
Applicant must be property owner-of-record with Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation or provide lease showing responsibility for paying water and sewer charges

Applicant must meet at least two of the following: receives energy assistance subsidy, receives Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or food stamps and medical assistance, receives public assistance, receives veterans benefits or social security or social security disability benefits, or meets gross income criteria (current income limits apply based on household size, adjusted annually per U.S. Poverty Guidelines)
For income verification: acceptable documents include pay stub, 1099, pension statement, income tax return, or letter from social security
Must provide proof of identification and proof of residency
Renters must provide copy of landlord/tenant lease agreement indicating tenant responsibility for water/sewer charges
Must provide copy of most recent water/sewer bill
The exemption is only valid for one year and applicants must reapply annually to maintain the benefit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download the application form from the website at https://www.baltimorecity.gov/publicworks/hardship-exemption-program or request it by phone at 410-396-5398, or obtain it at a Baltimore City Community Action Partnership Center. 2. Complete the front and back of the application form with all required information including all household members and income sources. 3. Gather required supporting documents: proof of identification and proof of residency, copy of most recent water/sewer bill, verification of any assistance being received (energy assistance, SSI, food stamps, medical assistance, veterans or social security disability benefits, or proof of household gross income), and for renters, a copy of the lease agreement indicating responsibility for water/sewer charges. 4. Submit the completed application and supporting documents by mail to Baltimore City Department of Public Works, Bureau of Water and Wastewater, Customer Support and Services Division, 200 Holliday Street, Room 404, Baltimore, Maryland 21202; or by email to dpw.billing@baltimorecity.gov; or bring in person to 200 Holliday Street, 4th floor, Baltimore, MD 21202. 5. Applications must be submitted annually to renew the exemption. The Department will review the application for eligibility and notify the applicant of approval or denial status.

structured_extraction.program_name: Historic Rehabilitation and Restoration Tax Credit (CHAP Tax Credit)
structured_extraction.program_description: A 10-year property tax credit program administered by the Commission for Historical and Architectural Preservation (CHAP) that reduces property taxes for owners who rehabilitate historically designated properties in Baltimore City. The credit is based on the increased property value resulting from qualifying rehabilitation work and is computed once, applied over the entire 10-year period, and is fully transferrable to a new owner for the remaining life of the credit. Both residential and commercial properties are eligible. Since 1997, over $1.3 billion has been invested in historic properties through this program, with over 4,300 projects completed. The program covers properties in 38 designated local historic districts and over 200 designated landmarks throughout Baltimore City.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 10-year property tax credit on the increased property value resulting from qualifying rehabilitation work on historic structures. The credit is computed once and applied over the entire 10-year period. It is fully transferrable to a new owner for the remaining life of the credit. The credit appears on your next issued tax bill as a 'Special Credit' after your project receives final certification. The credit is calculated by the Department of Finance and is based on your rehabilitation investment. Projects must involve a minimum 25% investment of the property's full cash value to qualify. For projects with construction costs of $5 million or less, the credit is 100% of the tax difference for all 10 years. For projects exceeding $5 million, the credit percentage phases down from 80% in years 1-5 to 30% in year 10. The credit cannot be combined with other City credits but can be combined with Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit and Federal Historic Preservation Tax Incentives. For projects over $3.5 million, additional Department of Finance review and approval is required. The credit is not applied to reduce tax liability below the amount owed at the time preliminary approval was issued.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - no specific deadline. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with no defined application window.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Baltimore City who own historically designated properties (including Baltimore City Landmarks, National Register Individual Designations, contributing structures in Baltimore City or National Register Historic Districts, or properties contributing to the Baltimore National Heritage Area) and wish to undertake qualifying rehabilitation and restoration projects, including both residential and commercial properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Historic rehabilitation and restoration work on historically designated properties, including both interior and exterior work that meets CHAP Design Guidelines. Eligible costs include material and labor costs, architect fees, engineering fees, and design fees. Ineligible costs include property acquisition, utility bills, property taxes, and holding costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Properties must be historically designated as a Baltimore City Landmark, National Register Individual Designation, Contributing to a Baltimore City Historic District (38 designated local historic districts), Contributing to a National Register Historic District, or Contributing to the Baltimore National Heritage Area. Over 200 designated landmarks are also eligible.
requirements_list: Property must be historically designated (Baltimore City Landmark, National Register Individual Designation, contributing to a Baltimore City or National Register Historic District, or contributing to the Baltimore National Heritage Area)
Minimum 25% investment of the property's full cash value required
Project must receive preliminary approval from CHAP staff before any work begins
All work must meet CHAP Design Guidelines
Complete online application with photographs, plans, and scope of work submitted via propertytaxcredits.baltimorecity.gov
Proof of ownership required
Pre-improvement appraisal must be completed within 90 days of application submission and must meet Department of Finance requirements
Post-improvement appraisal must be completed within 90 days of final Use and Occupancy Permit (or last permit inspection if no U&O permit required)
$50 review fee paid online
Authorization to Proceed Application required if property is in a local historic district
Enterprise Zone Verification Form required if property has commercial component

For projects over $3.5 million: documentation supporting economic necessity for credit, statement of projected economic impact and public benefits, and certification from Baltimore Development Corporation regarding Enterprise Zone eligibility
For projects over $3.5 million: proof of 75% vacancy for 3 years, documentation of high-performance market-rate rental housing status, or other evidence demonstrating credit necessity
Notarized statement detailing project costs required before final certification
All permits and Authorizations to Proceed must be completed
Work must adhere to CHAP design guidelines throughout the 10-year credit term or credit will be revoked
Property owner must maintain major historic features and comply with City Building, Fire and Related Codes to continue receiving credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Read the Tax Credit FAQ at propertytaxcredits.baltimorecity.gov. 2. Review the Program Rules and Regulations and CHAP Design Guidelines. 3. Register and create account on the Historic Tax Credit Application system at propertytaxcredits.baltimorecity.gov. 4. Submit complete online application including: high-resolution color photographs of all exterior elevations, roof, interior rooms and architectural details; existing and proposed drawings if building elevation or interior layout will change; detailed scope of work; proof of ownership; required forms for historic districts and enterprise zones; and appraisal meeting Department of Finance requirements. 5. Pre-improvement appraisal must be submitted within 90 days of application submission. 6. Pay $50 review fee online. 7. CHAP staff will review application; if approved, you receive preliminary certification in writing. Note: applications not receiving preliminary approval within 180 days of request expire. 8. Once preliminary approval received, complete rehabilitation work strictly following CHAP Design Guidelines and all approved plans. Work occurring before preliminary approval (except limited pre-approved work like basement excavation or underpinning) renders property ineligible. 9. Upon project completion, submit final certification application including: completion photographs, all final permits and Authorizations to Proceed, notarized cost documentation showing at least 25% investment, and post-improvement appraisal (must be submitted within 90 days of final Use and Occupancy Permit or last permit inspection). 10. Post-improvement appraisal is reviewed and accepted by Department of Finance. Final approvals by CHAP and Finance Director must be issued before credit calculation. 11. The tax credit appears on next issued tax bill as a 'Special Credit'. 12. For projects over $3.5 million: three years from acceptance date, must submit statement of actual economic impact and public benefits (if not provided within four years, credit is permanently removed). Applications not receiving final certification within 180 days of final certification request expire. Applications have 2 years from preliminary approval to receive final certification; may request one extension for additional 2 years (4 years total). For projects over $3.5 million, timeline extends to 3 years with one extension for additional 3 years (6 years total). Send questions to historictaxcredit@baltimorecity.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Accelerator Fund / HOME-ARP (Home Investment Partnerships Program American Rescue Plan Act)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Baltimore City program that provides grant funding for the development of new affordable housing units and the construction of permanent supportive housing, which combines affordable housing, health care, and supportive services. Funded through a combination of the City's American Rescue Plan Act State and Local Recovery Funds (SLFRF), HOME-ARP (Home Investment Partnerships Program – American Rescue Plan Act) funds, and other committed ARPA funds, the program aims to expand housing supply for low-income residents, individuals and families who are homeless, formerly homeless, or otherwise unable to maintain housing stability. Awards totaling approximately $29.8–$32.5 million were announced in March 2024 following a Notice of Funding Availability posted in October 2023.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Total committed funding of approximately $29.8–$32.5 million, comprised of $15.2–$15.4 million from HOME-ARP and $14.7 million from ARPA SLFRF. Maximum awards are up to $250,000 per unit for permanent supportive housing, up to $100,000 per unit for traditional affordable housing, and up to $500,000 for predevelopment costs. Eligible uses include architectural and engineering services, environmental assessments and testing, market and financial feasibility analyses, carrying costs, zoning analysis, staff time, development consultants, legal fees, and hard construction costs. Housing Accelerator Fund supports both hard and soft costs; HOME-ARP supports hard costs only. All PSH units funded through Housing Accelerator Fund must restrict leasing and occupancy for 15 years at 30% AMI. HOME-ARP units must restrict leasing and occupancy for 20 years for new construction and rehabilitation. Awards were announced on March 11, 2024.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and for-profit developers and organizations seeking to develop permanent supportive housing or affordable housing units in Baltimore City, as well as individuals and families who are homeless, formerly homeless, or otherwise unable to maintain housing stability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and construction of new affordable housing units (including deeply affordable units) and permanent supportive housing, as well as predevelopment costs associated with funded housing projects. Permanent supportive housing combines affordable housing, health care, and supportive services. Funds support architectural and engineering, environmental assessment and testing, market and financial feasibility analysis, carrying costs, zoning analysis, staff time, development consultants, and legal fees associated with closing, financing, and drafting legal documents necessary for development. Hard construction costs are eligible under both programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. All projects must accept referrals from Baltimore's Coordinated Access System. Projects receiving HOME-ARP funding must meet HUD Site and Neighborhood Standards for adequate size, exposure, contour, utilities, and street accessibility.
requirements_list: Permanent supportive housing units must follow Housing First model and fill vacancies through Coordinated Access System
Housing must be permanent and affordable with tenants holding standard leases; acceptance of services not a condition of occupancy
Comprehensive, individualized support services must be accessible to tenants at their residence
PSH units must target greater of 5 units or 20% of total units with dedicated project-based vouchers or other rental subsidy; or 25% leasing preference through Coordinated Access
All units funded through Housing Accelerator must restrict leasing at 30% AMI for 15 years
All HOME-ARP units must restrict leasing for 20 years for new construction/rehabilitation
At least 5% of all units must comply with UFAS requirements for persons with mobility impairments; at least 2% for hearing or vision impairments
Projects must comply with Section 3 local hiring requirements and Davis Bacon wage rates for HOME-ARP
Projects must comply with City Prevailing Wage Rates (excess of $5,000); MBE/WBE commitment required for contracts $50,000+
Projects must complete Green Construction Statement of Compliance; most multi-family dwellings must comply with Baltimore City Green Construction Law
All demolition must comply with federal, state, and local laws and industry standards
Site control must be demonstrated at submission; title within 12 months of executing Funding Agreement
Development approvals required (zoning changes, site plan review, street/alley closings, Planning Department pre-development meeting)
Culturally specific/culturally responsive project concepts will be prioritized
Applicants must demonstrate financial feasibility and ability to leverage additional public and private funds
Applicants must provide detailed development budgets listing all funding sources, uses, and fund status
Construction budgets must include line items for builder's profit, overhead, construction management, administration, and architecture/engineering
Qualifying populations served must be homeless, at risk of homelessness, fleeing domestic violence/sexual assault/trafficking, or other populations at greatest risk of housing instability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications were accepted through a combined Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) for Housing Accelerator Fund and HOME-ARP. A pre-proposal conference was held September 14, 2023. The Neighborly application portal opened October 20, 2023, with submissions accepted through November 20, 2023. Threshold review includes organizational, financial, and compliance-related documentation; applicants must submit authorization to submit, Commitment to Quality Readiness Checklist, debarment certification, identity of interest/conflict disclosure, commitment to comply with federal and city requirements, certification of compliance, owned property disclosure, and financial/organizational disclosures. Applications meeting threshold criteria are scored on project feasibility (70 points maximum), project management team experience and qualifications, and community engagement/equity (maximum 145 total points). Minimum score of 100 points required for award consideration. DHCD submits approved proposals to HUD for HOME-ARP funding. All funds must be obligated by December 31, 2024, and spent by December 31, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Navigation Program, funded through the American Rescue Plan Act and administered by Baltimore City's Mayor's Office of Homeless Services, provides housing navigation support and landlord recruitment assistance to help people experiencing or at risk of homelessness find and secure permanent housing. Community members can meet with Housing Navigators at participating Enoch Pratt Free Library locations (Cherry Hill, Walbrook, and Waverly branches) to receive help understanding housing problems, information on local resources to exit or prevent homelessness, personalized housing plans, referrals to shelters, completion of Coordinated Access Intake, guidance for housing selection and lease signing, and short-term case management. The program also includes landlord recruitment and engagement efforts, with community listening sessions to gather feedback on landlord incentive strategies. Approximately $7.6 million was awarded to support these efforts, launched in 2023.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $7.6 million awarded for housing navigation and landlord recruitment support. Free, in-person meetings with Housing Navigators at three Enoch Pratt Free Library locations (Cherry Hill, Walbrook, and Waverly) providing counseling, referrals, personalized housing plans, completion of Coordinated Access Intake, and short-term case management. The program also includes landlord recruitment and engagement support, including community listening sessions to gather feedback on landlord incentive strategies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community members experiencing or at risk of homelessness in Baltimore City, as well as landlords and non-profit organizations supporting housing placement
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing navigation assistance, counseling, personalized housing plans, referrals to shelters, Coordinated Access Intake completion, guidance for housing selection and lease signing, short-term case management, and landlord recruitment and engagement support
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only; in-person navigation services available at three Enoch Pratt Free Library branches: Cherry Hill, Walbrook, and Waverly
requirements_list: Individuals must be experiencing or at risk of homelessness in Baltimore City
Free and open to all eligible individuals without application barriers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Housing Navigators directly at participating Enoch Pratt Free Library locations (Cherry Hill, Walbrook, and Waverly) during posted hours of operation to schedule a free, in-person meeting. Individuals can walk in or call to arrange appointments. The program was launched in 2023 through the Mayor's Office of Homeless Services and accepts participants on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Opportunities for Persons with HIV/AIDS (HOPWA) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: HOPWA is a federal program administered by the City of Baltimore as the grantee for the Baltimore-Towson Eligible Metropolitan Statistical Area (EMSA). It provides housing assistance and supportive services to low-income persons living with HIV/AIDS and their families to help them find and maintain safe, sanitary, and stable housing, gain better access to health care, and participate fully in community living. Annual allocations are determined based on HIV case data shared by the Maryland Department of Health. The City of Baltimore contracts with localities within the EMSA to address the housing needs of persons living with HIV/AIDS in their communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HOPWA provides housing assistance including tenant-based or project-based rental assistance, conversion, lease and repair to facilities, new construction, and short-term rent, mortgage, and utility payments to prevent homelessness. All counties and cities within the Baltimore-Towson EMSA except Carroll County provide housing assistance in the form of tenant-based rental assistance. Supportive services include permanent housing placement, employment and education services, personal assistance, assistance gaining access to local, state, and federal benefits and services, and resources and referrals for drug and alcohol abuse treatment and counseling, daycare, nutritional services, intensive care, and physical and mental health services. Annual allocations are determined based on HIV case data shared by the Maryland Department of Health. Assistance is available on a continuous basis for eligible individuals and families living with HIV/AIDS.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Homeless Services (MOHS)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income persons (at or below 80 percent of area median income) medically diagnosed with HIV/AIDS and their families, including persons experiencing homelessness in Baltimore City and the broader Baltimore-Towson EMSA.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing assistance for rental payments (tenant-based or project-based), facility conversion and repair, new construction, and short-term rent, mortgage, and utility payments to prevent homelessness. Supportive services for permanent housing placement, employment and education, personal assistance, access to local, state, and federal benefits and social services, and referrals for drug and alcohol treatment, daycare, nutritional services, and physical and mental health services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Baltimore-Towson Eligible Metropolitan Statistical Area (EMSA), which includes Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, Carroll County, Harford County, Howard County, and Queen Anne's County. All counties and cities within the EMSA except Carroll County provide tenant-based rental assistance. Interested persons should contact their local provider for specific services and availability in their area.
requirements_list: Must be a person living with HIV/AIDS or a family member of a person living with HIV/AIDS
Must have low income (at or below 80 percent of area median income)
Must be medically diagnosed with HIV/AIDS
Must be seeking stable housing in the Baltimore-Towson EMSA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals seeking HOPWA assistance should contact the Coordinated Access System at 410-935-9862 or 410-545-1511 to begin the application process. Alternatively, contact the Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Homeless Services at 410-396-3757. The City of Baltimore contracts with localities within the EMSA, and interested persons should contact their local designated program provider for specific application procedures, eligibility verification, and available services in their respective county or jurisdiction. Services are provided on a rolling basis as funding and availability permit.

Grants are also available for specific repairs such as lead remediation and accessibility modifications for people with disabilities. Grants do not require repayment but have specific eligibility requirements. Applicants must have an income not to exceed the income limits set by the program, which vary based on household size.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for roof repairs, heating system repairs, plumbing repairs, electrical repairs, lead remediation, and accessibility modifications for people with disabilities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A local policy that requires developers to create affordable housing units as part of market-rate rental housing projects when the project receives a benefit from the city such as a tax credit or grant. The program makes housing affordable in neighborhoods with high housing values by requiring 10% of units in qualifying projects to be available as affordable units for 30 years.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Projects meeting eligibility criteria are required to make 10% of their units available as affordable units, dispersed throughout the project and not concentrated on particular floors or buildings. Of these affordable units, 5% must be available to households earning 50% of area median income (very low-income) and 5% to households earning 60% of area median income (low-income). Tenants pay maximum affordable rent not exceeding 30% of gross household income, as determined by HUD income limits adjusted for household size. The difference between market rate and affordable rent is covered by the High-Performance Inclusionary Housing Tax Credit, administered by the City's Finance Department. Inclusionary units must be designed and constructed at the same time as market-rate units, be dispersed throughout the project, and offer tenants the same amenities and access to common areas as market-rate tenants. Developers may offer additional inclusionary units (up to 5% more) to extremely low-income households (30% AMI) or very low-income households if they accept additional subsidy from the city. Inclusionary unit affordability is enforced through a 30-year covenant recorded in Baltimore City Land Records.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis - applications accepted at time of building permit submission
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit developers proposing new rental housing projects of 20 or more units in Baltimore City that will receive a major public subsidy or benefit from significant land use authorization.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The assistance covers the gap between market rent and affordable rent for designated affordable units in qualifying development projects, making housing affordable to households earning 50-60% of area median income (or 30% AMI for additional subsidy units) for a 30-year period. Funds support the creation and long-term affordability maintenance of inclusive housing within mixed-income developments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. The law applies to market rental projects that submit a building permit application on or after July 21, 2024. The Inclusionary Housing requirements are applicable to the project commencing on the date that the Certificate of Use and Occupancy is issued for the project, for a period of 30 years from such date.
requirements_list: Project must include 20 or more units
Project must receive a major public subsidy OR benefit from significant land use authorization
Project must be newly constructed, wholly renovated, or converted from non-residential use
Cost of construction or conversion must exceed $60,000 per unit

Developer must submit an Inclusionary Housing Plan that includes general project information, confirmation of eligibility criteria, unit descriptions and pricing, project schedule, and an Affirmative Marketing Plan before building permit is released
Inclusionary units must be designed and planned at the same time as market-rate units and designated prior to leasing
Inclusionary units must be dispersed throughout the project and not concentrated on a particular floor or building
Inclusionary units must be provided in the same proportion as market-rate unit floor plans throughout the building
Inclusionary units must have exterior appearance, number of bedrooms, and overall quality of construction consistent with market-rate units in the same project
Tenants of inclusionary units must be offered the same amenities as market-rate tenants
Penthouse units may not be included in the count of a project's total dwelling units for calculating inclusionary unit requirements
Fractional numbers of required inclusionary units must be rounded up to provide an additional unit to a low-income household
Developer must apply for occupancy permits for inclusionary units concurrently with market-rate units
Developer must maintain separate waitlists for income eligibility and bedroom size for applications that cannot be immediately approved
Developer must verify tenant income annually when lease is renewed and certify eligibility no later than when lease is signed
Developer may not group inclusionary units in a concentration on a particular floor or within a particular building if project includes multiple buildings
If over-income tenant reaches 100% AMI, developer must permit tenant to remain in unit and make an additional inclusionary unit available to lease to new inclusionary tenant
Developer must implement affirmative marketing plan to reach persons least likely to become tenants without special outreach
Developer may not include eviction records older than 3 years in tenant screening
Developer may not include in screening evictions where tenant prevailed, settlement was reached, or matter was dropped
Affirmative marketing plan must be written clearly in plain English
Declaration of Affordability/Covenant must be recorded in Baltimore City Land Records
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Developers attend a Pre-Development meeting with the Department of Planning where they receive information about Inclusionary Housing requirements and complete a Pre-Development Project Information Form. 2. Within 10 days of receiving the form, DHCD staff may request additional information to confirm if the project is subject to Inclusionary Housing obligations. 3. When applying for a building permit, developers must submit a completed Inclusionary Housing Plan electronically to inclusionaryhousingsubmission@baltimorecity.gov. The plan must include all required exhibits and documentation. 4. DHCD staff provides an initial threshold review within 10 business days of receipt and notifies the developer in writing of any requests for additional information or changes needed. 5. Developer has 5 business days to submit materials requested by DHCD. 6. Upon receipt of a complete plan, DHCD staff recommends whether the plan should be approved and prepares a project summary distributed to the Department of Finance, Department of Planning, and the Inclusionary Housing Board. 7. The Inclusionary Housing Board meets within 15 business days of receipt to provide comments on the plan. If the Board cannot meet, members may provide written comments within 5 days. 8. DHCD provides formal written response to developer within 45 business days of submission stating whether the plan has been approved or denied and whether a building permit may be issued. 9. Upon approval, the Inclusionary Housing Program Manager sends written notification to the Department's Permits and Plans Review Office with the developer, Commissioner, Chief Operating Officer, and Chief of Staff copied. 10. Building permits cannot be issued until the Inclusionary Housing Program Manager has submitted the notification of approved plan. 11. Approved plans are posted on DHCD's website. Building permit applications that fail to include the Inclusionary Housing Plan form will not be reviewed, and no building permit will be released without an approved plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City's process to acquire vacant and abandoned properties by foreclosing on municipal liens (unpaid property taxes, environmental citations, water bills) when the liens exceed the property's assessed value. The City takes title to the property and works with communities to determine redevelopment outcomes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City acquires vacant lots or buildings with Vacant Building Notices through judicial foreclosure, taking title to the property at no cost to the property seeker. DHCD then makes the cleared lots or vacant buildings available for redevelopment to potential homeowners, small developers, community development organizations, developers, or other interested parties. The process typically takes 6-8 months from filing to title award, and no auction is required once the City obtains title. DHCD works with communities to determine the best outcomes for individual properties or groupings of properties. Once the City is awarded title, properties are made available for redevelopment without requiring an auction process.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development (DHCD)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Communities, property owners, potential homeowners, small developers, community development organizations, and developers interested in acquiring vacant and abandoned properties in Baltimore City for redevelopment. Communities should have a community plan for desired outcomes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of vacant lots and vacant buildings for redevelopment purposes to meet community needs and goals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City properties only. Properties must be vacant lots or have a Vacant Building Notice (VBN). The property must be free of tax sale certificate holders.
requirements_list: Property must be a vacant lot or have a Vacant Building Notice (VBN)
Municipal liens must exceed the assessed value of the property
Property must not have a tax sale certificate holder
Community can submit property addresses to DHCD for review using the In Rem Eligibility Form at https://dhcd.baltimorecity.gov/rem-eligibility-form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Communities can submit property addresses to DHCD for review by completing the In Rem Eligibility Form at https://dhcd.baltimorecity.gov/rem-eligibility-form. DHCD will conduct analysis to determine if the property qualifies for In Rem foreclosure. If eligible and no tax sale certificate exists, DHCD files a Judicial In Rem foreclosure case in Circuit Court and provides proper notice to anyone with a legal interest in the property. After service of notice, if liens are not paid and foreclosure is not successfully contested, the Circuit Court awards title to the City. The process typically takes 6-8 months from filing to title award. Once the City obtains title, DHCD works with the community to determine redevelopment outcomes and makes the property available to interested parties.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant and loan program that helps homeowners and landlords identify and reduce lead hazards in homes to protect families and children from lead poisoning exposure.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding is provided in the form of either a grant or a loan, depending on income and financial status. For homeowner-occupied properties, assistance is available for households up to $72,950-$137,550 annual income depending on household size. For renter-occupied properties, assistance is available up to $45,650-$86,000 annual income depending on household size. Landlords are expected to contribute a portion of the cost. Interventions covered include window replacement, door replacement, wall stabilization, and minimal structural repairs. Services provided include education, lead risk-reduction, temporary relocation, and referrals to other programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with a pregnant woman or a child under age 6 living in the house. Also considers clients who have a child who does not live in the house but spends 3 hours a day on two separate days a week and a total of 60 hours per year at the property. Both homeowners and landlords may apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead hazard reduction interventions including window replacement, door replacement, wall stabilization, and minimal structural repairs to eliminate or reduce lead hazards in homes built before 1978.

requirements_list: Household must have a pregnant woman or child under age 6 living in the home
Property must be located in Baltimore City
Income must not exceed the maximum annual income guidelines for household size and property occupancy type (homeowner-occupied or renter-occupied)
For properties with a child not living there full-time, child must spend at least 3 hours per day on two separate days per week and a total of 60 hours per year at the property
Property must be built before 1978

Contact the program at 443-984-1613 for questions. structured_extraction.program_description: A $2 million pilot program administered by Baltimore City's Department of Housing & Community Development (DHCD) in partnership with the Mayor's Office of Older Adult Affairs & Advocacy. The program eliminates property tax debt for legacy residents who are 65 or older, have owned their home for more than 10 years, earn less than $73,000 annually, and enroll in the Tax Sale Deferral Program. Qualifying homeowners will have their tax bills cleared in the following year provided they complete financial literacy courses and enroll in payment plans for future bills. The program is designed to help older, long-term homeowners avoid displacement due to accumulated property tax debt.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program allocates $2 million in one-time funding to clear accumulated property tax debt for eligible legacy homeowners on a first-come, first-served basis. Each applicant's tax lien amount is subtracted from the $2 million total. Once the $2 million is exhausted, the program will close. Qualifying homeowners age 65 or older who have owned their primary residence for at least 10 years, earn less than $73,000 annually, have an assessed home value of $250,000 or less, received a Final Bill and Legal Notices (FBLN) in February, and enroll in the Tax Sale Deferral Program will have their accumulated tax debt forgiven. Recipients must enter into a payment plan for future tax year bills to receive and maintain the benefit.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Mayor's Office of Older Adult Affairs and Advocacy; Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City homeowners aged 65 or older who have owned their primary residence for at least 10 years, have annual household income less than $73,000, have an assessed home value of $250,000 or less, and are facing property tax debt or tax sale risk.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eliminates accumulated property tax debt for qualifying legacy homeowners, clearing their tax bills for the following year and helping them avoid displacement due to tax debt. Funds cannot be used for any other purpose.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Applicants must have received a Final Bill and Legal Notices (FBLN) in February 2026.
requirements_list: Homeowner must be 65 years or older
Must have owned the home as a primary residence for at least 10 years
Annual household income must be less than $73,000 for the 2025 tax year
Assessed value of home must be $250,000 or less
Must have received a Final Bill and Legal Notices (FBLN) in February 2026
Must be at risk for tax sale
Must be located in Baltimore City
Must enroll in the Tax Sale Deferral Program by April 15, 2026
Must enter into a payment plan for future tax year bills
Must agree to complete financial literacy courses
Property must be the homeowner's primary residence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must enroll in the Tax Sale Deferral Program, which opened on February 15, 2026. Eligible applicants can apply online at https://bit.ly/DHCD-Neighborly or submit a paper application. Paper applications are available at the 1st floor of the Abel Wolman Building and the 11th floor of 417 E. Fayette Street, Baltimore, 21202. Applicants can also pick up applications in person at these locations. Alternatively, applicants can attend the Legacy Homeowners Pilot Program sign-up event at Waxter Senior Center on Friday, April 10th, 2026, where city employees will be available to help with enrollment. Applicants for the 2026 Tax Sale Deferral Program are automatically reviewed for the Legacy Homeowners Pilot Program. The Mayor's Office of Older Adult Affairs and Advocacy conducts coordinated in-person and phone outreach through April 15 to eligible older adults. For the sign-up event, bring official government-issued ID, 2 utility bills addressed to the property, and proof of income for tax year 2025. FAQs are available online.

structured_extraction.program_description: This partnership program with participating employers encourages homeownership near places of employment by providing matching funds to help employees buy homes in neighborhoods close to their workplaces.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City matches employer contributions between $1,000 and $2,500 for total incentives of $2,000-$5,000 or more depending on the employer. This is provided as a grant that does not need to be repaid if the homeowner stays in the home for five years. All incentives require a minimum $1,000 investment from the home buyer's own funds towards the purchase of the property.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Funding is planned each year based on the City's fiscal calendar (July 1 to June 30). Incentives are given out on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employees of participating employers who are interested in buying homes near their workplaces in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The assistance can be used to reduce closing costs and support down payments when buying a home near the workplace.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: This program is available to homebuyers purchasing property in Baltimore City near their places of employment.
requirements_list: Must be employed by a participating employer
Must complete a homeownership class from a City-approved homeownership counseling agency within one year before writing an offer on a home
Must contribute at least $1,000 of your own money towards the house
Settlement date must be at least 30 days after submitting application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Confirm that your employer participates in the program. Register your account and submit an application through the Applicant Portal at https://portal.neighborlysoftware.com/baltimoremd/Participant. Allow at least 30 days between application submission and settlement date for processing. Checks typically take 10 to 15 business days to be sent after approval. When accessing the Portal for the first time, click on the Register link to create a user name (your email address) and password. The system will send a validation email to confirm ownership of your email address. Once registered, you may login using your email and password. If you forget your password, use the 'Forgot your Password?' link to reset it.

MOED and Maryland Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation partner with local businesses to support employer strategies for retention, growth expansion, and layoff aversion through skills training in in-demand occupations.

Maximum $4,500 training cap per trainee for a project or series of projects. Maximum request per year cannot exceed $40,000.
