structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Classroom-based training, in-house staff training, apprenticeships, and other skill-upgrading opportunities for current employees. Funds can support tuition, fees, books, materials, and training-related expenses.

structured_extraction.program_name: New Construction and/or Rehabilitation of Existing Affordable Rental Housing (Affordable Housing Trust Fund NOFA)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development administers the Affordable Housing Trust Fund, which provides grants to support new construction of affordable rental housing and/or rehabilitation of existing rental projects. The program has run through multiple rounds (including Round 4, Round 6, and Round 7), making tens of millions of dollars available over time. Each round includes set-asides for Community Land Trusts and emerging developers. Projects must serve households at or below 50% of Area Median Income, with at least half of units serving households at or below 30% AMI. The program is administered through a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) process with competitive review and scoring.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund to support new construction of affordable rental housing and rehabilitation of existing rental housing projects. Round 7 (FY26) makes up to $7,500,000 available. Individual project requests are up to $1,000,000. Trust funds can be used to fund up to 50% of a project's Total Development Cost or a maximum of $1,000,000 per project, whichever is less. Maximum request per unit is $75,000 for households earning 50% AMI and $120,000 for fewer than 10 units or $150,000 for 10+ units for units at 30% AMI (adjusted for family size). Up to 25% of total award can be used for predevelopment and/or acquisition costs (combined); up to 10% for operating costs directly related to project implementation; and up to 25% of total award can be advanced for predevelopment and/or acquisition costs (grant awards only). Set-asides of up to $1,000,000 each are reserved for Community Land Trusts and emerging developers per round.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 9, 2026 (Round 7 submissions deadline); Notification of Awards Week of April 13, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and for-profit developers, Community Land Trusts, and emerging developers sponsoring affordable rental housing projects in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction of affordable rental housing or rehabilitation of existing rental projects to create affordable housing for households at or below 50 percent of Area Median Income, with at least half of units serving households at or below 30 percent of Area Median Income. Eligible uses include: acquisition and stabilization of non-City owned properties; architectural and engineering; environmental assessment and testing; market and financial feasibility analysis; construction; carrying costs; financing and lender fees; legal fees associated with closing, financing, and drafting legal documents; consultant fees directly associated with project implementation; project management staff; infrastructure and utilities; single family, condos and co-operative building projects; demolition; customary landscaping; parking, infrastructure and utilities; and mixed-use buildings that include ground floor retail. Up to 25% can be used for predevelopment costs and up to 25% for acquisition costs. Up to 10% can be used for operating costs directly related to project implementation including staff costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only.

Must demonstrate development approvals required for project (zoning changes, site plan review, street and alley closings, predevelopment meeting with Department of Planning)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications submitted through Neighborly Portal. For Round 7: NOFA and guidelines posted November 21, 2025; Pre-proposal conference held December 10, 2025; Questions submitted by December 12, 2025; Answers posted by December 22, 2025; Submission deadline January 9, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST; Review and scoring January 20 through March 17, 2026; Notification of awards week of April 13, 2026. Program operates through a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) process with competitive review and scoring each round. Threshold review determines eligibility based on organizational, financial and compliance-related documentation. Applications meeting threshold criteria are scored on project feasibility (70 points), community engagement and participation (25 points), and achieving equity (25 points). Minimum score of 105 out of 120 points required to be considered for award (applicants not reaching 105 through base scoring may use bonus points to reach minimum threshold). Bonus points available for: Long Term Affordability (up to 10 points), Supports & Grows Local Businesses (up to 4 points), Serves Households at or below 30% AMI (up to 10 points), Provides Services for Permanent Supportive Housing (up to 5 points), Takes Advantage of Apprenticeships and Training programs (up to 4 points), Collaboration Across Multiple Neighborhoods (up to 5 points), Local Hiring Criteria (up to 7 points), Environmental Sustainability (up to 5 points), Developer Fee deferral (up to 10 points), and Markets of Strength Neighborhoods (up to 10 points). Applications reviewed by interagency panel. Recommendations submitted to Housing Commissioner who makes final award decisions. Following award notification, awardees attend orientation and initial meeting to review process and funding availability. No funds available until Board of Estimates approves Funding Agreement. Awardees required to submit progress reports detailing project completion percentages, reasons for schedule delays, MBE/WBE goal achievement, and local hiring plan updates.

structured_extraction.program_description: A community-driven grant program that provides funding to support meaningful and measurable change through community-led projects, including operating funds or physical improvements, in eligible neighborhoods near Pimlico Racetrack in Baltimore City. The program is funded by Pimlico Local Impact Aid, which is generated from video lottery terminal revenue. It serves the Park Heights Master Plan Area and the One-Mile Radius around Pimlico Racetrack, encompassing the Liberty-Wabash, Northwest Community Planning Forum, and Coldspring-Newtown neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $500 and $25,000 are awarded to tax-exempt organizations for projects during the 2025 calendar year. Grant funding is generally disbursed on a 40-40-20 schedule with 40% provided at the start of the project, 40% at the midway point of the project contingent on successful project progress, and 20% at the completion of the project upon submission of a final report. Startup payments are issued upon approval of the final scope of work, final line-item budget, and grant agreement execution, and within the first four weeks of the beginning of the grant period. Final payments are paid upon approval of the final report, which will be held until all reports have been submitted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible community organizations with 501(c)3 tax-exempt status, mission-based organizations with a tax-exempt fiscal sponsor, faith-based organizations proposing non-religious public-benefit projects, public schools proposing community-based projects that benefit their students, and City agencies, serving the Park Heights Master Plan Area and the One-Mile Radius around Pimlico Racetrack (including Liberty-Wabash, Northwest Community Planning Forum, and Coldspring-Newtown areas).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community development projects including public art projects (community sculptures, murals), local arts initiatives (painting or drawing workshops, culinary arts classes, dance or music classes and performances), community signage, bicycle amenities (bicycle racks, rentals), streetscaping/block projects (painted crosswalks, trees and flowers, artistic planters), marketing efforts (website development, promotional activities), education opportunities (speaker series, academic enrichment, podcasting/recording series), community events (neighborhood festivals, recreation), and technical assistance for community associations for professional design, financial, legal services, assistance to secure 501(c)3 nonprofit status, or development of a strategic plan. Operating funds and physical improvements that create meaningful and measurable change for residents are also eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must occur within the Park Heights Master Plan Area or the One-Mile Radius around Pimlico Racetrack, which includes Liberty-Wabash, the Northwest Community Planning Forum, and Coldspring-Newtown neighborhoods in Baltimore City. Specific boundaries: Park Heights Master Plan Area includes Northern Parkway (N), Wabash Ave. to Western Maryland Railroad (W), Liberty Heights Ave. (S), Druid Park Dr. (SE), Greenspring Ave. (E). Northwest Community Planning Forum Boundaries include Northern Parkway (S), County line (W/N), Jones Falls Expressway (E). Coldspring-Newtown Boundaries include Northern Parkway (N), Greenspring Avenue (W), West Cold Spring Lane (S), Jones Falls Expressway (E). Liberty-Wabash Boundaries include Liberty Heights Avenue (S), Northern Parkway (W), Wabash (N/E). Priority will be given to organizations based in eligible areas or who are partnering with an organization based in those neighborhoods.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a non-profit organization with 501(c)3 tax-exempt status recognized by the IRS, a mission-based organization without 501(c)3 tax-exempt status but with a tax-exempt fiscal sponsor, a faith-based organization proposing a non-religious project that benefits the public, or a public school proposing a community-based project that benefits its students
Organization must be based within Baltimore City

Organizations (or their fiscal sponsors) must have an active tax identification number

Baltimore City may require insurance for projects
Organization must be current with any City- or State-mandated quarterly reporting requirements tied to Pimlico Local Impact Aid that the organization has previously received
All activities and services must take place in eligible geographic areas (Park Heights Master Plan Area or One-Mile Radius)
Projects must be able to be completed within two years from the start of funding
Applicants do not include individuals, state or federal government agencies, or for-profit organizations or businesses
Physical improvement or construction projects must have land control or permission from the property owner

Activities must not improperly discriminate as to race, gender, marital status, sexual preference, age, disability, creed or ethnicity, and cannot be grants for religious indoctrination or other religious activities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Determine Eligibility: Review guidelines to confirm organization and expense eligibility. 2. Access Sessions and Technical Assistance: Attend the Applicant Information Session on Tuesday, March 11, 2025 at 7:00 PM EDT or submit technical assistance requests to pcda@baltimorecity.gov. Submit application questions to pcda@baltimorecity.gov with subject line '2025 NW Neighborhood Initiative Grant Application Question'. An FAQ will be posted and updated regularly, with a final FAQ posted by 5:00 PM EDT on Monday, March 10, 2025. 3. Submit Application: Complete the online grant application through the JotForm portal at https://form.jotform.com/250146365495057 by 11:59 PM EDT on Friday, March 28, 2025. The application must include: Project Title and Address, Organization Information, Point of Contact, Geographic Area, Type of Project, Requested Grant Amount ($500-$25,000), Project Overview and Scope (500 words or fewer), Project Budget with line-item descriptions, Project Schedule, IRS Determination Letter, Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland Department of Commerce, Board-Approved Organization Budget, Fiscal Sponsor Information if applicable, and optional Community Support and Equity Framework documentation. 4. Technical Review of Applications: Applicants will be assessed for ability to meet eligibility requirements and application completeness. If documentation is lacking, applicants will be provided at least five calendar days to provide information. 5. Panel Review of Applications: A panel including staff from the Department of Planning, Department of Housing and Community Development, and the Pimlico Community Development Authority (PCDA) will review applications using a standard rubric and consensus discussions to recommend awards. The Baltimore City Planning Department will confirm final award decisions. 6. Grant Announcement: All applicants will receive an application update by June 2025. If awarded, grantees will receive an email with a link to the Grant Agreement. 7. Grant Agreement: A Grant Agreement must be signed confirming the project and detailing roles and requirements of all parties before the project begins. It will include final detailed scope of work, final line-item budget, and projected schedule for access to funds. 8. Reporting: Grantees must submit quarterly reports by October 6, 2025; January 12, 2026; April 6, 2026; July 6, 2026; October 12, 2026; January 11, 2027; and April 12, 2027. A final report is due by July 12, 2027. If a project is completed before the end of the grant period, final reports and supporting documentation must be submitted within 60 days of project completion. structured_extraction.program_description: The Opioid Restitution Fund provides grants to nonprofit organizations in Baltimore City to support community efforts in addressing the opioid crisis through overdose prevention, treatment access, harm reduction, and recovery support. Funding supports programs and infrastructure related to prevention, treatment, recovery, harm reduction, social determinants of health, and other initiatives targeting harms caused by the opioid epidemic.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A total of $2 million is available for allocation in Round 1 (Fiscal Year 2026). Funding is distributed through three tiers: Tier 1 (up to $50,000, approximately 3-6 awards) supports low-barrier social support services; Tier 2 (up to $250,000, approximately 2-4 awards) supports comprehensive harm reduction services; Tier 3 (up to $500,000, approximately 2-3 awards) supports low-barrier mobile treatment and harm reduction services. Proposed project funding amounts can be spread across a project period of up to two years. Organizations that use their full award within a single year remain eligible to apply for funding in the following year. Awarded amounts may differ from the organization's proposed budget based on the scope of work and available funding. Organizations may charge up to 15% of modified total direct costs (MTDC) for indirect costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: November 23, 2025 at 11:59 p.m. EST for initial proposals; January 25, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EST for full applications
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations in Baltimore City working to address the opioid crisis through prevention, treatment, recovery, harm reduction, and social determinants of health initiatives
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports activities related to overdose prevention, treatment access, harm reduction, recovery support, and other community-led efforts in response to the opioid epidemic. Specifically, funds may be used for: (1) Programs, services, and supports that address substance use prevention, treatment, recovery, and harm reduction, including social determinants of health; (2) Infrastructure required for such programs and services; (3) Oversight, planning, assessing, and monitoring of programs; and (4) Evaluations of effectiveness and outcomes reporting. Unallowable uses include law enforcement-centered or carceral approaches, coercive or abstinence-only services, stigmatizing or discriminatory practices, capital campaigns or large-scale construction, fundraising costs, general organization overhead above 15% of the grant award, and services or supplies already funded through statewide settlements unless clearly distinct and non-duplicative.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Organizations must have an operating location in Baltimore City and demonstrate direct experience serving residents of Baltimore City. Proposed projects must address geographic areas disproportionately affected by overdose.
requirements_list: Organizations must be nonprofit entities (for-profit entities are ineligible)

Organizations applying for Tier 2 or Tier 3 must have 501(c)3 status; Tier 1 applicants must be community-based nonprofit organizations registered and in good standing with Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Organizations must be in good financial standing and have a valid Employer Identification Number (EIN)
Organizations must not have already received funding or have an earmark to receive funds in FY26 from Baltimore City's ORF
Organizations must not be named in Baltimore City Opioid Settlement Agreements or be quasi-City entities

Organizations must have proven experience in Baltimore City, including an operating location in Baltimore City and direct experience serving populations impacted by the opioid overdose crisis in existing programs
Organizations must have more than five years of proven experience serving identified populations in Baltimore City (for proposal scoring)
Organizations must align proposed projects with the Baltimore City Overdose Response Strategic Plan 2025-2027
Grantees must follow financial policies and compliance requirements outlined in the grant agreement, including monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting requirements
Projects must include performance measures aligned with standard ORF indicators provided in Appendix E
Proposals must address at least one of the identified priority areas and tiers
Organizations must be in good standing with the State of Maryland and the City of Baltimore
Grantees must maintain financial management systems to track fund usage and expenditures
Grantees must adhere to time allocation and staff certification requirements for personnel costs
All costs must be reasonable, allocable, necessary, and adequately documented
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process consists of five phases: (1) Proposal Phase (October 23 - November 23, 2025): Organizations submit concise proposals through the online portal addressing organizational eligibility, project overview, implementation plan, evaluation approach, and financial information. All proposals are screened by BCMOOR and MORP for completeness and eligibility. Eligible proposals are scored by a 5-member Restitution Advisory Board committee using scoring rubric in Appendix C. Proposals scoring at least 75 points advance to the application phase. (2) Full Application Phase (December 12, 2025 - January 25, 2026): Selected organizations submit detailed applications including project description, detailed budget with justification, workplan with goals and objectives, organizational risk assessment questionnaire, and performance measures. Applications are evaluated by a panel including RAB members, MORP, and BCMOOR staff. The RAB creates a ranked list within each tier for the Mayor's review. The Mayor's Overdose Cabinet and Mayor provide final executive approval. (3) Funding Phase: Upon executive approval, organizations execute grant agreements outlining terms, conditions, and disbursement procedures. (4) Administration Phase: Organizations implement projects and submit monthly, quarterly, and annual reports; comply with financial and programmatic requirements; participate in evaluation activities; and receive technical assistance. (5) Project Closing Phase: Upon completion or agreement conclusion, organizations reconcile all funds, resolve outstanding issues, return unused funding, file final reports, and retain records for audits. Proposal orientation sessions were held October 27-28, 2025. Application orientation sessions held December 16-17, 2025. Organizations can save and resume proposals and access a user guide for the online portal (Appendix G).

The project seeks to develop a minimum of 100 permanent supportive housing units across the Sleep Inn and Suites (300 N. Front Street), Holiday Inn Express (221 N. Gay Street), and parking lot (320 N. Front Street) with affordability levels up to 60% of area median income (AMI) and a 55-year binding affordability covenant.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding of $45,015,988 committed through competitive RFP process from American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) allocation. Awards support rehabilitation and operations of permanent supportive housing facilities converted from hotel properties. The selected respondent will receive the properties through a Land Disposition Agreement negotiated over 120 days following an Exclusive Negotiating Privilege (ENP). The City will transfer ownership of the Properties to the selected respondent by negotiating a purchase agreement for a nominal amount. The selected respondent is responsible for securing financing for rehabilitation, providing on-site supportive services and property management services, and securing sufficient, stable operating subsidies (such as Project Based Vouchers from Housing Authority of Baltimore City) to ensure that tenant rents do not exceed approximately 30% of adjusted household income. The project is eligible for an affordable housing Payments in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A funding program that provides grants to community partners and agencies for a variety of community development projects in the area around Pimlico Racetrack in Baltimore City. Funding is generated from state video lottery terminal revenue and is annually allocated by state statute to support infrastructure improvements, facilities, public safety, sanitation, economic and community development, housing, and other public services and improvements in neighborhoods near Pimlico Racetrack.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants available to support community development projects in neighborhoods near Pimlico Racetrack. Minimum funding request of $25,000 per project. Capital projects are generally disbursed on a reimbursement basis at project conclusion. Operating projects may be disbursed on a 40-40-20 schedule: 40% at project start, 40% at midway point contingent on successful progress, and 20% at completion upon submission of final report. The program is funded by state revenue generated by video lottery terminal funds (5.5% of gross VLT revenue) and is annually allocated by state statute. Of the local impact aid earmarked for the Pimlico area, 85% is allocated for the Park Heights Master Plan area, and 15% is allocated for neighborhoods in the One-Mile Radius. As of FY21, $2.4M or 24% of Pimlico Local Impact Aid (whichever is greater) is allocated directly to Park Heights Renaissance, Inc., and beginning in FY22, $3.5M was committed for annual debt service. Final funding decisions are made as part of the City budget approval process by the Mayor and City Council, with advice from the Pimlico Community Development Authority. The statute provides for Pimlico Local Impact Aid through fiscal year 2032.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review eligibility guidelines and program requirements. 2. Attend an optional information session (held in August) to learn about the application process and ask questions. 3. Complete the online project request form (JotForm) during the application period (typically August 18 - September 29). Form includes sections for: Organization and Project Background, Project Narrative, Goals and Activities, Budget and Timeline, Organization Financial Information, and optional Community Support Letters. 4. Submit complete application by the deadline at 11:59 PM EDT. 5. DOP conducts cure period and technical review of applications (September 26 - October 31). 6. PCDA reviews projects and meets for full-day project review and draft spending plan work session (typically November 15). 7. Preliminary Draft Spending Plan is published for 45-day public review and comment period (typically December 1 - January 15). 8. Public hearing on draft plan held for community comments (typically December 10). 9. PCDA conducts final work session to determine recommendations (typically January 13). 10. Final recommendations submitted to Mayor's Office (typically January 15). 11. Mayor's Office reviews recommendations and includes in City budget for City Council consideration (Spring). 12. Approved grantees enter into grant agreements and begin project implementation. Grantees must submit quarterly reports by specified deadlines (first Monday after the 5th of each quarter) and a final report within 60 days of project completion. Reports must include narrative updates, performance measure progress, and financial records with supporting documentation.

Applicants must choose no more than three of the seven B-CIITY Results to focus on
Applicants must match their chosen Results with at least two Indicators of Success

structured_extraction.program_description: A designated on-street parking space reserved for people with disabilities who have severe mobility limitations and lack accessible off-street parking options.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program assigns a designated parking space on the street in front of or near the applicant's home. The space must be for the applicant's personal use or the use of a person with impairment for whom the applicant is a caregiver, parent, or guardian. The Department of Transportation installs a sign to mark the space, which typically takes 4 to 6 weeks. Applicants agree that the zone will be removed if used for any other purpose, and the Parking Authority of Baltimore City retains the right to remove this zone at any time. Permits must be renewed annually during the month the permit was first obtained. Approval is subject to periodic review by the Parking Authority.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents with permanent disabilities that severely limit mobility who lack accessible off-street parking and cannot use public transportation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reserved on-street parking space for residents with severe mobility disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City residents only.
requirements_list: Have a permanent disability that severely limits mobility, certified by a licensed Maryland physician
The disability must be medically determinable (manifesting as laboratory findings or clinical signs, not symptoms alone)
Not have accessible off-street parking such as a driveway, garage, or parking pad on the property
Be unable to use any form of public transportation or rely on operating a personal vehicle as the sole means of transportation
Submit completed application form with all required information
Submit medical documentation from a licensed Maryland physician (examination must be within 6 months of application)
Medical documentation must establish a medically determinable impairment significantly impairing mobility
Obtain six signatures from homeowners on the applicant's block
Participate in a telephone interview or in-home interview
Property must be owner-occupied or applicant's principal place of residence
Application must be completely filled out, legibly, and not separated
Sign installation agreement agreeing that the zone will be removed if used for other purposes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the application form (available from the Parking Authority website or by calling 443-573-2800). 2. Submit the completed application along with medical documentation from a licensed Maryland physician to: The Parking Authority of Baltimore City, Reserved Residential Disabled Parking, 211 N. Paca Street, Baltimore, MD 21201. 3. A Parking Authority team member will contact the applicant to request additional paperwork, including six signatures from neighbors on the applicant's block. 4. Submit all required documents and medical evidence. 5. The applicant will be scheduled for a telephone interview or in-home interview. 6. Upon completion of the final review process, a determination will be made as to whether or not the applicant meets all criteria. If approved, the applicant will be assigned a parking space. 7. The Department of Transportation will install the sign within 4 to 6 weeks. 8. Permits must be renewed annually during the month the permit was first obtained. The applicant may be required to submit additional medical documentation to recertify continued eligibility at intervals as required by the Parking Authority.

structured_extraction.program_name: Ryan White Part A HIV/AIDS Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Ryan White Part A Program provides HIV-related medical and support services to people living with HIV who do not have sufficient health care coverage or financial resources. The program fills gaps in care not covered by insurance and serves more than 10,000 people each year across Baltimore City and six surrounding counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Part A funds provide core medical services including outpatient and ambulatory medical care, oral health, health insurance premium and cost-sharing assistance for low-income individuals, medical nutrition therapy, hospice services, mental health services, substance abuse outpatient care, and medical case management. Support services include outreach, medical transportation, substance abuse residential care, legal services, housing, psychosocial services, child care, and food bank services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People living with HIV who do not have sufficient health care coverage or financial resources for coping with HIV disease, with particular focus on individuals who know their HIV status but are not in care.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Core medical services (outpatient and ambulatory medical care, oral health, health insurance premiums and cost-sharing, medical nutrition therapy, hospice, mental health services, substance abuse outpatient care, medical case management) and support services (outreach, medical transportation, substance abuse residential care, legal services, housing, psychosocial services, child care, food bank services).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City and six surrounding counties: Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Carroll, Anne Arundel, and Queen Anne's.
requirements_list: Do not have sufficient health care coverage
Do not have sufficient financial resources for coping with HIV disease
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Baltimore EMA Planning Council sets service priorities and allocates Part A funds based on the needs of people living with or affected by HIV.

structured_extraction.program_name: SBA Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) - Francis Scott Key Bridge Collapse
structured_extraction.program_description: The U.S. Small Business Administration offers low-interest, long-term Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) to help small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small aquaculture businesses, and private nonprofit organizations recover from the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse on March 26, 2024. These loans provide funds to cover normal operating expenses including fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills that cannot be paid due to the disaster-related disruption. Eligibility is based solely on the financial impact of the disaster, not on actual property damage. Business Recovery Centers have been established in Baltimore City and Baltimore County to assist applicants with completing applications, submitting documents, and receiving status updates.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest, long-term Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDLs) of up to $2,000,000 for small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small aquaculture businesses, and private nonprofit organizations impacted by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse. Interest rates are fixed at 4% for small businesses and 3.25% for private nonprofit organizations, with loan terms up to 30 years. Interest does not accrue for the first 12 months from the date of first disbursement, and loan repayment begins 12 months from the date of first disbursement. Funds may be used to pay normal operating expenses such as fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills that cannot be paid because of the disruption. Applicants must demonstrate financial ability to repay and acceptable credit history. Collateral may be required. EIDLs cannot be used to refinance long-term debts. The actual loan amount is limited to the economic injury determined by SBA, less business interruption insurance and other recoveries. If a business is a major source of employment, SBA may waive the $2,000,000 statutory limit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small aquaculture businesses, and private nonprofit organizations impacted by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse on March 26, 2024, located in the State of Maryland and contiguous areas including the District of Columbia; Kent, New Castle, and Sussex in Delaware; Adams, Bedford, Chester, Fayette, Franklin, Fulton, Lancaster, Somerset, and York in Pennsylvania; Accomack, Independent City of Alexandria, Arlington, Fairfax, and Loudoun in Virginia; and Berkley, Grant, Hampshire, Jefferson, Mineral, Morgan, and Preston in West Virginia.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Normal operating expenses including fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills that cannot be paid because of the disaster-related disruption from the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse. EIDLs cannot be used to refinance long-term debts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The disaster declaration covers the entire State of Maryland including all 24 counties (Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester) and contiguous counties including the District of Columbia; Kent, New Castle, and Sussex in Delaware; Adams, Bedford, Chester, Fayette, Franklin, Fulton, Lancaster, Somerset, and York in Pennsylvania; Accomack, Independent City of Alexandria, Arlington, Fairfax, and Loudoun in Virginia; and Berkley, Grant, Hampshire, Jefferson, Mineral, Morgan, and Preston in West Virginia. Business Recovery Centers are located at CareFirst Engagement Center (1501 South Clinton Street, Baltimore, MD 21224) and Dundalk Renaissance Center (11 Center Place, Suite 201, Dundalk, MD 21222).
requirements_list: Must be a small business, small agricultural cooperative, small aquaculture business, or private nonprofit organization
Eligibility is based on the financial impact of the disaster only, not on actual property damage
Must demonstrate financial impact from the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse on March 26, 2024
Must demonstrate ability to repay the loan
Must have acceptable credit history
Applicants who have not complied with terms of previous SBA loans may not be eligible
Borrowers whose damaged or collateral property is located in a special flood hazard area must purchase and maintain flood insurance
Filing deadline is December 30, 2024
Must be restricted to small businesses without financial ability to offset the adverse impact without hardship
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants may apply online using the MySBA Loan Portal at https://lending.sba.gov or visit a Business Recovery Center to complete disaster loan applications, submit documents, or receive status updates. Business Recovery Centers are located at CareFirst Engagement Center (1501 South Clinton Street, Baltimore, MD 21224) and Dundalk Renaissance Center (11 Center Place, Suite 201, Dundalk, MD 21222). Both centers operate Monday–Friday 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. and Saturday 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. (closed Sundays). Centers opened April 1, 2024 with initial hours of 1 p.m. to 6 p.m. on the opening date. Applicants may also call the SBA Customer Service Center at (800) 659-2955, email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov, or dial 7-1-1 for telecommunications relay services for application assistance and more information on SBA disaster assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Sewage Onsite Support (SOS) Cleanup Program provides free cleaning, disinfection, and disposal services to Baltimore City residential customers whose properties have been damaged by sewage backups caused by capacity-related wet-weather events (heavy or sustained rain). Professional cleaning contractors remove health risks by cleaning, disinfecting, disposing of damaged materials, deodorizing, and drying affected areas at no cost to eligible residential customers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DPW contracts with third-party vendors and professional cleaning contractors to provide free services to eligible residential customers. Services include: disinfection and cleaning to eliminate dangerous viruses and bacteria; disposal and removal of soiled carpet, flooring, furniture, and other affected property; deodorization using professional-grade equipment and processes; and dehumidification and drying of affected areas. The cleaning contractor will contact the customer within approximately one hour of notification and offer appointments from 8 a.m. to midnight, seven days a week. Services are provided at no cost to the eligible customer. The City determines eligibility and deploys contractors directly to the property.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; customers encouraged to report as soon as sewage backup is discovered
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residential customers (property owners, tenants, or property managers) whose homes or properties have experienced sewage backup damage caused by capacity-related wet-weather events.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cleaning and disinfection of property damage caused by sewage backup from wet-weather events; removal and disposal of soiled materials including carpet, flooring, and furniture; deodorization using professional-grade equipment; and dehumidification and drying of affected areas. Customers may also contact the Baltimore City Law Department or use DPW's Expedited Reimbursement Program for Sewage Backups (up to $5,000 per home or apartment per event) for additional assistance with cleanup and disinfection costs or personal property damage claims.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Services are exclusively available to residential customers within Baltimore City. Both single-family and multi-family residential properties are eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City residential customer (homeowner, tenant, or property manager)
Property damage must be caused by a capacity-related wet-weather event (at least 1/4 inch of precipitation recorded within a 24-hour period that causes sewer lines to surcharge or overflow)
Sewage backup must not be caused by clogs from wet wipes, roots, fats, oils, grease (FOG), or maintenance-related issues; dry weather backups are not covered
Report to DPW must be made by calling 311 or visiting the 311 online services page as soon as the sewer backup is discovered
The City must determine that the damage was caused by a capacity-related wet-weather event
Cannot use both the SOS Cleanup Program and the Expedited Reimbursement Program for Sewage Backups—eligibility is limited to one or the other
Program does not cover water main breaks or stormwater seeping in from outside; only covers sewage water flooding from wet-weather events
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Report the sewage backup damage to DPW by calling 311 or visiting 311.baltimorecity.gov as soon as the backup is discovered. Step 2: DPW will send an inspector to determine the cause of the sewage backup and confirm it was caused by a capacity-related wet-weather event (at least 1/4 inch of precipitation within 24 hours). Step 3: Once confirmed, DPW will offer the SOS Cleanup Program and explain what services are included. Step 4: The on-call cleaning contractor will contact the customer within approximately one hour of notification about the affected address. Step 5: Cleaning appointments are scheduled based on customer availability, with contractors offering service from 8 a.m. to midnight, seven days a week. Step 6: Professional cleaning contractors perform the cleanup and disinfection at no cost. Step 7: Following completion, the contractor requests customer signature on a satisfaction/job completion form. Customers with concerns may call 410-396-3500.

Some properties are subject to annual ground rent that becomes the responsibility of the new owner after settlement. structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchased side lots may be used for gardens, landscaping, fencing, driveways, existing property expansion, or other permitted uses subject to Baltimore City zoning and code requirements.

Side yard properties must be physically contiguous to adjacent owner's principal residence
Side yard properties shall consist of no more than two lots incapable of independent development as determined by local zoning and code enforcement
Fixed pricing applies to lots up to 1,500 square feet; lots greater than 1,500 square feet subject to additional cost per square foot; maximum size 5,000 square feet
Applicant must have a record of responsible property ownership and management

The estimated timeline includes 30 days for review and award decision, 45 days for Board of Estimates approval, and 45 days for settlement, totaling approximately 120 days.
