structured_extraction.program_description: An overdose response program that provides overdose prevention education and dispenses naloxone (Narcan), a life-saving medication that reverses opioid overdoses, to Baltimore City residents free of charge. The program has trained over 155,000 residents and helped save more than 18,000 lives since 2015.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free naloxone kits are dispensed to residents at no charge. The program distributes two types of naloxone: nasal spray (administered by spraying 1/2 of the vial into each nostril) and Evzio auto-injector (administered by pressing against the outer thigh for 5 seconds). A second dose can be given if no response after about 3 minutes. The program also offers free overdose prevention education and training on how to administer naloxone, including live virtual training sessions and in-person training by request. Additional support includes referrals to substance use disorder treatment services through the Crisis Information and Referral Line.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents, friends, family members, and bystanders who want to learn how to prevent and respond to opioid overdoses. Priority populations include individuals recently released from jail, prison, rehab, detox, or the hospital.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Naloxone kits (nasal spray and Evzio auto-injector formulations) and medication for overdose prevention and reversal of opioid overdoses, as well as overdose prevention education and training on overdose recognition and naloxone administration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only.
requirements_list: Individuals must be Baltimore City residents or visitors to access free naloxone
No prior training required to receive naloxone kits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can obtain naloxone through multiple methods: (1) Request naloxone kits through an online form, (2) Register for virtual community naloxone training sessions through Eventbrite, (3) Submit a naloxone training request form for in-person training, or (4) Visit one of the Overdose Response Program or Syringe Service Program locations throughout Baltimore City to receive free naloxone via walk-in distribution. After using naloxone, individuals can call 443-615-7792 to receive a replacement free kit. For substance use disorder treatment assistance, call the Crisis Information and Referral Line at 410-433-5175. The Poison Center can be contacted at 1-888-222-1222 to report naloxone use.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Fee Credit Program for Single-Family Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: Single-family property owners in Baltimore City can receive a credit on their stormwater fee by installing and maintaining stormwater treatment practices such as trees, rain gardens, and rain barrels that treat runoff and decrease stormwater entering the City's drainage system, and by volunteering in hands-on community activities like clean-ups and tree plantings that provide water quality benefits. The program encourages residents to take an active role in managing stormwater runoff through both on-property best management practices and community stewardship activities.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners receive annual credits applied directly to their stormwater fee for installing and maintaining qualifying best management practices. Participation in volunteer water quality improvement events earns $10 credit per 4 hours of service (maximum $30 per year). Rain barrel systems (minimum 50 gallons) receive a one-time $25 credit. Small rain gardens (minimum 50 square feet) earn $8/year; large rain gardens (minimum 100 square feet) earn $16/year. Tree planting (minimum 2 trees, planted after 2010, 1+ inch diameter) earns $5/year per tree. Other residential best management practices are eligible for credits lasting three years. Credits are calculated based on the amount of impervious surface area treated and the reduction in stormwater runoff entering the City's drainage system.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - applications accepted throughout the year; renewal applications must be received within 30 days before the end of the credit period
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single-family property owners in Baltimore City who want to reduce their stormwater fees through installation of best management practices or participation in water quality improvement volunteer activities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credits reduce stormwater remediation fees for properties where owners install and maintain stormwater treatment practices (trees, rain gardens, rain barrels) or participate in organized volunteer activities (community clean-ups, tree plantings, de-paving) that reduce stormwater runoff and improve water quality. Credits are applied directly to monthly stormwater bills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Single-family residential properties must be located within Baltimore City to be eligible.
requirements_list: Property must be a single-family residential property located in Baltimore City
Complete and submit the Stormwater Fee Credit Application form

Install and maintain stormwater treatment practices such as rain gardens (minimum 50 sq ft for small, 100 sq ft for large), trees (minimum 2 trees, planted after 2010, 1+ inch diameter, conforming to City landscaping guidelines), or rain barrels (minimum 50 gallons with demonstrated proper installation and use for irrigation)

For participation credits: participate in organized volunteer events specifically certified by the City (trash clean-ups, tree planting, de-paving) and provide Stormwater Participation Event certificates
For best management practices: execute a simple right-of-entry agreement with the Department allowing inspections
Maintain all treatment practices in proper working condition; improper maintenance may result in credit rescission

Provide required documentation including photos of best management practices, sketches showing BMP location in relation to lot lines and other impervious areas, and certificates of event participation
Submit application materials to Customer Support and Services Division at 200 Holliday Street, Room 404, Baltimore, MD 21202 or publicworks@baltimorecity.gov
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Determine which credit type(s) apply to your property: participation in volunteer events, rain barrels, rain gardens, or tree planting. 2. Gather required documentation: for participation events, collect Stormwater Participation Event certificates from City-certified organizers; for best management practices, take photos of installations and prepare a sketch showing location relative to lot lines and impervious surfaces. 3. Complete the Single Family Property Stormwater Fee Credit Application form. 4. Submit the completed application with all required attachments to the Customer Support and Services Division at 200 Holliday Street, Room 404, Baltimore, MD 21202, or email to publicworks@baltimorecity.gov with subject line "STORMWATER CREDIT APPLICATION". 5. You will receive a letter confirming receipt and indicating the application is under review. 6. The Department will review and make a decision within 30 days of receiving a complete application package. 7. After review, you will receive a decision letter. 8. If approved, the credit will be applied to your subsequent monthly water bills. Note: You remain obligated to pay the full stormwater fee during the review period. For credit renewal, submit a new application before the credit period expires (typically 1-3 years depending on credit type). Credits must be renewed to remain active.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Fee Credit and Reduction Program for Non-Single-Family Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing credits and fee reductions on stormwater fees for businesses, churches, non-profits, and industries in Baltimore City who install stormwater best management practices, maintain green spaces, obtain relevant permits, or maintain private stormwater infrastructure. Eligible parties can reduce their stormwater fees by meeting various stormwater treatment practice requirements, including having lots with minimal impervious area, participating in small developments, holding NPDES permits, maintaining private storm drains, or maintaining cemetery streets open to the public.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Non-single-family property owners receive credits or reductions on their stormwater fees based on qualifying actions. The base stormwater fee is calculated at $6.50 per Equivalent Residential Unit (ERU) per month, where 1 ERU equals 1,050 square feet of impervious area. Available credits include: Green Space Credit (45% reduction for parcels with less than 50 square feet of impervious area, valid for 3 years); Small Development Credit (33% reduction for parcels with 50-820 square feet of impervious area, valid for 3 years); Treatment Practice Credit (up to 45% reduction for structural/environmental site design BMPs or activity-based BMPs, valid for 1-3 years); NPDES Industrial Permit Credit (55% reduction, valid for 5 years); Harbor Discharger Credit (up to 30% reduction for properties draining directly to Baltimore Harbor, valid for 5 years); Religious Structure Special Fee ($1/ERU/month for religious structures used exclusively for worship or K-12 education); and Maximum Fee Cap (20% of real property taxes for properties with annual stormwater fees exceeding $1,000). Total credits cannot exceed 100% of base fee. Certain credits can be combined according to specified eligibility matrix.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing - applications accepted at any time; credit renewal applications must be received within 30 days before end of credit period
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, churches, non-profits, and industries located in Baltimore City with non-single-family properties; includes commercial, industrial, and religious organizations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credits and fee reductions applied to stormwater fees for qualifying properties. Eligible uses include stormwater treatment practices and infrastructure that reduce stormwater runoff and pollution, maintaining green spaces with minimal impervious area, obtaining and maintaining NPDES Industrial Stormwater Discharge Permits, maintaining private stormwater infrastructure that drains directly to Baltimore Harbor, maintaining cemetery streets that are privately maintained and open to the public, and implementing environmental site design best management practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only
requirements_list: Install and maintain stormwater best management practices (BMPs) approved by Maryland Department of Environment (MDE)
Maintain lots with less than 50 square feet of non-absorbent/impervious area (Green Space Credit)
Own and maintain small developments or lots with 50 to 820 square feet of non-absorbent/impervious area (Small Development Credit)
Hold a National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Industrial Stormwater Discharge Permit or have MDE exemption certification for no exposure condition
Own and maintain private storm drains that discharge directly to Baltimore Harbor with documented site drawing showing drainage areas, flow patterns, and structural outfalls
Maintain cemetery streets that are privately maintained and open to the public
Religious structures must be exempt from State or City property tax, used exclusively for places of worship or K-12 education, and not enrolled in alternative compliance plan

For hardship exemption: must be 501(c)(3) or (d) tax-exempt charitable/nonprofit organization; annual stormwater fee must exceed 0.75% of total annual revenue; total annual revenue must not exceed $1,000,000; must own property or have current landlord/tenant lease agreement; must submit written alternative compliance plan to Department; must implement approved plan within one year; must re-certify eligibility annually
Properties seeking credits must submit completed application with supporting documentation including photos, site drawings, permits, maintenance records, or other verification materials
For treatment practice credits, property owner or designated representative must execute inspection and maintenance agreement granting Department access for regular inspections
BMP must be in same 8-digit watershed as property for off-site treatment credit eligibility
Customers must maintain active credit status and submit renewal applications within 30 days before end of credit period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download application and guidance document from PublicWorks.BaltimoreCity.gov or obtain at Abel Wolman Municipal Building. 2. Complete application form and gather supporting documentation appropriate to credit type (photos, site drawings, surveys, permits, maintenance records, proof of ownership/tax exemption status, etc.). 3. Submit application and materials to Bureau of Water and Wastewater either by mail to Abel Wolman Municipal Building, 200 Holliday Street, Room 404, Baltimore, MD 21202, Attn: Customer Support and Services Division, or by email to publicworks@baltimorecity.gov (include 'STORMWATER CREDIT APPLICATION' in subject line). 4. Customer receives letter confirming receipt and that application is under review. 5. Department reviews complete application and decides within 30 days. Participation, simple residential treatment practices, small development, and other simple credits may be processed faster. 6. Customer receives decision letter with application outcome. If approved, credit is applied to subsequent monthly water bills; if retroactive application applies (delay in 30-day review), credit will be applied retroactively. 7. For denied applications, customer may submit written appeal within 30 days to Bureau of Water and Wastewater with basis of appeal and supporting evidence. Director of Public Works makes final Department decision on appeals. 8. Credits require renewal according to type-specific approval periods using same application form; renewal applications must be submitted within 30 days before end of credit period to be reflected on subsequent bill. 9. Note: Customers remain obligated to pay full fee during credit application review period.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Fee Reduction for Faith Organizations
structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing stormwater fee reductions for places of worship and schools operated by faith organizations in Baltimore City. Faith organizations can receive a stormwater fee reduction based on their participation in stormwater management practices. Religious structures that are not subject to State or City property tax and are used exclusively for places of worship or K-12 education receive a special reduced fee of $1/ERU/month.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Faith organizations receive a reduction on their stormwater fees for their places of worship and schools based on their participation in stormwater management practices. The primary reduction available is the Religious Structure Special Fee, which caps fees at $1/ERU/month for structures belonging to religious non-profits that are not subject to State or City property tax, are used exclusively for places of worship or K-12 education, and are not enrolled in an alternative compliance plan. Additional credits may be available for treatment practices, green space, small development, and participation in public water quality improvement projects. The impervious area that receives the religious structure special fee is not eligible for additional credits, though other impervious area on the property may qualify. Reductions are applied to monthly water bills.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis; no specific deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Faith organizations in Baltimore City that operate places of worship and schools, including religious non-profits exempt from taxation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fee reductions applied to stormwater fees for qualifying faith-based facilities (places of worship and schools). Reductions based on stormwater management practices implemented on the property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Properties must be located within Baltimore City limits.
requirements_list: Be a faith organization operating a place of worship or school in Baltimore City
Organization must be a non-profit exempt from taxation under IRC Section 501(c)(3) or (d) for hardship exemptions, or IRC Section 501(c)(4) or (19) for veterans organizations
Property must be a place of worship or school used exclusively for these purposes
Structures must not be subject to State or City property tax
Provide proof of tax-exempt (religious) status certification
Provide a map of the property identifying structures eligible for the discounted rate
Maintain stormwater management practices on the property
For treatment practice credits, execute an inspection and maintenance agreement allowing Department access for regular inspections
Renew credit application before the end of each credit period to maintain active status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain application form from PublicWorks.BaltimoreCity.gov or the Abel Wolman Municipal Building (200 Holliday Street, Room 404), or by calling (410) 396-5398. 2. Complete the application form and gather supporting documentation including proof of tax-exempt status, property map identifying eligible structures, and photos/documentation of stormwater management practices as applicable. 3. Submit completed application and supporting materials to the Bureau of Water and Wastewater either by mail to 200 Holliday Street, Room 404, Baltimore, MD 21202, or by email to publicworks@baltimorecity.gov (include "STORMWATER CREDIT APPLICATION" in subject line). 4. Applicant will receive a letter confirming receipt of application materials. 5. Department reviews application within 30 days of receipt of complete application package. 6. Department sends decision letter with application outcome. 7. If approved, reduction is applied to subsequent monthly water bills. 8. Credits must be renewed before the end of each credit period using the same application form with updated documentation. Note: Customer remains obligated to pay full fee during application review period.

structured_extraction.program_description: A school-based violence prevention program that addresses teen dating violence and youth violence through evidence-based interventions. The program works with 9th graders in schools located in or adjacent to Safe Streets Outposts to promote healthy relationships, non-violent conflict resolution, and reduce violence and dating violence victimization and perpetration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides training and technical assistance through multiple components including Safe Dates (a 10-session program promoting healthy relationships), Safe Streets conflict resolution and violence interruption services, school-wide awareness events, and after-school clubs. A multi-sector advisory committee guides system-level efforts and helps plan for sustainability. Participants and families also receive resources and referrals to local support services including House Of Ruth Maryland, TurnAround Inc., and national resources such as Love is Respect, Choose Respect, Break the Cycle, and The Trevor Project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 9th grade students in schools located in or adjacent to Safe Streets Outposts, schools and community partners, youth, and parents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program components include multi-sector advisory committee coordination, Safe Dates curriculum implementation, Safe Streets conflict resolution and violence interruption services, school-wide awareness events, and after-school clubs focused on violence prevention and healthy relationships. Funds support evidence-based interventions promoting healthy relationships and non-violent conflict resolution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: 9th graders in schools located in or adjacent to Safe Streets Outposts in Baltimore City

structured_extraction.program_description: No-cost or low-cost vaccination clinics that provide immunizations to children, adolescents, and adults who qualify, including services for flu, COVID-19, pneumonia, and RSV.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Baltimore City Health Department provides vaccines at no cost. Vaccine administration fees are set by the Maryland Department of Health. The department offers a sliding scale discount on vaccine administration fees based on household size and income. Those unable to pay are not denied services. Clinics operate Monday through Thursday from 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM at the BCHD Eastern Health District location (1200 E Fayette St, Baltimore 21202), with regular schedule published monthly.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Baltimore City Health Department Immunization Program
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and adolescents 18 years old and younger who have no medical insurance, have or are eligible for Medicaid or Maryland's HealthChoice or Maryland's Children's Health Program, or are American Indian or Alaska Native. Adults 19 years old and older who have no medical insurance or are under-insured.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vaccinations against vaccine-preventable diseases including flu, COVID-19, pneumonia, and RSV. Blood lead testing services also available.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City - BCHD Eastern Health District location at 1200 E Fayette St, Baltimore 21202
requirements_list: For children and adolescents (18 years old and younger): must have no medical insurance, have or be eligible for Medicaid or Maryland's HealthChoice or Maryland's Children's Health Program, or be American Indian or Alaska Native.
For adults (19 years old and older): must have no medical insurance or be under-insured (medical insurance does not fully cover the cost of vaccinations).
Bring all shot records to appointment.
Bring medical insurance card, if available.
Appointments required - walk-ins not accepted (except adult walk-ins on Fridays).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-396-4454 to schedule an appointment, Monday through Friday 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM. Alternatively, register and schedule appointments online through CDC's VAMS portal at https://vams.cdc.gov/vaccineportal/s/landingpage?language=en_US by proceeding as a guest. Clients can schedule appointments in advance or pre-register without scheduling. Appointments are held Monday through Thursday from 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM at BCHD Eastern Health District (1200 E Fayette St, Baltimore 21202). Friday adult walk-ins are also accepted. Bring all vaccination records and insurance card (if applicable) to appointment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A financial instrument used by Baltimore City to fund development projects within designated TIF districts. Investment in these areas is expected to raise property values, and the increase in property tax revenue generated by the development is set aside to repay the bonds. Once the TIF debt is repaid, the district is dissolved and increased property tax revenue goes to the City's general fund. The program supports various redevelopment initiatives including mixed-income housing, commercial development, infrastructure improvements, and neighborhood revitalization.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax increment financing bonds fund development projects within designated TIF districts in Baltimore City. The increase in property tax revenue generated by development within the district is set aside to repay the bonds issued. Bond proceeds support hard construction costs for restoring vacant properties as homeownership and rental housing, construction of new commercial and office spaces, infrastructure improvements including schools, parks, roads, and public improvements. Once TIF debt is repaid, the district is dissolved and taxes from increased property valuations go to the City's general fund. Bond amounts vary by project; recent TIF districts authorized include approximately $105-150 million in bond issuance.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Stacy Freed; Alice Kennedy, Housing Commissioner; Kate Edwards, Deputy Commissioner for Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers, non-profit organizations, and public agencies seeking to fund major redevelopment projects, mixed-income housing developments, commercial development, and infrastructure improvements in designated TIF districts in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hard construction costs for vacant property restoration and new homeownership and rental housing for households earning up to 115% of area median income (AMI); new commercial and office spaces; public infrastructure including schools, parks, roads, utilities, and related improvements; neighborhood revitalization and community development projects; mixed-use developments with retail and residential components
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated TIF districts in Baltimore City. Current active districts include: Center/West at Poppleton (established May 5, 2015); Perkins Somerset Oldtown Neighborhoods (established June 11, 2018); and Vacancy Reduction and Affordable Housing TIF District citywide (established June 4, 2024, includes 4,285 properties in 126 neighborhoods, with 1,625 properties in Impact Investment Areas). TIF districts are located in areas with high vacancy rates, significant development potential, proximity to transit, employment centers, and anchor institutions.
requirements_list: Developer or applicant must submit a comprehensive TIF application to the Baltimore City Board of Finance
Application must include detailed project description and development team information
Application must identify the specific TIF district or area to be covered by the TIF
Application must include estimates on future property value increases and property tax revenue generation
Application must demonstrate private sector contribution to the project
Application must show project advances the City's land use, economic development and public improvement goals
Application must pass the but-for test demonstrating TIF financing is necessary for project feasibility
Application must demonstrate positive net fiscal impact to the City
Application must include project sources and uses analysis
Application must address risk to the City and fiscal impact analysis
Project must generate sufficient tax increment to repay the bonds
For housing projects: units must be priced for households earning up to 115% AMI or include affordable/deeply affordable components as specified
Projects should leverage additional private and public funds to achieve whole block outcomes
Developer must have demonstrated experience with comparable scale, scope, and complexity projects
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The TIF application process follows a multi-step Board of Finance policy. Step 1: Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) or sponsoring agency prepares the TIF application including detailed project information, fiscal analysis, and developer qualifications. Step 2: Application is presented to the Baltimore City Board of Finance for concept approval. The Board confirms the proposed TIF is consistent with City TIF policies. If concept approval is granted, Finance proceeds with drafting TIF legislation and bond issuance documents. Subsequent Board approvals are required for TIF legislation, bond authorization, and debt issuance. The application must be submitted by a City department or agency and include comprehensive documentation of project feasibility, financial projections, and public benefits.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps homeowners and property owners in Baltimore City avoid having their property sold in a tax sale by deferring the sale for one year. Successful applicants have their properties removed from the tax sale in the year they apply, giving them time to address unpaid property taxes and charges without losing their property to public auction.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program defers a property tax sale for one year, removing eligible properties from the tax sale list in the year they apply. This allows property owners time to pay unpaid property taxes and charges without losing their property to public auction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City homeowners and property owners with unpaid property taxes and charges who are facing a tax sale.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax sale deferral and property tax relief; allows property owners to defer tax sale proceedings for one year to address unpaid property tax obligations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only.
requirements_list: Property owner must be eligible based on criteria determined by the Departments of Finance and Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application by the deadline. Property owners should check their eligibility through the program's eligibility checker on the Baltimore City website. Free legal help is available through Tax Sale Clinics.

structured_extraction.program_description: A multi-agency task force committed to reducing unintended teen pregnancies in Baltimore City by providing age-appropriate sexual health education, access to effective family planning and youth-friendly clinical services, and community support to help adolescents and young adults make informed sexual health decisions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The initiative provides training to healthcare providers and clinics in the provision of safe, long-acting, and reversible contraceptives (LARCs) for teens and client-centered, youth-friendly care. It offers peer health advocacy training for youth council members. Community agencies receive free pregnancy prevention materials and access to collaborative planning and implementation support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adolescents and young adults ages 13-24 in Baltimore City, particularly African American and Hispanic youth; parents of pre-teens and adolescents; young males ages 15-20; foster care youth; pregnant and parenting teens; healthcare providers; community-based organizations; and agencies committed to reducing teen pregnancy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting strategic direction and planning for teen pregnancy prevention activities; training healthcare providers in LARC provision and youth-friendly care; conducting research and annual LARC roundtables; peer health advocacy; youth leadership development; social marketing and community outreach campaigns; home visiting for pregnant and parenting teens.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To join the coalition or participate, interested parties should contact Cassandra Davis at Cassandra.davis@baltimorecity.gov or call 410-396-1849. Young people can be encouraged to join the Youth Advisory Council through the same contact. Free pregnancy prevention materials are available upon request.

structured_extraction.program_description: Train Up provides unemployed and underemployed Baltimore City residents with free job training and skills essential to Baltimore's growing industries. Training is delivered by trusted community organizations located throughout Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Train Up provides free job training and skills development through community organizations located throughout Baltimore City. The program is designed to help unemployed and underemployed residents gain skills needed for Baltimore's growing industries.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unemployed and underemployed Baltimore City residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training and skills development for growing industries
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Must be unemployed or underemployed
Must be a Baltimore City resident
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Train Up form online.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tree distribution program that provides free trees to residents in designated Healthy Neighborhoods and half-price trees ($10) to residents in all other neighborhoods for planting on their lawns and yards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free trees for residents in designated Healthy Neighborhoods, or half-price trees ($10 per tree) for residents in all other Baltimore City neighborhoods. Minimum order of ten trees required to qualify for free delivery to a central neighborhood location. A neighborhood representative collects individual tree requests and submits them together on the TreeNeighborhood Group Order Form. Orders must be submitted by November for fall planting or April for spring planting. TreeBaltimore delivers trees to a central neighborhood location where residents can organize a planting party.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: November for fall plantings or April for spring plantings
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Baltimore City, including individuals, schools, businesses, and hospitals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Trees for planting on residential lawns and yards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Free trees available to residents of 18 designated Healthy Neighborhoods (Belair-Edison, Brooklyn and Curtis Bay, Charles Village, Coldstream/Homestead/Montebello, Coppin Heights, Cylburn and Levindale, Ednor Gardens-Lakeside, Edmondson Village, GarwynOaks/Hanlon/HowardPark, Glen, Greater Lauraville, Highlandtown and Bayview, Midtown, Mondawmin, Patterson Park, Remington, Reservoir Hill, and Waverly). Half-price trees available to residents of all other Baltimore City neighborhoods.
requirements_list: Neighborhood must order a minimum of ten trees to qualify for free delivery
One payment per neighborhood
A neighborhood representative must coordinate orders
Trees are for planting on residential lawns and yards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A neighborhood representative collects tree requests from residents using the individual order form. Orders are submitted together on the TreeNeighborhood Order Form (Group Order Form) to TreeBaltimore by November for fall planting or April for spring planting. TreeBaltimore delivers trees to a central neighborhood location, where residents can organize a planting party. Individual residents submit requests to the neighborhood representative, who aggregates and submits all requests as a single group order.

structured_extraction.program_description: An in-school job training program for high school juniors and seniors that provides internships and professional development to prepare young people for employment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers internships and professional development training to high school juniors and seniors to prepare them for careers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school juniors and seniors in Baltimore City aged 17-24
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job skills training, professional development, and internship placements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Must be a high school junior or senior
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program partner directly for enrollment information.

structured_extraction.program_description: An out-of-school job training program for young adults aged 18-24 that provides an 8-week internship at Sinai Hospital with training in patient transportation, environmental services, and dietary services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides an 8-week paid internship at Sinai Hospital with training in patient transportation, environmental services (EVS) technician roles, dietary and food service, and other areas based on participant interest.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young adults aged 18-24 who are Baltimore City residents with a high school diploma or GED
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid internship and on-the-job training in hospital patient services, environmental services, and dietary services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City resident
Must be aged 18-24
Must have a high school diploma or GED
Must be able to pass a drug and alcohol screening
Must pass a required background check
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program coordinator directly for enrollment information.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides financial assistance to homebuyers purchasing vacant properties that have been renovated or fixed up, helping to revitalize Baltimore neighborhoods by encouraging people to buy and occupy previously vacant homes. The $10,000 incentive is provided as a five-year forgivable loan to eligible buyers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $10,000 incentive provided as a five-year forgivable loan to help homebuyers purchase and renovate vacant properties in Baltimore City. The property must have been subject to a Vacant Building Notice for at least one year prior to rehabilitation by a developer or sale to a homebuyer who intends to renovate the property using an acquisition/rehabilitation loan. All incentives require a minimum $1,000 investment from the homebuyer's own funds towards the purchase of the property.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Funding is planned each year based on the City's fiscal calendar (July 1 to June 30). Incentives are given out on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homebuyers interested in purchasing and renovating vacant properties in Baltimore City that have been subject to a Vacant Building Notice for at least one year.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The assistance can be used to help with the costs of buying and fixing up vacant homes that meet the program criteria.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: This program is available to homebuyers purchasing vacant property in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Property must have been subject to a Vacant Building Notice for at least one year prior to rehabilitation or sale
Homebuyer must intend to renovate the property using an acquisition/rehabilitation loan or the property must have been rehabilitated by a developer
Must complete a homeownership class from a City-approved homeownership counseling agency within one year before writing an offer on a home
Must contribute at least $1,000 of your own money towards the house purchase
Settlement date must be at least 30 days after submitting application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register your account and submit an application through the Applicant Portal at https://portal.neighborlysoftware.com/baltimoremd/Participant by clicking the Register link and creating a user name (email address) and password. Include required documentation with your application. Allow at least 30 days between application submission and settlement date for processing. Checks typically take 10 to 15 business days to be sent after approval. For assistance, contact DHCD.Homeownership@baltimorecity.gov or call (410) 396-3124.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that works with communities and grocery stores to help older adults living in senior and disabled housing access healthy foods. The program teaches Baltimore residents online grocery shopping and community organizing skills. Neighborhood Food Advocates, who are trained community members, help generate community-driven approaches to increase food access.
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides training in online grocery shopping and community organizing skills to older adults living in senior and disabled housing. Neighborhood Food Advocates provide education and support to help residents access healthy foods.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults living in senior and disabled housing in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program facilitates access to healthy foods through education and community organizing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City, with focus on senior and disabled housing communities

structured_extraction.program_description: Vision for Baltimore is a citywide program offering free vision screening, eye exams, and eyeglasses to elementary and middle school students in Baltimore City Public Schools. The program screens students in pre-kindergarten through 8th grade, provides comprehensive eye exams to those who fail screening with parental consent, and furnishes free eyeglasses manufactured by Warby Parker. All services are provided at no cost regardless of ability to pay.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Vision for Baltimore provides free vision screenings to all enrolled pre-K through 8th grade students in participating Baltimore City Public Schools. Students who fail screening receive free comprehensive eye exams in a mobile vision clinic operated by Vision To Learn. Students needing glasses select frames in the mobile clinic, and Warby Parker manufactures and delivers the eyeglasses to students at their schools at no cost. Parents pay nothing. If a student is enrolled in Medicaid, the Medicaid provider may be billed for the eye exam only; glasses remain free.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Elementary and middle school students (pre-K through 8th grade) enrolled in Baltimore City Public Schools, particularly those who need vision correction but face barriers to obtaining eyeglasses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free vision screenings, comprehensive eye exams, and eyeglasses including frames and lenses. Services focus on identifying and correcting refractive errors and visual acuity problems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program serves select Baltimore City Public Schools. In Year 4 (2019-2020), approximately 45 schools across Baltimore City are served each year. The program cycles through schools, serving one-third of elementary and middle schools per year.
requirements_list: Student must be enrolled in a Baltimore City Public School
Student must be in pre-K through 8th grade
Student must attend a school selected for Vision for Baltimore services that year
Parent or guardian must sign a universal consent form indicating yes or no for participation
Student must fail the BCHD vision screening to be eligible for eye exam and glasses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No registration or application is required. All pre-K through 8th grade students in participating schools are screened automatically. Vision screenings are administered by Baltimore City Health Department during the school day and take approximately 30 minutes per student. Schools are served approximately 4 to 10 days depending on school size. Students who do not pass screening receive a consent form to take home. Parents sign and return the form indicating yes or no for follow-up exam and glasses. Several weeks to months after screening, Vision To Learn's mobile clinic visits the school to provide eye exams (approximately 30 minutes per student) and glasses fittings (approximately 20 minutes). Glasses are delivered to the school several weeks after the exam, and students are called to pick them up and have them fitted by an optician.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows property owners to request a reduction in their water or sewer bill if they used more water than usual due to a leak or a problem with a toilet or appliance. The program provides bill adjustments for interior leaks, situational usage increases, and underground leaks that have been repaired by a licensed plumber.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reduces water or sewer bills for customers who experienced higher-than-normal usage due to leaks or appliance problems. For interior or situational usage adjustments, the program subtracts 50 percent of the extra water used from the amount owed (or 100 percent for senior or hardship customers). For underground leaks, the program removes all extra water charges and adjusts sewer charges accordingly. Customers will only be granted one underground leak adjustment at a property every two years, and only one interior or situational usage adjustment at a property every three years. The adjustment appears on the customer's bill approximately 4 weeks after the request is approved. This form is not a guarantee that a credit will be applied to your utility bill. Customers will be notified by phone or letter if the request cannot be granted or if additional information is needed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within sixty (60) days of the bill being issued
structured_extraction.contact_name: DPW Customer Support and Services Division
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners or authorized representatives in Baltimore City who have experienced unusual water usage due to leaks or appliance problems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The assistance reduces water and sewer bills for customers who used more water than usual because of a leak inside the home, a problem with a toilet or appliance, or an underground leak that was professionally repaired.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only.
requirements_list: The property owner or an authorized person designated by the property owner must request the adjustment within sixty (60) days of the bill being issued.
Water loss due to theft or vandalism is not covered and is the customer's responsibility.
Customers may only be granted an underground leak adjustment at a property once every two years.
Customers may only be granted an interior or situational usage adjustment at a property once every three years.
For underground leaks, the date, type of repair, and proof of repair from a licensed plumber must be included.
Necessary repairs must be completed prior to submitting the form. Adjustments to the water or sewer portion of the bill cannot be made until repairs have been completed.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Customers can fill out the adjustment request form online or print it and mail it to DPW Customer Support and Services Division at 200 Holliday Street, First Floor, Room 8, Baltimore, MD 21202. The form must be submitted within sixty days of the bill being issued. If approved, the adjustment will appear on the customer's bill in about 4 weeks. Customers will be notified by phone or letter if the request cannot be granted or if additional information is needed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Water4All Program (Department of Public Works Water Bill Discount Programs)
structured_extraction.program_description: A water discount program administered by Baltimore City's Department of Public Works that helps Baltimore City residents who qualify get assistance paying their water and sewer bills. The program provides discounted water rates to eligible residents to help reduce household water expenses, and also screens homeowners for eligibility for additional available benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides discounted water and sewer rates to eligible Baltimore City residents to help reduce water and sewer bill expenses. The programs also screen homeowners for eligibility for other available benefits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents who have difficulty paying their water and sewer bills and potential financial need, including homeowners who may be eligible for additional benefits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces water and sewer bill expenses for eligible residents and homeowners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Homeowners and residents can visit the Affordability Portal or the Water4All program page at cityservices.baltimorecity.gov/water4all/ to explore available plans, apply, be screened for additional benefits, or find the closest office. Residents can also call 410-545-0900 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The WIC Program provides free nutritious foods, nutrition education, health screenings, and breastfeeding support to pregnant women, new mothers, infants, and children under 5 years old who meet income and nutritional need requirements. Benefits include food vouchers/eWIC card for healthy food purchases, nutrition education and counseling, growth and weight assessments, breastfeeding assistance from lactation specialists, referrals to health and social agencies, and participation in the annual WIC Farmers' Market Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive healthy foods at no cost on an eWIC card, nutrition education and counseling, health screenings including growth and weight assessments, breastfeeding assistance from lactation specialists, referrals to other health and social agencies, and participation in the annual WIC Farmers' Market Program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant women, new mothers, infants, and children under 5 years old who live in Maryland and have a nutritional need.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of healthy foods through an eWIC card; nutrition education and counseling; health screenings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must live in Maryland. Services are provided through Baltimore City WIC clinic locations.
requirements_list: Live in Maryland
Be pregnant or a new mother with an infant or child under 5 years of age
Have a nutritional need
Meet income eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the WIC appointment line at 410-396-9427 to schedule an appointment at a clinic location convenient to you. Bilingual staff and translators are available. For more information on how to prepare for your appointment, visit the Maryland WIC website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) Job Training for Youth
structured_extraction.program_description: A job training program that supports Baltimore City young people by connecting out-of-school individuals ages 18–24 and in-school seniors with opportunities to build their future careers. Participants can explore career pathways, gain occupational skills, and earn industry-recognized credentials through partnerships with training providers and community organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Job training and career pathway exploration connecting participants with training providers and community organizations to develop occupational skills and earn industry-recognized credentials.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Out-of-school individuals ages 18–24 and in-school seniors in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career exploration, skills training, and industry credential attainment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Must be ages 18–24 (out-of-school) or a current high school senior (in-school)

structured_extraction.program_description: A pre-apprenticeship and mentoring program offered in partnership with the Baltimore City Department of Public Works. The program provides Baltimore City residents ages 18–24 with hands-on training, mentorship, and workplace readiness skill development in the water and wastewater industry, as well as solid waste and information technology sections. It educates participants about water industry careers and develops a pipeline of skilled workers for entry-level positions in public works. Past graduates have attained positions such as Laborers, Community Aides, Operations Technician Apprentices, and Customer Care Analysts within the Department of Public Works.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides pre-apprenticeship training, career mentoring, and workplace readiness skill development to prepare participants for full-time employment in public works positions, including water, solid waste, and information technology sections. Past graduates have attained positions such as Laborers, Community Aides, Operations Technician Apprentices, and Customer Care Analysts within the Department of Public Works.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents ages 18–24 who have a high school diploma or GED, are unemployed or underemployed, and are not currently enrolled in a job training program or post-secondary education
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-apprenticeship training and career mentoring in water, solid waste, and information technology public works careers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City resident
Must be ages 18–24
Must have a high school diploma or GED
Must be unemployed or underemployed
Must not be currently enrolled in a job training program or post-secondary education
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals can visit the YH2O program website to submit an application and find more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: An in-school job training program for high school seniors at participating schools that provides professional development and internship opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers professional development and internships to high school seniors at participating schools (N.A.F, Douglass, A.C.C.E, Patterson) to prepare them for careers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school seniors at participating schools (N.A.F, Douglass, A.C.C.E, Patterson) in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development and internship placements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Must be a high school senior at a participating school (N.A.F, Douglass, A.C.C.E, or Patterson)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program coordinator directly for enrollment information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A support program designed for young adults ages 18–24 to explore their next steps toward education, employment, and career growth. Services include guidance on continuing education, GED preparation, job training, and employment connections. Services are available through a West Baltimore location and hub-based services at the Eastside Career Center.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Guidance, resources, and skill-building services to support young adults in education planning, GED preparation, job training, and employment connections at physical service centers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young adults ages 18–24 in Baltimore City seeking education, employment, or career guidance
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education, GED preparation, job training, and employment readiness services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City (West Baltimore location and Eastside Career Center)
requirements_list: Must be ages 18–24

structured_extraction.program_description: A summer employment program for Baltimore City youth that provides paid work experience, skills training, and employment opportunities. The program connects young people ages 14–21 with up to 6,600 paid summer positions with private, nonprofit, and city and state government employers across Baltimore City. Participants earn income while gaining workforce skills, career preparation, and hands-on work experience.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 6,600 paid work positions offered to young people ages 14–21, placed with private, nonprofit, and government employers. Participants earn wages while gaining workforce skills, career preparation, and hands-on work experience through summer employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents ages 14–21 seeking summer employment, skills training, and career development opportunities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wages for summer work experience, job training, and career preparation opportunities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only
requirements_list: Must be ages 14–21
Must be a Baltimore City resident
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Young people can apply through the YouthWorks website at youthworks.oedworks.com or visit the Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Employment Development website. Contact 311 for additional information on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded, congregate nutrition program established under the Older Americans Act in 1972. The program promotes health, reduces isolation, and provides nutritious meals in a social dining setting to seniors and their spouses. Operated in both Baltimore City and Baltimore County, participants enjoy meals at senior centers, community buildings, senior residences, and dedicated dining sites in a friendly atmosphere with opportunities to make friends, attend educational events, and participate in various activities. Nutrition education is also provided throughout the year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: In Baltimore City, the program provides free nutritious meals at more than 50 congregate dining sites. There is no fee to join or receive meals, though voluntary donations are suggested at $1.25 for regular meals and $2.00 for kosher meals. Meal options include regular, Kosher, and Korean. Participants swipe a membership card to attend meals. In Baltimore County, meals are provided at senior centers and nutrition sites with a voluntary, anonymous contribution requested — minimum $4 for regular meals and $5 for Kosher and Halal meals. Full meal costs range from $6.20 to $12.68 depending on meal type. Participants under 60 in Baltimore County must pay the full cost of the meal. Both programs offer free nutrition education throughout the year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors aged 60 years or older, their spouses regardless of age, and disabled persons younger than 60 years who reside in a residential building where an Eating Together meal program is in operation (Baltimore City). Baltimore County seniors aged 60 and over and their spouses of any age are also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants receive nutritious meals meeting one-third of daily recommended nutritional needs, including regular, box, super special, Kosher, Halal, and Korean meal options at select sites. Additional benefits include access to education seminars, health programs, volunteer opportunities, trips, speakers, group activities, special events, holiday celebrations, craft activities, parties, games, and entertainment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Baltimore City at more than 50 Eating Together sites, and throughout Baltimore County at multiple senior centers, community buildings, and senior residences.
requirements_list: Must be 60 years of age or older, OR spouse of a qualifying participant regardless of age, OR disabled person younger than 60 years residing in a residential building where an Eating Together program operates (Baltimore City)
Must be a Baltimore County resident or participant at a participating site (Baltimore County)
Participants under 60 in Baltimore County must pay the full cost of the meal
Must complete a registration form to participate (Baltimore City)
Must swipe membership card each time attending a meal (Baltimore City)
Reservations required two to five days in advance depending on meal type (Baltimore County)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: In Baltimore City, eligible individuals must complete a registration form to join the program. Upon registration, participants receive a membership card and can reserve meals by checking monthly posted menus, swiping their card when attending. In Baltimore County, participants visit their chosen meal site and make reservations two to five days in advance depending on meal type; reservations are made directly at the meal site.

structured_extraction.program_description: A six-week paid summer employment program for Baltimore County youth ages 14 to 21 that provides real-world work experience at private and public sector worksites. Youth workers earn $15 per hour and gain valuable employable training skills and financial literacy education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants earn $15 per hour for up to 25 hours per week over six weeks (July 6 through August 14, 2026). Participants receive paid work experience, employable training skills, and financial literacy education. Employer partners receive county subsidy support of up to $2,500 per youth position to offset wage costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Youth applications have reached capacity and are not currently being accepted
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County youth ages 14 to 21 and private, nonprofit, and county agency employers seeking to host youth workers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid work experience at employer worksites with training in employable skills and financial literacy. Employer positions can be onsite or virtual with activities that may include work-based learning support, entrepreneurial or leadership opportunities, academic skill connections, high-tech or high-demand industry experience, or pathways to year-round employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: Age 14 to 21
Baltimore County resident or student
Employer must complete employer registration form
Employer must be willing to host youth worker(s)
Employer must provide job description including job duties, proposed work schedule, age requirements, and site restrictions
If childcare or camp-related site, employer must provide copies of relevant licensing and documentation
County agencies and private employers may choose to fund position at $2,500 per youth
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Youth submit applications (currently at capacity). Employer partners complete the Summer Youth Employer Registration form at https://bcwebservices.wufoo.com/forms/summer-youth-employer-registration/, including company information, worksite supervisor details, industry field, job titles and descriptions, number of youth requested, and site verification information. Youth are matched with employers based on interests, employer needs, and worksite locations. A member of the Youth Services team follows up with employers regarding next steps.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free tax preparation and electronic filing services provided in collaboration with the Baltimore County Department of Aging for individuals with low-to-moderate income, with emphasis on those aged 60 and above.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free tax preparation and electronic filing services at select senior centers and other locations throughout Baltimore County and Baltimore City. Services are provided by appointment only on a first-come, first-served basis. Clients are asked to arrive 15 minutes early to complete paperwork. Accommodations such as American Sign Language interpreters are available upon request.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Reservations beginning January 12, 2026. Appointments filled on first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with low-to-moderate income, with emphasis on those aged 60 and above.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax preparation and electronic filing services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at select senior centers and other locations throughout Baltimore County and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Low-to-moderate income
Age 60 and above (emphasis)
Valid photo ID for all persons claimed on the tax return
Social Security Card for all persons claimed on the tax return
Prior year tax return or form from the last year filed
Required tax documents such as W-2s, 1099 forms, and other income documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the phone number listed for the desired site or register in person to schedule an appointment. Reservations began January 12, 2026. Appointments are filled on a first-come, first-served basis. Each site maintains a waitlist of up to 20 people. Clients should arrive 15 minutes early to complete paperwork.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time grant that helps qualifying Baltimore County residents with mental illness pay for medications used to treat mental illness. The fund assists those waiting for approval of Medical Assistance (MA) who have scheduled an appointment with a provider that accepts MA.

Applicants must be waiting for MA approval and have scheduled an appointment with a MA-accepting provider. Application must be completed by a case manager or other mental health professional on behalf of the applicant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents with mental illness who are waiting for Medical Assistance approval and have a scheduled appointment with a provider
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medications for treatment of mental illness
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County only
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Must have a mental illness
Must be waiting for Medical Assistance approval
Must have a scheduled appointment with a provider that accepts MA
Application must be completed by a case manager, therapist, physician or other mental health professional
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicant's case manager or mental health professional completes and submits the flex fund application form.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that provides financing to technology-based businesses and businesses acquiring technology equipment. The program helps businesses finance the acquisition and improvement of land, buildings, plant, and equipment, including new construction or facility expansion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $250,000 for technology-based businesses and businesses acquiring technology equipment. Funds may be used to finance the acquisition and improvement of land, buildings, plant and equipment, including new construction or facility expansion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Technology-based businesses and businesses acquiring technology equipment
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and improvement of land, buildings, plant and equipment, including new construction or facility expansion
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Baltimore County business development representative by calling 410-887-8000 or emailing businesshelp@baltimorecountymd.gov to learn more and apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Architect-On-Call program provides free professional architectural design services to owners of commercial properties in Commercial Revitalization Districts in Baltimore County. Property owners receive up to 10 hours of free services including an initial site visit, digital renderings of the building, design recommendations, and a rough cost estimate for exterior improvements to their buildings. The service is free when improvements are certified as complete within six months of receiving the services.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers up to 10 free hours of professional architectural design services. After an initial site visit and meeting, the architect prepares digital renderings of the building with design recommendations and a rough cost estimate. This service is free when improvements are certified as complete within six months. Eligible improvements include façade, landscaping, signage and awnings, parking lots, exterior lighting, and windows and doors. Interior and mechanical systems improvements are not eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial properties located within Baltimore County's Commercial Revitalization Districts
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior improvements to commercial buildings including façade, landscaping, signage and awnings, parking lots, exterior lighting, and windows and doors
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Commercial properties must be located within designated Commercial Revitalization Districts in Baltimore County, including Arbutus, Catonsville, Essex, Loch Raven, Perry Hall, Pikesville, and Towson.
requirements_list: Property must be located within a Commercial Revitalization District
Property owner must submit the Architect-On-Call Application
Improvements must be certified as complete within six months to receive free services
Properties in the Pikesville Commercial Revitalization District façade improvements are subject to Design Review Panel administrative review
Properties in Arbutus, Catonsville, Essex, Loch Raven, Perry Hall, Pikesville, and Towson that include new construction require full Design Review Panel review
Business must be located in a Commercial Revitalization District
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Architect-On-Call Application via email to planningaoc@baltimorecountymd.gov or mail to Iyad Abdi at the Baltimore County Department of Planning. The AOC Program Coordinator will set up a meeting with the property owner and architect, typically within 14 days of application review and approval. The meeting is held onsite to discuss improvements. The architect develops preliminary renderings and a scope of work outline, which are sent to the coordinator for the property owner to review and provide feedback. Based on feedback, the architect revises recommendations and produces a final proposal with before and after renderings, scope of work, and cost estimate. The property owner then makes improvements based on the architect's recommendations within six months.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arthritis Foundation's Walk with Ease Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A community-based physical activity and self-management education program that combines walking with health education, stretching, strengthening exercises, and motivational strategies to reduce arthritis pain and improve balance and strength.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-hour workshops meet three times a week for six weeks. Partially funded under Title III-D of the Older Americans Act of 1965. Individuals 60 and over are encouraged to make a suggested donation of $15 at the time of registration.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training program for arthritis management and physical activity
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: Age 60 and over
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email or call contact person for more information and registration

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides essential home repairs and safety modifications for homeowners aged 65 and older in Baltimore County to help them age safely in place. The program offers financial assistance with income-based eligibility and no asset test requirement.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance for home repairs and safety modifications to enable seniors to age in place safely. Financial eligibility: one person income $3,800 with no asset test; two people income $4,345 with no asset test.
