requirements_list: Age 65 or older
Homeowner status
Meet income limits: $3,800 for one person or $4,345 for two people
No asset test required

structured_extraction.program_description: Energy efficiency incentives and rebates for nonresidential customers from Baltimore Gas and Electric Company.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Large selection of energy efficiency incentives and rebates for commercial and nonresidential customers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: BGE commercial and nonresidential customers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements, equipment upgrades, and building performance enhancements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: BGE service territory
requirements_list: Must be a BGE commercial customer
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit BGE Smart Energy website to explore available energy solutions and rebates.

structured_extraction.program_description: A modified rural reforestation program for Baltimore County residents with less than one acre of land. The program plants between 20 and 145 native trees (representing one-tenth to three-fourths of an acre) with deer protection at no cost to eligible property owners. Designed to make reforestation accessible to property owners with smaller parcels of land, trees are planted in the fall by County-selected contractors.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County-selected contractors plant 20 to 145 native trees and equip them with deer protection at no cost to the property owner. Minimum planting area is one-tenth of an acre; plantings can range from 20 trees up to larger multi-acre reforestations. Trees are planted in the fall. Property owners are responsible for maintaining the trees and reporting their survival to EPS. Program focuses on reforestation and does not include planting of evergreens or small groupings of trees intended for landscaping or privacy screening.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents and landowners with one-tenth to three-fourths of an acre of open space available for planting.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reforestation of residential property with native trees, planted at no cost to the property owner.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County only
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County landowner
Property must have between one-tenth and three-fourths of an acre available for planting
Applicant must submit a Backyard Trees Program application
Property owner is responsible for tree maintenance and reporting tree survival to EPS
Program focuses on reforestation and does not include planting of evergreens or small groupings of trees intended for landscaping or privacy screening
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Backyard Trees Program application via email to forestmanagement@baltimorecountymd.gov or by mail to Baltimore County EPS Forest Management, 111 West Chesapeake Avenue, Room 305, Towson, Maryland 21204. Interested landowners may also apply through the County website or contact the Forestry Management Division for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore County ARPA Childcare Support Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funding to help licensed childcare providers recover from the COVID-19 pandemic by supporting operational expenses and stabilizing businesses affected by under-enrollment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each eligible childcare provider receives a $5,000 grant to support their childcare operation's recovery from COVID-19. Funds must be used by December 31, 2024. If applications exceed available funds, awards are made in order of application receipt.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed childcare providers in Baltimore County with 14 or fewer registered childcare slots who were licensed by the Maryland State Department of Education on or before March 11, 2021.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel costs, rent or mortgage, utilities, facilities, maintenance, insurance, personal protective equipment, cleaning and health and safety practices, equipment and supplies, goods and services necessary for childcare operation, and mental health services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County only
requirements_list: Must be a licensed childcare provider
Must have 14 or fewer registered childcare slots
Must have been licensed by the Maryland State Department of Education on or before March 11, 2021
Must have been impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application via email. Applications are accepted from Monday, May 22 at 9 am through Friday, June 2 at 5 pm. Abilities Network administers the program, distributes grant payments, and verifies childcare licenses. Applicants are encouraged to attend an informational webinar on May 15 from 6:30 p.m. to 7:30 p.m.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funding to help farms in Baltimore County recover from the economic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic by supporting ongoing production challenges and offsetting negative pandemic effects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each eligible farm receives a $5,000 grant. Funds must be used by December 31, 2024. Allowable uses include wages, non-salary personnel costs (supplies and materials), increased personnel salaries, rent/mortgage, utilities, facilities, maintenance and insurance, personal protective equipment, cleaning and health and safety practices, equipment and supplies, and goods and services necessary for the operation of a farm. If applications exceed available funding, grants are awarded in the order applications were received. Grant funds are subject to audit and recipients must keep accurate and complete accounting records including receipts. If grant funds are not spent on allowable expenses or are otherwise misused, recipients may be required to repay funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farms and farm producers located in Baltimore County that were impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wages, non-salary personnel costs (supplies and materials), increased personnel salaries, rent/mortgage, utilities, facilities, maintenance and insurance, personal protective equipment, cleaning and health and safety practices, equipment and supplies, and goods and services necessary for the operation of a farm.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Farm must have a physical location and address in Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Farm has a physical location or address in Baltimore County
Farm or producer is in good standing with the Internal Revenue Service, the State of Maryland, and Baltimore County Government
Farm or producer is in compliance with federal, state, and local human rights laws
Farm or producer has fewer than 500 employees and is considered a small business as defined by section three of the Small Business Act
Farm or producer earned 51% or more of its gross income from farming in IRS tax years 2020 and 2021
Business was open prior to March 11, 2021
Business is currently operating
UEI (Unique Entity Identifier) number required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted via email to grsigrants@baltimorecountymd.gov with the subject line 'Agricultural Support Grant [Agricultural Business Name]' from March 11, 2024 at 9 a.m. through March 22, 2024 at 5 p.m. All forms must be submitted as PDFs in one email. Required supporting documents include completed W-9 form and IRS Schedule F tax forms from tax years 2020 and 2021. Applications that are incomplete upon submission (missing documents, etc.) will not be considered. Only digitally submitted applications are accepted. Baltimore County hosted information sessions on February 8 and February 12. Technical assistance is available by scheduling an appointment with Erika Crowl at University of Maryland Extension, Baltimore County.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore County Commission on Arts and Sciences Project Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Arts and Sciences Project Grants program provides funding to community-based, not-for-profit organizations to produce and present arts, science, history and humanities programs and activities that serve Baltimore County residents. Eligible projects include performances, exhibits, lectures, classes, workshops, festivals, film screenings, exhibitions, poetry readings, dance, theatrical performances, and musical concert series. structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore County Property Tax Credit for Historical Restorations and Rehabilitations
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program that provides financial incentives to residential and commercial property owners in Baltimore County who rehabilitate or restore historic structures. Residential owner-occupied properties receive a tax credit equal to 20 percent of qualified rehabilitation expenditures, usable over up to 10 years. Commercial properties receive a 10-year tax freeze on the increased assessment resulting from rehabilitation work. The program recognizes qualified rehabilitation work that restores historic buildings to functional use while preserving historically, architecturally, or culturally significant features, and may be used in conjunction with the Maryland state historic tax credit program.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residential owner-occupied dwellings receive a property tax credit equal to 20 percent of qualified rehabilitation expenditures, with a minimum of $1,000 in eligible expenses. The approved credit is a fixed amount that owners can draw from over up to 10 years to reduce annual County property tax bills, with unused portions carried over for up to 10 additional tax years. Commercial property owners receive a tax credit equal to the difference between the assessed value before rehabilitation work and the increase in assessment from the rehabilitation work, functioning as a 10-year cap on the assessment and preventing property taxes from increasing due to the increased value from rehabilitation work. Commercial rehabilitation work must generally exceed $50,000 to generate a reassessment, and the credit may not exceed the actual amount of tax levied on the property in any tax year. Credits begin in the tax year after work is completed and certified as compliant with County standards. Credits are fully transferable to new property owners for the remaining life of the credit, and there is no limit on the number of credits received. Eligible work includes basement waterproofing, chimney repair and lining, exterior painting, interior plaster repair, masonry repointing, new storm windows, original wood floor refinishing, plumbing and electrical and mechanical systems, repair of historic outbuildings, roof repair and replacement, structural repairs, and tool/equipment rental. All work must conform to the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and Baltimore County's Historic Preservation Design Guidelines, and must be pre-approved by the Baltimore County Landmarks Preservation Commission before work begins.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: County Part I applications may be submitted at any time. County Part II applications without a State approved Part 2 are due two weeks before the next scheduled Landmarks Preservation Commission meeting.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential homeowners and commercial property owners with historic structures listed on the Baltimore County Final Landmarks List, contributing resources within Baltimore County Historic Districts, or individually listed properties or contributing resources on the National Register of Historic Places, who seek tax relief for restoration and rehabilitation work.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified rehabilitation and restoration expenditures for work that returns the historic structure to productive use while preserving historically, architecturally, or culturally significant portions and features. Eligible work includes basement waterproofing, chimney repair and lining, exterior painting, interior plaster repair, masonry repointing, new storm windows, original wood floor refinishing, plumbing and electrical and mechanical systems, repair of historic outbuildings, roof repair and replacement, structural repairs, and tool/equipment rental.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland. Properties must be designated as historic: either a contributing structure in a County Historic District, a contributing structure in a National Register Historic District, or individually listed on the National Register of Historic Places or the Final Landmarks List.
requirements_list: Property must be listed on Baltimore County Final Landmarks List, be a contributing resource within a Baltimore County Historic District, or be individually listed or a contributing resource within a Historic District on the National Register of Historic Places
For residential owner-occupied properties: qualified rehabilitation expenditures must be at least $1,000
For commercial properties: rehabilitation work must generally exceed $50,000 to generate a reassessment
The commercial credit may not exceed the actual amount of tax levied on the property in any tax year
All rehabilitation work must conform to the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and Baltimore County's Historic Preservation Design Guidelines
Work must be reviewed and approved by the Landmarks Preservation Commission or staff before starting
Credits begin in the tax year after work is completed and certified as compliant with County standards
Any work started or completed prior to approval is not eligible for the credit
Residential properties used for rental or investment purposes must complete the commercial application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process consists of three parts. Part 1, completed before the project begins, certifies that the building is eligible for the program. Part 2, also completed before the project begins, certifies that the proposed project meets the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and Baltimore County's Historic Design Guidelines. Part 3, completed after the project is complete, certifies that the completed project meets the Standards for Rehabilitation and the expenditures claimed are eligible for the tax credit. County Part I applications may be submitted at any time. County Part II applications without a State approved Part 2 are due two weeks before the next scheduled Landmarks Preservation Commission meeting. Applications may be submitted by email to histpres@baltimorecountymd.gov or by regular mail to Baltimore County Department of Planning, Historic Preservation, 105 West Chesapeake Avenue, Suite 101, Towson, Maryland 21204.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax relief program that exempts $15,000 of a property's assessed value from real property tax obligations for blind individuals or their surviving spouses in Baltimore County. Eligible individuals may also receive a retroactive refund of property taxes paid in years when an exemption was authorized but not granted, going back up to three years. The program is established under state law and administered in coordination with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). Applicants must meet the legal definition of blindness, which includes central visual acuity of 20/200 or less in the better eye with corrective glasses, or peripheral field defect of 20 degrees or less.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Food safety manager certification training to meet Baltimore County requirements for operating food service facilities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County only. Applies to organizations operating medium or high priority food service facilities in Baltimore County.

Organization must operate a medium or high priority food service facility
Organization must operate three days or less per week (for Level II requirement)
Must pre-register for training
Must have computer access to participate in virtual training

structured_extraction.program_name: Commercial Revitalization District (CRD) Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit for owners who make qualified improvements to commercially zoned properties, mobile home parks, or senior housing developments located in designated Commercial Revitalization Districts (CRDs) in Baltimore County. The program reduces the County real property tax obligation for five to ten years depending on improvement costs, and supports family-owned businesses and national retail chains in established communities throughout the County. Alongside the tax credit, businesses may also access the Building Improvement Loan Program (BILP), which provides interest-free loans up to $30,000 for facade improvements, and free architectural design services.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The tax credit equals 100 percent of the increase in County taxes for senior housing developments and mobile home parks in revitalization districts, or 100 percent of County property taxes for other commercial property in designated districts. For senior housing outside revitalization districts, the credit is 50 percent of the tax increase. The credit applies to qualified improvements with a full cash value of $100,000 or more and runs for five years, or ten years if improvements exceed $10 million. Additionally, businesses may access the Building Improvement Loan Program (BILP) providing an interest-free loan up to $30,000 for facade improvements, and free architectural design services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 120 days after the issuance of a notice of assessment by the State Department of Records and Taxation
structured_extraction.contact_name: Department of Planning Neighborhood Response Team; Taxpayer Services
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners making qualified improvements to commercially zoned properties, mobile home parks, or senior housing developments located in designated Commercial Revitalization Districts in Baltimore County, including family-owned businesses and national retail chains.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Physical improvements to eligible properties including commercially zoned properties, mobile home parks, and senior housing developments; facade improvements through the Building Improvement Loan Program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties located within Baltimore County designated Commercial Revitalization Districts. For commercial properties, improvements must be in designated commercial revitalization districts. Senior housing developments may qualify both inside and outside revitalization districts, with varying credit levels.
requirements_list: Property must be commercially zoned, a mobile home park, or a senior housing development
Property must be located in a designated commercial revitalization district (senior housing may qualify outside districts at a reduced credit rate)
Qualified improvements must have a full cash value of $100,000 or more as recorded by SDAT
Application must be filed within 120 days after SDAT issues notice of assessment including the improvements
Detailed receipts for all related expenses must be submitted with the application
Improvement costs must exceed $10 million to qualify for the 10-year credit
Property cannot be used for railroad or public utility purposes
Property cannot be covered by the Maryland Condominium Act
All applicants are required to meet with staff prior to submitting applications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schedule a pre-application meeting with staff by emailing businesshelp@baltimorecountymd.gov. File an Application for Revitalization Tax Credit with the Director of Budget and Finance within 120 days after receiving a notice of assessment from the State Department of Records and Taxation that includes the improvements. Include detailed receipts for all related expenses. For commercial properties in revitalization districts, contact the Department of Planning Neighborhood Response Team at 410-887-3480. Send the application to the Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration at 400 Washington Avenue, Room 149, Towson, Maryland 21204. For additional information, contact taxcredits@baltimorecountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Clean-Up Program allows communities of 50 households or more in Baltimore County to host bulk trash events (sometimes called Dumpster Days) to collect trash and debris that is not normally picked up for curbside collection. If an event is approved and sufficient funds are available, Baltimore County will subsidize the cost of renting roll-off dumpsters. Only one clean-up event per fiscal year (July through June) is permitted for each community association or clean-up area. Participating communities must select an approved County waste management contractor to provide the dumpsters.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Baltimore County subsidizes the cost of renting roll-off dumpsters for approved community clean-up events. The subsidy is provided if the event is approved and if sufficient funds are available. Participating communities must select an approved waste management contractor to provide the dumpsters.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: At least one month before your event
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community associations and clean-up areas with 50 households or more that want to host bulk trash events within Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The subsidy covers the cost of renting roll-off dumpsters for collecting bulk trash and materials not normally picked up for curbside collection.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to communities within Baltimore County boundaries. Events must be held at a location within the boundaries of your community.
requirements_list: Community must have 50 households or more
Only one clean-up event per fiscal year (July through June) is permitted for each community association or clean-up area
Event location must be available from 7 a.m. to noon on a Saturday
Location must have enough space for required dumpsters
Organization must have written permission from the authorized agent of the property for use of the location
If placing containers on Board of Education property, written permission from the public school system is required
Applicant must use an approved County waste management contractor
Application must be submitted at least one month before the event
Written permission for location use must be received by the Bureau prior to the event
Documentation must be provided explaining reasons for not using the lowest bid vendor, if applicable
Community organization is responsible for monitoring the site and loads of refuse at all times on the day of the clean-up
Containers must not be filled above the sides
Community organization is responsible for any additional costs incurred due to delays, wasted trips, or rehandling of prohibited or contaminated items
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Select a location and date for your event (must be available 7 a.m. to noon on a Saturday, with enough space for dumpsters, and you must have written permission from the property owner). 2. Find an approved County waste management contractor to provide dumpsters. 3. Submit the Community Clean-Up Application at least one month before your event, including written permission for location use and documentation explaining any deviation from lowest bid vendors. 4. Once approved, promote your event within your community only (flyers, community newsletter) and do not publicize in general-circulation newspapers. 5. Monitor your event on the day of the clean-up to ensure proper waste management and compliance with disposal regulations.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Baltimore County Department of Planning program that provides capital project grants to neighborhood and community-based organizations, businesses, non-profits, and individuals to implement projects that benefit communities, neighborhoods, and business districts throughout Baltimore County. Projects must advance the goals of Master Plan 2030 and can include commercial district improvements, community gardens, electric vehicle charging stations, public art, murals, signage, pedestrian or bicycle trails, and park or playground enhancements. Eligible projects must have a durability of 15 years or more and benefit the overall community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two-tiered grant structure with a total of $1.8 million in funding available. Tier 1 provides grants from $3,000 to $15,000 with $200,000 total available, accepted semi-annually. Tier 2 provides larger grants from $15,001 to $100,000 with $1 million total available, accepted on a rolling basis. Overall grant awards range from $3,000 to $200,000. Requests above $100,000 require County Executive approval.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Spring 2026 application deadline is Friday, May 1, 2026. Tier 1 grants are accepted semi-annually; Tier 2 grants can be submitted at any time on a rolling basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, non-profit organizations, community organizations, local Chambers of Commerce, and individuals based in or managing projects in Baltimore County seeking to undertake capital projects that strengthen neighborhoods, grow communities, and advance community development goals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects designed to benefit the community and advance the goals of Master Plan 2030, including commercial district improvements, community gardens, electric vehicle charging stations, building improvements, murals and public art, neighborhood signage, pedestrian or bicycle trails, and park or playground enhancements. Projects must have a durability of 15 years or more and benefit the overall community.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: Applicants must have a 501(c)(3), (c)(4), (c)(6), or (c)(7) designation (for non-profit applicants)
Applicants must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Proposed projects must have a durability of 15 years or more
Projects must not be portable in nature
Projects must benefit the overall community
Projects must be completed within two years of grant award
Projects should advance the goals of Master Plan 2030
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations and individuals apply through a survey or application form. Tier 1 grants are accepted semi-annually with submissions due by specified deadlines. Tier 2 grants can be submitted at any time on a rolling basis. The Spring 2026 application deadline is Friday, May 1, 2026. Additional details are available through the grant opportunities hub page.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grant funding to pay for structural changes to rental units that help people with disabilities. Eligible modifications can address hearing, physical, or vision impairment, such as grab bars, railings, ramps, and doorway widening. The program is available exclusively to active Housing Choice Voucher recipients or holders of other federally-issued housing vouchers who have at least one household member with a disability. There is no cost to eligible tenants or landlords who qualify.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grant funding to cover the full cost of structural modifications to rental units. Modifications are tailored to the specific accessibility needs of the disabled household member and may include features for hearing, physical, or vision impairment, such as grab bars, railings, ramps, and doorway widening. Licensed contractors selected by the Housing Opportunities and Finance Division complete the work. Landlords have the option to complete modifications themselves. Processing includes an initial response within approximately 10 days, followed by 2 to 4 months for modification completion after all approvals are obtained. Modifications can also include removal costs if the tenant moves out and the landlord requests the modifications be removed. There is no cost to eligible tenants or landlords.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tenants who are active Housing Choice Voucher program recipients or holders of other federally-issued housing vouchers and have at least one household member with a disability, and their landlords. Must reside in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Structural modifications to rental units to accommodate the accessibility needs of individuals with disabilities, including modifications for hearing, physical, or vision impairment. Examples include grab bars, railings, ramps, doorway widening, and other structural improvements. Modifications are approved on a case-by-case basis. Modifications can also include removal costs if the tenant moves out and the landlord requests the modifications be removed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must reside in Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Head of household must be an active Housing Choice Voucher program recipient or holder of another federally-issued housing voucher
Household must have at least one member with a disability
Must reside in Baltimore County
Must have a current and signed lease
Landlord must agree to the referral to CHAMP for the modification
Must be a renter
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application by email to rar@baltimorecountymd.gov with subject line 'Attention: Reasonable Accommodation Coordinator', by fax to 410-887-8804, by phone at 410-887-3435, or in person at the Office of Housing. The landlord must approve the referral. The application goes to the Housing and Finance Division for processing with an initial response within approximately 10 days. Once scope of work and grant agreement are drafted, both landlord and tenant sign off. Modifications are then completed, typically taking 2 to 4 months after all approvals.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in computer basics, file management, email, Google services, virtual meeting platforms, Microsoft Word, and Microsoft Excel

requirements_list: Must register at the Career Center you wish to attend
For Technology Basics for Employment: must attend all four workshops

structured_extraction.program_name: Disabled Law Enforcement Officers or Rescue Workers Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit that assists law enforcement personnel, fire personnel, and rescue workers (including volunteers) who have suffered permanent and total disability during their service to Baltimore County. The credit equals 100 percent of the Baltimore County real property tax obligation and continues annually for the lifetime of the disabled person, reducing their property tax burden on their qualifying dwelling.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The credit equals 100 percent of the Baltimore County real property tax obligation and continues annually for the lifetime of the disabled person. The credit applies only to the Baltimore County Real Property Tax obligation and does not include other charges on the bill. The credit does not extend to a surviving spouse or other individual residing in the dwelling after the disabled person's death.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before September 30 of the tax year for which the credit is requested to begin
structured_extraction.program_audience: Law enforcement officers, fire personnel, and rescue workers (including volunteers) who are permanently and totally disabled as a result of their service to Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit reduces the Baltimore County real property tax obligation for the qualifying disabled worker's dwelling.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland only. The dwelling must be located in Baltimore County.
requirements_list: The applicant must be a law enforcement officer, fire personnel member, or rescue worker (including volunteers) who has suffered permanent and total disability during service to Baltimore County
The applicant must conform to the requirements established within his or her agency in order to be deemed disabled
A verifying Court Order or Administrative Notice must be provided with the application

The dwelling must be owned by the disabled worker at the time he or she was adjudged to be disabled, OR the disabled worker was domiciled in the state as of the date adjudged to be disabled and the dwelling was acquired within two years of that date, OR the dwelling was acquired after the disabled worker qualified for a credit for a former dwelling under the previous methods
The dwelling cannot be eligible for any other Baltimore County real property tax credit
The credit is only awarded during the lifetime of the disabled person
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, send a copy of the verifying Court Order or Administrative Notice and the completed tax credit application form to the Office of Budget and Finance on or before September 30 of the tax year for which the credit is requested to begin. Mail the application request to the Property Tax Credit Administration at the specified address in Towson, Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Disabled Veteran and Surviving Spouse Property Tax Exemption or Refund
structured_extraction.program_description: This program exempts the home of a disabled veteran or surviving spouse of a disabled veteran from all Baltimore County real property tax obligations. Eligible individuals may also receive a refund of property taxes paid for up to three years before receiving the exemption. The exemption is established under Maryland state law and administered through the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT).
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Disabled veterans and surviving spouses of disabled veterans receive a full exemption from Baltimore County real property taxes on their home. Applicants may also request a refund of property taxes paid for up to three prior years (under Tax Property Article 7-208) by checking the refund box on the application and submitting it to SDAT with required documentation. The refund is processed after exemption approval.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) - Baltimore County Assessments Office
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disabled veterans and surviving spouses of disabled veterans who own residential property in Baltimore County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax exemption or refund on a residential home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County only. The exemption is established under Maryland state law and administered by the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). Applications must be filed with the Baltimore County Assessments office located at Hampton Plaza, 300 E Joppa Road, Suite 602, Towson, MD 21286.
requirements_list: Must be a disabled veteran or surviving spouse of a disabled veteran
Must own a home in Baltimore County
Cannot receive relief under the Blind Individual or Surviving Spouse Tax Exemption
Must have a service-connected disability rating of 100% permanent and total or 100% permanently unemployable from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA)
Must be a Maryland resident
Must provide proof of residency (current Maryland driver's license, voter registration, redacted prior year Maryland income taxes, or contract of sale if pending purchase)
Must provide a copy of Honorable Discharge or DD-Form 214
Must provide a copy of most recent VA rating notification packet showing 100% disability rating with effective date and date of VA rating decision
If VA rating document is not available, must have VA complete certification section on application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain the Application for Exemption for Disabled Veterans form (SDAT Form). 2. Complete the form with required personal information, property details, and check the refund box if requesting a refund. 3. Attach required documentation: copy of Honorable Discharge or DD-Form 214, most recent VA rating notification showing 100% permanent and total or 100% permanently unemployable status, and proof of Maryland residency. 4. File the completed application with the Baltimore County Assessments Office (Hampton Plaza, 300 E Joppa Road, Suite 602, Towson, MD 21286). 5. If approved, the exemption becomes effective on the date specified. 6. To apply for a refund, check the refund box on the original application; after exemption approval, submit copy of approved exemption to Baltimore County Council with letter requesting refund of taxes paid for up to three prior years.

structured_extraction.program_name: Diverse Teacher Recruitment Scholarship: Growing Our Own for BCPS

structured_extraction.program_audience: College students in their junior and senior years, current para-educators, and individuals changing careers who are Black, Indigenous, People of Color, or women pursuing teaching certificates in STEM fields or general education at local colleges and universities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition, fees, and books for teacher education programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County. Students must study at local colleges and universities and commit to internships in BCPS schools and teaching with BCPS for three years upon graduation.
requirements_list: Must be a college student in junior or senior year, a current BCPS para-educator, or an individual changing careers studying education
Must be Black, Indigenous, People of Color (BIPOC), or a woman pursuing teaching certificates in STEM fields
Must be studying at local colleges and universities
Must commit to completing internships in BCPS schools
Must commit to teaching with BCPS for three years upon graduation from an accredited teacher-education program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Education Foundation of BCPS website at www.educationfoundationbcps.org for application details and submission process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credits available to businesses located within Baltimore County's three designated Enterprise Zones (North Point, Southwest, and Federal Center at Woodlawn) that expand or add employees. The program offers both County and Maryland tax credits to encourage investment and redevelopment in older industrial and office areas. Credits include a real property tax credit offering a 10-year reduction on property taxes after major capital improvements, and an income credit allowing businesses a one-time state income tax deduction after creating new jobs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible businesses in Baltimore County's three Enterprise Zones (North Point, Southwest, or Federal Center at Woodlawn) that expand or add employees receive both County and Maryland tax credits. The real property tax credit offers a 10-year reduction on property taxes after major capital improvements are made. The income credit allows businesses a one-time state income tax deduction after creating new jobs.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Enterprise Zone Coordinator, Baltimore County Department of Economic Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses located within Baltimore County's designated Enterprise Zones (North Point, Southwest, or Federal Center at Woodlawn) that are expanding or adding employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits for businesses that expand or add employees in the Enterprise Zones, including credits for property investment and job creation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: North Point Enterprise Zone, Southwest Enterprise Zone, and Federal Center at Woodlawn Enterprise Zone in Baltimore County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must be located within one of the three designated Enterprise Zones (North Point, Southwest, or Federal Center at Woodlawn)
Business must be expanding or adding employees

For income credit: must create new jobs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Verify the eligibility of an address using the interactive map. Detailed maps of Baltimore County's enterprise zones are available for download.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that helps individuals with limited income pay for prescription drug costs under Medicare Part D by reducing monthly premiums, annual deductibles, and prescription drug copayments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individuals who qualify typically pay only small copayments for medications. Single applicants with qualifying income pay no monthly premium, no deductible, $5.10 for generic drugs, and $12.65 for brand name drugs. Couples pay the same copayments. The 2026 Regional Premium Benchmark is $43.61; plans below this benchmark have no premium. Individuals eligible for QMB or SLMB are automatically eligible for Extra Help.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with limited income who are Medicare beneficiaries and need help paying for prescription drugs. Single individuals with gross income under $24,180 per year or $2,015 per month and assets under $16,590, or couples with gross income under $32,700 per year or $2,725 per month and assets under $33,100. Individuals receiving full Medical Assistance (red and white card holders) are automatically eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medicare Part D premiums, annual deductibles, and prescription drug copayments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: United States
requirements_list: Single: gross income under $24,180 per year or $2,015 per month and assets under $16,590
Couple: gross income under $32,700 per year or $2,725 per month and assets under $33,100
Full Medical Assistance eligible individuals are automatically enrolled

Certain types of income and assets are not counted: the first $65 of monthly wages, one-half of monthly wages after the $65 is deducted, first house if owning more than one, first car if owning more than one, and $1,500 per person burial allowance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through Social Security by calling 1-800-772-1213 or visiting www.ssa.gov. Individuals receiving full Medical Assistance are automatically enrolled and do not need to apply. Those may also be eligible for QMB or SLMB; for an application, call Baltimore County SHIP at 410-887-2059 or the Department of Social Services.

Special consideration is given to organizations serving diverse communities, including LGBTQ+, Black/African American, and Hispanic/Latino populations. The program focuses on prevention and public awareness efforts related to tobacco use.

Special consideration is given to organizations that serve diverse communities, including LGBTQ+, Black/African American, and Hispanic/Latino populations.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tobacco prevention, education and awareness programs for youth ages 8 to 15

Programs must serve youth ages 8 to 15 in Baltimore County
Special consideration for organizations serving diverse communities including LGBTQ+, Black/African American, and Hispanic/Latino populations
Organizations must complete the Community Grant application
Organizations must complete the Baltimore County Financial Assistance Application

Applicants should email tobaccogrants@baltimorecountymd.gov to request a fillable application form. See the attached RFA document for full details. Questions can be directed to tobaccogrants@baltimorecountymd.gov or 410-887-0575.

structured_extraction.program_description: A court-supervised program that helps non-custodial parents who are behind on child support payments obtain full-time employment by requiring participants to submit job applications and meet with court coordinators weekly for job referrals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive weekly meetings with employment coordinators for job search strategy development, job referrals, and follow-up support for a minimum of one year after employment. Employers may receive tax incentive assistance, free employee screening including drug testing and background checks, and free Employee Assistance Program (EAP) services for hired participants covering family, elder care, child care, stress, financial, substance abuse, legal and work adjustment issues.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment services, job training coordination, and placement support for non-custodial parents.

Be highly motivated to support families

Submit employment applications
Meet weekly with court coordinators
Pass drug screening
Pass criminal background check

structured_extraction.program_name: Free iPads or Chromebooks for Seniors
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore County Department of Aging distributes free iPads and Chromebooks to eligible older adults through federal American Rescue Plan Act funding and a Maryland State device grant. Recipients receive training and support to learn their devices and access reduced or free internet through the Affordable Connectivity Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program distributes 250 iPads and 600 Chromebooks at no cost to eligible older adults. Recipients must be age 60 or older, reside in Baltimore County or be a member of a Baltimore County Senior Center, qualify as low-income (200 percent or less of poverty level), and have the ability to learn the device. Upon receiving an eligible application, BCDA schedules training or pick-up events, assesses need for the Affordable Connectivity Program for reduced or free WiFi, offers brief training on the equipment, and connects individuals with BCDA technology programs and free tech support on Fridays.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults age 60 and older who are low-income, reside in Baltimore County or are members of a Baltimore County Senior Center, and have the ability to learn to use a device.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The devices (iPads or Chromebooks) are provided at no cost. Individuals may also receive assistance applying for reduced or free internet through the Affordable Connectivity Program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County residents or members of a Baltimore County Senior Center.
requirements_list: Age 60 years or older
Reside in Baltimore County or be a member of a Baltimore County Senior Center
Qualify as low-income: 200 percent or less of poverty level (Single: $27,180; Couple: $36,620)
Have the ability to learn the device
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and submit the application. Upon receipt of an eligible application, BCDA Office of Communications will contact the individual to schedule a training or pick-up event in the county, assess if they need assistance applying for the Affordable Connectivity Program, offer brief training on the equipment, and connect them with BCDA technology programs and free tech support.

All future taxes must remain current to maintain program eligibility.

Application must be filed by end of February to avoid tax sale
All future taxes must be kept current to maintain eligibility

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for commercial buildings that achieve at least a silver rating using either the Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) Green Building rating system or the American National Standards Institute's National Green Building Standard (NGBS) rating system. The credit reduces the property's Baltimore County real property tax obligation.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Commercial buildings receive a tax credit that reduces their Baltimore County real property tax obligation for a specified duration. LEED-NC and LEED-CS credits range from 40 to 80 percent of property tax and last 5 years depending on rating level (silver, gold, or platinum). LEED-EB credits range from 10 to 50 percent and last 3 years. NGBS credits range from 50 to 80 percent and last 5 years depending on rating level (silver, gold, or emerald). The credit applies only to the Baltimore County real property tax portion of the bill.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought, or at any time if filed in conjunction with a Revitalization Property Tax Credit application
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners of commercial buildings that achieve high energy efficiency ratings
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit reduces the property's Baltimore County real property tax obligation. Other charges listed on the bill are not included in the credit calculation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland
requirements_list: Building must achieve at least a silver rating using either the LEED Green Building rating system or the NGBS rating system
Property owner must provide documentation from an energy systems professional confirming the property meets the definition of a high performance building
A property owner may receive only one High Performance Building Credit per building
Application must be filed under oath and accompanied by sufficient documentation proving the building meets the definition
Commercial building may include an income-producing, residentially used building of at least 50 units
Credit runs with the property; a change of ownership does not result in a lapse of the tax credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Application for High Performance Building Tax Credit form along with appropriate documentation from an energy systems professional to the Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration by June 1 (or at any time if filed with a Revitalization Property Tax Credit application).

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for residential properties in Baltimore County that meet energy efficiency standards through approved rating systems (HERS Index, LEED, or NGBS). The credit reduces Baltimore County real property tax based on the percentage of energy efficiency achieved and runs with the property for three consecutive years from the first year awarded, regardless of ownership changes.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit that reduces Baltimore County real property tax obligations based on energy efficiency achievement. LEED Silver and NGBS Silver provide a 40 percent property tax reduction. LEED Gold and NGBS Gold provide a 60 percent reduction. LEED Platinum and NGBS Emerald provide a 100 percent property tax reduction. For HERS Index ratings, the credit percentage matches the efficiency percentage achieved. The credit runs for three consecutive years from the first year awarded and continues if the property changes ownership. The credit does not apply to other charges or fees on the property tax bill.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Baltimore County with newly constructed or renovated residential properties meeting energy efficiency standards through approved rating systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit is applied as a reduction to Baltimore County real property tax obligations only; other charges or fees on the tax bill are not included in the calculation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Property must be residential

Property must meet one of three approved energy efficiency measurement standards: HERS Index (new construction must achieve rating of 70 or lower; renovated structures must achieve at least 30 percent increase in efficiency), LEED (Silver, Gold, or Platinum rating from U.S. Green Building Council), or NGBS (Silver, Gold, or Emerald rating approved by ANSI)
For renovated structures, HERS Rating completed before and after renovation must be submitted
Application must be submitted by June 1 of the year immediately preceding the first taxable year for which credit is sought
Must provide certificate indicating efficiency level from builder, contractor, or rater
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Gather required documentation including the efficiency rating certificate and any other relevant documentation. For renovated structures, submit before-and-after HERS Ratings. Apply either online using a valid email address and documentation, or by mail or in person by completing the printed application form and submitting it with documentation to the Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration at 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, Maryland 21204.

Funding recommendations are based on priorities identified in the County's 2020 to 2024 Consolidated Plan.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging generally from $15,000 to $200,000 annually to support nonprofit and government organizations providing homeless prevention and assistance services to Baltimore County citizens. Funding is derived from the County's annual federal HUD award (including Community Development Block Grant and Emergency Solutions Grant programs), along with state and local funds. Funding recommendations are based on priorities identified in the County's 2020 to 2024 Consolidated Plan.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects preventing homelessness or assisting those currently experiencing homelessness in Baltimore County

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit providing tax relief for homeowners of all ages based on a comparison of their tax bill to their household income.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Homeowners' Tax Credit Program provides tax credits for homeowners of all ages based on household income compared to tax bill. The Baltimore County Supplemental Credit applies only to County property taxes. The State Dept. of Assessments and Taxation determines if a homeowner qualifies for a supplemental credit due to hardship on the dwelling. Eligible homeowners receive both state and supplemental county credits.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) Homeowners' Tax Credit Division
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners of all ages whose household income compared to their property tax bill qualifies them for relief.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable; this is a property tax credit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide, including Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a homeowner
Property must be the homeowner's primary residence
Household income compared to tax bill must meet program eligibility standards
For supplemental credit, applicant must qualify for state HOTC and meet additional hardship criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for the State HOTC through the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. No separate application is required for the supplemental credit, but applicants must apply for the State HOTC to be considered.

For homeowners and renters

structured_extraction.program_description: Early intervention program serving families with children under three years old who have developmental delays or disabilities. Research-based services are coordinated based on family needs and priorities, provided at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free research-based early intervention services for eligible children with developmental delays or disabilities, coordinated based on family needs and priorities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children under three years old with developmental delays or disabilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Early intervention services to promote child development and family support in areas including social-emotional skills, knowledge and skills acquisition, and functional behavior development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County residents only
requirements_list: Child must be under three years old
Child must demonstrate 25 percent delay in one or more areas of development, atypical development in one or more areas, or a diagnosed condition placing them at risk for developmental delays
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Make a referral online at referral.mditp.org/ or by calling 443-809-2169. structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded loan program that provides low- and no-cost loans to income-eligible property owners to correct hazardous conditions, eliminate safety hazards, repair or replace major systems, correct interior and exterior deficiencies, make energy improvements, make modifications for persons with disabilities, and eliminate lead-based paint hazards. It helps bring properties up to building codes by addressing exterior and interior deficiencies, accessibility improvements, health or safety violations, energy efficiency, and lead-based paint hazard removal. Rental property landlords are not eligible for deferred loans. Secured debt, including the MHRP loan, may not exceed 110 percent of the after-rehab value as determined by assessment or appraisal. Administrative fee, closing costs, and recording costs may be included in the loan. Loan must be repaid upon discontinuance of owner occupancy or sale of the home. One loan is allowed per household per lifetime of ownership.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded program that coordinates transportation services for Medical Assistance (Medicaid) recipients in Baltimore County who need transportation to access medically necessary services. Transportation is provided by contracted vendors through shared-ride services for ambulatory and wheelchair clients, or private ambulance transport for stretcher-bound clients. Services operate Monday through Saturday from early morning (5 a.m.) to evening (7:30 p.m.), with 24/7 availability for medical facility discharges and transfers.

Must have absolutely no other means of transportation available
Medical certification from a physician required, certifying the patient is unable to use public or ADA transportation due to a specific medical condition
Medical certification must be completed, signed by the patient's doctor, and submitted to the Baltimore County Department of Health
Medical certification must be renewed at least annually
Requests for trips must be pre-scheduled one to seven days in advance
Must request transportation at least 24 hours prior to the appointment (except medical facility discharges and transfers)
Must be ready and waiting at the designated time and place for pickup
Failure to appear or canceling within 30 minutes of scheduled time counts as a no-show
Must call 24 hours in advance or the day before to schedule if multiple no-shows have occurred
For children 17 years and under, an adult must accompany them
Residents of skilled nursing facilities must be accompanied during transport
No eating, drinking, or smoking in vehicles
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact the Baltimore County Department of Health at 410-887-2828 to determine eligibility. 2. Once approved by the Health Department, call the appropriate transportation vendor to schedule rides. 5. Request rides one to seven days in advance by calling the vendor. 6. Be ready for pickup at the designated time.

structured_extraction.program_name: Project Home / Adult Foster Care Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A combined county- and state-funded program that enables individuals over 18 to remain in safe, protective living arrangements within a family setting in Baltimore County. Homes care for a maximum of four adults. Clients who cannot completely care for themselves or live independently but do not need significant nursing or institutional care can receive housing and supportive services while living in the community. The program includes two funding tracks: the Adult Foster Care Program (county-funded, with a subsidy paid directly to the home provider) and the Project Home Program (state-funded, with assistance through Public Assistance to Adults paid to the client or their representative payee).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two funding tracks are available: (1) Adult Foster Care (county-funded): Clients with insufficient income or assets receive a subsidy paid directly to the home provider. Clients receive a personal needs allowance of $75 and may keep an additional $32.50 from outside income. (2) Project Home (state-funded): Clients with insufficient income receive assistance to apply for Public Assistance to Adults (PAA)—a payment made to the client or their representative payee. Anyone eligible for PAA also receives Medical Assistance. Clients receive a personal needs allowance of $82 and may keep $20 from outside income. For both tracks, monthly cost of care ranges from $776 (Level 1/A) to $1,376 (Level 4/D) depending on client needs. Medical needs are typically covered by Medical Assistance.
