structured_extraction.program_description: An innovative workforce development partnership that connects residents in historically underserved communities with high-demand nursing positions through customized educational programming and community wraparound supports. The program provides scholarships covering tuition and fees for Certified Nursing Assistant training, monthly workforce stipends, and guaranteed employment with benefits upon completion. It is a partnership between Baltimore County, University of Maryland St. Joseph Medical Center, and the Community College of Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides 30 scholarships that fully cover tuition and all educational fees for the Community College of Baltimore County Certified Nursing Assistant program. Students also receive a $1,000 per month workforce stipend to supplement wages, address transportation or housing needs, pay for childcare, or cover other workforce-related barriers. Upon successful completion, graduates receive guaranteed employment with full benefits at University of Maryland St. Joseph Medical Center and continue their education in a Practical Nursing program. The total program includes 24 months of education: four months of Certified Nursing Assistant training, four months of prerequisites, and 16 months of Licensed Practical Nurse education.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents in historically underserved communities seeking careers in nursing and health care, particularly economically disadvantaged individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and educational fees for Certified Nursing Assistant training at Community College of Baltimore County, with monthly stipends for living expenses, transportation, housing, childcare, and other workforce-related barriers. Funds also support customized educational programming and community wraparound supports for high-demand nursing positions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland, with focus on historically underserved communities within the county.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program launches later in 2023. Interested residents should apply for the Certified Nursing Assistant program scholarship through the partnership between Baltimore County, University of Maryland St. Joseph Medical Center, and Community College of Baltimore County.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funding for public services projects that address the needs of low-income residents in Baltimore County in areas such as child care, crime prevention, drug abuse, education, employment, energy conservation, health and welfare, and recreational needs. Funded through federal, state, and county sources including the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and Emergency Solutions Grant (ESG) programs, as well as the County's annual federal HUD award. Funding recommendations are based on priorities identified in the County's 2020 to 2024 Consolidated Plan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants generally ranging from $15,000 to $200,000 annually to support nonprofit and government organizations providing public services to low-income Baltimore County residents. Funding is derived from the County's annual federal HUD award, along with state and local funds including the Community Development Block Grant and Emergency Solutions Grant programs. Funding recommendations are based on priorities identified in the County's 2020 to 2024 Consolidated Plan.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and government organizations providing public services to low-income Baltimore County residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects addressing the needs of low-income citizens in areas including employment, crime prevention, child care, health and welfare, drug abuse, education, energy conservation, and recreational needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit or government organization serving Baltimore County citizens
Projects must benefit low-income citizens
Must address one or more of the specified service areas (child care, crime prevention, drug abuse, education, employment, energy conservation, health and welfare, recreation)
Must benefit low-to-moderate income households
Must align with priorities in the County's 2020 to 2024 Consolidated Plan
Must submit required application documents including proposal questions, budget pages, and required attachments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the County Fiscal Year 2027 Grant Application Process. Download necessary grant proposal documents from the Public Services Projects section. Submit completed Appendix I Application Proposal Questions, required signatures, Appendix II Budget Pages and Application for Financial Assistance, and Appendix III Required Attachments through the grant application portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps people with limited income pay for their Medicare costs, including Part A premiums, Part B premiums, deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments. Individuals enrolled in QMB cannot be billed for Medicare-covered services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program pays for Medicare Part A and Part B monthly premiums, deductibles, and copayments. Eligible individuals receive a gray and white card once approved.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with limited income who are Medicare beneficiaries. Single individuals with gross income under $16,200 per year or $1,350 per month, or couples with gross income under $21,888 per year or $1,824 per month, with resources under $9,950 (single) or $14,910 (couple).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medicare Part A premiums, Medicare Part B premiums, Medicare deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland
requirements_list: Single: gross income under $16,200 per year or $1,350 per month and resources under $9,950
Couple: gross income under $21,888 per year or $1,824 per month and resources under $14,910
Certain types of income are not counted: the first $65 of monthly wages and one-half of monthly wages after the $65 is deducted
Assets do not include $1,500 per person burial allowance
Must reapply each year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request an application by calling the State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) at 410-887-2059. Submit applications in-person or by mail to the Department of Social Services. After processing, the Department of Social Services will send a letter notifying the applicant of eligibility status.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County provides grants to help residential property owners mitigate flooding problems on their properties through structural floodproofing solutions or localized green infrastructure projects. Eligibility is determined on a case-by-case basis following a thorough review of drainage conditions on the specific property. The program aims to reduce flooding risk for homeowners by funding a range of eligible improvements tailored to each property's needs.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided to residential property owners to fund eligible flood mitigation projects. Eligible improvements include basement waterproofing, elevation of mechanical systems like water heaters and furnaces, exterior curbs with fill and grading around doors and windows, stairwell elevation with fill and grading, rain barrels, permeable pavers, bioswales, rain gardens, French drains with sump pump eligibility, and dry wells. The specific grant amount and terms are determined on a case-by-case basis following a thorough review of drainage conditions on the property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners in Baltimore County experiencing flooding problems on their properties and seeking to reduce flooding risk on their homes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Residential property owners can use grant funds for structural floodproofing solutions such as basement waterproofing, elevation of mechanical systems, exterior curbs with fill and grading, and stairwell elevation, as well as localized green infrastructure projects including rain barrels, permeable pavers, bioswales, rain gardens, French drains with sump pump, and dry wells.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland. The County is not permitted by County Code to make improvements to private property; improvements must be implemented by the property owner or a private contractor.
requirements_list: Property must be located in Baltimore County
Affected parties must apply for the program
County must determine through case-by-case review that residential flood mitigation is the most impactful and economical option for addressing the flooding problem
Thorough review of drainage conditions on the property must be completed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Affected property owners experiencing flooding problems are invited to apply by reviewing the program documents. The application process includes submission of a Baltimore County Application for Financial Assistance. The County reviews drainage conditions on a case-by-case basis and determines eligibility. Upon approval, a Residential Flood Mitigation Grant Agreement is executed with the property owner.

structured_extraction.program_description: Services designed to provide assistance to eligible adults with serious and persistent mental illness who need psychiatric rehabilitation in a supervised residential setting. Services include help with daily living activities, community integration, medication monitoring, and development of independent living skills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Supervised residential care and rehabilitation services for adults with serious and persistent mental illness, including assistance with activities of daily living, community integration, medication monitoring, and independent living skills development. Residents are expected to contribute to the cost of care according to their ability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County adults with serious and persistent mental illness who need psychiatric rehabilitation in a residential setting
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Residential rehabilitation services including housing, meals, medication monitoring, and skills development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County only
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Baltimore County
Must have a diagnosis that meets the priority population definition for adults
Must be eligible for Medical Assistance
Must have a clear need for psychiatric rehabilitation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicant completes RRP services application and submits by mail or fax to the Residential Specialist.

structured_extraction.program_description: Virtual workshop on effective resume writing strategies, including introduction and summary of education, experience, and expertise.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free virtual workshop teaching effective resume writing strategies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers preparing resumes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in resume writing strategies and presentation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for the virtual workshop. Check the Upcoming Events list for dates and times.

structured_extraction.program_description: The SALS Program provides monthly financial assistance to eligible Baltimore County residents to help low and moderate income seniors afford assisted living in small group homes licensed by the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene for four to 16 residents. The subsidy covers the cost of services including meals, personal care, and 24-hour supervision for elderly residents who are frail and unable to live independently. The program is also known as the Senior Assisted Living Group Home Subsidy and provides up to $1,000 toward the cost of an assisted living group home facility for qualifying seniors age 62 and older.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly financial assistance of up to $1,000 is paid on behalf of eligible residents to cover the cost of assisted living services in licensed group homes, including meals, personal care, and 24-hour supervision. Financial eligibility: one person income limit $4,358/month with assets not exceeding $20,064; two people asset limit $26,400.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents age 62 or older who are low and moderate income seniors, require personal care assistance, and cannot afford assisted living in a licensed group home.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The subsidy covers the cost of assisted living services in licensed group homes, including meals, personal care, and 24-hour supervision.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County (other counties also offer this program).
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Must be at least 62 years of age
Must require personal care assistance and complete a Functional Assessment to determine level of care
Monthly income cannot exceed $4,358 for an individual
Assets cannot exceed $20,064 for one person or $26,400 for two people
Must reside in a facility or be approved for entrance into a facility that has a service agreement with the Department of Aging
Eligible for a limited number of assisted living group home residencies
Low and moderate income
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Department of Aging Housing Office at 410-887-4632 or Maryland Access Point at 410-887-2594 to obtain the application or learn more about eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: A five-week course designed for senior adults with little to no computer experience, covering basic computer functions, internet navigation, and email communication.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free five-week in-person training course covering basic personal computer functions, internet navigation, and sending and receiving emails.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior adults with little to no computer experience
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in basic computer functions, internet navigation, and email communication
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Career Center to register. Course offered at Liberty, Hunt Valley, and Eastpoint Career Centers.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland program that helps eligible residents lower their prescription drug costs by providing assistance with Medicare Part D premiums and reducing overall medication costs for people who may not qualify for full Extra Help.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides up to $100 toward the monthly Medicare Part D premium and permits beneficiaries to change Part D plans once mid-year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents with limited income who need additional financial assistance paying for prescription medications. Single individuals with gross income under $47,880 per year or $3,990 per month, or couples with gross income under $64,920 per year or $5,410 per month.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medicare Part D premiums and prescription medication costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Single: gross income under $47,880 per year or $3,990 per month
Couple: gross income under $64,920 per year or $5,410 per month
Assets are not counted in eligibility determination
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call SHIP at 410-887-2059 or apply through the Maryland Senior Prescription Drug Assistance Program (SPDAP) by calling 1-800-551-5995 or visiting www.marylandspdap.com.

structured_extraction.program_description: One-time emergency assistance for seniors with limited income and assets.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time emergency assistance. Financial eligibility: one person income $2,608 with assets $11,000; two people income $3,525 with assets $14,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income seniors with emergency needs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency assistance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: One-time only assistance
Meet income limits: $2,608 for one person or $3,525 for two people
Meet asset limits: $11,000 for one person or $14,000 for two people

structured_extraction.program_description: The SFC program provides counseling and in-home services to strengthen and maintain families and prevent family breakdown. It serves low-income families whose problems threaten to dissolve the family unit or lead to chronic dysfunction, and families receiving temporary cash assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers counseling, in-home services, and connection to community resources. It targets families with total family income at or below 80 percent of the state median income (adjusted for family size).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income families with children, including families receiving temporary cash assistance
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counseling, in-home services, and referrals to community resources to strengthen families and prevent dissolution or dysfunction
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: Family income at or below 80 percent of state median income (adjusted for family size)
Or currently receiving temporary cash assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-853-3000 and select option one to learn more about the program

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore County Fire Department provides smoke alarms and installation at no cost to residents of Baltimore County. The program is available to all residents but is designed to help residents at higher risk of residential fires.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fire department provides smoke alarms and installation services at no cost to eligible residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Baltimore County, with emphasis on those at higher risk of residential fires.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Smoke alarms and installation in residential properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County only.
requirements_list: Applicants must be residents of Baltimore County
Applicants must fill out the program form to determine if they qualify
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents fill out a form with their contact information and property information to determine eligibility. The form asks whether the applicant is the property owner, if the property is hardwired for smoke alarms, and if there are currently any working alarms in the property.

structured_extraction.program_description: A subsidized surgical program providing spay and neuter services for Baltimore County resident-owned cats and dogs. The package includes the surgery, rabies vaccine, additional vaccines, deworming, a county animal license, and microchip.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A complete spay or neuter surgical package including rabies vaccine, additional vaccines (distemper and Bordetella for dogs), deworming, county animal license for Baltimore County residents, and microchip. Total cost is $20 per pet. Appointments are required and payment is required at time of scheduling. Services are available at the Dundalk Spay and Neuter Surgical Center.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing program with no specific deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents who own cats or dogs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Spay and neuter surgical services for pets, including related vaccines, deworming, microchip, and animal license.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County residents and Baltimore County-owned cats and dogs only. Rescue and foster groups are not eligible.
requirements_list: Pet owner must be a Baltimore County resident
Pet must reside in Baltimore County
Dogs cannot be boxers, bulldogs (all breeds), pugs, or Shih Tzus (other short-faced and mixed breeds evaluated case by case)
Dogs must be at least four months old and no older than six years
Dogs must weigh at least five pounds and no more than 60 pounds if female or 80 pounds if male
Cats cannot be hairless, Himalayan, or Persian
Cats must be at least five months old and no older than six years
Cats must weigh at least five pounds
Pet cannot have known illness, injury, or medical condition
Pet cannot present increased anesthetic risk (feline leukemia, heart murmurs, kidney disease, seizure disorder, retained testicles, upper respiratory infections)
Appointments are required; walk-ins not accepted
Valid email address required for pre-surgical documents
Owner must drop off pet to sign consent forms and provide medical history
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request an appointment online through the county website or clinic scheduling system. Provide accurate pet information including gender and weight. Complete payment by credit card at time of scheduling. You will receive a confirmation email when your appointment is accepted. Bring medical records if available. Arrive by 8 a.m. on surgery day with pet in carrier (cats) or on non-retractable leash (dogs). Owner signs consent and provides medical history at drop-off. Pet is discharged the same day; pick-up time assigned in morning but not before 3 p.m. If unable to pick up at assigned time, pet is transferred to main shelter location.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps people with limited income pay for their Medicare Part B premiums, eliminating the monthly premium cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program pays for Medicare Part B premiums, which are $202.90 per month. It does not cover deductibles or copayments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with limited income who are Medicare beneficiaries. Single individuals with gross income under $21,792 per year or $1,816 per month, or couples with gross income under $29,460 per year or $2,455 per month, with resources under $9,950 (single) or $14,910 (couple).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medicare Part B premiums.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland
requirements_list: Single: gross income under $21,792 per year or $1,816 per month and resources under $9,950
Couple: gross income under $29,460 per year or $2,455 per month and resources under $14,910
Certain types of income are not counted: the first $65 of monthly wages and one-half of monthly wages after the $65 is deducted
Assets do not include $1,500 per person burial allowance
Must reapply each year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request an application by calling the State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) at 410-887-2059. Submit applications in-person or by mail to the Department of Social Services. After processing, the Department of Social Services will send a letter notifying the applicant of eligibility status.

structured_extraction.program_description: A mental health initiative that partners with the Maryland Division of Rehabilitation Services to provide employment opportunities and support for eligible adults with mental illness. Services include job readiness training, job coaching, assistance finding employment, and ongoing support to maintain employment in the community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employment support services including job readiness training, job coaching, assistance with job search and placement, and ongoing support to help maintain employment in the community for eligible adults with mental illness.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County adults with mental illness who want employment support and assistance finding and maintaining jobs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment services including job training, coaching, and placement support
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County only
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Must have a mental illness
Must be eligible for publicly-funded mental health services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Adult Services Team at 410-887-3828 to learn more and enroll in the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Surviving Spouses of Fallen Law Enforcement Officers or Rescue Workers Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for the surviving spouse of a law enforcement officer or rescue worker, including volunteers, who died in the State of Maryland during the course of or as a result of their employment with Baltimore County. The credit equals 100 percent of the Baltimore County real property tax obligation and continues from year to year without requiring reapplication after initial approval.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 100 percent property tax credit on Baltimore County real property tax obligations. The credit continues from year to year without the need for further application after initial approval. The credit applies only to the real property tax portion of the bill and does not include other charges such as utilities or special assessments.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before September 30 in the taxable year for which the credit is desired to begin
structured_extraction.contact_name: Property Tax Credit Administration / Taxpayer Services
structured_extraction.program_audience: Surviving spouses of law enforcement officers or rescue workers, including volunteers, who died in the State of Maryland during the course of or as a result of their employment with Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit applied to Baltimore County real property tax obligations only. Does not include other charges on the tax bill.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland only. The death must have occurred in the State of Maryland during employment with Baltimore County. The surviving spouse must have been domiciled in Maryland at the time of death or acquired the dwelling within two years of the date of death. The credit applies solely to Baltimore County real property tax.
requirements_list: Applicant must be the surviving spouse of a law enforcement officer or rescue worker (including a volunteer)
The death must have occurred in the State of Maryland during the course of or as a result of the individual's employment with Baltimore County

The dwelling was owned by the decedent at the time of death, OR the decedent or surviving spouse was domiciled in the state as of the date of death and the dwelling was acquired by the spouse within two years of the date of death, OR the dwelling was acquired after the surviving spouse qualified for a credit for a former dwelling
The credit cannot be combined with any other credit or tax relief program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an Application for Surviving Spouse of a Fallen Law Enforcement Officer or Rescue Worker to the Property Tax Credit Administration on or before September 30 in the taxable year for which the credit is desired to begin. Mail the application to: Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration, 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, Maryland 21204. Once approved, the credit continues from year to year without the need for reapplication.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tai Chi Quan: Move for Better Balance
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that empowers adults 60 years and older to carry out health behaviors that reduce the risks of falls through Tai Chi classes that improve balance, strength, physical performance, postural stability, walking, self-management, and quality of life.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Classes meet two days a week for 12 weeks. Partially funded under Title III-D of the Older Americans Act of 1965. Individuals 60 and over are encouraged to make a suggested donation of $25 at the time of registration. Space is limited; pre-registration is required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults 60 and over
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training program for balance improvement and fall prevention
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County at Arbutus, Cockeysville, Edgemere, Liberty, Overlea-Fullerton, Reisterstown, Rosedale, and Victory Villa senior centers
requirements_list: Age 60 and over
Pre-registration required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact senior centers directly to register

structured_extraction.program_description: Bond financing available to manufacturers and 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations. Bond proceeds may be used to finance the acquisition and improvement of land, buildings, plant and equipment, including new construction or facility expansion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bond financing available from $2.5 million to a maximum of $10 million. Bond proceeds may be used to finance the acquisition and improvement of land, buildings, plant and equipment, including new construction or facility expansion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Manufacturers and 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and improvement of land, buildings, plant and equipment, including new construction or facility expansion
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: Applicant must be a manufacturer or 501(c)(3) non-profit organization
Financing range: $2.5 million to $10 million
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Baltimore County business development representative by calling 410-887-8000 or emailing businesshelp@baltimorecountymd.gov to learn more and apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A rural reforestation program administered by Baltimore County that converts lawn or grass areas of one acre or larger into forested ecosystems at no cost to eligible landowners. The program plants approximately 200 native trees per acre, spaced 15 feet apart in staggered rows, and provides deer and pest protection through stakes and shelters. Trees are planted in the fall, and the program includes three years of free maintenance with a 90 percent survival guarantee. The program focuses on reforestation and does not include planting of evergreens or small groupings of trees intended for landscaping or privacy screening.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County plants 200 native trees per acre to create rural reforestations at no cost to the landowner. Trees are planted in the fall, spaced 15 feet apart in staggered rows, with deer and pest protection provided through stakes and shelters. The program includes three years of free maintenance following planting, with a 90 percent survival guarantee. Maintenance includes seasonal mowing, vine and invasive species management, shelter upkeep, watering during drought, and pesticide or herbicide application as needed. Yearly inspections are conducted during the maintenance period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County property owners and landowners with one acre or more of open space (lawn or grass) away from utility easements, Forest Conservation Easements, septic systems, and septic reserves. Intended for larger tracts of open land suitable for rural reforestation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting and three years of maintenance for converting turf or lawn areas to forested ecosystems on eligible residential or rural properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County only
requirements_list: Property must have one acre or more of open space (lawn or grass)
Open space must be away from utility easements
Open space must be away from Forest Conservation Easements
Open space must be away from septic systems and septic reserves
Applicant must submit a Reforestation Property Form
Must be a Baltimore County landowner
Program focuses on reforestation and does not include planting of evergreens or small groupings of trees intended for landscaping or privacy screening
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Turf to Trees page on the Baltimore County website to learn about the process and submit a Reforestation Property Form to determine eligibility. Interested landowners may also contact the Forestry Management Division directly for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Urban Reforestation Program for Managed Grounds
structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing urban tree plantings for managed grounds such as homeowners associations, apartment complexes, and businesses to maintain and increase tree canopy in densely populated areas. Plantings include landscape-style trees and larger shade trees in County public rights-of-way and park settings.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county plants native trees at no cost to the property owner. Projects must include 20 trees or more. Urban tree plantings come with an initial one year of maintenance and 100 percent survival guarantee. Maintenance may include watering, pruning, and shelter upkeep. EPS conducts two inspections during the maintenance period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: HOAs, businesses, property managers, and apartment complex operators in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Urban tree planting on managed grounds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, with priority for areas inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line and Census Designated Places.
requirements_list: Project must include 20 trees or more
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: HOAs, businesses, and property managers may request an urban reforestation planting by emailing forestmanagement@baltimorecountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program for qualifying waterfront businesses in Baltimore County. Funds can be used for exterior improvements to waterfront properties such as bulkhead repair, slip renovations, signage, landscaping, and facade improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans for the lesser of 90 percent of the project cost or $75,000. Loan terms are seven years with zero percent interest.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualifying waterfront businesses in Baltimore County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior improvements including bulkhead repair, slip renovations, signage, landscaping, facade improvements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County waterfront
requirements_list: Business must be a waterfront business
Business must be located in Baltimore County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Baltimore County business development representative by calling 410-887-8000 or emailing businesshelp@baltimorecountymd.gov to learn more and apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Association Restoration, Planning and Implementation Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore County Department of Environmental Protection and Sustainability awards annual grants to locally-based watershed associations and nonprofit organizations to identify and implement restoration projects and educational activities that help restore local watersheds, increase public participation in watershed restoration, and meet water quality requirements. The program also supports commercial green infrastructure and landscaping improvements that provide cooling shade, beautiful landscapes, and reduce stormwater runoff into local streams.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $30,000 are available to cover staff hours dedicated to conducting environmental restoration activities and increasing public awareness of environmental stewardship. Funds support salaries for staff conducting restoration planning and implementation and watershed education and outreach. Fringe benefits up to 30 percent of salary and indirect costs up to 10 percent of combined salary and fringe may be included. The ratio of staff hours to dollars must be a minimum of one hour of staff time for every $30 in grant funds requested. Additionally, grants are available for green infrastructure and landscaping improvements for businesses and organizations, including stormwater management and cooling shade installations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Locally-based watershed associations and community groups with membership in Baltimore County that are registered as 501(c)(3), 501(c)(4), or 501(c)(6) nonprofit organizations in good standing with the State of Maryland. Also open to businesses, homeowners associations, neighborhood associations, congregations, and community organizations in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating expenses to foster staffing capacity for ongoing restoration work and watershed education and outreach. Funds support salaries for staff conducting restoration planning, implementation, and watershed education activities. Materials and equipment are not funded. Eligible restoration activities include tree plantings, stormwater best management practice design and maintenance, downspout disconnections, rain gardens, rain barrels, stream cleanups, stream monitoring programs, conservation landscapes, watershed education and outreach, invasive plant removal, and storm drain marking. Also supports green infrastructure improvements including landscaping, stormwater management, and cooling shade installations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All grant-funded activities must be implemented in Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Be a locally-based watershed association or community group with membership in Baltimore County
Be a registered 501(c)(3), 501(c)(4), or 501(c)(6) organization in good standing with the State of Maryland
Have a demonstrated history of successfully identifying and conducting resident-based and community restoration projects
Have fulfilled all grant requirements on past grants if previously funded through this grant program
Link all planned restoration actions to Small Watershed Action Plans (SWAPs), Total Maximum Daily Load (TMDL) Implementation Plans, or the Trash and Litter Reduction Strategy as appropriate
Offer a Stream Watch program to engage volunteers in monitoring streams and reporting pollution
Participate in Baltimore County watershed planning steering and implementation committees
Follow Baltimore County guidance on tree plantings, tree giveaways, and stormwater best management practices
Coordinate with DEPS on inspection and verification of past planting projects and other best management practices per Maryland Department of Environment guidelines
Maintain a minimum ratio of one hour of staff time for every $30 in grant funds requested
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit three components: (1) Complete the DEPS Watershed Grant Application Questions addressing organization eligibility, planned restoration and stewardship activities, grant deliverables by quarter, Stream Watch participation, watershed planning involvement, linking actions to watershed plans, education and outreach plans, capacity building efforts, project guidance and inspections, and past year accomplishments. (2) Complete the standard Baltimore County Application for Financial Assistance (AFA) form. (3) Submit all required supporting documents including proof of good standing, detailed budget proposal, financial statements, and any additional attachments. Email all materials as separate PDF files to Erin Watts at ewatts@baltimorecountymd.gov with the subject line [Organization's Initials] – FY XX Grant Application. structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grants that help homeowners reduce risk from natural hazards like flooding and cliff erosion. Grants cover up to 75% of project costs for mitigation work, with homeowners responsible for the remaining 25% and any cost overruns.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants covering up to 75 percent of project costs for hazard mitigation projects. Eligible projects include acquisition and demolition of high-hazard properties, elevation of structures in flood plains, and other mitigation measures to reduce risk from natural hazards. Homeowners are responsible for the remaining 25 percent of costs and any project cost overruns. Funding is provided through the Flood Mitigation Assistance program (currently available) and the Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC) program (currently suspended as of April 2025). Grant amounts and specific funding availability vary by program year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 1st for pre-screening questionnaire; August 31st for final application materials
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners with high-hazard properties, particularly those in flood plains or along cliffs, and properties with repetitive or severe repetitive flood losses under the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and demolition of structures, elevation of structures above base flood elevation, mitigation of cliff erosion risks, and other hazard mitigation projects to reduce risk from natural hazards including flooding and coastal erosion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Calvert County. High-risk houses along cliffs and NFIP Repetitive Loss or Severe Repetitive Loss properties are most competitive. Elevation projects are available for properties in the flood plain with flood insurance through the National Flood Insurance Program. Priority consideration given to properties with documented history of repetitive losses.
requirements_list: Property appraisal (for acquisition and demolition projects)
Plat survey of the property
Color photos of the house
Copy of National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) insurance policy (for flood projects)
Documentation of past flood events including dates and damages (for flood projects)
Certified imminent threat letter from a licensed engineer (for cliff mitigation projects)
Itemized cost estimate for demolition or elevation work from qualified contractor
Elevation certificate completed by certified surveyor or engineer (for elevation projects)
Certified structural stability letter from a licensed engineer (for elevation projects)
Proof of property ownership
Evidence of financial need or inability to fund project without assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete and submit the Pre-Screening Questionnaire by July 1st. 2. County staff will contact the homeowner to discuss project eligibility and request additional information. 3. Submit all required final application materials to the Calvert County Division of Emergency Management by August 31st. 4. Refer to the appropriate homeowner guide (Acquisition and Demolition Guide or Elevation Guide) for detailed instructions and documentation requirements. 5. County staff develops subapplications for submission to FEMA in November. 6. FEMA reviews and scores all applications. 7. FEMA releases final funding decisions in late summer. 8. Approved projects begin kick-off and implementation in mid-spring of the following year. Note: Processing times and funding availability depend on annual FEMA appropriations and program cycles.

requirements_list: Property must be located in a designated historic district in Calvert County
Work must comply with Secretary of Interior Standards for Historic Preservation

Applicant must submit pre-approval application prior to starting work or application after work completion
Applicant must provide invoices, contractor licenses, photographs (before and after), and documentation of work performed

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. structured_extraction.program_description: A fund established to allow Agricultural Preservation District owners to sell Transferable Development Rights to the county. Unlike typical TDR transactions that move density, this program retires TDRs, removing development potential entirely to preserve land.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Agricultural Preservation District owners can sell TDRs to the county at a price set by the Board of County Commissioners based on Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board recommendation. For Fiscal Year 2026, the approved purchase price is $6,230 per TDR. Landowners submit applications during the specified application window (September through December). TDRs purchased by the county are permanently retired and removed from the market, reducing overall development potential in the county. This ensures that development rights cannot be transferred to receiving areas, thus preserving agricultural and forest lands in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural Preservation District owners seeking to sell development rights to the county for permanent retirement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Landowners receive payment for TDRs sold to the county at the approved rate per TDR. The retired TDRs are permanently removed from circulation, preserving agricultural and forest lands. Proceeds from the sale belong to the landowner.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Agricultural Preservation District owners throughout Calvert County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must own property located within a designated Agricultural Preservation District in Calvert County
Must be an eligible Agricultural Preservation District owner as defined by county regulations
Property must not have outstanding liens that would prevent conveyance, or applicant must obtain lien holder consent for conveyance of TDRs
Applications are evaluated and ranked by the Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board based on established criteria
Applicants must complete and submit the official PAR application form during the designated application period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted during a designated window (typically September through December each year). During January, applications are reviewed and ranked by the Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board according to established selection criteria. Offer letters are sent from January through February to successful applicants, ranked until available funding is exhausted. Once an offer is accepted, a conveyance document is executed transferring the TDRs to the county. Transactions are concluded by June of the fiscal year. The purchase price is established annually by the Board of County Commissioners based on the Advisory Board's recommendation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows agricultural land owners to sell the development potential of their property to another party. The sale requires recording restrictive covenants that permanently restrict development on the sending property. Purchasers can use TDRs to increase density on receiving properties in designated growth areas, helping to preserve farms and forest lands.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners in Agricultural Preservation Districts can certify Transferable Development Rights (TDRs) based on acreage (1 TDR per acre), adjusted for existing residences (5 TDRs deducted per residence) and grandfathered lots (5 TDRs added per unused authorized lot). Once certified, TDRs can be sold to other parties or listed on the County's TDRs for Sale list. Receiving property owners can purchase TDRs to increase residential and commercial density in designated receiving areas, which must be located within county residential or commercial growth zones. The program facilitates private market transactions between sellers and buyers of development rights.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural land owners with properties in Agricultural Preservation Districts (APDs) seeking to sell development rights, and receiving property owners in designated growth areas seeking to purchase development rights to increase density.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: For sending property owners: Proceeds from TDR sales are retained by the landowner with no restrictions on use. For receiving property owners: TDRs purchased are used to increase residential and commercial density potential on properties located in designated receiving areas within county growth zones.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Agricultural Preservation Districts (APDs) in Calvert County serve as sending areas where development rights can be certified and sold. Designated receiving areas exist within county residential and commercial growth zones where TDRs can be used to increase density. Both sending and receiving areas must comply with county zoning and growth management policies.
requirements_list: Property must be located in an Agricultural Preservation District (APD)
APD covenant must be recorded on the property
TDR certification requires application approval by the Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board (APAB)
TDR certification must be approved by the Board of County Commissioners (BOCC)
TDRs are calculated based on gross acreage, minus existing residences (5 TDRs deducted per residence), plus grandfathered lots (5 TDRs added per unused authorized lot)
Development rights being transferred must be permanently restricted through recordation of restrictive covenants
For TDR use on receiving properties: Receiving property must be located in designated receiving areas (residential or commercial growth zones)
Receiving property must comply with county zoning requirements to utilize TDRs for increased density
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Landowner submits Application for TDR Certification to Calvert County planning department. 2. County staff calculates the number of TDRs available based on property acreage, existing residences, and grandfathered lots using the established formula. 3. Application is submitted to the Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board (APAB) for review and recommendation. 4. APAB forwards recommendation to the Board of County Commissioners (BOCC) for final approval. 5. Upon BOCC approval, TDR certification is recorded in the county land records. 6. Landowner receives TDR certificate and can then sell TDRs through private transactions or list them on the County's TDRs for Sale list. 7. Purchaser records Conveyance of Development Rights document (with or without lienholder) in land records. 8. County staff assists with TDR allocation and tracking to ensure proper use on receiving properties.

structured_extraction.program_description: A county-administered revolving fund that allows citizens to buy and sell Transferable Development Rights through the government rather than through private negotiations. The county purchases TDRs from Agricultural Preservation District owners and sells them to developers and other property owners.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Sellers: Receive $6,230 per TDR on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to available funding. Buyers: Purchase TDRs at the price paid by the county plus a 1% administrative fee. TDRs can be used to increase density potential in designated residential growth areas. The program operates as a county revolving fund, meaning proceeds from TDR sales are reinvested back into the program to purchase additional TDRs from sellers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural Preservation District owners wishing to sell TDRs, and developers or property owners wishing to purchase TDRs for density increases.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: TDR sellers receive payment for development rights from their properties in Agricultural Preservation Districts. Purchasers use TDRs to increase density potential on their properties in designated receiving areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Agricultural Preservation District owners throughout Calvert County and to purchasers in designated residential growth areas.
requirements_list: Sellers must own TDRs from Agricultural Preservation Districts or be owners of record of TDRs conveyed from original APD
TDRs must be certified by Calvert County
Purchases subject to available funding and TDR supply
Sellers must complete Application to Sell TDR
Buyers must complete Application to Purchase TDR
Transactions processed through the county revolving fund
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete separate applications depending on whether they are selling or purchasing TDRs. Sellers apply on a first-come, first-served basis when funding is available, and must provide proof of TDR ownership and certification. Buyers submit purchase applications specifying the number of TDRs desired and their intended use in designated growth areas. The county processes both applications and facilitates transactions through the revolving fund, with funding subject to program availability.

requirements_list: Located in Calvert County
Property adjacent to streams or on slopes of 25% or greater
Applicant must provide matching funds or in-kind contributions
Project must focus on native tree species appropriate for water quality protection and erosion control
Applicant must be able to maintain planted trees for a specified period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should contact the Calvert County Department of Public Works or Environmental Services for application materials and guidelines. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Applicants must submit project proposals including site plans, species selection, budget, and maintenance plans. Projects are evaluated based on ecological benefit, erosion reduction potential, and water quality improvement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A subscription program that protects Caroline County residents from unexpected medical expenses by ensuring that enrolled individuals will not be charged for ambulance transportation to the hospital in the event of an emergency.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides subsidized ambulance transportation to the hospital at no charge to enrolled members. Individual membership costs $25, family of two costs $45, family of three or more costs $75. Business plans cost $100 for up to 10 employees, $150 for 11-25 employees, and $200 for businesses with more than 25 employees. Enrollment guarantees no charges for emergency ambulance transportation by Caroline County providers to the hospital. Membership is valid for one year from the date of enrollment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Caroline County residents and businesses seeking protection from unexpected ambulance transportation costs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enrollment fees support Caroline County's emergency service providers, including eight volunteer fire companies and county paramedics.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Caroline County residents and businesses located in Caroline County.
requirements_list: Applicant must provide address of residence or business to be covered by plan
Applicant must select appropriate plan type based on household or business size
Family members or employees listed must be consistent with selected plan level
Membership provides coverage for emergency ambulance transportation only
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the enrollment form online with personal or business information, select the appropriate plan type, provide address details, and agree to authorization terms. After form submission, applicants are directed to a payment processing page. Membership becomes effective upon payment processing.

structured_extraction.program_description: Competitive grant funding to support opioid remediation, prevention, and support services for Caroline County residents. Funds come from national legal settlements with opioid manufacturers and distributors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time competitive grants totaling $250,000 for fiscal year 2027. Funding amounts range from unspecified minimum to amounts determined by the grant review process. Funds must be used for opioid mitigation and remediation activities between July 1, 2026, and June 30, 2027. Applications may receive partial funding depending on available resources and alignment with program goals. Funds must be used exclusively within the stated performance period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations that have operated in Caroline County for at least two years and are registered or authorized to conduct business in Maryland. County agencies and departments are also eligible to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Opioid remediation, prevention, and support services for Caroline County residents. Funds must be used exclusively for opioid mitigation activities consistent with national opioid settlement agreements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Caroline County only. Services and programs must benefit Caroline County residents and communities.
requirements_list: Nonprofit organizations must have been operating in Caroline County for at least two consecutive years prior to application
Nonprofit organizations must be registered or otherwise authorized to conduct business in the State of Maryland
County agencies and departments are eligible applicants
All proposed activities must be directly related to opioid mitigation and remediation
Funds must be used exclusively between July 1, 2026, and June 30, 2027
Services must benefit Caroline County residents
Applicants must complete all required forms including cover letter, grant application, and Exhibit E (National Agreement)
Proposed programs must align with opioid settlement priorities and eligible use categories
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit a complete application package including: (1) a cover letter introducing the organization and proposed project; (2) the completed FY27 Caroline County Opioid Grant Application form with detailed project description, budget, and outcomes; and (3) Exhibit E documenting compliance with National Opioid Settlement Agreement requirements. All documents must be submitted to Stacy Seward, Grant Coordinator, in the Caroline County Office of Finance by 4:30 p.m. on February 6, 2026. Applications must address how the proposed activities support opioid remediation goals and serve Caroline County residents. Award decisions will be made based on competitive review of alignment with program priorities, feasibility, and organizational capacity.

Qualified project expenses eligible for reimbursement

structured_extraction.program_name: Carroll County Difficult to Serve – Long Driveway Grant Program (Home Stretch – Difficult to Serve Properties Grant)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program funded through the State of Maryland's FY24 Home Stretch – Difficult to Serve Properties Grant that provides financial assistance to Carroll County homeowners with driveways too long for internet service providers to connect for free as part of standard installation. The program provides up to $14,000 per qualifying property to cover the cost of extending broadband, internet, or cable TV infrastructure from the service provider's existing infrastructure to the applicant's home. Only homes that already have an internet service provider passing by the property are eligible. The program aims to close the broadband connectivity gap for hard-to-reach residential properties in Carroll County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $14,000 in grant funding per qualifying property to cover the cost of connecting homes with long driveways to broadband, internet, or cable TV service. For connection costs exceeding $14,000, the homeowner is responsible for the balance. The grant does not cover equipment or services. Only one grant is available per house or address, and the grant is not retroactive — homeowners who have already paid to connect are not eligible for reimbursement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Carroll County homeowners with long driveways that prevent internet service providers from offering a free connection as part of standard installation, where a provider already passes the property with existing broadband, internet, or cable TV infrastructure.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding covers the cost of extending broadband, internet, or cable TV infrastructure from the service provider's existing infrastructure to the applicant's home with a long driveway. Does not cover equipment or services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Carroll County, Maryland. Eligible properties must have existing broadband, internet, or cable TV infrastructure passing by the property. Homes located in areas scheduled for future broadband installation are not eligible.
requirements_list: Property must be located in Carroll County
Home must have existing broadband, internet, or cable TV infrastructure currently passing by the property
Driveway must be longer than what an internet service provider will connect for free as part of standard installation
Home cannot be located in areas scheduled for future broadband installation
Only one grant is available per house or address (homes with apartments or businesses cannot apply for multiple grants)
Grant is not retroactive — homeowners who have already paid to connect are not eligible for reimbursement
Grant does not cover equipment or services
Maximum grant amount is $14,000 per property; costs above this are the homeowner's responsibility
Interested parties should complete the Carroll County Broadband Survey and answer yes to the long driveway question
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested Carroll County residents should complete the Carroll County Residential Broadband Survey at https://carrollcountymd.jotform.com/form/230754830587059 and indicate 'yes' to the long driveway question (question 16: 'Do you have a long driveway where you have been told you will have to pay to get your house connected?'), providing their name, full address, phone number, and email address. Once the grant is awarded to Carroll County, all survey respondents who answered yes will be notified by email with application details. Submitted applications are verified by the county with the service provider for eligibility, and applicants receive an email regarding the eligibility status of their property. Note: The program is currently no longer accepting applications.

Classes meet once a week for 2.5 hours over six consecutive weeks and cover stress management, strength and endurance activities, communication skills, healthy lifestyle development, problem-solving with health care teams, action planning, symptom management, and goal-setting. Both virtual and in-person options may be available depending on the county.

Participants receive a copy of 'Living a Healthy Life with Chronic Conditions' textbook upon program completion. Led by trained facilitators. A minimum number of participants is required for the program to be offered.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in diabetes self-management training workshops covering stress management, strength and endurance activities, communication and decision-making skills, healthy lifestyle development, problem-solving with health care teams, action planning, symptom management, and goal-setting.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Legally blind individuals with central visual acuity of 20/200 or less in the better eye, or those with significant field defects, who are Maryland residents and own their principal residence
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax exemption for principal dwelling house and surrounding yard

requirements_list: Central visual acuity of 20/200 or less in the better eye with corrective glasses, OR central visual acuity of more than 20/200 with field defect in which the peripheral field has contracted to no greater than twenty degrees on the better eye
Doctor's certification from a licensed medical doctor or optometrist required

Must be the legal owner of the property

structured_extraction.program_name: Cecil County Enterprise Zone Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: Businesses locating in the Cecil County Enterprise Zone may earn income tax and real property tax credits in return for job creation and investments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real property tax credits provide an 80% credit against local real property taxes on a portion of real property improvements for the first five years, decreasing 10% annually to 30% in the tenth and final year. Income tax credits provide a one-time $1,000 credit per new worker, or $6,000 per economically disadvantaged employee over three years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses locating in the Cecil County Enterprise Zone
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Businesses must create jobs and make investments to be eligible for the credits. Property improvements and expansions can qualify for real property tax credits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in one of the 17 designated enterprise zones in Cecil County. The location of each zone is indicated on the Enterprise Zone map.
requirements_list: Business must be located in a designated Cecil County Enterprise Zone
For real property tax credits: must apply to the Office of Economic Development prior to completing the construction or expansion project
Property tax credits cannot be granted retroactively
New jobs must be created and investments must be made
For income tax credits: must hire new workers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses seeking property tax credits must apply to the Office of Economic Development prior to completing the construction or expansion project. Email the Office of Economic Development at EconomicDevelopment@cecilcountymd.gov for more information and application materials.

Training that contributes to, expands, or improves the company's production and competitiveness
50/50 matching cost share requirement (company must match grant funds)
Preference given to training conducted through Cecil College

structured_extraction.program_description: A marketing certification program that helps agricultural producers in Cecil County promote their locally grown products. Farmers and agricultural businesses can use the Cecil Grown logo on marketing materials, labels, and packaging to help consumers identify products grown or raised in Cecil County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides registered farms with a high-resolution round Cecil Grown logo for use on marketing, packaging, and promotional materials. Participants also receive an "Our products are proudly Cecil Grown" banner to display at market stands or on-farm markets, and price signs to use on Cecil Grown products. Additional marketing materials may be available upon request. There is no fee to register with the Certified Cecil Grown Program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers and farmers operating in Cecil County who grow raw agricultural crops or produce value-added agricultural products in or using ingredients from Cecil County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Marketing and promotional materials including logos, banners, price signs, and other materials to help promote locally grown agricultural products.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Farm or agricultural business must operate in Cecil County, Maryland. Raw agricultural crops must be grown in Cecil County. Value-added products must use ingredients that are at least 75% grown in Cecil County.

Raw agricultural crops using the Cecil Grown logo must be grown in Cecil County
If producing a value-added agricultural product with non-local ingredients, at least 75% of inputs must be grown in Cecil County
If growing crops in Cecil County and offering a value-added product made outside the county, at least 75% of product inputs must be grown in Cecil County
Applicant must complete the Certified Cecil Grown Registration Form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prospective participants should complete the Certified Cecil Grown Registration Form and email it to Malik Grace at mgrace@cecilcountymd.gov. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with no specific deadline. Upon approval, registrants receive their marketing materials including the Cecil Grown logo, banners, and price signs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Opioid Restitution Fund (ORF) Community Grant Program – FY2027
structured_extraction.program_description: An annual funding program administered by Cecil County that distributes settlement funds from opioid pharmaceutical manufacturers and distributors to nonprofit, not-for-profit, and government agencies. Grants support community initiatives addressing substance use prevention, overdose response, treatment, and recovery support services. The program distributes approximately $1 million per fiscal year, with a maximum grant award of $100,000 per application. Eligible organizations may submit up to two applications, each addressing a different legislative provision as outlined in the Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA).
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual spring funding cycle distributing approximately $1 million in grants from opioid settlement funds. Maximum grant amount is $100,000 per application. Organizations may submit no more than two applications, each addressing a different legislative provision outlined in the Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA). Funds are generated from settlements with prescription opioid pharmaceutical manufacturers and distributors. Grant funding may be used for projects addressing one or more of the following Maryland State legislative provisions: (1) treatment of opioid use disorder and co-occurring substance use disorders; (2) prevention of opioid use disorder; (3) evidence-based recovery support services; (4) opioid antagonist and overdose response programs; (5) public health education and awareness programs; and (6) law enforcement support for opioid-related issues. Grants may support direct service provision, program development, capacity building, training, equipment purchase, and other activities necessary to implement eligible projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit, not-for-profit, and government agencies (state, county, and municipal) located within and/or serving Cecil County citizens.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects meeting Maryland State legislative provisions to address substance use prevention, overdose response, treatment, and recovery support services; prevention and treatment of substance use and opioid addiction. Eligible uses include direct service provision, program development and implementation, capacity building, staff training, equipment purchase, and other activities directly supporting opioid-related initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cecil County, Maryland. Organizations must be located within Cecil County and/or serve Cecil County citizens.
requirements_list: Organization must be a nonprofit, not-for-profit, or state, county, or municipal government agency
Organization must be located within and/or serving Cecil County citizens
Project must address substance use prevention, overdose, treatment, or recovery support services as defined by Maryland State legislative provisions
Project must meet one or more of the six Maryland State legislative provisions outlined in the FY27 ORF Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA)
Maximum grant request amount is $100,000 per application
Organizations may submit no more than two applications, each addressing a different legislative provision
Organizations must complete the FY27 ORF Application form and FY27 ORF Budget Template
Organizations must provide detailed project narrative describing how the project aligns with eligible legislative provisions
Organizations must demonstrate capacity to implement the proposed project and serve the target population
Organizations must provide evidence of community need and alignment with Cecil County priorities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the FY27 ORF Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) to understand the six eligible legislative provisions and program requirements. 2. Complete the FY27 ORF Application form with detailed project information and narrative. 3. Complete the FY27 ORF Budget Template, including all project costs and funding sources. 4. Ensure the project budget does not exceed $100,000. 5. Submit the completed application form and budget template by 5:00 PM on May 1, 2026. 6. Applications may be submitted by mail, email, or in person to the Cecil County Office. 7. All submissions must include the organization's name, contact information, project title, and EIN/Tax ID. 8. Applications will be reviewed for eligibility, completeness, and alignment with program priorities. 9. Grant awards will be announced following the review and selection process. 10. Refer to the FY27 ORF NOFA for additional application details, evaluation criteria, and post-award requirements.

The credit is applied directly to the annual property tax bill.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program funded by Video Lottery Terminal revenues to help businesses and organizations in Cecil County improve their exterior appearance and function along the Route 40 corridor. The program aims to enhance the visual appearance of the Route 40/Pulaski Highway business corridor and increase community utilization of businesses, while supporting economic growth and community revitalization in Cecil County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds up to $25,000 for revitalization projects or up to $50,000 for blight removal projects. Applicants must provide matching funds dollar-for-dollar (except for blight removal applications which may require no match). Funds are distributed on a reimbursement basis after project completion and submission of invoices and proof of expenditures. Matching funds must be documented and approved by Cecil County Government.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit businesses and organizations located in Cecil County along the Route 40/Pulaski Highway corridor that want to improve their exterior appearance and visual presence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior improvements visible from Route 40 including signage, lighting, siding, painting, entrance improvements, porches, decks, fencing, landscaping, hardscaping, sidewalks, driveways, parking areas, ADA ramps, and demolition or removal of blight. Up to 20% of grant funds may be used for related interior improvements with prior approval.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses and organizations must be located within Cecil County, Maryland, along the Route 40 corridor with a Route 40/Pulaski Highway address. The property must be on Route 40 and visible from Route 40.
requirements_list: Property must have a Route 40/Pulaski Highway address
Property must be on Route 40 and visible from Route 40
Applicant must be the owner or tenant of the property (tenants must provide written authorization from owner)
Applicants must match grant funds dollar-for-dollar (except blight removal applications)
Applicants must be in good standing with the IRS, State of Maryland, and Cecil County
Projects must improve exterior façade (up to 20% may be interior)
Existing businesses with residential accommodations must be clearly identified predominantly as a business with regular operating hours
One application per address
Project must be completed by June 30, 2026
Projects completed prior to application submission are ineligible
Grant funds cannot be used to pay off debt from prior projects
Design must be approved by Cecil County Government
Proof of insurance on property and business required
Two years of tax returns required if applicable
Business or organization must be located on Route 40
Project must improve exterior image and function of the property
Applicant must submit detailed cost estimates for all work
Applicant must provide current photos of property from Route 40
Applicant must demonstrate site control/ownership or authorization
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis beginning August 1, 2025. Applicants should contact the Grant Administrator (Lisa Crouse) to discuss their project before applying. Complete the application with cover sheet and submit with all required supporting documents including: two years of tax returns, proof of good standing with IRS and State of Maryland, current photos of property from Route 40, detailed cost estimates, documentation of matching funds, proof of insurance, evidence of site control, and for non-profits, IRS exemption determination letter. Applications may be submitted online through OpenGov portal, mailed to Cecil County Administration Building, emailed to lcrouse@cecilcountymd.gov, or dropped off in person. The Grant Review Committee evaluates applications on a rolling basis and notifies applicants by email of decisions. All work must be completed by June 30, 2026.
