structured_extraction.program_description: This program reimburses a limited amount of transportation costs each fiscal year for qualified senior citizens, people with disabilities, and low-income individuals who use Cecil Transit services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides reimbursement for transportation costs incurred through Cecil Transit bus services. For fiscal year 2026, eligible participants can receive up to $350 in reimbursement per person per fiscal year. A minimum reimbursement request of $50 is required. Participants must request and retain receipts from the driver for each transit ride and submit them with a completed TRP Reimbursement Request Form to claim reimbursement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing program; applications accepted throughout the fiscal year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior citizens age 60 and older, people with disabilities, and low-income individuals residing in Cecil County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for fares paid on Cecil Transit buses within Cecil County
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cecil County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a senior citizen (age 60 or older), person with a disability, or low-income individual
Must be a Cecil County resident
Must provide disability verification form (for people with disabilities) completed by a physician or healthcare provider
Must provide income certification form (for low-income individuals)
Must keep receipts from Cecil Transit rides
Each reimbursement request must total at least $50
Annual reimbursement limit is $350 per person per fiscal year
Must use receipts from Cecil Transit; reimbursement is only for fares paid on Cecil Transit buses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the Transportation Reimbursement Program Application form and submit it with appropriate verification documents (Disability Verification Form for people with disabilities or Income Certification Form for low-income individuals). 2. Once approved and deemed eligible, riders request receipts from the Cecil Transit driver for each bus ride. 3. Retain all receipts. 4. Complete the TRP Reimbursement Request Form with original receipts attached. 5. Submit the completed reimbursement request form to Cecil County. 6. Reimbursement will be processed up to the annual limit of $350 per person per fiscal year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Video Lottery Terminal (VLT) Local Community Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A funding program that distributes video lottery terminal revenue generated from the State's gaming facilities to nonprofit, not-for-profit, and government agencies located in or serving Cecil County. Funds support projects aligned with the County's Strategic Plan in the areas of Economic Development, Education, Infrastructure, and Safe, Healthy and Active Communities. Grants have traditionally supported public safety initiatives, economic and community development, public service projects, and projects addressing community needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual spring funding application process for fiscal year projects. Grants are awarded to various organizations to support local community programs and projects. Funds are generated from the State's video lottery terminals and gaming facilities. Organizations may apply for grants to support initiatives in Economic Development, Education, Infrastructure, and Safe, Healthy and Active Communities. Grants have traditionally been used to provide support for public safety initiatives, economic and community development, public service projects and programs, and projects addressing community needs. Funding is contingent on the passage of the County Executive's budget by the County Council. Applications must include a completed FY27 VLT Application form and FY27 VLT Budget Form.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit, not-for-profit, and government agencies (state, county, and municipal) located within and/or serving Cecil County citizens.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects supporting the County's Strategic Plan in the areas of Economic Development, Education, Infrastructure, and Safe, Healthy and Active Communities, including public safety initiatives, community development, and public service programs.

Project must align with County Strategic Plan areas (Economic Development, Education, Infrastructure, Safe/Healthy/Active Communities)
Funding is contingent on the passage of the County Executive's budget by the County Council
Applicant must complete the FY27 VLT Application form
Applicant must complete the FY27 VLT Budget Form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit a completed FY27 VLT Application and FY27 VLT Budget Form by the April 10, 2026 deadline. The FY27 Notice of Funding Availability provides detailed process and submission steps. All instructions, forms, and supporting materials are available on the Cecil County Local Community Grants page at https://www.cecilcountymd.gov/846/Local-Community-Grants. Applications should be submitted in accordance with the requirements outlined in the Notice of Funding Availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: A special-purpose rental housing assistance program funded by HUD that combines Housing Choice Vouchers with case management and clinical services provided by the Department of Veterans Affairs. The program is designed to help homeless veterans and their families find and afford rental housing. The VA provides comprehensive supportive services at VA medical centers and community-based outreach clinics. The program is administered locally by participating housing authorities, including Cecil County Housing and Prince George's County Housing Authority, as well as Rockville Housing Enterprises in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.agency: Cecil County / Prince George's County / Montgomery County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental assistance provided through Housing Choice Vouchers combined with case management and clinical services from the Department of Veterans Affairs. In Cecil County, veterans must be referred to Cecil County Housing by the Perry Point VA. In Prince George's County, the VA screens applicants and makes referrals to the Housing Authority. In Rockville/Montgomery County, applications are processed through Rockville Housing Enterprises. VA services are delivered at VA medical centers and community-based outreach clinics.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeless veterans and their families, including those at risk of homelessness, seeking rental housing assistance in Cecil County, Prince George's County, and the City of Rockville/Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental housing assistance and supportive case management and clinical services for eligible veterans
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cecil County (referrals from Perry Point VA required), Prince George's County, and City of Rockville/Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a veteran
Must be homeless or at risk of homelessness
Must be referred to Cecil County Housing by the Perry Point VA (for Cecil County applicants)
The Department of Veterans Affairs screens applicants and makes referrals to the Housing Authority (for Prince George's County applicants)
Must meet specific program eligibility criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Veterans seeking rental assistance should contact their local VA office to be screened and referred to the appropriate local housing authority. In Cecil County, contact the Perry Point VA to obtain a referral, then contact Cecil County Housing at 410-642-2411. In Prince George's County, the VA screens applicants and refers them to the Housing Authority. In Rockville/Montgomery County, apply through Rockville Housing Enterprises.

structured_extraction.program_name: ARPA Funds for Surface Transportation Projects
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds to Charles County for surface transportation projects, including highway, bridge, and other road projects that are not receiving funding from the Department of Transportation. Funds support maintenance, preservation, and improvement of roadways, shoulders, roadsides, structures, and traffic-control devices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: ARPA State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds are provided for eligible surface transportation projects. Funds must supplement, not supplant, other federal, state, territorial, tribal, and local government funds. Costs incurred from December 29, 2022 must be obligated by December 31, 2024, and expended by September 30, 2026. Eligible projects include highway, bridge, and other road projects under title 23, United States Code, and maintenance of highways including surface, shoulders, roadsides, structures, and traffic-control devices. Projects must be within Charles County and cannot receive concurrent funding from the Department of Transportation.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jenifer Ellin, Acting Deputy County Administrator
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charles County government agencies for surface transportation infrastructure projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Surface transportation projects including highway, bridge, and other road projects; maintenance and preservation of highways, shoulders, roadsides, structures, and traffic-control devices; eligible projects under title 23, United States Code
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland only
requirements_list: Projects must not receive funding from the Department of Transportation
Funds must supplement, not supplant, other federal, state, territorial, tribal, and local government funds
Costs must be incurred from December 29, 2022 or later
Projects must be obligated by December 31, 2024
Projects must be expended by September 30, 2026
Projects must be eligible under title 23, United States Code
Projects must be located within Charles County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Charles County Fiscal and Administrative Services Division at 301-645-0570 or 301-870-2542 for application procedures and project eligibility determination. No Treasury approval is required prior to using funds on surface transportation projects under Pathway 2. Project applications should be submitted to the county for review and approval of eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Application for Surviving Spouse of Fallen EMS Officer Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit available to the surviving spouse of an emergency medical services officer who died in the line of duty, designed to reduce the surviving spouse's annual property tax liability in Charles County, Maryland.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit to reduce annual property tax liability for the surviving spouse of a fallen EMS officer who died in the line of duty. The credit amount and terms are determined by Charles County based on the applicant's eligibility and the assessed property value.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Surviving spouses of emergency medical services officers in Charles County who died in the line of duty.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To reduce annual property tax liability on residential or other property owned by the surviving spouse.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland. The surviving spouse must own property located within Charles County to be eligible for this credit.
requirements_list: Spouse must be the surviving spouse of a fallen EMS officer
The EMS officer must have died in the line of duty
Spouse must have been married to the EMS officer at the time of death
Surviving spouse must own property in Charles County, Maryland
Property must be the primary residence or qualifying property to receive the credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Application for Surviving Spouse of Fallen EMS Officer Credit form to the Charles County Treasury Department. Submit the application with supporting documentation including proof of marriage, proof of the EMS officer's death in the line of duty, proof of property ownership, and any other required verification documents. The county will review the application, verify the applicant's eligibility through appropriate documentation and records, and process the property tax credit accordingly. Once approved, the credit will be applied to reduce the annual property tax liability.

structured_extraction.program_name: Charles County Small Local Business Enterprise Program (SLBE)
structured_extraction.program_description: A certification and procurement preference program that supports local, for-profit businesses based in Charles County. Certified vendors receive exclusive access to certain county government procurements under $50,000 and cost or scoring preferences on larger purchases between $50,000 and $500,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified SLBE vendors receive exclusive access to county government procurements under $50,000 (as long as at least three qualified SLBE firms exist; otherwise SLBE bidders receive an advantage). For formal procurements between $50,000 and $500,000, SLBE firms receive cost or scoring preferences: up to 10% cost preference on Invitations to Bid (ITB) and Requests for Quotation (RFQ), and up to 10 points on Requests for Proposals (RFP). Preferences are prorated based on documented SLBE firm participation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses independently owned and headquartered in Charles County, or with a branch or satellite office in Charles County generating at least 50% of annual gross sales or employing 50% of full-time equivalent employees in Charles County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualification for county government procurement opportunities and bid preferences on county goods and services purchases.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland. Businesses must have headquarters located in Charles County or have a branch or satellite office in Charles County that generates at least 50% of annual gross sales or has 50% of full-time equivalent employees.
requirements_list: Be a for-profit business and independently owned (no brokers or subsidiaries)

Have headquarters located in Charles County, or have a branch or satellite office in Charles County generating at least 50% of annual gross sales or having 50% of full-time equivalent employees in Charles County
Meet Maryland Small Business Reserve (SBR) industry-specific thresholds for gross sales and employees
Be certified in the State of Maryland's Small Business Reserve (SBR) Program
Be registered with eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Charles County Economic Development Department. Businesses must first be certified in Maryland's Small Business Reserve (SBR) Program and registered with eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA). Download and submit a Charles County SLBE application. The program is race and gender neutral; however, minority-owned or women-owned businesses may also apply for the County's MWBE program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Family Caregiver and Support Program provides support services to family caregivers to help fill gaps and alleviate emotional and financial burdens associated with informal caregiving. The program offers information, outreach, caregiver training on skills for providing care, maintaining self-care, employment laws for home care workers, and when to seek professional help. It also provides counseling, monthly support groups, care coordination services at no cost, and financial assistance for respite care and supplemental services such as supplies, durable medical equipment, and prescription assistance. Priority for funded services is given to persons who are financially needy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides information, outreach, and care coordination services at no cost. It offers caregiver training on skills for providing care, maintaining self-care, employment laws for home care workers, and when to seek professional help. Caregiver counseling and support groups meet monthly. Financial assistance may be available for respite care (temporary relief from caregiving duties) and supplemental services such as durable medical equipment, prescription assistance, supplies, and other one-time or short-term benefits. Priority for funded services goes to persons who are financially needy.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family caregivers of any age who meet eligibility criteria, including those caring for older adults age 60 and older who are Charles County residents, caregivers age 55 and older who are primary caregivers for children under 18 in Charles County, and caregivers of persons with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders regardless of age.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Respite care to provide temporary relief from caregiving responsibilities; supplemental services including durable medical equipment, prescription assistance, supplies, and similar one-time or short-term benefits to fill gaps in care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County residents only. The person being cared for must be a resident of Charles County and at least 60 years old, OR the caregiver must be a Charles County resident at least 55 years old caring for children under 18, OR the caregiver cares for a person with Alzheimer's disease or a related disorder regardless of age.
requirements_list: The person cared for must be a resident of Charles County and at least 60 years old, OR the caregiver must be a resident of Charles County at least 55 years old and the primary caregiver for children under age 18, OR the caregiver cares for a person with Alzheimer's disease or related disorder regardless of age
Priority given to persons who are financially needy

structured_extraction.program_name: Perpetual Conservation Easement Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit available to property owners in Charles County who have placed their land under a perpetual conservation easement. The program reduces the assessed value and annual tax liability on the encumbered property, encouraging land conservation across the county.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit that reduces the assessed value of property subject to a perpetual conservation easement. The credit amount is based on the property's reduced value due to the conservation easement restrictions. Property owners must submit an application to Charles County Treasury with documentation of the perpetual conservation easement. Once approved, the property's tax assessment is adjusted annually to reflect the reduced value, resulting in lower annual property tax liability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners (individuals and non-profits) in Charles County, Maryland who have placed their real property under a perpetual conservation easement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To reduce annual property tax liability on properties encumbered by a perpetual conservation easement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be subject to a perpetual conservation easement recorded with Charles County
Property owner must be the fee simple owner or have legal interest in the property
Application must include a copy of the recorded perpetual conservation easement document
Application must be submitted to Charles County Treasury with supporting documentation
The county will review the application and property records to verify the conservation easement status and eligibility
Property must meet the definition of perpetual conservation easement under Maryland law
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners interested in this tax credit should complete the Perpetual Conservation Easement Property Tax Credit Application and submit it to Charles County Treasury along with a copy of the recorded perpetual conservation easement document. The application should include the property address, account number, and documentation proving the perpetual nature of the conservation easement. Charles County Treasury will review the submitted materials and verify the conservation easement status against county records. Upon approval, the property's assessed value will be adjusted to reflect the conservation easement restrictions, reducing the owner's annual property tax liability. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis throughout the fiscal year.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses seeking financing through private activity bonds for qualified economic development projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified economic development purposes as defined by program guidelines
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Maryland Department of Commerce for more information and application procedures

structured_extraction.program_description: A program in which Charles County directly purchases development rights from property owners. Development rights are permanently extinguished and not transferred. Property use is restricted to agricultural, forestry, and open space.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Charles County purchases development rights directly from property owners through periodic competitive application cycles when funding is available. Development rights are permanently extinguished and not transferred to increase development elsewhere. The county compensates landowners based on fair market value appraisals. Applications are evaluated using ranking criteria consistent with the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Periodic competitive cycles when funding is available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Charles County with agricultural or forestry land who want to sell development rights to the county
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase price paid by Charles County for development rights on eligible agricultural, forestry, and open space properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be eligible for the PDR program
Property must be in agricultural, forestry, or open space use
Applications are evaluated using the same ranking applied to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) program
Property owners must be willing to permanently restrict development rights
Program operates on periodic competitive application cycles when county funding is available
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners should contact Charles County Planning and Growth Management staff to learn more about the program and to apply. The county provides guidance on property eligibility and the application process. Applications are submitted during designated competitive cycles and are evaluated using MALPF ranking criteria. Selected properties are appraised by independent appraisers, and the county makes purchase offers based on fair market value. Once an agreement is reached, development rights are permanently extinguished through a deed restriction.

structured_extraction.program_description: Charles County Government and University of Maryland Extension Program offer workshops throughout the year that demonstrate practical uses for rain barrels and how they reduce runoff impact on local waterways and Chesapeake Bay. Participants learn how to install rain barrels and become eligible for a tax deduction.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Discounted rain barrel purchases for Charles County residents (painted 60-gallon barrels at $40-$49, unpainted at $40-$45). Participants become eligible for a property tax credit for installing up to two rain barrels. Applications will be verified and processed within 12 weeks of receipt. A reimbursement check will be mailed to the address provided in the application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides $14,000 in down payment assistance for eligible first-time homebuyers in Charles County to purchase existing housing units. Funds are applied as a grant if the homebuyer resides in the home as their principal residence for at least five years.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides $14,000 in down payment assistance to eligible first-time homebuyers in Charles County. The funds are structured as a forgivable loan that converts to a grant if the homebuyer occupies the home as their principal residence for at least five years. If the homebuyer sells, refinances, or stops occupying the home as their primary residence before five years, the remaining balance must be repaid. Applicants must first be approved for the county's Settlement Expense Loan Program (SELP) to qualify for SELP+. This is a temporary program funded through American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds and concludes when those funds are exhausted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers in Charles County who are approved for the Settlement Expense Loan Program (SELP).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing cost assistance for the purchase of existing housing units. Funds are used to reduce the purchase price and associated costs of the home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County only. Applicants must have lived or worked full-time in the county continuously for the last three years.
requirements_list: First-time homebuyer
Approved for Settlement Expense Loan Program (SELP)
Household income no more than 100% AMI
Lived or worked full-time in Charles County for at least three years continuously
Purchasing existing housing unit (new construction excluded)
Intent to occupy home as principal residence for at least five years
Funds convert to grant only if homebuyer maintains principal residence for full five-year period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants must work with a SELP-Approved lender to complete an application. Applicants should contact a participating lender to begin the SELP application process. Once approved for SELP, borrowers may then apply for the additional $14,000 SELP+ assistance through the same lender.

Low or moderate income

structured_extraction.program_description: A fee reduction program that allows property owners with stormwater management practices to receive up to a 50% reduction on their annual Stormwater Remediation Fee charged by Charles County.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners can receive a credit reducing the annual Stormwater Remediation Fee by up to 50%. The fee is $162 per improved property in Fiscal Year 2026. Residential properties qualify if constructed after July 1, 2001 and meeting 2000 Maryland Stormwater Design Manual standards, or if constructed before that date but featuring approved stormwater management practices such as rain barrels (110+ gallons), rain gardens, pervious pavement, or other infiltration or filtration facilities. Agricultural and forested properties qualify with a current Forest Management Plan or approved Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plan. Non-residential properties qualify if constructed after July 1, 2001 meeting design standards, or if constructed prior to that date and verified by a professional engineer to meet those standards.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Charles County with improved residential, agricultural, forested, or non-residential properties who have installed stormwater management practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit reduces the annual Stormwater Remediation Fee. Funds collected support the Watershed Protection and Restoration Fund, which improves water quality of streams and waterways and reduces impacts of stormwater runoff.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: For residential properties: constructed after July 1, 2001 and meeting 2000 Maryland Stormwater Design Manual standards, OR constructed before July 1, 2001 but featuring one or more approved stormwater management treatments (rain barrels totaling 110+ gallons, rain garden capturing runoff from 800+ sq ft of impervious surface, pervious pavement of 800+ sq ft, Bay-Wise certified landscape, or other infiltration/filtration facilities)

For agricultural/forested properties: current Forest Management Plan prepared by licensed forester, OR tax-assessed agricultural property with approved Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plan from Charles Soil Conservation District

For non-residential properties: constructed after July 1, 2001 meeting design standards, OR constructed prior to July 1, 2001 with stormwater management facilities verified by professional engineer to meet standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners apply using the Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Application available on the county website. For non-residential properties, a statement and description from a professional engineer is required with the application.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows rural landowners to sell their development rights to private developers who can then build at higher density in designated growth areas. The property remains restricted to agricultural, forestry, and open space uses.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners sell development rights to private developers through a voluntary program. The price is negotiated between willing buyer and willing seller. Once certified by Charles County, transferring development rights permanently restricts the property to agricultural, forestry, and open space uses through covenants recorded in Charles County Land Records. The property owner receives compensation for the transfer of these rights while retaining ownership of the land.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural property owners in Charles County who want to sell development rights while maintaining agricultural or open space use of their property
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Proceeds from the sale of development rights to the property owner. Development rights are transferred to designated growth areas where private developers build at higher density. Funds are generated through private market transactions between property owners and developers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, established in 1992. The program was created to preserve agricultural land and open space in Charles County by enabling the transfer of development rights from rural areas designated as sending zones to growth areas designated as receiving zones.
requirements_list: Property must be eligible for TDR participation
Property owner must work with Charles County to certify the number of development rights associated with the property
Participation is completely voluntary
Certified TDRs are tracked by Charles County
Property owner must negotiate price directly with private developers
Development rights must be permanently restricted through recorded covenants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners interested in the TDR program first contact Charles County Planning Staff to certify the number of TDRs associated with their property. A list of available TDRs can be obtained from the County. Once TDRs are certified and the County maintains a registry of available rights, the property owner then negotiates the purchase price of development rights directly with interested private developers. The transfer is completed through a private agreement and recorded in Charles County Land Records.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit available to volunteer emergency responders in Charles County — including firefighters, rescue squad members, and emergency medical services personnel — to reduce their annual property tax liability in recognition of their service to the community.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit that reduces the annual property tax liability for qualifying volunteer emergency responders. The credit amount and specific benefit level are determined based on the applicant's service status and hours of service as verified by their respective volunteer emergency services organization. Eligible responders must submit documentation of their volunteer service along with their property tax information to receive the credit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis - applications accepted on a continuous basis

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To reduce annual property tax liability for qualifying volunteer emergency responders.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland. Applicants must own property located within Charles County to be eligible for the tax credit.
requirements_list: Must be a volunteer emergency responder (firefighter, rescue squad member, or emergency medical services personnel)
Must be actively serving with a recognized volunteer emergency services organization in Charles County
Must be a property owner with property tax liability in Charles County
Must meet minimum service requirements as specified in program guidelines
Must submit completed Volunteer Emergency Responders Tax Credit Application form
Must submit Affidavit for Volunteer Emergency Responders Tax Credit Application
Must provide verification of volunteer service status from their emergency services organization
Verification of property ownership and tax account information required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain the Volunteer Emergency Responders Tax Credit Application form and Affidavit for Volunteer Emergency Responders Tax Credit Application from Charles County Treasury or the county website. 2. Complete all required sections of the application form with personal information, property details, and volunteer service information. 3. Have your volunteer emergency services organization (fire department, rescue squad, or EMS agency) verify your service status and hours on the affidavit form. 4. Submit both the completed application and affidavit to Charles County Treasury. 5. The county will verify your eligibility, confirm your property tax account, and process the tax credit. 6. Once approved, the credit will be applied to your property tax account in the following billing cycle.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Façade Improvement Program provides funding to existing commercial buildings within the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor (WURC) in Charles County to upgrade the visible, corridor-facing components of their properties. structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applications must be for commercial buildings within the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor (WURC) in Waldorf, Charles County, Maryland. Priority will be given to projects fronting Old Washington Road.

Projects can only be external building façade improvements
Applications cannot be for works started prior to receiving a commitment letter from Charles County

Applicant must agree to maintain all improvements made per the approved plans in their finished state

structured_extraction.program_name: Adopt a Community FY 2024 Building Resilient Communities Together: Boots on the Ground Community Engagement Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant funds community-based organizations to develop programs that build resilient, empowered communities in Annapolis through hands-on outreach and engagement. Organizations work directly in specific at-risk neighborhoods to develop one-on-one relationships, provide mentorship, mental health support, and trauma-informed programming while connecting residents to needed resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $200,000 in total one-time grant awards distributed among eligible organizations. A maximum of $20,000 will be granted to each organization. Only one organization will be funded per neighborhood. Maximum of 10 percent of funds may be used for overhead costs. Funding period is September 2023 through June 30, 2024. Organizations may request funds to support staff salaries, program supplies, community engagement activities, and other direct service delivery costs related to their community engagement and mentorship programs. Grantees must submit a detailed itemized budget proposal explaining fund utilization.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis; the application will remain open until funds are used
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations with 501(c)(3) status working in at-risk neighborhoods in Annapolis
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mentorship programs, neighborhood-targeted engagement, mental health services and counseling, trauma-informed programming, community ownership and engagement activities, inclusive and equitable approaches. Funds can be used for staff salaries, program supplies, training, and direct service delivery costs. Funds cannot be used for one-time engagement projects, one-time pop-up events, projects outside Annapolis, or programs focusing on more than one neighborhood.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to specific at-risk communities within Annapolis: Bay Ridge Gardens, Harbour House/Eastport Terrace, Madison Apartments, Bywater, Robinwood, Annapolis Gardens, Admiral Oaks, Clay Street/Obery Court/College Creek Apartments, Woodside, Parole, Allen Apartments, Admiral Farragut, Quiet Waters, and Watergate Village. Each organization focuses on one specific community. Applicants may also reference the Budget Template spreadsheet for detailed budget guidance and examples.
requirements_list: Organization must have 501(c)(3) nonprofit status
Proposal must outline a community engagement and relationship building plan for one specific community
Work plan must include practical timeline with objectives, activities, dates, logistics, SMARTIE goals and objectives, and follow-up process
Proposal must include performance measures and expected outcomes
Itemized budget proposal required with explanation of fund utilization
Maximum 10 percent of funds may be used for overhead costs
Organization must attend quarterly meetings to share progress and updates
Grantees must submit reports twice: mid-grant period and end of program
One organization will be selected per neighborhood
Proposed program must focus on building resilient, empowered communities through hands-on community engagement and relationship building
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through an online application portal. Applicants may copy application questions into a separate document to complete them offline before entering them into the portal. Submit an itemized budget proposal (using the provided Budget Template spreadsheet as a guide) and work plan with the application. Organizations unable to submit through the portal may contact communityservices@annapolis.gov to request approval to submit via paper at City Hall or by email. All application sections must be completed for the application to be considered fundable. The application form includes questions about the organization's mission, target neighborhood, community engagement strategy, expected outcomes, and detailed budget justification. Information sessions and technical assistance meetings are available to support applicants.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay Trust - Chesapeake Conservation Climate Corps
structured_extraction.program_description: A year-long service program that places Corps Members at host organizations supporting environmental projects across Maryland. Participants work as Climate Coordinators supporting climate adaptation, community resilience, and implementation of climate action plans. The program includes stipend support, health care, professional development training, networking opportunities, and a capstone project.

Participants receive health care coverage if not already covered by private source, 15 professional development trainings, 4 all-cohort project days, 4-10 networking visits, 1 capstone project, 1 grant opportunity, and funding to attend a regional professional conference.

Both design-phase and construction/implementation-phase projects are eligible for funding.

Design grants may fund engineering firms, public outreach, and maintenance agreements. Construction grants support permitting and implementation of projects. structured_extraction.program_name: City of Annapolis Rental Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A financial assistance program administered by the City of Annapolis that helps low and moderate-income renters pay rent, security deposits, and utility bills to stabilize housing, prevent eviction, prevent utility shutoffs, and address housing instability. The program provides direct financial payments made by the city's finance department to property managers or utility companies on behalf of eligible residents. Assistance is available once per fiscal year per applicant, and approvals are not guaranteed. The program serves employed residents, those employed within the last 90 days, or those receiving retirement benefits who live in the City of Annapolis and rent their home.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct financial assistance is provided by the city's finance department, which mails checks directly to property managers or utility companies on behalf of approved applicants — payments are never made directly to the applicant. Assistance covers past-due rent, security deposits, and unpaid utility bills. Payment amounts are based on the applicant's qualifications. Checks typically take 4–6 weeks to be received after approval. Applicants can only receive assistance once every fiscal year. Upon approval, applicants receive a promissory letter for their records during the processing period. Approvals are not guaranteed. If denied, the program provides information on other available resources and connects applicants with a social worker.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low and moderate-income renters living in the City of Annapolis who are employed, have been employed in the last 90 days, or are receiving retirement benefits, and who are at risk of eviction, housing instability, or utility shutoff.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rent payments, past-due rent, security deposits, and unpaid utility bills for residential rental properties. Payments can only be made to rental properties, not owner-occupied homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be living and renting within the City of Annapolis, Maryland. Applications can be submitted in person at the Robinwood Community Services office at 1453 Tyler Avenue, Annapolis, MD 21403 by scheduling an appointment.
requirements_list: Must be living in the City of Annapolis
Income at or below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI)
Must be employed, have been employed in the last 90 days, or receiving retirement benefits
If employment has not yet started, an offer letter is acceptable
Unemployment benefits are not accepted as proof of income
One or more household members must demonstrate risk of homelessness or housing instability with evidence such as a past-due utility or rent notice, eviction notice, or other evidence
Must hold a lease or sublease in applicant's name, or will hold a lease in the case of security deposit assistance
Renting in a household with a current and valid City rental license
Account balances must not be more than 60 days past due
Can only receive assistance once every fiscal year
Payments can only be made to rental properties, not owner-occupied homes
Approvals are not guaranteed

Must provide proof of current residency and lease information; an official letter on company letterhead from the property manager confirming current residency and listing all individuals on the lease is acceptable
Must provide verification of household income such as W-2, pay stubs, tax returns, bank statements, or proof of retirement benefits
Must provide rental/lease agreement or sublease
Must provide photo identification for all adult household members
Must provide at least one of: eviction notice or court judgment showing arrears and amount owed, or unpaid utility bill or utility shutoff notice
If applying for both rental and utility assistance, the applications must be submitted simultaneously
Can only apply for rental assistance, or rental and utility assistance simultaneously — cannot apply for utility assistance alone after being denied rental assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online application form at the program website, or apply in person at the Robinwood Community Services office at 1453 Tyler Avenue, Annapolis, MD 21403 by scheduling an appointment. Provide information about your household and income. Submit supporting documentation including income verification (W-2, pay stubs, tax returns, bank statements, or proof of retirement benefits), rental/lease agreement or sublease, photo identification for all adult household members, and evidence of past-due rent or utilities (eviction notice, court judgment, unpaid utility bill, or shutoff notice). A case manager reviews the application to determine eligibility. Allow up to three business days to receive an approval or denial notice via email. If approved, the finance department mails a check directly to the property manager or utility company, which may take 4–6 weeks to arrive; a promissory letter is provided during the processing period. If denied, the city provides information on other available resources and connects applicants with a social worker for additional support.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis offers low-interest loans to help property owners in the downtown Historic District pay for fire sprinkler system retrofits. Loans are available for up to five years at 1% annual percentage rate, with maximum loan amounts of $25,000. Priority is given to projects with residential use on upper floors and those using certified minority contractors.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Five-year loans at 1% annual percentage rate for up to $25,000 per property owner to cover the cost of installing automatic fire sprinkler systems. Loans are available until the annual allocation of the fund is exhausted. Payment is disbursed as a check to the applicant once the contract is finalized and building permits are issued.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in the Annapolis downtown Historic District on Main Street and Francis Street who are required to retrofit their buildings with automatic fire sprinkler systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding is used to pay for the cost of installing automatic fire sprinkler systems that comply with National Fire Protection Association Standard 13.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties located on Main Street and Francis Street in the downtown Historic District of Annapolis that have a dedicated City water line for sprinkler system connection.
requirements_list: Property must be located on Main Street or Francis Street in the Annapolis Historic District
Property must have a dedicated City water line for sprinkler system connection
Work must be performed by a licensed contractor
Building permits must be obtained before work begins
Fire sprinkler system must comply with National Fire Protection Association Standard 13
Installation must be completed no later than April 6, 2027
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, have a licensed contractor create a sprinkler retrofit plan for your building by visiting Maryland OneStop. Complete the online loan application using the keyword 'sprinkler loan' at www.annapolis.gov or by scanning the provided QR code. The City finance office reviews the application and shares it with the Fire Marshal to check with the permit office. Once approved, the Fire Marshal sends it to the City Attorney's office to prepare the contract. Once the contract is complete and building permits are issued, the loan funds are disbursed as a check to the applicant.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Annapolis – Owner Occupied Housing Rehabilitation

Home improvement work is performed by a licensed contractor at no cost to the homeowner. If the home is sold, rented, or transferred within 15 years, repayment is required within 11 years. structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis distributes federal Community Development Block Grant funds from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development to support local community development projects. The program aims to develop viable urban communities by providing decent housing and suitable living environments, and expanding economic opportunities, principally for persons of low and moderate income. The city allocates funds for capital projects involving physical infrastructure or construction that benefit low and moderate-income individuals and households, as well as historically supporting homeownership opportunities, housing rehabilitation services, and social services for low-income populations in Annapolis.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Annapolis anticipates receiving approximately $278,182 in CDBG funds for fiscal year 2027 (beginning July 1, 2026). Funds are awarded as grants to community organizations and low-income homeowners for capital projects involving physical infrastructure or construction. These grants support activities such as homeownership opportunities, housing rehabilitation services, home repairs for low-income homeowners, infrastructure improvements, and financial support for human service organizations serving low-income populations. Applicants must demonstrate that proposed projects will benefit low- and moderate-income residents of Annapolis.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Denise Ruffin; Alexis Robinson, AICP, Senior Comprehensive Planner
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations, non-profit organizations, low-income homeowners, and social service agencies seeking to fund capital projects that benefit low and moderate-income residents of Annapolis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects involving physical infrastructure or construction that benefit low and moderate-income individuals and households, including homeownership opportunities, housing rehabilitation services, home repairs, infrastructure improvements, and support for human service organizations. Public service projects are no longer funded through this program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis only. Projects must be located within the City of Annapolis corporate limits and serve Annapolis residents.
requirements_list: All proposed activities and projects must benefit low- and moderate-income individuals and households

Public service projects are not eligible
Projects must be located within the City of Annapolis
Applicants must demonstrate community need and project feasibility
Projects should align with the City's Consolidated Plan and Annual Action Plan priorities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Community organizations and eligible applicants submit CDBG applications to the City of Annapolis Planning and Zoning Department by the established deadline (4:30 PM on Friday, March 6, 2025). Applications must include detailed project descriptions, budgets, evidence of community benefit, and demonstration that projects will serve low- and moderate-income residents. The Affordable Housing and Community Equity Development Commission reviews all submitted applications and recommends funding allocations to the City Council. City Council reviews recommendations and approves all CDBG-funded projects. Approved projects become the basis for the CDBG Action Plan submitted to HUD. The City facilitates an annual CDBG application and approval process for federal funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Front Yard, Street Tree, and Community Canopy Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis offers two free tree programs to residents and property owners. The Front Yard and Street Tree Program provides free trees planted by city contractors at no cost in the public right-of-way (typically the strip between the sidewalk and the curb) or in the front yard of homes or businesses. Recipients agree to water and care for the tree for the first three years. The Community Canopy Program is a partnership with the Arbor Day Foundation that gives away free trees to residents, and includes an online mapping tool to identify the best planting locations in a yard to maximize cooling, energy savings, and financial benefits. Together, these programs aim to increase the urban forest, improve air quality, provide shade, reduce stormwater runoff, and make streets more beautiful and livable.

Under the Front Yard and Street Tree Program, city contractors plant the tree at no cost; the recipient must agree to water and care for the tree for the first three years. Under the Community Canopy Program (in partnership with the Arbor Day Foundation), free trees are distributed to residents along with access to an online mapping tool that identifies optimal planting locations on a property to maximize cooling, energy savings, and financial benefits.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting in the public right-of-way (typically the strip between the sidewalk and the curb), front yard, or residential yard of properties within the City of Annapolis

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The city provides funds as a loan with zero percent interest and no required monthly payments. Repayment is due upon sale or transfer of the property, or at the end of 10 years, whichever comes first. A lien is placed on the property through a Deed of Trust. Up to $10,000 is available depending on the borrower's need.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homebuyers purchasing moderately priced dwelling units in Annapolis who have an MPDU Certificate of Eligibility.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing costs for the purchase of an MPDU home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis only.
requirements_list: Have an MPDU Certificate of Eligibility
Be a graduate of a HUD-certified Homeownership Counseling Program
Be prequalified by a participating lender or a lender of your choice
Contribute a minimum of one percent of the sales price in cash from your own funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MPDU Eligibility Certificate holders will receive this information in their Home Buyer Packet when the city notifies them of MPDU availability for sale. Applicants may also call the office for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis MPDU Program ensures that housing options remain available to moderate-income residents and employees by requiring that 15% of houses for sale and 15% of rental units in new subdivisions of 10 or more units be priced affordably for moderate-income households. Eligible applicants can purchase or rent MPDU units at below-market prices set at or below 100% of the Baltimore Metropolitan Statistical Area median family income. No direct subsidy is provided by the city or developers, but participants may use federal, state, or local government assistance including Section 8 housing choice vouchers, medical assistance subsidies, rental assistance, or rent supplements. Purchase prices are controlled for 30 years from the initial sale, and units must be owner-occupied and resold to another MPDU-eligible household at a city-determined price if sold within the 30-year occupancy period. After the 30-year period, the owner may sell at fair market value. Rental units at participating complexes are offered at reduced rates. Down payment and closing cost assistance up to $10,000 may be available through the MPDU Settlement Expense Assistance program, as well as through the Maryland Mortgage Program (MMP) and Arundel Community Development Services' Mortgage Assistance Program (MAP).
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program sets affordable purchase and rental prices for moderately priced dwelling units based on HUD median family income guidelines. Prices are controlled for 30 years from the initial sale. No direct subsidy is provided by the city or developers; applicants purchase or rent at affordable prices set at or below 100% of the Baltimore MSA median family income. Buyers must qualify for a mortgage equal to the house price. Renters should earn approximately $40,000 or above annually, or use government housing assistance such as Section 8 housing choice vouchers. Maximum income limits for FY 2023 range from $82,875 for a single person to $137,250 for a household of six. Down payment and closing cost assistance up to $10,000 is available through the MPDU Settlement Expense Assistance program. Additional assistance is available through the Maryland Mortgage Program (MMP) and Arundel Community Development Services' Mortgage Assistance Program (MAP). Units subject to 30-year resale price controls and owner-occupancy requirements; after 30 years the owner may sell at fair market value.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Moderate-income residents and employees of the City of Annapolis, including city employees, people employed within city limits for at least 12 months, full-time teachers and staff in elementary, middle, or high schools within city limits or in the Annapolis Senior High School district, Naval Academy or Annapolis Naval Base employees (12+ months), Anne Arundel County residents with disabilities, and first-time and low-to-moderate income homebuyers seeking affordable housing in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase or rental of moderately priced dwelling units (apartments, condominiums, townhouses, or single-family homes ranging from efficiency/studio units of approximately 600 square feet to four-bedroom units of approximately 2,000 square feet) to be used as a primary residence. Settlement expense assistance can cover down payment and closing costs for purchases. Funds from partner programs (MMP, MAP) may be used for down payments, settlement costs, and mortgage assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must meet one of the following criteria: be a resident within the corporate limits of the City of Annapolis; be an employee of the City of Annapolis; be employed within the city limits for at least 12 months; be a full-time teacher or staff member in an elementary, middle, or high school within city limits; be a full-time teacher or staff member in the Annapolis Senior High School district; be employed at the Naval Academy or Annapolis Naval Base for at least 12 months; or be an Anne Arundel County resident with a documented disability. MPDU units must be located within the City of Annapolis.
requirements_list: Income at or below 100% of Baltimore Metropolitan Statistical Area median family income adjusted for household size (FY 2023 limits: $82,875 for one person to $137,250 for six-person household)
Must not currently own a home
Must meet one of the geographic/employment eligibility criteria
Must complete MPDU Program application for Certificate of Eligibility

Must complete homebuyer classes from an approved agency (Arundel Community Development Services, Anne Arundel County Community Action Agency, or HUD-certified program) before signing sales contract (for purchase applicants)
Ability to qualify for mortgage and pay down payment and closing costs (for purchase program)
Good credit rating acceptable to property management (for rental program)
Must live in the MPDU as primary residence
If sold within 30 years, must be sold to another MPDU-eligible household at a city-determined price
Owner must adhere to MPDU rules and covenants tied to the property
Deposit required shall not exceed $1,000
For settlement expense assistance: must have MPDU Certificate of Eligibility, be a graduate of a HUD-certified Homeownership Counseling Program, and be pre-qualified by a lender
First-time homebuyers seeking down payment or cost assistance through MMP or MAP must obtain housing counseling through ACDS
Current gross household income documentation for a one-month period (pay stubs, child support, alimony, SSI/SSA or retirement income statements)
Copies of last two statements from all asset accounts
Copies of last two federal tax returns with all schedules and W2s for each applicant and co-applicant
Copy of photo ID for each applicant and co-applicant
Credit report with credit score for each applicant (not more than 6 months old)
If dependent is 18 or older, verification of work or student status
If claiming disability, must provide medical documentation in accordance with Social Security Administration definition
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete a HUD-certified homebuyer education course through Arundel Community Development Services (ACDS) or Anne Arundel County Economic Opportunity Committee and obtain a Home Buyer's Certificate (required for purchase applicants before signing a sales contract). 2. If seeking down payment or mortgage assistance, obtain housing counseling through ACDS. 3. Submit the MPDU Application with all required documentation in person, by mail, or electronically to the Department of Planning and Zoning, 145 Gorman Street, 3rd floor, Annapolis MD 21401. 4. MPDU staff reviews application and supporting documentation; if eligible, applicant receives a Certificate of Eligibility within four weeks. Certificates are valid for one year and may be renewed. 5. Once a Certificate of Eligibility is issued, the applicant will be notified by letter when units become available; return the completed interest form by the indicated date if interested. For rental units, the management at participating complexes (e.g., Bell Annapolis on West) will contact you by phone. 6. For purchase: qualify for financing through a conventional lender, mortgage company, or the Maryland Mortgage Program; make an offer on an available MPDU unit; execute a sales contract and complete settlement. For rental: apply directly to the property manager at the participating complex.

structured_extraction.program_description: A city-funded tree planting program in its fourth year of operations focused on helping the City of Annapolis achieve 50 percent urban tree canopy by 2050. The program restores Annapolis's forest canopy by planting trees at homes, congregations, businesses, and schools across various communities. It trains volunteer community leaders through the Tree Trooper program to identify planting sites and oversee projects. From September 2023 to December 2025, the program planted 380 trees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free tree planting services provided directly by the program for homes, congregations, businesses, and schools across the City of Annapolis. The program also provides free training for volunteer Tree Troopers consisting of 4 virtual sessions and one in-person planting event. Volunteers trained through the Tree Trooper program help identify planting locations and oversee tree planting projects. From September 2023 to December 2025, the program planted 380 trees as part of its efforts to expand urban forest canopy.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents, congregations, businesses, and schools in the City of Annapolis seeking to plant trees and restore the city's forest canopy to achieve 50 percent urban tree canopy by 2050.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting projects to expand urban tree canopy and restore the city's forest canopy through planting at residential properties, congregations, businesses, and schools.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis only.
requirements_list: Applicants must be located within the City of Annapolis
Volunteer community leaders must complete Tree Trooper training program consisting of 4 virtual sessions and 1 in-person planting event
Selected volunteers commit to identifying planting sites and overseeing tree planting projects
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals apply to become Tree Troopers by visiting the program website and completing an interest form under the 'Become a Tree Trooper' section. Selected volunteers receive free training through 4 virtual sessions and one in-person planting event. After training completion, volunteers help identify suitable planting locations and assist with overseeing tree planting projects throughout Annapolis.

Funds are distributed as available and are not guaranteed for all programs at all times.

structured_extraction.program_name: City Historic Preservation Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A local property tax credit program for owners of historic properties in Frederick who undertake preservation work.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit available to owners of historic properties in the City of Frederick who preserve their historic properties. The credit is applied against the local property tax bill. Credit amount varies based on the scope and cost of the eligible preservation work performed. Applicants must submit documentation proving completion of preservation work that meets the Secretary of the Interior Standards for Historic Preservation. The credit is administered annually for properties that meet eligibility criteria and have completed approved preservation projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic properties in the City of Frederick
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Historic preservation work on eligible historic properties, including rehabilitation, restoration, and maintenance of structures that are historically significant or located within a historic district.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland. Properties must be located within the City of Frederick city limits and be either individually listed on the National Register of Historic Places, contributing structures in a locally designated historic district, or individually designated as historic landmarks by the City.
requirements_list: Property must be historically significant or located in a locally designated historic district in the City of Frederick
Property owner must be current on all property taxes and have no outstanding code violations
Owner must undertake preservation work meeting the Secretary of the Interior Standards for Historic Preservation
Preservation work must be approved by the City of Frederick Historic Preservation Commission prior to commencement
Work must be completed and documented with receipts, contractor invoices, and photographic evidence
Owner must apply for the tax credit within the established deadline following completion of work
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners must submit a Historic Preservation Property Tax Credit Application through the online portal on the City of Frederick website. Applications must include: completed application form, proof of property tax payment, photographs documenting the completed preservation work (before and after), itemized receipts and invoices from contractors, and evidence that work was approved by the Historic Preservation Commission. Supporting documentation must demonstrate that work meets the Secretary of the Interior Standards. Applications are reviewed by the City's Historic Preservation Office, and approved credits are applied to the property tax bill.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time reduction to water and sewer charges on excessive bills resulting from an interior or exterior leak for residential customers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a one-time bill adjustment for water and sewer charges when a leak causes usage to be at least 2 times normal usage based on the average of the last three billing cycles. After the leak is repaired and confirmed by the Water Department to have returned to normal usage levels, the bill is adjusted from the first service day on the protested bill to the first normal reading.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential customers of the City of Frederick who experience excessive water and sewer bills due to leaks.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of water and sewer charges resulting from interior or exterior leaks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to any residential customer in the City of Frederick. Not offered to apartments, condominiums, or any multi-family structure served by one meter.
requirements_list: Water and Sewer bill must be at least 2 times normal usage based on average of last three billing cycles
Property must have an interior or exterior leak
Leak must be repaired
Water Department must perform two readings to confirm usage has returned to normal
Property must be residential (not apartment, condominium, or multi-family structure with single meter)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Water and Sewer Finance Team to report an excessive bill. The Team will instruct the resident to have the leak repaired and/or coordinate with the Water Department to inspect the property. Once repaired, the Water Department will perform two readings to ensure usage has returned to normal. After normal usage is confirmed, the bill will be adjusted.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps homeowners who are behind on mortgage payments by teaching them the best course of action to protect their home investment and credit rating. Counselors help determine the direction that best serves the client's needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free counseling for homeowners delinquent on mortgage payments. Counselors help evaluate options and develop a plan to address mortgage delinquency and protect credit standing. The program assists clients in understanding their rights and available alternatives to foreclosure, including loan modifications, forbearance agreements, and other loss mitigation options.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners delinquent on mortgage payments with no income limit
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counseling to address mortgage delinquency and develop payment solutions, including guidance on loan modification options, forbearance agreements, and foreclosure alternatives
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All of Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner delinquent on mortgage payments
Must complete the Mortgage Default/Client Intake Packet
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Mortgage Default/Client Intake Packet and submit it to the Housing Counseling Office. Contact the office if you have additional questions. Counselors will work with you to evaluate your situation and develop an appropriate action plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: Reimbursable grants that support the LGBTQ+ community in Frederick during Pride Month 2026. Funding is available to community organizations and civic groups organizing LGBTQ+ pride events in June 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable grants to support LGBTQ+ pride events. Funds are distributed after July 1, 2026. Partial funding may be awarded in lieu of a full award. All awards are subject to the availability and approval of FY27 funding.
