structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To support LGBTQ+ pride events that promote visibility, inclusivity and support for the LGBTQ+ community in the City of Frederick during June 2026
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Events must be hosted in the City of Frederick
requirements_list: Host an event in June 2026 that promotes visibility, inclusivity and support for the LGBTQ+ community in the City of Frederick
Submit an event budget and project budget
Submit a final report due December 31, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted through the online grant portal at the provided link. Requests received via email, phone, or direct mail will not be reviewed. The application deadline is May 1, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: Assists senior homeowners in determining whether a reverse mortgage, also known as a Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM), is the right option to decrease monthly expenses or increase cashflow. HUD-required comprehensive counseling is provided to help homeowners understand how reverse mortgages work, explore alternatives, and answer questions about this financial product.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual counseling appointments for reverse mortgage education and HUD-required comprehensive HECM counseling. The counseling fee is $100 per session, though the fee may be waived or reduced based on household income. Clients complete the HECM/Client Intake Packet prior to their appointment to gather necessary financial and personal information.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners age 62 or older with no income limit
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Comprehensive counseling on reverse mortgage options, alternatives to reverse mortgages, and how HECM programs work
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All of Maryland
requirements_list: Must be age 62 or older
Must be a homeowner
Must complete the HECM/Client Intake Packet before scheduling an appointment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the HECM/Client Intake Packet (available at https://www.cityoffrederickmd.gov/DocumentCenter/View/20152/HECM-Intake-Packet). 2. Contact the Housing Counseling Office at (301) 600-2077 (Steven Rose) or (301) 600-3974 (Tina Weedon) to schedule an individual counseling appointment. 3. Attend the counseling session to receive HUD-required comprehensive HECM education and guidance. 4. A $100 counseling fee applies, though it may be waived based on income.

structured_extraction.program_name: SECURE Initiative (Supporting Emergency Capacity, Urgency, Resiliency, and Equity)
structured_extraction.program_description: An emergency relief program that provides one-time, flexible bridge funding to eligible local nonprofits who sustain critical services and serve the city's most vulnerable residents. The program addresses significant disruptions in funding for nonprofits by offering financial support to maintain operations and service continuity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time, flexible bridge funding. Up to $50,000 per award. Total program pool is $700,000. Funding is non-renewable bridge funding designed to support nonprofits that have experienced disruptions in state or federally funded grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations in good standing, including 501(c)(3) and other nonprofit classifications or fiscally sponsored projects, that operate in Frederick County and provide services to City of Frederick residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bridge funding to support critical services including food access, housing support, healthcare, youth development, mental health care, and other community needs or essential services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must operate in Frederick County and provide services to City of Frederick residents.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization in good standing, including 501(c)(3), other nonprofit classifications, or fiscally sponsored projects
Must operate in Frederick County and provide services to City of Frederick residents
Must deliver programs that support community needs or essential services
Must have experienced a loss in state or federally funded grants and/or subgrants that disrupted program timelines or operations
Must have lost a previously reliable funding source due to non-renewal, reduced awards, or policy changes
Must demonstrate an increased demand for services compared to the same time last year due to specific federal cuts within a similar or adjacent service
All reporting must be up to date if previous funding has been granted by the City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants login or create an account on the City's application portal at grantinterface.com/Home/Logon?urlkey=cityoffrederickmd. Starting October 15, 2025, eligible organizations can apply through the online portal on a rolling basis. All reporting must be current if the organization has previously received City funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: A local tax credit supplement for eligible senior homeowners in Frederick that supplements the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program. The State of Maryland administers the combined credit.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A local supplement to the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit for qualifying senior homeowners. The State administers both the state credit and the city supplement credit together.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Frederick who are at least 70 years old, own their principal residence, and meet income and net worth limits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces property tax liability for eligible senior homeowners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to City of Frederick homeowners only.
requirements_list: Must be at least 70 years old as of the end of the calendar year preceding the taxable year for which the credit is sought
Combined gross household income cannot exceed $40,000 for the city supplement (state program allows up to $60,000)
Must own or have a legal interest in the property

The dwelling must be your principal residence where you live at least six months of the year, including July 1, unless you are a recent home purchaser or unable to do so because of health or need of special care
Net worth, not including the value of the property or qualified retirement savings or Individual Retirement Accounts, must be less than $200,000
Must be qualified for the state tax credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Homeowners file for the State credit. The State determines if the taxpayer is eligible for the City supplement. If eligible, the State processes both the State credit and the City supplemental credit together.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides affordable homeownership access in the City of Frederick by offering interest-free loans for down payment and closing cost assistance to first-time homebuyers. Funded by the City of Frederick's Community Development Block Grant program from the Department of Housing and Urban Development. The program aims to support homebuyers in Frederick through financial incentives and assistance to make homeownership accessible.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Interest-free loans up to $25,000 for down payment and closing cost assistance. No payments are required until the property is sold, refinanced, or is no longer the primary residence of the borrower. Funds must be used for down payment and closing costs on the purchase of a home located in the City of Frederick. Applicants must meet income requirements and participate in homebuyer counseling.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers who are residents of the City of Frederick interested in purchasing their first home
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing cost assistance for home purchases in the City of Frederick
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland. Applicants must be purchasing a property located within the City of Frederick corporate limits.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of the City of Frederick
Must be interested in purchasing a home in the City of Frederick
Must be a first-time homebuyer
Must meet income eligibility requirements
Must complete homebuyer counseling
Must obtain a commitment letter from a lender
Debt-to-income ratio requirements must be met
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Frederick Housing Counseling Office to begin the application process. Applicants must complete homebuyer counseling, obtain a pre-approval letter from a lender, and submit a loan application with supporting financial documentation. The Housing Counseling Office will review the application and determine eligibility. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis as funding is available.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides a 50/50 cost share subsidy for residential tree planting in the City of Frederick. Residents can purchase containerized native trees at a discounted price, with the city covering half the cost. The program aims to increase tree canopy, improve air and water quality, and reduce energy costs for homeowners.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The city provides a 50/50 cost share for containerized native trees purchased through the Tree Frederick online storefront. Trees are already discounted to reflect the city's contribution, with the resident paying their portion directly. The program covers a variety of native species suitable for the Frederick area. Residents pick up their trees on a designated date at Harry Grove Stadium. Each resident can purchase up to 5 trees in one transaction.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 26th, 2026, or until all trees sell out
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Frederick residents who own or rent property with permission from their landlord and wish to plant trees on their residential property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and planting of native containerized trees in residential yards to increase urban tree canopy and provide environmental and energy efficiency benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is limited to City of Frederick residents only. Participants must live within the city limits and provide proof of residency to be eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a City of Frederick resident
Must provide valid proof of City of Frederick residency
Must plant tree in appropriate location in front or back yard of residential property
Renters must have written permission from landlord
Each resident limited to purchasing up to 5 trees per season
Trees must be ordered and purchased together in one transaction
Trees must be planted on residential property within City of Frederick limits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Enter your address on the Tree Frederick website to verify City of Frederick residency. Step 2: Select native trees from available options through the Tree Frederick online storefront. Step 3: Review your selection and proceed to checkout. Step 4: Pay the discounted price (reflecting the 50/50 cost share with the City). Step 5: Receive pickup confirmation with date and location details. Step 6: Pick up your trees on the designated date (March 28th, 2026 at Harry Grove Stadium, 21 Stadium Drive, Frederick, MD 21703) during scheduled pickup times.

structured_extraction.program_description: Financial assistance program administered by the Office of Home Energy Programs to help income-eligible households pay utility bills and make utility expenses more affordable.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to help income-eligible households pay utility bills and manage utility expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible households in Frederick, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of utility bills; making utility expenses more affordable
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick, Maryland and surrounding area
requirements_list: Household income at or below eligibility threshold
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit OHEP application with required documentation

structured_extraction.program_description: A weatherization program that audits homes for a full range of energy-efficiency improvements, including air sealing, insulation, ventilation upgrades, lighting replacements, and appliance upgrades. The program provides free grant-funded work to reduce energy bills.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free grant-funded weatherization work including air sealing, insulation installation or upgrades, heating and cooling system repairs or replacements, energy-efficient LED lighting installation, health and safety improvements, and programmable thermostat installation. Work includes sealing air leaks around walls, ceilings, windows, doors, lighting and plumbing fixtures, switches, and electrical outlets. Insulation improvements address attic, wall, and other building envelope areas based on professional energy audit recommendations. On average, households save $372 or more per year on energy bills. Sealing uncontrolled air leaks alone can save 10%-20% on heating and cooling bills.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income homeowners and renters in Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties, including nonprofits serving eligible clients.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Air sealing, insulation improvements, heating and cooling system upgrades, energy-efficient lighting, health and safety work, mechanical ventilation installation, and thermostat installation. Eligible work includes caulking and weatherstripping seams and cracks, installing foam gaskets behind outlet and switch plates, foam sealant application around window trims and baseboards, fireplace damper sealing, chimney balloon installation, attic stair insulation boxes, blown-in insulation, rigid foam insulation, and smart or programmable thermostat installation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties in Maryland.
requirements_list: Income must meet household income limits (ranging from $68,500 for one person to $129,100 for eight people)
Homeowners must own the property
Renters must have landlord permission via a signed building owner agreement
For landlords: apartment buildings must have up to 4 units per building to be eligible for State weatherization funds; buildings with more than 4 units reviewed on case-by-case basis

Applicants on certain income-eligible programs (Energy Assistance, Maryland Fuel Assistance Fund, SNAP, DHCD Rehab, TANF, Baltimore Lead Hazard Control, SSI, Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids, HUD housing assistance, Medicaid) can submit abbreviated applications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the City of Frederick online form. Once approved, a qualified professional will conduct a comprehensive home energy audit to identify energy losses and recommend cost-effective improvements. The audit evaluates home construction, inspects equipment and insulation, checks for signs of mold and moisture, and conducts safety and air leak tests using diagnostic equipment such as house air leakage tests and infrared scans. The auditor provides prioritized recommendations for energy-saving work. Qualified contractors then install the recommended improvements. After completion, a follow-up evaluation is conducted to verify the contractor's work. The State prioritizes applications from elderly individuals, families with children, persons with disabilities, high residential energy users, and households with high energy burden. Applicants on certain income-eligible programs can submit abbreviated three-page applications with proof of benefit approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown allocated $600,000 in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding to provide grants to eligible nonprofit organizations for projects in categories including Children & Families, Seniors, Education, Economic Recovery, Mental Health, Health/Health Disparities, and Transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Nonprofit organizations can receive grants up to a maximum of $50,000 per category for eligible projects. Funds must be used for projects that fall within one or more of the eligible categories: Children & Families, Seniors, Education, Economic Recovery, Mental Health, Health/Health Disparities, or Transportation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(19) status located in or serving the Hagerstown area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds must support projects in one or more of the following categories: Children & Families, Seniors, Education, Economic Recovery, Mental Health, Health/Health Disparities, or Transportation. Projects must benefit the Hagerstown community.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Hagerstown area. Organizations must be located in or serving the Hagerstown area.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization with 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(19) status
Cannot be an individual, business, sole proprietor, partnership, limited liability corporation, or other for-profit organization
Must submit IRS Nonprofit Designation Letter
Must provide Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), dated within past 30 days or current screenshot
Must submit Project Budget including all current and anticipated funding sources
Must provide evidence of active SAM.gov registration showing Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)
Project must fall under one or more of the eligible categories
Project must benefit the Hagerstown community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed application and all required supporting documents via email to grantsmail@hagerstownmd.org by 4:00 p.m. on September 1, 2023. Required documents include: IRS Nonprofit Designation Letter, SDAT Certificate of Good Standing (dated within past 30 days or current screenshot), Project Budget with all current and anticipated funding sources, and SAM.gov registration evidence showing UEI. Questions about the application must be submitted by a specified deadline prior to the final submission deadline. Applications will be reviewed and awards determined based on eligibility and available funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: Arts and entertainment businesses located in Hagerstown's Arts and Entertainment District are exempt from paying Maryland's Admissions and Amusement Tax. Qualifying businesses register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office to receive the exemption.

Businesses must register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Combined Registration Application (CRA) form to activate and maintain the exemption.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Admissions and amusement revenue from arts and entertainment activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located within Hagerstown's designated Arts and Entertainment District in Washington County, Maryland.

Located within Hagerstown's Arts and Entertainment District
Must register with Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Comptroller of Maryland Combined Registration Application (CRA)
Business must be actively engaged in arts and entertainment operations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Comptroller of Maryland Combined Registration Application (CRA) form. Submit completed registration to activate the exemption. Contact the City of Hagerstown or Maryland State Comptroller's Office for assistance with the application process and to verify business location eligibility within the Arts and Entertainment District.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps Maryland families pay past-due utility bills and avoid heating crises by making energy costs more affordable.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Assistance paying past-due electric utility bills to help resolve arrearages and prevent heating crises.

structured_extraction.program_description: A designated district program that supports arts and entertainment businesses through incentives and support services to develop a vibrant cultural and entertainment area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Incentives and support for arts and entertainment businesses in the designated district.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants for redevelopment projects in Hagerstown's city center. Developers receive grants ranging from $150,000 to $250,000 with a required 2:1 match, resulting in total projects valued from $450,000 to $750,000 or more.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from a minimum of $150,000 to a maximum of $250,000, requiring a minimum 2:1 match from the developer. Total project costs range from $450,000 to $750,000 or more. Funds support redevelopment projects including but not limited to adaptive reuse of buildings, new construction, and infrastructure improvements in the designated city center area.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit developers undertaking redevelopment projects in Hagerstown's city center.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Redevelopment projects in the city center including adaptive reuse, new construction, demolition, site preparation, and related infrastructure improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City center of Hagerstown, Maryland, as defined in the program guidelines and maps provided in the application materials.
requirements_list: Minimum 2:1 match from developer required
Project must be located within the designated City Center redevelopment area
Applicant must complete the formal application using the provided Guidelines and Application Form
Project must meet city planning and zoning requirements
Applicant must demonstrate financial capacity to complete the project

Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: City Center Vacant Storefront Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown offers grants to revitalize vacant storefronts in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use Zoning District. The program aims to bring first-floor commercial spaces up to current code standards, decrease blight, preserve structures, and generate employment opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants with no minimum amount and a maximum of $50,000. Funds are disbursed after staff verification that all work has been completed to code, all required site inspections have been approved, and final receipts have been provided. A Letter of Commitment from the City may be used to assist in financing the project. The program provides up to 100% reimbursement for eligible renovation and upgrade costs.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Department of Community and Economic Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Business owners and property owners seeking to revitalize vacant storefronts in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use Zoning District
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovation and upgrades to bring vacant first-floor commercial spaces up to current code standards in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use Zoning District. Eligible costs include structural repairs, building systems upgrades, accessibility improvements, façade improvements, and interior finishing to comply with city code and make spaces suitable for commercial use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use (CC-MU) Zoning District in Hagerstown, part of the City's Sustainable Communities Area. Projects must be located within the specifically designated Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use Zoning District.
requirements_list: Projects must be located in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use Zoning District
All upgrades must be performed to City Code
All projects must comply with federal, state, and local codes, laws, and ordinances
A development plan outlining the renovation schedule and major project components must accompany the application
All work must be verified as completed to code with all required site inspections approved
Final receipts must be provided before funds are disbursed
Property must have been vacant for a minimum period or meet specific vacancy criteria
Owner must demonstrate financial commitment to the project

Projects will be evaluated based on economic impact, proximity to Public Square, renovation budget, square footage being revitalized, building condition and code violations, and length of prior vacancy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit an application form with a detailed development plan outlining the renovation schedule and major project components. The application is reviewed by a cross-department Review Committee that evaluates proposals using specific criteria including economic impact, proximity to Public Square, renovation budget, square footage being revitalized, building condition and code violations, and length of prior vacancy. Approved applicants receive a Letter of Commitment from the City which may be used to assist in securing financing. Once renovation work is completed, applicants must provide documentation of completion and all work is verified by City staff. Site inspections are conducted to confirm compliance with code requirements. Upon final verification and submission of receipts, the grant funds are disbursed to reimburse eligible costs.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Redevelopment projects city-wide including commercial, mixed-use, and residential rehabilitation and improvements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A matching grant program administered by the City of Hagerstown that provides incentives to businesses and property owners to enhance their building's presentation with improved storefront designs, façade elements, and attractive signage. structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 50% matching grant program providing reimbursement for approved projects. Commercial Sign grants range from a minimum of $250 to a maximum of $1,500, with a required 1:1 applicant match (minimum $250, maximum $1,500). Façade grants range from a minimum of $2,500 to a maximum of $7,500, with a required 1:1 applicant match (minimum $2,500, maximum $7,500). All projects must pertain to commercial or mixed-use buildings. The program is on a first-come, first-served basis subject to funding availability. Applicants must complete an application form with project details and submit it to the City of Hagerstown Department of Community and Economic Development (DCED). Upon approval and project completion, applicants receive reimbursement for the approved grant amount.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and property owners in Hagerstown who own or operate commercial or mixed-use buildings and seek to improve signs and building exteriors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Storefront design improvements, façade elements, and commercial signage enhancements for commercial or mixed-use buildings, including sign installation or renovation and building façade improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Hagerstown, Maryland city limits, including commercial areas throughout the city.
requirements_list: Projects must pertain to commercial or mixed-use buildings
Applicant must provide a 1:1 matching investment
Projects must be approved by the city before work begins
Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis
Property must be a commercial or mixed-use location
Work must involve sign and/or façade improvements
Commercial Sign projects range from $250-$1,500 with matching funds required
Façade projects range from $2,500-$7,500 with matching funds required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application form along with project details, photos, cost estimates, and other required documentation to the City of Hagerstown DCED (Department of Community and Economic Development). Applications are reviewed and approved on a first-come, first-served basis subject to funding availability. The city will review the application and notify the applicant of approval status. Upon approval and project completion, applicants submit receipts and proof of completion to receive reimbursement for the approved grant amount (up to 50% of project costs). Contact the DCED team at DCED@Hagerstownmd.org for detailed application guidelines and required documentation.

structured_extraction.program_description: An incentive program for businesses operating within the Enterprise Zone boundaries in Hagerstown, providing tax and regulatory benefits to encourage business development and investment in designated areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax and regulatory benefits for businesses located within the Enterprise Zone boundaries.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses and entrepreneurs locating or expanding in the Hagerstown Enterprise Zone.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business operations and development within the Enterprise Zone.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Enterprise Zone areas within Hagerstown, Maryland, including the CC-MU zoning area with expanded boundaries effective June 2021.
requirements_list: Business must be located within the Enterprise Zone boundaries
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department for application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps property owners install or upgrade fire suppression systems by funding water service lines, meter vaults, water meters, and other utility infrastructure directly associated with fire suppression systems that meet National Fire Protection Association standards.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants range from a minimum of $7,500 to a maximum of $50,000. Applicants must provide a 1:1 matching investment from their own funds. For example, a $25,000 grant requires an additional $25,000 investment from the applicant for a total project cost of $50,000. Matching costs can include all work related to fire suppression system installation, both interior and exterior. Projects must have a water service meter that is 4 inches or larger. Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to available funding.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Hagerstown Department of Planning and Economic Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of residential, commercial, professional office, retail, and mixed-use buildings in Hagerstown's Sustainable Communities Area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation or upgrade of fire suppression systems that meet National Fire Protection Association standards, including automatic sprinkler systems, water service and fire lines, meter vaults, water meters, sprinkler heads, piping, mains, and backflow devices. Must be associated with brick and mortar renovation projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the City of Hagerstown's Sustainable Communities Area.
requirements_list: Fully residential, commercial, professional office, retail, or mixed-use projects
Projects must be located within the City's Sustainable Communities Area
Applicants must be in good standing with the City of Hagerstown
Total project cost must demonstrate a minimum 1:1 match of applicant funds
Fire suppression projects with water service installations associated with brick and mortar renovation projects with service meters that are 4 inches or larger
Application must be aligned with the City of Hagerstown's overall vision
Applicants must complete and submit the Fire Suppression System Grant Application with required documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed Fire Suppression System Grant Application form with all required documentation to the Department of Planning and Economic Development. Applications are reviewed and approved on a first-come, first-served basis subject to available funding. Contact the Department of Planning and Economic Development at dped@hagerstownmd.org for more information and to request application materials.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Hagerstown Fire Department provides and installs free smoke detectors to eligible residential properties as part of their fire prevention efforts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free smoke detectors are provided and installed at no charge. Eligible residents in 1 to 3 family dwellings can receive one free smoke detector on each living level of their home.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of 1 to 3 family dwellings in Hagerstown
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of smoke detectors for fire safety
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Hagerstown city limits. Residents of apartment buildings with 4 or more units are not eligible as their landlords are required to have electric detectors installed per City code.
requirements_list: Must live in a 1 to 3 family dwelling in Hagerstown
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request free smoke detectors by clicking the request form link on the Fire Department website or by calling (301) 790-2476.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZone) program helps small businesses in urban and rural communities gain preferential access to federal procurement opportunities through the Small Business Administration. It provides certification and contracting opportunities for small businesses located in Historically Underutilized Business Zones, including designated areas in Hagerstown, Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HUBZone-certified small businesses receive competitive and sole source contracting opportunities with the federal government, plus a 10% price evaluation preference in full and open contract competitions and subcontracting opportunities. The federal government has a goal of awarding 3% of all dollars for federal prime contracts to HUBZone-certified small business concerns.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses located in historically underutilized business zones in urban and rural communities, including HUBZone areas in Hagerstown, Maryland, seeking federal contracting opportunities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Businesses certified through this program can compete for federal procurement contracts and subcontracting opportunities, enabling business development through federal contract awards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in designated HUBZone qualified tracts in historically underutilized areas. Hagerstown, Maryland has designated HUBZone areas.
requirements_list: Must be a small business
Must be located in a designated HUBZone qualified tract
Business must meet HUBZone eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses can apply for HUBZone certification through the Small Business Administration. The SBA determines which businesses are eligible, maintains a listing of qualified HUBZone small businesses, and adjudicates protests of eligibility. Businesses may also contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department for local HUBZone certification details.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Hagerstown Homeownership Initiative offers financial assistance to help reduce barriers to homeownership within the City of Hagerstown. The program provides up to $7,500 in down payment and closing cost support through a forgivable loan-to-grant program, designed to support neighborhoods across the city by reducing vacant homes and boosting new homeownership.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides up to $7,500 in down payment and closing cost incentives through a forgivable loan-to-grant program. Funds are provided as a forgivable loan that converts to a grant if the borrower meets program conditions, including maintaining owner occupancy for a specified period. No payments are required to the City if conditions are met.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homebuyers in the City of Hagerstown, including first-time home buyers, current renters, and those purchasing vacant or distressed properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing cost assistance for home purchases within the City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible properties must be located within the City of Hagerstown. Eligible property types include single-family homes, townhomes, and condos. Program prioritizes purchases of vacant or distressed properties.
requirements_list: Applicant must be purchasing property within the City of Hagerstown
Applications must be submitted at least 30 days prior to settlement
Priority given to first-time home buyers, current renters, and those purchasing vacant or distressed properties
Applicant must meet income and credit requirements as specified by the program
Property must be used as primary residence
Applicant must obtain financing approval from a lender before application submission
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete the Hagerstown Homeownership Initiative Application Form and submit it at least 30 days prior to settlement. The application should include documentation of loan approval, proof of income, and property details. Guidelines and application forms are available on the city website and through the program contact.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program administered by the City of Hagerstown that provides ongoing financing to small businesses and developers for growth, expansion, rehabilitation, code compliance, and façade enhancement projects in Hagerstown. Repaid funds are recycled back into the program to support additional businesses, ensuring a continuous source of capital for the local business community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $200,000 or 80% of total project cost (whichever is less), with a minimum loan of $5,000. Micro-enterprise loans available up to $5,000. Working capital loans capped at $30,000. Fixed interest rate of PRIME plus 1% (minimum 3%). Loan terms up to 7 years (5 years for working capital). Requires minimum 20% cash equity investment of total project costs (40% for new restaurants open 3 years or less). Repayment begins within one month of project completion or equipment purchase. Repaid funds are recycled back into the program to support additional businesses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses or developers organized as a proprietorship, partnership, limited liability company, or corporation with annual business sales less than $5,000,000 for each of the last two years, located in Hagerstown and seeking loan financing for business growth, expansion, rehabilitation, code compliance, or façade enhancement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land improvements (grading, streets, parking lots, utilities, landscaping), building purchase or renovation, machinery or equipment with at least 5 years useful life, building construction, leasehold improvements, micro-enterprise activities (5 or fewer employees), working capital, business expansion, equipment, and other approved business needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Hagerstown, Maryland
requirements_list: Business sales must be less than $5,000,000 annually for each of the last 2 years
Organized as proprietorship, partnership, limited liability company, or corporation
Minimum 20% cash equity investment of total project costs (40% for new restaurants open 3 years or less)
Credit check required
Non-refundable application fee based on requested loan amount
For leasehold improvements, lease must equal or exceed loan term and city must secure lien on land, building, and improvements
Business must be located in Hagerstown
Owner must be actively involved in business operations
Personal guarantee required from business owner(s)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application with required documentation including business plan, personal financial statements, tax returns, credit authorization, and project details to the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department. A credit check will be conducted and a non-refundable application fee is required based on the loan amount requested. The program reviews applications on a rolling basis. Complete program guidelines and application form available through the program office.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that offers incentives to building owners to renovate buildings within the PEP Zone in Hagerstown's City Center and assists with attracting businesses to those renovated buildings. The program supports business development and economic growth through partnerships between the City of Hagerstown and participating businesses and property owners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners receive an annual grant equal to city property tax for 5 years, two free EDUs (equivalent dwelling units) valued at $13,800, one year of free parking and 50% discount for 4 years, waiver of development fees, expedited review through Planning Department and Historic District Commission, code flexibility using Maryland Building Rehabilitation Code, and 2 hours of consultation on historic tax credits. Businesses in approved buildings can receive rent assistance providing a maximum of $30,000 paid to the property owner for the first two or three years of operation.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building renovation and improvement within the PEP Zone. Property owners must meet minimum investment requirements: $250,000 for commercial projects, $100,000 for residential projects, and $200,000 for mixed-use projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides Maryland renters and landlords statewide with free information and assistance about tenant rights and responsibilities, including lease reviews, eviction procedures, rent-related issues, housing code enforcement, substandard housing complaints, security deposits, and lead paint concerns. The program also offers referrals to legal service providers and other agencies that can help tenants. The program operates under Economic Action Maryland Fund, a multi-racial, people-centered movement dedicated to expanding economic rights and housing justice for working families, low-income communities, and communities of color.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free technical assistance including lease reviews, eviction notification guidance, information on nonpayment of rent procedures, code enforcement education, substandard housing complaint assistance, security deposit information, rent escrow guidance, and lead paint education. The program provides information via intake form, hotline, online assistance, one-page fact sheets, and comprehensive tenant guides. Assistance covers topics such as researching landlords, understanding lease agreements, application processes, security deposits, move-in procedures, common tenant issues including maintenance and repairs, lease breaking, rent payment problems, automatic lease renewal clauses, property sales, noise and harassment, landlord retaliation, security deposit returns, and eviction processes. Referrals to legal service providers and other agencies are also available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland tenants and landlords with housing questions or rental issues
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides information and guidance on tenant rights and responsibilities. It does not provide financial assistance. Services include lease reviews, guidance on eviction procedures, rent payment issues, housing code enforcement, security deposits, lead paint concerns, and referrals to legal services and other agencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland, covering all counties and Baltimore City
requirements_list: Applicants must be tenants or landlords with housing questions or rental issues within the scope of the program's services
Tenants seeking assistance should have questions or problems related to lease agreements, rental housing conditions, eviction matters, or fair housing discrimination
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested parties can submit an intake form online and receive a response within 24 to 48 hours. The program also provides direct assistance via hotline (call Tuesday through Friday from 10 AM until 2 PM at 443-447-7336) and online channels. Downloadable fact sheets, comprehensive guides, and self-help resources are available as self-help resources. Individuals can also contact the District Court Self-Help Center (Monday through Friday, 8:30 AM to 8:00 PM, 410-260-1392) for additional assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Voluntary Crime-Free Multi-Housing Program (Crime-Free Housing Training)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to help owners and managers of rental properties keep drugs and other illegal activity off their properties, while educating landlords and residents to improve neighborhood livability by reducing crime. The program includes a basic 4-hour training course that introduces landlords, property owners, and managers to best practices for achieving crime-free properties, providing tools and techniques to promote safe communities. The full program consists of three phases: management training, premises security assessments, and resident training. While voluntary, some property owners and managers may be required to attend if their property receives a certain number of notices from the city.

list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

The training also meets Excessive Use of City Services training requirements. Classes may be cancelled if no registrations are received 48 hours prior to the start time. Participants receive tools and resources to implement crime prevention strategies at their properties.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and education on crime prevention practices, management techniques, premises security assessments, and resident education on crime prevention.

Participation is voluntary unless property has received multiple notices from the city

Classes are held at Washington County Free Library, Room 334. Classes may be cancelled if no registrations are received 48 hours prior to the start. Program is free and voluntary with no obligation to continue after the initial training.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program established to commission site-specific public art works for installation on property owned by the City of Rockville. The program has been operating since 1978 and commissions artworks that reference historical, cultural, or socially relevant themes. The program aims to nurture, inspire and expand citizens' awareness and educational experience with the visual arts, enhance the community's uniqueness, and augment Rockville's perception as a leader in civic cultural achievements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program is funded through multiple sources: (1) Art in Public Places (AIPP) Ordinance #15-13 provides funding equal to one-tenth of one percent of the prior year's adopted General Fund budget, subject to appropriation by Mayor and Council; (2) Incorporation of Works of Art in Public Architecture (AIPA) Ordinance #30-78 provides one percent of capital improvement project costs for eligible projects; (3) Publicly Accessible Art in Private Development Ordinance #3-04; and (4) private donations and public-private partnerships. All project budgets are all-inclusive covering design, fabrication, installation, site enhancements, and a two-year warranty, with no in-kind supplemental funding by the city. Artists and organizations submit proposals for public art commissions through competitive selection processes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Artists and arts organizations proposing public art for Rockville's public spaces. Both emerging and established artists are encouraged to submit applications.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commissioning and installation of site-specific public artwork on city-owned property. Funds support visual arts projects including paintings, sculptures, engravings, carvings, frescoes, mobiles, murals, collages, mosaics, statues, bas reliefs, tapestries, photographs, drawings, stained glass, fountains, and other artworks for exterior and interior sites. Artwork must address the community's character and environment while referencing historical, cultural, or socially relevant themes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rockville city limits, specifically on property owned by the City of Rockville. Priority focus areas include: Gateways (major city entrances), Metro Stations (Rockville and Twinbrook Stations and adjacent properties), Town Center revitalization areas, neighborhood parks (especially frequently used parks with good visibility and access), and key neighborhood sites such as crossroads, shopping areas, rotaries, and subdivision entrances.
requirements_list: Artwork must be site-specific
Works should reference historical, cultural, or socially relevant themes of the surrounding site
Artwork must reflect the city's dynamism and diversity
Artists must collaborate whenever possible with designers or contractors working at the project site
Strong consideration given to durability, life expectancy, and safety issues
Commissioned works become property of the City of Rockville and part of the public art collection
All works must be completed within the all-inclusive budget with no city in-kind supplemental funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The City of Rockville uses three types of selection processes depending on the project: (1) Full and Open Competition (most widely used): An artist nomination committee is established with CAC members, neighborhood representatives, and art professionals. The committee visits sites, develops project guidelines, and issues a 'Call for Entries' nationwide with emphasis on regional and emerging artists. Finalists are selected and given honorariums to prepare detailed proposals. Each finalist presents their proposal at a public meeting. The artist nomination committee recommends to the CAC, which makes its own recommendation to Mayor and Council for final approval. (2) Limited Invitational Competition: Pre-selected artists (identified by nomination committee or CAC) are invited to develop proposals, particularly appropriate for collaborative projects with architects or engineers. (3) Direct Invitation: Rarely used, only with consensus that one artist is uniquely qualified, bypassing the competition process. Throughout all processes, community input is encouraged and all recommendations are documented and presented to subsequent reviewing bodies.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville purchases and installs basic, inverted-U style bicycle parking racks for businesses to enhance bicycle parking and support the bikeway network. The racks are provided and installed at no cost to eligible business owners or property managers whose properties lack nearby bicycle parking. Racks can be installed in public rights-of-way or on private property with a signed agreement, and are designed for short-term bicycle parking available for public use by anyone at any time.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Rockville provides and installs basic, inverted-U style bicycle racks at no cost to eligible businesses on a first-come, first-served basis. Applicants can request either 1 or 2 bicycle racks. Each bicycle rack requires a parking space of 72 inches by 24 inches. If racks are placed along a sidewalk or pedestrian path, there must be at least a five-foot clear walkway once the bicycle racks have been installed. Racks can be installed in public rights-of-way or on private property with a signed agreement. The City of Rockville has final decision authority over all decisions regarding adherence to specifications and rack locations. The program covers the full cost of purchasing and installing racks at the applicant's property.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of basic, inverted-U style bicycle parking racks on the business owner's or property manager's premises to support bicycle parking and enhance the bikeway network.
