structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the Bike Rack Grant Program application form. Complete the application by providing your business name, address, contact information, number of racks requested (1 or 2), description of your interest in providing bike racks, description of existing bike parking on site, property ownership information, and proposed location details (photos are optional but recommended). Submit the completed application by email to bikeways@rockvillemd.gov or by mail to City of Rockville Bicycle Rack Grant Program, c/o Bryan Barnett-Woods, 111 Maryland Avenue, Rockville, MD 20850. A Department of Public Works staff person will review your application and contact you to discuss the project. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. You will be notified once the City determines if you qualify for the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A cooperative purchasing program that helps residents and small business owners install rooftop solar systems at reduced prices by leveraging group buying power. Battery storage and electric vehicle charger options are available. The program typically secures pricing about 20% lower than standard market rates.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Group purchasing program that secures a discount of approximately 20% off the standard installation price. Members receive individual proposals after roof evaluations and choose whether to purchase or lease solar panels at the negotiated group rate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents and small business owners in the Rockville area who want to install solar systems on their homes or businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of rooftop solar systems, battery storage, and electric vehicle chargers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rockville, Maryland area served by Capital Area Solar Switch Together program.
requirements_list: Roof suitable for solar installation
Participants can verify roof suitability through the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up for the contact list through the Solar Switch website. Participants receive roof evaluations. After evaluation, members receive individual proposals and choose whether to sign a contract with the selected installer. Joining the contact list does not commit participants to purchase.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant that funds housing and community development projects benefiting low- and moderate-income households or neighborhoods.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants fund community development and housing projects that serve low- and moderate-income residents or neighborhoods. FY 2027 allocated funding supports eligible activities including: homeowner repair and rehabilitation, acquisition and clearance of land for homeownership or rental housing, acquisition and rehabilitation of rental housing, direct homeownership assistance (down payment or closing costs), development of housing for homeless or formerly homeless individuals, improvements to public facilities and facilities for persons with special needs, economic development activities, and historic preservation activities. Public services and administrative costs for social services are not eligible. Minimum grant request is $15,000. CDBG funds must be expended within a 12-month period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations with 501(c)(3) designation and government/quasi-governmental agencies working on housing and community development projects in Rockville that benefit low- and moderate-income households or neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Homeowner repair, rehabilitation, and reconstruction; acquisition and clearance of land for homeownership or rental housing; acquisition and rehabilitation of rental housing; direct homeownership assistance; development of housing for homeless or formerly homeless individuals; improvements to public facilities and facilities for persons with special needs including accessibility improvements; economic development activities; historic preservation activities. Public services and administrative costs for social services are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must benefit low- and moderate-income households or neighborhoods; beneficiaries must meet HUD income limits (30%, 50%, or 80% of area median income depending on activity type)
Applicant must be a non-profit organization with 501(c)(3) designation or a government/quasi-governmental agency; nonprofits must have 501(c)(3) designation in place by July 1, 2026
Project must comply with federal CDBG eligibility requirements and HUD regulations
Minimum grant request is $15,000
Project must be completed within 12-month period from funding availability (after October 1, 2026)
Davis-Bacon requirements apply for construction or rehabilitation of commercial buildings or residential properties with 8+ units
Section 3 requirements apply - must provide employment, training, and business opportunities for low-income project area residents and businesses
Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) participation and outreach required in bidding process for construction/rehabilitation projects
Montgomery County environmental review and Historic Preservation review (SHPO) must be completed prior to project work beginning
Radon testing and mitigation required if levels are 4.0 pCi/L or greater (Montgomery County is EPA Zone 1)
Applicant must obtain City and Montgomery County general commercial liability insurance and provide certificate of insurance
Funding recipients must comply with federal, county, and city regulations for financial management of CDBG funds
Quarterly reporting required with information on number of individuals/households served including demographic information
Complete all application information; do not alter format or questions
Only complete applications received by deadline will be reviewed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact Sarah Maizel (240-314-8304 or smaizel@rockvillemd.gov) to confirm project eligibility and receive technical assistance. 2. Review FY 2027 CDBG guidelines and eligible activities. 3. Submit a separate online application for each funding request no later than 5:00 p.m. on October 17, 2025. 4. Complete all required forms including the CDBG Project Budget Form. 5. Include all required attachments per the Attachments Checklist. 6. Use the Completeness Checklist to ensure application is complete. 7. Incomplete applications with minor omissions will be returned and applicant will have 7 calendar days to provide missing information. 8. Applications substantially complete with missing information will be resubmitted. 9. If approved by Mayor and Council, you will be notified by December 31, 2025. 10. Approved applications are submitted to Montgomery County for staff funding recommendations to County Executive in January/February 2026. 11. Applications incorporated into County budget approval process. 12. Funds become available after October 1, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides matching grants to neighbors and community organizations working together to accomplish common goals that support the health, vitality, and inclusivity of their neighborhoods. Grant recipients must match funding through cash, in-kind donations, or volunteer hours.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants typically ranging from $500 to $1,000. Applicants must match the grant funds through cash donations, in-kind donations, or volunteer hours valued at $29.95 per hour. Funds can be used for community building programs, community improvement projects, or livability initiatives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Neighbors and community organizations living within Rockville city limits, including neighborhood associations, civic associations, homeowners associations, community groups, groups of neighbors, and student groups.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds may be used for programs or projects that promote community building (development or sustainability of neighborhood associations or community groups, activities promoting inclusion and diversity), community improvement projects (enhancing shared spaces, strengthening community identity), or livability initiatives (education and outreach efforts that strengthen social connections, increase safety, address neighborhood challenges, serve low-income residents, or welcome newcomers).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants and projects must benefit those who live within Rockville city limits.
requirements_list: Applicants must designate one individual to manage the grant contracts and funds.
Each group must have at least three members.
If applying on behalf of an established organization, applicants must provide documentation of authorization.
All funds provided through this grant are subject to taxes.
The total matching funds (cash and in-kind donations combined) must match or be greater than the amount requested.
Volunteer hours must be detailed with information about volunteers and their specific contributions; volunteers are valued at $29.95 per hour.

Grant recipients must submit a summary of project outcomes, receipts showing proper use of funding, and at least two visual items (such as photos or printed materials) to illustrate the project by Dec. 18, 2026.
All funds must be used by Dec. 14, 2026, and any unused funds must be returned to the City of Rockville by Dec. 18, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Community Empowerment Matching Grant Budget Worksheet to estimate costs and matching funds. Create an account on the online grant portal at grantinterface.com. Click the Apply button and complete the Eligibility Form to determine if your project qualifies. Complete the full application and submit by 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 5, 2025. Award notifications are sent by Feb. 13, 2026. After project completion, submit receipts, visual items, and a project summary through the online portal by Dec. 18, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: Personalized services providing resource referrals, emergency financial information, home and hospital visits, counseling resources, notary services, and financial aid to qualified candidates for recreational classes and membership.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial aid to qualified candidates for recreational classes and membership; resource referrals and counseling support; notary services available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville residents in need of resource referrals, emergency financial information, or financial assistance; Spanish-language support available.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial aid for recreational classes and membership; resource referrals and emergency financial assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville residents.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified candidate for financial aid
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-314-8816 or 240-314-8817 for more information and to apply. A Spanish speaker is available if needed.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville provides annual grants to local nonprofit organizations that partner with the city to support community services and enrichment programs that benefit city residents and visitors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Rockville providesannual grants with approximately $1.5 million in total funding available. Approximately 40 applicants are typically awarded. Grants are provided on a reimbursement basis for expenses incurred per the grant budget, requiring receipts and documentation of expenses for each quarter. Grant recipients must report required outputs and outcomes data quarterly through an online grant portal, with specific reporting deadlines: Quarter 1 report due after October 1, 2025; Quarter 2 report due after January 1, 2026; Six-month program measures report due January 15, 2026; Quarter 3 report due after April 1, 2026; Quarter 4 report due after July 1, 2026; and Year-end program measures report due after July 4, 2026. Grantees must comply with all insurance requirements and respond to City communications within 10 weekdays.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations that provide human services or community enrichment programs to individuals residing in the corporate city limits of Rockville
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for community services and enrichment programs that benefit city residents and visitors, including but not limited to: scholarship programs, emergency response and safety services, theater and cultural programming, enrichment events and festivals, arts and science education, historic preservation programs, clothing distribution, elderly support services, emergency and permanent shelters, developmental day care, food pantries, health clinics, language and citizenship education, mental health services, parenting support and education, youth development and therapeutic recreation, information and referral services, housing services for adults with disabilities, and skilled job training and placement services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only organizations serving individuals residing in the corporate city limits of Rockville are eligible. Applicants may use the Rockville Address and Residency Check featured map to verify the city limits of Rockville and check the Rockville residency status of addresses.
requirements_list: Organization must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit
Must provide community services and/or enrichment programs to individuals residing in the corporate city limits of Rockville
Must serve individuals residing in the corporate city limits of Rockville
Must submit audit, financial statement, or compilation for most recent completed operating year
Must submit IRS Form 990 for most recent completed operating year
Must provide board roster identifying officers, term limits, addresses, and phone numbers
Must submit report from last formal and/or informal evaluation of the program if applicable
Must submit document of application submission authority signed by executive director and board president on organization letterhead
Must complete and submit Budget, Outputs, and Outcomes Worksheet

Must attend mandatory virtual technical assistance session (one of three sessions offered: Tuesday, September 9th, 10:00-11:00 a.m.; Wednesday, September 17th, 2:00-3:00 p.m.; or Wednesday, September 24th, 4:00-5:00 p.m.)
Must be able to provide supporting documentation with quarterly invoices for reimbursement
Must meet quarterly reporting deadlines and six-month and year-end program measures reporting requirements
Must comply with HIPAA regulations if organization is a healthcare provider, or obtain signed client authorization to disclose personal client information for grant reporting purposes
Must maintain required insurance coverage before contract execution, evidenced by certificate of insurance and/or copies of insurance policies
Must respond to all City of Rockville communications within 10 weekdays
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations must: (1) Review eligibility requirements and complete the eligibility quiz to confirm 501(c)(3) status and service to Rockville residents; (2) Attend one of three mandatory virtual technical assistance sessions (Tuesday, September 9th, 10:00-11:00 a.m.; Wednesday, September 17th, 2:00-3:00 p.m.; or Wednesday, September 24th, 4:00-5:00 p.m.); (3) Create a new account and set up login credentials on the City's online grant portal; (4) Complete the online application form; (5) Select appropriate unit of service and program type definitions based on the organization's services; (6) Develop a logic model covering situation, priorities, intended outcomes, inputs, activities, participation, and outcomes; (7) Complete the Budget, Outputs, and Outcomes Worksheet; (8) Gather and submit all required supplemental documents: audit or financial statement for most recent completed operating year, IRS Form 990, board roster with officer information, program evaluation report (if applicable), and document of application submission authority signed by executive director and board president; (9) Submit all materials by 11:59 p.m. on October 17, 2025. Applications must include relevant outputs and outcomes based on service type (e.g., for clothing distribution, food services, elderly support, health care, information/referral, language/citizenship education, and human services agencies).

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville waives all permit fees assessed by the Inspection Services Division that are directly associated with the residential installation of solar photovoltaic systems, electric vehicle charging stations, and energy-efficient heating and cooling upgrades such as heat pumps during the month of April.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Rockville waives all permit fees assessed by the Inspection Services Division for residential installation of solar photovoltaic systems, electric vehicle charging stations, and energy-efficient heating and cooling upgrades including heat pumps. Eligible homeowners submit applications by April 30 and must have them accepted by city staff by 5 p.m. on May 1. Fee waivers cover: solar PV systems including panels, inverters, and critical components; electrical panel upgrades necessary to accommodate solar PV or EV charging systems (including service entrance cable, meter enclosures, conduit, disconnects, panels, grounding conductors, feeders); EV charging systems including receptacles, charging cords, conductors, disconnects, overcurrent devices; and geothermal or high-efficiency heat pump HVAC systems with associated electrical work and duct installation/modification. Energy Storage Systems up to 20kWh are included. Structural modifications, site modifications, driveway installations, right-of-way permits, and public works permits are not covered.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Thursday, April 30, with applications accepted by city staff by 5 p.m. Friday, May 1
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single-family homeowners in the City of Rockville making eligible residential home improvements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of solar photovoltaic systems (including panels, inverters, conductors, disconnects, transfer switches, overcurrent devices), electric vehicle charging stations (including receptacles, charging cords, conductors, disconnects, overcurrent devices), energy-efficient heating and cooling upgrades such as geothermal or high-efficiency heat pump HVAC systems, electrical panel upgrades necessary to accommodate these installations, Energy Storage Systems up to 20kWh, and associated ductwork installation/modification
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville, Maryland
requirements_list: Installation must be single-family residential only (commercial and multifamily residential projects not eligible)
Work must involve solar photovoltaic systems, electric vehicle charging stations, or geothermal/high-efficiency heat pump HVAC upgrades
Application must be submitted by April 30 with acceptance by city staff by 5 p.m. on May 1
Applicants must submit plans that clearly identify location, nature, and extent of proposed work
For rooftop solar panel installations, a statement from a licensed engineer verifying existing structure can support proposed array is required
Structural modifications, site modifications (driveways, footings, piers), right-of-way permits, and public works permits are not covered by fee waiver
Energy Storage Systems must not exceed 20kWh rating
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the City of Rockville's permit page at https://www.rockvillemd.gov/services/apply-for-a-building-or-trade-permit/ or apply directly through MGO at https://www.mgoconnect.org/cp/portal if you have an existing account. Submit your permit application with required plans clearly identifying location, nature, and extent of proposed work. For rooftop solar installations, include a statement from a licensed engineer verifying the existing structure can support the proposed array. City of Rockville staff will process the fee waiver on your behalf and send email notification confirming your permit qualifies for the waiver. Applications must be submitted by April 30 and accepted by city staff by 5 p.m. on May 1.

structured_extraction.program_name: Eat Fresh Rockville SNAP/EBT FMNP-WIC Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides matching funds to customers who use federal nutrition benefits at the Rockville Farmers Market. The program matches SNAP/EBT, P-EBT, and FMNP-WIC benefits with Maryland Market Money tokens up to $15 per customer per market day to purchase locally grown produce, meat, cheese, and dairy.
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides matching funds (Maryland Market Money tokens) up to $15 per customer, per market day. Customers using SNAP/EBT or P-EBT cards receive one-to-one matching. Customers using FMNP-WIC checks receive matching tokens when they exchange their receipt at the information tent.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with SNAP/EBT, P-EBT, or FMNP-WIC benefits who shop at the Rockville Farmers Market.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The matching tokens can be used to purchase locally grown fruit, vegetables, meat, cheese, and dairy at the Rockville Farmers Market.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available at the Rockville Farmers Market, located at the corner of Route 28 and Monroe Street in Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have valid SNAP/EBT, P-EBT, or FMNP-WIC benefits
Must visit the Rockville Farmers Market during market hours (Saturdays, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.)
Matching funds are given once per customer per market day
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For SNAP/EBT or P-EBT: Visit the farmers market with your card, find the information tent at the market entrance, tell staff you want to use your card, get SNAP tokens using your card and receive one-to-one matching MMM tokens up to $15. For FMNP-WIC: Visit the market with your FMNP-WIC check, purchase produce from vendors and get a receipt, take the receipt to the information tent, and exchange it for matching MMM tokens.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program offers financial assistance through matching reimbursement funds to residents and property owners who have made improvements to their properties to mitigate future damage from flooding events.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides up to 50% reimbursement of total costs for approved flood mitigation measures, with a maximum assistance amount of $5,000 per applicant. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. Itemized receipts or invoices are required for reimbursement. Approved measures include cost-effective methods such as routine gutter and downspout maintenance and redirection, cleaning drainage ditches and storm drains, building up sunken areas around foundations, installing drainage channels or drains, improving yard slope, flood alarm installation, watertight storage containers, sump pump installation with battery backup, raised appliances and outlets above flood level elevation line, window and door flood protection, flood stoppage equipment, protective materials and equipment, protective flood walls with impermeable materials around foundations, surface grading with earthen berms, and French drain systems.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents and property owners in Rockville who have made or plan to make improvements to mitigate flooding damage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Approved measures to improve properties and mitigate future damage from flooding events, including drainage improvements, flood-proofing measures for homes and yards, and protective equipment and materials.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rockville, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Property owner or resident of Rockville
Made improvements to property for flood mitigation or planning to make improvements
Measures must be approved by the program
Itemized receipts or invoices required for reimbursement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants apply online through the Chesapeake Bay Trust portal at rockvillemd.gov/floodassistance. The Chesapeake Bay Trust reviews and processes all applications. Only approved measures will be reimbursed. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state economic development program that provides eligibility for grants and loan assistance for acquisition, development, public interpretation, and programming, as well as tax incentives for the rehabilitation of non-designated historic buildings and non-historic buildings in active tourism use within Rockville's Heritage Area.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants and loan assistance for eligible projects including acquisition, development, preservation, restoration, public interpretation, and programming of historic properties. Capital grants are available to local jurisdictions for up to 50% of eligible project costs, with applicants able to provide 25% of their grant match 'in kind.' Tax credits (Sustainable Communities Rehabilitation Tax Credit) are available to private property owners for rehabilitation of properties listed or eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places. Non-capital grants are available to non-profits and local jurisdictions for exhibits and educational products.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, non-profit organizations, and local jurisdictions within the Rockville Heritage Area eligible for historic building rehabilitation, preservation, adaptive reuse, and tourism-related projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, development, preservation, restoration, public interpretation, and programming of historic properties; rehabilitation of non-designated historic buildings and non-historic buildings in active tourism use; heritage education and recreational programming; streetscape and wayfinding improvements; and infrastructure improvements to heritage sites.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Certified Heritage Area (CHA) encompasses approximately the City of Rockville's 1949 annexation boundaries and includes the largest concentration of heritage resources. Non-contiguous historically significant sites may also be included. The area includes downtown Rockville, surrounding residential neighborhoods, and greenway access along Rock Creek and Watts Branch.
requirements_list: Property must be located within the Certified Heritage Area (CHA) or be a designated Target Investment project
For tax credits: property must be listed in or eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places
For grants: projects must align with the Heritage Area themes (Farming, Underground Railroad and Quaker culture, Technological advances)
Projects must further educational and recreational objectives of the Heritage Area
Grant applicants must provide minimum 50% match funding (25% may be provided in-kind)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible applicants submit proposals to the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority (MHAA) for consideration. Target Investment projects are identified as highest priority and implementation is proposed between two to five years depending on funding. Applicants should work with City staff to ensure project alignment with Heritage Area goals and management plan objectives.

structured_extraction.program_description: HEAP provides one-time financial assistance to eligible City of Rockville residents who live in housing with documented energy inefficiencies. The program helps residents access weatherization services, home energy assessments, and energy audits, and supplements up to $1,000 for utility efficiency retrofits.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides up to $1,000 in financial assistance for utility efficiency retrofits. Funding may be used for energy-efficient home upgrades including insulation, air infiltration reduction, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace work, refrigerator retrofit, health and safety items such as moisture and mold remediation, asbestos abatement, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, radon mitigation, roof repair, plumbing and electrical repair, structural repair, and removal of lead hazards. The applicant may contribute additional funds to supplement HEAP assistance. DHCD will match contributions and the total assistance amount will be paid directly to the approved contractor or payee.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Housing and Community Development Department, Community Services Division
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Rockville residents who reside in housing with documented energy inefficiencies and meet income guidelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy-efficient upgrades including insulation, air infiltration reduction, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and repair, refrigerator retrofit, health and safety items (moisture and mold remediation, asbestos abatement, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, radon mitigation, roof repair, plumbing and electrical repair, structural repair, lead hazard removal). Funds cannot be used for past-due utility bills or household repairs that are not energy-efficient.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only residents within the corporate city limits of Rockville. Applicants must have resided in Rockville for at least six months prior to application and at the time of application. Property must be applicant's primary residence.
requirements_list: Reside in Rockville city limits for at least 180 days (six months) prior to application

Meet 60% Area Median Income (AMI) guidelines based on 2018 income eligibility limits (1-person: $24,280; 2-person: $32,920; 3-person: $41,560; 4-person: $50,200; 5-person: $58,840; add $8,640 for each additional person)
Be a previous or new Emergency Assistance Program recipient
Use electricity or natural gas for energy and heating purposes
Be a PEPCO, BGE, Delmarva Power, SMECO, or First Energy customer
Be a renter or homeowner (renters need landlord written verification and approval for retrofits)

Have already been approved for one of: Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP), EmPOWER Maryland Low-Income Energy Efficiency Program (LIEEP), Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP), or Enhanced Weatherization Program
Provide documentation of three months of utility bills
Provide documentation of a comprehensive home energy audit completed before application
Provide proof of home ownership or current dated and signed lease
Provide one additional proof of residency (utility bill, etc.)
Provide signed affidavit of income and tax forms (1040) from previous year for all adults
Provide two most recent paystubs for all adults and documentation of any other income
Provide monthly budget documentation
Renters must provide documentation of portion of rent paid and RHE/HOC/other subsidy if applicable
Renters must provide landlord or property manager approval for energy-efficient retrofits
Agree to reside at the property for one year post-retrofit
Provide documentation of three months of utility bills post-retrofit as delineated in service agreement
Property must be applicant's primary residence
Demonstrate previous rent payments have been made for the property
If applicant leases space in primary residence to renter(s), must have express consent of community services manager
Provide driver's license or other photo ID with address for all adults in household
Provide Social Security Number/TIN card for all family members
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review eligibility criteria, eligible expenses, and ineligible expenses. 2. Obtain a completed home energy audit from an approved provider. 3. Complete the HEAP application form and return it to the Community Services Division at hcd@rockvillemd.gov or call 240-314-8310. 4. Gather all required documentation including income verification, proof of residency, utility bills, and home audit documentation. 5. Submit documentation checklist with required supporting documents. 6. The community services referral coordinator will review the application for completeness and eligibility. 7. If approved, eligible residents will be referred to appropriate local and statewide programs providing weatherization services and energy assessments. 8. Applicant may contribute additional funds which DHCD will match. 9. Upon final approval, payment is issued to the approved contractor or payee by check.

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Choice Voucher Program (Rockville Housing Enterprises)
structured_extraction.program_description: Rockville Housing Enterprises (RHE), the city's public housing authority, administers the Housing Choice Voucher Program to help low-income families, the elderly, and persons with disabilities afford decent and safe housing. Vouchers can be used to rent market-rate apartments at more affordable prices, with certain vouchers applicable at any qualifying residence. RHE serves Rockville, Maryland and surrounding areas within its service territory.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Housing vouchers that can be used to rent market-rate apartments at reduced costs, helping low-income families, the elderly, and persons with disabilities afford decent and safe housing. Vouchers may be used at any qualifying residence within the RHE service territory.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Waitlist currently closed to new applicants as of February 28, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income families, elderly individuals, and persons with disabilities in Rockville and surrounding areas seeking affordable rental housing through vouchers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance for housing, including renting market-rate apartments at reduced costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville, Maryland and surrounding areas within RHE service territory.
requirements_list: Low-income status meeting income eligibility requirements
Elderly or disabled status (for applicable voucher categories)
Waitlist currently closed to new applicants as of February 28, 2025
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit rockvillehe.org to learn more and apply through Rockville Housing Enterprises. The waitlist is currently closed to new applicants as of February 28, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Homeownership Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville requires some for-sale properties to be available to Rockville residents at more affordable prices than market-rate homes. The MPDU Homeownership Program helps first-time homebuyers purchase homes at below-market prices within the City of Rockville. Non-U.S. citizens may apply. Buyers must maintain the property as their primary residence for a full 30-year ownership commitment period, with resale guidelines if selling before 30 years. After the 30-year control period expires, the original owner must pay 50% of profits to the City's Affordable Housing Fund upon the first sale on the open market.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides access to for-sale properties priced below market rate. Homes are offered exclusively to eligible first-time homebuyers who must maintain the property as their primary residence for the entire 30-year control period. Maximum household income limits are based on area median income (AMI) percentages: 50% AMI, 60% AMI, or 80% AMI, depending on home pricing. Buyers must obtain bank financing with a minimum mortgage of $150,000 and commit to a 30-year ownership period. If selling before 30 years, the city's resale guidelines apply, which allow credits for home improvements up to 10% of the original purchase price (with appropriate documentation). Upon the first sale after the 30-year control period expires, the owner must pay 50% of the sale profits to the City's Affordable Housing Fund. Refinancing is permitted during the control period with City approval.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; applications accepted at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers who are Rockville residents or work in the City of Rockville and meet income limits. Non-U.S. citizens may apply. Priority on the waiting list is given to households with members who currently live or work in the City of Rockville, have a household member older than 55, or have a larger household size.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of a home to be used as the owner's primary residence for the full 30-year MPDU control period. Owners may make improvements to the property and claim credits for certain permanent improvements (up to 10% of purchase price) when reselling during the control period.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available in the City of Rockville, Maryland. Priority on the waiting list is given to households with members who currently live or work in the City of Rockville, have a household member older than 55, or have a larger household size.
requirements_list: First-time homebuyer status; cannot have owned a home or been on the deed to a home anywhere within the past 5 years
Household gross income must be within specified AMI limits (50%, 60%, or 80% AMI) at time of sales agreement
All household members over 18 years old must submit proof of income; all sources of income must be disclosed
Qualify for a minimum mortgage of $150,000
Obtain bank financing and provide a notarized pre-qualification letter from lender (validity one year from date)
Attend a six-hour HUD-approved First-Time Homebuyer Class and obtain completion certificate
Obtain mortgage pre-approval letter from lender showing all household income and verified financial information
Home must be owner's primary residence for full 30-year MPDU control period and may not be rented to others without City written permission
Cannot own a second home while owning the MPDU
Commit to own the home for 30 years; if selling before 30 years, must follow city resale guidelines
Cannot purchase another residential property during the control period
Non-U.S. citizens may apply
Must certify that no household member currently owns another residence
Refinancing requires City approval
Income eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Attend a six-hour First-Time Homebuyer Class through Montgomery County's Housing Initiative Partnership or any HUD-approved counseling agency and obtain completion certificate. Step 2: Obtain a mortgage pre-qualification letter from your bank lender. The pre-qualification letter must be on company letterhead, notarized, and include all household income from all sources, household size, available assets, credit score, loan parameters, and a disclaimer that it is valid for one year and is for MPDU program purposes only. Step 3: Complete the MPDU Homeownership Program Application online or request a hard copy or PDF version by emailing rockvillempdu@rockvillemd.gov. The application must be renewed every two years. Step 4: Once your application is received, an MPDU certificate will be sent by email within three to four weeks. You will then be placed on the city's MPDU waiting list based on priority criteria. Step 5: When MPDUs become available, sellers or developers will contact waiting list households to see if they are interested in purchasing. Step 6: Upon agreement to purchase, complete the MPDU Purchaser Agreement and acknowledge receipt of MPDU covenants and Chapter 13.5 of the City Code. For additional information or questions regarding improvement eligibility or resale pricing, contact the Housing Programs Division at hcd@rockvillemd.gov or 240-314-8300. Department of Planning and Development Services can be reached at 240-314-8242 or permit@rockvillemd.gov for permit questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Historic Preservation Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program that provides a 25% tax credit against county real property taxes for qualified expenses on exterior maintenance, restoration, or preservation of historically designated properties in Rockville.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Montgomery County provides a property tax credit equal to 25% of qualified costs expended on documented exterior maintenance, restoration, or preservation work on historically designated properties. Work must be certified eligible by the Historic District Commission. Owners must spend a minimum of $1,000 in a calendar year, and the tax credit is applied against the following year's property taxes. Any unused portion may be carried forward for up to five years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic properties in Rockville that are designated as historic by the Mayor and Council.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified expenses for exterior maintenance, restoration, or preservation of historically designated properties, including approved exterior storm windows and doors, chimney repairs, exterior painting, roof repairs or replacement in-kind, window repairs, architectural trim repairs, gutter replacement, and professional services such as architectural or engineering fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be designated as historic by the City of Rockville Mayor and Council or be within a historic district in Rockville. Properties listed only in the National Register of Historic Places are not eligible for this county tax credit.
requirements_list: Property must be designated as historic by the Mayor and Council or within a Rockville historic district
Work must be certified eligible by the Historic District Commission
Minimum of $1,000 in qualified expenses expended in a calendar year
Application must include copies of receipts for materials or paid receipts from a licensed contractor
Application must include before and after photographs showing the work completed
Owner's labor costs are not eligible; only material costs and professional services qualify
Work must be approved by the Historic District Commission or be ordinary maintenance that does not require HDC review
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Owner submits an application to the Historic District Commission with documentation of expenses, receipts, and photographs. The HDC determines eligibility of expenditures and sends findings to the Montgomery County Department of Finance. The director of finance reviews documentation and notifies the applicant of approval or disapproval.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hot and cold lunches provided daily at noon and bi-monthly Chinese lunch. Donations are welcomed and recommended.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Meals provided daily and bi-monthly special meals.

requirements_list: Reservation required
Program not accepting new registrants at this time
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-314-8810 for reservation information. Monthly meal menu available in multiple languages at Montgomery County Congregate Meal Program.

Eligible projects include permeable pavers and pavements, native landscaping, large-scale tree plantings, community outreach and engagement to reduce pollution, and environmental and sustainability projects that assist or benefit underserved communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to nonprofit organizations for stormwater pollution reduction and natural resource protection projects within Rockville city limits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations with projects within Rockville city limits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that reduce stormwater pollution and protect natural resources, including permeable pavers and pavements, native landscaping, large-scale tree plantings, community outreach and engagement to reduce pollution, and environmental and sustainability projects that assist or benefit underserved communities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Publicly Accessible Art in Private Development Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that requires most private development projects in Rockville to include an expenditure for publicly accessible art based on an annually adjusted fee schedule. Developers can comply through various options including commissioning art, contributing to a public art fund, providing arts spaces or arts-based infrastructure, or making monetary donations to eligible arts organizations.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This is a requirement for private developers rather than a financial assistance program. Developers must allocate funds for publicly accessible art as part of their development projects based on an annually adjusted fee schedule (effective February 2025-June 30, 2026): Single-family/townhouse: $680.84 per unit (first 100), $510.57 (second 100), $340.36 (excess); Multi-family: $1021.33 per unit (first 100), $766.02 (second 100), $510.57 (excess); Commercial: $0.58/sq ft (first 100,000), $0.45 (second 100,000), $0.26 (excess); Industrial: $0.12/sq ft. Required contributions can be applied to: installing or presenting art on site, contributing to the Art in Public Places Program or City-Managed Arts Program, providing arts spaces or arts-based infrastructure, or making monetary donations to eligible arts organizations. Developers may combine multiple options.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private developers undertaking development projects in Rockville that meet or exceed project size thresholds
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Publicly accessible art projects, contributions to public art funds, arts spaces, arts-based infrastructure, or monetary donations to eligible arts organizations. Allowable costs include artist fees, consultant fees (up to 10% maximum), freight, shipping, fabrication, installation, purchase of arts-based infrastructure, and construction costs associated with arts spaces.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rockville city limits
requirements_list: Most private development projects must include art expenditure based on the AIPD Ordinance
Amount calculated based on annually adjusted fee schedule reflecting Builder's Cost Index
Projects subject to determination by Arts and Culture Program Manager during Development Review
Some projects are exempt from the ordinance
Required contribution must be met through one or more compliance options
Single-family/townhouse, multi-family, commercial, or industrial projects of qualifying size
For installed art on site: must be permanent in nature lasting at least 30 years with regular maintenance
For installed art on site: artist contract must comply with Visual Artists Rights Act of 1990
For arts space provision: must meet identified community need and demonstrate sustainability beyond 10 years
For monetary donations to eligible arts organizations: recipient must have met five specific criteria for at least 24 consecutive months
Publicly accessible art must be installed and maintained in perpetuity
Art may not be removed within 5 years of installation without replacement or contribution payment per specified schedule
Agreement and bond required for installation, presentation of art, arts space not included in site plan, or arts-based infrastructure
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: After receiving Development Review Committee Comment Letter indicating AIPD Ordinance applies, applicant meets with Arts and Culture Program staff to discuss requirements and options, review AIPD Guidelines and ordinance, and learn about contribution uses and staff support. Step 2: Applicant determines which option(s) to select and submits AIPD Application. Step 3: For monetary contributions to Art in Public Places or City-Managed Arts Program, submit AIPD Contribution Form and check before permit issuance. For installed art on site: submit concept plan, cost itemization, artist qualifications, and commissioning process with application; meet with Arts and Culture staff before permit issuance to present artist concept and budget for approval; enter contract with artist per Visual Artists Rights Act; present final concept for staff approval; install art and pass inspection before Certificate of Occupancy. For presented art on site: submit concept plan with timeline, duration, location, and selection process; submit cost itemization to staff before permit issuance. For arts space provision: include space in site/project plan or detailed plan with application; submit valuation demonstrating required contribution met, cost itemization, and business plan demonstrating sustainability; submit executed agreement with arts organization before permit issuance. For arts-based infrastructure: submit detailed description with cost itemization and need documentation; submit executed agreement with receiving organization before permit issuance; confirm delivery, installation, and operational status before Certificate of Occupancy. For monetary donations to eligible arts organizations: provide written confirmation from developer and recipient before permit issuance. Contact Arts and Culture Program Manager for assistance throughout process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A rebate program that helps Rockville residents and eligible organizations reduce stormwater runoff and pollution by installing small-scale sustainable drainage projects such as rain gardens, conservation landscaping, permeable pavements, rain barrels, cisterns, trees, and green roofs. The program provides up to $5,000 in lifetime rebates per eligible property for installing native plantings, rain gardens, rain barrels, cisterns, trees, permeable pavers, green roofs, or removing impervious pavement, helping improve water quality and providing cooling and wildlife habitat benefits.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates for approved stormwater management projects with a lifetime maximum of $5,000 per eligible property. Rebate rates: Conservation landscaping: $5–$6 per square foot. Rain gardens: $10 per square foot. Pavement removal: $3–$6 per square foot. Rain barrels and cisterns: $1 per gallon. Trees: $150 per tree. Permeable paver retrofit: $14 per square foot. Green roofs: $9 per square foot. Applicants can implement best management practices (BMPs) such as gutters and downspouts, rainwater collection systems, rain gardens, swales, pervious hardscapes, ground covers, cross drains, retaining walls, and terracing to manage stormwater runoff on their properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single-family and townhome residents, homeowners associations, condominium associations, religious institutions, private schools, and other nonprofits located in the City of Rockville. The program provides educational support including free workshops, on-site stormwater runoff evaluations, and cost-share assistance for implementing stormwater Best Management Practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of stormwater management and sustainable drainage projects including conservation landscaping, rain gardens, pavement removal, rain barrels, cisterns, native trees, permeable paver retrofits, and green roofs to improve water quality and provide cooling and wildlife habitat benefits. Eligible practices include gutters and downspouts for roof runoff management, rainwater collection systems, outlet protection, swales, pervious hardscapes (permeable pavers, turf block, paver stones), ground covers (mulch, gravel, wood chips), cross drains, retaining walls, and terracing to slow, spread, and sink stormwater runoff.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available to eligible properties within the City of Rockville, Maryland only. Properties should be located in one of the City's watersheds including Rock Creek Watershed (Twinbrook area), Watts Branch Watershed (King Farm or West End areas), or other designated Rockville watersheds.
requirements_list: Property must be located in the City of Rockville
Must be a single-family residence, townhome, homeowners association, condominium association, religious institution, private school, or other nonprofit
Applicants must own eligible property types: detached homes, townhomes, HOA properties, condominium associations, or nonprofits
Projects must meet program specifications for eligible project types

Prior to implementation of any practices, applicants should seek technical assistance from a licensed professional engineer, landscape architect, or certified professionals in erosion and sediment control
Site-specific designs that address individual site needs and constraints are essential
Some techniques may require permits or permission, particularly when working in the right-of-way or on a City easement; applicants must check with the City to determine if a permit is necessary
Call Miss Utility at 811 or 1-800-257-7777 at least two working days before any digging projects to mark publicly maintained utilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website or contact the City of Rockville Environmental Management Division. The trust will review and process applications, perform site visits, and provide support for questions. Applicants should conduct a do-it-yourself stormwater runoff evaluation of their property by sketching the property, noting the five major zones (roofs, elevated structures, walkways and patios, driveways and parking areas, and bare soils/landscapes), walking the property during a rainy day to observe where runoff flows, and identifying potential locations for implementing best management practices. Applicants are encouraged to contact City staff or visit www.rockvillemd.gov/environment or www.rockvillemd.gov/rainscapes for assistance, educational workshops, and on-site evaluations before submitting applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville offers emergency financial assistance to eligible residents in need of temporary relief for evictions, utility shut-offs, prescription medications, medical and dental expenses, food, and other basic needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct emergency financial assistance for eligible residents experiencing financial hardship. Assistance covers rent (for residents with eviction notices), utility bills (for residents with shut-off notices), prescription medications, medical and dental expenses, food, and other basic needs. The program also provides referrals for emergency food, clothing, financial counseling, and employment counseling. For residents over 60, assistance with prescription costs under $200 is available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current residents of the City of Rockville who are experiencing financial hardship due to loss of employment, ongoing financial difficulty, loss of family wage earner, unexpected medical bills, or other financial emergencies. The program also assists furloughed federal employees experiencing financial crisis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency financial assistance for evictions, utility shut-offs, prescription medications, medical and dental expenses, food, and other basic needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Current residents of the City of Rockville for a minimum of six months. Use the address finder at rockvillemd.gov/services to determine if you live within Rockville city limits.
requirements_list: Applicants must be current residents of the City of Rockville for a minimum of six months.

Applicants seeking rent assistance must have a current eviction notice from the court, such as a Summons to Appear for Failure to Pay Rent, a Writ or Warrant of Restitution, or a red-and-white Final Eviction Notice from the Montgomery County Sheriff's Office.
Applicants seeking utility assistance must have a current utility shut-off notice, or the service must already have been disconnected.
Applicants must demonstrate financial need due to loss of employment, ongoing financial difficulty, loss of family wage earner, unexpected medical bills, or other financial emergencies.
Applicants must first apply for emergency assistance through the Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents must first apply for emergency assistance through the Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS). Montgomery County DHHS will then submit a referral to the City of Rockville on behalf of eligible city residents. If you have received a referral from Montgomery County DHHS, schedule an appointment with the City of Rockville Housing and Community Development Department by calling 240-314-8300. Note: if you have a third-party utility provider, you will still need a referral from Montgomery County DHHS before scheduling an appointment with the City of Rockville.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rockville Safe Waters: Swim Scholarship Program for Youth with Autism
structured_extraction.program_description: A targeted scholarship program providing financial support for inclusive swim lessons for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder at the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center. The initiative aims to create a safe and supportive swim instruction environment while fostering water safety, physical development, and family engagement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarships will be awarded to up to 10 eligible children to cover swim lesson costs at the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center. Each scholarship covers one child for one class season of inclusive swim lessons. Exact subsidy amounts are not specified in the program materials.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis until 10 scholarships are awarded
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children ages 3-10 with confirmed Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis who are Rockville residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Inclusive swim lessons at Rockville Swim and Fitness Center
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to City of Rockville residents.
requirements_list: Child must be aged 3-10 with a confirmed Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis
Must be a resident of the City of Rockville
Commitment to attend in-person swim lessons at Rockville Swim and Fitness Center
Youth must be ready to engage in group swim lessons
Adult must be present at facility or on deck during lessons
Must provide proof of residency (one of: current City of Rockville water and sewage bill, property tax bill, or state-issued identification with City of Rockville address)

Must meet financial requirements (proof of enrollment in one of: Temporary Cash Assistance, Food Stamps, Transitional Emergency Medical and Housing Assistance, Working Parents Assistance Program, Montgomery County medical assistance, public housing, HUD Section 8 housing, shelter residence, Supplemental Security Income, MCPS Free and Reduced Meals Program, Care for Kids, Maryland Energy Assistance Program, Montgomery County HHS Rental Assistance Program, Maryland unemployment benefits, or Women Infants and Children program)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the completed scholarship application form by email to programaccess@rockvillemd.gov. The application should include information about the applicant, family details, child's comfort with water and group settings, description of disability/needs, and the desired course number. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until the 10 scholarships are awarded. Selection is performed by the Rockville Safe Waters Committee.

Must provide proof of income documentation (W-2 form, Social Security benefit letters, VA pension, Medicaid, Food stamps, SSI, pay stubs, interest statements, family support letters, income tax forms, or other income verification)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Senior Assistance Fund application form with personal information, address, telephone number, and date of birth. structured_extraction.program_description: The Single-Family Rehabilitation Program assists eligible Rockville homeowners with making necessary improvements to their homes to correct code deficiencies and housing problems. The program provides no-interest, forgivable loans to low-to-moderate income homeowners. A lien is placed on the property and forgiven over a five-year period at a rate of 20% per year. The program covers work such as roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, and kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation. For homes built before 1978, lead testing and remediation of deteriorated lead-based paint is also covered.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides no-interest, forgivable loans to eligible low-to-moderate income homeowners for necessary home repairs and rehabilitation work. A lien is placed on the property, which is forgiven over a five-year period at a rate of 20% per year. If the home is sold, rented, or ownership is otherwise transferred during the five-year period, the recipient is required to pay back the remaining percentage of the lien. The maximum expenditure per household is $25,000. Work is assessed and prioritized by a Rehabilitation Specialist based on the severity of code deficiencies and repair needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-to-moderate income City of Rockville homeowners who own their primary residence and meet HUD maximum gross income requirements based on family size
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds must be used to correct code deficiencies and address serious housing problems including roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation, and lead-based paint remediation for homes built before 1978. Program is intended to correct code deficiencies, not make property improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: This program is available to homeowners in the City of Rockville, Maryland. Applicants must live within the City Limits of Rockville and currently reside at the property.
requirements_list: Must live within the City Limits of the City of Rockville
The home must be owner-occupied and be the owner's sole and principal residence
The owner must currently reside at the property
The owner must not owe more than the home's assessed value (not underwater)
Total assets must not exceed $150,000 excluding the value of the home being applied for
Property taxes and personal taxes must be current
Ownership must be verified through property tax records and the deed

Gross household income must not exceed HUD maximum limits based on family size: 1 person $68,500; 2 persons $78,250; 3 persons $88,050; 4 persons $97,800; 5 persons $105,650; 6 persons $113,450; 7 persons $121,300; 8 persons $129,100 (effective May 2024)
Properties with reverse mortgages are reviewed on a case-by-case basis

Applicants must provide copies of most recent Federal and State of Maryland tax returns, all income statements, current homeowner's insurance declaration page, most recent mortgage or home equity loan statement, and most recent checking and savings bank statements for last 2 months
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process has three steps. First, complete and mail the Eligibility Assessment Application to the Housing and Community Development Department at 111 Maryland Avenue, First Floor, Rockville, MD 20850. Second, once your assessment is accepted, you will be notified by the Rehabilitation Specialist to complete the eligibility review by submitting required documents including copies of recent Federal and State tax returns, all income statements (W-2s, 1099s, Social Security or pension benefit statements, retirement savings or investment accounts), current homeowner's insurance declaration page with property address and coverage dates, most recent mortgage or home equity loan statement showing balance and current payments, and checking and savings account bank statements from the last 2 months. Third, application materials are reviewed and work is prioritized by the Rehabilitation Specialist based on severity of repair need. The review process typically takes seven to ten business days.

structured_extraction.program_name: A&E District Income Tax Subtraction Modification
structured_extraction.program_description: A state and local income tax exemption for qualifying resident artists on income derived from artistic work created and sold within the Arts & Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying resident artists do not pay state or local income tax on income derived from artistic work created and sold within the A&E District. Artists subtract qualifying income on their tax form before state and local taxes are calculated (federal taxes still apply). One-member Limited Liability Companies may be treated as individuals and may be eligible for this modification.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualifying resident artists who create and sell artistic work within the A&E District.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The exemption applies to income derived from the sale of artistic work created by the qualifying resident artist.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicable only to qualifying resident artists operating within the designated Arts & Entertainment District in Salisbury, Wicomico County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a qualifying resident artist
Artistic work must be created and sold within the A&E District
Income must be derived from the sale of artistic work
The artist must reside in the A&E District
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Comptroller of the Treasury office or the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation for current information and tax forms. Complete the appropriate income tax form and claim the subtraction modification when filing state and local income taxes.

structured_extraction.program_name: A&E District Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for the renovation of existing buildings or the construction of new buildings that are capable for use by qualifying resident artists in the Arts & Entertainment District.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Salisbury and Wicomico County offer a property tax credit for a period of 6 years from approval of the resolution. The local jurisdiction may apply any percentage credit up to 100%. The credit applies to the increased assessed value of real property that has been renovated or newly constructed for use by qualifying resident artists or arts and entertainment enterprises within the A&E District. The specific credit percentage is determined by local legislation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualifying resident artists and arts & entertainment enterprises located in the A&E District seeking to renovate or construct buildings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit applies to real property renovations or new construction capable of use by qualifying resident artists or arts and entertainment enterprises.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicable only within the designated Arts & Entertainment District in Salisbury, Wicomico County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be located within the A&E District
For renovations: a building permit must be obtained
The establishment must meet the definition of an 'arts and entertainment enterprise' (a for-profit or nonprofit entity dedicated to visual or performing arts) or qualifying resident artist use
The credit is for real property only, not personal property
The Department of Assessments and Taxation must approve the project and determine increased value
Credit term is 6 years from resolution approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation or the local office to discuss your project. Obtain a building permit for renovations. The Department of Assessments and Taxation will review plans and determine the increased value of the renovated or newly constructed space and the applicable tax credit.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of acrylic barriers and floor distancing stickers to create safer, more protected business environments in compliance with COVID-19 safety measures.
