structured_extraction.program_name: COVID-19 Emergency Relief Business Microgrant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time emergency relief grant program providing $2,300 to small businesses in the City of Salisbury that were impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and related State Executive Orders mandating business shutdowns. Funds were sourced from Delmarva Power donations and the City's Revolving Loan Fund. The program aimed to help businesses recover and continue operations during the post-COVID period, with a lottery-based award system prioritizing businesses within the Revolving Loan Boundary area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant award of $2,300 with no repayment required. All eligible applications are entered into a lottery system, with Tier 1 applicants (mandated full closure) receiving first priority and Tier 2 applicants (mandated partial closure) considered if funds remain. Awardees are selected at random and receive grant checks by mail. Awardees must complete a disbursement form and produce receipts within 60 days of City approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses registered with the State of Maryland and the City of Salisbury that were impacted by COVID-19 and related State Executive Orders, with no more than 25 full-time employees as of March 5, 2020, and having a physical establishment within the City of Salisbury.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid sick leave for employees unable to work due to coronavirus; maintaining payroll and retaining employees during business disruptions; obtaining materials due to interrupted supply chains; making rent or mortgage payments; repaying obligations from revenue losses; and purchasing personal protective equipment or implementing safety measures to reduce COVID-19 spread.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must have a physical establishment in the City of Salisbury. Businesses within the Revolving Loan Boundary map receive priority for all available funds. Businesses outside the Revolving Loan area are eligible for lottery consideration using funds donated by Delmarva Power.
requirements_list: Must be a registered business entity in good standing with the State of Maryland and City of Salisbury
Must have a physical establishment in the City of Salisbury, within or outside the Revolving Loan Boundary map
Must have no more than 25 full-time employees as of March 5, 2020
Must be engaged in activities regulated or impacted by COVID-19 Maryland State of Emergency with required license or permit
Must have no pre-existing tax liens or legal judgments prior to March 5, 2020
Business must have been impacted by COVID-19 mandated shutdowns

Not eligible if home-based business, church, medical service provider, non-profit, bank or financial institution, investment real-estate entity, food truck, national franchise, government agency, or contractor/construction/service repair business
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants apply online or by email. Applications are reviewed by the Director of Business Development, a Finance Department officer, and the Deputy City Administrator for completeness and to verify tangible and immediate need. Approved applicants are classified as Tier 1 (mandated full closure) or Tier 2 (mandated partial closure). Tier 1 applicants receive first priority and are entered into a lottery system. If funds remain, Tier 2 applicants are entered into a lottery. Awardees are selected at random and receive grant checks by mail. Awardees must complete a disbursement form and produce receipts within 60 days of City approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program offered by the City of Salisbury to assist businesses within the Main Street District recover from the negative impacts of COVID-19. Each eligible business can receive up to $20,000 as a one-time grant with no repayment required.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant awards of up to $20,000 per business entity with no repayment required. Funds can be used for employee paid sick leave, payroll maintenance, rent or mortgage payments (past due or future), repaying past or future obligations, purchasing personal protective equipment, building improvements to reduce COVID-19 spread, business equipment to expand services in response to COVID-19, or other COVID-19 related recovery uses as justified by the applicant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered business entities in good standing with the State of Maryland and City of Salisbury that have a physical establishment within the designated Main Street area of the City of Salisbury.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for employee paid sick leave due to COVID-19, maintaining payroll and retaining employees during business disruptions, obtaining materials from alternate sources due to supply chain interruptions, making past due or future rent or mortgage payments, repaying past due or future obligations, purchasing personal protective equipment, building improvements to reduce COVID-19 spread, business equipment to help expand services in response to COVID-19, or other COVID-19 related recovery purposes as justified by the applicant.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must have a physical establishment located within the designated Main Street area of the City of Salisbury. Employees funded through this grant must spend over 50% of their time doing work in the Main Street area.
requirements_list: Must be a registered business entity in good standing with the State of Maryland and City of Salisbury
Must have a physical establishment in the City of Salisbury within the designated Main Street area
Must have no pre-existing tax liens or legal judgements prior to March 5
Limited to one award per business entity
Home-based businesses are not eligible
Churches are not eligible
Banks and financial institutions are not eligible
Investment real-estate entities are not eligible unless applying for payments for a business located in the Main Street area or COVID-related investments on a Main Street property
Food trucks are not eligible
Government agencies are not eligible
Contractors, construction, or service repair-based businesses are not eligible unless applying for COVID-related investments on a Main Street property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application during the open period. Applications will be graded by a committee on the degree the business has been negatively impacted by COVID-19, how the funds would help the business recover, and the degree to which the business contributes to the vitality of the Main Street area. Applicants will be notified of grant awards by March 5. Funded businesses must submit proof of receipts and use of funds narrative by the end of April.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay Trust Outreach and Restoration Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that funds local nonprofits seeking to implement environmental projects including tree plantings, trash cleanups, rain gardens, and educational programs. Projects must engage communities in environmental issues or accomplish on-the-ground restoration that improves Maryland's natural resources through water quality improvement or habitat enhancement. The program also funds training individuals in environmental stewardship, creating action plans for community organizations, and removing impervious surfaces to reduce stormwater runoff and pollution related to the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $75,000 in total grant funding is available for local nonprofits in Salisbury/Wicomico County. Statewide, the program has awarded 45 grants totaling over $1.3 million, matched by $2.2 million in partner funding for a total impact of $3.5 million. Specific individual grant amounts vary by project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local nonprofits working on environmental outreach, education, and restoration projects related to water quality, natural resource restoration, and the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree plantings, trash cleanups, rain gardens, educational programs, training individuals in environmental stewardship, creating action plans for community organizations, removing impervious surfaces and replacing them with permeable pavement and native plants, and other water quality improvement or habitat enhancement projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide in Maryland through municipalities participating as partners with the Chesapeake Bay Trust. The City of Salisbury (Wicomico County) is a program partner. Projects should result in improvements to the health of Maryland natural resources.
requirements_list: Organization must be a local nonprofit

Projects must engage members of a specific audience in community and environmental issues through knowledge building or behavior change efforts at multiple stages of the project, OR accomplish on-the-ground restoration that improves the health of a Maryland natural resource through water quality improvement or habitat enhancement
Projects must meet specific goals for each project type as specified in the Outreach and Restoration packet
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the City of Salisbury Sustainability Specialist or visit the Chesapeake Bay Trust website for application instructions and the Outreach and Restoration packet detailing project type requirements. Organizations submit project proposals, which are reviewed by the Chesapeake Bay Trust's Technical Review Committee and awarded based on environmental impact and alignment with program goals.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Conversion from Rental to Homeowner-Occupied Dwelling Tax Abatement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax abatement and incentive program offered by the City of Salisbury that encourages the purchase of rental properties and their conversion to owner-occupied family dwellings within Salisbury city limits. Participating property owners receive full abatement of city property taxes for the first five years, followed by a gradual phase-in of taxes over four years at 20, 40, 60, and 80 percent per year in years six through nine, until the tenth year when full property taxes become due. The program aims to increase homeownership and reduce rental housing density in Salisbury.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: City property taxes are fully abated (exempt) for the first five years of program participation. In year six, the property is taxed at 20 percent of the prevailing residential tax rate. In year seven, it is taxed at 40 percent. In year eight, it is taxed at 60 percent. In year nine, it is taxed at 80 percent. Beginning in year ten and thereafter, the property is taxed at the full prevailing residential tax rate. The abatement period is nine years total. If a property's participation is terminated before the nine-year period ends, all previously abated taxes become due.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1 annually (for annual certification of qualification)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Director of Internal Services, City of Salisbury
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who own rental properties and want to convert them to owner-occupied family residences within Salisbury city limits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The abatement applies to city property taxes on residential properties being converted from rental use to owner-occupied family residences. The program provides tax savings to incentivize conversion of rental properties to primary owner-occupied dwellings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The property must be located within Salisbury city limits (Wicomico County, Maryland).
requirements_list: Property must be a single-family detached dwelling
Property must be located within City of Salisbury limits

Property must have been used exclusively as a rental property for at least three years immediately prior to purchase by the applicant, or was purchased from a person or entity that rehabilitated the property after rental use for three consecutive years
Applicant must purchase the property with intent to convert it to owner-occupied family residence
Applicant must intend to occupy the home as an owner-occupied family residence within one year of purchase
Property must be occupied as the principal residence of the homeowner
Property must be actually occupied or expected to be actually occupied by the homeowner for more than six months of a twelve-month period beginning with the date of finality for the taxable year

Applicant must agree to continue using the property as an owner-occupied family residence for the entire nine years of participation in the program, or sell it only to a person who will use it as an owner-occupied family residence until expiration of the property's participation, or pay the city for all taxes abated during the period of ownership
Applicant must file a certificate of qualification by April 1 of each year to remain eligible for the tax abatement program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must apply at the City Finance Office located at 125 N Division Street, Room 103, Salisbury, MD 21801. The director of internal services distributes and receives all required forms for application to the program, agreement to participate, and annual certification of qualification. Each applicant must file a certificate of qualification by April 1 of each year with the director of internal services to remain eligible. Applicants should review the Participation Form and FAQ documents available on the program page for application procedures and eligibility requirements. Contact the Finance Office at 410-548-3110 or the Housing and Community Development department for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Owner-Occupied Housing Repair Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Salisbury partners with Habitat for Humanity of Wicomico County and Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services to provide grants for critical repairs to owner-occupied homes within Salisbury city limits. The program uses Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funding to help low-income homeowners make repairs that bring their homes into compliance with city codes.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to a maximum of $20,000 per property (unless extenuating circumstances apply) to cover costs of repairs to bring owner-occupied homes into compliance with city codes. Repairs include fixing mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems; building components; energy conservation improvements; lead paint hazard reduction; and accessibility upgrades. A 5-year lien document must be signed and recorded. Applicants must meet income limits based on household size, ranging from $52,500 for a household of one to $98,950 for a household of eight.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income homeowners who own single-family homes within the City of Salisbury corporate limits and meet income and property eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repair or replacement of defective mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems; repair or replacement of building components and surfaces such as foundations, roofs, porches, stairways, floors, ceilings, walls, doors, windows, siding, and trim; energy conservation activities including insulation, caulking, weather-stripping, doors, and windows; lead paint hazard reduction; accessibility improvements for disabled persons; and incipient repairs and general property improvements of a non-luxury nature.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within the City of Salisbury corporate limits.
requirements_list: Total gross household income before taxes must be below 80% of Area Median Income
Applicant must own the property in fee simple, as joint tenants, or tenants by the entireties (not tenants in common)
At least one owner must reside in the property
Applicant must have legal capacity to incur obligations
All mortgage payments must be current for the previous three months
Applicant must be free of any tax lien or judgment
Bankruptcies must have been discharged for a minimum of two years
If combined with a loan, collections must be placed on a payment plan and other negative credit must be addressed
Maximum grant of $20,000 per property unless extenuating circumstances exist
After receiving grant, applicant is ineligible again until the 5-year lien term expires
All property taxes and city-issued invoices must be current
Applicant must have clear title to the property
All existing mortgages must be current for the previous three months
Property must be free of all judgments including IRS liens
Property must be insured for the entire loan term; properties in the 100-year floodplain must have flood insurance
Owner-occupants must not own any other house and must not have substantial assets enabling them to secure rehabilitation funds elsewhere
A 5-year Notice of Lien document must be signed and recorded in Land Records
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should contact either Habitat for Humanity of Wicomico County (410-546-1551) or Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services (410-543-4626) for further information and to apply. The non-profit subrecipient agencies will administer the application and award process and perform the repairs. Basic qualification is not a guarantee that the project will be funded.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Summer Youth Employment Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A paid 6-to-8-week summer employment program for youth and high school students in the Salisbury area that provides work experience, job skills training, and community service learning opportunities. Participants work in various City of Salisbury departments and community settings including city parks, community centers, and community gardens. The program includes structured learning and mentoring through collaboration with Junior Achievement volunteers to develop workforce readiness and career-specific skills. Participants meet regularly to complete service learning projects, discuss current events, develop resumes, improve soft skills, and access business resources in the community. Upon completion, participants receive a stipend and/or educational award.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid 8-week summer employment program where students work up to 28 hours per week for 8 weeks. Participants receive wages, on-the-job training, mentoring, resume writing assistance, and soft skills development through Junior Achievement collaboration. Upon completion, participants also receive a stipend and an educational award. The 2026 program ran from June 22, 2026 to August 14, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for Summer 2026 are now closed. Applications for Summer 2027 will open in January.

Residency in the City of Salisbury is preferred but not required. Typically 10-12 participants are selected.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid employment in City of Salisbury departments with on-the-job training, service learning projects, community improvement activities at city parks, community centers, and community gardens, resume development, and career readiness skill-building.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Salisbury, Maryland. Students must be enrolled in the Wicomico County school district. Residency in the City of Salisbury is preferred but not required.

Must be currently enrolled in Wicomico County school district

Must provide 2 forms of updated identification (birth certificate, social security card, current student ID or state-issued ID)
Must have consistent reliable transportation to and from work
Must be able to work up to 28 hours per week for the 8-week program period
Youth must be eligible applicants
Applicants from the spring application period will be considered, along with new applicants

Applications can be submitted via the online application portal. Ten to twelve applicants are selected to participate. Applications for Summer 2027 will open in January. For prior cycles, applications were available at https://bit.ly/2NMozjg.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) – Entitlement Communities
structured_extraction.program_description: The CDBG Program provides annual formula-based grants to entitled metropolitan cities and urban counties to implement community and economic development activities directed toward neighborhood revitalization, economic development, and improved community facilities and services. The program aims to develop viable urban communities by providing decent housing and a suitable living environment, and by expanding economic opportunities, principally for persons of low and moderate income. Activities must meet one of three national objectives: benefit persons of low and moderate income; aid in prevention or elimination of slums and blight; or meet other urgent community development needs. The City of Salisbury administers CDBG funds locally, conducting annual competitive funding rounds for eligible subrecipients including nonprofits and government entities. Recent award examples include $387,418 in 2020 funds allocated to sidewalk construction, community center renovation, and workforce development positions, and $399,903 in program year 2021 funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual formula-based grants to entitled metropolitan cities and urban counties for community and economic development activities. For Program Year 2021 (7/1/2021–6/30/2022), the City of Salisbury received $399,903 in CDBG funds: $70,000 in administrative funds and $329,903 in program/project funds. The maximum amount for public service projects is $59,985. No more than 20% of the grant may be spent on planning and administrative costs, and no more than 15% on public service activities. The maximum amount any applicant may seek in any competitive funding round is $150,000. Funds are awarded on a reimbursement basis only — applicants must expend funds first and then submit documentation for reimbursement. In 2020, Salisbury received $387,418, allocated to approximately $170,000 for sidewalk construction and improvement in low-to-moderate income neighborhoods, $125,000 to renovate the Truitt Community Center, and $25,000 to fund a Community Kitchen Program Manager position.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by program year; most recent competitive round deadline was Monday, January 11, 2021 by 4:30 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entitled metropolitan cities and urban counties; eligible non-profit organizations and community groups that are registered 501(c)(3) nonprofits; government agencies; Community Based Development Organizations (CBDOs); and municipal governments and local jurisdictions working to address urban blight, improve walkability and pedestrian safety, and create economic opportunity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible activities include: acquisition and clearance of real property; public improvements and facilities such as senior centers, recreation centers, and day care centers; public services including child care, health care, job training and education programs, recreation programs, drug abuse counseling and treatment, and services for the homeless; relocation payments and assistance; rehabilitation of residential, commercial, industrial, and nonprofit-owned nonresidential buildings; historic preservation; lead-based paint hazard evaluation and reduction; code enforcement; assistance to micro-enterprises; homeownership assistance; urban renewal completion; technical assistance to increase capacity of public and private nonprofit organizations; assistance to institutions of higher education; sidewalk construction and improvement in low-to-moderate income neighborhoods; renovation and improvement of community facilities; creation of workforce development positions; and program administration costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Salisbury, Maryland and the surrounding entitled metropolitan area. Salisbury is a participating entitlement jurisdiction under the federal CDBG program administered by HUD.
requirements_list: Eligible non-profit community groups or organizations must be registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations and must provide supporting documentation confirming this status

Activities must meet one of three national objectives: benefit persons of low and moderate income; aid in prevention or elimination of slums and blight; or meet other community development needs of particular urgency
Each activity must be eligible under CDBG guidelines
Any capital project proposed on property not held by the subrecipient must include written approval by the property owner
Subrecipients requesting funds for community services must be either developing a new public service or proposing a quantifiable increase in service for an existing program
Applicants must have sufficient operating funds available to expend on project expenses before reimbursement
Maximum amount any applicant may seek in any competitive funding round is $150,000
Applications must be received (not postmarked) by the deadline
Applications must be submitted to the Housing & Community Development Department
Grantees must determine activities to fund based on community needs and priorities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are made available at the start of each annual funding round (typically November) via email or in person at the Housing & Community Development Department office at 207 W. Main Street, Suite 102, Salisbury, MD 21801. Contact Deborah Stam to receive an application. Completed applications must be submitted (not postmarked) by the stated deadline to: City of Salisbury – Housing & Community Development Department, 207 W. Main Street, Suite 102, Salisbury, Maryland 21801. Eligible non-profit community groups or organizations may apply for either a public service or capital grant as subrecipients. Recipients develop an Action Plan describing how funds will be allocated to address community needs; the plan undergoes public review and input before adoption by local government. Funds are awarded on a reimbursement basis only — applicants expend funds first and then submit copies of paid invoices, cancelled checks, and other requested documentation for reimbursement. Activities are initiated and developed at the local level based on community perception of local needs and priorities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps property owners in Downtown Salisbury connect to Maryland Broadband's high-speed fiber network that runs along Main Street. The program covers the construction costs of bringing fiber into private properties and ending at the termination point where the modem will be located.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available in amounts not to exceed $2,500 and will be made on a reimbursement basis only. Grants will be made on a first come, first served basis until funds run out for the fiscal year. This program is contingent upon the availability of appropriated funds. Eligible costs are limited to construction costs of bringing fiber to the termination point for the modem. Construction costs cannot be passed along to those who will ultimately use the service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and tenants in Downtown Salisbury who want to connect to high-speed fiber internet service.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction costs of bringing fiber into the private property and ending at the termination point where the modem will be located. Costs cannot be passed along to those who will ultimately use the service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within Downtown Salisbury, using existing conduits that have been abutted to buildings as part of the Main Street project. The eligible area is shown on the Historic District map provided by the City of Salisbury.
requirements_list: Property must be located within Downtown Salisbury using existing conduits from the Main Street project
Eligible costs are limited to construction cost of bringing fiber to the termination point for the modem
Application must be made by the legal property owner or by the tenant with written approval from the property owner
Applicant must use a licensed contractor to perform work
Applicant must have approval of the Historic District if necessary
The City will not approve digging up sidewalks or work that would alter improvements from the Main Street Construction project completed in November 2020
Grant amount must not exceed $2,500
Construction costs cannot be passed along to those who will ultimately use the service
Grants are made on a first come, first served basis until funds run out for the fiscal year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application form with your property information, project details, and photographs of the building facade showing where you plan to tap into the fiber and how it will run into the property. If you have already completed the project, submit copies of all receipts and paid invoices. If you are a tenant, include a letter from the property owner approving the work. Use a licensed contractor for the work and obtain Historic District approval if necessary. The City will reimburse eligible costs up to $2,500 on a first come, first served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax exemption program for businesses that own and operate machinery and equipment used in manufacturing or research and development activities in Salisbury. Eligible businesses must either locate, expand operations, or develop new products or industrial processes in the city. The exemption applies to personal property taxes on qualifying equipment and can be granted for a term up to five years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Personal property tax exemption on machinery, equipment, and tools used in manufacturing or research and development operations. Exemptions are granted for a specific year in which equipment was purchased and can extend up to five years. The exemption term must be approved by the City of Salisbury Council. To receive the maximum five-year term, applications must be received within two years from December 31st of the calendar year the equipment was purchased. Once granted, a copy of the personal property tax return must be submitted for each year of the exemption.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within two (2) years from December 31st of the calendar year in which equipment was purchased
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sandra Green, Director of Finance; Phillip Menzel, Assistant Director Finance - Accounting
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses engaged in manufacturing or research and development that locate, expand operations, or develop new products or processes in Salisbury.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The exemption reduces personal property tax liability on machinery, equipment, and tools used in manufacturing or research and development activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The manufacturing or research and development operation must be located in Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Facility must either locate, expand operations, or develop a new product or industrial process in Salisbury
Equipment must be used for manufacturing or research and development purposes
Application must include a detailed explanation of how the business meets location, expansion, or product development requirements
Must provide information on raw materials used and products produced or research and development activity conducted
Must specify number of employees used in manufacturing or research and development and number of administrative employees
Must attach a schedule describing each asset claimed, including description, original cost, and acquisition date
Must attach a copy of the State of Maryland Personal Property Return for the year of acquisition
To receive maximum five-year exemption term, application must be received within two years from December 31st of the calendar year equipment was purchased
A separate application must be made for each year
Once granted, a copy of the personal property tax return must be submitted for each year of the exemption
Approval required from City of Salisbury Council
County exemption does not automatically grant city exemption
General asset descriptions such as Equipment, Various, or Miscellaneous are not acceptable; detailed descriptions required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an exemption application form with required documentation to the Finance Department at 125 North Division Street, Salisbury, Maryland 21801-4940. The application must include: business name, Maryland Department ID, mailing address, phone number, contact name, the equipment year being claimed, the manufacturing or research and development operation address, the date operations began in Salisbury, detailed information about how the business meets location, expansion, or product development requirements including raw materials used and products produced or R&D activity conducted, number of employees in Manufacturing/R&D and number of administrative employees, an equipment schedule with detailed descriptions (not general terms), original costs, and dates of acquisition for each item, and a copy of the State of Maryland Personal Property Return for the year of acquisition. Mail the completed application to the Finance Department. The application will be reviewed and forwarded to the City of Salisbury Council for approval. A separate application must be submitted for each year. Once an exemption is granted, a copy of the personal property tax return must be submitted for each year of the exemption.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit applied to City of Salisbury real property tax for residential properties owned by public safety officers including full-time firefighters, EMTs, paramedics, police officers, volunteer firefighters meeting service requirements, individuals with service-related disabilities, retirees in good standing, and lifetime volunteer members.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The tax credit may be granted in an amount up to $2,500, but may not exceed the amount of the real property tax imposed on the dwelling. The tax credit is available for a period of one taxable year and must be renewed annually. Applicants must re-apply each year to receive the tax credit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is sought. Applications filed after April 1 are treated as applications for the next succeeding taxable year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time firefighters, EMTs, paramedics, and police officers employed by the City of Salisbury Fire Department or Police Department with at least one year of full-time employment; active volunteer firefighters meeting service requirements; individuals with service-related disabilities; retirees in good standing; and lifetime volunteer members with more than twenty years of active service.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit is applied to the City real property tax for the primary residence of the eligible public safety officer.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The property must be located in the City of Salisbury and must be the primary residence of the applicant.
requirements_list: Applicant must be currently employed as a full-time Firefighter/EMT, Firefighter/Paramedic, or Police Officer for the City of Salisbury with at least one year of full-time employment, OR be an active volunteer firefighter meeting service requirements, OR have a service-related disability, OR be a retiree in good standing, OR be a lifetime volunteer member with more than twenty years of active service
The property must be the primary residence of the applicant
The applicant must own the property to which the credit will be applied
Supporting documentation must be provided such as current paystub, letter of retirement or separation, or letter evidencing volunteer status
The applicant must not have already received a real property tax credit permitted under Title 9 of the Tax-Property Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland
The application must be filed on or before April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is sought

The tax credit terminates if the public safety officer is no longer employed full-time by the public safety agency for a reason other than retirement or service-related disability, or no longer resides in the dwelling for which the tax credit was granted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application form providing property parcel number, fiscal year, applicant name, property owner name, address, phone, and email. Select the applicable public safety officer designation and provide supporting documentation. Answer questions about property ownership, primary residence status, and prior tax credits. Sign the certification acknowledging eligibility requirements and understanding of the program terms. File the application on or before April 1 of the taxable year for which the credit is sought.

requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland resident or organization

structured_extraction.program_description: The Water Incentive Program (WIN) provides financial assistance to eligible households to help pay their water and/or sewer bills issued by the City of Salisbury. Eligible households may receive one payment per year in an amount up to $2,000 toward their water and/or sewer bills (assuming the property has no leaks) and up to $1,000 one-time annual payment (assuming the property has a leak). Applicants must meet monthly gross income thresholds, though households automatically qualify if they receive assistance from programs such as OHEP, TCA, TDAP, SNAP, SSI, ERAP, or Means Tested Veteran Benefits (MTVB). The program is available to both homeowners and tenants who live at the property for which assistance is being requested.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible households receive one payment per year in an amount up to $2,000 toward their water and/or sewer bills (assuming the property has no leaks) or up to $1,000 one-time annual payment (assuming the property has a leak). The amount of assistance is limited to the actual charges on the water and/or sewer bill. Applicants must meet household gross income thresholds based on 60% of the State Median Income. Income limits effective October 1, 2024 are: 1 person: $3,574/month; 2 people: $4,639/month; 3 people: $5,730/month; 4 people: $6,822/month; 5 people: $7,913/month; 6 people: $9,005/month; 7 people: $9,209/month; 8 people: $9,414/month. For each additional household member, add $205/month. Applicants automatically qualify if they receive energy assistance from the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP), Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Supplemental Security Income (SSI), Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP), or Means Tested Veteran Benefits (MTVB).
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Salisbury residents, including both homeowners and tenants, who are responsible for paying water and/or wastewater bills from the City of Salisbury and meet household gross income thresholds. Residents who live at the property for which assistance is being provided are eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment toward water and/or sewer bills issued by the City of Salisbury.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Salisbury residents only. Applicants must live at the property for which assistance is being provided and be responsible for a water and/or wastewater bill issued by the City of Salisbury. Applicants must be Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must live at the property for which assistance is being provided
Must be responsible for payment of a water and/or wastewater bill issued by the City of Salisbury
Household gross income must not exceed specified thresholds based on 60% of State Median Income
Must submit most recent water and/or sewer bill
Provide a copy of a driver's license or government-issued identification card
Provide proof of residence (such as a water and/or wastewater bill)
Provide copies of Social Security cards for all household members

Provide proof of all gross pre-tax income for all household members for the last 30 days (paystubs, Social Security letters, child support letters, unemployment letters, or self-employment documentation)
If household received no income in the 30 days prior to application, sign a Declaration of Zero Income and provide additional information on how household is meeting basic needs
If renting and water bill is in landlord's name, provide copy of most recent rental receipt or lease stating that water is covered in rental fee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply online at salisbury.md/win, in person at the Wicomico County Department of Social Services (201 Baptist Street, Suite 27, Salisbury, MD 21801) or at the City of Salisbury utility billing office (125 N. Division Street, Room 103, Salisbury, MD 21801), or by mail. Complete the WIN application form and provide supporting documentation including: a copy of a driver's license or government-issued identification card, proof of residence (such as a water and/or wastewater bill), copies of Social Security cards for all household members, proof of all gross pre-tax income for all household members for the last 30 days (paystubs, Social Security letters, child support letters, unemployment letters, or self-employment documentation), and the most recent water and/or sewer bill. If your household received no income in the 30 days prior to application, sign a Declaration of Zero Income and provide additional information on how your household is meeting basic needs. The Declaration of Zero Income form is available on the Home Energy Programs website at https://dhs.maryland.gov/office-of-home-energy-programs/. If you rent and the water bill is in your landlord's name, provide a copy of your most recent rental receipt or lease stating that water is covered in your rental fee. Questions can be directed to the City of Salisbury Finance office by phone at 410-548-3115 or by email at finance@salisbury.md.

Individuals must submit an application on or before May 1st of each year, including the MSFA-P.22 form provided by their Dorchester County volunteer fire company.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit of $500 against county real property taxes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Dorchester County
requirements_list: Must be a volunteer firefighter with a bona fide Dorchester County volunteer fire department
Must have maintained active service for three or more years
Must qualify for the State of Maryland Tax Incentive Program
Must own the property to which the credit will be applied
Property must be used as principal residence
Must occupy the property for more than 6 months of a 12-month period
Must submit application on or before May 1st each year
Must include MSFA-P.22 form from volunteer fire company
Credit must be renewed annually by reapplying
Credit is terminated if volunteer status is lost or if applicant no longer resides in or owns the property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the completed Dorchester County Volunteer Fire Department Member - Property Tax Credit Application and the supporting MSFA-P.22 form (Tax Incentive Form) provided by your volunteer fire company to the Dorchester County Finance Department by May 1st each year. structured_extraction.program_description: A policy that allows Dorchester County to waive landfill disposal and tipping fees on the disposal of construction debris for certain projects designed to encourage community development, reduce blight, and increase property values.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County waives tipping fees on the disposal of construction debris for eligible projects. Tipping fees are charged at $65 per ton (as of FY2021). Maximum award per project is determined annually as part of the budget request. No organization can exceed awards of $20,000 per year or $100,000 over the life of the organization, unless special requests to exceed these amounts are approved by Council after Review Committee approval. Applicants submit a Tipping Fee Waiver Request Form estimating the tonnage of construction debris. Upon approval, the awardee receives an award letter used at the Landfill to allow for waived fees. Tonnage is tracked and recorded upon delivery of debris.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: August 15th, November 15th, February 15th, and May 15th for consideration at the next quarterly meeting
structured_extraction.contact_phone: Dorchester County Office Building, Room 108, 501 Court Lane, Cambridge, MD 21613
structured_extraction.program_audience: County projects funded by grants, economic development projects supported by County or grant funds, school construction projects, and other blight removal and economic development projects approved by the Review Committee
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Disposal of construction debris
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Dorchester County, Maryland. Debris must be disposed of at the Dorchester County Landfill at Beulah.
requirements_list: Project must be designed to encourage community development, reduce blight, or increase assessable values

Project must fall into one of the following categories: (1) County projects funded by grants, (2) Economic development projects supported by County or grant funds, (3) School construction, or (4) Economic development and blight removal projects approved by the Review Committee
Organization cannot exceed awards of $20,000 per year or $100,000 over the life of the organization without special Council approval
If actual tons exceed estimate by more than 10%, request must be resubmitted to Review Committee for approval
Award letter and tonnage tracking form must be presented to landfill personnel upon delivery of debris
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Prepare a Tipping Fee Waiver Request Form (Attachment A) with project details and estimated tonnage. 2. Submit the form to Dorchester County Office Building, Room 108, 501 Court Lane, Cambridge, MD 21613 on or before the quarterly deadline dates (August 15th, November 15th, February 15th, or May 15th). 3. The Review Committee meets quarterly on the first business day of September, December, March, and June to review requests. Requests may be deferred if more information or review time is needed. 4. Upon approval, the awardee receives an award letter to be used at the Landfill to waive fees. 5. Present the award letter and tonnage tracking form to landfill personnel upon delivery of debris. 6. After project completion, submit receipts and tonnage tracking form to Finance for recording.

structured_extraction.program_name: Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program administered by FEMA that helps municipalities and local fire departments improve their staffing and deployment capabilities to respond to emergencies more effectively. The grant provides funding for hiring and retaining additional firefighters, improving emergency response coverage and public safety services. Both Anne Arundel County and the City of Salisbury have received SAFER grants, demonstrating the program's availability to a range of jurisdictions across Maryland and the United States.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A three-year grant that pays for 75 percent of salary and benefits for additional firefighters in years one and two, and 35 percent in year three. Award amounts vary by jurisdiction; for example, Anne Arundel County received up to $8.5 million over three years to support up to 70 new firefighter positions, while the Salisbury Fire Department received $1,527,738 to hire additional firefighters.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Fire Chief Trisha L. Wolford; John Tull
structured_extraction.program_audience: Municipalities and local fire departments seeking to improve staffing and emergency response capabilities by hiring and retaining additional firefighters.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hiring of additional firefighters and covering salary and benefits for those firefighters, as well as improving service delivery to residents, businesses, and visitors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible municipalities and local fire departments nationwide. In Maryland, recipients have included Anne Arundel County and the City of Salisbury's Fire Department.
requirements_list: Municipality or local fire department eligible to apply
Competitive selection process
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Municipalities and fire departments submit applications for consideration through FEMA's competitive SAFER grant process. Applicants must present the award notification to their city council or governing body for approval to accept the grant funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that helps low-income households reduce the cost of their phone or internet services. Monthly discounts of up to $9.25 are available to qualifying low-income customers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly discount of up to $9.25 on phone and internet costs. Eligible individuals may receive reduced cost landline phone service or a free cell phone. Financial eligibility: one person income $1,760 with no asset test; two people income $2,379 with no asset test. Also eligible if enrolled in Supplemental Security Income (SSI), Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Medicaid, Medical Assistance, food stamps, or energy assistance.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Phone and internet service costs (landline, cell phone, or internet service)

No asset test required
Low-income household status

structured_extraction.program_description: TAP is a supplemental transportation service that provides taxi fare subsidies to eligible seniors and people with disabilities in Frederick County. Participants receive a reloadable swipe card with a monthly allotment of subsidized taxi funds based on their home zip code.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible users receive a monthly allotment of taxi fare subsidies loaded onto a reloadable swipe card with photo ID. The subsidy amount varies by zip code: in zip codes 21701, 21702, and 21703, the county pays $60 monthly with the customer paying $10 per trip for a total of $70 monthly in available funds. In all other Frederick County zip codes, the county pays $120 monthly with the customer paying $20 per trip for a total of $140 monthly in available funds. Users can accumulate up to three months of funds on the card and make payments in smaller increments ($5 or $10 twice monthly for flexibility). Participating taxi companies swipe the card to receive payment. Funds must be used for taxi trips within Frederick County on weekdays and weekends based on taxi availability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors age 60 and older and people with disabilities who are registered with the Transit Plus program and have scheduled or attempted to schedule three Transit Plus rides over the course of a month.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Taxi fare payment for trips within Frederick County on weekdays and weekends based on taxi availability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service is available within Frederick County on weekdays and weekends based on taxi availability. Subsidy amounts vary by zip code: zip codes 21701, 21702, and 21703 receive lower subsidies; all other Frederick County zip codes receive higher subsidies.
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or older or have a disability
Must be registered with the Transit Plus program
Must have scheduled or attempted to schedule three Transit Plus rides over the course of a month
Must have a valid photo ID to receive the reloadable swipe card
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To participate in TAP, users must first register with the Transit Plus program. Once registered and meeting the eligibility requirements (age 60+ or disability status and having scheduled/attempted three Transit Plus rides in a month), eligible participants can apply for the program. After approval, users receive a reloadable swipe card with photo ID. To load fare funds onto the card, users can visit the online portal at eztransport.net/fred/members or contact the program directly for assistance. Funds can be loaded in smaller increments ($5 or $10 twice monthly) for user convenience. The program operates on a rolling basis with no set application deadlines.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and groups or organizations in Frederick County who want to learn how to use public transit effectively.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The training covers learning to read bus schedules, locating bus stops, understanding how to use Google Transit, and gaining confidence in commuting with transit.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals or groups/organizations should email the program contact to request travel training.

structured_extraction.program_description: Garrett County Government offers subsidies to help residents in difficult-to-reach areas afford broadband service. If a resident receives a quote from an internet service provider that exceeds their budget, the county may provide financial assistance to help cover some or all of the provider's requested customer contribution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county provides financial assistance to qualified residents to help pay for broadband infrastructure installation costs that the internet service provider has quoted. Residents may need to contribute up to 10% of the requested subsidy amount if possible. The county pays the internet service provider directly, not the customer. Program funding and per-project funding are limited.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Garrett County residents living at addresses that are difficult to serve with broadband and who cannot fully afford the internet service provider's quoted cost to extend service to their home.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Valid expenses directly related to connecting a customer to broadband service. The subsidy covers only infrastructure and installation costs quoted by the internet service provider, not direct customer expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Difficult-to-serve addresses in Garrett County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Resident must have received a quote from an internet service provider for broadband service
The quoted customer contribution must be beyond the resident's budget
Internet service provider must contribute to the project
Internet service provider must participate in the Affordable Connectivity Program (if the program is funded)
Address must not already be served by a broadband provider offering minimum service of 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload
Only valid expenses directly related to connecting a customer to broadband service qualify
Resident may be asked to contribute up to 10% of the requested subsidy amount if possible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A potential customer either reaches out to an internet service provider requesting service, or contacts the Broadband Division directly. The internet service provider assesses the situation and develops a budget to reach the home. If the customer cannot afford the full amount or any portion of the requested customer contribution, they can ask the internet service provider to request a subsidy, or contact the Broadband Division directly. If approved, the internet service provider begins the project. Permits, easements, and other legal requirements may delay actual connection.

Served by Potomac Edison or Somerset Rural Electric Cooperative (eligible for group purchasing plan)
Residential property owners interested in solar installation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up for a free solar estimate by contacting FREE at the provided phone number or email. Bulk group sign-ups enable contractors to offer lower prices through volume purchasing. Estimates are provided at no cost.

Property located in Garrett County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME)
structured_extraction.program_description: HUD entitlement grants administered by Harford County that provide annual formula-based funding for housing, infrastructure, revitalization, and services benefiting low- to moderate-income citizens. The CDBG Program funds capital projects and services that offer decent housing, suitable living environments, and economic opportunities for low- to moderate-income persons, and may also address slum and blight. The HOME Program expands the supply of decent, safe, sanitary, and affordable housing for low-income families and builds the capacity of nonprofit Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) to develop and manage affordable housing. Funding amounts are determined by a pre-determined HUD formula allocation. Harford County disperses funds annually to nonprofits, CHDOs, and in some cases for-profit entities, and submits a Consolidated Plan and Annual Action Plan to HUD each year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Harford County receives annual HUD formula allocations for both CDBG and HOME programs and disperses these funds to nonprofits, CHDOs, and in some cases for-profit entities throughout Harford County. Funds are not available directly to individuals. CDBG projects must meet one of three national objectives: benefit low-to-moderate-income persons (through housing, limited clientele benefit, area benefit, or jobs creation), address slum and blight (on an area, spot, or urban renewal basis), or address urgent need. HOME funds support activities that expand affordable housing supply; a 25% non-federal match is required for each eligible HOME activity. HOME affordability periods vary: $15,000–$40,000 requires 15 years; amounts over $40,000 require 15 years for refinancing of rental housing and 20 years for new construction of rental housing. Nonprofit subgrants can support public facility improvements, nonprofit services, tenant-based rental assistance, low-to-moderate income housing construction, first-time homebuyer support, and critical repairs. The Town of Bel Air and City of Aberdeen each receive a predetermined percentage of CDBG funding per HUD Urban County Agreement. All selected programs and projects are subject to the availability of funding and Harford County's budget review process.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Typical application period runs during January/February; rolling deadline based on annual funding cycle
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private nonprofit organizations with IRS 501(c)(3) status, Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs), non-profit developers, local government agencies, and in some cases for-profit entities serving low- to moderate-income persons in Harford County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing, infrastructure, revitalization, and services for the benefit of low- to moderate-income citizens; capital projects providing decent housing, suitable living environments, and economic opportunities; activities that expand the supply of decent, safe, sanitary, and affordable housing for low-income families; housing with support services such as case management and job readiness training; public facility improvements; nonprofit services; tenant-based rental assistance; low-to-moderate income housing construction; first-time homebuyer support; critical repairs; projects by CHDOs and nonprofit developers; and reduction of slum and blight.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland. The Town of Bel Air and City of Aberdeen each receive a predetermined percentage of CDBG funding per HUD Urban County Agreement.
requirements_list: Projects and activities must be submitted to and approved by HUD through a 5-year Consolidated Plan
Private nonprofit organizations must have IRS 501(c)(3) status
In some cases, for-profit entities may be eligible
All proposed programs and projects must meet applicable federal regulations
Projects must meet one of the CDBG national objectives: benefit low-moderate-income persons, address slum and blight, or address urgent need
A 25% non-federal match is required for each eligible HOME activity
For rental housing projects, rents must be restricted to income-eligible residents
Properties assisted with HOME funds must remain affordable for restricted time periods based on funding amount and activity type
Community Housing Development Organizations must provide decent housing affordable to low- and moderate-income persons as part of their organizational mission
CHDOs must have effectively carried out HOME-funded activities
CHDOs must have a history of serving the community
CHDOs must be organized under state or local laws and exempt from taxes under IRC 501(c)(3)
CHDOs must meet standards of financial accountability
One-third of CHDO governing board must be made up of low-income community residents or their elected representatives
CHDOs must maintain a formal process allowing low-income residents and program beneficiaries to provide input on relevant decisions
All selected programs and projects are subject to the availability of funding and Harford County's budget review process
Harford County maintains the right to reject, accept, or reduce the amount of funding requested
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact Housing & Community Development at 410-638-3045 to discuss project feasibility. The typical nonprofit subgrant application period runs during January and February each year. Applications are submitted through the Harford County Grants Portal Page. The County submits an Annual Action Plan (AAP) each winter for the upcoming fiscal year, with a public comment period in March/April before final submission to HUD in May. A 5-year Consolidated Plan is submitted to HUD outlining proposed uses of CDBG and HOME funds. Applicants must ensure their projects align with the current Consolidated Plan and Annual Action Plan priorities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund (CRRF) (Harford County)
structured_extraction.program_description: A fund established from state revenue generated by recreational cannabis sales to provide money to local governments for distribution to community-based initiatives serving low-income communities and those with higher rates of cannabis prohibition enforcement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Harford County distributes grants from recreational cannabis sales revenue to community-based initiatives and local government entities. Funds are allocated based on criteria established in Harford County Bill No. 24-030. The Maryland Office of Social Equity has identified zip codes 21001 (Aberdeen), 21009 (Abingdon), and 21040 (Edgewood) as priority areas within Harford County for funding consideration.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis through Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) process; FY2027 NOFA issued; community input meetings held in 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations and local government entities serving low-income communities and those disproportionately impacted by cannabis prohibition enforcement in Harford County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based initiatives as determined by Harford County legislation (Bill No. 24-030) serving low-income communities and those with higher rates of cannabis prohibition enforcement. Eligible uses include projects and programs benefiting priority geographic areas (zip codes 21001, 21009, 21040).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland. Priority areas identified by Maryland Office of Social Equity: zip codes 21001 (Aberdeen), 21009 (Abingdon), and 21040 (Edgewood).
requirements_list: Serve low-income communities
Serve communities with higher rates of cannabis prohibition enforcement
Align with Harford County Bill No. 24-030 criteria
Community-based or government organization status required
Priority consideration for projects in zip codes 21001, 21009, or 21040
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted through a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) process managed by Harford County. Interested applicants should: (1) Review the public notice and current NOFA announcement; (2) Attend community input meetings or review recorded town hall information for details on application requirements and priorities; (3) Submit applications according to the NOFA timeline and specifications; (4) Applications are evaluated and awards are made based on community input and alignment with CRRF criteria.

structured_extraction.program_name: Drinking Water State Revolving Fund Bipartisan Infrastructure Law Funding for PFAS/Emerging Contaminants
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides 100% loan principal forgiveness for projects that address emerging contaminants, including perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), in drinking water through the State Revolving Fund (SRF) program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% principal forgiveness on loans for drinking water projects that address emerging contaminants, including PFAS. Applicants must prepare project plans and meet eligibility criteria outlined in the Drinking Water Intended Use Plan (IUP) and Investment Priority Policy Statement (IPPS). Technical assistance is available through MDE and EPA to help with project development and application preparation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entities operating public drinking water systems in Maryland seeking to address PFAS and other emerging contaminants in their water supplies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that address emerging contaminants, including PFAS, in drinking water systems. Funds can support treatment systems, testing, remediation, and related infrastructure improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. All counties and public drinking water systems are eligible to apply.
requirements_list: Project must address emerging contaminants, including PFAS, in drinking water
Applicant must operate a public drinking water system
Project must comply with Safe Drinking Water Act requirements
Applicant must meet SRF program eligibility requirements
Technical assistance should be obtained from MDE or EPA before application submission
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact MDE for technical assistance and project guidance. 2. Prepare project plan addressing emerging contaminant issues. 3. Review Maryland's Drinking Water Intended Use Plan (IUP) and Investment Priority Policy Statement (IPPS) for current priorities and procedures. 4. Submit application through the Maryland Water Infrastructure Financing Administration (MWIFA) following state SRF application procedures. 5. Access EPA's Tackling Emerging Contaminants (TEC) Water Technical Assistance program for additional support: https://www.epa.gov/water-infrastructure/tackling-emerging-contaminants-tec-water-technical-assistance-waterta. 6. Consult preparation resources available from MDE at https://mde.maryland.gov/programs/water/WQFA/Documents/Prepare%20to%20apply_Oct%202024.pdf.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that provides funding to small businesses in Harford County to support their overall growth through capital investment, job creation and retention.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $200,000 with flexible terms depending on each unique project and business. Funds can be used for building and land purchases, renovations, technology upgrades, or equipment purchases. Can be used in conjunction with other lending institutions through gap financing and partnership. Collateral is required, though exceptions may be made for loans less than $10,000. Loans over $75,000 must be approved by the Harford County Council.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses as defined by the US Small Business Administration located in Harford County that have been operating for at least one year and are in good standing with Harford County and the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building or land purchase, expansion, technology upgrades, or equipment purchases for projects in Harford County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland
requirements_list: Business must be located in Harford County
Business must have been operating for at least one year
Business must be in good standing with Harford County and the State of Maryland
Business must be classified as small business by US Small Business Administration
Submit Business Plan
Submit two years of Cash Flow Projections
Submit two years of Business Tax Returns
Submit two years of Financial Statements including Balance Sheets and Income Statements
Submit Schedule of Business Debts including rates and terms
Submit two years of Income Tax Returns for all owners with interest greater than 5% and any individuals and corporate entities personally guaranteeing the loan
Submit Personal Financial Statement dated within the last 3 months for all owners with interest greater than 5% and any individuals and corporate entities personally guaranteeing the loan
Submit description of all available collateral with current lien values
Submit Resolution authorizing the business to enter into the loan and/or guaranty
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Click the application button on the Harford County Economic Development website, which redirects to the Harford County EDOF Loan information page. Review all tabs on the information page, then click apply to access the eCivis portal. Create a profile and log in to begin the application. Submit all required documentation through the portal. The Harford County Economic Development Advisory Board Loan Committee meets monthly to review applications. Loans over $75,000 also require approval by the Harford County Council. Settlement occurs within 90 days of approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that funds renovation and new construction projects to improve business exteriors along designated stretches of U.S. Route 40 (Pulaski Highway) and MD-755 (Edgewood Road) in the Edgewood Sustainable Community Area. The program aims to transform business exteriors to generate economic development and increase investment in a historically underserved community. The pilot round was funded with $200,000 in Maryland State Revitalization Program funds.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible projects costing $10,000 or less receive 100% reimbursement with zero match required. Eligible projects exceeding $10,000 receive reimbursement for up to 80% of approved costs over the first $10,000, with the business required to provide a 20% cash match for costs exceeding $10,000. The program is funded with a total of $200,000 from the Maryland State Revitalization Program. Funds are used for project reimbursement only.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program currently closed; all $200,000 in pilot funding has been expended. Applications held on file pending additional funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Business owners with non-residential properties located in the designated Edgewood area along U.S. Route 40 or MD-755 in the Edgewood Sustainable Community Area overlay district.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Facade (exterior only) improvements and enhancements including ADA compliant exterior and site accessibility improvements, awnings, cleaning and repair of building exteriors, landscaping, lighting, exterior painting, parking lot improvement, siding, signage, and window and door upgrades, replacement and repair. Interior renovation, projects completed before approval, equipment or inventory purchase, property purchase, roofing, and structural repairs are prohibited.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located within the designated eligibility area bordering U.S. Route 40 (Pulaski Highway) or MD-755 (Edgewood Road) located in the Edgewood Sustainable Community Area overlay district in Harford County, as shown on the program map.
requirements_list: Business must be located within the designated eligibility area bordering U.S. Route 40 or MD-755 in the Edgewood Sustainable Community Area overlay district
Business must be in Good Standing with Harford County Government and the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Business and project must comply with all Harford County planning, zoning, licensing, permitting, and public works requirements and regulations

Business must NOT be one of the following industries: adult entertainment facilities, adult video/book shops, check cashing facilities, gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, or tattoo parlors
Application must contain a detailed project description and statement of how the project will improve business exterior and stimulate economic growth
Application must include an architectural rendering, detailed budget, project scope of work, and invoices and proofs of payment

structured_extraction.program_description: Supports individual nonprofits or municipalities with creating, expanding, or enhancing events that drive tourism and economic growth in the county. This can include festivals, events, exhibits, and other programming that attract individuals to either overnight stays or day trips. Funds not used by the Partnership Grant program are set aside for use by the Community Impact Grant program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided to nonprofits or municipalities for tourism-related festivals, events, exhibits, and programming. Support can cover direct tourism-related marketing costs, non-marketing expenses for festivals and events, internal operational expenses including up to 75 percent of key employee salaries for first-year awards, with salaries declining to 50 percent in year two, 25 percent in year three, and zero percent in subsequent years. Funds cannot be used for daily operating costs, capital improvements, property acquisition, debt reduction, or office equipment. Award amounts are at the discretion of the County Executive after applications are reviewed and recommended by the Economic Development Advisory Board Tourism Activity Review Committee. No matching funds are required. Funds not used by Partnership Grant program are allocated here. Reporting requirements include quarterly budget and activity reporting with receipts and proof of payment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications will open on Monday, February 23, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual nonprofits or municipalities in Harford County. Nonprofit organizations must be 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) and registered in Harford County. Municipalities are also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct tourism-related marketing costs for festivals, events, exhibits, and programming; non-marketing expenses for festivals, events, and programming that attract local attendance or visitors from outside the county and state; internal operational expenses including up to 75 percent of key employee salaries for first-year awards with declining coverage in subsequent years (50% year two, 25% year three, 0% thereafter); festivals, events, exhibits, and programming beneficial to community culture and quality of life; or festival and event sponsorships. Funds cannot be used for daily operating costs, capital improvements, property acquisition, debt reduction, or office equipment.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through an online portal (https://portal.ecivis.com/). Applicants must complete and upload the Tourism Grant Budget and Expense Report (spreadsheet) and the Quarterly Narrative Activity Report (QNAR) with program/event overview and objectives. Approved applications are funded based on priority order: first priority is direct tourism-related marketing costs by a nonprofit tourism-related organization or municipality; second priority is non-marketing expenses by a nonprofit or municipality that attract attendance locally or visitors from outside county and state; third priority is internal operational expenses by a nonprofit tourism-related organization with salary caps; fourth priority is festivals, events, or programming beneficial to community culture by a nonprofit non-tourism-related organization; fifth priority is festival sponsorships by a nonprofit non-tourism-related organization or municipality. The Economic Development Advisory Board Tourism Activity Review Committee submits recommendations; final amount disbursed is at the discretion of the County Executive.
