structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Enterprise Zone Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax incentive program for businesses located in designated Enterprise Zones in Harford County, Maryland. The zones are designated by the State of Maryland to retain and expand resident businesses, encourage well-paying job creation, promote development and occupancy of vacant or underutilized land and buildings, and revitalize older industrial areas. Harford County has two Enterprise Zone areas: the Aberdeen/Havre de Grace zone and the Edgewood/Joppa zone. The program provides real property tax credits on capital investments as well as state income/job creation tax credits, including enhanced credits for hiring economically-disadvantaged employees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two types of tax credits are available. Real property tax credits provide an 80% credit on increases in the assessed value of real property for the first five years, decreasing by 10% annually for the remaining five years, available for up to 10 years on capital investments. Income/job creation tax credits include a one-time $1,000 tax credit per new job created, submitted with the annual tax filing using Form 500 CR. An additional tax credit is available for businesses hiring economically-disadvantaged employees, increasing the credit to $6,000 total per eligible employee distributed over three years ($2,000 per year for three years).
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses located within the designated Enterprise Zones in Harford County (Aberdeen, Havre de Grace, Edgewood, and Joppa) looking to expand, construct, or rehabilitate real property, create new jobs, or hire economically-disadvantaged employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits for capital investments in construction and rehabilitation of real property, and for creation of new jobs. Credits can be applied toward increases in assessed property value and new job creation wages, including enhanced credits for hiring economically-disadvantaged employees. Real property must be occupied to receive the real property tax credit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located within a designated Enterprise Zone in Harford County. The Aberdeen/Havre de Grace Enterprise Zone encompasses a 9,738-acre area including properties along U.S. Route 40, Aberdeen and Havre de Grace municipalities, portions of Aberdeen Proving Ground to the east, Belcamp and Perryman to the south, and the HEAT Center to the west. The Edgewood/Joppa Enterprise Zone covers businesses in the Edgewood and Joppa areas of Harford County.
requirements_list: Business must be located within a designated Enterprise Zone
Minimum capital investment of $100,000 if business has 10 or fewer employees, or $125,000 if business has 11 or more employees
Minimum job creation of 2 new jobs if business has 10 or fewer employees, or 5 new jobs if business has 11 or more employees
New jobs must require 35 hours per week or more at hourly pay of at least 150% of minimum wage
Half of work time for new jobs must be within the Enterprise Zone
Real property tax credit requires the building to be occupied to receive the credit
Enterprise Zone Administrator must be contacted prior to construction to discuss timeline and ensure real property tax credits are timed with July 1st assessment date
Itemized cost breakdown for construction and/or renovation must be submitted with application
Site plan showing changes to interior/exterior of buildings must be submitted with application
All required documentation must accompany the application
Business must meet state and county eligibility criteria
Business must be engaged in activities that support job creation and business expansion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Enterprise Zone Administrator, Karen Holt, prior to construction to discuss timeline and requirements and to ensure real property tax credits are timed with the July 1st assessment date. Submit a completed application with an itemized cost breakdown for construction/renovation, a site plan showing building changes, and all required documentation to the Enterprise Zone Administrator by October 1st each year. For income/job creation tax credits, submit Form 500 CR (Maryland Individual Income Tax Return) with your annual tax filing. The Enterprise Zone Administrator will review applications and verify eligibility requirements have been met. Contact the Harford County Office of Economic Development at 410-638-3059 or klholt@harfordcountymd.gov for information on eligibility and the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Harford County Grant-in-Aid Program enhances the ability of public and private sector organizations to provide human services and address the resource needs of organizations that meet the emergency and daily needs of Harford County citizens. Harford County allocates more than $1 million each year to support local nonprofits working in a full range of supportive services, including housing and homeless prevention services. Funds are available on a competitive basis to organizations that meet certain eligibility criteria and submit requests by a predetermined date. New applicants are eligible to receive up to $5,000 in starter funds to give growing service providers financial and technical support. For housing-related grants, applicants should visit the Community Development office.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Harford County provides competitive grant funding to qualifying non-profit organizations. The county allocates more than $1 million annually to support local nonprofits. New applicants are eligible to receive up to $5,000 in starter funds. Organizations receiving grant funds enter into an agreement with the county and must comply with financial and programmatic procedures and submit required forms. Funds are awarded on a competitive basis to organizations that meet eligibility criteria and submit requests by a predetermined date using an application form provided by Harford County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit, tax-exempt organizations (501(c)(3)) that provide human services to low- to moderate-income residents of Harford County, including those serving homeless individuals, at-risk homeless individuals, or providing affordable housing. New and growing service providers are also encouraged to apply.

Applications are reviewed by the Community Development Review Board, which makes funding recommendations. Funds are awarded on a competitive basis. Selected organizations enter into an agreement with Harford County and must comply with financial and programmatic procedures and submit required forms.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Historic Preservation Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program administered by Harford County that provides financial incentives for owners of structures designated as Harford County historic landmarks and properties located within Harford County historic districts. Credits are available for restoration and rehabilitation expenses incurred on qualifying properties, as well as for the added value of restored historic landmarks, provided work is completed in accordance with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Historic Rehabilitation and Harford County Historic Preservation Design Guidelines.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits are available for expenses incurred in the restoration or rehabilitation of structures designated as Harford County historic landmarks or located within Harford County historic districts. The tax credits apply to qualifying restoration and rehabilitation expenses as well as the added value attributed to the restored historic landmark. There is no maximum or minimum dollar amount specified in the program guidelines. Applicants must submit a Certificate of Appropriateness (Part 1 of the application) before beginning any work. After completing the work, applicants must submit a Certification of Completed Work application (Part 2) along with an itemized expense sheet and supporting documentation demonstrating compliance with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Historic Rehabilitation and the Harford County Historic Preservation Design Guidelines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of structures designated as Harford County historic landmarks and property owners whose properties are located within Harford County historic districts, including individuals, for-profit entities, and non-profits undertaking qualifying historic preservation or rehabilitation projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoration and rehabilitation of historic landmarks designated by the Harford County Historic Preservation Commission and properties located within Harford County historic districts. Funds must be used for work completed in compliance with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Historic Rehabilitation and Harford County Historic Preservation Design Guidelines.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland only. Eligible properties must be either (1) designated as Harford County historic landmarks by the Historic Preservation Commission, or (2) located within a Harford County historic district.
requirements_list: Property must be designated as a Harford County historic landmark or located within a designated Harford County historic district
Rehabilitation work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Historic Rehabilitation
Work must comply with Harford County Historic Preservation Design Guidelines
A Certificate of Appropriateness must be obtained and approved before work begins
Applicants must submit an itemized expense sheet with detailed documentation of all costs incurred
Applicants must provide supporting documentation demonstrating compliance with design standards
Work must be substantially completed before submitting the Certification of Completed Work application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted in two parts: (1) Certificate of Appropriateness Application (Part 1) - Applicants must submit this before beginning any rehabilitation work. The application is reviewed by the Harford County Historic Preservation Commission, and applicants are required to attend a Historic Preservation Commission meeting for review and approval. (2) Certification of Completed Work Application (Part 2) - After completing all rehabilitation work, applicants submit this application along with an itemized expense sheet and supporting documentation demonstrating compliance with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards and Design Guidelines. Applicants are strongly encouraged to contact historic preservation staff at historic@harfordcountymd.gov before beginning the application process to discuss their project and ensure it qualifies for the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program administered by Harford County that subsidizes rents for eligible participants who rent units in the private market. The program is designed to assist very low-income families, the elderly, and people with disabilities to rent decent, safe, and sanitary housing. A housing subsidy is paid directly to the landlord on behalf of a participating family. Eligible applicants are placed on a waiting list; when selected, they complete a formal application, attend a briefing on program rules and family obligations, and receive a Housing Choice Voucher. Families can remain on the program as long as they remain eligible and in compliance with program obligations, provided funding continues. Payment standards vary by number of bedrooms, ranging from $1,082 to $3,703 per month as of November 1, 2025.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Housing Choice Voucher Program provides subsidies that cover the difference between the family's contribution toward rent (typically 30% of adjusted income) and the actual rent. Families receive a voucher that can be used to rent private market units that meet HUD Housing Quality Standards. Payment standards vary by number of bedrooms: 1-bedroom: $1,082; 2-bedroom: $1,299; 3-bedroom: $1,554; 4-bedroom: $1,728; 5-bedroom: $2,008; and 6-bedroom: $3,703 per month (as of November 1, 2025). The subsidy is ongoing as long as the family remains eligible and in compliance with program obligations, provided funding continues. Families must pay a tenant share of rent, and landlords receive direct payment from Harford County for the subsidy portion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Waiting list closed as of December 15, 2025; will reopen when there is a reasonable number of applications remaining and estimated wait time is less than two years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Very low-income families, the elderly, people with disabilities, single people, working families, families with dependent children, veterans, and homeless individuals who live or work in Harford County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rent subsidies for private market rental units that meet HUD Housing Quality Standards and Livability Code standards for safety, decency, and sanitation. Families must find housing within 60 days of receiving their voucher, and rent must be within the Housing Authority's allowable payment standards by bedroom size. Units must include basic equipment, facilities, light, ventilation, heating, and sanitation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland. Priority is given to applicants who live or work in Harford County. Residents within the municipal limits of Bel Air, Havre de Grace, or Aberdeen should contact their local government. Residents outside of town limits should contact the County Department of Inspections, Licenses & Permits. The program serves the entire county outside of incorporated municipalities.
requirements_list: Household income must meet Federal Income Limit Guidelines (very low-income, at or below 50% of area median income)
Must be a very low-income family, elderly individual, or person with a disability
Must live or work in Harford County to receive priority consideration
Head of household must be placed on the Housing Agency's waiting list
Must complete preliminary application to be added to waiting list
Must complete a formal application when selected from the waiting list and undergo eligibility determination
Must attend a mandatory briefing on program rules, regulations, and family obligations
Must find housing within 60 days of receiving the voucher
Rent must be within Housing Authority payment standards for the applicable number of bedrooms
Housing must meet HUD Housing Quality Standards (includes basic equipment, facilities, light, ventilation, heating, and sanitation)
Rental units must meet Livability Code for Rental Housing standards for health and safety
Units are inspected before contract is signed and at least annually thereafter
Families must maintain compliance with family obligations including lease terms, rent payments, and program requirements
Applicants on the waiting list must keep their address current and submit address change requests if contact information changes
Must not have been evicted from public housing for drug-related criminal activity in the past 3 years
Must not owe money to any housing authority
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete a preliminary application by mail, online, or in person and have the head of household's name placed on the Housing Agency's waiting list (waiting list closed December 15, 2025; will reopen when estimated wait time drops below two years). 2. Applications are processed and maintained on the waiting list in order received, subject to local housing authority preferences. 3. When selected from the waiting list based on wait time and preferences, an enrollment interview is scheduled. 4. Eligibility is determined based on income, citizenship, criminal history, and other HUD requirements. 5. If eligible, family completes a formal application. 6. Attend a mandatory briefing session on program rules, regulations, family obligations, and lease responsibilities; Housing Choice Voucher is issued at the end of the briefing. 7. Family has 60 calendar days to find housing that meets HUD Housing Quality Standards and program requirements. 8. Family negotiates lease terms with the landlord. 9. Harford County reviews the lease and inspection is conducted by the Housing Authority inspector. 10. Harford County approves or denies the lease and unit based on inspection results. 11. Upon approval, Harford County Housing Authority and the landlord enter into a Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) contract on behalf of the family. 12. Family moves into unit and rent subsidy begins. Application status can be checked by calling 1-877-204-9098. Appointments are required to speak with a program analyst; the office is open from 8:00 am to 5:00 pm for document drop-offs. Questions can be directed to housingagency@harfordcountymd.gov or 410-638-3045.

structured_extraction.program_description: A down payment and closing cost assistance program designed for first-time homebuyers purchasing a home in Harford County, Maryland. structured_extraction.assistance_description: Deferred loans up to $20,000 for properties within the Southern County Task Force Area or up to $10,000 for properties outside that area. Interest rate is zero percent (0%). The loan is deferred, meaning the borrower does not need to repay the loan as long as they occupy the property as their primary residence. A lien is recorded through a Deed of Trust. Assistance covers down payment, closing costs, or loan reduction monies. Borrower must contribute a minimum of 1% of the sales price in cash. The loan becomes due if the property is sold or if the borrower no longer occupies it as their primary residence.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers in Harford County purchasing a home with limited funds for down payment and closing costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment, closing costs, or loan reduction monies for the purchase of a home in Harford County.

Maximum household income of 80% of County Area Median Income
Maximum purchase price of 95% of Area Median Home Value
Minimum cash contribution from borrower of 1% of sales price
Borrower must occupy property as primary residence
Property must be 1-4 unit single-family dwelling, attached home, condominium, townhome, planned unit development, or manufactured home
Property must be inspected by a Harford County Housing Inspector
First mortgage must be LP Accept or DU Approve/Eligible
First mortgage must be 30-year, fixed rate, fully amortizing
Applicant must complete first-time homebuyer counseling
Cash to pocket is not permitted
A monthly cash flow analysis is required by the Housing Agency
Properties in flood zones are not eligible
Maximum household size eligibility based on income limits

Gasparovic at 410-638-3045 or smgasparovic@harfordcountymd.gov to confirm funds availability, as the program is subject to limited funding. 2. Applicant must complete first-time homebuyer counseling. 5. Upon approval, the deferred loan is documented with a Deed of Trust lien recorded on the property. 6. Loan funds are provided at closing to cover down payment, closing costs, or loan reduction amounts.

structured_extraction.program_description: A county-level real and personal property tax credit available to eligible nonprofit swim clubs. In Harford County, the program provides a 50% credit on real and personal property taxes. In Montgomery County, a property tax credit is available to qualifying nonprofit swim clubs that use their facilities exclusively to provide recreational outlets for local communities. Both programs aim to reduce the property tax burden on nonprofit swim club organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: In Harford County, a tax credit equal to 50% of real and personal property taxes owed on the nonprofit swim club facility. In Montgomery County, a property tax credit applies to County Taxes only (General County Tax and Special Service Area Taxes). The credit is applied annually to reduce the organization's property tax liability. Both programs require annual application and certification of nonprofit status and exclusive use of the facility for community recreational purposes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit swim clubs operating in Harford County or Montgomery County that use their facilities exclusively to provide recreational outlets for local communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of real and personal property tax bills for eligible nonprofit swim clubs operating community recreational facilities.

requirements_list: Must be an eligible nonprofit swim club organization
Organization must hold valid Articles of Incorporation
Organization must hold current Certificate in Good Standing from the State of Maryland, Department of Assessments and Taxation
Organization must use its facility exclusively to provide a recreational outlet for a local community
Organization must be properly registered as a nonprofit entity
Annual application and recertification required if there have been changes to incorporation status or good standing certification
Property must be used exclusively for nonprofit swim club operations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Nonprofit Swim Club Property Tax Credit Application form annually by May 1 preceding the taxable year. In the first year of application and in any subsequent years if there have been changes to organizational status, applicants must provide: (1) Articles of Incorporation, and (2) a current Certificate in Good Standing from the State of Maryland, Department of Assessments and Taxation. The applicant must certify under oath that the property is a nonprofit swim club using its facility exclusively to provide a recreational outlet for a local community. Submit required documentation to the appropriate county treasury or finance division.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Howard County residential program that reimburses homeowners for installing stormwater management features like rain gardens, permeable pavers, rainwater harvesting systems, tree canopy expansion, conservation landscaping, dry wells, green roofs, and pavement removal. Participants can reduce their Watershed Protection Fee and receive cash reimbursement for qualifying projects that absorb stormwater runoff and reduce pollution.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners receive reimbursement for approved stormwater management projects installed by licensed contractors. Reimbursement is 75% of project cost up to specified caps per BMP type: Rain Gardens up to $5,000, Conservation Landscaping up to $3,000, Rainwater Harvesting up to $750 or $2 per gallon of treated volume, Permeable Hardscaping up to $5,000, Impervious Surface Removal up to $2,000, Dry Wells up to $2,000, Urban Tree Canopy Expansion up to $1,000 per tree ($150 maximum per tree), and Green Roofs up to $7,000. Applicants meeting hardship criteria may be eligible for up to 100% reimbursement. Additionally, approved projects can reduce the homeowner's annual Watershed Protection Fee. All BMPs must be installed by licensed contractors and comply with Maryland Department of Environment Stormwater Design Manual standards.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Site Visit Request Form open April 1st until full (75 spots); Project Applications due November 30th
structured_extraction.program_audience: Howard County residential homeowners and renters (with homeowner permission) whose homes were built before 2003
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of stormwater best management practices (BMPs) including rain gardens, conservation landscaping, rainwater harvesting systems, permeable hardscaping, tree canopy expansion, dry wells, green roofs, and impervious surface removal/pavement removal
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Howard County, Maryland only
requirements_list: Home must have been built before 2003
Applicant must be homeowner or renter working with homeowner
Projects must be installed by a licensed contractor (certified for certain BMPs like permeable hardscaping and green roofs)
Site visit and project approval required before installation
Rain gardens: minimum 75 square feet, maximum 25 feet sheet flow distance, must comply with Maryland DEM Stormwater Design Manual Chapter 5 (2000)

Conservation landscaping: minimum 150 square feet, 2-3 inch ponding depth, 6 inch soil de-compaction with 2 inch soil amendment, maximum 25 feet sheet flow distance, must comply with Maryland DEM Stormwater Design Manual Chapter 5 (2009)
Rainwater harvesting: minimum 250 gallons for single-family homes, 100 gallons for townhomes, rain barrels/cisterns must be recertified every 3 years, must treat roof impervious surfaces
Permeable hardscaping: minimum 100 square feet paved area, installer must have appropriate certification, must comply with Maryland DEM Stormwater Design Manual Chapter 5 (2009)
Impervious surface removal: minimum 100 square feet removed and restored to permeable surface or planted state, must comply with permeable hardscaping criteria if applicable

Dry wells: must demonstrate A or B hydrologic soil groups or 0.52 inch per hour or higher infiltration rate within 50 feet, must treat roof, sidewalk, driveway, or patio impervious surfaces, must comply with Maryland DEM Stormwater Design Manual Chapter 5 (2009)

Urban tree canopy expansion: minimum 2 trees planted, deciduous trees minimum 1 inch caliper or evergreens minimum 3 feet tall, species must be native and non-invasive, trees must intercept runoff from impervious surfaces like roof downspouts, patios, driveways, or sidewalks to receive WPF credit
Green roofs: minimum 300 square feet or 1/4 of roof area, must be installed by certified contractor, must comply with Maryland DEM Stormwater Design Manual Chapter 5 (2009)
All vegetated BMPs: must contain 75% native plants (by count), no invasive plants, planting density must achieve full coverage after 3 years, minimum 2 inches mulch at initial planting
Projects must not have been installed before November 2011 program start date
Reimbursements not granted for items unrelated to project, in excess of project needs, or structural BMPs required by development regulations
Project applications must be submitted by November 30th with contractor estimate and project detail sheets
Reimbursement requests must include signed Credit and Reimbursement Agreement
Post-installation inspection required before reimbursement processing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit Site Visit Request Form (open April 1st, limited to 75 spots). 2. Receive site visit and recommendations from county staff (August-September). 3. Contact licensed contractor and obtain project design and cost estimate. 4. Submit Project Application by November 30th with contractor estimate and project detail sheets specific to each BMP type. 5. Technical Review Committee evaluates applications (December-February). 6. Receive project approval notification by February 21st. 7. Coordinate installation with contractor starting February 21st. 8. Submit reimbursement request with signed Credit and Reimbursement Agreement after project completion. 9. County conducts post-installation inspection on rolling basis starting April 1st. 10. Reimbursement processed bi-weekly starting April 15th.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides up to 26 weeks of temporary financial assistance to qualified individuals who are unemployed through no fault of their own.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Weekly payments ranging from $50 to $430 for up to 26 weeks (6.5 months). The exact amount depends on prior wages earned. Eligibility requires earning at least $1,176.01 in one quarter during the base period (18 months before application) and a minimum of $1,800 over at least two quarters.

requirements_list: Be unemployed through no fault of your own
Be ready to work hours normal for your job as soon as possible without restrictions
Have earned at least $1,176.01 during one quarter of the base period and minimum $1,800 over at least two quarters during the 18 months before application
Register for a Maryland Workforce Exchange account after filing claim
Document weekly job search activities with at least 3 activities per week
Complete weekly certification to continue receiving benefits
For federal civilian employees: complete 935 affidavit and provide proof of income and federal employment documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Determine if you qualify based on unemployment reason and wage requirements. Step 2: Gather required information including Social Security Number, employment history from last 18 months, and employer details. Step 3: File claim online through Maryland Unemployment Insurance Portal (BEACON) or by phone at 667-207-6520 (Monday-Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.). Allow up to 21 days for claim decision. Step 4: Register with Maryland Workforce Exchange System and document at least 3 job search activities each week. Step 5: Complete weekly certification every Sunday starting new week using BEACON portal, mobile app, or automated phone line. Federal employees must complete additional 935 affidavit with proof of income and employment documentation.

Cards and coupons are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis and are valid from July 1 through November 30 of the distribution year.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified low-income seniors receive an electronic card or coupon worth $50 that can be used to purchase fresh fruits, vegetables, cut herbs, and honey at designated farmers' markets and approved farmers throughout Maryland. The card/coupon is valid from July 1 through November 30 of the distribution year. Cards are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis at designated senior centers and activity centers. Cards should be treated as cash and cannot be replaced if lost. This is a one-time annual benefit per eligible senior (each qualified senior may only receive the $50 SFMNP benefit 1x each year). In Anne Arundel County, coupons are distributed and applications may be submitted by visiting a local Senior Activity Center, emailing senior_nutrition@aacounty.org, or mailing to the Senior Nutrition Program. In Baltimore City, cards are distributed at senior centers during scheduled distribution dates and proxy designees may obtain cards for eligible older adults (limit 2 cards per proxy). In Baltimore County, applicants call 410-887-0311 or complete an online form.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Cards valid July 1 - November 30 annually; Baltimore County no longer accepting applications for 2025; Baltimore City 2024 distribution dates were July 2-12, 2024
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income older adults aged 60 and older who are residents of Maryland (Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, or Baltimore County) and meet income guidelines (household income within 185% of Federal Poverty Guidelines; e.g., annual income below $28,953 for an individual or $39,128 for a two-person household).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of fresh vegetables, fruits, cut herbs, and honey at authorized farmers' markets and from authorized/approved farmers throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, and Baltimore County. Once cards or coupons are obtained, they can be used at designated farmers' markets and approved farmers throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be 60 years old or older with proof of age
Must be a resident of Maryland, specifically of the applying county (Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, or Baltimore County) with proof of residence
Must meet low-income guidelines (household income within 185% of Federal Poverty Guidelines; e.g., annual income below $28,953 for an individual or $39,128 for a two-person household)
Income may be verified through self-certification with older adult's signature
Must provide name, address, phone number or email, date of birth, ethnicity and race
Each qualified senior may only receive the $50 SFMNP benefit 1x each year; cannot seek additional cards from other locations after receiving one
Baltimore City: Proxy designees may obtain cards for eligible older adults (limit 2 cards per proxy)
Participants must certify that information provided for eligibility determination is correct to the best of their knowledge
By signing the application, participant acknowledges they are 60 years of age and household income is within income eligibility guidelines effective for July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants may apply through their local county program. In Anne Arundel County, submit a completed application (available in English, Spanish, and Korean) by visiting a local Senior Activity Center, emailing it to senior_nutrition@aacounty.org, or mailing it to the Senior Nutrition Program at 7320 Ritchie HWY, Glen Burnie, MD 21061. Accepted applicants will be notified within 15 business days after submission. Participants must complete the application form with personal information and certify their eligibility, and may opt in to receive text message communication from Healthy Together regarding the program and benefit information. In Baltimore City, older adults visit one of the designated senior centers during scheduled distribution dates and times, provide proof of age and residence, complete the application with income self-verification, and receive cards on a first-come, first-served basis while supplies last. Proxy designees may obtain cards for eligible older adults by taking the completed proxy form to a distribution site in the county the participant resides within. In Baltimore County, applicants call 410-887-0311 or complete an online form with required personal information.

structured_extraction.program_description: SHIP provides free, unbiased counseling and assistance to Medicare-eligible beneficiaries, their families, and caregivers. Trained staff and volunteer counselors help people understand Medicare coverage options, compare plans, navigate enrollment, address billing issues, and learn about fraud protection. The program also includes Senior Medicare Patrol to help prevent healthcare fraud and abuse. Services are available in both Charles County and Prince George's County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Aging / Local County Agencies (Charles County and Prince George's County)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free one-on-one counseling appointments with trained SHIP counselors to review Medicare plans, compare coverage options, and help with enrollment decisions. Group computer labs are also available at libraries and senior centers during Open Enrollment Period to help beneficiaries enroll in Medicare plans online with staff support. The program also provides fraud prevention education through Senior Medicare Patrol. All services are provided at no cost. No financial assistance is provided; services are technical assistance only.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; Open Enrollment Period typically October 15 - December 7
structured_extraction.contact_phone: Charles County: 301-609-5712 (La Plata area); 240-448-2816 (Waldorf area); 301-934-9305 (Western Charles County). Prince George's County: 301-265-8450
structured_extraction.program_audience: Medicare-eligible individuals (and Medicare beneficiaries), their families, and caregivers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance only — no financial assistance provided. Services include understanding coverage and costs, plan comparison and enrollment assistance, Medicare Advantage versus Medigap information, prescription payment guidance, billing issue resolution, fraud protection education through Senior Medicare Patrol, and referrals to other resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County and Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be Medicare-eligible or a Medicare beneficiary, or a family member or caregiver of a Medicare-eligible person
For group computer lab sessions: attendees must be able to use a computer and bring a list of medications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To schedule a free one-on-one counseling appointment with a SHIP counselor, call the Information and Assistance Office in your county. In Charles County, beneficiaries can also attend open computer lab sessions held at Charles County Public Libraries and Senior Centers during the Annual Open Enrollment Period (October 15 – December 7). Labs are held from 9:30am to 12:30pm and require attendees to be able to use a computer and bring a list of medications. In Prince George's County, contact the Aging and Disabilities Resource Center at 301-265-8450 for assistance with scheduling appointments and enrollment support.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program established in 1977 that preserves prime agricultural land and woodland by purchasing development rights (conservation easements) from eligible landowners on a permanent, in-perpetuity basis. Administered cooperatively between the Maryland Department of Agriculture and participating counties including Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Talbot, Charles, and others, the program protects prime agricultural soils and woodland from conversion to non-agricultural uses, safeguards agricultural resources, promotes sustainable food production, preserves rural landscapes, and supports farming communities. Landowners receive payment in exchange for voluntarily agreeing never to develop their land for non-agricultural or non-forestry purposes, while retaining ownership and the right to farm, timber, or otherwise use the land within easement terms. Recent easement offers have ranged from $8,000 to $10,000 per acre with cash at settlement. As of November 2024, over 5,912 acres in Anne Arundel County alone and over 10,000 acres in Charles County have been permanently preserved through the program. County-level programs such as the Anne Arundel County Agricultural and Woodland Preservation Program and the Baltimore County Agricultural Land Preservation Program operate in parallel and collaboration with MALPF, using innovative and collaborative funding mechanisms.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program purchases agricultural preservation easements (development rights) from eligible landowners, permanently restricting the land to agricultural or forestry use in perpetuity. Payment is made to landowners at settlement; recent easement offers have ranged from $8,000 to $10,000 per acre. Under the state MALPF program, payment can be up to 75% of the appraised Fair Market Value of the easement; under the Anne Arundel County local program, payment is 60% of the appraised Fair Market Value. Landowners retain ownership and all agricultural and forestry use rights within easement terms. The Foundation makes offers based on the lower of: (1) the asking price, (2) the calculated easement value, (3) a cap set by the County, or the statutory State cap of 75% of the recommended appraised value. Funding is contingent on State and County budget availability and Board of Public Works approval. Any approval to obtain an option contract is subject to available funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by county and program: Anne Arundel County — November 1 and April 1; Talbot County — April 1, 2026 (FY2027); State MALPF — July 1 annually; Baltimore County — annual basis; Charles County — rolling/ongoing
structured_extraction.contact_name: Billy Gorski (Anne Arundel County); Elisa Deflaux (Talbot County); Baltimore County Land Preservation Staff; Charles County Planning Staff
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of prime farmland, agricultural land, or woodland across Maryland, including working family farm owners in Baltimore County, landowners with parcels 50 acres or greater in Anne Arundel County, property owners in Charles County with prime farmland or woodland, and owners of eligible farmland and woodland in Talbot County who wish to preserve their agricultural properties. May include entities (trusts, LLCs, limited partnerships, corporations) holding title to farmland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of agricultural preservation easements that permanently restrict development on prime farmland and woodland, maintaining agricultural and forest land uses in perpetuity. Permitted activities on preserved land include farming, timbering, and any agricultural use within easement terms. Funds received by landowners from easement sales may be used for any purpose.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland program, administered at the county level. County-specific programs operate in Anne Arundel County, Baltimore County, Talbot County, Charles County, and other participating Maryland counties. In Baltimore County, property must be located in designated Agricultural Preservation Protection Areas. State MALPF applications are submitted through county administrators.
requirements_list: Property must contain prime farmland and/or woodland eligible for agricultural preservation
Applicant must own the farmland and/or woodland

For Anne Arundel County: parcel must have 50 acres or more of agricultural land with specific soils criteria and an active Soil and Water Quality Conservation Plan, OR a minimum of 25 acres of contiguous woodland with an active Forest Stewardship Plan
For Anne Arundel County: up-to-date Soil and Water Quality Plan and Forest Management Plan required
For Baltimore County: farm must be at least 20 acres if contiguous to a preserved farm
For Baltimore County: property must be located in Agricultural Preservation Protection Areas
For Baltimore County: must meet certain soil criteria
For Baltimore County: all property owners in title must sign the application
For Baltimore County: landowner must maintain a current soil and water conservation or forestry plan

If farm is owned by an entity, specific entity document requirements must be met (Articles of Organization/Incorporation, Operating/Partnership/Corporate Agreements, Certificate of Good Standing, roster of members/partners/officers)

For properties with 25+ acres of contiguous woodland: Forest Stewardship Plan performed by a Maryland-certified forester is required, created or updated within the last ten years, and must be followed according to its implementation schedule
For properties where required under Md. Code Ann. Agric. Section 8-801: current Nutrient Management Plan must be implemented prior to easement sale settlement

Property application documentation must include deeds, surveys, tax maps, aerial maps identifying structures, organizational documents (if entity-owned), assessments and taxation data, and forest or nutrient management plans if applicable
Easements are voluntary and permanent (in perpetuity)
Property owner must be willing to participate
Property owner must affirm no known environmental issues or reasons why property cannot be productively farmed
Once application is submitted, property cannot be subdivided, conveyed, altered in configuration, or encumbered by additional restrictions without MALPF approval
Lot selection cannot be changed after application submittal; applicant must withdraw and reapply in subsequent cycle to make changes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application processes vary by county and program level. For Talbot County MALPF: Complete the FY2027 application using the provided fillable PDF or Word document; submit physically to the Talbot County Planning and Zoning Office or by email to edeflaux@talbotcountymd.gov by April 1, 2026. If entity-owned, include a summary of entity document requirements. For Anne Arundel County: Submit applications during designated periods (November 1 and April 1 deadlines); funding is requested during the County Capital Budget cycle contingent on approval by the County Executive and County Council. For Baltimore County: Contact Land Preservation staff before filing at landpres@baltimorecountymd.gov or (410) 222-7432; applications must include landowner signatures from all owners in title, property and easement details, soil and forestry plans, and other required information; applications are submitted on an annual basis. For Charles County: Contact Charles County Planning Staff at 301-645-0692 or PGMadmin@CharlesCountyMD.Gov to learn more and complete an application. For State MALPF Program: Work with your County Program Administrator to complete a typed application. Once completed and signed by all property owners and County Administrator, provide one paper application in color with supporting documentation and email a copy with same supporting documentation (attachments in color) to the MALPF Administrator by July 1 of the application year. All applications require: deeds/surveys describing property; organizational documents if entity-owned; assessments and taxation data; tax map with property boundaries and withheld acreage clearly indicated; aerial map with identified structures; Forest Stewardship Plan if 25+ acres of contiguous woodland; and Annual Implementation Review Sheet for Nutrient Management Plan if available. Applications cannot be changed after submittal. Incomplete applications will be returned. All landowners of record and entity members must sign application. If there are life estate interests or right of first refusal, those parties must also sign. If applicant is contract purchaser, both contract purchaser and current owner must sign with copy of agreement of sale provided. Title review by Department of General Services may be required; if title issues exist or multiple tax parcels need combining, this may delay settlement. There is no guarantee an offer will be made or accepted.

structured_extraction.program_description: A complete property tax exemption from real property taxes on the dwelling house and surrounding yard for un-remarried surviving spouses of disabled veterans who qualified for the Disabled Veterans Exemption. This program is available statewide in Maryland, with specific administration at the county level including Calvert County.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Complete exemption from real property taxes on the dwelling house and surrounding yard. The exemption applies to the homestead property where the surviving spouse resides. There is no limit on the assessed value of the property. The exemption is granted for the duration that the surviving spouse remains unmarried and owns and occupies the property as a principal residence.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Un-remarried surviving spouses of disabled veterans whose deceased spouse qualified for the Disabled Veterans Exemption
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax exemption for principal dwelling house and surrounding yard; exemption covers all real property taxes owed on the homestead property
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; administered locally by county Treasurer's Offices and Assessors, including Calvert County. Application and eligibility determination handled through State Department of Assessments and Taxation and county-level offices.
requirements_list: Un-remarried surviving spouse (exemption is lost if remarried)
Deceased spouse qualified for and received the Disabled Veterans Exemption
Surviving spouse must own the property
Property must be the principal residence (primary dwelling) of the surviving spouse
Veteran must have been a resident of Maryland at time of death or disability determination
Property must be residential in nature
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation or their local county Assessor's office for application forms and instructions. In Calvert County, submit the Exemption for Surviving Spouses of a Disabled Veteran application along with required documentation (such as proof of the deceased veteran's Disabled Veterans Exemption status, marriage certificate, proof of current ownership, and proof of principal residence) to the Calvert County Treasurer's Office. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis throughout the year.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide Maryland program that helps homeowners of limited income keep their homes out of tax sale for at least three years and assists them in paying taxes owed on their principal residence. The program diversion diverts vulnerable homeowners from the tax sale process into an alternative loan program that minimizes their tax collection costs, helps them to pay their taxes, and allows them to remain in their homes. Enrollment is limited and eligibility does not guarantee enrollment. Priority enrollment is given to homeowners aged 60 or older, those receiving federal disability benefits (Social Security Disability Insurance or Supplemental Security Income), or those whose dwelling has been their principal residence for 10 years or more.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides an alternative loan program that helps homeowners pay their delinquent property taxes and provides protection against tax sale foreclosure for at least three years. The loan allows homeowners to remain in their homes. Applicants must demonstrate they can afford a monthly loan payment based on their total monthly expenses. The program minimizes tax collection costs for participating homeowners. Applications must be filed at least four weeks prior to the county's tax sale date to be considered prior to the sale, but applicants may apply during any phase of the tax sale process throughout the year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be filed at least four weeks prior to the county's tax sale date to be considered prior to the sale; however, applicants may apply during any phase of the tax sale process throughout the year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners of limited income whose principal residence has an assessed value not exceeding $300,000 and whose combined annual household income does not exceed $60,000, with total assets not exceeding $200,000 (excluding the dwelling value), who are at risk of having their home sold at tax sale and have delinquent property taxes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of back property taxes owed on the applicant's principal residence and protection against tax foreclosure sale. Funds help homeowners pay delinquent property taxes and provide a tax lien repayment plan.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland in all counties.
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner with a legal interest in the property
Dwelling must be the applicant homeowner's principal residence
Will reside in the property on July 1, 2025 and for more than 6 months thereafter
Assessed value of dwelling must not exceed $300,000
Combined annual household income for 2024 must not exceed $60,000
Total value of assets must not exceed $200,000 (not including the dwelling value)
Assets include but are not limited to other real property, investment/retirement accounts, and/or bank accounts
Must have limited income
Must currently owe county $7,000 or less (prequalification requirement)
Must be on county's tax sale list, have a lien sold in recent tax sale, be in tax sale foreclosure, or have real property taxes included in escrow but delinquent
Priority given to homeowners aged 60 or older
Priority given to those receiving federal disability benefits (SSDI or SSI)
Priority given to those whose dwelling has been their principal residence for 10 years or more
Enrollment is limited; eligibility does not guarantee enrollment
Must complete all sections of the application with supporting income documentation
Must provide copies of 2024 Federal Income Tax Return if filed
If receiving disability benefits, must include copy of current benefits statement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete the Homeowner Protection Program loan application form and submit it with all required supporting documents. Required documents include copies of 2024 wages and income documentation, Federal Income Tax Return (if filed), and proof of disability benefits (if applicable). Applicants must first answer prequalification questions to determine if they meet basic eligibility criteria including owing $7,000 or less, having 2024 household income of $60,000 or less, home assessment of $300,000 or less, and assets of $200,000 or less. Applicants should print clearly, complete all sections, and submit copies only (not originals) without stapling documents. Applications can be submitted to the State Tax Sale Ombudsman at the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation, 700 Pratt St., Suite 2600, Baltimore, Maryland 21202. Applications must be filed at least four weeks prior to the county's tax sale date to be considered prior to the sale, but applicants may apply during any phase of the tax sale process throughout the year. Applicants should contact the State Tax Sale Ombudsman for immediate assistance via email at sdat.taxsale@maryland.gov or phone at (410) 767-4994 or (833) 732-8411 toll free. Applicants may also apply online through the website at https://dat.maryland.gov/Pages/hpp.aspx (recommended for faster processing). The application may be subjected to an audit at any time, and applicants may be asked to submit additional verification or evidence of income to substantiate their application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state-administered tax credit program that reduces the real property tax bill on the primary residence of homeowners of all ages who qualify based on gross household income. The credit is applied when property taxes exceed a fixed percentage of the applicant's gross household income, effectively setting a limit on property taxes relative to income. The program is available statewide in Maryland and is administered by the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). Many counties, including Calvert County, Montgomery County, and Baltimore County, supplement the state credit with additional local credits. Homeowners age 70 and older may file up to three years retroactively for credits not previously claimed. St. Mary's County residents age 70 and over who receive the credit may also receive an additional credit up to the amount of the remaining tax bill (less the Bay Restoration Fund fee). The program has been available in Calvert County since July 1, 2006. A single application generally covers both state and applicable county supplemental credits.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a tax credit applied against the homeowner's annual real property tax bill on the principal residence. The credit amount is determined by comparing the homeowner's gross household income to the property tax bill. The program uses a maximum property assessment of $300,000 to compute the credit. Homeowners with combined gross household income not exceeding $60,000 and net worth (excluding home and qualified retirement accounts) not exceeding $200,000 are eligible. Property taxes on the home (based on no more than $300,000 of assessed value) must exceed a specified threshold relative to the applicant's income level. Credits approved by October 1 appear on the following tax bill; credits approved after October 1 are typically refunded by the county Finance Office. In some counties (e.g., Cecil County), credits approved after May 1 are refunded. Homeowners age 70 and older may file retroactively for up to three prior years of unclaimed credits. Some counties provide supplemental credits in addition to the state credit (Montgomery County, Baltimore County, Calvert County, Harford County, and others). A single application generally covers both the state credit and applicable county supplemental credits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1st each year (Baltimore County and some localities: September 1; Calvert County: September 1, often extended to October 31; Harford County: September 1)
structured_extraction.contact_name: State Department of Assessments and Taxation, Tax Credit Office
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners of all ages throughout Maryland who own or have a legal interest in their principal residence and whose combined gross household income does not exceed $60,000 and net worth does not exceed $200,000 (excluding the home and qualified retirement accounts). Heirs without their name on the deed may still qualify. Additional benefits available to seniors age 70 and older. St. Mary's County residents age 70 and over may receive additional credits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces the amount of real property taxes owed by the homeowner on their principal residence. Credits do not apply to metropolitan charges, portions of buildings used for business purposes, or taxes on excess land or other buildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland program. Applicant must live in the property as their principal residence for at least 6 months of the year, including July 1 (exceptions for recent home purchasers or those unable to reside due to health or special care needs). County-specific supplemental credits available in Calvert, Baltimore, Montgomery, Harford, and other counties. Calvert County program available since July 1, 2006.
requirements_list: Must own or have a legal interest in the property (heirs without their name on the deed may still qualify)

The dwelling must be the applicant's principal residence where they live at least six months of the year, including July 1 (exceptions for recent home purchasers or those unable to reside due to health or special care needs)
Combined gross household income cannot exceed $60,000
Net worth (excluding the value of the property for which the credit is sought and qualified retirement savings or Individual Retirement Accounts) must be less than $200,000
Property taxes on the home (based on no more than $300,000 of assessed value) must exceed the specified tax limit for the applicant's income level
Must file a new application every year by the applicable deadline (generally October 1; September 1 in Baltimore County and some other localities)
Homeowners age 70 and older may apply retroactively for up to three prior years of unclaimed credits
For Calvert County applicants: must submit HTC-60 application form and include a copy of the federal income tax return; application deadline typically September 1, often extended to October 31
For Harford County applicants: deadline is typically September 1
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Homeowners can apply online at onestop.md.gov by selecting the Department of Assessments and Taxation, or download a paper application at dat.maryland.gov. First-time applicants may obtain the application from the local Assessment Office or county Finance/Treasurer's Office. Once approved, applicants typically receive renewal applications by mail annually. A single application generally covers both the state credit and applicable county supplemental credits (e.g., Montgomery County Supplemental Homeowners Property Tax Credit and Senior Tax Credit, Calvert County HTC-60, or Baltimore County local supplement, or Harford County supplement). Submit completed application by October 1 (or September 1 in Baltimore County, Harford County, and some other localities; Calvert County deadline often extended to October 31). For questions, email sdat.homeowners@maryland.gov or call 410-767-5900 (statewide), 800-944-7403 (Montgomery County/Somerset County), or 410-767-4433 (Baltimore County/City of Salisbury). Applicants can check if they are already receiving the credit by looking up their home at sdat.dat.maryland.gov/RealProperty. If denied, applicants may file an appeal. Credits approved by October 1 appear on the following tax bill; credits approved after October 1 are generally refunded by the county Finance Office. Some counties (e.g., Cecil County) issue refunds for credits approved after May 1.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state program providing six financing capabilities — loans, grants, and direct assistance — to businesses, non-profits, and local jurisdictions for economic development projects located in Priority Funding Areas. The program encourages development through various forms of financial support across eligible industries statewide, as authorized under the 1997 Priority Funding Areas Act.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Six financing capabilities: Significant Strategic Economic Development Opportunities (loans up to $10 million or 20% of fund balance); Local Economic Development Opportunity (loans up to $5 million, conditional loans and grants up to $2 million); Direct Assistance to Local Jurisdictions (up to $3 million for land acquisition, infrastructure improvements, and feasibility studies); Regional or Local Revolving Loan Fund (grants up to $250,000 annually with matching requirement); Special Purposes Loan (for brownfield revitalization, seafood and aquaculture, animal waste, arts and entertainment, and child care); Economic Development Opportunities Fund/Sunny Day Fund (assistance requires minimum capital investment of five times the assistance amount). Assistance generally cannot exceed 70% of total project costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, non-profits, and local jurisdictions with economic development projects located in Priority Funding Areas in eligible industries
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fixed asset financing, land acquisition, infrastructure improvements, leasehold improvements, feasibility studies, economic development plans, highways, sewer and water construction, and related growth infrastructure
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area as designated under the 1997 Priority Funding Areas Act; available statewide
requirements_list: Project must be located in a Priority Funding Area
Must be in an eligible industry sector
Assistance cannot exceed 70% of total project costs with some exceptions
For local economic development opportunities, local jurisdiction must sponsor and participate with at least 10% of state assistance
For Sunny Day Fund, applicants must have strong balance sheet and be credit worthy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Economic Development Corporation or Maryland Department of Commerce for information on applying to specific MEDAAF programs

structured_extraction.program_name: State Lottery Terminal (SLoT) Fund / Small, Minority & Women-Owned Business Account - Video Lottery Terminal Fund (VLT)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state program that uses proceeds from video lottery terminals (1.5% of VLT proceeds) to assist small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses. At least 50% of allocations are reserved for businesses located within 10 miles of Maryland's casinos, with the remaining 50% available to eligible businesses statewide. The program provides below-market-rate loans for business and commercial real estate acquisition, expansion, leasehold improvements, equipment, and working capital needs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Commerce / Local County Economic Development Offices
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides below-market-rate loans between $10,000 and $500,000 to targeted small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses. At least 50% of allocations go to businesses within 10 miles of Maryland's casinos (Hollywood Casino Perryville in Cecil County, Ocean Downs in Worcester County, Maryland Live! in Anne Arundel County, Rocky Gap Casino in Allegany County, and Horseshoe Casino in Baltimore City). The remaining 50% is available to eligible businesses located throughout Maryland. Funds may be used for business and commercial real estate acquisition and expansion, leasehold improvements, equipment, and working capital.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses, with priority for those located in targeted areas within 10 miles of Maryland's casinos.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business and commercial real estate acquisition and expansion, leasehold improvements, equipment, and working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: At least 50% of funds reserved for businesses within 10 miles of Maryland's casinos (Hollywood Casino Perryville, Ocean Downs, Maryland Live!, Rocky Gap Casino, and Horseshoe Casino); remaining 50% available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a small, minority, women, or veteran-owned business
Loans range from $10,000 to $500,000
Priority given to businesses located within 10 miles of a Maryland casino
Located in targeted area surrounding a Maryland casino for priority consideration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through TCCWMD's lending program Summit Financing Solutions, or contact the local county Office of Economic Development (e.g., Cecil County Office of Economic Development) for more information and to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot project by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) in partnership with the Maryland Department of Aging that provides deferred loans at zero percent interest to help seniors make accessibility-related improvements to their homes. Improvements may include installation of grab bars and railings, widening doorways, installation of wheelchair ramps, and bathroom modifications to help older people remain independent in their homes. The program is available statewide, with local administration in counties such as Baltimore County and St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Deferred loans at zero percent interest for a term of 30 years. Loans are up to 85 percent of the property value. All closing costs are included in the loan. Loans must be repaid upon sale, transfer, or refinancing of the property. Income eligibility thresholds include: one person household income less than $45,976 (or $6,079/month); two-person household less than $52,544 (or $6,950/month); three-person household less than $59,112.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior homeowners age 55 or older who own and occupy their home and need accessibility improvements to maintain independence. Available to eligible residents statewide, including Baltimore County and St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessibility-related home improvements including installation of grab bars and railings, widening of doorways, installation of wheelchair ramps, bathroom modifications, and similar accessibility improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Local administration available in Baltimore County (contact: 410-887-2594) and St. Mary's County, among others.
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner who owns and occupies the home to be renovated
At least one resident of the home must be age 55 or older
The home must be structurally sound and free of health and safety hazards
No outstanding federal or state tax liens, open bankruptcy, or foreclosure
Household income must be less than $45,976 for one person, less than $52,544 for two people, or less than $59,112 for three people
If senior resides in a relative's home, eligibility is based on owner's income and considered case-by-case
For Baltimore County: must be a Baltimore County resident
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Households are recommended to start with a free in-home comprehensive assessment to identify needed improvements and enroll in programs best suited to their situation. For Baltimore County residents, call Senior Information and Assistance at 410-887-2594 to apply. For all other areas, contact the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development at DHCD.SpecialLoans@maryland.gov or 301-429-7409.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (BRNI) program aims to demonstrate how strategic investment in local housing and businesses can lead to healthy, sustainable communities with a growing tax base and enhanced quality of life. The program focuses on areas where modest investment and a coordinated strategy will have an appreciable neighborhood revitalization impact, targeting Sustainable Community Areas in Baltimore City and the inner beltway of Baltimore and Anne Arundel counties.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fundingfor communitydevelopmentorganizationswith approvedstrategicneighborhoodrevitalizationplanstosupport projectsincludingdownpaymentassistance,propertyacquisitionandrehabilitation,energyefficiencyimprovements,mixed-usedevelopment,communityopenspaceandpublicinfrastructuredevelopment,workforcedevelopment,strategicdemolition,andoperatingcostsfor communityenhancementprojects.Assistancemayalsoinclducetechnicalassistanceand information.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Organizations with an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan located in Sustainable Community Areas in Baltimore City and inner beltway of Baltimore and Anne Arundel counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance to attract home buyers, acquisition or rehabilitation of vacant or blighted properties, improvement of existing residential and business properties, energy efficiency through weatherization and energy retrofits, mixed-use projects combining housing retail and office space, community open space or public infrastructure development, workforce and employment development programs, strategic demolition, and operating costs for community enhancement projects.
