structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative (BVRI) (formerly Project C.O.R.E.)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides capital to Baltimore City, Maryland Stadium Authority, and community-based development organizations to redevelop vacant properties through acquisition, stabilization, renovation, and demolition activities, focusing on whole block outcomes where every property on a block has a productive use. Originally launched as Project C.O.R.E. (Creating Opportunities for Renewal and Enterprise), a partnership between the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, the Maryland Stadium Authority, and the Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development, the program demolishes vacant and blighted buildings to catalyze redevelopment, reinvestment, and stabilization in Baltimore City neighborhoods. The program is part of Reinvest Baltimore, a coordinated effort established by Governor Moore's Executive Order on October 1, 2024, to move at least 5,000 vacant properties into homeownership or other positive outcomes over five years, with the state deploying $50 million annually through BVRI funding.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and loans to finance acquisition, stabilization, and renovation of vacant buildings; acquisition and aggregation of vacant lots for new infill housing construction, mixed-use projects, and community-managed open space; urgent demolition of properties or vacant buildings for near-term redevelopment projects; and other predevelopment activities including architectural, engineering, site infrastructure, and site development for renovation and new construction projects. FY27 BVRI funds are provided as partially forgivable subordinate loans from Maryland Community Investment Corporation (MCIC), with forgiveness based on Net Sale/Refinance Proceeds and project appraisal gap. Loans are available for acquisition and pre-development soft costs, construction financing gaps, and closeout appraisal gap coverage. Grant funds may fill the gap between total development costs and sale prices. The State has committed to invest $75 million and the City has committed to contribute $18.5 million over four years, with the State also committing to leverage an estimated $600 million through existing programs to encourage new investment in challenged communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based development organizations (CDOs) that operate to improve the physical, economic, or social environment of their geographic areas of operation in Baltimore City with a track record of completing the rehabilitation of vacant property and/or infill new construction projects. CDOs may have sub-recipients including for-profit and non-profit development partners. Also available to local governments and property owners or redevelopers seeking to rehabilitate and redevelop properties in challenged communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, stabilization, and renovation of vacant buildings, prioritizing those with a city-issued vacant building notice (VBN), with emphasis on homeownership outcomes. Acquisition and aggregation of vacant lots for new infill housing construction, mixed-use projects, and community-managed open space. Urgent demolition of properties that pose a community health risk or when demolition furthers a near-term redevelopment project. Architectural, engineering, site infrastructure, and site development. Stabilization of selected properties for future rehabilitation and redevelopment. Other predevelopment activities for renovation and new construction projects. Renovation and new construction loans or lines of credit to be repaid through home sales or refinance into permanent financing for rental projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Activities must be located in Sustainable Community Areas in Baltimore City. Special consideration given to projects in the Baltimore City Vacancy Reduction Priority Geographies (VRPGs), which includes the Impact Investment Areas. Program focuses on half- and whole-blocks of blight to maximize neighborhood impact. Eligible target areas should include contiguous clusters of whole blocks where the organization can directly abate or facilitate the abatement of all vacant property, particularly buildings with Vacant Building Notices. Each cluster should be approximately 5 blocks by 5 blocks and be walkable. Additional consideration given to projects in ENOUGH (Engaging Neighborhoods, Organizations, Unions, Governments and Households) areas and Just Communities.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit community development organization (CDO) with a track record of completing the rehabilitation of vacant property and/or infill new construction projects
Applicant's organizational mission must include community development work and a service area in Baltimore City
Project must be located in a cluster of contiguous blocks within Sustainable Community Areas
Applicant must demonstrate capacity and a plan to address all vacant property over time
Funds will primarily support activities that accelerate remediation of vacant buildings with city-issued Vacant Building Notices
Applicant must submit completed property pipeline spreadsheet listing all properties expected to be redeveloped; applications without completed spreadsheet will not be accepted
If funded, CDOs may be required to provide a government resolution, corporate board resolution, and charitable registration

All CDO applicants must submit By-Laws, Articles of Incorporation, Board Roster, Annual Report, IRS Letter of Determination, Financial Audit, Operating Budget, Profit & Loss Statement, Balance Sheet, and signed Public Disclosure Authorization
Applicants must demonstrate the strategy builds from community strengths and assets and achieves whole block outcomes where every property on a block has a productive use
For residential rehabilitation projects, applicants must describe their sales strategy for properties acquired, renovated, and resold, or describe experience financing and managing rental properties
For infill residential construction and mixed-use projects, applicants must provide evidence of site control status and sources and uses budgets
For modular infill projects, applicants must provide site assessment for modular or off-site construction feasibility and site plans or building designs if developed
For green space and placemaking projects, applicants must demonstrate site control, right of entry, activation and use plans, and long-term stewardship plans
Letters of support required from each development partner that will be a sub-recipient of BVRI funding
Applications must be submitted exclusively through Survey123 online portal; paper applications not accepted
All required documents must be included with application before submission
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit applications exclusively through the Survey123 online portal; paper applications are not accepted. The application is automatically saved in the browser and does not require account creation. Applications including all necessary attachments must be submitted by 11:59 PM on April 1, 2026. Training and resources are available to assist with the application process, including an application guide, template, training presentation slides, and property pipeline worksheets. Application training is offered via webinar with training recording and step-by-step instructions posted on the BVRI website. A 1-on-1 scheduling link is available to discuss questions specific to applicant organizations. DHCD will be available for application support throughout the application period. The application includes key components: (1) Identified Target Area - applicants create a simple map showing target area within their organization's existing service area and justify selection based on geographic boundaries, organizational assets, and community strengths; (2) Vacant Revitalization Strategy - narrative description of vacancy reduction strategy including blocks to begin with, remediation strategies and prioritization, and attainable outcomes for first 6 months; (3) Vacant Properties Pipeline List - completion of template with all properties that could be part of vacant revitalization strategy, including property characteristics, proposed remediation strategies, expected cost, and expected uses; (4) Additional Project Types - applications may include residential infill new construction, modular infill, commercial/mixed use, and open space projects with required documentation including current project status, sources and uses budgets, applicant and partner experience, support letters, and sales/rental strategy. During application review, review teams may make visits and/or hold meetings with applicants. Applicants may be contacted for follow-up discussions prior to awards. All capital projects receiving State financial assistance are subject to the Maryland Historical Trust Act, which requires consideration of effect on historic resources; the Department has a Programmatic Agreement with the Maryland Historical Trust and initiates historic preservation compliance reviews after awards are made. Application scoring includes: Organization Experience and Development Capacity (30 points), Whole-Block Redevelopment Strategy and Program Alignment (30 points), Vacant Property Pipeline and Production Readiness (25 points), Budget and Financing (15 points). Projects located in ENOUGH and Just Communities areas receive up to 10 bonus points each.

structured_extraction.program_description: An innovative financing program operated by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that offers low interest rate loans to homeowners to improve the energy efficiency and comfort of their homes. The program supports replacement and upgrading of appliances, heating, cooling and ventilation systems, insulation, air sealing, and whole house envelope improvements. Borrowers can save on utility bills through these improvements while working with approved weatherization and energy efficiency professionals whose qualifications have been reviewed by DHCD.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Unsecured loan with a 6.99% APR. Up to $30,000 in financing available for energy efficiency measures with a term of up to 10 years. Minimum loan amount is $5,000. The loan is based on verification of credit and ability to pay. Borrowers must have a credit score of 640 or greater and a debt-to-income ratio not exceeding 50%. Financing for solar photovoltaic installation is capped at a 1:1 match to the cost of energy efficiency measures. Up to 25% of the cost of energy measures can be used for health and safety improvements necessary for the energy improvements. Homeowners may choose their weatherization and energy efficiency professionals from a list of eligible providers whose qualifications have been reviewed by DHCD.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners seeking financing for home energy efficiency improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements including insulation and air sealing, ENERGY STAR heating and cooling systems, ENERGY STAR hot water heating equipment, ENERGY STAR appliances and windows and doors, lighting and controls, programmable and smart thermostats, ceiling fans and ventilation fans, geothermal heat pumps, solar photovoltaic installation, health and safety costs related to energy improvements, replacement and upgrading of appliances and HVAC systems, whole house envelope improvements, and other improvements identified in a certified energy audit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; available to Maryland homeowners only.
requirements_list: Maryland homeowner status
Credit score of 640 or greater
Debt-to-income ratio does not exceed 50%
Projects or upgrades cannot be already purchased or already completed
Use of approved providers from eligible provider list
Current employment information (employer name, address, and contact phone number)
Work history documentation (if employed at current job for less than 2 years, include previous employer contact information)
Contractor details (name, address, email, and phone number of contractor performing upgrades)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit the online BeSMART Loan Application. 2. Email all required income documentation to get pre-approved on a financial basis. 3. Submit project specifications including scope of work, contractor estimates, and ENERGY STAR equipment specifications. 4. Complete loan documents by signing and notarizing the loan documents provided by DHCD. 5. Start your project with an initial draw of funds. 6. Complete your project and submit photos and a Certificate of Completion for the final draw. Homeowners select qualified professionals from an approved provider list.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Business Boost Microgrant provides grants ranging from $20,000 to $50,000 to support small businesses seeking to expand their business or establish a new location. Funded through the Neighborhood BusinessWorks program, it prioritizes home-based businesses establishing their first commercial location outside the home. Funding prioritizes businesses in Sustainable Communities areas, innovative businesses, minority-owned enterprises, and businesses that leverage partnerships with educational institutions. Up to $2,000,000 in total funding is available.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $20,000 to $50,000 available to eligible small businesses. Applicants must provide a matching contribution equal to or greater than the grant request amount. Funds can be used towards capital and operating expenses that support revenue growth from September 23, 2024, through March 23, 2025, including salary, rent, utilities, product advertising, product development, commercial real estate acquisition, and professional services. Only new expenses are eligible; existing expenses such as current rent or payroll cannot be counted. Up to $2,000,000 in total funding is available across all awards.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Monday, October 14, 2024, at 5 PM EST. NOTE: The round may close sooner if grant requests exceed available funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit small businesses located in Sustainable Communities areas with greater than 2 and 50 or fewer full-time equivalent employees (as of September 23, 2024) and annual revenue between $50,000 and $1 million. Also open to new and expanding small businesses establishing a presence in designated Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital and operating expenses that support revenue growth from September 23, 2024, through March 23, 2025. Eligible uses include salary, rent, utilities, product advertising, product development, commercial real estate acquisition, and professional services. Only new expenses are eligible; existing expenses such as current rent or payroll cannot be counted. Funds can support increased rent, increased payroll for hiring new employees, new equipment, and marketing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in a designated Sustainable Communities area. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper at https://portal.dhcd.state.md.us/GIS/revitalize/index.html to verify eligibility by entering your business address.

Be located in a Sustainable Communities area

Be located at an eligible location in Maryland
Have greater than 2 employees and 50 or fewer employees (full-time equivalent) as of September 23, 2024

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online through the DHCD Application Portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/NBWOZGrant/account/login. All applicants create an account to initiate an application, make updates, check application status, and receive communications. Applicants must provide a brief description of their organization, answer questions about the organization, complete a budget table on how grant funds and matching contribution will be used, and submit required supporting documents. Applications are evaluated based on meeting eligibility requirements and review of business financials. Priority of funding is based on: (1) location of the business, (2) impact of the business's expansion including new employees to be hired, capital investment, and additional square footage, (3) presentation of the business's financials and supporting documents, and (4) priority impact attributes including innovative businesses, businesses in growing industries, businesses focused on regional strengths, businesses leveraging partnerships with educational institutions, and minority-owned enterprises. Only fully completed applications will be considered for funding. Award announcements will be made on a rolling basis during December 2024 to January 2025. Grant awards are expected to be paid in February-March 2025. Awardees must submit a final report by March 31, 2026, and will be contacted nine months after receiving funds to complete a questionnaire and provide a one-page summary of fund use and impact.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides funding to strengthen Maryland's communities by expanding affordable housing opportunities, creating jobs, stabilizing neighborhoods, and improving overall quality of life. Funded projects must benefit low- and moderate-income persons, eliminate slum and blight, or meet an urgent community need. Eligible projects include housing, public facilities like water/sewer systems and community centers, and economic development initiatives.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Congress allocates funds to the Community Development Block Grant Program annually. The federal government distributes approximately 30% of the total federal allocation to states and small cities. Maryland administers these funds as grants to non-entitlement counties, cities, and towns. For State Fiscal Year 2026, the State received $7,416,560, allocated as follows: State Administration (2% + $100,000) = $248,331; Technical Assistance (1%) = $74,165; Community Development (82% - $100,000) = $6,000,000; Special Projects (15%) = $1,094,064. The state must cumulatively use at least 70% of its allocation to benefit persons of low and moderate income over a three-year period. Funds are provided primarily as gap funding for projects selected by jurisdictions. Awards are made through two categories: Community Development (awarded annually through competition) and Special Projects (awarded on a first-come, first-serve basis). Throughout the year, any funds from previous years not awarded or other funds that become available will be awarded as needed under Special Projects or through the next competitive funding round.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Community Development applications accepted once each year; Special Projects applications accepted at any time after written approval
structured_extraction.program_audience: Units of general local government in non-entitlement counties with a population of less than 200,000 and non-entitlement cities and towns with a population of less than 50,000. Multiple jurisdictions may jointly apply. Sub-recipients can be public or private non-profit entities, government agencies, for-profit businesses in good standing, Community Based Development Organizations (CBDOs) certified by the CDBG Program for new housing construction, and Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) certified by the State HOME Program for new housing construction.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of real property; acquisition, construction, reconstruction, or installation of public works facilities; code enforcement in deteriorating areas; clearance, demolition, removal, reconstruction, and rehabilitation of buildings; removal of architectural barriers for elderly or handicapped persons; provision of new or quantifiable increase in public services; planning; housing projects including single-family rehabilitation, new rental housing construction, and acquisition-renovation-resale programs; public facilities such as water and sewer systems, streets, childcare centers, senior centers, community centers, and shelters; economic development projects; assistance to neighborhood-based non-profit organizations and local development corporations; energy conservation projects; and direct assistance to facilitate homeownership.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Non-entitlement counties (those with population under 200,000) and non-entitlement cities and towns with populations under 50,000. Ineligible entitlement areas include Anne Arundel County, Baltimore County, Harford County, Howard County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, and the municipalities of Annapolis, Baltimore, Bowie, Cumberland, Frederick, Gaithersburg, Hagerstown, and Salisbury. Baltimore City is not eligible. Projects must be located in a Maryland Priority Funding Area, except for public services; single family housing rehabilitation; acquisition, renovation and sale of existing houses; downpayment assistance; or where exceptions have been granted. Eligible jurisdictions are listed in the Eligible Jurisdictions document.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an eligible non-entitlement jurisdiction: municipal government with population under 50,000 OR county government with population less than 200,000 (excluding HUD entitlement jurisdictions)

Project must meet one of the three national objectives: benefit persons of low and moderate income, eliminate slum and blight, or meet an urgent need that is an immediate threat to community health, safety, or welfare
Proposed activities must be eligible under Title I of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974, as amended (42 U.S.C. § 5305)
Proposed subrecipient or business must be eligible
Project must be located in a Maryland Priority Funding Area with noted exceptions
Over a three-year period, the state must cumulatively use at least 70% of its allocation to benefit persons of low and moderate income
For projects benefiting an entire town/city or primarily residential area through area benefit activities, the area must have low and moderate income population of 51% or greater
For housing activities, households must be qualified based on family size and income using HUD income limits
For job creation or retention activities, at least 51% of created or retained jobs must be held by low and moderate income persons
Single Audit required if grantee spends more than $750,000 of federal funds in a single fiscal year
Construction projects with minimum $200,000 of CDBG and other HUD funding must comply with Section 3 requirements (25% of labor hours by Section 3 workers, minimum 5% by Targeted Section 3 workers)

Build America, Buy America (BABA) requirements apply to infrastructure projects: all iron, steel, manufactured products and construction materials must be produced in United States (with exceptions for projects under $250,000 or housing rehabilitation under $250,000 per house)
Environmental review must be completed prior to initiation of project activities; no activities to begin until Release of Funds issued
Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity compliance required; grantees must comply with non-discrimination laws and regulations
Conflict of interest restrictions apply; grantees must adopt written conflict of interest policy
For housing rehabilitation programs, maximum of $40,000 provided as grant per house
For acquisition, renovation and resale programs, maximum of $200,000 CDBG funds per house
For construction or substantial rehabilitation of buildings with more than 4 rental housing units, broadband infrastructure must be installed
Generators with minimum capacity to power lighting in common areas required for multi-family rental housing and government facilities
Housing rehabilitation programs only accepted from county governments with limited exceptions
Rents for rental properties must be affordable and remain affordable for defined term (10-20 years based on CDBG funding amount)
For homeownership financial assistance, properties must have lien placed (5-10 years based on assistance amount)
Homeownership requirements: no subprime or adjustable rate mortgages, fixed rate minimum 30 years, minimum 8 hours HUD-approved housing counseling required
Buildings for general conduct of government are ineligible; exceptions for ADA improvements to public buildings
Eligible non-profit organizations must have organizational by-laws and mission statements clearly stating they primarily serve low and moderate income persons or specific eligible populations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The State notifies eligible localities of fund availability and conducts training sessions on application development. Community Development applications are accepted once per year through a competitive process. The State awards funds for Community Development category through annual competition based on rating criteria. Special Projects and Planning applications can be submitted at any time throughout the year after receiving written approval from CDBG program staff. For projects meeting the national objective of urgent need, applicants must contact CDBG program staff first to determine if their proposed project qualifies; if approved, supplemental application pages must be completed. Grantees must submit a Citizen Participation Plan, conduct public hearings, and obtain local resolution prior to funding. Upon funding approval, grantees are required to execute either a Subrecipient Agreement or Jobs Agreement with specific entities.
