structured_extraction.program_description: A program that awards state tax credit allocations to IRS-designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations to use as incentives for attracting charitable contributions from individuals and businesses to benefit local community projects and services. Donors who contribute $500 or more to approved projects receive tax credits equal to 50 percent of their contribution value, supporting activities such as education, housing, job training, arts, and economic development.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Donors who contribute $500 or more to a qualified nonprofit organization's approved project receive tax credits equal to 50 percent of the value of their cash, goods, or real property contribution. These credits can be used against Maryland state income taxes owed in the year the contribution was made and are in addition to federal and state charitable deductions. The CITC program awards up to $1.75 million in total state income tax credits annually. Organizations can request a maximum of $50,000 in tax credits per award. Credits must be used during the 24-month award contract period. Organizations must raise double the amount of tax credits requested to fund their projects (for example, a $50,000 credit request requires $100,000 in donations). Credits provide both operating and capital support for programs and services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY26 CITC application round opens May 19, 2025 and closes on June 19, 2025, at 5:00 PM (EDT)
structured_extraction.program_audience: IRS designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations seeking tax credit allocations to fund community projects, and individuals and businesses interested in making charitable donations to benefit local community projects and services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects can be capital and/or operating expenses for activities including: education and youth services, housing and community development, job and self-sufficiency training, neighborhood and business district enhancement, arts, culture and historic preservation, economic development and tourism promotion, technical assistance and capacity building, and services for at-risk populations. Eligible budget line items include staff costs, rent, utilities, program supplies, training, travel, construction soft costs such as planning, design, engineering, and permitting, as well as direct construction expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (PFA). For capital projects, the project site must be within a PFA boundary. For operating projects, organizations must document that clients served reside within a PFA and provide a summary of the total numbers and percentage of clients residing within designated PFA areas.
requirements_list: Applicant organization must be IRS designated as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit with current IRS determination letter
Organization must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Organization must be registered as a charity with the Maryland Secretary of State or hold an exemption letter (for religious entities)
Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (PFA)
For capital projects, organization must document site control via deed, executed lease with owner's permission to alter property, or evidence of real estate settlement and title
Donors must contribute a minimum of $500 to be eligible for tax credits
Individual donors must be natural persons or fiduciaries with personal tax liability in Maryland
Business donors must conduct a trade or business in Maryland and be subject to state income tax, public service company franchise tax, or insurance premiums tax
Donors must obtain a Donor Acknowledgement Form from the nonprofit
Organizations with affiliate status must provide documentation that the IRS recognizes the organization under the umbrella organization's tax identification number
Religious organizations claiming exemption must provide documentation from the Maryland Secretary of State
Applications must include current Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws with all amendments
Applications must include current list of Board of Directors and Officers
Applications must include Priority Funding Area (PFA) map(s) showing each address where project work will occur or services will be delivered
For the FY26 award, the contract period runs from January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2027
All project work must begin on or after January 1, 2026 and conclude by December 31, 2027
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations must first register in the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's IGX Project Portal. New users should click 'New User? Register Here' and indicate interest in the FY26 CITC application round (registration approval takes up to 72 hours). Organizations must ensure their organization information and all required legal documents are uploaded and current on their Profile before creating an application. The FY26 CITC application round opens on May 19, 2025 and closes on June 19, 2025 at 5:00 PM. Applications must be submitted online through the Project Portal and must include all required supporting documents in PDF format: Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, IRS 501(c)(3) Determination Letter, current Board of Directors and Officers list, Charitable Registration Letter or Exemption Letter from Maryland Secretary of State, current SDAT Good Standing status screenshot, Executed Corporate Resolution/Authorized Officers template, and Priority Funding Area (PFA) map(s) for each project address. Capital project applications must also include evidence of site control. Award notifications are expected to be announced in Fall 2025. Upon award, organizations may announce that tax credits will be available to donors starting January 1, 2026. Organizations must submit electronic Tax Credit Certification Requests within 30 days of receiving each donation. Semi-annual reports are required on July 10 and January 10 throughout the award period, with a final report due January 10, 2028. Organizations must maintain charitable registration and good standing status throughout the award period and retain records for seven years following award completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Legacy program provides local governments and community development organizations with funding for essential projects aimed at strengthening communities. Projects include business retention and attraction, homeownership encouragement, and commercial revitalization activities in designated Sustainable Communities or in Opportunity Zones in eligible counties. The program supports reinvestment and revitalization in older communities to stabilize neighborhoods, reverse economic or physical decline, and encourage sustainable growth.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and loans are provided to support revitalization projects in Sustainable Communities or in Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties. Projects can include mixed-use development (residential, commercial, and open space), business retention, expansion and attraction initiatives, streetscape improvements, homeownership and home rehabilitation programs, residential and commercial facade improvements, real estate acquisition including land banking, strategic demolition, and infrastructure improvements. For example, the City of Salisbury received $500,000 toward a Town-Center infill development project including mixed-use residential apartments, retail spaces, streetscaping, public utilities improvements, and a public parking garage. The FY27 proposed funding includes support for residential facade improvements in Lonaconing and Westernport in Allegany County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, community development organizations such as county councils, community development corporations, main street organizations, downtown partnerships, and groups of local governments sharing common goals. Also open to non-profit organizations pursuing revitalization in designated Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mixed-use development with residential, commercial, and open space components; business retention, expansion, and attraction initiatives; streetscape improvements; homeownership and home rehabilitation programs; residential and commercial facade improvements; real estate acquisition including land banking; strategic demolition; site development; construction and building renovations (including roofs, windows, ceilings, floors, and kitchen updates); infrastructure improvements; public utilities improvements; and parking facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in designated Sustainable Communities or in Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties. Applicants can use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility.
requirements_list: Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities or Opportunity Zones in eligible counties (Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico)
Projects should capitalize on community strengths while addressing revitalization challenges
Projects should help achieve a local government's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Projects should aim to stabilize a community, reverse decline, or encourage sustainable growth
Project must be located in a designated Sustainable Community or qualifying Opportunity Zone
Project must support economic development and community revitalization
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's State Revitalization Programs process. For information on how to apply, refer to the State Revitalization Programs webpage. Contact the Economic Development Corporation and speak with a Business Development Specialist for additional guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Schools Rental Assistance Program provides emergency financial assistance to families and students enrolled in designated Community Schools across participating Maryland jurisdictions who are at risk of eviction, losing housing, or experiencing homelessness. The program helps eligible renters cover past due rent and utility bills, moving costs and deposits for a new rental home, and future rent and utility costs related to housing instability. It operates in multiple counties including Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's, Washington, and Wicomico. Funding is administered at the local level, with some jurisdictions partnering with organizations such as Cornerstone Franciscan Ministries (Baltimore County) and Housing Initiative Partnership (Montgomery County). Funding availability varies by jurisdiction, with most areas on a waitlist or interest-only basis.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Emergency financial assistance is provided directly to eligible families to prevent or address housing loss. Covered expenses include: past due rent or utility bills including late fees and court fees related to eviction; moving costs and deposits needed to rent a new home such as security deposit, first month's rent, and utility deposit; and future rent and utility assistance related to housing instability. Households may receive up to 3 months of prospective rent and/or utility assistance at a time, with recertification required after 3 months to determine continued eligibility. The maximum length of assistance a household can receive is 15 months. Eligible households are able to receive repeat assistance, contingent on availability of program funds and qualifying circumstances. Assistance is provided based on need and availability of funds, per the local providers. Funding is administered locally, with most jurisdictions currently on a waitlist-only or interest-only basis as funding is nearly exhausted.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Most jurisdictions are on a waitlist only or interest only basis; Montgomery County is currently accepting applications.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 1-800-485-0041 (Press 3, Anne Arundel); 410-538-2830 (Cornerstone Franciscan Ministries, Baltimore County); 410-887-8463 (Coordinated Entry, Baltimore County); 301-916-5946 (Housing Initiative Partnership, Montgomery County)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families and students enrolled in designated Community Schools in participating jurisdictions who are renting their homes and are at risk of eviction, at risk of losing housing, or already experiencing homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Past due rent or utility bills including late fees and court fees related to eviction; moving costs and deposits needed to rent a new home such as security deposit, first month's rent, and utility deposit; future rent and utility assistance related to housing instability; relocation costs such as security deposits and application fees for those living place-to-place or in emergency shelters; water and other utilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program operates in Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Frederick County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Washington County, and Wicomico County. Eligibility is limited to families enrolled in designated Community Schools within each participating jurisdiction. Assistance can only be provided to households that have a student enrolled in a community school in the county where they are requesting assistance. Funding availability varies by jurisdiction.
requirements_list: At least one student in the household must be enrolled in a designated Community School in a participating jurisdiction
Be experiencing homelessness or at risk of housing instability (e.g., past due utility or rent notice, eviction notice, unsafe or unhealthy living conditions)
Be responsible for paying rent or utilities in a qualifying rental unit
Be renting your home or trying to rent a new home (homeowners are not eligible)
Proof of citizenship is not required; eligibility is based on renter status and community school enrollment, not immigration status
Voucher holders and those living in subsidized units may apply and will receive assistance for the portion of rent they legally owe as the tenant
Subletting arrangements eligible as long as the lease holder can verify the subletting arrangement or a history of rent payments is shown
Expired leases eligible as long as landlord can verify continued occupancy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local jurisdiction program administrator or local agency supporting your county. Applications can be obtained from the local agency supporting your county via online or paper copy. Required documents include proof of student's community school enrollment, proof of rental agreement, and invoice or proof of missed rent or utility payments. In Anne Arundel County, submit an interest form via Google Form or contact Natali Landaverde at 1-800-485-0041 (Press 3). In Baltimore County, contact Cornerstone Franciscan Ministries at 410-538-2830 or email participantservices@cfmins.org, or call Coordinated Entry at 410-887-8463 option 1 (Mon-Fri, 8:30 a.m. to 7 p.m.). In Montgomery County, contact Housing Initiative Partnership at 301-916-5946. Most jurisdictions are currently on a waitlist-only or interest-only basis. Previously submitted applications continue to be reviewed in the order received.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to support activities and programs conducted by Community Action Agencies or other non-profit organizations to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization. Funds are distributed to seventeen designated Community Action Agencies across Maryland to offer services that help low-income individuals and families achieve self-sufficiency in areas such as employment, education, housing, nutrition, emergency services, and health. Funds may also be used to provide training and technical assistance and to support coordination and communication among Community Action Agencies.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to Community Action Agencies and non-profit organizations to support activities and programs that eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization. The program distributes 90% of Maryland's allocated funds to designated Community Action Agencies, with the remaining 5% used for discretionary funding to support activities that fight poverty. Funding can also support training, technical assistance, and coordination among agencies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland's designated Community Action Agencies, non-profit organizations, and local government units that serve low-income individuals and families working on poverty elimination and community revitalization.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Activities and programs to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization; direct services for low-income individuals in areas of employment, education, housing, nutrition, emergency services, and health; training; technical assistance; coordination and communication among Community Action Agencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland
requirements_list: Services must benefit individuals and households with incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines.
Community Action Agencies must have a specific board composition: one-third public officials, one-third representatives of low-income persons, and one-third from community groups.
Applicants for discretionary funds must propose a program with measurable outcomes for self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Check the program's webpage for information about current and future application opportunities. The FY25 application round has closed.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps local governments, community organizations, non-profits, and anchor institutions create or upgrade public computer labs and centers to provide internet and device access for vulnerable populations including people with disabilities, those experiencing homelessness, veterans, and individuals who are incarcerated or returning from incarceration.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $65,000 for computer equipment purchases (covering up to 100% of eligible costs) and up to $10,000 for internet service subscription costs for up to three years. Grants can also fund networking equipment, marketing and outreach (up to 10% of total project budget), operational expenses (up to 15% of total project budget), administrative expenses (up to 15% of total project budget), software, audiovisual equipment, assistive technology, and miscellaneous items necessary for computer lab operation. Total funding available: $2 million.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications deadline: November 29, 2024 by 11:59 PM ET
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, incorporated municipalities, local government agencies, non-profit 501(c) entities, and community anchor institutions (such as schools, higher education institutions, public housing organizations, or community support organizations) serving individuals with disabilities, homeless/unhoused individuals, veterans, and incarcerated or returning citizens.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creation, upgrade, and retrofit of public computer labs and centers providing internet and device access. Eligible uses include: computer equipment (desktops, laptops, keyboards, mice, monitors, webcams, headphones, microphones), networking equipment (routers, switches, network cables, Wi-Fi access points, firewalls), internet service subscription costs (up to 3 years of wired internet connection only), marketing and outreach (up to 10% of budget), operational expenses including staff salaries (up to 15% of budget), administrative expenses including training and security monitoring (up to 15% of budget), software (operating systems, productivity suites, educational/training software, antivirus/security), audiovisual equipment (projectors, screens, smartboards for training, speakers), assistive technology (screen readers, magnifiers, adaptive keyboards/mice), and miscellaneous items (cables, connectors, adapters, security devices).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; projects must be completed by December 31, 2026.
requirements_list: Applicant must be Maryland local jurisdiction, incorporated municipality, local government agency delegated by local jurisdiction, not-for-profit IRS approved 501(c) entity providing services within Maryland, or Community Anchor Institution within Maryland
At least 50% of lab users must be from one or more covered populations: individuals with disabilities, homeless/unhoused individuals, veterans, incarcerated/returning citizens
Grant not to exceed $65,000 for computer equipment purchase
Internet service subscription assistance not to exceed $10,000
Application must include federal Form W-9 and Certificate of Good Standing (501(c) documentation for nonprofits if applicable)
Application must include UEI/SAM.gov number and DUNS number (if applicable)
Application must include written executive summary and scope of work with timeline
Application must include detailed project budget
Funds are from American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds; all federal rules regarding this funding must be adhered to
All awardees must execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) outlining obligations
Projects must demonstrate viability and potential impact on digital equity for covered populations
Applicants must provide evidence of capability and experience related to proposed project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit complete application by November 29, 2024 at 11:59 PM ET using the MD-CLP Application Form and Application Guide. Applications may be submitted electronically via email to osb.de@maryland.gov (subject line: 'Maryland Computer Labs Program Application – Organizational Applicant name'), postmarked/shipped/hand-delivered as paper copies with original signatures to Ronnie Hammond, Office of Statewide Broadband, DHCD, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706, or hand-delivered between 8:00 AM-4:00 PM ET (excluding weekends and state/federal holidays). All required materials must be included: completed application form, executive summary, scope of work with timeline, detailed project budget, W-9 form, and Certificate of Good Standing (501(c) documentation for nonprofits). Technical assistance available prior to November 22, 2024. Awards are anticipated to begin in December 2024.

structured_extraction.program_name: Connect Maryland: FY23 Network Infrastructure Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program funds the construction of new broadband networks to serve unserved households, providing infrastructure grants to local jurisdictions and their internet service provider partners. The State of Maryland is utilizing $95 million in Federal Coronavirus Capital Projects Funding (ARPA) to support broadband expansion into unserved areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $800,000 to $4,500,000 covering 70% to 90% of capital construction costs for new broadband network construction. Match requirements vary by infrastructure type and density: Wired (fewer than 8 premises per mile: 10%; 8-14 premises per mile: 20%; 15+ premises per mile: 30%). Wireless (fewer than 40 premises per tower: 10%; 40-69 premises per tower: 20%; 70+ premises per tower: 30%). Local match must be cash and available upon execution of grant agreement. Match calculation excludes middle mile transport, interconnection plants between service areas, and service drops. Grant eligible expenses are limited to new capital items including outside plant construction (last mile and middle mile), electronic equipment, customer premises equipment, and other capital costs directly necessary to provide broadband service. Operating expenses, tower purchases, land, building purchases, and customer devices are not eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions and their internet service provider partners seeking to construct new broadband networks for unserved areas in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for new broadband network infrastructure serving unserved homes and businesses. Eligible uses include: construction of outside plant facilities (last mile and middle mile infrastructure), electronic equipment necessary to deliver service (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radios, antennas, equipment shelters), customer premises equipment and installations to deliver service at Broadband Grant Speed (100 Mbps downstream/upstream with maximum 50 millisecond latency). Ineligible uses: operating expenses, leases, bandwidth and spectrum expenses, salaries not directly related to construction, tower purchases, land purchases, building purchases or renovations, customer devices (handsets, laptops, tablets), tower upgrades, acquisition of facilities or companies, middle mile infrastructure not directly necessary to serve end users, duplication of existing broadband service, expenses related to telephone or video service not necessary for broadband delivery.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Unserved areas throughout Maryland where broadband service does not currently exist. Areas that received past state grant funding are ineligible. Service area must be entirely unserved (no existing Broadband Service at 100 Mbps download/20 Mbps upload speeds). Proposed Funded Service Area (PFSA) may be within a single jurisdiction or multiple jurisdictions and does not need to be contiguous.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction, incorporated organization recognized as a partner by local jurisdiction, or other legal entity (cooperative, private corporation, limited liability company) organized on for-profit or not-for-profit basis and recognized as partner by local jurisdiction
Individual applicants and partnerships are not eligible
Applicant must have legal capacity and authority to own and operate broadband facilities
Applicant must have DUNS number and Unique Entity ID from SAM.gov
Applicant must provide evidence of good standing and legal existence (corporate information from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation)
Service area must be entirely unserved with no existing Broadband Service
Local jurisdiction partnership letter required documenting extent of participation and any support offered
Grant request minimum: $800,000; maximum: $4,500,000

Project must achieve minimum 100 Mbps downstream and 100 Mbps upstream with maximum 50 millisecond latency (or reduced requirement of 100 Mbps down/20 Mbps up if certified circumstances prevent higher speeds)
All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated
Match requirement: 10% to 30% based on density calculation (wired or wireless)
Match must be in cash and available upon execution of grant agreement
In-kind contributions are not eligible for match
Federal funds may be used as match only if specifically requested and approved by OSB
Applicant must commence project by September 1, 2023
Applicant must complete project by August 31, 2026
At least 50% of grant funds must be expended by second anniversary of effective date
No costs incurred prior to application submission or before effective date are eligible for funding
Applicant may not supplant other federal funding previously awarded for broadband in same area
If applicant is partnering with another entity to operate system, agreement must be provided with application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted by December 5, 2022 at 11:59pm ET via one of three methods: (1) Postmarked or shipped paper copy with original signatures accompanied by electronic version on USB Flash Drive to Kenrick M. Gordon, P.E., Director, OSB of Statewide Broadband, Department of Housing and Community Development, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706; (2) Email to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with files as zipped attachment (subject line: 'Maryland Network Infrastructure Grant Application – your company name'); (3) Hand delivery. Application package must include: Broadband Grant Application Form (Schedule A-1), IRS Form W-9, evidence of good standing and legal existence, Executive Summary of Project (covering PFSA description/need, applicant description/history, partnership details, project benefits/subscriber numbers, service area demographics, and financing plan), Scoring Criteria Documentation, System Design (network diagram showing technology and infrastructure), Service Area Demographics, Scope of Work (construction build-out schedule and project milestones per Schedule F-1), Project Construction Budget (Schedule F-2), Financial Information and Sustainability (historical financial statements and pro forma per Schedule G-1), Statement of Experience, Evidence of Additional Funding Commitments, proof of local jurisdiction partnership. All files except Excel spreadsheets should be converted to PDF. Late applications will not be considered. Prior to submission, technical assistance available until November 18, 2022. Upon approval, applicant must execute grant agreement and comply with all conditions precedent to disbursement. After award, disbursement is on reimbursement basis as project progresses with quarterly progress reports required.

structured_extraction.program_name: Connect Maryland: FY24 Network Infrastructure Grant Program – Smith Island
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants specifically for constructing new broadband networks on Smith Island to serve unserved households and businesses in this geographically isolated area. Funding supports capital construction costs for broadband infrastructure necessary to deploy service at the Broadband Grant Speed (100 Mbps down/100 Mbps up) to all residents, businesses and anchor institutions on the island.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $1 million to $3 million (total available: $3 million) covering up to 90% of capital construction costs for new broadband network construction on Smith Island. Minimum 10% cash match (11.11% of requested grant amount) of capital construction costs required. Matching funds must be in cash and cannot fund operational costs. Exceptions to match requirements may be available for federal funding, Maryland Broadband Cooperative backhaul costs (up to 3 years), or tower construction/improvements. Grant funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis as the project progresses. At least 50% of grant funds must be expended by the second anniversary of the agreement effective date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions and internet service provider partners (for-profit corporations, cooperatives, limited liability companies, or incorporated organizations recognized as partners by local jurisdictions) seeking to construct broadband networks on Smith Island
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for new broadband network infrastructure including: construction of facilities to deploy service at Broadband Grant Speed (100/100 Mbps) to all end users; middle mile infrastructure directly necessary to provide service; electronics necessary to deliver service (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radios, antennae, access points, equipment cabinets or shelters); all capital expenses with final asset owned by applicant. Tower construction and structural improvements are eligible but may only be treated as match. Customer premise equipment (CPE) beyond the ONT or fixed wireless antenna is not eligible. Laptops, handsets, tablets and similar customer devices are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Smith Island, Somerset County, Maryland. Project must serve entire Identified Service Area (ISA) where broadband service does not currently exist (all 278 locations on Smith Island). Service area coordinates provided in Appendix A of application materials.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction, incorporated organization recognized as a partner by local jurisdiction, cooperative legally formed in Maryland and recognized as partner, limited liability company recognized as partner, or other legal entity (not individual or partnership) recognized as partner by local jurisdiction
Applicant must provide IRS Form W-9 and DUNS Number that match across all documents
Applicant must obtain Unique Entity ID from SAM.gov
Applicant must demonstrate legal existence and good standing with State of Maryland
Local jurisdiction partnerships must include letter from sponsoring jurisdiction documenting extent of participation and support; any legal agreements must be provided
Project must serve all unserved premises in the Identified Service Area (278 locations on Smith Island)
Minimum 10% cash match (11.11% of requested grant amount) of capital construction costs required

Network must be capable of providing minimum 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds (100x100) with maximum 50 millisecond latency, or reduced speeds (100 Mbps down/20 Mbps up) if scalable to symmetrical speeds and ISP submits certification of circumstances preventing higher speeds
Project must not duplicate existing broadband service by other entities
All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated
No costs incurred prior to application submission are eligible for grant or match purposes
Grant must not supplant other federal funding; may only supplement previously awarded federal funds
Applicant must have legal capacity and authority to own and operate broadband facilities, enter into contracts, and comply with applicable federal and state statutes and regulations
Prior to project commencement, applicant must obtain all federal, state, and local government approvals, permits, and licenses
Project commencement required by September 1, 2024
Project completion required by August 31, 2027
Applicant must maintain accurate financial, management, programmatic and other records for five years following final report approval
Applicant must submit interim progress reports on January 1, April 1, July 1, and October 1 of each year during agreement term
Applicant must submit final report within 45 calendar days after project completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed application package by January 31, 2024 at 11:59 PM ET via mail, commercial carrier, or email. Application may be mailed/shipped as paper copy with original signatures accompanied by electronic version on USB Flash Drive, or submitted electronically via email. If mailed, proof of mailing required (USPS postmark, USPS-dated mail receipt, or commercial carrier shipping label/receipt). Electronic submissions via email to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with subject line 'Maryland Network Infrastructure Grant Application – Smith Island – [company name]'. If files too large, may split into multiple emails labeled 'X of Y'. Mail address: Kenrick M. Gordon, P.E., Director, Office of Statewide Broadband, Department of Housing and Community Development, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. Application must include: completed Broadband Grant Application Form (Schedule A-1), IRS Form W-9, evidence of good standing and legal existence, local jurisdiction partnership letter (if applicable), Executive Summary of the Project, Scoring Criteria Documentation, System Design with network diagram, Service Area Demographics, Scope of Work with construction milestones and project budget, Financial Information and Sustainability (historical financial statements and pro forma), Statement of Experience, Evidence of Additional Funding Commitments, and completed Application Checklist with authorized representative signature. Technical assistance available upon request prior to January 19, 2024. Applications submitted after deadline will not be considered.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to help local jurisdictions, community-based organizations, non-profits, and anchor institutions build or expand broadband networks to provide low-cost or no-cost internet access to low and moderate income households and other underserved populations. The program addresses the affordability challenge that low and moderate income households face when subscribing to internet service by supporting the creation and expansion of community-based gap networks. Funded through American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $25,000 to $250,000 to cover up to 100 percent of project costs for construction, deployment, expansion or continuation of community-based broadband gap networks and community networks that reliably provide a minimum of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds (with limited exceptions for 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload if scalable to symmetrical 100/100 Mbps). Maximum latency of 50 milliseconds measured at served subscribers' location. Funds may be used for equipment, hardware, software, network infrastructure, installation, operation and maintenance, including optical line terminals (OLTs), optical network terminals (ONTs), routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennas, access points, modems, and necessary equipment shelters. Total FY22 funding available: $5 million. Applicants are encouraged to identify and leverage other funding sources. Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (county or municipality), non-profit organizations (501(c) entities), community-based organizations, and community-based anchor institutions seeking to deploy broadband networks for covered populations including individuals in households with income at or below 150 percent of federal poverty level, seniors, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers (including English learners and those with low literacy levels), and racial or ethnic minorities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction, deployment, expansion or continuation of broadband gap networks and community networks to deliver services at low or no cost to covered populations. Funds may cover equipment, instrumentation, networking capability, hardware and software, digital network technology, optical line terminals, optical network terminals, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennas, access points, modems, and necessary equipment shelters. Funds can support building and deployment of new gap/community networks, upgrading or expanding existing networks, and operating and maintaining networks at the required speed standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Applicants must be providing services within the State of Maryland. Project areas must be identified as having a need for additional broadband investment, including lack of access to connections that reliably meet or exceed symmetrical 100 Mbps download and upload speeds, lack of affordable access to broadband service, or lack of reliable broadband.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government (county or municipality), a non-profit 501(c) organization providing services in Maryland, a community-based anchor institution, or other community-based organization
Applicant must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation

Project must provide broadband access to covered populations including individuals in households with income at or below 150 percent of federal poverty level, seniors, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers (including English learners and those with low literacy levels), and racial or ethnic minorities

Networks must reliably provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds measured at served subscribers' location (with limited exceptions for 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload if network is scalable to symmetrical 100/100 Mbps)
Grant request between $25,000 and $250,000
Only fully complete applications at submission will be considered

Application must include project summary with executive summary, statement of experience, network design, community profile, subscriber cost, potential barriers, partners and engagement plan, intended outcomes and metrics, schedule, and funding scope and budget
Completed and signed application form (FY22 MD-GAPS Grant Application Form) required
IRS Determination Letter of non-profit status if applicable
Online verification of Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation required
IRS W-9 form required
Dun and Bradstreet DUNS Number required
Applicant name must match W-9 form
Federal EIN Number required
Applicant must confirm applicant will ultimately own and operate the network constructed and describe any restrictions to be placed on future use of equipment and network
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov with subject line 'MD-GAPS: Name of Applying Organization' on or before March 31, 2022. Complete application package must include: (1) Completed FY22 MD-GAPS Grant Application Form in its entirety; (2) Project Summary addressing all required sections (executive summary, statement of experience, network design, community profile, subscriber cost, potential barriers, partners and local engagement, intended outcomes and sustainability, implementation schedule, and funding scope and budget); (3) Simple budget showing how funds will be spent, organized by categories including Operations (equipment, payroll, supplies, materials), Contracted Services (payments to independent contractors and external organizations), Travel (related to program deployment), and any other funding necessary for the project including anticipated sources; (4) Federal Form W-9 with applicant name matching legal name; (5) Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. Successful applicants will be chosen based on qualifications, evaluation of responses, and possible interviews. Awards are intended to begin in May 2022. All awardees must execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) outlining obligations of awardee and State to the Project. No reimbursement will be made for costs incurred in responding to the RFA or developing responses.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide Maryland grant program designed to advance digital equity and inclusion by providing new, internet-enabled devices (HP Chromebooks) to families with the greatest need who cannot afford to purchase devices themselves. Administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Office of Statewide Broadband, the program distributes devices through county and municipal governments to eligible households with incomes at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines. The program works alongside discounted and free internet services such as the Maryland Emergency Broadband Benefit and Federal ACP subsidy. Approximately 145,000 devices were procured statewide across two rounds. At the county level, St. Mary's County received approval for 4,500 Chromebooks valued at $894,375 plus $27,000 in distribution funding, all of which have been issued. Extended distribution events have continued in St. Mary's County, including a December 2024 event for remaining or additional devices.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of internet-enabled devices (HP Chromebook 14 G7 or similar, with minimum specifications: 13-inch screen, Chrome OS, SD card reader, dual band Wi-Fi, 2 USB ports, headphone and video output jacks, one-year warranty) distributed by counties and municipalities to eligible households with incomes at or below 200% of Federal Poverty Guidelines. One device per address. County/municipal applicants receive a $6 per device distribution stipend ($198.75 per device equipment cost). Stipend may be used for: cost of securing devices in storage; cost of securing devices during distribution; cost of distribution venue; and personnel costs associated with distribution. Performance period is 6 months from delivery of first device shipment. Approximately 145,000 devices total were procured statewide across two rounds (Round 1: 91,300 devices; Round 2: remaining allotment). St. Mary's County specifically received 4,500 Chromebooks valued at $894,375 plus $27,000 in distribution grant funding, all of which have been distributed. Devices must be received at a maximum rate of one shipment per month over a five-month period, with all devices delivered within five months of MOU execution.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Round 2 applications accepted through September 29, 2023 at 11:59 PM ET
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and municipal governments distributing devices to eligible households with incomes at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines; end recipients are families most in need who cannot afford to purchase internet-enabled devices, including eligible households in St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Internet-enabled Chromebook devices for household use to access online services, participate in the digital economy, and improve digital access and connectivity. For distributing jurisdictions, the $6 per device stipend may be used for: cost of securing devices in storage; cost of securing devices during distribution; cost of distribution venue; and personnel costs associated with distribution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; St. Mary's County has conducted extended local distribution events including a December 14, 2024 event at the St. Mary's County Sheriff's Office, District 4 Station, 21633 Great Mills Rd, Lexington Park.
requirements_list: Applicant (for state program) must be a Maryland local jurisdiction (county or incorporated municipality) as recognized by the Maryland Manual On-Line website
Applicant must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) before submitting a complete application packet and provide a valid unique entity identifier
Applicant must supply a Dun and Bradstreet Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number
Applicant must provide a Federal Form W-9
Eligible households must have income at or below 200% of Federal Poverty Guidelines

Eligible households may qualify by: proof of income at or below 200% of federal poverty level; enrollment in the federal Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP); or participation in government assistance programs (SNAP, Medicaid, WIC, SSI, FPHA, Veterans Pension and Survivors Benefit, Free and Reduced-Price School Lunch/Breakfast Program, or Federal Pell Grant in current award year)
Only one device per address or recognized MDU unit is allowable
Applicant must develop and describe an eligibility verification process
Applicant must develop an outreach program to inform the targeted community and public of the program, eligibility, location and times of distribution events
Applicant must ensure bulk shipment receiver has loading/unloading capabilities and secure storage space

Applicant must develop a scope of work detailing establishment of partnerships, collection of data, storage, distribution method, eligibility verification, and methodology to ensure one device per household
Applicant must provide estimated number of qualifying households and explanation of how device request was determined
Applicant must maintain records of distribution and be able to provide household-level data upon request
Applicant must use the Department Device Tracking Portal for address verification during distribution
Applicant must inspect devices upon receipt and notify OSB immediately of damaged products
Any devices not distributed within 6 months of first delivery must be returned to the Department at the awardee's cost
Round 2: new eligible applicants receive priority consideration over returning applicants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: County and municipal governments apply to the Office of Statewide Broadband using the MD-CDP Application Guide, application form, project narrative, scope of work, schedule, and monthly device delivery request. Applications must be submitted electronically via email to OSB.MD@maryland.gov or by USPS/shipping with proof of postmark/receipt by 11:59 PM ET on September 29, 2023. Electronic submission is preferred. All applications must be complete; missing information may result in ineligibility. The application must include: legal name matching W-9, Federal EIN, DUNS number, SAM.gov unique identifier, entity type (county or municipality), address, partnerships if applicable, contact information, estimated eligible households, estimated households in need, number of devices requested, receiver information with secure storage and loading dock status, device delivery method, project narrative (executive summary, verification and distribution process, scope of work, outreach program, potential barriers, partners and engagement, intended outcomes and metrics), schedule with milestones, and monthly device delivery request. Round 1 awarded 91,300 devices; Round 2 awarded the remaining allotment with a deadline of September 29, 2023. Technical assistance available until September 22, 2023. Successful applicants are chosen based on qualifications and evaluation of responses; OSB may conduct interviews and is entitled to conduct investigations. Successful applicants will be required to execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) that outlines obligations. At the local level, eligible households can obtain Chromebooks at distribution events. A St. Mary's County distribution event was held on Saturday, December 14, 2024, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. at the St. Mary's County Sheriff's Office, District 4 Station, 21633 Great Mills Rd, Lexington Park, where eligible households could bring proof of eligibility and address to receive one device per household while supplies lasted. The St. Mary's County program page offers a notification sign-up option suggesting future rounds may be possible.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development to advance digital inclusion efforts in Maryland by enabling access to high-speed internet and expanding digital literacy. Funds support digital inclusion planning, program implementation, workforce development training, and public access computing centers serving underserved populations. The program provides funding to local jurisdictions, non-profit organizations, and community-based anchor institutions to support digital inclusion planning and implementation efforts that help residents access and use broadband services. Funded through American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two funding tracks: Digital Inclusion Planning grants provide up to 50 percent of planning costs, with a maximum of $30,000 and minimum of $5,000. Digital Inclusion Implementation grants provide up to 100 percent of implementation, expansion, or continuation costs, with a maximum of $75,000 and minimum of $10,000. Total funding available: $2 million from American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds. While not required, applicants are highly encouraged to identify other funding sources to leverage the available grant funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties and municipalities), non-profit 501(c) organizations, foundations, corporations, institutions, associations, coalitions, and community-based anchor institutions serving underserved populations including low-income individuals (at or below 150% of federal poverty level), aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers, racial and ethnic minorities, and rural residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing digital inclusion plans, implementing digital inclusion activities, facilitating broadband adoption, implementing training programs covering basic, advanced, and applied skills, implementing workforce development programs, constructing, upgrading, expanding, or operating public access computing centers for covered populations, researching and identifying populations with low adoption rates for home internet and computers, and furthering other qualifying digital inclusion or equity goals. Grant funds may not be used for construction of broadband infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All communities in Maryland are eligible to apply. However, covered populations most at need receive priority consideration, including individuals living in households with income at or below 150 percent of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers (including English learners and those with low literacy levels), individuals who are members of racial or ethnic minority groups, and individuals who primarily reside in rural areas.

Only fully complete applications will be considered for funding
For Planning track: request between $5,000 and $30,000
For Implementation track: request between $10,000 and $75,000
Must submit completed and signed application form

Must provide executive summary including project overview, population needs, barriers to digital inclusion, partners and local engagement, intended outcomes and metrics, and statement of experience demonstrating capability and expertise
Must provide scope of work specific to funding requested with detailed breakdown by budget categories (Operations, Contracted Services, Travel, Equipment, Supplies, Other)
Must provide project budget showing planned spending and any other funding sources
Non-profits must submit IRS Determination Letter of nonprofit status or other proof of 501(c) status
Must submit IRS W-9 form
Must provide Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must provide Dun & Bradstreet DUNS Number
All federal rules and requirements regarding ARPA funding must be adhered to by the applicant if an award is made
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit all required application materials and attachments via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov with subject line 'MD-DIG: Name of Applying Organization'. Applications must be complete to be considered for funding. Required components include: (1) Completed application form with applicant information and project details, (2) Executive summary addressing project overview, population needs, barriers, partners, intended outcomes and metrics, and statement of experience, (3) Scope of work specific to the funding requested, (4) Budget breakdown by categories (Operations, Contracted Services, Travel, Equipment, Supplies, Other) and any leveraged funding, (5) IRS W-9 form, (6) Proof of nonprofit status (for 501(c) organizations), (7) Certificate of Good Standing, and (8) DUNS Number. The Office of Statewide Broadband will review applications to ensure completeness and eligibility. Successful applicants will be chosen based on qualifications and evaluation of responses, with possible interviews. Awardees will be required to execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) outlining obligations. Funding awards are anticipated to be made beginning in May 2022.

structured_extraction.program_name: EmPOWER Maryland Limited Income Energy Efficiency Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide energy efficiency and conservation program created by the EmPOWER Maryland Energy Efficiency Act of 2008. For limited income households, the program provides no-cost installation of energy conservation materials and major appliances — including insulation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and repairs, refrigerator retrofits, and health and safety improvements — to reduce energy use, lower monthly power bills, and improve home comfort and air quality. Maryland's five largest electric utilities also offer incentives to help all households and businesses save energy and money through free or discounted energy audits, weatherization, and efficient appliances. The program was updated in 2024 to include new incentives for switching from fossil fuel-powered heating and appliances to efficient electric alternatives.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides installation of energy efficiency materials and equipment at no charge to eligible limited income households. Services include insulation installation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and repairs, refrigerator retrofits if applicable, and health and safety items. A local agency conducts an energy audit to prioritize the most effective improvements, schedules contractors to complete work, and conducts a follow-up evaluation after upgrades are completed. For limited income households: a local agency will contact applicants to schedule an energy audit, discuss results, and schedule a contractor to complete recommended work at no cost. Additionally, Maryland's five largest electric utilities offer free or discounted energy audits, weatherization services, and discounts on efficient appliances for all households and businesses. Income eligibility examples: one person household up to $5,708/month; two person household up to $6,520/month (or at or below 250% of federal poverty level). Maximum initial deposit for critical repair work is 33% of total project cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Limited income households that meet income qualifications and have utility accounts with BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas; as well as all Maryland households and businesses served by participating electric utilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency upgrades including insulation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and safety repairs, refrigerator retrofits, health and safety improvements, energy audits, weatherization, and efficient appliances including major appliance replacements. For homeowners only, critical repairs such as structural, electrical, water leaks, lead, asbestos remediation (maximum $50,000 for repair programs).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Households must be customers of one of six participating utility companies: BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas. Program operates statewide through participating local agencies.
requirements_list: Household income must be at or below 250% of federal poverty level based on household size (e.g., $5,708/month for one person; $6,520/month for two people)
Must have a utility account with one of six participating companies (BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas)

Automatically income-eligible if currently participating in Utility Bill Pay Assistance through OHEP, SNAP, TANF, SSI, HUD housing assistance programs, Fuel Fund Assistance, DHCD Rehab Programs, Baltimore Lead Hazard Control Program, Medicaid, MEA Energy Equity Grant, or MEEHA
Low-income household status required for no-cost installation services
Home must have power to the home (applicants without power should call DHCD directly at 855-583-8976)
For homeowners applying for critical repair funding: must provide deed and current mortgage statement; funding available only for primary residence; maximum project cost cannot exceed $50,000
For renters: landlord consent information required; renters do not qualify for critical repair funding
For mobile home owners: copy of title or bill of sale required to prove ownership
Documentation of medical condition requiring functioning heating, cooling, or water heating systems may qualify for expedited service (physician's letter required)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Complete either the Quick Application (for those receiving eligible benefits) or Standard Application (all programs). Quick Application requires Client Information, Household Income Information, Energy Consent Form, copy of recent electric utility bill, and copy of benefit approval notice. Standard Application requires Client Information, Household Information, Energy Consent Form, recent electric utility bill, proof of last 30 days gross household income, Social Security card copies for all household members, and photo ID for applicant. 2) For zero income household members, complete Zero Income Form. 3) For homeowners seeking critical repairs, submit Supplemental Financial Information, Tax Affidavit, Credit Pull Consent, and repair documentation including bids from licensed contractors with photos, MHIC license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and W-9 forms. 4) Submit complete application to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Attn: Weatherization, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. 5) After determining eligibility, a local agency will contact applicant to schedule energy audit. 6) Local agency discusses audit results and schedules contractor to complete recommended work. 7) Follow-up evaluation conducted after upgrades completed. For utility-based programs, contact your electric utility directly.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY24 Home Stretch - Difficult to Serve Properties Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) that helps county jurisdictions and individual property owners cover the cost of installing broadband internet service to remote, geographically isolated, or otherwise difficult-to-serve properties. The program addresses situations where distance from broadband infrastructure, long driveways, or other geographic challenges discourage internet service providers from delivering service economically. In FY24, the program awarded $19.6 million through the U.S. Treasury's American Rescue Plan Coronavirus Capital Projects Fund to extend broadband access to approximately 2,400 unserved Maryland households across 18 jurisdictions. County jurisdictions develop sub-grant programs with ISP partners, and individual homeowners and businesses may also be eligible depending on county implementation. In Montgomery County, the program specifically targets properties more than 300 feet from the road in partnership with Comcast.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $1,100,000 total per county jurisdiction to support installation of broadband service to difficult-to-serve premises. Maximum state funding per location is $8,000 (covering up to two-thirds of installation cost). In Montgomery County, Comcast covers up to one-third of the cost (maximum $4,000); if total installation cost exceeds $12,000, the resident pays the difference. There is no installation charge to extend facilities 300 feet in Montgomery County. A 25% match of eligible project costs is required at the county level. County jurisdictions develop a sub-grant program with ISP partners. Grant funds may be used to finance capital construction of facilities for connecting unserved difficult-to-reach premises to existing broadband networks, including minor extensions of ISP existing infrastructure. Eligible costs include construction materials, equipment (ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennae, access points, modems), equipment shelters, and related necessary infrastructure. All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 22, 2023 for county jurisdictions; March 16, 2025 for Montgomery County individual homeowners round
structured_extraction.program_audience: County jurisdictions applying on behalf of remote or geographically isolated properties lacking broadband access; homeowners and business owners in hard-to-reach areas with properties set more than 300 feet from the road who need high-speed internet service; unserved Maryland households without internet access.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for broadband service installation to remote or geographically isolated properties that are difficult for private providers to serve economically, including installation of high-speed broadband internet service to residential homes and businesses. Eligible uses include construction of facilities for connecting premises to existing broadband networks, installation of service drops and related infrastructure, electronic equipment and materials for network delivery (ONTs, modems, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless equipment, antennae, access points), equipment shelters, and minor extensions of existing ISP infrastructure. Operating expenses, telephone or video services not necessary for broadband delivery, land purchases, tower construction, building renovations, and middle mile infrastructure are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland county jurisdictions statewide. In the first round, 18 jurisdictions received awards and every jurisdiction that applied received funds. Montgomery County implementation targets properties more than 300 feet from the road in areas served by Comcast, particularly in Agricultural Reserve areas. Somerset County also participates, targeting areas with broadband speeds less than 25 Mbps.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a county jurisdiction (for county-level grants) with an established partnership with an ISP partner prior to entering funding agreement
Properties must be unserved with no current access to broadband at speeds of 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload with latency of 50 milliseconds or less
Properties must have difficulty obtaining service due to remoteness, distance from broadband infrastructure, long driveways, or other geographic challenges that discourage ISP service
Maximum $8,000 state funding per location
25% match of eligible capital construction costs required at county level from any combination of county jurisdiction, ISP partner, property owner, or other sources (must be cash, not in-kind)
Property must be more than 300 feet from the road (Montgomery County)
Must be in an area served by the partnering ISP (Montgomery County: Comcast)
Cannot be a current subscriber to existing broadband service from the partner ISP (Montgomery County: not a current Comcast Xfinity or Verizon FiOS subscriber)
Project must be completed by December 31, 2025

Network must deliver minimum 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum 50 milliseconds latency, or with certification of geographic/topographic/cost constraints: 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload with same latency requirement
ISP partners must participate in federal Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP)
Must complete grant submission form by applicable deadline
Must sign agreement and return within 30 days of receiving cost estimate (individual applicants)
Must agree to pay any contribution required if total cost exceeds state and ISP contributions (Montgomery County residents)
All equipment purchased must be new and non-depreciated
Unserved households with no current access to broadband are prioritized
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For county jurisdictions: County jurisdictions with ISP partner(s) develop a jurisdictional-specific sub-grant program and submit a complete application package to DHCD's Office of Statewide Broadband. Applications include an Executive Summary of unserved properties to be served, demonstration of ISP partnership and cooperation, statement of experience from key team members, network description with technology details and speed capabilities, subscriber profile with demographic data, subscriber cost options including low/moderate income offerings, detailed budget with capital construction cost estimates, program overview detailing end-user selection criteria, assistance for low-income users, acceptable ISP costs, ACP promotion and assistance, and project implementation schedule with milestones. For individual applicants (Montgomery County): Step 1: Complete the online grant submission form. Step 2: Montgomery County requests a cost estimate from Comcast. Step 3: Montgomery County provides the cost estimate and agreement to the resident. Step 4: Resident returns the signed agreement and any required contribution within 30 days. Step 5: Comcast completes construction within 90 days after receiving all necessary documents and payment. Full application details and forms are available on the DHCD Broadband website at https://dhcd.maryland.gov/broadband.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that helps Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) participants pursue higher education, improve their employment status, and achieve economic independence. The program works with participants to define career and financial goals, eliminate obstacles to self-sufficiency, and provides access to a wide range of support services including childcare assistance, transportation help, education support, job search and retention skills training, financial planning, credit repair counseling, career counseling, English language services, and homeownership counseling. Participants also benefit from an interest-bearing escrow savings account that accrues as their household's portion of rent increases due to earned income. Upon successful completion of the five-year contract, participants receive the escrow account balance and accrued interest. The program is administered at both the state level through DHCD and locally by county housing agencies including Harford County and Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive case management, goal-setting support, and access to support services including childcare assistance, transportation, education support, job search and retention skills training, financial planning, credit repair counseling, career counseling, English language services, homeownership counseling, and transportation support. Participants also receive an interest-bearing escrow (savings) account that accrues as the household's portion of rent increases due to earned income. The escrow account accrues interest and monthly deposits are made based on employment wage increases. Upon successful graduation and achievement of self-sufficiency within the five-year contract period (or potentially earlier if all goals are met), participants receive the accumulated escrow account balance and accrued interest, which is nontaxable per IRS guidelines. Housing Choice Voucher subsidy is not affected by participation. The contract can be extended for an additional two years with good cause.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing - applications accepted at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) participants statewide, including in Cambridge (Dorchester County), Harford County, and Baltimore County, who have employment goals and wish to achieve financial independence and economic self-sufficiency through education, career development, and financial planning.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support toward achieving career and financial goals including childcare, transportation, education, job search and retention skills, financial planning, credit repair, career counseling, English language services, homeownership counseling, and escrow savings accrued from increased earned income. Early escrow withdrawals may be permitted in urgent situations or for goal-related expenses such as vehicle repair or testing fees on a case-by-case basis.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland, with specific program offices in Cambridge (Dorchester County), Harford County, and Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Must be a Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) participant
Must have employment and/or financial independence goals
Head or co-head of household must sign an FSS Contract of Participation
Must complete a Needs Assessment outlining rights, goals, and responsibilities
Must maintain a current, signed training plan
Must maintain contact with FSS specialist and follow through on commitments
All household members 18 years or older are eligible for services once contract is signed
Have up to five years to reach goals and complete all contract activities (contract can be extended up to two additional years with good cause)

To graduate and access full escrow account: must complete all goals before end of contract period, be free of Maryland Temporary Cash Assistance (TANF) benefits for at least 12 months, and be employed at time of graduation

Two required long-term goals: obtain employment/earned income and be free of temporary cash assistance (social security and assistance for disabled family members do not count toward TANF requirement)
Disabled individuals may participate as long as goal is to obtain employment/earned income and be free of TANF benefits; may designate another adult household member as head of household
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DHCD at 410-901-4080 or email fss.dhcd@maryland.gov, or complete the online inquiry form at dhcd.wufoo.com/forms/family-selfsufficiency-program to have a program coordinator contact you and begin the application process. As soon as you start receiving rental assistance, you can join FSS at any time. For Harford County, complete and submit the interest form or call 410-638-3045 to make an appointment. The head of household completes and submits an application and signs a Contract of Participation. After submission, the applicant and program coordinator complete a Needs Assessment which outlines and identifies the rights, goals, and responsibilities of both parties. Participants then work with a case manager to assess strengths, identify barriers, set goals, and develop a plan to achieve economic independence over the five-year program period. Goals may be set by all family members and can include higher education, job training, homeownership, and entrepreneurship. The FSS case manager assists each family with creating realistic and achievable goals and directs families to supportive services from the community to help resolve obstacles. Participants should communicate quarterly with their FSS coordinator to stay on track. Classes, workshops, and opportunities are regularly scheduled at the Shore Community Engagement Center.

structured_extraction.program_name: HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME) Multi-Family Development Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development and local governments (including Prince George's County) that provides funding to support affordable housing. Funds are used to build, buy, rehabilitate, and preserve rental housing, owner-occupied housing, and special needs housing such as group homes. At the county level, HOME Investment Partnership entitlement funds are used to develop, rehabilitate, and preserve affordable housing through partnerships with real estate and non-profit developers, with a focus on areas with projected rent growth. The program also provides gap financing to real estate developers to build affordable housing developments for families and individuals with income below 80% of the Area Median Income. The program operates on a rolling basis with ongoing funding allocations.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HOME funds are provided with flexible terms determined by the State and project needs. Funds may be awarded as non-interest bearing or deferred loans with terms ranging from 20 to 40 years, amortizing loans, or recoverable grants requiring repayment when property is sold or discontinued for low-income use. For homeownership projects, funds may be used as soft seconds to reduce home costs, for land, development costs, or construction financing. For rental projects, equity sharing may be required when low-income usage is discontinued, with the State sharing in proportion to HOME funds involved. The program provides gap financing to make projects viable and serve households with income below 80% of Area Median Income. The maximum assistance to a single project generally will not exceed the amount needed to make the project viable and comply with federal HOME regulations. HOME funds are allocated among multifamily housing programs, single family programs, administrative costs, and CHDO set-asides (minimum 15% of formula allocation reserved for CHDOs). Up to 5% of the State HOME allocation may be used for administrative expenses and CHDO operating assistance (up to $50,000 per year for existing CHDOs).
structured_extraction.program_audience: State Government Agencies, Local Governments, Local Housing Agencies, Nonprofit Organizations, Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs), mission-oriented real estate developers, and for-profit developers seeking to develop, rehabilitate, or preserve affordable housing. Projects may also include homeownership assistance, single-family rehabilitation, group homes for special populations, and tenant-based rental assistance.
