structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building, buying, rehabilitating, or preserving rental housing, owner-occupied housing, and special needs housing such as group homes. Also covers new construction, housing rehabilitation, preservation of naturally affordable housing, gap financing for affordable housing development, soft seconds for homeownership, land acquisition, development costs, construction financing, site control costs, feasibility studies, security deposit assistance, and disaster victim assistance. Projects must comply with both Maryland DHCD program eligibility requirements and HOME program federal requirements. Funds may be used in conjunction with other DHCD housing programs or as standalone funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. HOME funds are used primarily in non-Participating Jurisdictions throughout the State, which include all Maryland counties except Baltimore City, Anne Arundel (except City of Annapolis), Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties, which receive direct HOME allocations from HUD. The State may provide funds in Participating Jurisdictions as deemed necessary. State Government Agencies are automatically eligible and receive either their formula allocation or $3 million, whichever is greater. Prince George's County programs focus particularly on areas with projected rent growth.
requirements_list: For rental housing units, residents' household incomes must be 50% or less of the area median household income (based on household size and set annually by HUD)
For owner-occupied housing units, owners' household income must be 55% or less of the area median household income (based on household size and set annually by HUD)
Target households with income at or below 80% of Area Median Income, adjusted for household size
The number of income-restricted units is usually calculated by dividing HOME funds by total project cost, then multiplying by the total number of units in the project
If using HOME funds with other CDA programs, projects must meet both CDA program eligibility requirements and HOME program federal requirements
For homeownership projects, federal regulations set forth equity restrictions that must be governed

For CHDOs seeking predevelopment assistance, must meet HUD's Community Housing Development Organization qualifying criteria and may request loans up to $50,000 for project feasibility or site control costs
Property rents must comply with HUD-calculated Low HOME Rent Limits and High HOME Rent Limits by unit type and county
If property is sold or stops being used for low-income housing, borrower must share any equity gain with the State in proportion to HOME funds involved
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications may be submitted by local governments, nonprofits, developers, and state agencies. Project applications may include requests for HOME funds or DHCD staff may propose HOME fund use during project evaluation and underwriting. For the HOME Special Reserve Fund (used for special projects or programs filling needs not met by other DHCD programs), applications are reviewed and allocated on a first-come, first-serve basis with priority given to CHDOs producing CHDO-reserve eligible projects. Applications from CHDOs and nonprofits as well as local governments applying in conjunction with nonprofits receive priority consideration. Rating criteria include readiness to proceed, demonstrated ability, matching contributions, geographic distribution, and performance on prior HOME awards. Applications should be directed to the Community Development Administration. Contact the HOME Program Manager for specific application procedures and current funding availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to owners of public housing to install broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units, addressing digital equity gaps in low-income housing communities. The program aims to optimize utilization of limited resources by assisting local jurisdictions in implementing solutions for the delivery of high-speed internet services with a minimum of 100Mbps download and 100Mbps upload speeds to unserved residents.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Round 1: Grants between $500,000 and $9,000,000 covering 95% of eligible project costs (5% match required). Expanded Round FY24 Affordable Housing: Grants between $250,000 and $5,000,000 also covering 95% of eligible costs (5% match required) for municipal, non-profit public housing owners and internet service providers. Eligible uses include: installation or extension of fiber optic facilities to public housing structures; installation of end-user facilities including wiring, wireless access points and necessary electronics to individual units; and educational and technical assistance outreach to support adoption. Projects must provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds to each dwelling unit. Common area WiFi should deliver minimum 100Mbps download and 20Mbps upload speeds. All equipment must be new and non-depreciated. Applicants must maintain and secure project equipment and acquire necessary hardware warranty and service agreements for at least 5 years after project completion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Expanded Round FY24 Affordable Housing deadline extended to January 31, 2025 (updated from February 7, 2025)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions (county or municipal), housing authorities, internet service providers, municipally owned and non-profit public housing owners seeking to provide broadband infrastructure to individual dwelling units in low-income housing communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units in public housing; extension of fiber optic facilities to public housing structures; installation of end-user facilities including wiring, wireless access points and necessary electronics; wireless access points in public and common areas to provide free broadband service; community engagement and educational support costs (capped at 3% of total project cost, not to exceed $15,000); engineering design services; low voltage contracting work; broadband network equipment (hardware and software), modems, switches, routers, firewalls for network security; taxes, shipping and insurance costs directly related to broadband network equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Projects must serve publicly owned housing developments identified as having a need for additional broadband investment, including lack of access to reliable connections meeting or exceeding minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload speeds.
requirements_list: Applicant must be owner of public housing (publicly owned, not just publicly supported)
For Expanded Round: must be municipal or non-profit owner of public housing, or existing internet service provider actively offering high-speed internet services
5% match of eligible project costs required (can be local, state, or federal funds)
Projects must provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds at each dwelling unit
For broadband only at 100/20 speeds, network must be scalable to 100/100 speeds based on future technology advances
ISP must submit certificate if unable to achieve minimum connectivity due to geography, topography, or excessive cost
Applicants must maintain and secure project equipment and hardware for minimum 5 years after project completion
Applicant must commit to providing range of service options and extending free broadband service via WiFi connectivity through all common areas
Internal wiring infrastructure must be designed to facilitate open access for all service providers (from cabinet to individual unit)
Non-capital administrative costs capped at 1% of total project costs
Community engagement costs capped at 3% of total project cost, not to exceed $15,000
Must provide ACP (Affordable Connectivity Program) registration assistance and/or educational assistance to ensure connectivity per unit
All equipment purchased must be new and non-depreciated
Projects must be completed by June 30, 2026 (for Round 1)
For Expanded Round: ISP applicants must demonstrate they are existing internet service providers with strong letters of support from municipal or non-profit property owners
For Expanded Round: Property owners must provide documentation of municipally owned or non-profit (501(c)(3)) status
For Expanded Round: ISP must offer low-price options for low-income residents and affordable pricing for different speed tiers starting at 100/20 Mbps
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit one (1) electronic PDF copy of complete application package via email to osb.md@maryland.gov. 2. Complete application form in its entirety (missing information may result in ineligibility). 3. Include project summary addressing: Executive Summary describing the public housing location, how it was chosen, problems residents face, and how the project will alleviate those problems; Statement of Experience with demonstrated capability and past network deployments; Network Design describing speed, latency capabilities, backhaul requirements, technology type, underlying ISP and bandwidth size, MPOE technology, proposed speed capabilities, and network diagram; Community Profile with demographic data and existing internet service description; Subscriber Cost information if applicable; Potential Barriers discussion; Partners and Local Engagement list; Implementation Schedule with major milestones, start/end dates, and milestone risks; and Funding Scope and Budget with line item capital construction budget. 4. Submit supporting documentation including IRS W-9 Form, network diagrams (wireless and wired if applicable), and project budget form with detailed line-item breakdown. 5. For Expanded Round: Submit letters of support from property owners, financial information covering 3 years historical and 3-5 years projected data, sustainability plan, and community engagement strategies. 6. Applications are reviewed for completeness and eligibility. Projects must demonstrate viable and eligible scope. 7. Selected applicants may be asked to revise proposals to address any technical issues identified before final consideration.

structured_extraction.program_description: HSP helps communities across Maryland prevent and end homelessness by providing technical support and funding to Continuums of Care and Local Homeless Coalitions for homeless services and activities. The program provides over $15 million in annual funding and prioritizes projects that divert at-risk households, rapidly connect people experiencing homelessness with permanent housing, serve vulnerable groups, implement evidence-based practices, and deliver services in a safe, inclusive, equitable, and accessible manner.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HSP provides grants and technical support to lead agencies for Continuums of Care and Local Homeless Coalitions. The program provides over $15 million in annual funding to deliver and organize homeless services. For SFY2026, total anticipated funding is $15,200,000 ($14,000,000 in State HSP Funds and $1,200,000 in Federal Emergency Solutions Grant funds). Lead agencies receive grants that may be subgranted to government agencies or nonprofit organizations. Funds can be used for street outreach, emergency shelter, rapid rehousing, homeless prevention, permanent supportive housing case management, HMIS data collection and system administration, special events, and administrative costs. Administrative costs are capped at 10% of the grant request. A minimum of $1 million is allocated specifically for projects dedicated to serving unaccompanied youth. All lead agencies must provide matching funds of at least 25% of requested funding. The grant period for SFY2026 is 18 months (July 1, 2025 through December 31, 2026).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Lead agencies for Maryland Continuums of Care (HUD-approved Collaborative Applicants) and DHCD-approved lead agencies for Balance of State Local Homeless Coalitions applying on behalf of homeless services providers in their communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Street outreach, emergency shelter, rapid rehousing, homeless prevention, permanent supportive housing case management, HMIS data collection and system administration, special events (Homeless Resource Days, Point-in-Time Count activities), and administrative costs for homeless services. Eligible supportive services include case management, employment assistance, training, health services, mental health services, substance abuse treatment, legal services, child care, transportation, mediation, credit counseling, and services for special populations including homeless youth, veterans, and domestic violence survivors. New in SFY2026: direct cash transfer programs for unaccompanied youth, returning citizens from incarceration, pregnant or parenting households with children under 5, and flex funds for landlord incentives and removal of tenant housing barriers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all Maryland communities served through 16 Continuums of Care and Balance of State Local Homeless Coalitions.
requirements_list: Only eligible lead agencies (HUD-approved Collaborative Applicants/CoC lead agencies or DHCD-approved LHC lead agencies) can submit applications
Only one application per Continuum of Care or Local Homeless Coalition permitted
Applications must be submitted online via the Project Portal
Organizational Profile Review with required documentation due March 21, 2025
All grantees must provide a 25% match of requested funding
All grantees and subgrantees must be enrolled in HMIS (or comparable database for victim services providers) and in compliance with all HUD and local HMIS lead agency requirements
All grantees must be participating in the Maryland State Homelessness Data Warehouse (MSHDW)
Grantees must comply with Housing First principles
Grantees must have sound financial management and maintain records for at least 5 years
Lead agencies must certify that subgrantees meet HSP requirements
Lead agencies must perform at least one risk assessment of all subgrantees over the grant term
Lead agencies must conduct monitoring and compliance visits to high-risk subgrantees and to medium- and low-risk subgrantees based on risk assessment criteria
Subgrantees must demonstrate collaboration with local homeless provider groups and local mainstream service providers
Subgrantees must participate in Continuum of Care planning appropriate to their jurisdiction
Lead agencies must use transparent and competitive project selection processes with performance-based scoring methods

CoCs/LHCs should allocate 50% of total funding request to RRH and PSH projects OR allocate funding for RRH and PSH projects that is 10% higher than FY24 HSP budget for these activities to improve application scores
Grantees must comply with all Fair Housing, Equal Access, ADA, and non-discrimination requirements
Victim service providers must establish a comparable database approved by HMIS lead agency and document confidentiality procedures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process has three key deadlines and reviews: (1) Organization Profile Review due March 21, 2025 - submit required organizational documents via Project Portal including W-9, organizational chart, financial audit, articles of incorporation/bylaws, tax exemption letter, certificate of good standing, charity registration status, and board list; (2) Application submission due April 25, 2025 at 5pm via Project Portal - lead agencies must complete the online application, upload the CoC/LHC application narrative (Word document addressing 8 parts: Strategy, Project Selection, System Performance, Coordinated Entry, Equity, Compliance & Quality, Youth Projects, and RRH & PSH Projects), detailed budget template (Excel with both level and 30% increase budgets), project performance tool (Excel), and performance data (Stella P Report, 2024 System Performance Measures Report, HUD Annual Performance Reports for renewal projects, Housing Inventory Count and Point in Time Count data); (3) Three-part application review - Threshold Review (Organization Profile Review verifying eligibility and required documents), CoC/LHC Performance Evaluation (scoring application narrative on strategy, project selection, system performance, coordinated entry, equity, compliance, youth projects, RRH/PSH projects), and Project-Level Performance Evaluation (scoring based on prior spending/compliance history, HMIS compliance, renewal project performance). Training session provided March 3, 2025. Award notifications and grant agreements issued June 2, 2025. Grant period begins July 1, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) WholeHome Critical Home Repairs Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps Maryland homeowners facing financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic by funding critical repairs in primary residences that could lead to displacement if not addressed. Assistance is provided on a first-come, first-served basis until funds are exhausted. The program is part of Maryland's Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) initiative administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $10,000 per project for critical home repairs. There is no minimum amount. Grants may be approved for up to $15,000 in extenuating circumstances on a case-by-case basis with documentation of need. Eligible repairs include: Mold/Mildew Remediation, Asbestos removal, No Heat/No Air (HVAC), Electrical Repairs, Plumbing and Septic Repairs, Wells, Roof repair/replacement, Reduce/eliminate Lead Paint Hazards, Structural/Maintenance issues, and Trip/Slip issues. Payment to contractors can be structured as either 33% deposit with 67% at completion, or 0% deposit with 100% at completion. This is grant assistance with no deed of trust recorded and no lien on the property.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 2, 2026 (closed early because funds ran out)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners facing financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic who own and reside in their primary residence and have critical home repair needs that could lead to displacement. Applicants must have experienced financial hardship after January 21, 2020.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical repairs in primary residences including non-functioning heating/cooling systems, water heaters, electrical and plumbing/septic repairs, wells, roof repair/replacement, mold/mildew remediation, lead paint/asbestos removal, structural and maintenance issues, and trip/slip hazards. Funds cannot be used for remodeling or other non-critical repairs. Prior deposits or material purchases made by homeowners will not be reimbursed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Income eligibility is based on County Area Median Income (AMI) limits at 150% of County AMI by household size. Specific income limits vary by county and household size as detailed in the Income Limits Chart.
requirements_list: Experienced eligible financial hardship after January 21, 2020 (hardships that began before January 21, 2020 but continued after that date are eligible)
Household income at or below 150% of County Area Median Income (AMI) based on household size - see Income Limits Chart by county
Must be a Maryland homeowner
Must reside in the property as primary residence
Must be named on the deed of the property
If other persons are named on the deed but do not occupy the property, must provide proof they live elsewhere (copy of driver's license, utility bill, notarized statement, or other evidence)
Must provide at least one detailed estimate from a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement Contractor, dated within the last 60 days
Contractor estimate must include photographs documenting the critical repairs
Contractor must be currently licensed as a Maryland Home Improvement Contractor or hold appropriate trade license (Electrical, Plumbing, HVAC, etc.)
Contractor must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Contractor must have active limited liability insurance with per occurrence limits equal to or greater than $1 million
Contractor must provide executed W-9 form
Applicant attestation of COVID-19 financial hardship required
One-time financial assistance per household only
No minimum credit score required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the WholeHome Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) grant application form. 2. Gather required income documentation: photo ID(s), recent paystubs (8 for weekly pay, 4 for bi-weekly), or employer verification letters; for self-employed, most recent 2 years of complete Federal Income Tax Returns; for Social Security/disability/pension/public assistance, award letters and current statements; for unemployment benefits, documentation of benefits; for no income, signed and notarized Zero Income Statement. 3. Provide documentation of home ownership. If others are on the deed but don't live there, provide proof of their different address. 4. Obtain at least one detailed estimate from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractor dated within the last 60 days. Contractor must complete the Bid Cover Page and provide: copy of current MHIC License or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance (current with $1M+ per occurrence limits), Letter of Good Standing, and executed W-9. 5. Submit completed application and all supporting documentation via email to Rehab.HAFApplications@Maryland.gov or by mail to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA Special Loan Programs- Rehab Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF), 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. 6. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. 7. Upon approval, sign commitment letter, grant agreement, rehabilitation contract, W-9 form, and final invoice from contractor(s) accepting work as completed. 8. Homeowner is responsible for managing the work and quality control; concerns about workmanship should be escalated to the Maryland Home Improvement Commission.

structured_extraction.program_description: The federal Housing Choice Voucher Program provides rental subsidies in the form of vouchers to eligible families or individuals to use toward housing payments. Local public housing agencies administer the program in their jurisdictions. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development administers this program statewide through regional offices and subcontractors.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental subsidies provided in the form of vouchers that eligible families or individuals can use toward housing payments. Voucher amounts are based on family income, family size, and local payment standards. Families typically pay 30% of their adjusted monthly income toward rent, with DHCD paying the difference between the family share and the approved rent (up to the payment standard). Payment standards are established based on Fair Market Rent for the jurisdiction. Families may move to units of their choice if the rent is reasonable and the unit meets Housing Quality Standards.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 30, 2026, at 5:00 PM (for Eastern Shore and Town of Elkton waitlist reopening)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible families or individuals seeking rental housing assistance. Priority includes extremely low-income families (at or below 30% of area median income), very low-income families, families with children, elderly families, families with disabilities, and homeless or formerly homeless individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental housing payments. Vouchers can be used for rental assistance in units throughout the jurisdiction that meet Housing Quality Standards. Special-purpose vouchers are available for Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (VASH), Family Unification Program (FUP), Mainstream Vouchers for persons with disabilities, and Non-Elderly Disabled (NED2) programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local public housing agencies in the following jurisdictions: Allegany County, Caroline County, Dorchester County, Frederick County, Garrett County, Kent County, Somerset County, Talbot County, Wicomico County, Worcester County, and the City of Cumberland and Town of Elkton. Waitlist is currently reopening for Eastern Shore counties (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Talbot, Somerset, Wicomico, Worcester) and the Town of Elkton, with application period from April 1, 2026 to April 30, 2026. The program administers 2,583 housing choice vouchers statewide.
requirements_list: Must meet eligibility criteria set by local public housing agency
Subject to lottery selection process for waitlist placement
Must have valid Social Security Number
Must establish U.S. citizenship or eligible immigration status
Must pass tenant screening for criminal history, credit, and rental history per PHA policies
Family income must not exceed limits set by HUD (generally 80% of area median income for initial eligibility, with targeting preference for families at or below 30% of area median income)
Must complete full application and verification process including income verification, asset verification, and non-financial factors verification
Must attend mandatory Housing Choice Voucher briefing to understand program rights and responsibilities
Must cooperate with all verification procedures and provide required documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit preliminary application through the Waitlist Status Portal during designated application periods or check status online. 2. Selected applicants are notified to attend an eligibility interview appointment at a regional office. 3. Attend mandatory briefing session to learn about program policies, rights, and responsibilities. 4. Complete full application with verification of income, assets, family composition, Social Security numbers, and citizenship/immigration status. 5. PHA conducts background screening and tenant screening. 6. Upon approval, family receives Housing Choice Voucher and housing search assistance. 7. Family locates suitable unit meeting Housing Quality Standards and landlord agrees to participate. 8. PHA conducts initial Housing Quality Standards inspection. 9. PHA executes Housing Assistance Payments contract with owner. 10. Family moves into unit and begins receiving rental assistance. In-person assistance is available at specific regional office locations for individuals needing support. Applications are accepted during designated periods; current reopening for Eastern Shore and Elkton is April 1-30, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Innovation Pilot Program provides low- or no-interest loans to local housing authorities or county governments partnering with housing developers to increase housing production and reward innovative solutions to housing scarcity. The program may also be used for projects where a county, in conjunction with a local housing authority or housing developer, purchases existing privately owned housing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low- or no-interest loans provided to local housing authorities or county governments partnering with housing developers through the Housing Innovation Fund. In FY 2026, $5 million total funding is available with up to $2.5 million maximum award per project, with a maximum of one award selection per jurisdiction. Loan terms are offered in two structures: Short-term loans (3-5 years) with approximately 3% interest rate, or longer-term loans (7-10 years) with approximately 5.5% interest rate. HIPP loans are subordinate loans, though positioning will be considered on a case-by-case basis. The fund may also be used for projects where a county purchases existing privately owned housing in conjunction with a local housing authority or housing developer. Loans will follow DHCD's Multifamily Fee Schedule.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public housing authorities and county governments partnering with housing developers to increase mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing production
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction and acquisition or rehabilitation of rental housing, including apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities. Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing with at least 20% of units for households earning 50% or less of area median income, or at least 40% of units for households earning 60% or less of area median income.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; all Maryland counties eligible; projects located within ¾ mile from rail station, within ENOUGH Act approved award locations and/or Just Community designations, or within Community of Opportunity receive priority consideration.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a public housing authority or county government
County must partner with a housing developer, or county must partner with PHA or developer to acquire existing housing
Sponsors must have an ownership interest in the project's ownership entity as demonstrated by organizational chart and/or partnership agreement
Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing

At least 20% of units must be set aside for households with gross annual income of 50% or less of area median income, OR at least 40% of units must be set aside for households with gross annual income of 60% or less of area median income
Eligible housing types include new construction and acquisition or rehabilitation of rental housing
Project must be ready for occupancy within two years of award selection date
Projects competing for HIPP funds must meet Threshold Criteria established in the Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide
Project must comply with affirmative fair housing marketing requirements
Project must comply with relocation and displacement requirements and tenant selection policies
Projects must meet Uniform Federal Accessibility Standards (UFAS) requirements and Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) standards
Maximum of one award selection per jurisdiction
Application fee of $2,500 must be submitted
Application must use the Housing Innovation Pilot Program Application Submission Kit and CDA Form 202 dated March 2025
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit pre-application meeting request form (optional but recommended). 2. Complete the Housing Innovation Pilot Program Application Submission Package including all required forms and exhibits. 3. Submit a complete electronic application via Procorem WorkCenter, including all attachments, exhibits, and clearly tabbed sections. 4. Submit CDA Form 202 Multifamily Rental Financing Application (dated March 2025) with estimated development and operating budgets and pro forma. 5. Include required certifications and threshold checklist. 6. Provide organization chart showing proposed or current ownership entity structure. 7. Submit evidence of development team qualifications including Form 203 (Developer's Qualifications) and property manager information. 8. Include general contractor qualifications (AIA Document A305 and supplement). 9. Provide architect information and qualifications. 10. Include letters of intent or commitment letters for all other financing sources (loans, grants, and equity). 11. Submit Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing Plan certification using HUD Form 935.2A. 12. Include minimum 3 references for developer and sponsors. 13. Submit applicant self-scoring. 14. Submit waiver request forms (if applicable) at least 15 days prior to application deadline (by May 4, 2026). 15. Submit application fee of $2,500 directly to Community Development Administration, Post Office Box 2524, Landover Hills, MD 20784 by or before application submission deadline. 16. All applications must be received by May 18, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. via Procorem WorkCenter. Incomplete applications will be returned and not processed. A scoring committee will review complete applications using established scoring criteria. DHCD may only select one project per jurisdiction. Awards will be recommended to CDA Director for approval, then submitted to Secretary for final approval and allocation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state income tax credit available to residents who are renovating or modifying their home to make it more accessible and enable independent living. Eligible applicants who make qualifying home modifications can receive a tax credit certificate to reduce their state tax liability.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit certificate is issued to approved applicants to reduce their Maryland state income tax liability for home renovations or modifications made to improve accessibility and enable independent living.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1st of the current calendar year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents making home renovations or modifications to improve accessibility and enable independent living.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home renovations and modifications to improve accessibility and enable independent living.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application and supporting documents online or by paper form before the June 1 deadline. DHCD reviews applications by August 31 and issues a tax credit certificate if approved. DHCD may contact applicants for additional information. The tax credit can also be applied during the tax filing process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides loans to help homeowners and rental property owners install or repair indoor plumbing in single-family and multi-unit residential properties, including wells, septic systems, water and sewer connections, plumbing fixtures, and related improvements. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development through a network of local administering agencies, including county housing offices, nonprofit organizations, and local banks.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans for indoor plumbing improvements with interest rates ranging from 0% to 6% based on ability to pay and household income. For households with income at or below 80% of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income, interest rates range from 4.5% to 6.0%. For households with income at or below 60% of median income, interest rates range from 0% to 4.5%. The maximum loan amount is generally 95 percent of the property value (accounting for any existing mortgages) for a maximum term of up to 30 years, with a typical maximum loan of $50,000. Deferred loans are available for borrowers needing health, safety, or accessibility improvements for families with incomes at or below 50% of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income. Deferred loan amounts may be forgiven annually for families with incomes below 30% of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income. Landlords are not eligible for deferred loans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes and owners of rental residential properties (one to twenty units) with household income at or below 80% of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income, owners of rental residential properties where units will be occupied by income-eligible households, homeowners with lead service lines or lead pipes inside their homes, and homeowners requiring plumbing repairs for health and safety reasons.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wells, septic tanks and drain fields, piping from septic systems, connection expenses to public water or sewer systems, plumbing fixtures and equipment including handicapped fixtures, additions and modifications to provide private space for toilet and bath facilities, sand mound systems, purification systems, percolation tests, alternative or innovative septic and water systems, replacing lead service lines and indoor plumbing, and critical plumbing repairs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Loan requests are generally processed directly by local governments for properties within their jurisdiction. Also available in Frederick County and Wicomico County through local administering agencies. Applicants in Washington D.C. PMSA counties (Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's) may have different income limits.
requirements_list: Single-family, owner-occupied house with inoperative or unsafe plumbing, or rental property with one to twenty units
Property must be structurally sound
Household income at or below 80% of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income for owner-occupants and rental unit residents
For rental properties, all tenants must have income at or below 80% of the statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income depending on property location
Landlords are not eligible for deferred loans
Must be an individual with limited income
Applicant must provide proof of home ownership including deed and current mortgage statement
Applicant must provide two months of recent paystubs or letter from employer, or two years of federal income tax returns, or other income verification documents
All other household members age 18 and over must have income documented
Critical repair must be identified with a bid from a licensed Maryland tradesperson or contractor not more than 60 days old
Contractor must provide current MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance with per occurrence limits of at least $1 million, Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9 form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants contact their local housing office or the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Special Loan Programs at (301) 429-7409, 877-218-8101, or 1-844-369-4150. Applicants must complete the Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program Application and submit it with required documentation including income verification, proof of home ownership, photo ID, property tax bill, homeowners insurance declaration page, and contractor bid with photos documenting the plumbing issues. All contractor documentation including MHIC license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and W-9 must be submitted with the bid. Completed applications and supporting documentation should be emailed to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mailed to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Loans are originated, packaged, and closed by a network of local administering agencies including county housing and community development offices, nonprofit organizations, and local banks.

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Hazard Reduction Grant and Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant and loan program funded in part by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development to assist Maryland homeowners and landlords lessen the risk of lead poisoning and preserve the housing stock by reducing or eliminating lead-based paint hazards in residential buildings and daycare centers. The program also includes the Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids Lead Initiative, which helps families with children who have elevated blood lead levels reduce lead exposure in homes built before 1978.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $25,000 per eligible property for lead abatement services. For-profit sponsors must provide 20% match; nonprofit sponsors and owner-occupants with income above 80% of median require 10% match; owner-occupants with limited income (below 80% of median) require no match. Amortizing loans available at 0%-7% interest over 20 years with maximum unit amount of $25,000. Deferred loans available at 0% interest over 20 years with 100% debt-to-value ratio (exceptions available for owner-occupant properties with lead-affected households). Loan forgiveness may be considered if no equity is available upon resale, transfer, or after 20 years. Funding is available statewide except in the City of Baltimore until April 1, 2029. The Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids Lead Initiative provides funding for lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed for eligible families with children who have elevated blood lead levels. Licensed day care centers are eligible to apply. Clearance testing is required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners and landlords with lead hazards in their properties, including single-family homes, multi-family residential units, rental properties, and licensed childcare facilities. Also available to families with children under 19 years old who have elevated blood lead levels and live in Maryland homes built before 1978. For Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids, eligible children must have a blood lead level of 5 micrograms per deciliter or higher.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction or elimination of lead-based paint hazards, including lead abatement services performed by a licensed and accredited lead abatement contractor, and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide; grant funding available statewide except in the City of Baltimore.
requirements_list: Property must be owner-occupied single family home or rental property
Must be registered with Maryland Department of the Environment Lead Poisoning Prevention Program
Units must be structurally sound upon completion of lead hazard reduction activity
Licensed childcare facilities may also be eligible
Clearance testing is required
For Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids: child must be under 19 years old
For Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids: child must live in Maryland
For Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids: child must have a recent blood lead test of 5 micrograms per deciliter or higher
For Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids: child must be enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid or Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program (MCHP)
For Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids: child must spend 10 hours or more per week in the location where lead exposure occurred
For grants: must be in target area or must plan to utilize an innovative lead hazard reduction treatment
For grants: underwriting must show no affordability to repay loan or property does not have sufficient value to secure debt
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Households are recommended to start with a free in-home comprehensive assessment to identify needed improvements and enroll in programs best suited to their situation. Submit application through Special Loan Programs. Contact DHCD for application details. For Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids, contact the Environmental Health Help Line at 866-703-3266, contact your local health department, or email mdh.healthyhomes@maryland.gov for eligibility and application information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that issues tax-exempt bonds on behalf of Maryland counties, municipalities, and their agencies to finance infrastructure projects that serve the community. The Community Development Administration manages the bond issuance and loans the bond proceeds to local governments at market rates determined by the pooled bond issue. The program provides long-term capital financing with advantageous terms and reduces issuance costs through economies of scale by pooling local demand.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bonds are issued and the proceeds are loaned to local governments. The interest rate is based on market conditions at the time of bond sale and the rate attained on the pooled bond issue. Local governments repay the debt and pay their pro-rata share of bond issuance costs. Loan terms are set by the local government but cannot exceed the useful life of the project or 30 years, whichever is less. Loans can range from $150,000 to $10 million or more.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis - applications accepted on ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland counties, municipalities, and their agencies that need long-term capital financing for community infrastructure projects and do not routinely issue bonds or have limited resources to finance independently.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Street lighting, landscaping, sidewalks and public space improvements; public safety vehicles and equipment; water production, treatment, storage and distribution systems; storm water control and sewer collection and treatment facilities; government office and meeting facilities; police, fire, transportation, education, health, recreation, maintenance and other service-related facilities; refinancing of existing debt for eligible projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties and municipalities.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland county, municipality, or their agency
Applicant must have legal authority to construct, operate, and maintain the proposed project
Applicant must have legal authority to pledge security for and repay the proposed loan
Applicant must have legal authority to pledge income tax payments and various other shared revenue from the State
Project must support an essential physical element of a municipality's public service system
Project must meet federal tax law requirements
Project must be undertaken by or on behalf of a local government, including its agencies
Loan term cannot exceed the useful life of the project or 30 years, whichever is less
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The local government completes an application that requests information similar to what a bond rating agency would require to evaluate creditworthiness. Technical assistance is available; local governments can submit an Expression of Interest form outlining the proposed project or specific questions to request technical assistance from the Community Development Administration. When bonds are issued depends on the volume and frequency of participation by local governments.

structured_extraction.program_name: Low Income Housing Tax Credit Program (LIHTC)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit program that encourages private sector investment in the construction and rehabilitation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. Tax credits are awarded on a competitive basis to nonprofit and for-profit sponsors of eligible housing projects. State and local LIHTC-allocating agencies have the authority to issue tax credits to buy, rehabilitate, or build rental housing targeted at lower-income households.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits are awarded to sponsors of qualifying residential rental buildings based on criteria outlined in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP). The tax credit equals the applicable percentage of the qualified basis of each qualified low-income rental housing building, as determined by the IRS. Project sponsors or their investor partners claim the tax credit on their federal income tax return. Ten percent of the state's annual allocation is set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors. Buildings must remain in compliance for a minimum of 40 years during the initial compliance period, followed by an extended use period of at least 15 additional years. Competitive funding rounds are held once or twice annually. Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible for tax credits outside of the competitive process. During the Extended Use Period (after year 15), owners must continue to operate projects in accordance with LIHTC covenant requirements, though monitoring becomes less frequent (at least once every 5 years). Owners must obtain, verify, and document tenant annual income at initial certification and first annual recertification, then conduct full recertifications at least every five years. Annual household self-declarations of income are required in non-recertification years but do not require third-party verification.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Competitive funding rounds held once or twice annually; applications accepted on rolling basis within designated funding rounds
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and nonprofit sponsors, as well as government entities, developing or preserving low-income rental housing projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction, rehabilitation, or purchase of residential rental housing for low- and moderate-income families.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Priority Funding Areas receive emphasis. Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible outside of the competitive process. All 24 Maryland counties are eligible, though some areas receive priority consideration based on Qualified Census Tracts (QCTs) and Difficult Development Areas (DDAs) designations.
requirements_list: Residential rental building must be placed in service in or within two years after the year the allocation is made
Building must provide at least in part for low-income occupancy

Owner must rent either 20 percent of units to households with incomes at 50 percent or less of area median income, or 40 percent of units to households with incomes at 60 percent or less of area median income (minimum set-aside election)
Building must comply with tenant income and maximum rent level requirements

Building must remain in compliance and is subject to a covenant to enforce compliance for a minimum of 40 years (initial compliance period) followed by at least 15 additional years (extended use period)
Awards based on criteria outlined in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP)
Projects must comply with requirements regarding tenant income, maximum rent levels, and percentage of low-income occupancy
Residential rental units must be used on a non-transient basis (except for transitional housing for the homeless)
Annual certifications of continuing program compliance required from project owners
For nonprofit sponsors receiving 10% set-aside allocation: nonprofit entity must materially participate in operation of development
Tax credit projects not already monitored by DCA in connection with other funding sources will be assigned a project manager and portfolio administrator at end of compliance period

Owners must maintain detailed records including total number of residential units, percentage of low-income units, rent charged, applicable utility allowances, unit vacancies, tenant income certifications, and supporting documentation

Physical inspections and file reviews conducted by DCA annually during initial 15-year compliance period; during extended use period (years 16-30+), inspections conducted at least once every five years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Tax credits are awarded on a competitive basis through funding rounds held once or twice annually, based on criteria in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP). Applicants should review the current QAP for specific evaluation criteria, procedures, and scoring mechanisms. Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible for tax credits outside of the competitive process through a non-competitive pathway. During funding rounds, applications are submitted to the Community Development Administration (CDA) within the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. CDA reviews applications for compliance with program requirements and QAP criteria. Successful applicants receive a tax credit allocation. Before IRS Form 8609 is issued, the owner's certified public accountant must certify the total costs for each building and verify all program requirements have been met. Upon receiving the cost certification, CDA completes and executes Part I of the IRS Form 8609 and sends it to the owner. The owner then completes and executes Part II and submits it to the IRS when filing their tax return. A fully executed copy must be forwarded to CDA. Application documents and forms are available in the Multifamily Document Library on DHCD's website. Project owners are responsible for maintaining compliance throughout the 40-year initial compliance period and subsequent 15+ year extended use period. Annual Owner's Certifications of Continuing Program Compliance must be submitted by annual deadlines published in CDA notices. During the compliance period, CDA conducts annual physical inspections and file reviews. For projects entering the extended use period, the Division of Credit Assurance (DCA) assumes monitoring responsibilities with less frequent inspections (minimum once every 5 years). Owners must notify CDA of any changes in ownership, management, or significant project modifications.

structured_extraction.program_name: MEER: Maryland Emergency Education Relief Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to schools, libraries, and anchor institutions to help close the digital divide for K-12 students and school staff by funding internet access and devices needed for remote classroom connection.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $50,000 to $350,000 covering up to 100% of eligible program costs for projects completed between September 1, 2021 and September 15, 2022. Total MEER program funding awarded: $4,999,251.80. Grants were awarded to eligible organizations across multiple counties including Baltimore, Baltimore City, Cecil, Montgomery, Prince George's, Howard, and Wicomico counties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: K-12 schools, libraries, anchor institutions, and community organizations serving students lacking internet access or devices for remote learning
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Internet access and devices needed for K-12 students and school staff to connect to classroom services, including broadband access for residential facilities and community centers serving students
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide, with awards distributed across multiple counties including Baltimore, Baltimore City, Cecil, Montgomery, Prince George's, Howard, and Wicomico counties
requirements_list: Applicant must be a school, library, anchor institution, or community organization
Project must serve K-12 students and related school staff or residents of community facilities
Eligible program costs must be incurred between September 1, 2021 and September 15, 2022
Grant awards ranged from approximately $34,000 to $250,000

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development provides funding to designated and affiliate Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods to build capacity and achieve community revitalization and economic development goals in Sustainable Community areas throughout the state.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Designated Main Street Maryland Communities with full accreditation receive expected awards of $33,000 each. Designated Main Street Maryland Communities accredited as affiliate receive expected awards of $25,000 each. Main Street Maryland Aspiring Communities receive expected awards of $12,000 each. Funds are for operating expenses only, including salary, professional services contracts, technology costs, staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, and other costs related to administering the Main Street program. No funding match is required. Projects and activities must be completed within one year. The performance period is one year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Designated and aspiring Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating expenses only, including salary, professional services contracts, technology costs, staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, and placemaking initiatives. Funds support projects and activities that align with the applicant's annual work plan and contribute to the community's transformation strategy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated Sustainable Community areas throughout Maryland, including designated and aspiring Main Street Maryland communities, affiliate Main Street communities, and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods.
requirements_list: Must be a designated or aspiring Main Street Maryland community
Must be located in a designated Sustainable Community area
Projects and activities must align with the applicant's annual work plan
Projects and activities must contribute to the community's transformation strategy
All projects and activities must be completed within one year
Organization profile must include all required documents before submitting application

Current Operating Assistance Grant Program awardees must be in full compliance with all existing award agreements, including meeting all reporting deadlines and submitting all required final reports and payment requests from prior awards
Must submit evidence of nonprofit status (Bylaws, Articles of Incorporation, IRS Determination Letter)
Must submit evidence of good standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must submit evidence of charitable registration from Maryland Secretary of State
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online through the DHCD Project Portal at https://projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us/. To apply, register as a new user in the Portal system by selecting 'New User?' and completing the registration request form. Approval may take up to 72 hours. New organizations should request access and submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline to expedite processing. First-time applicants must contact a project manager for eligibility verification and system access. Ensure your organization profile includes all required documents before submitting your application. Submit your complete application through the Project Portal. Training documents, including a program overview and step-by-step application guide, are available in the DHCD Project Portal. A virtual application training was scheduled for March 3, 2026. Individual technical assistance sessions are available via Calendly. Late applications will not be accepted. Applications must align with the Main Street annual work plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: An emergency program that provides financial assistance through loans to help small businesses and nonprofit organizations recover from disasters. The program is activated by the Secretary of the Department of Housing and Community Development for specific disasters.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides emergency loans to help small businesses and nonprofits cover costs related to disaster recovery, including renovations, repairs and replacement of furniture, fixtures and equipment, inventory replacement, loss of revenues, operating and leasing expense assistance, and other recovery-related working capital needs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not specified - program is not currently active
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based small businesses and nonprofit organizations located in commercial spaces that have been affected by qualifying disasters
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovations, repairs and replacement of furniture fixtures and equipment, inventory replacement, loss of revenues, operating and leasing expense assistance, and other costs associated with business recovery including working capital
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is limited to businesses located in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Howard County, Frederick County, and Washington County that show evidence of damage or loss associated with qualifying disaster events (such as the May 2018 flooding events)
requirements_list: Maryland-based small business
Business must be located in a commercial space
Must show proof of insurance status
Must be located in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Howard County, Frederick County, or Washington County
Must show evidence of damage or loss associated with qualifying disaster events
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Business Lending Programs for application procedures. The program is currently not active and must be activated by the Secretary for specific disasters.

structured_extraction.program_description: A credit enhancement program that supports the growth and success of small businesses in Priority Funding Areas throughout Maryland. The program enables private lenders to establish a loan loss reserve fund from fees paid by lenders, borrowers, and the State of Maryland, leveraging State funds to develop small business loans.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit enhancement program that allows private lenders to establish a loan loss reserve fund. Enrolled loan amounts range from $10,000 to $1,000,000. Borrowers and lenders each contribute typically 1.5 percent of the loan amount, and the Maryland Capital Access Program matches that amount with 3 percent, for a total reserve of 6 percent of the original loan amount. The reserve protects lenders against loan defaults. In the event of loan default and after the lender's normal collection methods are exhausted, the lender files a claim to draw from the reserve account. The program leverages $1 million of State funds to develop approximately $33 million in small business loans.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, including nonprofit organizations, located in Maryland's Priority Funding Areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, equipment purchases, real estate purchases, and other business expenses. Cannot be used for passive real estate ownership, residential or transient living facilities, community facilities like fire stations or hospitals, certain adult entertainment or leisure facilities, or sectarian religious instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects financed must be located in a Priority Funding Area approved by the Maryland Department of Planning for State funding in accordance with the Smart Growth Act of 1997.
requirements_list: Business must be located in Maryland's Priority Funding Areas
Enrolled loan amounts must range from $10,000 to $1,000,000
Borrower and lender must each contribute to the reserve fund
Project cannot involve passive real estate ownership
Project cannot be residential or transient living facilities
Project cannot be certain types of facilities such as community halls, fire stations, hospitals, colleges, or universities

Project cannot involve adult bookstores, adult video shops, adult entertainment facilities, check cashing facilities, gambling facilities, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn or gun shops, tanning salons, or tattoo parlors
Loan proceeds cannot be used for sectarian religious instruction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A small business applies to a participating lender. The lender underwrites and enrolls an appropriate loan. The lender, borrower, and the Maryland Capital Access Program each deposit their contributions into a reserve account. A one-page enrollment form with summary information is submitted to the Maryland Capital Access Program by the lender.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) / Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) and Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) are state and federally funded programs that help low-income Maryland households afford energy costs. MEAP provides annual grants paid directly to heating suppliers to assist with heating expenses, helps pay utility and fuel bills, minimizes heating crises, and makes energy costs more affordable for homeowners, renters, and boarders. OHEP provides bill assistance grants for gas, electric, and water utility bills, including shut-off prevention and service restoration assistance. Additionally, MEAP helps eligible households repair or replace heating, cooling, and water heating systems at no cost through a home assessment and contractor work process. The programs operate year-round on a rolling basis until funding is depleted. Energy assistance received does not reduce other public assistance benefits such as Temporary Cash Assistance, Food Stamps, or Social Security benefits.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants are awarded directly to heating suppliers to help pay heating expenses. Grants for gas and electricity bill payments help prevent utility disconnection and restore service. One application covers both MEAP and the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP). Benefit amounts vary by income level, household size, and fuel type. Financial eligibility examples: one person income up to $2,608/month; two people income up to $3,525/month; no asset test required. Households may receive a benefit once per program year (July 1 to June 30). Additionally, eligible households may receive at-no-cost repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and water heating systems based on a home assessment and funding availability. Due to limited funding for equipment repair/replacement, applicants may be placed on a waitlist. Special flood assistance is available for homes in Allegany or Garrett County affected by flooding. Energy assistance grants do not need to be paid back.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis until funding is depleted; program year July 1 to June 30. Applications for heating assistance accepted between July and May each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Maryland homeowners, renters, and boarders (including roomers) who need help paying heating, electric, gas, and water utility bills; households facing utility disconnection or service shutoff; and eligible households with non-functioning heating, cooling, and/or water heating systems. Households automatically income-eligible if receiving Utility Bill Pay Assistance through OHEP, SNAP, TANF, SSI, or HUD housing assistance programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of heating, gas, electricity, and water utility bills; prevention of utility service disconnection and restoration of service; repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and water heating systems; reducing energy-related crises and making energy costs more affordable.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Local administration varies by county. Special flood assistance available for Allegany and Garrett County residents affected by flooding. In-person locations include: Baltimore County (Drumcastle Government Center, 6401 York Road, Baltimore, MD 21212); Montgomery County (1301 Piccard Drive, 4th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850); Washington County (117 Summit Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21740); Frederick County (420 East Patrick Street, PO Box 3929, Frederick, MD 21705); St. Mary's County (senior activity centers via Tri-County Community Action Committee).
requirements_list: Household income must be at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Level based on household size (e.g., one person: $2,608/month; two people: $3,525/month); no asset test required
Must be a homeowner, renter, boarder, or roomer
Completed and signed application listing all household members
Copy of photo ID for the applicant
Copy of Social Security Cards for all household members (at least one legal resident with a Social Security number required; applicant does not need one)
Proof of citizenship for all household members
Proof of gross household income for the last 30 days for all household members (including unemployment, Social Security, etc.)
Proof of residency (lease or mortgage statement)
Copy of electric and/or heating bills
If heat is included in rent, rental or living arrangements verification required

Eligible participants automatically income-eligible if receiving: Utility Bill Pay Assistance through OHEP, Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), Supplemental Security Income (SSI), or HUD housing assistance programs
For equipment repair/replacement: must have a non-functioning heating, cooling, and/or water heating system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at MyDHR (mydhrbenefits.dhr.state.md.us) or MyMDThink (mymdthink.maryland.gov), or download/print the application in English or Spanish. Paper applications can be mailed, emailed, dropped off in person, or submitted at document drop boxes at local offices. Call 1-800-332-6347 to request paper applications. Phone appointments available at local offices. In Montgomery County, call 240-777-4450; in Frederick County, call 301-600-2410 or email ohep@cityoffrederickmd.gov; in Washington County, call (301) 797-4161 or email WashingtonCountyOHEP@wccac.org; in Calvert County, call (301) 274-4474 ext. 1. In Baltimore County, apply in person at Towson office (no appointment required, Mon–Fri 8am–4:30pm). In St. Mary's County, applications available at senior activity centers through the Tri-County Community Action Committee. For equipment repair/replacement (DHCD MEAP), submit application and required documents to the DHCD office; once eligibility is determined, a local agency will schedule a home assessment, then a contractor will complete recommended work. Check application status at myohepstatus.org. Processing typically takes 45 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to improve the exterior facades of businesses located in Maryland Sustainable Communities. Applicants (local governments, groups of local governments, and community development organizations) establish a grants fund and develop an application process for businesses to improve their building exteriors, supporting community revitalization.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided to local governments, groups of local governments, and community development organizations to capitalize a local grants fund. Local businesses can then apply to that fund for capital costs related to exterior facade improvements. Eligible uses include signage, exterior painting, storefront reconstruction, siding, exterior lighting, window and door upgrades, public-facing masonry or cornices, murals, removal of unattractive exterior finishes, and roofs. Individual business improvements must be between $1,000 and $50,000 of MFIP funding during a single award cycle. Ineligible uses include any improvements banned by local building codes or zoning, improvements outside designated Sustainable Communities, interior work, electric charging stations, solar panels, changes to completed improvements within 12 months, and improvements for prohibited businesses or properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, groups of local governments, and community development organizations (such as community development corporations or Main Street organizations) serving Maryland Sustainable Communities, as well as businesses and municipalities seeking to improve commercial property exteriors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements to properties occupied by businesses to make the outside appearance of the building more attractive. Eligible uses include signage, exterior painting, storefront reconstruction, siding, exterior lighting, window and door upgrades, public-facing masonry or cornices, murals, removal of unattractive exterior finishes, and roofs. Projects should prioritize aesthetic improvements over routine maintenance and improvements on or attached to primary elevations of commercial properties. Interior work, electric charging stations, solar panels, and routine maintenance are ineligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within a designated Maryland Sustainable Community. Applicants should use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility.
requirements_list: Project must be located in a designated Sustainable Community
Project should capitalize on the strengths of a community while addressing its challenges to revitalization
Project should help achieve a local government's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Applicants must establish a local grants fund and develop their own application process for local businesses
Individual business improvements must be between $1,000 and $50,000 of MFIP funding during a single award cycle
Work completed prior to receiving a letter of commitment is ineligible for funding
Local program guidelines must include criteria for rating qualified businesses and awarding grants
All MFIP projects are subject to the Maryland Historical Trust Act and Federal Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
Properties over 50 years old must comply with historic preservation standards
Site control documentation, photographs, written consent from landlord/lessee, project description, two cost estimates, and proof of good standing with the State must be submitted
Applicants must provide evidence of expenditures including receipts or canceled checks
Applicants must maintain valid and sufficient insurance coverage
Applicants must maintain the property and improvements including promptly removing graffiti
Applicants agree to return pro-rated grant money if improvements are removed within two years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants (local governments, groups of local governments, and community development organizations) apply to DHCD to receive MFIP funding to capitalize a local grants fund. Awardees develop and enforce their own program guidelines that comply with state requirements and establish a local application process for businesses. Local program guidelines must include criteria for rating and awarding grants to qualified businesses. Awardees are encouraged to include matching fund requirements, additional ineligible uses, requirements for broad distribution of grants, and geographic targeting. Once the local fund is established, individual businesses apply to the local program (not directly to DHCD) with required documentation including site control evidence, existing condition photographs, landlord/lessee consent, project description, two cost estimates, and proof of good standing with Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. All improvements must undergo historic preservation review before work begins. Applications can be submitted through Main Street organizations or directly to the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Housing Counseling Fund (MHCF) supports non-profit and local government organizations that provide a range of housing counseling services, as well as free or low-cost legal assistance to avoid foreclosure and eviction. Awards are made annually on a competitive basis. HUD-approved housing counseling agencies with HUD-certified counselors on staff receive priority funding consideration.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual competitive grants providing operating support for housing counseling programs including homebuyer education, pre-purchase counseling, foreclosure counseling, rental counseling, and financial capability coaching. Also supports non-profit legal services providers assisting homeowners concerned about foreclosure and renters concerned about eviction.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Poverty Solutions Team, Division of Homeless Solutions
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and local government agencies providing housing counseling and legal assistance services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating support for housing counseling programs including homebuyer education, pre-purchase counseling, foreclosure counseling, rental counseling, financial capability coaching, and legal services assistance for homeowners facing foreclosure and renters facing eviction
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide
