requirements_list: Must be a non-profit organization or local government agency
Must provide housing counseling services or free or low-cost legal assistance
Grantees must submit quarterly progress reports by the fifteenth of the month following the end of each quarter
Priority funding consideration is given to HUD-approved housing counseling agencies with HUD-certified counselors on staff
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through competitive process by emailing the program team at mhcf.dhcd@maryland.gov to request an application. Grantees must report quarterly on progress during the grant term.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program provides affordable loans to homeowners to address critical health and safety issues and bring properties into compliance with applicable building codes and standards. The program supports rehabilitation of owner-occupied single-family homes, funding repairs related to health, safety, accessibility, and structural integrity.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with interest rates based on applicant income and ability to repay. Generally, the maximum loan is $50,000 or up to 110% of home equity, whichever is less. Interest rates range from 0% to 6% depending on the applicant's ability to pay. For households earning at or below 80% of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area (PMSA) median income, interest rates are 4.5%-6.0%. For households earning at or below 60% of area median income, interest rates are 0%-4.5%. Maximum loan term is 30 years. Loans exceeding $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a deed of trust mortgage on the property. Families with incomes at or below 50% of statewide or Washington D.C. PMSA median income may qualify for deferred principal and interest payments if necessary for project feasibility. There is a minimum loan amount of $5,000. Maximum initial deposit is 33% of total project cost. In some cases, grants may be available based on affordability and program guidelines. The program is primarily designed to provide loans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes with household income not exceeding 80 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical health and safety repairs including mold remediation, gas leaks, roof repair and replacement, gutters, asbestos abatement, vermiculite removal, lead abatement, combustion appliance repair and replacement, chimney repair, foundation and sub-space waterproofing and drainage with bulk water mitigation by drain tile and sump pump, radon mitigation, electrical hazards and knob-and-tube removal inclusive of necessary service upgrades, electrical upgrades for future home electrification (less than 100A to 200A upgrades), plumbing issues, water and well repairs, septic and sewer work, windows and doors for health and safety or water intrusion, structural repairs (atrophy, rot, insect, settling, storm-related), accessibility improvements for disabled and seniors including chairlifts, handicap ramps, bars, railings, and doors, fall prevention measures (handrails, rubber treads, bathroom grab bars), ductwork upgrades and installations (primarily for solid fuel-burning households—mainly in Allegany and Garrett counties), building shell stabilization (repair/replace missing sheetrock on exterior walls, point up deteriorated masonry that allows water infiltration), pest treatments (rats, roaches, and mice), HVAC replacement for end of service life, and lead paint removal.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. All loan requests are generally processed directly by local governments for properties within their jurisdiction. Applicants should contact their local housing office by county. The program is administered through a network of county housing and community development offices and nonprofit organizations.
requirements_list: Household income cannot exceed 80 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income (see income limits document for specific thresholds by household size and area)
Property must be an owner-occupied single-family home (duplexes, townhomes, condos, manufactured homes, and mobile homes are excluded)
Applicant must be owner-occupant and primary resident; anyone on the deed but not occupying the property must provide proof of residence elsewhere
Work must be performed by licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement Contractor (MHIC) or other licensed trade professionals (electrical, plumbing, HVAC, etc.)

Contractor must provide current MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance (current with per occurrence limits equal to or greater than $1 million), Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9 form
Bid must be from lowest qualifying contractor and should not be more than 60 days old
Bid must include photographs documenting the critical repairs, contractor's phone number and email address
Grand total of all bids should not exceed $50,000
Applicant must provide completed application with all required documentation
No minimum credit score required; however, active bankruptcy or foreclosure will disqualify applicants until dismissed for a minimum of 2 years
For properties built before 1978, lead-based paint disclosure and acknowledgment required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Contact your local housing office by county or Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Special Loan Programs at (301) 429-7409 or toll free (877) 218-8101 for application materials. 2) Obtain at least one detailed estimate within the past 60 days from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractor or licensed trade professional documenting the scope of work and critical repairs needed, with supporting photographs. 3) Contractor must complete the Bid Cover Form and provide their current MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and signed W-9 form. 4) Complete the Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program Application with all required supporting documentation including income verification, proof of homeownership, and personal financial information. 5) Submit completed application and all documentation to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mail to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. 6) DHCD staff will review the estimate to verify the work meets health and safety requirements and that the contractor meets State of Maryland business requirements. 7) Once approved, applicant will sign commitment letter, rehabilitation contract, construction agreement, and W-9 form. 8) Local administering agencies including county housing offices and nonprofit organizations originate, package, and close loans.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative that reduces interest rates on loans for certified Minority Business Enterprises and Small Businesses by up to 2%. The program works by having the Maryland State Treasurer's Office deposit funds with participating banks at a reduced rate, which allows those banks to offer borrowers lower-cost loans.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Borrowers can receive up to a 2% discount on loan interest rates. The program leverages $50 million of state funds. Loans must be for a term of 10 years or less, have fixed rates with one disbursement, and be used for projects located in Maryland. Loan points cannot exceed 1% of the loan amount. The interest rate reduction applies for the full term of the loan as long as the borrower remains in good standing. Participating lenders include Bank Annapolis, Industrial Bank, and Columbia Bank.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified Minority Business Enterprises and Small Businesses in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects or activities located in Maryland. Loans cannot be used for the furtherance of sectarian or religious purposes or instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Maryland. The program is statewide.
requirements_list: Borrower must be a certified Minority Business Enterprise in good standing with the Maryland Department of Transportation, OR a small business in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Borrower must notify the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development prior to obtaining the loan
Borrower must obtain the loan from a participating financial institution enrolled in the program
Loan must have a fixed rate or be a term loan with one disbursement
Loan term cannot exceed 10 years
Loan proceeds must be for a project or activity located in Maryland
Lender points cannot exceed 1% of the loan amount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The eligible applicant or participating lender submits a brief application via the Internet or paper form to the Linked Deposit Program at the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. The department verifies the applicant's eligibility and forwards the application to all enrolled banks or notifies the lender of the borrower's eligibility. The borrower receives a list of participating banks and contacts them to complete their full loan application. The participating bank underwrites the loan with an interest rate up to 2% lower than standard rates. Upon loan approval and acceptance, the bank enrolls the loan in the program. The Maryland State Treasurer's Office then deposits funds equal to the loan amount with the bank at a reduced interest rate.

structured_extraction.program_description: The State of Maryland provides a tax credit of up to $1,000 per year to eligible renters to help offset the share of rent that goes toward property taxes. The program recognizes that renters indirectly pay property taxes and deserve similar relief as homeowners. Eligibility is based on gross household income compared with the amount paid toward rent. Eligible renters must be age 60 or older, under 60 with at least one dependent child under 18, or 100% disabled. Renters must have lived in Maryland for at least six months of the prior year, have a bona fide leasehold interest and actually pay rent, and meet net worth and income thresholds. In Montgomery County, qualifying renters also automatically receive a supplemental county check equal to 50% of the state credit amount with no separate application required.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A direct check payment (tax credit) of up to $1,000 per year to eligible renters, calculated based on the difference between 15% of annual rent (excluding utilities) and a tax threshold determined by income. Renters in Montgomery County additionally receive a county supplement equal to 50% of the state credit amount, automatically mailed once per year with no separate application required. Combined net worth of applicant and spouse or co-tenant must be under $200,000 as of December 31. A new application must be filed every year if applicant wishes to be considered for a tax credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland renters who have lived in Maryland for at least 6 months of the previous year, are age 60 or older, under 60 with at least one dependent child under 18, or are 100% disabled, and who meet applicable income and rent requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To offset the share of rent that goes toward property taxes; provides rental cost relief and reduces state tax liability for eligible renters.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applications may be submitted online through the One Stop portal at www.taxcredits.sdat.maryland.gov or mailed to State Department of Assessments & Taxation, Renters' Tax Credit Program, P.O. Box 49006, Baltimore, MD 21297. Montgomery County renters who qualify for the state credit automatically receive an additional county supplement.
requirements_list: Must have a bona fide leasehold interest in the property and be legally responsible for the rent

First time applicants and those who moved during the previous year must submit a copy of lease(s), rental agreement, cancelled checks, money order receipts or other proof of rent paid; other applicants must submit upon request
The principal residence must be in Maryland and where the applicant resided for at least six (6) months in calendar year 2024
The dwelling may be any type of rented residence or a mobile home pad, but may not include any unit rented from a public housing authority or from an exempt organization
Applicant, spouse and/or co-tenant(s) must have a combined net worth of less than $200,000 as of December 31

Must be age 60 or older as of December 31, 2024, OR 100% totally and permanently disabled as of December 31, 2024 (with proof from Social Security Administration, federal retirement system, Federal Armed Services, or local City/County Health Officer), OR under age 60 with at least one dependent under age 18 living with applicant during the year and listed on Federal Income Tax Return
For age 60 or older: income of $20,000 with rent over $423 per month may qualify (Chart 1 provides income and rent thresholds)
For 100% disabled: same standards as seniors

For under 60 with dependents: must have at least one dependent under 18; did not receive federal or state housing subsidies; 2024 total gross household income below limits in Chart 2 (e.g., $20,440 for 2 persons, $25,820 for 3 persons, $31,200 for 4 persons)
Unit must not be tax-exempt
Utilities included in rent reduce the amount eligible for credit (e.g., 18% reduction if heat and electricity are included)
If applicant is under age 60 with dependent children, must include copy of dependent social security card(s) and birth certificate(s)
If receiving rental assistance/subsidy, must disclose source; renters receiving federal or state housing subsidies do not qualify if under 60 with dependents
If renting from related person including in-laws, must disclose name and relationship
Cannot own any real estate in Maryland or elsewhere (or must disclose if owned)
If filed Federal Income Tax Return, copy of completed return including all schedules and forms must be submitted with application
If income derived from partnership or corporation, copy of partnership return (Form 1065 with Schedule K-1) and/or corporate return (Form 1120 or 1120S with Schedule K-1) must be included
Social Security Form SSA-1099, Railroad Retirement Verification, or Rate Letter must be included as applicable
All accompanying schedules and documents must be submitted; original documents should not be sent
Monthly rent should not include subsidies paid on applicant's behalf (such as HUD/Section 8 payments), monthly fees for services (meals, pet fees, garage charges, late charges), or security deposits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File a new application every year. Apply online at www.taxcredits.sdat.maryland.gov or download and mail a paper application (Form RTC-1) to State Department of Assessments & Taxation, Renters' Tax Credit Program, P.O. Box 49006, Baltimore, MD 21297. Applications must be submitted by October 1 each year. A properly completed application requires all questions answered, the form signed, copies of the entire Federal Income Tax return with all schedules and forms, and necessary Social Security Form (SSA-1099), Railroad Retirement Verification, or Rate Letter. Do not staple documents and do not send original documents. Find your total gross household income and monthly rent before applying. For questions, contact sdat.renters@maryland.gov, call 410-767-4433 (Baltimore Area) or 1-800-944-7403 (Toll Free). Montgomery County renters who are approved for the state credit do not need to submit a separate application for the county supplement—the state notifies the county, which automatically calculates 50% of the credit and mails a check to the renter. Applicant may later be requested to submit additional information to verify reported information, which may include a statement of living expenses when insufficient means appear to exist to pay rent and other living expenses.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative funded through federal SSBCI allocations, administered in partnership with the Maryland Department of Commerce and the Maryland Technology Development Corporation. The program provides loans and equity investments to support small businesses, with a focus on communities and areas with high concentrations of small, micro, and Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individual (SEDI) businesses that have limited opportunities for growth and access to traditional capital. Funding is deployed through various mechanisms including capital access programs, loan participations, loan guarantees, collateral support, and venture equity programs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_prioritized_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The SSBCI Direct Loan Program offers flexible loans to small businesses. Loan amounts range from a minimum of $500,000 to a maximum of $5 million, with total project costs not exceeding $20 million. Loans require a minimum 1:1 private capital match. Eligible uses include costs to sustain or expand a small business such as purchasing machinery or equipment and working capital, as well as owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation (renovation projects must be at least 51% owner-occupied upon completion; new construction must be at least 60% owner-occupied). Loan terms are flexible, with terms of up to 30 years, and senior or subordinate loan positions available. Interest rates are determined by underwriting analysis. Program fees include a $250 application fee, $250 closing fee, and 1% origination fee. Special focus is given to projects with significant community impacts, including job retention or creation, child care access, fresh food access, and community revitalization.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis. Contact program managers for additional details.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with fewer than 500 employees; micro-businesses; and Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI) in Maryland seeking to grow with limited access to traditional capital.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs to sustain or expand a small business, such as purchasing machinery or equipment and working capital; owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation (renovation projects must be at least 51% owner-occupied upon completion; new construction must be at least 60% owner-occupied upon completion). NOT permitted: passive real estate investment, refinancing existing debt with the same lender, tax repayment (delinquent federal or state income taxes unless repayment plan is in place, or trust/escrow taxes such as payroll and sales taxes), equity buyouts (except for majority ESOPs or worker co-ops), lobbying activities, federally guaranteed loans, conflicts of interest, or prohibited refinancing of tenant improvement loans from landlords.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland, with targeting of communities and areas with high concentrations of small, micro, and socially and economically disadvantaged businesses.

Adequate collateral required
Minimum loan amount of $500,000 and maximum of $5 million

Technical assistance is available through the MD Business Opportunity Center and F3Tech SEDI Program, which provide financial consulting and loan packaging support. Email dhcd.businesslending@maryland.gov for a consultation about whether SSBCI is the right solution for your business.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Town Manager Circuit Rider Program assists small town and city governments with building their administrative capacity. The program provides grants to hire professional staff who work as a 'circuit rider' to multiple towns, assisting with specific municipal functions and activities over a two-year period.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided to cover salary and fringe benefits for circuit rider staff over a two-year period. The annual funding allocation is determined by an appropriation of the General Assembly each year.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds can only be used to pay for salary and fringe benefits for circuit rider staff over a two-year period.

Circuit sponsors can be municipal governments, county governments, regional governmental organizations, or private organizations
Municipalities within a circuit must be within reasonable proximity to each other
Existing circuits will be evaluated on past performance
Applicants are evaluated based on need, proposed accomplishments, and financial commitment and support

Existing circuits are also judged on their past performance. Technical assistance is available for interested governments and sponsors.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Microenterprise Loan Program (MLP) expands opportunities for microenterprise development and small business growth by providing flexible financing for microenterprise startups and expansions in designated Sustainable Communities and Priority Funding Areas throughout Maryland. The state partners with community-based microlenders and local CDFIs to originate and administer the loans, providing entrepreneurs easier access to capital and training while sustaining local economies in Maryland communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Microenterprise loans of up to $50,000 are available through the program, with additional funds potentially added by the intermediary lender. Interest rates go up to 12 percent annual percentage rate. Loan terms cannot exceed 5 years. Collateral is required and may include personal guarantees, liens on business assets, and pledges of accounts. There are no prepayment penalties. The state also provides loans directly to local Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs), which in turn lend to small businesses.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Microentrepreneurs and small business owners seeking to start or expand businesses in designated Sustainable Communities and Priority Funding Areas, as well as local CDFIs serving Maryland communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, marketing, planning and feasibility studies, real estate acquisition down payments, minor renovations, minor leasehold improvements, machinery and equipment, and certain other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Multifamily Bond Program provides tax-exempt bonds and notes for construction and permanent financing of multifamily rental housing for families with limited incomes. The program leverages federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits to support new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of rental housing with a minimum of five units. It aims to increase the availability of affordable rental housing for low- and moderate-income families statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bonds and notes provide construction and permanent financing through multiple financing options. Interest rates are based on the Community Development Administration's bond rate and market conditions. Construction loan terms range from 20-24 months. Permanent loan terms are typically 35-40 years, with mortgages amortized over 35-40 year periods. A first lien position is generally required. All loans must be insured or have other forms of credit enhancement acceptable to the program, including FHA/CDA Risk Sharing (Section 542(c)), GNMA MBS (Section 221(d)(4)), Freddie Mac Tax Exempt Loans, or FNMA MBS collateral. The program participates in the Federal Housing Administration/Housing Finance Agency Risk Sharing Program and leverages federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (4% unallocated LIHTCs for bond-financed projects). Multiple financing structures are available: (1) FHA-CDA Risk Sharing with 40-year final maturity and estimated all-in rates around 5.92%; (2) GNMA MBS with 17-year balloon and estimated all-in rates around 5.72%; (3) Freddie Mac TEL with 17-year balloon and estimated all-in rates around 6.67%; (4) Cash Collateral/GNMA MBS with 2-year short-term financing and estimated all-in rates around 5.90%; (5) FNMA MBS with immediate or forward start options and estimated all-in rates around 5.87%-6.22%. Upfront costs range from approximately $1.1 million to $2.1 million depending on structure. CDA financing fees are 1.625% of bond/loan amount for most structures and 3% for Tax/TE financing. Additional fees include bond counsel, trustee fees ($4,000-$5,750 annually), CDA issuer fee (0.40% annually), servicing fee (0.25%), and other closing costs. Tax/TE financing permits pairing of taxable GNMA loans with tax-exempt bonds to reduce borrowing costs. Unrated private placements or rated bond transactions are available for Tax/TE financing. Bond proceeds must be 100% cash collateralized and satisfy the 50% test for Tax Credits.

For new construction or substantial rehabilitation projects with 20-24 month construction periods, interest is typically capitalized during construction.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability (MEEHA) Program - EmPOWER
structured_extraction.program_description: Promotes energy efficiency and housing affordability in affordable multifamily rental housing developments by providing grants or loans to reduce electric or gas consumption, support greenhouse gas reductions, and fund limited health and safety or incidental repairs. The program serves owners of affordable or low-income multifamily properties statewide.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: EmPOWER provides grants or loans (with 0% interest and deferred payments) to fund energy efficiency measures that reduce electric or gas consumption, as well as measures that reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Gas-reducing measures are only eligible in Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) or Washington Gas Light Company (WGL) utility territories. Funding is allocated at $134.9 million for calendar years 2024-2026. Projects must maintain affordability with a minimum of 20% of households at 80% Area Median Income (AMI) or less for a minimum of 5 years (Tier 1 funding) or 15 years (Tier 2 funding). Eligible measures include energy efficiency upgrades to building shell, HVAC and water heating systems, lighting, appliances, fenestration, electrification measures, and other greenhouse gas reduction measures evaluated on a case-by-case basis. Limited health and safety repairs and incidental repairs necessary for measure installation are also eligible. The MEEHA Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP) provides grants and loans specifically for electrification of covered buildings under Maryland's Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS) with funding limited to $15,000 per unit and requiring a minimum of 51% of units at or below 80% AMI for 15 years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of affordable multifamily rental housing developments, including government bodies, for-profit companies, non-profit organizations, individuals, and higher education institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To reduce electric or gas consumption through energy efficiency measures including building shell improvements, HVAC and water heating system upgrades, lighting and appliance replacements, fenestration upgrades, and electrification measures. Limited health and safety repairs or incidental repairs required to allow installation of energy measures or protect program-funded measures are also eligible. Funds may support energy audits, electrification add-on expenses, and other greenhouse gas reduction measures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Gas-reducing measures are only eligible in Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) or Washington Gas Light Company (WGL) utility territories. All building sizes and configurations are eligible including single family units as a group project, individually metered, or master metered buildings. GHGRP eligibility requires a single building with 35,000 sq ft or more gross floor area, or two or more buildings with combined 35,000 sq ft or more served by the same meter or heating/cooling system.

Minority Business Enterprise Plan Form required
ACH Direct Deposit Form required
Proof of affordability through Regulatory Agreement or Tax Covenant required (minimum 20% of units at 80% AMI for 5 years, or 51% at 80% AMI for 15 years for GHGRP)
W-9 Form required for grantee
Energy conservation measures must be entered into DHCD's Hancock Mobile Intake Tool (MINT) or Rehab Funding Request Form with actual contractor bids for materials, equipment, and installation costs
Authentic pictures required for each recommended measure showing unique identification and equipment location, plus model/serial numbers where applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Contact a Qualified Energy Professional (QEP) from DHCD's approved list to conduct energy audit (for rehabilitation projects) or energy certification review (for new construction). 2) Complete the MEEHA Application Form with all required information about property, owner, grantee, and project details. 3) For rehabilitation projects, QEP performs comprehensive whole-building energy audit per BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards, inspects representative unit sample, confirms ASHRAE 62.2 ventilation compliance, and identifies eligible energy conservation measures (ECMs). 4) QEP completes MEEHA Funding Request by entering recommended ECMs into DHCD's Hancock Mobile Intake Tool (MINT) (or Rehab Funding Request Form until MINT is fully operational in 2026) with contractor bids, measure specifications, and required documentation including photos. 5) QEP submits Funding Request to DHCD on behalf of project owner with owner approval. 6) Gather and submit required documents: application, utility bills, customer consent forms, property deed, SDAT checks, MBE plan, ACH form, affordability proof, W-9 form. 7) Email complete application package to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov. 8) DHCD reviews and approves Funding Request during underwriting process. 9) DHCD creates funding agreement with project owner. 10) Project installs approved measures. 11) DHCD inspects completed work. 12) DHCD releases funding after equipment installation verification. 13) Project enters affordability compliance period after construction completion with annual monitoring to confirm compliance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability (MEEHA) Program - Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Promotes energy efficiency and housing affordability in affordable multifamily rental housing developments by providing grants to reduce direct greenhouse gas emissions through replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment and building energy conservation and alternative energy generating systems.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: GHGRP provides grants to fund greenhouse gas reduction measures including replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment and building energy conservation and alternative energy generating systems. Funding is limited to $15,000 per unit. Funding allocation is $8.75 million in fiscal year 2024 and $5 million each for fiscal years 2025 and 2026. Projects must maintain affordability with a minimum of 51% of households at 80% Area Median Income (AMI) or less for a minimum of 15 years. Electrical upgrades needed to support electrification measures may be included as electrification add-on expenses, with total electrification costs not exceeding 10% of total funding for electrification measures.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of affordable multifamily rental housing developments with existing buildings of 35,000 gross square feet or more
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To reduce direct greenhouse gas emissions through replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment, building energy conservation, alternative energy generating systems, and measures that reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Eligible measures include HVAC system replacements, domestic hot water heating upgrades, electrification of space heating and water heating systems, insulation improvements, air sealing, lighting upgrades, fenestration replacement, and renewable energy systems such as solar.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible for existing buildings with 35,000 gross square feet of floor area or more (excluding parking garages), or two or more buildings with a combined gross floor area of 35,000 square feet or more that are served in whole or in part by the same electric or gas meter or the same heating or cooling systems.
requirements_list: Single building must have gross floor area of 35,000 sq ft or more (not including parking garages), OR two or more buildings with combined gross floor area of 35,000 sq ft or more (excluding parking garage area) served in whole or in part by the same electric or gas meter or the same heating or cooling systems
Project must maintain a minimum of 51% of households at 80% Area Median Income (AMI) or less for a minimum of 15 years
Minimum of 20% of units must be at or below 80% AMI with a minimum 5-year affordability requirement (EmPower program)
GHGRP funding is limited to $15,000 per unit

Qualified Energy Professional must complete an energy certification review for new construction projects or conduct an energy audit for rehabilitation projects in compliance with BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards
Energy audit must include comprehensive whole building assessment and sampling protocol of at least 10% of units or minimum of 5 units, whichever is greater

Project owner must submit complete application package including application form, commercial utility bills, customer consent form, grantee signature block, property deed with legal description, SDAT ownership and status checks, minority business enterprise plan, ACH direct deposit form, proof of affordability, and W-9 form
Regulatory Agreement or Tax Covenant required with minimum 20% of units at or below 80% AMI for minimum 5 years; if not existing, DHCD will create one
Qualified Energy Professional must submit Funding Request to DHCD using MINT tool or Rehab Funding Request Form with actual contractor bids for all measures
All space heating and cooling equipment must be evaluated for capacity reduction based on post-retrofit conditions
For GHGRP, program discourages installation of new fossil fuel HVAC systems and encourages electrification
Air sealing is mandatory and must address plumbing penetrations, electrical penetrations, mechanical penetrations, duct registers, weatherstripping, and fenestration gaps
Insulation in accessible gabled attics is mandatory if existing insulation below R-19
Duct systems must be sealed; accessible ducts must be sealed including ducts outside building envelope
ASHRAE 62.2 ventilation standards must be met post-retrofit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Property owner or representative completes MEEHA Application form with project and property information. 2. Qualified Energy Professional from DHCD's approved list conducts comprehensive energy audit (rehabilitation) or energy certification review (new construction) per BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards. 3. Qualified Energy Professional completes energy audit documentation including sampling of units, ASHRAE ventilation calculations, and photographic evidence of existing conditions. 4. Qualified Energy Professional enters recommended energy conservation measures (ECMs) into DHCD's MINT tool or Rehab Funding Request Form with actual contractor bids and measure specifications. 5. Qualified Energy Professional submits Funding Request to DHCD on behalf of project owner. 6. Project owner submits complete application package to MultifamilyEnergy.DHCD@maryland.gov including application form, utility bills, utility consent forms, SDAT checks, affordability documentation, and required forms. 7. DHCD reviews and approves Funding Request and creates funding agreement with project owner. 8. Project installs approved energy measures per contractor bids and specifications. 9. DHCD inspects completed work and releases funding after equipment installation verification. 10. Project enters affordability compliance period after construction completion, with ongoing monitoring by DHCD.

structured_extraction.program_description: Designed exclusively for Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) for relending to small businesses, combined with a required private capital match. The program focuses on businesses owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI), very small businesses, and businesses located in CDFI Investment Areas. Provides targeted loans to CDFIs, which in turn relend to eligible small businesses. DHCD will make SSBCI Loans to CDFIs; and the CDFIs in turn will make small business loans to qualified small businesses according to SSBCI guidelines and DHCD requirements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Targeted SSBCI Loans to CDFIs of $2,000,000 to $15,000,000. SSBCI Loans will bear interest at a rate as low as 0%-2%, and have a loan term up to 7 years with annual renewal options thereafter. CDFIs in turn relend to eligible small businesses with individual loan amounts up to $250,000 (unless DHCD gives prior written approval). Small business loan interest rates cannot exceed 18% (subject to change by DHCD). Small business loan terms cannot exceed 5 years unless financing is for acquisition of assets with longer useful lives. Maximum combined origination fee and points: 1%. Application fee maximum: $100. Requires private capital match from a qualified private source, with a target leverage goal of 10:1. Initial private capital match to SSBCI funds targeted at 70-30 (30% SSBCI, 70% private for SEDI/VSB; 20% SSBCI, 80% private for non-SEDI businesses), with final terms to be determined based on credit worthiness. CDFIs must have 20% at risk. SSBCI Loan repayments to DHCD may be recycled into new small business loans. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis and must be closed within 90 days of approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) seeking capital to relend to small businesses, particularly those owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals, very small businesses, and businesses located in CDFI Investment Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: CDFIs use funds for relending to eligible small businesses for working capital, marketing/planning/feasibility studies, real estate acquisition down payment, minor renovations, minor leasehold improvements, machinery and equipment acquisition, and other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business. Ineligible uses include: residential or transient living businesses, multifamily or single-family housing developments, nursing homes, assisted living facilities, crisis care centers, group homes, transitional housing, homeless shelters, facilities such as community halls, fire stations, hospitals, colleges or universities, and adult bookstores, adult video shops, adult entertainment facilities, gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, or tattoo parlors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based CDFI Investment Areas. Priority given to small business loans in CDFI investment areas.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) certified by the U.S. Department of Treasury or the Community Development Trust
Demonstrate financial stability and good standing with the State and the Internal Revenue Service

Experience in administering a small business loan program, including origination, credit and compliance underwriting, loan servicing, post-closing asset management and monitoring of businesses, and compliance with reporting requirements
Ability to leverage eligible required private capital as a match to SSBCI funding with minimum 1:1 match ratio
Capacity to comply with SSBCI Statutes, Regulations and Policies as well as DHCD's requirements
Readiness to provide adequate resources and staff to start making small business loans within 90 days of closing the SSBCI Loan
Ability to provide technical assistance to small business borrowers

Outreach capabilities to very small businesses (fewer than 10 employees) and to socially and economically disadvantaged individual-led businesses (SEDI) or businesses operating in CDFI investment areas
CDFIs must have 20% at risk on each small business loan
Small business loan targets up to $250,000 unless DHCD gives prior written approval
Priority for small business loans to businesses owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals
Priority for very small businesses
Priority for businesses in CDFI investment areas
Lender cannot act as participant, have security interest or be stakeholder in any small business borrower
Must provide monthly, quarterly and annual reports and annual audited financial statements
Must maintain up-to-date information regarding applicable program policies and guidelines
Must notify DHCD of any changes in address or key personnel affecting loan service delivery
Must not discriminate in origination, underwriting, servicing, or administration of loans based on race, color, religion, sex, handicap, familial status, or national origin
No outstanding liabilities with the State of Maryland (income taxes, sales taxes, payroll withholding taxes, unemployment taxes, or other penalties and fines)
SSBCI funding only for small businesses with fewer than 500 employees
SSBCI individual loan amount not to exceed $5,000,000; total financing not to exceed $20,000,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: CDFIs submit an SSBCI NBW Loan to Lender Application form (Appendix A) to DHCD at 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706 or via email at dhcd.ssbci@maryland.gov. The application must include: organization information, explanation of capacity and experience in small business lending, projected annual loan production for 6-year period, explanation of leverage with other funding and private capital terms, verification of financial stability and committed resources, description of lending program with demographic, geographic and industry targets, description of outreach capabilities to very small businesses and SEDI-led businesses, description of loan products with specific terms, capabilities to handle reporting and audit activity, explanation of technical assistance and training resources provided, and confirmation of no outstanding state liabilities. Applicant must attach most recent Annual Report, Annual Financial Statement, 501(c)(3) organizational documents, and last 3 years of organization tax returns. Once approved, CDFIs receive a commitment letter reflecting total SSBCI Loan commitment amount, required private capital match, and proposed small business loan funding timetable. SSBCI Loans must be closed in accordance with terms and conditions provided by the Maryland Office of the Attorney General. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: Dedicated to funding and growing the next generation of outstanding early-stage businesses in Maryland with high potential job growth. The program provides bridge financing to high-potential businesses that have already raised equity from early-stage investors and are seeking additional capital to reach the next equity raise. It offers venture debt or convertible note financing (SSBCI-backed) as well as equity investment to help companies achieve growth milestones and scale to their next equity round.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Venture debt or convertible note financing with target SSBCI portion of $500,000 to $2,500,000. SSBCI funds must be on at least a pari passu basis (equal standing) with private capital match. SSBCI funds must cause and result in the private capital match. Repayment in principal and interest or convertible note structure. Aggregate funding round must be less than $20,000,000. Typical bridge rounds are greater than $2,000,000. Provides bridge financing to help companies achieve growth milestones and scale to the next equity raise.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage businesses in Maryland with less than 500 employees that have already raised equity from early-stage investors and are seeking bridge financing to scale and reach the next equity raise. Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and businesses owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bridge financing to achieve business milestones, support scaling, and reach the next equity raise.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based businesses only.
requirements_list: Less than 500 employees
Minimum required private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 1:1
Target matching private capital to SSBCI funds greater than 2:1
Existing paid-in capital greater than $2,000,000 or revenues greater than $1,000,000
High potential for job growth
Must have already raised equity from early-stage investors
Early-stage business status
Most companies positioned to scale
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested businesses should email dhcd.ssbci@maryland.gov to express interest and receive application instructions. Applications are being accepted through the NBW Venture Funds Program.

structured_extraction.program_name: National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: The National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund (NED) provides competitive funds in support of commercial and residential development activities in areas targeted for revitalization. The program focuses on areas where modest investment and a coordinated strategy will have an appreciable neighborhood revitalization impact, making targeted investments through coordinated strategies to achieve significant community outcomes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants and loans provided to support commercial and residential development projects including down payment assistance for homebuyers to purchase and rehabilitate homes, acquisition or rehabilitation of vacant or dilapidated properties, improvement of existing residential and business properties, energy efficiency through weatherization and energy retrofits, affordable housing development, mixed-use projects combining housing and retail or office space, development or enhancement of community open space or public infrastructure, and strategic demolition. Technical assistance and information are also available. Regional Project Managers are available to provide guidance and support throughout the application and implementation process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (county government, municipalities/towns) and non-profit community development organizations seeking to revitalize targeted neighborhoods in Prince George's and Montgomery Counties through coordinated commercial and residential development strategies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible uses include down payment assistance for homebuyers to purchase and rehabilitate homes, acquisition or rehabilitation of vacant or dilapidated properties, improvement of existing residential and business properties, energy efficiency through weatherization and energy retrofits, affordable housing development, mixed-use projects combining housing and retail or office space, development or enhancement of community open space or public infrastructure, and strategic demolition. All projects must support goals and objectives outlined in the targeted area's Sustainable Communities Action Plan.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: In Prince George's County, projects must be located at least in part within the boundary created by Interstate 495 and the District of Columbia. In Montgomery County, projects must be within an Enterprise Zone or the boundary created by Prince George's County, Maryland Route 200, Interstate 270, Interstate 495 to the Maryland state line, and the District of Columbia. All projects must be located in Sustainable Communities.
requirements_list: Projects must support goals and objectives outlined in the targeted area's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Located in eligible geographic areas within Prince George's or Montgomery County
Must be in a Sustainable Communities area
In Prince George's County, the project must be at least partly inside the Capital Beltway (I-495)
In Montgomery County, the project must be within an Enterprise Zone or within the boundary of Prince George's County, MD-200, I-270, and I-495
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For application procedures and more information, visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage. Regional Project Managers are available to answer questions about whether a specific address is eligible and to provide technical assistance. For Montgomery County and Southern Maryland (including Prince George's County), contact Jean Cannon, Program Officer, at 410-209-5806, 443-679-8523, or jean.cannon@maryland.gov. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to view your jurisdiction's NED boundary.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal affordable housing production and financing program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that increases and preserves the supply of decent, safe, and sanitary affordable housing for extremely low-income and very low-income households. The program supports both the development and preservation of affordable rental housing through grants and financing mechanisms, with priority given to projects located in Priority Funding Areas. The program targets extremely low-income (ELI) households defined as those earning at or below 30% of Area Median Income (AMI) or at or below the poverty line.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HTF funds may be used as broadly and flexibly as permitted by federal regulations to address unique underwriting needs of each project and the number of ELI tenants served. Forms of assistance include equity investments; interest-bearing or non-interest-bearing loans or advances; deferred payment loans; grants; and other forms approved by HUD. Ninety percent (90%) of the HTF annual allocation is used for production, preservation and rehabilitation of affordable rental housing through acquisition, new construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation of non-luxury housing with suitable amenities. Ten percent (10%) is retained for allowable administrative and planning expenses. Operating cost assistance may be provided up to one-third of the state's annual HTF allocation, must be fully utilized within 5 years of award, and can be subsequently renewed within the 30-year affordability period. The Department awards HTF funds to eligible projects through a non-competitive, first-ready first-served basis based on readiness to proceed and financial feasibility. Funding must be committed within 24 months of HUD's execution of the HTF grant agreement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; applications accepted throughout the year
structured_extraction.contact_email: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Community Development Administration
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit developers, sponsors of affordable rental housing developments seeking to create or preserve affordable rental housing for extremely low-income and very low-income households, including homeless families. Eligible recipients must demonstrate financial capacity, experience, and ability to own, construct, rehabilitate, manage and operate affordable multifamily rental housing developments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development hard costs, acquisition costs, related soft costs, relocation costs, and operating/rental assistance (limited to one-third of annual allocation). Funds support production, preservation, and rehabilitation of affordable rental housing through acquisition, new construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation of non-luxury housing with suitable amenities. HTF housing must be permanent housing. Operating costs eligible for assistance include insurance, utilities, real property taxes, maintenance, and scheduled payments to reserves for replacement of major systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland, with Priority Funding Areas (PFAs) prioritized. Priority Funding Areas under Maryland's Smart Green and Growing Initiative include: all incorporated municipalities including Baltimore City (with exceptions for water, sewer, and density for areas annexed after January 1, 1997); all areas between the Baltimore beltway and Baltimore City limits and the Washington DC beltway and DC boundary; all areas designated as Sustainable Communities; Federal and State enterprise zones; all areas designated by county governments as PFAs including rural villages designated in county comprehensive plans as of July 1, 1998; and certified heritage areas within locally designated growth areas. All new construction projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area. HTF funds available statewide for preservation and rehabilitation projects.
requirements_list: Eligible recipients must be for-profit or non-profit organizations with demonstrated financial capacity and experience to complete projects and meet ongoing compliance requirements
Recipients must provide certification of compliance with HTF program requirements for entire project period
Developers must demonstrate ability and financial capacity to undertake, comply, and manage eligible activities
Developers must demonstrate familiarity with requirements of other federal, state, or local housing programs that may be used with HTF funds
Demonstrated experience and capacity to own, construct, rehabilitate, manage and operate affordable multifamily rental housing development required
Market assessment of housing needs of ELI individuals must be submitted; assessment must demonstrate current demand for proposed unit types and numbers

Sponsors must have sufficient site control extending at least 180 calendar days after application date; acceptable evidence includes deeds, contracts of sale, leases, purchase options, Land Disposition Agreements

For existing property acquisitions: Capital Needs Assessment (CNA) by competent third party required documenting remaining useful life of all major systems; CNA must identify work needed for health/safety, federal/state/local code violations

Phase I Environmental Site Assessment required for all multifamily projects (more than four units); if Phase I identifies recognized environmental concerns, Phase II ESA required; assessments must not be more than one year old; must include lead-based paint and asbestos testing for acquisition/rehabilitation projects
Evidence that public water, sewer, electric, gas, telephone, internet, and cable services available at project site or will be available during construction/rehabilitation period
Sites must be properly zoned for intended use; if zoning change/variance/exception required, documentation of present status and detailed schedule with projected approval dates required
All new construction projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area; letter from local government certifying PFA location required

Projects must demonstrate readiness to proceed; status of other financing with firm written commitments required prior to HTF commitment; completion of Anticipated Development Schedule required; projects expected to meet proposed schedules
Minimum vacancy rate of 5% underwriting required; Market Study must support proposed vacancy level; projects requiring 10% or more vacancy rejected as infeasible

Annual operating expenses (including real estate taxes, excluding replacement reserve) must be $4,000-$7,000 per unit per year; waivers may be requested for small projects, master-metered utilities, or unusual circumstances
All projects must budget at least $300 per unit per year in reserves for replacement deposits; RFR deposits must be adequate as determined by qualified third-party CNA

Operating reserves equal to 3-6 months of underwritten operating expenses, debt service, and required reserve deposits must be established; maintained until project achieves 1.15 minimum debt service coverage ratio, economic break-even operations for one complete fiscal year, and 90% occupancy for 12 consecutive months
Rents projected to increase no more than 2% annually; operating expenses (including property taxes) projected to increase at least 3% annually
All projects must be underwritten to minimum debt service coverage ratio of 1.15 in first year of stabilized operations; DSCR calculated including all must-pay debt service payments

Market Study commissioned by applicant required demonstrating need for affordable rental housing in local market; must be prepared by independent professional with affordable multifamily rental housing experience in Maryland; firm must have undergone peer review by National Council of Housing Market Analysts (NCHMA); study not more than six months old from application submission; must meet HOME Rule requirements at §92.250(b)(2) with executive summary, detailed project description, geographic definition of primary and secondary market areas with maps, site and surrounding area description; must assess market demand within 18 months of project completion, evaluate capture rate and absorption rate, analyze competition

Primary Development Team (Developer/Owner, general contractor, architect, property manager) must demonstrate record of accomplishment during past five years with similar size, scope, and complexity projects; team members without appropriate experience must establish partnerships with experienced entities

Financial statements for three fiscal years prior to application plus interim statements through previous quarter required for project sponsor, project owner, guarantor, and general partner/managing member with ownership interest; statements must identify contingent liabilities, income taxes, operating deficits; must include calculations of Total Assets, Total Liabilities, Current Assets, Current Liabilities; audited financial statements requirement may be waived upon written request and Department discretion
HTF-assisted rental housing must meet minimum affordability period of 30 years

All HTF-assisted rental properties must be free of hazardous materials, contamination, toxic chemicals and gases, and radioactive substances where hazard could affect occupant health/safety or conflict with intended use

Projects must comply with applicable federal, state, and local environmental laws and regulations including historic preservation, farmland protection, airport zones, coastal barrier resource systems, coastal zone management, floodplains, wetlands, explosives/hazards standards, contamination avoidance, noise standards, endangered species protection, wild and scenic rivers, safe drinking water, and sole-source aquifer protections

All rehabilitation projects must meet applicable HTF rehabilitation standards and requirements of 24 CFR §93.301(b); rehabilitation standards address site conditions, exterior building criteria, foundation, structural integrity, building envelope, roofing, interior components, kitchens, bathrooms, bedrooms, electrical, plumbing, building water-tightness, HVAC, disaster mitigation, replacement housing, lead-based paint, and energy conservation

Projects must comply with Section 3 of Housing and Urban Development Act of 1968 requiring employment and economic opportunities for low and very low income persons; applies to construction projects with total cost exceeding $200,000 in federal funds

Geographic diversity required; HTF funds available statewide with funds reasonably dispersed to allow physical mobility and promote social/economic mobility; eligible projects must be in Qualified Census Tracts, Difficult Development Areas contributing to concerted community revitalization plans, or meet other geographic diversity criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: HTF projects are selected by the Department for funding consideration subject to availability of funds. Applications are reviewed for eligibility and evaluated using threshold criteria. HTF projects will be selected and awarded on a non-competitive, first-ready first-served basis. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis throughout the year with funding awarded based on readiness to proceed. HTF funds may be requested by a sponsor as part of a project application, or Department staff may propose use of HTF funds during project review and underwriting. All applicants must submit a comprehensive Application Submission Package including: detailed description of eligible activities; market assessment; site control documentation; Capital Needs Assessment (for acquisitions); Phase I Environmental Site Assessment; utility evidence; zoning documentation; Anticipated Development Schedule; market study; developer experience documentation; financial statements; and other supporting materials per Department requirements. DHCD staff review all applicants to ensure compliance with minimum threshold requirements. If an application meets threshold requirements, it is evaluated for funding consideration. Successful recipients receive a Notice of Award stating the Department's intent to award HTF funds. The Department will ensure projects comply with HTF requirements at project completion including property standards, affordability requirements, and environmental provisions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) loan program provides financing to new and expanding small businesses and nonprofit organizations whose efforts help improve and revitalize existing commercial districts and town centers. Through the Community Development Administration (CDA), the program issues bonds to fund loans for business projects located in Priority Funding Areas or Sustainable Communities. NBW has a 20-year history of investing in small businesses throughout Maryland and operates with lending partners including banks, community development financial institutions (CDFIs), and mixed-use developers. The program serves as a gap lender and has successfully deployed recovery financing following emergencies such as civil unrest and flooding.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bond-funded and direct loans for small businesses and nonprofits during all phases of business growth. Financing options include: (1) Commercial real estate construction and permanent financing for commercial and mixed-use projects; (2) Acquisition or refinancing of stabilized commercial and mixed-use projects; (3) Non-profit facility loans for acquisition, rehabilitation, and new construction for 501(c)(3) organizations. For-profit borrowers require minimum 10% equity contribution with maximum 90% CLTV financing; nonprofit borrowers require minimum 5% equity with maximum 95% CLTV financing. Loan terms include 6-month debt service reserves and minimum 1.50 DSCR (for CDA loans) or 1.25 DSCR (for credit-enhanced non-CDA loans) throughout loan life. Upfront costs include 0.5% to 1% financing fee, $25,000 DHCD legal counsel fee, plus normal real estate and closing costs. Interest rates vary by project and risk profile.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and expanding small businesses and nonprofit organizations in Maryland seeking to improve and revitalize commercial districts and town centers, particularly those located in Priority Funding Areas or Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business financing during all phases of business growth; acquisition, permanent financing, and refinancing of commercial and mixed-use real estate; non-profit facility acquisition, rehabilitation, and new construction; commercial district revitalization; mixed-use development projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas as defined in section 5-7B-02 of the State Finance and Procurement Article, or in Sustainable Communities as defined in §6-205 of DHCD Article, Title 5 Subtitle 13 of the Economic Development Article, or §7-101 of the Transportation Article. Available statewide.
requirements_list: Project must be located in a Priority Funding Area or Sustainable Community
Project must be acquired, owned, developed, constructed, reconstructed, rehabilitated or improved for the purposes of carrying on a business
Must be a new or expanding small business or nonprofit organization
For-profit borrowers: minimum 10% equity or total cost borrower contribution
Nonprofit borrowers: minimum 5% equity or total cost borrower contribution
For-profit borrowers: maximum 90% CLTV financing based on independent professional collateral valuation
Nonprofit borrowers: maximum 95% CLTV financing based on independent professional collateral valuation
Minimum pro-forma 1.50 DSCR throughout loan life for CDA-funded loans
Minimum pro-forma 1.25 DSCR for credit-enhanced non-CDA loans unless underwriter determines otherwise
Loan debt service reserve equal to 6 months of maximum annual debt service
Conservative loan-life pro-forma demonstrating adequate debt service coverage
Acceptable collateral valuation by qualified professional independent of lender
Project must demonstrate revitalization impact on community including elimination of blight and job creation/retention
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can start with a pre-application form and then submit a financing application through the online portal. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. For CDA-funded loans over $250,000, the application is reviewed and recommended for approval by the 5-member NBW Loan Review Committee (comprised of Director of CDA, Director of Neighborhood Revitalization, CFO, Director of Division of Credit Assurance, and Program Manager of Small Business Financing from Department of Commerce), then forwarded to the Secretary of DHCD. All CDA business loan underwriting is reviewed by the 7-member Housing Finance Review Committee. Contact the program or a Business Development Specialist at 301-583-4650 for more information or to discuss your project.

structured_extraction.program_description: Assists small businesses with working capital and owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation through below-market rate loans. Provides financing up to $5 million for eligible businesses looking for new space or expansion opportunities. Designed to support small businesses operating in Maryland, with priority given to very small businesses and socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Senior or Junior Debt loans ranging from $350,000 to $5,000,000. Interest rate based on underwriting analysis. Flexible loan terms up to 30 years depending on use and loan amount. Program provides up to 30% match. Requires private capital match of 4:1 (80-20) for non-SEDI/VSB businesses or 2.3:1 (70-30) for SEDI/VSB businesses, with minimum 1:1 match required. Personal guarantees and collateral required. Applicants must pay $250 application fee and $250 closing fee.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses operating in Maryland with less than 500 employees, with priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI) who own or operate for-profit or nonprofit Maryland-based small businesses. structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation, mixed-use projects combining residential and commercial uses in the same building, machinery and equipment, working capital, and certain other costs associated with sustaining or expanding a small business. Eligible uses include manufacturing, service providers, retail, office or mixed-use facilities.
