structured_extraction.program_description: This program provided funding to local jurisdictions and their internet service provider partners to extend existing broadband service into unserved neighboring areas. The program was funded through the American Rescue Plan Act (ARP) administered by the US Treasury, with a minimum of $13 million available for broadband expansion in unserved areas of Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $50,000 to $500,000 covering 70% to 90% of eligible capital construction costs for extending service to unserved areas. Local match of 10% to 30% required (cash or in-kind from ISP) based on service area density. For wired infrastructure: fewer than 8 households per mile requires 10% match; 8-14 households per mile requires 20% match; 15+ households per mile requires 30% match. For wireless infrastructure: fewer than 40 households per tower requires 10% match; 40-69 households per tower requires 20% match; 70+ households per tower requires 30% match. Match from non-ISP sources must be in cash; ISP match may include in-kind capital construction costs for last-mile facilities and subscriber installations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications were due on or before December 23, 2021. Program closed; not accepting applications.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions (counties and municipalities) and their internet service provider partners extending broadband to unserved residents and businesses in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for extending existing broadband service to unserved areas, including: construction of facilities to deploy service at minimum broadband speeds; middle mile infrastructure directly necessary to provide service; and electronics necessary to deliver service (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennae, access points, modems, and equipment shelters).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Unserved areas in Maryland lacking terrestrial, fixed internet service at speeds above 25 Mbps download and/or 3 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50 milliseconds. Areas that received past state grant funding are ineligible. All Maryland counties are eligible to apply.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction (County or Municipality) listed on the Maryland Manual On-Line website with an ISP Partner
Service area must be unserved, lacking service at speeds above 25 Mbps download and/or 3 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50 milliseconds
Local jurisdiction must have entered into a partnership with an ISP Partner prior to entering into a funding agreement

Projects must be able to provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds measured at the served subscribers' location (reduced requirements allowable under certain circumstances with ISP Certification)
Match requirement of 10% to 30% based on density calculation (households per mile for wired or households per tower for wireless)
Projects must serve ALL end users located within the Proposed Funded Service Area (PFSA) at the Broadband Grant Speed
Grant funds cannot duplicate existing broadband service provided by other entities
All equipment purchased must be new and non-depreciated
Costs incurred prior to submission of completed application are not eligible for grant or match purposes
Project must be completed by December 31, 2023
Applicant or ISP Partner will be the owner of any facilities constructed as part of the Project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications were submitted electronically to osb.md@maryland.gov on or before December 23, 2021. The application package included: completed Grant Application Form (fillable PDF available on program website); Executive Summary describing the unserved area and project benefits; Application Partnership statement naming ISP Partner; Experience statements from senior team members; Network Design and Construction description including network speeds, latency, backhaul methods, and infrastructure details; Subscriber Profile with demographic data and take rate estimates; Subscriber Costs and Limitations listing ISP service options and pricing; Capital Budget with line item breakdown on both PDF and Excel spreadsheet; Project Schedule with key milestones and implementation timeline; GIS shapefiles (.shp, .kmz, or .kml) showing PFSA properties and infrastructure layout; and all documents combined into a single zip file. Applications were evaluated and scored based on Need for Service and Project Benefits (up to 5 points), Match Contribution Source (up to 6 points), Network Delivery Speed (up to 10 points), and Subscriber Options (up to 4 points), for a maximum score of 25 points. Funding awards were facilitated beginning in April 2022. The PFSA limits were published on the OSB website as part of a challenge process before awards were finalized.

structured_extraction.program_description: The state provides matching grants to support the operating costs of certified Neighborhood Housing Services (NHS) corporations. These organizations partner with residents, financial institutions, community organizations, local governments and the state to stabilize and improve the housing market in targeted low- and moderate-income neighborhoods. NHS corporations provide homeownership opportunities, home rehabilitation, closing cost assistance, homebuyer education and counseling, and community-organizing activities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each eligible NHS corporation may apply for a matching grant up to $50,000 that does not exceed one-third of its annual operating budget. Each eligible NHS umbrella corporation may apply for a grant for each program under its supervision up to $50,000 that does not exceed one-third of the annual operating budget of the program. The state grant must be matched by funds from local governments, private businesses, and individual contributions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- and moderate-income households in targeted neighborhoods served by certified Neighborhood Housing Services corporations. Eligible applicants are NHS corporations certified by the Neighborhood Reinvestment Corporation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs of Neighborhood Housing Services corporations that provide homeownership opportunities, closing cost assistance, homebuyer education and counseling, home rehabilitation for ownership and rental, and community-organizing activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: NHS of Baltimore and St. Ambrose Housing Aid Center serve several neighborhoods in Baltimore City and Baltimore County. Salisbury NHS serves residents in the West Side, Church Street, and Camden neighborhoods of Salisbury, Maryland. Montgomery Housing Partnership Inc. also serves the state.
requirements_list: Must be a Neighborhood Housing Services corporation certified by the Neighborhood Reinvestment Corporation
Must have agreement from local political subdivision for financial support
Must have local political subdivision participation on board of directors
The state grant must be matched by funds from local governments, private businesses, and individual contributions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the eligible NHS corporations or the Poverty Solutions Team in the Division of Neighborhood Revitalization at mhcf.dhcd@maryland.gov for application procedures and deadlines.

structured_extraction.program_description: A targeted investment program designed to address the persistent issue of fresh food unavailability in communities across Maryland by providing direct grants to eligible food retailers. The program supports the development, stabilization, and expansion of retail outlets that provide fresh food in areas where residents have limited or no access to nutritious food options.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_prioritized_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $25,000 to $150,000 per applicant to support capital-related needs for business stabilization or expansion. A total of up to $2 million in grant funding is available under this program. A $250 processing fee is deducted from the award amount if the applicant is approved for funding. Additionally, applicants may request supplemental loan funding through DHCD's Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) business development division, which will undergo a thorough financial review to assess the applicant's capacity to manage debt. Applicants approved for NourishMD grants may also be eligible for co-awards through the Maryland Market Money (MMM) program administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit or nonprofit food retailers serving communities with a Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher, including grocery stores, corner stores, co-ops, farm stands, farmers' markets, delivery retailers, and small food-focused stores with a maximum of 500 employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment purchases such as refrigeration and shelving; buildout and facility upgrades; capital costs for inventory expansion; initial inventory costs; working capital tied to expansion or construction; infrastructure and technology for SNAP/EBT setup; and equipment to reduce fossil fuel reliance or energy consumption.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass (MCBC) Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher. A fresh food gap score of 60% or higher is required, though exceptions may be granted on an individual basis. Your business does not need to be listed on the Maryland Community Business Compass to be eligible for the NourishMD grant program. However, if you don't see your business on the Maryland Community Business Compass and would like to add it, please email compass@maryland.gov.
requirements_list: Serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass (MCBC) Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher (exceptions may be granted on an individual basis)
Operate at least 5 days per week, year-round (farmer's markets and on-farm markets exempt from 5-day requirement but must operate year-round)
Employ a maximum of 500 workers
Be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)

Currently or plan to offer fresh, frozen, or minimally processed healthy foods including fresh/frozen fruits and vegetables, whole grains, dairy products, fresh/frozen/lean proteins, minimally processed items, and healthy pantry staples
Dedicate at least 20% of inventory or food-sales space to healthy food items (measured by square footage of food display space or dollar value of inventory)
Must meet SNAP eligibility or plan to adopt SNAP functionality
Submit detailed written plan describing how grant funds will be used (not to exceed two pages)
Provide documentation demonstrating how business currently meets or will meet healthy and fresh food criteria
Submit one year of business tax returns or audited financial statements (or alternative documentation if operating less than one year)
Submit relocation and expansion documentation if applicable (lease agreement, letter of intent, or proof of site control)
If no more than 25% of gross sales derived from alcohol/tobacco products
A $250 processing fee is required for all applications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process follows a competitive timeline: Notice of Funding Availability is made public in December with full program information and guidelines on the website. The application portal opens January 20th at 12:00 p.m. EST, and applicants may submit completed applications online through February 20th at 5:00 p.m. EST. To be considered, applicants must include all required documents at the time of submission; incomplete applications will not be reviewed until all missing components are submitted and verified. DHCD staff evaluate eligible applications for completeness, impact, and alignment with program priorities from February through March, referring the final list to the Review Committee for determinations. Funding recommendations are finalized in April for internal approval. Award announcements occur in May when applicants are notified of funding decisions and award agreements begin processing. The Board of Public Works approves grants and disbursements are made in June. Applicants can schedule an initial consultation with DHCD prior to submission.

structured_extraction.program_name: Operating Assistance Grants - Technical Assistance Grant (TAG)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Technical Assistance Grant (TAG) program provides funding to nonprofit organizations and local governments to support operating and technical assistance costs associated with local housing and community revitalization efforts. Funds help cover administrative expenses related to community and economic revitalization activities, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, and other related operating expenses. Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $50,000 maximum per request. No matching funds required. Funds support operating costs including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, and other related administrative expenses. Capital project costs are not supported. Projects should be completed within one year. An initial advance of up to 25% of the total award amount is permitted for the first payment request with no supporting documentation required. Subsequent reimbursement requests require evidence of expenditures such as paid invoices, contracts, or other documentation. Minimum recommended payment request amount is $1,000. Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) is strongly encouraged for faster and more secure payment processing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and local governments involved in community and economic revitalization activities, including housing, economic development, and related initiatives. Eligible applicants include nonprofit organizations engaged in community and economic revitalization activities in Maryland, and Maryland city, town, or county government entities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs related to administering community revitalization efforts, including salaries, professional services contracts, design plans, comprehensive studies, capacity building, technology costs, and other related administrative expenses. Projects and/or initiatives should align with local Sustainable Community Action Plans and/or support activities related to capital projects receiving funds from other Department or state agencies. Capital project costs and ineligible expenses such as alcohol, controlled substances, entertainment, personal souvenirs, fines, or parking tickets are not supported.

requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization or local government involved in community and economic revitalization activities

Nonprofit applicants must provide evidence of nonprofit status (Bylaws, Articles of Incorporation, IRS Determination Letter), evidence of good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and evidence of charitable registration with Maryland Secretary of State
Local government applicants must be a Maryland city, town, or county government entity; multiple local governments may apply jointly with a resolution from each municipality
Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area

Organization profile must include all required documents before submitting application

Site control is required at the time of award agreement execution for any project involving acquisition, demolition, construction, or rehabilitation
Awardees must disclose any actual or potential conflicts of interest
Organizations must maintain project-related records for a minimum of three years after official close-out of the award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Maryland DHCD Project Portal (https://projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us/). New users must register by selecting 'New User?' and completing the registration form; approval may take up to 72 hours. First-time applicants must contact a project manager for eligibility verification and system access. New organizations should request access and submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline to expedite processing. Ensure your organization profile includes all required documents before submitting. Virtual training sessions and step-by-step application guides are available in the DHCD Project Portal. All applications must be submitted online through the Project Portal by the stated deadline; late applications will not be accepted. Applications are evaluated using a single 5-point scoring scale reflecting overall strength and readiness. Projects in ENOUGH Act Grantee areas may receive up to 10 bonus points, and projects in Just Communities areas will receive 10 bonus points.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program established under the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 that encourages investment in economically distressed communities by providing preferential tax treatment for capital gains reinvested into designated Opportunity Zones. The program is designed to spur economic development and job creation in low-income census tracts. Maryland has 149 designated Opportunity Zones across the state. Investors who reinvest capital gains into Qualified Opportunity Funds can receive three types of tax incentives: temporary deferral of capital gains, a step-up in basis, and permanent exclusion of gains on long-term investments. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development supports the program at the state level, while local jurisdictions including Washington County, Wicomico County (City of Salisbury), and the City of Hagerstown promote the program locally.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three types of federal tax incentives are available: (1) Temporary Deferral — investors can defer including capital gains in taxable income if reinvested into a Qualified Opportunity Fund, with the deferred gain recognized by December 31, 2026 or upon disposition of the investment; (2) Step-Up in Basis — basis increases by 10% if the Opportunity Fund investment is held for at least 5 years and an additional 5% if held for at least 7 years, excluding up to 15% of the original gain from taxation; (3) Permanent Exclusion — capital gains from an Opportunity Fund investment held for at least 10 years are permanently excluded from taxation, though this applies only to gains accrued after the investment is made. Investors also gain access to additional capital sources for business start-up or expansion in designated zones.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Investors with capital gains seeking to reinvest in economically distressed communities designated as Opportunity Zones in Maryland, as well as businesses seeking to start or expand in Maryland Opportunity Zones.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in eligible property and businesses located within designated Opportunity Zones to support economic development, job creation, and redevelopment of underserved communities. Funds may be used for business capital, property development, and qualifying investments within Opportunity Zone areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated Opportunity Zones across Maryland. Eligible areas are low-income census tracts with an individual poverty rate of at least 20% and median family income no greater than 80% of the area median. Maryland has 149 designated Opportunity Zones statewide, including zones in Washington County, Wicomico County (City of Salisbury), and the City of Hagerstown.
requirements_list: Investment must be made through a Qualified Opportunity Fund structured as either a partnership or corporation
Investment must be in eligible property located within a designated Opportunity Zone
Investors must use capital gains from prior investments to fund the Opportunity Fund
For Step-Up in Basis benefit: investment must be held for at least 5 years (10% basis increase) or 7 years (additional 5% basis increase)
For Permanent Exclusion benefit: investment must be held for at least 10 years
Capital gains must be reinvested within the specified IRS timeframe
Investor must have capital gains to invest
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Investors should identify designated Opportunity Zones using the Maryland Opportunity Zones map available through DHCD or local jurisdiction maps. They must then establish or identify a Qualified Opportunity Fund set up as a partnership or corporation. Investors structure their capital gains reinvestment through the Opportunity Fund and work with investment partners as needed. Detailed investment procedures and final guidelines for Opportunity Funds are provided by the U.S. Treasury and IRS. Local contacts such as the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department and Washington County Department of Business Development can provide jurisdiction-specific guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides financial assistance to help small businesses buy property they can operate in and use to build wealth. The program offers loans to support property acquisition and renovation for eligible small businesses. Funding is provided through the federal State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) program.

list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

Loans can be in senior or subordinate positions. Borrowers must provide a minimum 1:1 private capital match for every dollar of DHCD loan. Funds can be used to purchase, construct, or renovate commercial real estate. Senior or subordinate loan positions are available with focus on maximizing community benefit.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase, construct, or renovate commercial real estate, including buying the space where you currently operate, moving to a new location, buying property for the first time if you do not have a storefront, or buying property as part of an expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.

Project cannot be 100% residential (mixed-use projects may qualify)

Business cannot be adult entertainment facilities, check cashing facilities, gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, or cannabis businesses
Provide a minimum of 1:1 private capital match

Personal guarantees required from all owners with more than 20% equity
Provide adequate collateral
Total project costs cannot exceed $20 million
Renovation projects must be at least 51% owner-occupied upon completion
New construction must be at least 60% owner-occupied upon completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit dhcd.maryland.gov/Business/Pages/Own-Your-Future.aspx or email dhcd.businesslending@maryland.gov to schedule a consultation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that expands the supply of affordable housing for low-income households by providing loans for rental housing development. Projects typically involve partnerships between state and local governments. The program also serves non-governmental entities creating housing for individuals with disabilities or special needs. Housing is for households that earn less than 50% of the statewide median income.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides loans for rental housing projects. For large projects, loan amounts are limited to $75,000 per unit. For small projects (40 units or fewer), loans can be up to $2 million without a per-unit cap. Loan repayment is generally deferred for up to 40 years as long as the local government entity continues to own the housing and rent it to income-eligible households. The department may establish different funding amounts for units serving individuals with disabilities or special needs on an annual or per-project basis.

For-profit and non-profit rental housing developers, county governments, and municipalities are also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for new construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation of rental housing including apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities, as well as for developing and preserving affordable rental housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Projects must be located in priority funding areas. Local government or housing authority must make a contribution of land or equal value from non-state resources.
requirements_list: Local governments, housing authorities, and entities owned in part by a local government or housing authority are eligible applicants
Non-governmental entities are eligible for funds to be used for individuals with disabilities or special needs units
Local government must contribute land or equal value from non-state resources
Local participant must manage the project or arrange for another party to manage it
Resident households must have gross income not exceeding 50% of statewide median income adjusted for family size
Resident households for individuals with disabilities or special needs units must have gross income not exceeding 30% of Area Median Income adjusted for household size
Residents must contribute maintenance or other services to the facility, grounds, or neighborhood
Projects must arrange for occupants to provide tenant-contributed services as detailed in program statute and regulations
Any profits from sale of project must be used for other low-income housing purposes
Rental units must be occupied by households with incomes below 50% of the statewide median
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests for funding are accepted on an ongoing basis. Applications are evaluated and processed based on meeting the program purpose, readiness to proceed, and availability of funding. If Partnership Rental Housing Program funding is requested with other department funds, the application requirements and applicable deadlines of the other funding must be met. Applicants can find application documents in the agency's Multifamily Document Library. Contact the program representative for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) that provides funding to place-based economic development organizations to activate vacant storefronts and buildings in local business districts, including downtown and historic commercial areas. These organizations, such as designated Main Streets and Arts and Entertainment Districts, receive funding to sub-grant to businesses for rental assistance, renovation, fit-out, and equipment. The program aims to support small businesses, create jobs, improve commercial corridors, and increase local economic activity across Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $300,000 per applicant awarded to designated Main Streets, Arts and Entertainment Districts, and other place-based economic development organizations in designated Sustainable Communities. Organizations sub-grant funds to businesses for rental assistance, renovation, fit-out of vacant buildings, and furniture, fixtures, and equipment. For example, $282,000 was awarded for the build-out of three new businesses in Downtown Salisbury. Businesses receiving sub-granted funds must be open and operational by December 2025.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Place-based economic development organizations such as designated Main Streets, Arts and Entertainment Districts, and other community development organizations in designated Sustainable Communities, as well as small businesses in downtown and historic commercial areas seeking to open or expand in vacant street-level properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance, renovation and fit-out of vacant storefronts or buildings, furniture, fixtures, and equipment to activate vacant spaces in local business districts and historic commercial corridors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, with a focus on designated Sustainable Communities, Main Street districts, and downtown and historic commercial areas.
requirements_list: Organizations must be designated place-based economic development entities such as Main Streets or Arts and Entertainment Districts
Must be located in or serve designated Sustainable Communities
Must have identified priority vacant storefronts or buildings in local business districts
Applicant businesses must be opening in a vacant street-level property in a downtown or historic commercial area
Projects must be approved through a local government application process
Businesses receiving sub-granted funds must open and be operational by December 2025

In some jurisdictions, such as the City of Salisbury, the local government solicits proposals from potential businesses, and selected projects are then submitted to DHCD for funding consideration. Organizations then sub-grant funds to approved businesses for renovation, fit-out, and equipment.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Rental Housing Program provides financing to rehabilitate or create affordable multifamily rental housing. It supports the development of affordable rental housing through competitive funding and can be combined with federal HOME funds, tax-exempt or taxable bond financing, low-income housing tax credits, and other private or public funding sources. The program aims to preserve and expand the supply of affordable rental units for low-income households across Maryland.

list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

Loans may be used for acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and development costs including lender fees, architectural and engineering fees, market studies, appraisals, legal fees, and other costs directly related to housing development.

Projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area
