Applicants can download application documents from the agency's Multifamily Document Library.

structured_extraction.program_description: Subordinate gap financing program to create jobs and strengthen the Maryland economy by providing funding for the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing financed through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and Low Income Housing Tax Credit Program.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subordinate loans funded from State general obligation bonds provided to borrowers creating or preserving affordable rental housing. Maximum loan amount is $2.5 million per project (subject to waiver), though loans must not exceed the amount necessary to make a project financially feasible and viable as determined by the Department and in accordance with Section 42 of the Internal Revenue Code. Loans carry 2% simple interest with no regular interest accruing during the Construction Loan Period. During the Permanent Loan Period (commencing after construction completion), borrowers pay surplus cash on an annual basis with payments applied to reduce the outstanding principal balance. The Applicable Surplus Cash Percentage is determined at closing and payments are limited to available surplus cash. Loans have a 40-year term (Maturity Date is the 40th anniversary of the first day of the Permanent Loan Period) but are due upon sale, refinancing, any voluntary or involuntary transfer of the property, or the occurrence of an Event of Default. Contingent interest may be payable from surplus cash or borrower net proceeds upon occurrence of certain Capital Events. Repayment is expected on an amortizing basis from surplus cash. Late charges of 5% apply if payments are not made within 10 days of the due date.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; applications accepted on rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers, project sponsors, for-profit businesses, non-profit organizations, county governments, and municipalities creating or preserving affordable rental housing financed through the Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Gap financing for the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing. Funds must be used in conjunction with Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's tax-exempt bonds and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits. RHW loans may not be used as cash collateral for short-term bonds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Maryland. Statewide eligibility.
requirements_list: Project must be financed using Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits

Required zoning for use and density of development must be in place at time of application. A letter from the local zoning office or approved PUD resolution satisfies this requirement. Development or site plan approval is not required at application. Conditional use or special exception approval is not required at threshold.
Award of any competitive public and private sources of funding necessary for the project's financial feasibility must have been made
Project's projected Full Time Equivalent must be documented using the Rental Housing Works Full Time Equivalent Job Calculator (an FTE equals 2,080 hours per year)
Board of Public Works must approve all Rental Housing Works funding awards
Projects must meet requirements of Multifamily Bond Program and Qualified Allocation Plan
Rental Housing Works loans may not be used as cash collateral for short-term bonds
Borrower must certify that information contained in the application is accurate
Maximum loan amount per project is $2.5 million, subject to waiver for projects where additional funding is necessary for financial feasibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on an ongoing/rolling basis in conjunction with an application for the Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits. Applicants must submit: (1) a completed RHW Application with certification; (2) a completed CDA Form 202 clearly identifying RHW funds and conforming to RHW funding limitations; (3) written documentation from local zoning office showing required zoning for use and density is in place; (4) documentation certifying award of any competitive public and private funding necessary for project feasibility; and (5) a completed RHW Full Time Equivalent Job Calculator. A separate application for the Multifamily Bond Program, LIHTC, and any other DHCD funding must be submitted using the Department's standard Application Submission Package in advance or at the same time as the RHW application. Department tracks applications by date of receipt and reviews them in conjunction with Multifamily Bond Program applications. If threshold criteria are not met, the application is rejected and applicant is notified in writing. Projects passing threshold are scored using Evaluation Criteria. Kick-off meetings are scheduled after scoring is complete. Projects are funded on a first-ready-to-proceed basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: Financing for the development and preservation of affordable rental housing in priority funding areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financing provided for the development and preservation of affordable rental housing in priority funding areas.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and owners of multifamily rental housing
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and preservation of affordable rental housing
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in priority funding areas
requirements_list: Property must be affordable rental housing
Property must be located in priority funding areas

structured_extraction.program_name: Request for Interest: Federal Funding Application Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers grants to help local jurisdictions and internet service providers pay for costs related to preparing federal funding applications for broadband projects. It covers expenses like market studies, engineering assessments, legal services, financial analysis, and other consulting services needed to develop a competitive federal application.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $125,000 in 100% grant coverage for properly contracted services required for federal broadband funding application preparation. Eligible costs include engineering consultants, financial consultants, marketing studies, legal consultants, and other costs considered on a case-by-case basis. Reimbursement is only provided for projects that submit a completed application for the federal funding program and meet the terms and conditions of that federal funding program. The OSB will also assist with preparing and reviewing federal funding applications to ensure they are complete and competitive, and will coordinate with other State Agencies on the use of State assets where feasible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions and their internet service provider partners seeking federal broadband funding for unserved rural areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Market studies, engineering assessments, legal services, financial analysis, and other approved consulting services necessary for federal broadband funding application preparation. Projects must serve unserved areas with a minimum internet connectivity of 1000 Mbps down and 1000 Mbps up with a maximum latency of 50 milliseconds (or meet more restrictive federal program requirements).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Unserved rural areas in Maryland defined as areas without internet service at 25 Mbps down and 3 Mbps up, unless the federal funding program defines a different standard. Areas must comply with the specific federal program's geographic and service requirements.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction or ISP partner of a local jurisdiction
Proposed service area must meet all applicable federal program requirements
Must serve unserved areas meeting the OSB definition of broadband service
Project must submit a completed application for the identified federal funding program
Project must meet all terms and conditions of the federal funding program
Local jurisdiction and ISP partner must jointly apply via completed application form
Applicant must provide W-9 form and Federal EIN number
Must demonstrate network capability to provide minimum 1000 Mbps down and 1000 Mbps up with maximum 50 milliseconds latency (or meet more restrictive federal program requirements)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should submit one electronic copy of their response to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with the name of the applicant and 'Federal Funding Assistance RFP response' in the subject line. The response must include: (1) cover letter with local jurisdiction and partner contact information, (2) completed and signed application form, (3) business model summary outlining network operations and customer operations, (4) statement of experience of team members, (5) network design and construction description including speed, latency, backhaul method, and infrastructure approach, (6) customer profile and competitive service analysis, and (7) implementation schedule with key milestones. The OSB will evaluate responses to guide partnership and funding allocation decisions. Selection is based on qualifications and evaluation of submittals with possible interviews. Partnerships are offered on a rolling basis depending on federal funding opportunity and available state funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: Expands affordable housing for low-income adults with disabilities by providing project-based rental assistance tied to specific units in approved rental housing. Federally funded through HUD, the program is operated through a partnership between DHCD, the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD), and the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). It helps eligible residents live in stable housing with access to supportive services.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible rental properties receive project-based rental assistance to subsidize the contract rent of eligible participants. Units are rented to eligible adults with disabilities referred by the Maryland Department of Disabilities. The program is funded by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Housing developers and property owners who receive federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits or State Rental Housing Funds and wish to provide housing to low-income adults with disabilities, as well as for-profit and non-profit sponsors of affordable rental housing developments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance to subsidize contract rent for eligible adult residents with disabilities in approved rental housing properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Projects must be located in priority funding areas. In the FY 2012 demonstration, approximately 75% of units were anticipated to be in the Baltimore and Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Areas, with remaining units on the Eastern Shore and Western Maryland.
requirements_list: Rental property must be eligible for project-based rental assistance through existing DHCD financing programs
Property must receive financing from DHCD
Eligible residents must be between ages 18 and 61
Eligible residents must have a qualifying disability and receive Medicaid
Eligible residents must have household income at or below 30% of the Area Median Income (AMI)
Eligible residents must be referred by the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: DHCD meets with an Interagency Committee to review projects that align with the program's goals. The committee includes representatives from MDOD and the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). Once a project is selected, DHCD issues a Reservation Award Letter to the developer confirming that the property is eligible for funding to support unit subsidies for people with disabilities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides competitive grants and loans to anchor institutions that build relationships with the community to generate jobs, strengthen partnerships between anchor institutions and the state, and lead to safer, healthier, and more attractive communities. Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities or areas of the state that have not been invested in. Eligible anchor institutions include institutions of higher education and qualifying hospital institutions in Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants and loans awarded to anchor institutions for capital improvement projects, including construction, facility development, workforce training centers, skilled trades education programs, and public access projects. Anchor institutions must provide matching funds equal to the amount of financial assistance received from the Fund (1:1 match requirement). Funds can be used for projects located in Sustainable Communities or areas of the state that have not been invested in. Maximum project sizes and funding amounts vary based on the specific funding round.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anchor institutions, defined as institutions of higher education or hospital institutions in Maryland that meet specific criteria regarding medical staff organization, diagnostic and treatment services, and overnight care capabilities, committed to job creation and community improvement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvement projects in eligible project locations (Sustainable Communities or areas of the state that have not been invested in), including construction, facility development, workforce training centers, skilled trades education programs, public access projects, community resources centers, makerspaces, adaptive reuse projects, and facility renovations that support community engagement and economic development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Funds can only be used in Sustainable Communities or areas of the state that have not been invested in. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility. The program is available statewide, including Kent County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an anchor institution (institution of higher education or hospital institution in Maryland)
Hospital institutions must have a group of at least five physicians organized as a medical staff
Hospital institutions must maintain facilities to provide diagnostic and treatment services for two or more unrelated individuals under medical staff supervision
Hospital institutions must admit or retain individuals for overnight care
Anchor institution must provide matching funds equal to the amount of financial assistance received (1:1 match)
Project must be located in Sustainable Communities or areas of the state that have not been invested in
Project should build an ongoing relationship between the anchor institution and the community
Project should support workforce development, job creation, or community revitalization
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's competitive grant and loan process. Applicants should visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage for detailed guidance on how to apply, including any required forms, supporting documentation, and submission procedures. Competitive review occurs on a regular basis with funding announcements made accordingly.

structured_extraction.program_name: Shelter and Transitional Housing Facilities Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to improve, create, or acquire transitional housing and emergency shelters that include supportive services. The program aims to reduce homelessness in Maryland by supporting new construction, acquisition, rehabilitation, and purchase of capital equipment. The Program provides capital financing for emergency shelters and transitional housing facilities that provide housing and support services to households to prevent homelessness and assist households to be able to live independently, utilizing a 'Harm Reduction' approach for supportive services.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for new construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment. Grant funds generally may not exceed one-half of total project costs. Under certain conditions, grants may cover as much as 75 percent of total project costs. Recipients must maintain the project as transitional housing or emergency shelter for 15 years or the grant becomes repayable. Eligible uses include: acquiring land and buildings; studies, surveys, plans, specifications, appraisals; site preparation; labor and materials for construction and rehabilitation; acquisition of necessary machinery, equipment, and furnishings including HVAC systems; and fees and premiums such as bonds and insurance. Ineligible uses include: refinancing existing debt, operating assistance, salaries and wages, administrative or legal costs, maintenance, fund-raising activities, and replacement of furnishings in existing facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status and local governments seeking to create or improve transitional housing or emergency shelters for homeless or at-risk individuals and families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing facilities and emergency shelters that provide supportive services. Eligible activities include acquiring land and buildings, site preparation, construction and rehabilitation costs, equipment and furnishings with at least 15-year life expectancy, architectural and engineering services, utilities installation, and site development improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. All projects involving new construction must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA). PFAs include all incorporated municipalities including Baltimore City, all areas between the Baltimore beltway and Baltimore City limits and Washington, DC beltway and Washington, DC boundary, all areas designated as Sustainable Communities, Federal and State enterprise zones, all areas designated by county governments as PFAs including rural villages designated in county comprehensive plans as of July 1, 1998, and certified heritage areas within locally designated growth areas. Local government letters of support are required for all projects, and letters certifying location in a PFA are required for projects involving new construction.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or local government
Project must be transitional housing or emergency shelter that includes supportive services for residents
Residents served must be homeless households and individuals, defined as households without permanent housing and lacking resources to obtain permanent housing and in imminent danger of homelessness
Sponsor must agree to maintain the project as transitional housing or emergency shelter for 15 years
Local government letter of support is required for all projects
Letter from local government certifying project location in a Priority Funding Area required for projects involving new construction
Grant generally cannot exceed one-half of total project costs unless conditions warrant up to 75 percent coverage
Applicants must identify and serve a specific homeless target population throughout the 15-year funding term
Supportive services must be clearly defined with identified service providers
Commitment letters, agreements, or documents identifying sources of funding for services and operating expenses must be submitted
All projects involving new construction or substantial rehabilitation are subject to thorough review by Department's Construction Management staff
Compliance with State roofing policy for any roofing projects (minimum 20-year, no-dollar-limit warranty)
Compliance with Maryland Historical Trust requirements with letter stating review is complete before fund disbursement
Compliance with Minority Business Enterprise requirements with goal of at least 29% certified MBE participation
Compliance with LEED building standards encouraged
Compliance with Forest Conservation Program if construction on land greater than 40,000 square feet
All contractors must be checked against State debarment list
If applicable, must sign Affidavit Not to Use Funds for Religious Purposes
Equipment and furnishings must have life expectancy of at least 15 years, not become technically obsolete for 15 years, be of durable construction, and not be elaborate or extravagant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should refer to the Shelter and Transitional Housing Facilities Grant Program Guidebook for detailed application procedures and requirements. Applicants must submit a complete application including a threshold review. The Department's Multifamily Housing Programs will conduct underwriting review and construction review for eligible applications. Processing time will be determined based on completeness of application and complexity of project. The Department will enlist assistance from the Maryland Department of Human Resources' Office of Transitional Services or Department of Health Office of Health Care Quality to review the adequacy and sufficiency of proposed supportive services programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program designed to preserve and improve single-family owner-occupied homes by rehabilitating them and bringing properties up to applicable building codes and standards or a minimum housing quality standard. STAR loans may also be used to build replacement houses under certain conditions. Loans are funded with federal HOME funds and certain HUD requirements apply. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development and processed directly by local governments.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent interest rate loans that are fully deferred (no monthly payments required during the loan term). The maximum loan is generally 100 percent of the property value, though in Frederick County the maximum may be up to 110 percent of the after-rehabilitation value, with exceptions to the debt-to-value limit considered on a case-by-case basis. Interest rates for other programs range from 0% to 6% based on the applicant's ability to pay. The maximum loan term is 30 years. Loans securing families with incomes at or below 50 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income may have deferred payments if necessary for project feasibility. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage or Deed of Trust. Grants may be considered on a case-by-case basis in certain jurisdictions. Loans are processed directly by local governments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes with household income at or below 80 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income. Generally income cannot exceed 50 percent of HUD income limits; however, some loans are available to households at 80 percent of limits with special circumstances. In Frederick County, income eligibility may also be based on 30 percent of the Washington, D.C. MSA median income, or 55 percent of the statewide median income for families with poor credit ratings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of owner-occupied single-family homes to bring properties up to applicable building codes and standards or a minimum housing quality standard. Addressable items include mold remediation, gas leaks, roof repair and replacement, asbestos abatement, lead abatement, combustion appliance repair, chimney repair, foundation waterproofing, radon mitigation, electrical hazards and upgrades, plumbing issues, water and well issues, septic and sewer, windows and doors for health and safety concerns, structural repair, accessibility for disabled and seniors, fall prevention, ductwork upgrades, building shell stabilization, and pest treatment. STAR loans may also be used to build replacement houses under certain conditions. Maximum funding requests should not exceed $50,000.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Maryland jurisdictions outside of Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford County, Howard County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County. Includes Frederick County, where the program is administered locally. Available in 18 eligible counties statewide.
requirements_list: Owner must occupy the single-family home as primary residence
Household income generally cannot exceed 80 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
Household income generally cannot exceed 50 percent of HUD income limits (some loans available to households at 80 percent of limits with special circumstances)
Property must be a single-family home, duplex, townhome, condo, or manufactured home

In Frederick County, income at or below 30 percent of the Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area (MSA) median income, or consideration may be given to families with income at or below 55 percent of the statewide median income with a poor credit rating
In exceptional cases in Frederick County, borrowers with incomes up to 80 percent of HUD-defined median income may qualify
Property must meet HUD's definition of modest housing
Applicants must provide a scope of work and bid from a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement contractor or other trade professional

Contractor must provide current MHIC license or applicable trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance with per occurrence limits of $1 million or greater, Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9 form
Property ownership must be proven with deed and current mortgage statement
Most recent property tax bill and homeowners insurance policy declaration page required
Photos must document critical repairs requiring funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted directly to local governments or to DHCD Special Loan Programs. Applicants must complete the Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program Application and provide all required supporting documentation including: two months of paystubs or recent tax returns for income verification; proof of home ownership; property tax bills and insurance information; contractor bids with photos documenting critical repairs; and contractor credentials including MHIC license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and W-9 form. Bids should not be more than 60 days old and the grand total should not exceed $50,000. Incomplete applications will not be processed. Applications can be submitted via email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mailed to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Strategic Demolition Fund seeks to accelerate economic development and job production in existing Maryland communities by improving the economic viability of greyfield development projects, which often face more barriers than sprawling greenfield development. The Fund aims to catalyze activities that create high economic and revitalization impact in existing communities, supporting demolition of derelict structures and site preparation to enable redevelopment.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants (and loans) to support demolition of derelict non-contributing structures, site acquisition and assembly to create redevelopment-sized parcels for solicitation or planned development, site development, and construction-level architectural and engineering designs. Awards focus on projects with high economic and revitalization impact. FY27 proposed funding totals $10,000,000. Example projects include: City of Salisbury received funding for Lot 16 Pavilion and Riverwalk Crossing Phase 2 ($340,000) for infrastructure to support mixed-use retail/residential building reconstruction; City of Frederick Downtown Hotel and Conference Center ($500,000) for predevelopment and architectural/engineering designs; Town of Easton Crossing ($500,000) for site development on former Perdue Agribusiness industrial site; Howard County Court Avenue/Court Place Placemaking ($600,000) for public green space with demolition of vacant building; Baltimore County Security West ($1,000,000) for demolition and BGE substation establishing to catalyze Woodlawn revitalization and Security Square Mall redevelopment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (county governments, municipalities/towns) and nonprofit community development organizations working outside of Baltimore City on projects in Sustainable Communities or Opportunity Zones. Also available to Sustainable Community designated areas statewide.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Demolition of derelict non-contributing structures; site acquisition and assembly to create redevelopment-sized parcels for solicitation or planned development; site development; construction-level architectural and engineering designs; mixed-use development, residential and commercial construction, riverwalk and waterfront improvements, bulkhead upgrades, and streetscape enhancements; roof replacement for low-income homeowners; fire suppression systems; sewer and stormwater infrastructure; parking facilities; commercial kitchens; historic preservation and adaptive reuse; public green spaces and placemaking amenities; recreational facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in designated Sustainable Communities outside Baltimore City, or in Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties. Available statewide outside Baltimore City in eligible designated areas. Based on FY27 funding, projects are being supported in Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Charles, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Somerset, Talbot, and Wicomico Counties.
requirements_list: Lead applicant must be a local government or nonprofit community development organization working outside of Baltimore City
Project must be located in a designated Sustainable Community outside Baltimore City or in an Opportunity Zone in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, or Wicomico County
Project must involve demolition of derelict structures or site preparation activities
Project must be aimed at accelerating economic development and job production
Must be located in an existing Maryland community
Project should demonstrate high economic and revitalization impact
Projects should create redevelopment-sized parcels or enable productive reuse of properties
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For information on how to apply, refer to the State Revitalization Programs webpage at https://dhcd.maryland.gov/Communities/Pages/StateRevitalizationPrograms/default.aspx. Applications are submitted through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's State Revitalization Programs process. For county-level inquiries in Kent County, contact Jamie Williams at jlwilliams@kentgov.org or 410-810-2168. For Prince George's County inquiries, contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 and ask to speak with a Business Development Specialist. Funding is awarded on an annual basis, typically with specific rounds of funding announced each fiscal year.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state designation program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that provides local governments with a shared geographic designation to support community development, revitalization, and sustainability through coordinated strategies. The program combines resources for historic preservation, housing, and economic development under a single designation, focusing on infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, and development that strengthens existing communities. It enables designated areas to access state funding programs and promotes growth that is environmentally, economically, and socially responsible.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a geographic designation that qualifies local areas for access to various state funding programs and coordinated state investment in community revitalization, historic preservation, housing, and economic development. It does not directly distribute funds but rather enables designated communities to access other state assistance programs such as Community Legacy and Strategic Demolition Fund. The designation is valid for five years and can be renewed. State Designated Transit Oriented Development Areas approved after 2023 automatically constitute Sustainable Community Areas.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis - applications accepted at any time; no specific deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Municipal and county governments seeking to revitalize older communities and promote sustainable growth that is environmentally, economically, and socially responsible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The designation itself does not fund projects directly. However, designated Sustainable Communities become eligible to apply for state funding programs that support historic preservation, housing development, economic development, infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, and community strengthening initiatives. Local governments can coordinate state resources across these areas once designated.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All proposed Sustainable Communities areas must be located entirely within a Priority Funding Area and be within or near a town center or transportation center. The program has approved Sustainable Communities designations across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. State Designated Transit Oriented Development Areas approved after 2023 automatically constitute Sustainable Community Areas. For TOD areas approved before 2023 seeking SRP funding, applicants must either have an approved Sustainable Community Action Plan or update their TOD Designation Applications.
requirements_list: Entire area must be within a Priority Funding Area
Proposed community should be within or near a town center or transportation center
Must demonstrate financial need for local revitalization
Must have defined geographic area with existing built environment needing revitalization or additional state investment
Must have local government resolution supporting boundary designation and Action Plan
Must include Sustainable Community Action Plan summarizing key initiatives and projects
Action Plan must be consistent with other existing community or comprehensive plans
For new designations, must have meeting with Sustainable Communities Program staff before applying
Must show a targeted approach to revitalization
For TOD areas approved before 2023 seeking SRP funding, must either have an approved Sustainable Community Action Plan or update their TOD Designation Applications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Request an application template by emailing Tynan Stevenson with subject line indicating whether it is a new designation or renewal application and including the community name and sponsoring jurisdiction. New designations require a meeting with program staff before applying. Step 2: Submit application including a defined geographic area with built environment, a Sustainable Community Action Plan, and a local government resolution. Step 3: An interagency panel led by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development reviews the application. Step 4: The panel presents the application to the Governor's Smart Growth Subcabinet for final approval. Step 5: Once approved, the designation is valid for five years and can be renewed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Designed to assist technology-based businesses during the pre-seed to pre-venture capital funding stage.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Equity investment for technology-based businesses in pre-seed to pre-venture capital funding stages. Investment size ranges from $500,000 to $2,000,000 in the form of convertible notes or equity. Minimum 1:1 private capital match required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Technology-based businesses seeking venture-stage equity investment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-seed to pre-venture capital equity investment for technology-based businesses.
requirements_list: Less than 251 employees
Equity raised to date less than $15M
Minimum 1:1 private capital match
Must be a technology-based business
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are being accepted through TEDCO Maryland Venture Fund.

structured_extraction.program_description: Designed to assist businesses with seed stage investing across multiple technology and innovation sectors.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Seed stage equity investment in four types of investment areas: cyber tech/information technology, life sciences, general technology commercialization, and gap funding. Investment size ranges from $200,000 to $750,000 in the form of convertible notes or equity. Minimum 1:1 private capital match required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage technology businesses seeking seed stage investment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Seed stage investment for technology commercialization, cyber tech, information technology, life sciences, and gap funding.
requirements_list: Less than 15-30 employees based on funding source
Minimum 1:1 private capital match
Equity raised to date between $2M - $5M based on funding source
Must focus on one of four investment types: cyber tech/info tech, life sciences, general technology commercialization, or gap funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are being accepted through TEDCO SEED Investment Funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: Designed to assist pre-seed technology startups founded by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Pre-seed equity investment for technology-based startups founded by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals. Investment size ranges from $200,000 to $500,000 in the form of convertible notes or equity. Minimum 1:1 private capital match required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-seed technology startups founded by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-seed equity investment for technology-based business development.
requirements_list: 50% or greater founders ownership
Founders must demonstrate economic and social disadvantage
Minimum 1:1 private capital match
Less than 251 employees
Equity raised to date less than $15M
Must be a technology-based business
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are being accepted through TEDCO Social Impact Funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: Designed to fund early-stage venture capital funds focused on investing in Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Limited partnership investment in early-stage venture capital funds focused on investing in Maryland. Investment terms follow TEDCO standard limited partnership terms and fees are structured to meet SSBCI guidelines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage venture capital funds focused on investing in Maryland-based businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital for venture capital funds to invest in Maryland-based companies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Focus on Maryland investment.
requirements_list: Investment thesis and return on investment potential
Fund management focus and sector experience
Commitment to Maryland
Fees must meet SSBCI guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are being accepted through TEDCO Venture Capital Limited Partnership.

structured_extraction.program_name: UPLIFT (Utilizing Progressive Lending Investments to Finance Transformation)
structured_extraction.program_description: UPLIFT helps close the appraisal gap in historically redlined communities by funding the difference between the cost to build or renovate quality affordable housing and the price the property can sell for on the market. The program accelerates development, construction, and sale of affordable homes in low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities to increase property values and provide wealth-building homeownership opportunities for targeted households. It also couples development loans with a commitment from DHCD to offer grants and loans to nearby Legacy Homeowners, often living in energy inefficient and deteriorated housing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State covers the appraisal gap (the difference between the total eligible cost to develop a property and the price the property can sell for on the market) through UPLIFT funding. Selected qualified development teams acquire, develop, build, and sell quality affordable housing in targeted neighborhoods using a combination of public and private financing, with UPLIFT covering the gap. Homebuyers acquire fee simple title using a combination of down payment, down payment assistance, first mortgage loan (Maryland Mortgage Program or other source), other acceptable subsidy support, and a soft promissory note with the Department. The Department may also provide loans to nearby Legacy Homeowners for rehabilitation and energy efficiency improvements. Program fees include a $1,000 non-refundable application fee per project and a 1% origination fee on the loan amount paid at initial closing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and for-profit developers, builders, and community organizations seeking to develop, construct, and sell quality affordable housing in targeted low-income neighborhoods and Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding covers the appraisal gap to make affordable housing development financially feasible in low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities. Funds support acquisition, development, construction, and sale of quality affordable homes. Development teams must use public and private financing in combination. Projects must meet UPLIFT Design and Construction Standards. Funds may also support grants and loans to Legacy Homeowners for rehabilitation and energy efficiency improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program targets low-income census tracts (where 50 percent of households have incomes below 60 percent of the Area Median Income or have a poverty rate of 25 percent or more) and designated Sustainable Communities across Maryland. Projects must be located in both a Low-Income Census Tract and a Maryland Sustainable Community area. New Construction projects are not permitted in FEMA Flood Zone A or A99. Projects in Zone C may submit waiver requests with engineer documentation. Projects in Zone X may submit waiver requests with flood mitigation plans. An UPLIFT Qualified Areas Map is available to identify eligible locations.
requirements_list: Project must be located in both a low-income census tract and designated Sustainable Community
Development team must include qualified developers or builders with comparable project experience
Project must meet UPLIFT Design and Construction Standards including energy efficiency, environmental requirements, and accessibility standards
Project must comply with one of the following building standards: US EPA Energy Star, Enterprise Green Communities, LEED, NGBS Green Promise, or Earthcraft
Applicant must submit $1,000 non-refundable fee per project with application
Project must comply with program underwriting and accountability standards
Applicants must schedule and attend a pre-application meeting before submitting formal application
Applicants must submit both electronic (via Dropbox) and physical hard copy of complete application
Development team must demonstrate site control and readiness to proceed
Projects must consist of newly constructed or substantially rehabilitated formerly vacant structures
All development team entities must submit audited, reviewed, or compiled financial statements prepared according to GAAP
Individuals providing guarantees must submit personal financial statements
Development team must have acceptable credit history and financial capacity to execute project
Project must include neighborhood engagement and affirmative fair housing marketing
Developer fees must be sized according to program formula
Sales prices must be approved by the Department
Project must meet specified design and construction quality thresholds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 0: Review UPLIFT Program Guide and prepare project details, timelines, plans, and logistics. Schedule and complete Pre-Application Meeting, submitting all required pre-application materials at least two business days before scheduled meeting date. After Pre-Application Meeting, complete Electronic Application Submission Request Form to receive Dropbox access. Step 1: Download Application Documents Package from UPLIFT website. Step 2: Complete each section of application, consulting detailed instructions. Step 3: Use Dropbox link to upload each application document to respective folder. Create free Dropbox account, open shared link, click 'Join folder' button to gain upload access. Step 4: Complete Final Submission Checklist confirming all parts submitted and sign off for each section. Step 5: Submit both electronic application (via Dropbox) and physical hard copy to DHCD Operations & Administration Office at 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. Notify UPLIFT team when physical copy will arrive. Submit $1,000 non-refundable application fee via ACH or check simultaneously with or before application submission. Step 6: DHCD conducts threshold review of materially complete applications for compliance with Threshold Criteria. Materially incomplete applications will not be evaluated. Step 7: Applications passing Threshold Review are scored against Evaluative Criteria (Development Team Capacity, Project Impact, Leveraging Resources, Readiness to Proceed, Design Quality). Step 8: UPLIFT Loan Committee reviews and recommends projects to Secretary for approval. Step 9: Secretary determination authorizes commitment and investment of resources. Step 10: If approved, commitment letter issued specifying terms and conditions. Step 11: Project Kick-off Meeting held 45-60 days after complete application to determine underwriting schedule and requirements. Step 12: Final Underwriting Submission prepared updating financing, design, construction, and marketing elements. Step 13: Underwriting approval leads to closing checklist submission to Office of Attorney General. Step 14: Initial financing closing with Notice to Proceed issued to builder. Step 15: Construction Kick-off Meeting held to coordinate construction phase processes, marketing, and occupancy requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state program created to help homeowners who are struggling to pay their mortgage or other housing costs due to COVID-19 related financial hardships. The fund provides direct financial assistance to qualifying homeowners statewide to help prevent foreclosure and address housing cost burdens arising from the COVID-19 pandemic.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers direct financial assistance to eligible homeowners to help them pay their mortgage and other housing costs to avoid foreclosure. Specific benefit amounts and terms are available on the Maryland Homeowner Assistance Fund webpage.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mortgage payments and other housing costs to prevent foreclosure.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland WholeHome Program helps homeowners make valuable repairs and enhancements to their homes that can lower monthly utility bills and improve quality of life. The program offers grants and low-interest loans for home repairs, energy efficiency improvements, and accessibility upgrades including energy efficient appliances, heating and cooling system repair or replacement, insulation replacement, accessibility features for seniors or those with special needs, lead paint removal, plumbing and septic upgrades, roof repair/replacement, and structural and maintenance issues.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and low-interest loans for home repairs and energy efficiency improvements. Maximum interest rate is 4% and may be as low as zero. Payments may be deferred and there is no application fee. Loan and grant amounts are based on the type of work needed, household income, and ability to repay. Eligible improvements include energy efficient appliances, heating and cooling system repair or replacement, insulation replacement, accessibility features for seniors or those with special needs, lead paint removal, plumbing and septic upgrades, roof repair/replacement, and structural and maintenance issues.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides time-limited cash assistance to low-income adults aged 18-64 with physical or mental disabilities who do not have dependent children under 18 living in the home and have no other resources. The program supports individuals unable to remain in the workforce due to disability, including while their Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) application is being processed. Available statewide in Maryland and administered locally through county Departments of Social Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Temporary cash assistance for disabled individuals. Benefits are provided to those with verified physical or mental disabilities lasting at least 3 months. Income of a spouse is used to determine eligibility except for SSI benefits. Applicants may be required to apply for SSI and SSDI and must agree to reimbursement from any SSI payments received. Processing can take up to 30 days or more.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) Program provides time-limited cash assistance to needy families with dependent children when available resources do not fully meet the family's needs. The program helps adults find employment and promotes self-sufficiency through work participation requirements, employment resources, and support services. Families with minor children can receive benefits for a total of 60 months (5 years) over a lifetime. The program is available statewide in Maryland, with local administration through county Departments of Social Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cash benefits issued through Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card (Independence Card). Cash benefits are made available from the 2nd to the 4th of every month based on the first letter of last name. The maximum monthly benefit varies by family size: 1 person ($328), 2 people ($575), 3 people ($727), 4 people ($870), 5 people ($1,010), 6 people ($1,110), 7 people ($1,247), 8 people ($1,372). Eligibility is based on household size and income; earned and unearned income (excluding SSI income) cannot exceed the benefit level for the assistance unit size. Families with minor children can receive benefits for a total of 60 months (5 years) over a lifetime. Recipients must meet income guidelines and participate 40 hours per week in the Work Program to continue receiving the full TCA benefit amount. Processing can take up to 30 days or more. Pregnant women and caretaker relatives applying for children not their own may have different work participation requirements.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash assistance to meet basic household living expenses, including living costs for families with children; also supports employment preparation and self-sufficiency activities through the Work Opportunities Program which provides job readiness classes, job search assistance, work programs, childcare, and transportation assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) / Food Supplement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The largest federal nutrition assistance program in the nation, SNAP (formerly known as Food Stamps and also referred to as the Food Supplement Program in Maryland) helps low-income individuals and households buy nutritious food needed for good health. Monthly benefits are issued through an Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card, known as the Independence Card, and can be used at participating retail stores. Eligibility is based on the USDA Thrifty Food Plan and is determined by household size, gross income, and allowable expenses. The program is administered statewide in Maryland, with county-level offices handling applications and interviews.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Human Services / County Departments of Social Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly food supplement benefits issued through an Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card known as the Independence Card. The benefit amount depends on household size, gross income, and allowable expenses. Benefits are issued within 30 days of application approval, or within 7 days for those qualifying for expedited benefits due to very low income. Issuance dates are scheduled monthly based on the first three letters of the applicant's last name, with issuance occurring between the 4th and 23rd of each month. Benefits can be used at participating retail stores to purchase food for household consumption. Households may also need to supplement benefits with their own cash to afford a full month of food.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income individuals, families, and households whose income is at or below eligibility thresholds based on household size. U.S. citizens and non-citizens with qualified immigrant status are eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of nutritious food and essential food items for household consumption at participating retail stores.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP) is a statewide Maryland program administered locally through the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) that helps income-eligible homeowners and renters pay their electric utility bills and make energy costs more affordable. Grants are paid directly to the electric utility to help with past due or ongoing electric bills. Eligible customers are placed on a budget billing plan with their utility company, which spreads annual utility bills into even monthly payments to avoid seasonal spikes. The program is available statewide and administered locally in each county. One application covers both EUSP and the Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Human Services, Office of Home Energy Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: EUSP provides grant assistance paid directly to the electric utility to help with past due or ongoing electric bills. Eligible households may receive a benefit once per program year (July 1 to June 30) and must reapply each fiscal year. Eligible customers are placed on a budget billing plan with their utility company, which spreads annual utility bills into even monthly payments. Financial eligibility is based on household gross monthly income over the last 30 days and household size. For households with no members 67 years or older: maximum income limits range from $1,878/month for one person to $2,540/month for two people, $3,203/month for three people, $3,865/month for four people, $4,527/month for five people, $5,189/month for six people, $5,851/month for seven people, $6,513/month for eight people, with $662 added for each additional person. For households with one or more members 67 years or older: maximum income limits range from $2,147/month for one person to $2,903/month for two people, $3,660/month for three people, $4,417/month for four people, $5,173/month for five people, $5,930/month for six people, $6,687/month for seven people, $7,443/month for eight people, with $757 added for each additional person. There is no asset test. Grant amounts are calculated based on income from the last 30 days and fuel type. Participation in Budget Billing is required to receive EUSP. All energy assistance dollars are grants and do not need to be repaid.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis (July–May each year) until funding is depleted; program year runs July 1 to June 30. Benefits may only be received once per fiscal year. OHEP is a year-round program.
