structured_extraction.program_name: Low Income Household Water Assistance Program (LIHWAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: LIHWAP is a statewide Maryland program that helps income-eligible renters, homeowners, and public housing residents pay water and wastewater bills. It is part of a federally-funded American Rescue Plan program. Grants can be used to restore disconnected services, prevent disconnection, or pay past due balances and standard fees. Benefits range from $100 to $2,000 depending on household income, size, and arrearage balance. In some instances, a one-time grant of up to $10,000 may be available toward arrearages for residential water and/or wastewater bills. Applications are processed first come, first served in each jurisdiction until funding is depleted.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Human Services, Office of Home Energy Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: LIHWAP provides grants of $100 to $2,000 (and in some cases up to $10,000) to help pay water and wastewater bills. Benefits can be used to restore services to disconnected households, prevent disconnection, or pay past due balances (arrearages of 30 days or more) and standard fees including reconnection fees. The three types of assistance include: (1) Reconnect Household Water/Wastewater Services - up to $2,000 to pay off balance and reconnection fees if service has been disconnected; (2) Prevent Disconnection of Household Water/Wastewater Services - grant funds to pay all or part of bill if disconnection notice received; (3) Reduce Current Household Water/Wastewater Past Due Balance - temporary assistance for households struggling to afford current water bills. Applications are processed first come, first served in each jurisdiction until funding is depleted. Benefit amounts are based on household income, household size, and the arrearage balance owed. All energy assistance dollars are grants and do not need to be repaid.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis until funding is depleted; first come, first served
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible renters, homeowners, and public housing residents statewide in Maryland who need help paying water or wastewater bills, including those at risk of disconnection or with past due balances.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of water and wastewater bills, past due balances (arrearages of 30 days or more), and standard fees including reconnection fees. Can restore disconnected services or prevent disconnection. Applicants must be responsible for payment of a water and/or wastewater bill issued by a public water system or treatment works and must live at the property for which assistance is being provided.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; available in all counties. Applicants must be Maryland residents and live at the property for which assistance is being provided.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident responsible for payment of a water and/or wastewater bill issued by a public water system or treatment works
Must live at the property for which assistance is being provided

Must be low-income and meet program income limits based on household size (Effective July 1, 2021 - June 30, 2022: 1 person: $3,121/month; 2 persons: $4,081/month; 3 persons: $5,041/month; 4 persons: $6,000/month; 5 persons: $6,962/month; 6 persons: $7,922/month; 7 persons: $8,102/month; 8 persons: $8,283/month; add $180/month for each additional person)
Household gross income must not exceed the income thresholds listed in the program guidelines
Service address must have a minimum arrearage balance of $100 (unless categorically eligible)

May be categorically eligible if at least one household member is currently receiving Energy Assistance from OHEP, Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP), Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Supplemental Security Income (SSI), means-tested veterans benefits, or Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP)
Only one water/wastewater bill account per service address is eligible to receive program benefit
Must provide government-issued photo ID (copy of Driver's License or other government-issued identification card)

Must provide Social Security cards (copies) for all household members including children, or federal government-issued documents with name and Social Security number for all household members (at least one legal resident with Social Security number required)
Applicant does not need Social Security number if at least one household member is a legal resident with a Social Security number
Must provide proof of where you live (utility bill, water and/or wastewater bill, rental receipt, or lease)
Must provide water and/or wastewater utility bill or termination notice

Must provide documentation of household income for all household members over age 18 for the last 30 days (paystubs, Social Security letter, child support letter, unemployment letter, self-employment documentation, or similar)
If household received no income in the 30 days prior to application, must sign Declaration of Zero Income and provide additional information on how household is meeting basic needs
Must provide proof of all gross (pre-tax) income for all household members for the last 30 days
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can submit applications through the following methods: (1) Online at mymdthink.maryland.gov; (2) By mail to Office of Home Energy Programs, 1301 Piccard Drive, 4th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850; (3) In-person drop-off; (4) By email; (5) By fax to the Office of Home Energy Programs at 1301 Piccard Drive, 4th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850; (6) Contact local Department of Social Services for information and assistance. Submit all required supporting documents with application for fastest processing, including copy of photo ID, proof of income, proof of residence, Social Security cards, and water/wastewater bill or termination notice. Missing documents or signatures will delay application processing. The office reviews applications within 14 days of receiving a complete application and makes a final determination within 45 days. Applicants can check application status at myohepstatus.org, by calling 1-800-332-6347 or 240-777-4450, or by emailing ohep@montgomerycountymd.gov. Allow 15 days for application to appear on status website. Free translation services are available by calling local Department of Social Services, local OHEP office, or 1-800-332-6347. OHEP is a year-round program and applications can be submitted at any time.

structured_extraction.program_description: Program Open Space provides financial and technical assistance to local subdivisions and jurisdictions for the planning, acquisition, and development of recreation land or open space areas for public use. The program has assisted more than 6,200 park and conservation area projects since 1969. It acquires outdoor recreation and open space areas for public use and administers funds made available to local communities through the Outdoor Recreation Land Loan of 1969 and the Land and Water Conservation Fund from the National Park Service, U.S. Department of the Interior. Since 1970, Baltimore County alone has utilized nearly $163 million in POS funding for acquisition of properties to serve as parks and recreation sites, and for construction, enhancement, and renovations of recreational facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Program Open Space Local provides grants to local communities and jurisdictions for open and recreational space. Funds are drawn from the Outdoor Recreation Land Loan of 1969 and the Land and Water Conservation Fund of the National Park Service, U.S. Department of the Interior. Grants support planning, acquisition, and development of recreation land or open space areas, as well as construction, enhancement, and renovation of recreational facilities and preservation of woodlands, stream valleys, and other sensitive lands. Funds can be used for property acquisition, site development, facility construction, renovation and enhancement of existing parks and recreation areas, and preservation of natural areas. Since 1970, Baltimore County has utilized nearly $163 million in POS funding for these purposes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY26 public comment deadline through Thursday, October 16th; ongoing program with annual cycles
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local subdivisions, jurisdictions, and government entities throughout Maryland seeking to acquire, develop, or improve recreation land and open space areas for public use. Allegany County local subdivisions are specifically noted as eligible applicants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, acquisition, and development of recreation land or open space areas for public use; construction, enhancement, and renovations of recreational facilities; preservation of woodlands, stream valleys, and other sensitive lands; site improvements and infrastructure development for parks and recreation areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to local subdivisions and jurisdictions throughout Maryland. Allegany County local subdivisions are specifically noted as eligible. The program serves all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local subdivision, jurisdiction, or government entity
Project must involve planning, acquisition, or development of recreation land or open space for public use
Eligible uses include park acquisition, facility construction, enhancement of existing parks, and preservation of natural areas
Local matching funds may be required depending on project type and funding source
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested local jurisdictions and subdivisions should contact Andrew Cowan for specific information about the application process and current funding cycles. The county commissioners review and approve proposed Program Open Space funding allocations. Applications are evaluated on a competitive basis, and funding cycles typically occur annually. Public comment periods are held on proposed recommendations for county commissioners review and approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to innocent victims of crime in Maryland when no other resources are available. The Board compensates victims who suffer physical injury for their medical expenses and loss of earnings. In some circumstances, the Board may cover psychological injuries for counseling or lost wages. In cases of homicide, the Board may assist with funeral expenses and loss of support for the victim's dependents. Eligible claimants also include parents or guardians of victims, dependents of deceased victims, persons who paid funeral expenses, persons injured while preventing a crime or assisting a police officer, and persons injured or killed as a result of someone driving while intoxicated.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Board provides compensation for innocent crime victims to cover unreimbursed medical expenses, loss of earnings (minimum two continuous weeks or combined with more than $100 in other unreimbursed eligible costs), psychological counseling costs, and in homicide cases, funeral expenses and loss of support for dependents. Applicants must have incurred at least $100 of unreimbursed costs related to the victimization to qualify. Compensation is typically paid directly to providers or to the victim for out-of-pocket expenses. The Board may award compensation for medical and/or funeral expenses resulting from a crime when no other resources are available. Awards are made based on documented losses and financial need.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 3 years from the date of the crime or death of the victim. In cases of child abuse, within three years of the date the claimant knew or should have known of the abuse. Some sources indicate within 180 days of the crime. Crime must be reported to police as soon as possible or within the applicable timeframe.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Innocent victims of crime who have suffered physical injury, psychological injury, or loss as a result of criminal victimization; parents or guardians of victims; dependents of deceased victims; persons who paid funeral expenses; persons injured while preventing a crime or assisting a police officer; and persons injured or killed as a result of someone driving while intoxicated
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical expenses, loss of earnings, counseling or psychological treatment costs, funeral expenses (in cases of homicide), loss of support for dependents of homicide victims, and other unreimbursed costs directly related to victimization
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. The crime must have occurred in Maryland or the victim must be a Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Must be an innocent victim of crime — the victim bears no responsibility for the crime or the injury
Crime must be reported to police, preferably as soon as possible after the incident
Must have incurred at least $100 of unreimbursed costs related to the victimization
To receive lost wages, must have lost at least two continuous weeks of earnings or support, or have more than $100 in other unreimbursed eligible costs related to victimization
In cases of child abuse, claim must be filed within three years of the date the claimant knew or should have known of the abuse
Physical injury or death must be directly related to the crime
Serious financial hardship resulting from the crime
Completed claim form must be submitted to the CICB within the applicable deadline (within 3 years of the crime or within 180 days depending on circumstances)
Applicants must provide documentation of expenses and losses
Income and financial resources may be considered in determining award amounts
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain claim forms by calling 410-585-3010 or 1-888-679-9347, or download them online from the Maryland Department of Public Safety website (available in English and Spanish). 2. Complete the claim form with detailed information about the crime, injuries, expenses, and financial hardship. 3. Gather supporting documentation including police reports, medical records, proof of expenses, and proof of lost wages. 4. Submit the completed claim form and documentation to the Criminal Injuries Compensation Board at: 6776 Reisterstown Road, Suite 206, Baltimore, Maryland 21215, or by mail. 5. The Board will review the claim for eligibility and notify the claimant of the determination. 6. If approved, compensation is issued based on documented losses and the applicant's financial need. Claims must be submitted within the applicable deadline (generally within 3 years of the crime, or 180 days in some circumstances).

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-supported program administered locally by county health and environmental departments that provides financial assistance to upgrade failing or conventional septic systems with best available technology (BAT) nitrogen-reducing units, or to connect properties to public sewer systems where available. The program's primary goal is to reduce nitrogen and other nutrient pollution entering the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries. Funding is available to residential property owners, non-profits, and in some jurisdictions for-profit entities. For low-income households, funding can also cover replacement of failing septic systems. The program is administered at the county level in jurisdictions including Baltimore County, Charles County, Prince George's County, Talbot County, and others across the Chesapeake Bay watershed.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) / County-Administered
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant or subsidy funds from the State's Bay Restoration Fund to cover the cost and installation of best available technology (BAT) nitrogen-reducing septic systems plus two years of maintenance, or the cost of connecting to public sewer systems including connection fees and permits. For residential properties, funding is based on household income: properties with household income less than $300,000 per year receive 100 percent funding. Non-profit entities receive 100 percent funding. Non-residential properties receive 50 percent funding. For the Perry Hall Manor Sewer Extension Project in Baltimore County, grants of up to $20,000 are available. For low-income households, funding may also cover replacement of failing septic systems. Eligible BAT technologies include Fuji Clean, Orenco, Advantex RT, and SeptiTech systems, which have been certified or approved by NSF or EPA for nitrogen reduction. All systems must include professional maintenance by qualified operators and allow periodic county inspections. In Charles County, the program assisted 95 residents between November 2007 and December 2011. Applications in Prince George's County are processed through the Momentum portal.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sanitary District Officer (Talbot County); Ground Water Management (Baltimore County); Environmental Engineering (Prince George's County); Health Department (Charles County)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners (residential, non-profit, and in some counties for-profit) with private septic systems or properties needing sewer connections across the Chesapeake Bay watershed. Priority is given to low-income households with failing systems and properties within the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area (within 1,000 feet of mean high tide).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of best available technology (BAT) nitrogen-reducing septic tank units with two years of maintenance; connection to public sewer systems including permits and connection fees; proper abandonment of existing septic systems; replacement of failing septic systems for low-income households; obtaining plumbing permits for sewer connections.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland counties within the Chesapeake Bay watershed, administered locally. Confirmed participating jurisdictions include Baltimore County, Charles County, Prince George's County, Talbot County, and Anne Arundel County. Priority consideration is given to properties in Priority Funded Areas and properties within the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area (within 1,000 feet of mean high tide). The Perry Hall Manor Sewer Extension Project is specific to that Baltimore County community.
requirements_list: Property must have a private septic system eligible for upgrade or replacement with nitrogen-reducing technology, or access to public sewer
Property must be located within an eligible Maryland county in the Chesapeake Bay watershed
Property owner must submit a completed application form with proof/verification of income
Property owner must allow access for initial site inspection
For BAT installation, property owner must sign and record an agreement to maintain the system with a qualified operator and allow periodic county inspections
If property has access to public sewer, grant may only be approved for sewer connection
Residential properties with household income under $300,000/year qualify for 100% funding; non-residential properties qualify for 50% funding
Non-profit entities receive 100 percent funding
For Perry Hall Manor Sewer Extension Project: must obtain low bids from at least three qualified contractors
For Perry Hall Manor Sewer Extension Project: property owner must be connecting to the Perry Hall Manor Sewer Extension Project
Low-income households may qualify for replacement of failing septic systems
Must own an existing dwelling (Talbot County requirement)
Resident of applicable county with on-site septic system (Charles County)
BAT system must be one of the approved vendors: Fuji Clean, Orenco, Advantex RT, or SeptiTech, certified by NSF or EPA standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Steps vary by county. Generally: (1) download and complete the county-specific application form (an application checklist is available for Priority Funded Areas and non-Priority Funded Areas in Charles County); (2) submit the completed form with proof of income to the relevant county department (Ground Water Management office in Baltimore County; Environmental Engineering in Prince George's County via the Momentum portal at momentumhome.princegeorgescountymd.gov; Charles County Health Department or Planning and Growth Management; Talbot County Sanitary District Officer); (3) allow access for an initial site inspection to verify septic system condition and site characteristics; (4) if approved, sign required agreements to maintain the BAT system with a qualified operator and allow periodic county inspections; (5) for Perry Hall Manor (Baltimore County): obtain bids from at least three qualified contractors and submit the low bid with application; (6) upon final approval, funds are provided to cover system installation and two years of professional maintenance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fund Financial Hardship Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: A financial hardship exemption program that allows eligible residents to request relief from the Chesapeake Bay Restoration Fund fees (flush tax) mandated by the State of Maryland. Available in multiple Maryland counties, the program provides property tax and fee exemptions to individuals experiencing financial hardship who are subject to Bay Restoration Fund requirements. A new application must be completed every year to maintain exemption eligibility.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of the Environment / County Governments
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible individuals experiencing financial hardship may apply for a full exemption from the Chesapeake Bay Restoration Fund fees (flush tax) and/or related property tax obligations. The exemption provides complete relief from mandatory Bay Restoration Fund fees for qualifying residents. Applicants must demonstrate financial hardship and reapply annually to maintain exemption eligibility. Each county administers the program locally with its own application requirements and procedures.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted year-round; must reapply annually
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 301-777-5965 (Allegany County); Calvert County Treasurer's Office for Calvert County
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland county residents (including Allegany and Calvert County) experiencing financial hardship who are subject to the Chesapeake Bay Restoration Fund fees or related property tax obligations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The exemption provides relief from mandatory Bay Restoration Fund fees and/or related property tax obligations tied to bay restoration requirements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Allegany County and Calvert County, Maryland. Program is administered locally by each county government with separate application processes and eligibility determinations.
requirements_list: Must be experiencing financial hardship
Must demonstrate inability to pay Bay Restoration Fund fees or related property tax obligations
Must apply annually to maintain exemption eligibility
Must be subject to Chesapeake Bay Restoration Fund fees or related property tax obligations
Residency in Allegany County or Calvert County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete the Bay Restoration Fund Financial Hardship Exemption Application form annually. In Allegany County, submit the completed application to the Tax & Utility Office (phone: 301-777-5965). In Calvert County, submit the Bay Restoration Hardship Exemption Application to the Calvert County Treasurer's Office. Applications must be resubmitted each year, and new applications must be completed to be considered for the exemption. Each county may have specific submission deadlines and procedures.

structured_extraction.program_name: Donald "Doc" Lumpkins Memorial Scholarship Program (MDEMA Annual Student Scholarship)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Emergency Management Association (MDEMA) offers annual scholarships to financially assist students pursuing an associate or baccalaureate degree in emergency management or a closely related field. Five $1,500 scholarships are awarded annually, with one scholarship distributed to students in each of five geographic regions of Maryland (Western Maryland, National Capital, Central Maryland, Eastern Shore, and Southern Maryland). The program aims to develop future emergency management professionals by supporting their educational pursuits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Five $1,500 scholarships are awarded annually, with one scholarship distributed to each of five geographic regions in Maryland: Area I (Western Maryland: Allegany, Garrett, Washington); Area II (National Capital: Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's); Area III (Central Maryland: Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Carroll, Harford, Howard); Area IV (Eastern Shore: Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester); Area V (Southern Maryland: Calvert, Charles, St. Mary's).
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school seniors attending accredited Maryland high schools who have been accepted to a two- or four-year college or university and plan to major in emergency management or a closely related field, as well as students currently accepted or enrolled in a two- or four-year college or university pursuing a degree in emergency management or a closely related field.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To further education through pursuit of an associate or baccalaureate degree in emergency management or a closely related career field, covering educational expenses associated with those programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students across all Maryland counties through five geographic association areas: Area I (Western Maryland: Allegany, Garrett, Washington); Area II (National Capital: Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's); Area III (Central Maryland: Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Carroll, Harford, Howard); Area IV (Eastern Shore: Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester); Area V (Southern Maryland: Calvert, Charles, St. Mary's).
requirements_list: Applicant must be either a high school senior attending an accredited Maryland high school who has been accepted to a two- or four-year college or university and plans to major in emergency management or a closely related field, or a student currently accepted or enrolled in a two- or four-year college or university pursuing a degree in emergency management or a closely related field.
Student must be studying emergency management or a related career field.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the MDEMA website at https://www.marylandema.org/scholarship.php. Additional information and the application form are available on that site.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program providing financial assistance to low- and moderate-income households for residential solar system installation in Maryland, including leasing and financing options. Also provides broader incentives for residential solar energy systems to Maryland residents at all income levels.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $7,500 per system for qualifying low- to moderate-income households. For example, a family of four with an annual income up to $195,375 may qualify. Leasing and financing options are available for all income levels. Additional tax credit and rebate incentives may also be available for residential solar energy systems.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income households in Maryland seeking to install residential solar systems, as well as all Maryland residents interested in residential solar energy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation and implementation of residential solar energy systems, including leasing and financing options.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Household income must meet low- to moderate-income thresholds for grant funding
Example income limit: up to $195,375 annually for a family of four
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit https://energy.maryland.gov/residential/Pages/incentives/Maryland-Solar-Access-Program.aspx for program details and application information.

structured_extraction.program_name: African American Heritage Preservation Program Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants offered by the Maryland Historical Trust that preserve and enhance places important to the African American experience. The program supports non-profit organizations, government entities, and other eligible applicants focused on projects that preserve and promote African American heritage across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants supporting African American heritage preservation. Specific amounts and terms are outlined in program guidelines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, government entities, and other eligible applicants focused on African American heritage preservation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preservation and enhancement of places important to the African American experience, including projects that preserve and promote African American heritage.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review program guidelines to confirm project eligibility before applying.

structured_extraction.program_name: Certified Local Government Grant Funding (Historic Preservation Non-Capital Grant Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) administers multiple grant programs supporting historic preservation activities statewide. The Certified Local Government (CLG) Grant Program provides annual funding to local governments that participate in the CLG program to strengthen preservation programs, document historic resources, and promote education and outreach. Grants support commissioner and staff training as well as non-capital preservation projects such as surveys, planning documents, design guidelines, and public education. The Maryland Heritage Areas Program designates and supports heritage areas throughout Maryland that promote place-based experiences for visitors and residents, highlighting historic, cultural, and natural resources to strengthen local economies; heritage area management entities receive annual grants for management, marketing, and mini-grants to local organizations. Additional non-capital grants are available for research, survey, planning, and educational activities related to historic preservation for eligible non-profits and government entities statewide. Multiple grant programs are available with different eligibility standards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CLG Training and Education Grants provide non-competitive funding for annual commissioner and staff training, with specific amounts and payment schedules outlined in grant guidelines each year. CLG Project Grants are competitive with maximum awards up to $25,000 for non-capital preservation projects. No match requirement, though a 15% match is encouraged for project grants. Heritage area management entities receive annual grants for management activities, marketing, and mini-grants to local organizations within their designated heritage areas. Additional non-capital research, survey, planning, and educational grants are available with varying amounts specified in program guidelines. All funding comes from 10 percent of the Maryland Historical Trust's federal Historic Preservation Fund allocation from the National Park Service. Projects must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Historic Preservation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Typically due end of February; rolling deadline depends on program year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified Local Government participants (local government staff and historic preservation commission members), heritage area management entities and local organizations within certified heritage areas, non-profit organizations, and other eligible entities pursuing historic preservation projects and activities statewide.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commissioner and staff training, historic property surveys, National Register of Historic Places nominations, design guidelines for historic districts, training for local preservation commission members, preservation plans or planning studies, public education and outreach about preservation topics, heritage area management and marketing, mini-grants to local organizations supporting heritage area operations, property acquisition and rehabilitation, documentation and survey, heritage tourism development, architectural and archaeological standards-compliant investigations, and professional qualifications-based projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. CLG grants are only available to the 24 Certified Local Government (CLG) jurisdictions in Maryland, including 13 CLG cities (Annapolis, Baltimore, Bel Air, Cambridge, Chestertown, Cumberland, Frederick, Gaithersburg, Hagerstown, Havre de Grace, Rockville, Salisbury, Sykesville) and 11 CLG counties (Baltimore, Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Harford, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico). The state's heritage area boundaries touch all 23 counties and the city of Baltimore; thirteen heritage areas are currently designated and certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Certified Local Government (CLG) for CLG training and project grants

For CLG certification, must have a preservation ordinance meeting state and federal standards, a qualified historic preservation commission, and a system for identifying and protecting historic properties
CLGs must complete annual training and file annual reports
Projects must be non-capital or training-focused for CLG grant eligibility
Projects must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Historic Preservation and applicable survey/archaeology standards
Professional staff or consultants must meet Secretary of the Interior professional qualifications standards
Applications must be submitted through the MHT grants portal or directly to CLG contacts when application rounds open
Heritage areas must be designated and certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority
Each program has different eligibility standards, operating regulations, and funding amounts specified in annual guidelines
Applicants are strongly encouraged to contact MHT staff early in the planning process for guidance and to discuss draft applications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should review detailed grant guidelines provided when the application round opens, typically in late fall or early winter. Applicants must confirm project eligibility and are strongly encouraged to consult with MHT staff early to discuss draft applications and align local goals with grant priorities. For CLG programs, applications for education and training are sent directly to CLG contacts when the application round opens, while project applications are submitted through the MHT grants portal. For Heritage Areas Program, areas are designated through MHT and must be certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority; each heritage area is managed locally by an organization with its own staff and board that submits annual grant applications. All applications must be completed and submitted through the designated channel before the posted deadline, typically by end of February. MHT staff review applications for compliance with standards and provide feedback. Awards are announced and funding is distributed according to program guidelines. Applications may be accepted on a rolling basis for certain program types.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state income tax credit program that helps property owners preserve historic commercial or income-producing buildings. Qualifying projects receive a state income tax credit equal to 20% of eligible rehabilitation expenses, capped at $5 million, provided the rehabilitation expenses exceed the property's adjusted basis or $25,000.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A state income tax credit equal to 20% of eligible rehabilitation expenses, capped at $5 million per project. Projects in qualified Opportunity Zones may be eligible for additional state tax credits. Property owners may use the state historic tax credit in combination with federal and local historic tax credits. Projects receiving $1 million or more in tax credits must meet corporate diversity requirements unless exempt (sole proprietorships, single-member LLCs, family-owned companies with 75% family shareholders, or businesses with annual budget or sales under $5 million). These exemptions and corporate diversity standards are detailed in the 2026 Corporate Diversity Addendum.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted by August 31 each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, investors, and nonprofit organizations seeking to rehabilitate historic commercial or income-producing buildings in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation expenses for historic properties, including repairs and changes that bring a property to functional use while protecting important historical, architectural, or cultural features. All work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Projects in qualified Opportunity Zones may be eligible for additional state tax credits. Some properties in Maryland heritage areas may also be eligible.
requirements_list: Property must be a certified historic structure (individually listed in the National Register of Historic Places, a contributing resource in a National Register Historic District, or locally designated and determined by MHT to be eligible for the National Register)
Property must be primarily income-producing or rehabilitated for commercial use, which can include use by nonprofits
Rehabilitation expenses must exceed the adjusted basis of the structure or $25,000
All work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
Work must not begin until Part 2 approval is received from MHT

Projects receiving $1 million or more in tax credits must meet corporate diversity requirements unless exempt (sole proprietorships, single-member LLCs, family-owned companies with 75% family shareholders, or businesses with annual budget or sales under $5 million)
Applicants must own the property or have permission from the property owner

Federal Part 2 approval by the National Park Service prior to the state application deadline waives the requirement to wait for MHT's Part 2 approval, but work started prior to MHT approval will not be eligible for the state tax credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process has three parts: Part 1 - Applicants submit a description of the property and its historic significance for evaluation by MHT. Part 2 - Applicants submit a description of the proposed rehabilitation work for approval by MHT. Part 3 - After project completion, applicants submit documentation of the completed project for final certification. Successful competitive commercial applicants receive an award letter outlining additional fees that must be paid prior to Part 2 approval. Applicants are encouraged to contact MHT early in the planning process for consultation before beginning applications. Applications must be submitted by August 31 each year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Historic Preservation Tax Incentives Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax incentive program that provides tax credits to owners of income-producing historic buildings who undertake substantial rehabilitation projects. The program applies to certified historic structures determined by the National Park Service to be listed in the National Register of Historic Places or eligible state and local historic districts. The Maryland Historical Trust serves as the state historic preservation office and assists Maryland applicants through the certification and application process, conducting site visits and making certification recommendations to the National Park Service.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal income tax credits for the rehabilitation of certified historic, income-producing structures. The rehabilitation project must be substantial, defined as expenditures of at least $5,000 or an amount equal to the adjusted basis of the building, whichever is greater. The project typically must be completed within a 24-month period. The tax credit is applied to federal income taxes for qualifying rehabilitation projects on historic properties listed in the National Register of Historic Places or eligible state and local historic districts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of income-producing historic buildings listed in the National Register of Historic Places, eligible state and local historic districts, or otherwise certified by the National Park Service as historic structures, who wish to undertake substantial rehabilitation projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation expenditures for certified historic, income-producing buildings and structures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be listed in the National Register of Historic Places, eligible for state and local historic listing, or determined by the National Park Service to be certified historic structures. Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Building must be income-producing
Building must be listed in the National Register of Historic Places or eligible for state and local historic listing, or determined by the National Park Service to be a certified historic structure
Rehabilitation project must be substantial (minimum $5,000 or amount equal to adjusted basis of building, whichever is greater)
Rehabilitation project must meet Secretary of Interior Standards for Historic Preservation
Project typically must be completed within 24 months
Application must be submitted to National Park Service with Maryland Historical Trust certification recommendation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the application form from the National Park Service website, complete it with project details, and submit it along with necessary documentation to the Tax Credit Program contact. The Maryland Historical Trust will advise on the rehabilitation project, conduct site visits, and make certification recommendations to the National Park Service. For additional details, visit the National Park Service Tax Incentives Homepage at https://www.nps.gov/tps/tax-incentives.htm.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that promote the acquisition, restoration, and rehabilitation of historic properties.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, restoration, and rehabilitation of historic properties.
