list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquiring, rehabilitating, or refinancing historic properties.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Heritage Areas Program Emergency Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Emergency grants provide funding outside the regular grant cycle for sudden or emergency needs caused by unexpected events. Funding supports heritage-related projects when sudden or emergency needs arise from unexpected events.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Emergency grants provide funding for heritage-related projects when sudden or emergency needs arise from unexpected events. Applicants must demonstrate that the need was not known during the last grant cycle and explain why the project cannot wait until the next regular round or demonstrate why something new has happened since the last round making the activity urgent. Projects must support the program's goal of creating or improving heritage-related places or experiences that the public can visit and enjoy.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, local governments, and state or federal agencies with eligible projects in heritage areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects related to preserving heritage and creating or improving heritage-related places or experiences that the public can visit and enjoy. Funds support heritage preservation, interpretation, visitor experience improvements, and community engagement activities within certified heritage areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within one or more certified Maryland heritage areas. The program is available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Show that the need was not known during the last grant cycle
Explain why the project cannot wait until the next round or show that something new has happened since the last round making the activity urgent
Support the program's goal of creating or improving heritage-related places or experiences that the public can visit and enjoy
Must discuss project with the executive director of the heritage area where the project will take place before applying
Nonprofit organizations must be in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Project must be located within a certified Maryland heritage area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Before applying, discuss your project with the executive director of the heritage area where the project will take place. Demonstrate that the need is urgent and could not have been anticipated during the last grant cycle. Submit application materials according to Emergency Grant Policy requirements. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis as emergencies arise.

structured_extraction.program_description: Loans provided to nonprofits, local governments, businesses, and individuals to support projects that create or improve place-based heritage resources within a heritage area.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans can cover up to 50% of the total project cost based on the applicant's financial need. The exact amount available depends on funding. Refinancing is not eligible as part of the project cost. Loan terms and interest rates are determined based on project feasibility and applicant creditworthiness.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofits, local governments, businesses, and individuals with projects in Maryland heritage areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of property or rights to use property (easements); development including repair, alteration, or new construction for heritage tourism; rehabilitation to make property usable again; restoration to return property to appearance at a specific time in history; leasehold improvements; purchasing equipment, furnishings, or inventory
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Within Maryland's designated heritage areas
requirements_list: Project must create or improve place-based heritage resources within a heritage area
Loan can cover up to 50% of total project cost
Refinancing is not eligible as part of the project cost
Leasehold improvements must have a lease term lasting at least as long as the loan term
Applicant must demonstrate financial need and project feasibility
Project must align with heritage area goals and preservation priorities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prospective applicants should contact the Maryland Heritage Areas Program staff to discuss project eligibility and obtain application materials. Submit a completed application form with project documentation, financial information, and heritage resource impact assessment. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. The program staff will evaluate projects based on alignment with heritage area mission, financial need, project viability, and available funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: Mini-grants for heritage-related projects that do not involve capital construction. These grants support educational programming, planning efforts, and similar activities under $5,000 in Maryland's 13 heritage areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each of Maryland's 13 heritage areas may offer mini-grants for heritage-related non-capital projects under $5,000. The specific amount available depends on the individual heritage area.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations, agencies, and other local partners within Maryland's heritage areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Heritage-related non-capital projects such as educational programming or planning efforts
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Within Maryland's 13 heritage areas. Visit individual heritage area websites for specific information.
requirements_list: Project must be heritage-related
Project must be non-capital (not involving capital construction)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the individual heritage area to apply. More information available through the Maryland Heritage Areas Program staff.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Heritage Areas Program Project Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that support heritage-related projects to enhance place-based experiences.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Heritage-related projects that enhance place-based experiences.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Heritage Preservation Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state income tax credit program that provides financial incentives to property owners who rehabilitate certified historic or heritage structures. The program is administered by the Maryland Historical Trust and encourages preservation of historic buildings by reimbursing 20% of qualified capital costs spent on rehabilitation of certified heritage structures. Eligible properties include those listed on the National Register of Historic Places or designated as local historic properties, and rehabilitation must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation. The program covers both residential and commercial properties, and credits may be combined with county tax credits.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a Maryland income tax credit equal to 20% of qualified capital costs expended in the rehabilitation of a certified heritage structure. Eligible costs include plumbing, HVAC, electrical system upgrades, kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation, architectural and engineering fees, and restoration of historic landscape features. The minimum project cost threshold is $5,000 for owner-occupied residential projects or the greater of the adjusted basis of the structure or $5,000 for all other projects. Rehabilitation must occur within a 24-month period, though projects can be phased into smaller units. These credits may be combined with county tax credits. Applicants must apply before any renovations are started.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners of certified historic or heritage structures — including owners of properties on the National Register of Historic Places or designated as local historic properties — who are planning to rehabilitate residential (primary or secondary) or commercial properties in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified capital costs and rehabilitation expenditures for certified historic or heritage structures, including structural repairs, plumbing, HVAC, and electrical system upgrades, kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation, architectural and engineering fees, and restoration of historic landscape features.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Properties must be listed on the National Register of Historic Places or designated as local historic properties, including historic districts in Salisbury (Newtown Historic District, Camden Historic District, and Downtown Historic District). The Maryland Historical Trust maintains lists of National Register properties; local planning offices maintain lists of locally designated historic properties.
requirements_list: Property must be a certified historic or heritage structure listed on the National Register of Historic Places or designated as a local historic property
Rehabilitation work must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
Application must be submitted before any renovations are started
Costs must be qualified capital costs for rehabilitation
Minimum project cost of $5,000 for owner-occupied residential projects, or the greater of the adjusted basis of the structure or $5,000 for all other projects
Rehabilitation must be completed within a 24-month period (projects may be phased into smaller units)
Work must not negatively impact historic elements of the interior or exterior (for certain improvements like plumbing, HVAC, electrical)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Historical Trust to determine if your property is eligible. Applicants must submit an application to the Maryland Historical Trust before any renovations begin. If pursuing both federal and state tax credits, complete the federal form in full and complete only the first sheet of each part of the state form. The Maryland Historical Trust will review project plans against the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation. Before and after rehabilitation photographs must be provided for verification. Projects can be phased into smaller units, with each phase requiring a separate application. For more information, call 410-514-7644 or 410-514-7625, or visit https://mht.maryland.gov/Pages/funding/tax-credits.aspx.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program (Heritage Areas)
structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credits of up to 20% of eligible rehabilitation costs for historic properties within heritage areas. Credits are available for properties listed on the National Register of Historic Places, historic buildings eligible for listing, and non-historic buildings certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority as contributing to the heritage area.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit of up to 20% of eligible rehabilitation costs. These credits are in addition to other state tax credits available for qualified rehabilitation work on historic structures.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers working on historic rehabilitation projects within heritage areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation work on eligible historic properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Within Maryland's heritage areas
requirements_list: Property must be individually listed on the National Register of Historic Places, or considered contributing to a historic district listed in the National Register
OR property must be a historic building eligible for listing on the National Register of Historic Places
OR property must be a non-historic building certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority as contributing to the importance of the heritage area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program page for full details and application process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program - Homeowner Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A state income tax credit program that encourages investment in historic neighborhoods and helps homeowners preserve their historic homes. Qualifying homeowners can receive a tax credit equal to 20% of eligible rehabilitation expenses, capped at $50,000 in a 24-month period, with a minimum of $5,000 in eligible rehabilitation expenses required.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A state income tax credit equal to 20% of eligible rehabilitation expenses, capped at $50,000 in a 24-month period. Minimum eligible rehabilitation expenses of $5,000 are required to qualify. The tax credit is calculated on Maryland state income taxes owed by the homeowner.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted year-round on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Historical Trust Tax Credits Program
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners who own and occupy a certified historic single-family residence as their primary or secondary home, either individually or through a cooperative.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible rehabilitation expenses for historic properties including roof repair or replacement, chimney repair and relining, structural repairs, window and door restoration, masonry repair or repointing, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing work, interior finish restoration, professional design or architectural fees, tool or equipment rental, and repair of historic outbuildings. Ineligible expenses include landscaping, new construction, appliances, decorative items, and tool purchases.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Some properties in heritage areas or curatorship properties may be eligible; applicants should contact staff for specific questions.
requirements_list: Applicants must own and occupy the property as their primary or secondary residence, either individually or through a cooperative
Property must be a single-family, owner-occupied residence

Property must be a certified historic structure (individually listed in the National Register of Historic Places, a contributing resource in a National Register Historic District, or locally designated and determined by MHT to be eligible for the National Register)
Minimum of $5,000 in eligible rehabilitation expenses required
All work must be approved by MHT for consistency with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation before the project begins
Any work begun prior to MHT review and approval will not qualify for the tax credit
If a project changes or new work is added, an Amendment form must be submitted and approved by MHT before starting the new work
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications have three parts: Part 1 describes the property and its historic significance for evaluation by MHT; Part 2 describes the proposed rehabilitation work for approval; Part 3 documents the completed project for final certification. Applicants should contact MHT early in the planning process, particularly for large or complex projects. Once a complete application is received, review typically takes 30-45 days but may vary depending on submission clarity and project complexity. If a project changes, an Amendment form must be submitted and approved before starting the new work. Applications are submitted to Maryland Historical Trust and reviewed for compliance with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Museum Assistance Program (MAP) offers grants to support Maryland museums and institutional collections. The program helps historical and cultural museums strengthen operations, build professional capacity, and improve long-term sustainability by funding everyday operational activities. It is administered by the Maryland Historical Trust and supports museums interpreting Maryland's cultural heritage, history, natural history, or history of science and technology.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $20,000 are available, with typical awards between $10,000 - $15,000. No match is required. In FY26, $285,000 total funding is available statewide. Grants support eligible everyday museum operations including staff salaries, training, administrative costs, environmental monitoring, and security and safety systems. Capital projects such as construction, restoration, or building repairs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofits and local governments that operate museums, particularly those interpreting Maryland's cultural heritage, history, natural history, or history of science and technology.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grants can be used for paying staff, training staff or volunteers, office or administrative costs such as insurance and accounting, environmental monitoring such as pest management or humidity control, and security and safety systems. Capital projects such as construction, restoration, or building repairs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Applicant museums must interpret Maryland's cultural heritage, history, natural history, or history of science and technology.
requirements_list: Museum must have been open and operating for at least three years
Nonprofit applicants must be in good standing with the state and be tax-exempt or have applied for tax-exempt status
Local government applicants must operate a museum that has been open and operating for at least three years
Museums operated in whole or in part by the state or federal government are not eligible
If an applicant operates more than one museum, each museum seeking funding needs a separate application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the grant guidelines to confirm project and applicant eligibility. Prepare required attachments such as cost estimates, photographs, and proof of ownership or site control. Submit a completed application through the grants portal before the posted deadline in October. Applicants will be notified of funding decisions and grants will be disbursed according to program requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that funds projects to protect historic maritime resources and increase public awareness of the nation's maritime heritage. The program provides funding for education and preservation projects demonstrating clear public benefit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides $380,192 in total funding. Applicants may request between $10,000 and $100,000 per project. Projects must have total costs between $20,000 and $200,000 and require a 1:1 non-federal match.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tribal governments, state governments, local governments, and nonprofit organizations seeking to protect historic maritime resources and educate the public about maritime heritage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Identification of historic maritime resources including archaeological sites; repair, rehabilitation, stabilization, maintenance, or limited reconstruction of historic maritime buildings, structures, vessels, and sites; and improvements that increase public access to maritime resources. All projects must include a public education component.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide and nationwide eligibility for applicants. Projects addressing impacts of flooding, erosion, or changing environmental conditions on maritime resources are prioritized.
requirements_list: Projects must demonstrate clear public benefit
Must follow the Secretary of the Interior's Standards and Guidelines for Archeology and Historic Preservation
Must follow Standards for Historic Vessel Preservation Projects where applicable
All projects must include a public education component

Must support at least one eligible activity: identification of historic maritime resources, repair/rehabilitation/stabilization/maintenance/limited reconstruction of historic maritime buildings/structures/vessels/sites, or improvements increasing public access
Grant funds cannot support work that has already started or been completed
Require 1:1 non-federal match
Applicant must be a tribal government, state government, local government, or nonprofit organization
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review grant guidelines and manual for detailed requirements. Confirm applicant and project eligibility. Prepare a complete application including scope of work, budget, and required documentation. Submit the completed application through the grants portal before the June 1 deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state income tax credit program that helps owners of historic buildings rehabilitate their income-producing properties to strengthen communities and encourage local economic growth. Qualifying projects receive a state income tax credit equal to 20% of eligible rehabilitation expenses, capped at $50,000 in a 24-month period.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A state income tax credit equal to 20% of eligible rehabilitation expenses, capped at $50,000 in a 24-month period. Qualifying projects must have between $5,000 (minimum) and $500,000 (maximum) in eligible rehabilitation expenses. Projects in a qualified Opportunity Zone (1 or 2) may be eligible for additional state tax credits. Property owners may use the state historic tax credit with federal and local historic tax credits if the project meets eligibility requirements for all programs. The tax credit is applied against Maryland state income tax liability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Year-round, rolling, first-come, first-served basis until the program's annual $2 million funding cap is reached
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of income-producing historic buildings, including commercial and mixed-use properties, and owners of properties that will be sold to homeowners after rehabilitation. Projects must be located in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repairs or changes that bring a historic property to functional use while protecting important historical, architectural, or cultural parts of the building, site, and surroundings. Eligible projects include: roof repair or replacement, chimney repair and relining, structural repairs, window and door restoration, new storm doors and windows, masonry repair or repointing, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing work, interior finish restoration (plaster, flooring, trim), professional design, architectural, or engineering fees, tool and equipment rental, and repair of historic outbuildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Some properties located in Maryland heritage areas may be eligible for this program. Properties must be located in Maryland and either individually listed in the National Register of Historic Places, be a contributing resource in a National Register Historic District, or be locally designated and determined eligible for the National Register.
requirements_list: Building must be a certified historic structure (individually listed in the National Register of Historic Places, a contributing resource in a National Register Historic District, or locally designated and determined by Maryland Historical Trust to be eligible for the National Register)
Building must be primarily income-producing, or rehabilitated as part of a development project to be sold to a homeowner, or rehabilitated for a commercial use (which can include use by nonprofits)
Eligible projects must have between $5,000 (minimum) and $500,000 (maximum) in eligible rehabilitation expenses
All work must be approved by Maryland Historical Trust before the project begins
All work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
No work can begin prior to Maryland Historical Trust review and approval or it will not qualify for the tax credit
Property must be in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The tax credit application has three parts. Part 1 describes the property and its historic significance for evaluation by Maryland Historical Trust. Part 2 describes the proposed rehabilitation work for approval. Part 3 documents the completed project for final certification. Applications are submitted year-round on a rolling, first-come, first-served basis. Review of a complete application typically takes 30 to 45 days but timing may vary depending on the clarity of the submission and project complexity. For projects with changes or new work, an Amendment form must be reviewed and approved by Maryland Historical Trust before starting the work for it to be eligible for the credit. Multiple Amendments can be submitted during the 24-month period. Step 1: Submit Part 1 application with property description and historic significance documentation. Step 2: Receive Maryland Historical Trust approval of Part 1 before proceeding. Step 3: Submit Part 2 application describing proposed rehabilitation work. Step 4: Receive approval of Part 2 from Maryland Historical Trust. Step 5: Complete the rehabilitation work in compliance with approved plans. Step 6: Submit Part 3 application with documentation of completed work and expenses. Step 7: Receive final certification and tax credit amount. Applicants should contact the Tax Credit Program for application forms and specific submission instructions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credits for homeowners as well as commercial and small commercial projects undertaking historic preservation work.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, commercial businesses, and small commercial projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Historic preservation and revitalization projects.

structured_extraction.program_name: Income Tax Subtraction Modification Program for Residing Artists
structured_extraction.program_description: Qualified artists who live in Maryland and create or sell artistic work within a designated Maryland Arts and Entertainment District are not taxed on that income at the state level. Artists can claim an income tax subtraction modification on their Maryland state income tax return for income earned from in-district sales, performances, or internet sales originating in the district. The benefit applies only at the state level; federal income tax obligations remain unchanged.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified residing artists claim an income tax subtraction modification on their Maryland state income tax return. The subtraction reduces taxable income by the amount derived from art sales, performances, or internet sales originating in a designated Arts and Entertainment District. Artists must file Maryland State Tax Form 502AE with their state income tax returns to claim the benefit. The form instructions include the state's definition of art-derived income. The tax benefit applies only at the state level; federal income tax obligations remain unchanged.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual artists who live in Maryland and create or sell artistic work within a designated Arts and Entertainment District, including performing artists and those conducting internet sales originating in the district.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Income tax subtraction modification on income derived from the sale or performance of art within a designated Arts and Entertainment District, including internet sales originating in the district.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Artists must live in Maryland and conduct their sales or performances within a designated Maryland Arts and Entertainment District.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified residing artist
Must live in Maryland
Own or rent residential property within Maryland
Must create artistic work in any Arts and Entertainment District
Must sell artistic work or perform in a designated Maryland Arts and Entertainment District
Have generated income from the sale or performance of art within any Arts and Entertainment District
For performing artists, income from performances in the district qualifies
For all artists, internet sales originating in the district qualify
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit Maryland State Tax Form 502AE with your annual state income tax return. The form instructions include the state's definition of art-derived income. Review eligibility requirements on the Maryland State Arts Council website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Admissions and Amusement Tax Exemption Program (Arts & Entertainment District)
structured_extraction.program_description: Enterprises and qualifying resident artists dedicated to visual or performing arts located within a designated Arts and Entertainment District are exempt from collecting the State of Maryland's Admissions and Amusement Tax on gross receipts from admissions or amusement charges. This exemption is available to qualifying for-profit and nonprofit arts and entertainment enterprises as well as individual resident artists operating within designated A&E Districts across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Arts and entertainment enterprises and qualifying resident artists in designated A&E Districts are exempt from the state admissions and amusement tax levied on gross receipts from admissions or amusement charges for performances, exhibits, or other entertainment events. The exemption applies to taxes collected on ticket sales, admission fees, and other amusement charges. Businesses must register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Combined Registration Application to be eligible and to claim the exemption.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualifying for-profit and nonprofit arts and entertainment enterprises and individual resident artists located within designated Arts & Entertainment Districts in Maryland that generate income from admissions or amusement charges.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax exemption from collecting the Maryland State Admissions and Amusement Tax on gross receipts from admissions or amusement charges for performances, exhibits, or other entertainment events.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicable within designated Arts & Entertainment Districts in Maryland, including but not limited to Baltimore County and Salisbury (Wicomico County).
requirements_list: Be an 'arts and entertainment enterprise' (a for-profit or nonprofit entity dedicated to visual or performing arts) or a qualifying resident artist
Be located within a designated Arts & Entertainment District
Charges must be admissions or amusement charges (ticket sales, admission fees, event attendance fees)
Register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Combined Registration Application
Maintain current registration status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To qualify for the exemption, businesses and individual artists must: (1) Register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Combined Registration Application; (2) Verify location within a designated Arts & Entertainment District; (3) Provide documentation of business activities related to visual or performing arts; (4) Maintain registration and compliance with state tax reporting requirements. Contact the Maryland State Comptroller's Office or the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation for application forms and detailed instructions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Homestead Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state and local tax credit program that limits the annual increase in taxable property assessments on a homeowner's principal residence to a fixed percentage, protecting homeowners from large property tax increases due to reassessment. The credit is available statewide to all owner-occupied homeowners regardless of income. The state cap is 10% per year; local governments may adopt a lower cap (e.g., the Town of Kensington in Montgomery County uses a 5% cap). The homeowner pays no property tax on the market value increase above the applicable limit. Homeowners need only apply once; the credit is applied automatically each year thereafter. The program is administered by the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit calculated on any annual assessment increase exceeding 10% (or the lower cap set by local governments, e.g., 5% in the Town of Kensington). The homeowner pays no property tax on the market value increase above the applicable annual limit. The credit amount is calculated by SDAT based on market conditions and applicable caps. The credit applies to the land and dwelling of owner-occupied principal residences. Homeowners apply once and receive the credit every year thereafter with no income requirement. The credit does not apply in the first year following the purchase of a home. The Homestead Property Tax Credit may significantly reduce the amount of property taxes owed by limiting the assessment increase on which eligible homeowners pay county, municipal, and state property taxes each year, regardless of the property's value or income level.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No annual deadline; ongoing program. File application with SDAT by May 1, 2026 to ensure the County Income Tax Offset Credit (ITOC) appears on future tax bills (Montgomery County).
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) Homestead Tax Credit Division
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-767-2165 (toll-free 1-866-650-8783); Baltimore County SDAT: 410-512-4900; Charles County: 301-645-0685 or 301-932-2440; City of Salisbury/SDAT: 410-767-4433
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of principal residential dwellings throughout Maryland, including homeowners in Montgomery County, Baltimore County, Charles County, Queen Anne's County, and all other Maryland jurisdictions, who may be subject to significant increases in property assessments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax relief through limitation of annual taxable assessment increases on a principal residence. The credit reduces property tax liability on annual assessment increases above the applicable cap (10% statewide, or lower local cap).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland program. Every county and municipality in Maryland is required to limit taxable assessment increases to 10% or less per year. Local governments may set a lower cap. Montgomery County municipalities use a 10% cap except the Town of Kensington which uses a 5% cap. Available to all owner-occupied properties regardless of income.
requirements_list: Property must be owner-occupied
Dwelling must be the owner's principal residence

Owner must have lived in the property for at least six months of the year, including July 1 of the year for which the credit is applicable, unless temporarily unable to do so due to illness or need of special care
The property was not transferred to new ownership during the previous tax year
There was no change in zoning classification requested by the homeowner that resulted in increased property value
A substantial change did not occur in the use of the property
The previous assessment was not clearly erroneous
Credit applies only to one property — the principal residence
Not applicable in the first year following the purchase of a home
Must complete and submit the Homestead Tax Credit Eligibility Application (HST) to SDAT
Application reviewed by Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation to determine qualifications
Married couples may only have one principal residence under the provisions of the law
Property address must be the location where homeowner(s) expect to file their federal and Maryland income tax return, if one is filed
Property address should be the location from which homeowner(s) have received a Maryland issued driver's license or identification card, if applicable
Property address should be the location from which homeowner(s) are registered to vote, if registered
No portion of the principal residence may be rented
Homeowner must provide Social Security Number of all homeowner(s) and spouse(s), even if spouse is not listed as an owner on the deed
Information submitted will be verified against income tax, motor vehicle records, Internal Revenue Service records, Maryland Comptroller's Office records, and Motor Vehicle Administration records
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Check if you already have a homestead application on file by visiting the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) Real Property search at https://sdat.dat.maryland.gov/RealProperty/ (search by property address or account number), and review your homestead application status. If you have previously filed and been approved for the Homestead Tax Credit, there is no need to reapply, as the Homestead Credit Eligibility stays in place as long as the dwelling remains your primary residence. Step 2: If no application is on file, obtain your SDAT Real Property Tax Identification Number from your assessment notice or the property search results. The identification number is composed of the two-digit county code where the property is located followed by an account number. Step 3: Apply using one of two methods: (a) Online at https://onestop.md.gov (recommended) by selecting Department of Assessments and Taxation and completing the Homestead Tax Credit Eligibility Application (HST), or (b) Download and mail a paper application available at https://dat.maryland.gov/realproperty/Documents/Homestead_application.pdf to the Department of Assessments and Taxation, Homestead Tax Credit Division, 301 West Preston Street, 8th Floor, Baltimore, MD 21201. Step 4: Complete all required fields in Section I (property identification number and address) and Section II (answer all questions including homeowner names, Social Security numbers of all homeowner(s) and spouse(s), and signatures). Step 5: Montgomery County homeowners should file by May 1, 2026 to ensure the County Income Tax Offset Credit (ITOC) appears on future tax bills. You only need to apply once; renewal is not required each year as long as the property remains your principal residence. For questions or to schedule an in-person service appointment, contact sdat.homestead@maryland.gov or call 410-767-2165 / toll-free 1-866-650-8783.

Community learning centers must offer families of participating students literacy instruction and related educational development programs. The program targets students and families attending schools eligible for Title I schoolwide programs or schools serving a high percentage of students from low-income families.

Grantees are required to attend bi-monthly networking meetings for technical assistance and peer support.

Services must be provided to students and families of students who primarily attend Title I schoolwide eligible schools or schools serving a high percentage of low-income families.

requirements_list: Must be a local education agency, interagency, interdepartmental, community-based organization, faith-based organization, institution of higher education, for-profit corporation, or consortium of two or more of these entities
Must provide services to students and families of students who primarily attend Title I schoolwide eligible schools or schools serving a high percentage of low-income students
Grantees must attend bi-monthly networking meetings for technical assistance and peer-to-peer support

structured_extraction.program_name: Accreditation Support Fund (Maryland and National Accreditation)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to licensed child care centers, registered family child care providers, and public pre-kindergarten programs to help cover the costs associated with obtaining Maryland Accreditation and/or national accreditation. For Maryland Accreditation, the fund covers the cost of instructional and classroom learning materials required during the accreditation process. For national accreditation, the fund covers required application fees including initial application, renewal application, and annual update fees. The program is administered through Maryland EXCELS and supports early childhood, school-age, and family child care programs statewide in improving quality through accreditation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Accreditation Support Fund offers two tracks of financial assistance: (1) Maryland Accreditation Support — reimburses or pays for instructional and classroom learning materials required for Maryland Accreditation. Maximum reimbursement: $2,500 for programs serving 100 or fewer children; $3,000 for programs serving more than 100 children per accreditation cycle. Materials must be non-consumable items specified on the Maryland Accreditation Classroom Learning Materials Checklists (Infant and Toddlers; Preschool and School-Age). Reimbursement cannot exceed the actual cost of materials and cannot exceed the amount charged by the accreditation organization. Purchases must have been made within 12 months before the date of application. (2) National Accreditation Support — reimburses or pays national accreditation application fees (initial, renewal, and annual update) on behalf of eligible child care providers. Funds are paid directly to the accrediting organization on the applicant's behalf. Reimbursement cannot exceed the actual fee charged by the accrediting organization. Funds cannot be used for facility improvements, association membership fees, staff training, costs already covered by other funding sources, or any costs greater than the fee charged by the accreditation organization.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing — no defined deadline. Applications accepted year-round.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers, registered family child care providers, public pre-kindergarten programs, and school-age child care programs participating in Maryland EXCELS and pursuing Maryland Accreditation or national accreditation (e.g., NAFCC, NAEYC, AMS, AMI/USA, AIMS, AWSNA, Cognia, COA/ASA, Lumen, MSA-CESS, NAC, NECPA).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: (1) Maryland Accreditation track: instructional and classroom learning materials specified on the Maryland Accreditation Classroom Learning Materials Checklists (Infant and Toddlers; Preschool and School-Age), including books, manipulatives, blocks, technology equipment, outdoor play equipment, science and sensory materials, music instruments, dramatic play materials, and other non-consumable learning materials. Consumable items (paint, crayons, markers, glue, paper, etc.) are not reimbursable. (2) National Accreditation track: required application fees including initial application fees, renewal application fees, and annual update fees charged by recognized national accrediting organizations. Funds may not be used for facility improvements, association membership fees, staff training, or costs already paid through another funding source.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to eligible licensed child care centers, registered family child care providers, and public pre-kindergarten programs throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care center, registered family child care provider, or public pre-kindergarten/school-age program
For Maryland Accreditation track: applicant must be a licensed child care center or school-age only program (family child care homes are not eligible for this track)
For National Accreditation track: family child care providers, child care centers, and school-age only programs are eligible

Must be pursuing Maryland Accreditation or accreditation from a recognized national accrediting organization (MSDE-recognized organizations include: American Montessori Society (AMS), Association Montessori International/USA (AMI/USA), Association of Independent Maryland Schools (AIMS), Association of Waldorf Schools of North America (AWSNA), Cognia Early Learning Accreditation, Council on Accreditation – After-School Accreditation (COA/ASA), Lumen Accreditation, Maryland Accreditation (MSDE), Middle States Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Elementary and Secondary Schools (MSA-CESS), National Accreditation Commission (NAC), National Association for the Education of Young Children (NAEYC), National Association for Family Child Care (NAFCC), National Early Childhood Program Accreditation (NECPA))
For Maryland Accreditation track: materials must be those specified on the Maryland Accreditation Classroom Learning Materials Checklists and must be non-consumable items
For Maryland Accreditation track: purchases must have been made within 12 months before the date of application
Each child care center with an individual license number may submit a separate application
Applicant must not use funds for costs already paid through another funding source
Requested amount cannot exceed the actual cost/fee charged by the accreditation organization
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Maryland Accreditation Support: (1) Complete the Application for Maryland Accreditation Support through the online form portal at onestop.md.gov; (2) Compile required documentation including receipts/invoices for materials purchased and complete the appropriate Classroom Learning Materials Checklist for your program type (Infant and Toddlers or Preschool and School-Age); (3) Submit application and all documentation through onestop.md.gov; (4) MSDE Accreditation Specialist will review the application, request any missing documentation, and process for payment. Approval typically takes 10-30 days after submission. For National Accreditation Support: (1) Complete the Application for National Accreditation Support through the online form portal at onestop.md.gov; (2) Compile required documentation including: copy of your completed application submitted to the accrediting organization, completed Accreditation Work Plan detailing steps to achieve accreditation, copy of the Accrediting Organization's Fee Page, and copy of current accreditation certificate if currently accredited; (3) Submit application and all documentation through onestop.md.gov; (4) Within 30 days, MSDE Accreditation Manager will review and notify you via email of application status. If approved, payment is processed and paid directly to the accrediting organization on your behalf.

structured_extraction.program_description: A mandatory 90-minute annual training update for all child care staff and family child care providers to meet ongoing professional development requirements. Upon successful completion, participants receive a certificate of participation that qualifies for 1.5 Core of Knowledge hours in health, safety, and nutrition.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 90-minute online training update accessed through the MSDE Canvas learning platform (msde.instructure.com). The training consists of multiple modules including an Introduction to Basic Health and Safety and additional topic modules covering health, safety, and nutrition. Participants must complete the Introduction first, then can access other modules in any order. Upon completion of all topics and the Final Review Activity with a score of 80% or higher, participants receive a Certificate of Completion that qualifies for 1.5 Core of Knowledge hours in health, safety, and nutrition. Must be completed by December 31, 2025. Newly approved family child care providers and staff hired from October to December 2025 must complete by March 31, 2026. Training is recommended for substitutes and volunteers.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Must be completed by December 31, 2025. Newly hired staff from October-December 2025 must complete by March 31, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All child care staff and family child care providers in Maryland. Recommended for substitutes and volunteers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This is a training program. The training covers updated health, safety, and nutrition topics for child care professionals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Currently employed or registered as a child care provider in Maryland
Must complete the 90-minute training by the deadline
Must successfully complete all training modules including Introduction and Final Review Activity with a score of 80% or higher
Must successfully complete all training components to receive certificate of participation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Go to https://msde.instructure.com/login/canvas. 2. Log in with your email address and password. 3. Access the MSDE Canvas Welcome Page and click on the Educator Resources button. 4. Click on Early Childhood Modules button. 5. Click on the Basic Health and Safety Annual Update 2025 button. 6. Select Introduction to Basic Health and Safety first (other modules are locked until completion). 7. Load the Introduction module in a new window. 8. Use the EXIT COURSE button in the upper right corner to return to the main training. The system remembers where you left off if you prefer to complete training one section at a time. 9. Complete all available topic modules in any order. A green check mark appears as each topic is completed. 10. Once all topics are complete, access and complete the Final Review module with a score of 80% or higher. 11. Upon meeting all requirements, the Certificate of Completion module will unlock. Download and save the certificate to your device.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides customized assessments and training to help job seekers with disabilities find and learn to use appropriate technology and equipment to support their employment goals. Staff offers individualized assessments, training on AT hardware and software, and ongoing technical support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DORS RTS staff provides customized assessments for individuals with disabilities to identify appropriate assistive technology. Services include training and technical support on AT hardware and software use, delivered at the Work Training Center (WTC) in Baltimore or in the individual's community. Examples of assistive technology include desktop or portable video magnifiers, note-taking devices, specialized software (voice recognition, screen readers, reading and writing assistance), and mobile devices for organization and time management. Training classes may cover JAWS screen reading software, ZoomText magnification and screen reading software, and specialized classes based on individual needs. Services are available at no cost to eligible DORS consumers.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services available statewide; assessments and training held at the Work Training Center (WTC) campus in Baltimore or in the individual's community.

Must have an employment or school goal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local DORS office to request a customized AT assessment. The DORS RTS team will evaluate individual needs and recommend appropriate technology and training. Services can also be requested via QR code available on program materials.

The program includes classroom instruction, videos, lectures, product demonstrations, and hands-on training in customer service, interior and exterior cleaning techniques, equipment operation, chemical safety, and professional detailing skills.

Training covers customer service skills, interior and exterior cleaning techniques, proper safety and use of equipment such as orbital dual action buffers, power washers and drill brushes, proper safety and use of chemicals and solution mixing, use of clay bar, removing minor defects and scratches, compounding and waxing using multispeed buffer, and quality hands-on work required by high-end detail shops or dealerships.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and skill development in automotive detailing techniques, customer service, equipment operation, chemical safety, and professional detailing skills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is provided at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center campus in Baltimore.

3rd grade or higher reading comprehension level
Basic math skills

Ability to squat, stoop and kneel
Certain criminal backgrounds may disqualify an individual from the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local office for more information or request DORS Services.

Training includes lubrication and changing fluids, changing and balancing tires, testing, charging and starting systems, battery replacement, tune-ups, vehicle inspections, and brake repair. structured_extraction.program_description: A free online training course required by state and federal law for all child care providers, staff, substitutes, and adults responsible for child care and safety in licensed child care programs. The training covers health and safety topics and best practices aligned with Maryland child care regulations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training course consisting of four modules plus a final review and survey. Participants must complete all modules in order and score a minimum of 80% on all topic reviews and the final review to receive a certificate of completion. The course takes approximately three hours to complete. Participants may stop and return to the module they were on without restarting by clicking EXIT COURSE and logging back in. Accounts expire at the end of the 21-day course period. Each registrant is allowed two attempts to pass the final assessment. Participants must print their certificate of completion immediately upon receiving it; MSDE does not maintain copies of certificates. Participants who do not complete the training within the course period must register again and start over in another cohort if they have not completed any course sections.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers, staff, substitutes, and adults responsible for the care and safety of children in licensed child care programs in Maryland. New employees must complete within 90 days of hire.

requirements_list: Must work in or be associated with a licensed child care program
Must have a valid email address to register and use for login; each email address can only register one person
Must have basic computer skills including mouse use, typing, email, video viewing, and internet navigation
Must complete all four training modules in order
Must score a minimum of 80% on all topic reviews and the final review and survey
Must print certificate of completion before course end date
New employees must complete training within 90 days of hire to be in compliance
Cannot register for the course more than once if previous registration resulted in completion of any course sections with a score below 80%; the final grade will stand
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online at https://earlychildhood.marylandpublicschools.org/basic-health-safety-training during the one-week registration period each month (13th through 23rd at 12:00 pm). After registration closes, participants receive an email with login information. Log into the training platform at https://msde.instructure.com/login/canvas using the email address used to register as the username and the password created during registration. Select Introduction to Basic Health and Safety first (other modules are locked until it is completed). Complete all four modules in order, taking notes as needed. Use the EXIT COURSE button when stopping to save progress. Once all modules are complete, the Final Review module becomes available. Print the certificate immediately and keep it in personnel files. Accounts expire at the end of the 21-day course period.

structured_extraction.program_name: Broadening Options and Opportunities for Students Today (BOOST) Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The BOOST Scholarship Program provides scholarship awards to help eligible low-income students attend a participating nonpublic school. Priority is given to students who qualify for the free or reduced-price school meals program (FARMs) and to students who received a BOOST scholarship in the previous year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides scholarship awards to cover tuition at participating nonpublic schools. Award amounts are determined by the BOOST Advisory Board and based on household income (expressed as a percentage of federal poverty levels), academic level of the student, and any financial assistance the school provides. Special education students may receive an additional award amount. The award may be reduced if it exceeds the tuition owed to the school. The scholarship check is sent to the school, and the parent or guardian must endorse the back of the check. For fiscal year 2027, estimated funding is $9,000,000 plus carryover from the previous year, with an estimated 2,500 awards available. Funds must be used for tuition and required fees for enrollment only and cannot be used for transportation or meals.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 9 - May 8, 2026 (parent applications); March 6, 2026 (nonpublic school applications)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Allison Sanborn (Program Manager) / James Clark (Administrative Support)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in kindergarten through 12th grade who qualify for free or reduced-price school meals (FARMs) and are enrolled or accepted at a participating nonpublic school in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and required fees at participating nonpublic schools for kindergarten through 12th grade. Funds cannot be used for transportation or meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Only nonpublic schools registered to operate in Maryland, approved to participate in the Nonpublic Textbook Program, and holding a certificate of approval from or being registered with the State Board of Education are eligible schools. Estimated 175 participating nonpublic schools across Maryland.
requirements_list: Student must qualify for free and reduced-price meals (FARMs) based on 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns
Student must be enrolled or accepted at a participating nonpublic school for the 2026-2027 school year
Student must be entering grades kindergarten through 12th grade for the 2026-2027 school year (Pre-K students are not eligible)
Parents must upload 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns to verify annual income and household size
Household income must meet FARMs income guidelines set by the U.S. Department of Agriculture
Nonpublic school must hold a certificate of approval from or be registered with the State Board of Education
Nonpublic school must be approved to participate in the Nonpublic Textbook Program
Nonpublic school must provide more than only Pre-K and Kindergarten programs (at least first grade)
Nonpublic school must complete an application to the BOOST program by March 6, 2026

Nonpublic school must comply with all reporting requirements including teacher certification data, student withdrawal/expulsion data, assessment results (English Language Arts, Math, and Science), and enrollment confirmation by September 25, 2026

Nonpublic schools must comply with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and not discriminate in student admissions, retention, or expulsion based on race, color, national origin, sexual orientation, or gender identity or expression
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Parents complete the online BOOST Scholarship application through Submittable between March 9 and May 8, 2026. Parents must upload their 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns to verify income and household size. Applications are reviewed for eligibility and completeness on a rolling basis and are not first-come, first-serve. After May 30, 2026, all application data is submitted to the BOOST Advisory Board, which convenes in summer 2026 to determine award amounts and priorities. Eligible students are ranked by priority level: (1st) renewals and their siblings; (2nd) new applicants from public schools qualifying for free meals; (3rd) new applicants from public schools qualifying for reduced meals; (4th) students remaining at nonpublic schools qualifying for free meals; (5th) students remaining at nonpublic schools qualifying for reduced meals. Parents/guardians will receive email notification of awards by August 2026 and must accept or decline by the deadline. Schools must confirm student enrollment and special education status. Scholarship checks are mailed to schools between October and December 2026. No new awards will be offered after December 11, 2026. Nonpublic schools must submit applications by March 6, 2026, and complete all reporting requirements by September 25, 2026. MSDE offers customer service support sessions on March 10 and March 12 (with interpreter), and weekly Wednesdays from March 18 through May 6, 2026 (12-1 pm with certified interpreter).

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF)
structured_extraction.program_description: A tuition assistance and professional development program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that helps child care providers pay for college education at participating Maryland colleges and universities. The fund pays tuition directly to accredited colleges and universities on behalf of participants to earn degrees in early childhood education, child development, elementary education, or special education. Participants must be enrolled in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program at Level Two or higher and maintain employment as a child care provider while participating. After degree completion, recipients are required to fulfill a service commitment working in child care in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides tuition assistance by making payments directly to the college or university on behalf of the participant. Awards cover tuition, college fees, and required textbooks for college coursework toward a degree in an approved field. Funds can only be used for actual college expenses incurred after an award is issued and cannot be used to pay for previously incurred college costs. Funds are distributed directly to the college/university on an annual basis. Participants must maintain employment as a child care provider at least 20 hours per week while participating. After degree completion, recipients must serve a required commitment period in licensed Maryland child care: one month per college credit successfully completed, two years for an associate's degree, four years for a bachelor's degree, or two and a half years for a master's degree. First-time applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis with priority given to applicants who have not yet completed any college courses for credit from an accredited college or university. If a recipient does not complete the employment service requirement or withdraws without good cause, they must repay the State of Maryland the full amount paid on their behalf.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First-time applications due by March 1st each year; Continuation applications due by June 30th each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care center workers and registered family child care providers in Maryland who participate in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program at Level Two or higher, work at least 10 hours per week, have at least one year of documented experience working with groups of children in an approved setting, and are seeking to advance their education and careers in early childhood education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition, fees, and required textbooks for earning a degree in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education at participating Maryland colleges and universities. Payments are made directly to the college or university. Funds can only be used for college coursework expenses incurred after an award is issued and cannot be used for previously incurred college costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide at participating accredited institutions throughout Maryland, including community colleges and universities. Participants must work in a licensed child care center or be a registered family child care provider in Maryland and must maintain employment in Maryland while participating in the program and after degree completion.
requirements_list: Participant must be currently enrolled in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program at Level Two or higher
Work in a licensed child care center or be a registered family child care provider in Maryland
Work at least 10 hours per week
Have at least one year of documented experience working with groups of children in an approved setting
Must pursue degree at an accredited college or university recognized by the U.S. Department of Education and participating in CCCPDF
Degree must be in one of the following fields: Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education
Fulfill entrance requirements at the participating college of choice
Maintain employment in child care in Maryland at least 20 hours per week while participating in the program
Maintain employment in an approved child care facility in Maryland at least 20 hours per week after completion of the degree
Participate in professional development
Maintain at least a 2.50 cumulative GPA from the point of first entering the program
Submit all required documentation before application deadlines
Complete the applicable service commitment period upon degree completion without breaks in employment or face repayment obligation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Apply directly to a participating CCCPDF college or university and obtain acceptance. Step 2: Schedule an appointment with the CCCPDF Coordinator at the participating college to which you have been accepted and review the application checklist and required documentation. Step 3: Complete the CCCPDF application form with all required documentation, including a signed letter from current employer (or current family child care license), documentation of at least one year of child care experience, proof of Maryland Child Care Credential participation at Level Two or higher, letter of acceptance from the college with declared major, and professional development plan with course(s) and timeline to complete degree. Step 4: Coordinator signs the application checklist confirming all required documents are included. Step 5: Submit the completed application and checklist to the Office of Child Care by the application deadline (March 1 for first-time applications, June 30 for continuation or transfer applications). Step 6: MSDE or the college/university will send an approval or denial letter to the applicant. Payments are made directly to the college or university upon approval. Annual continuation requires submission of updated documentation including continued employment letter and current transcript.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Quality Incentive Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that provides funds to licensed child care centers and family child care homes to improve the quality of care and help children prepare for school. Providers can use funds to purchase supplies, materials, and equipment that create stimulating learning environments based on early childhood development training and aligned with Kindergarten Readiness and Early Learning Assessment guidelines. Grants are awarded quarterly and are intended to incentivize quality improvements in child care settings statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded quarterly during each state fiscal year in January, April, July, and October. Funding amounts are based on facility size: up to $1,000 for facilities serving fewer than 10 children, up to $1,500 for facilities serving up to 29 children, and up to $2,500 for facilities serving more than 30 children. Child care providers are eligible for a grant award once every three years. Funds support acquisition of supplies, materials, and equipment to create stimulating learning environments aligned with Kindergarten Readiness and Early Learning Assessment guidelines and to implement knowledge gained through professional training.

Purchases must demonstrate how they implement knowledge gained through professional training. Applicants must itemize all supplies, materials, and equipment and describe how each item will be used to improve or enhance quality of care.

structured_extraction.program_description: A payment system for child care providers through the Maryland Child Care Scholarship Program where the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) pays providers in advance each month based on enrollment rather than retroactively based on actual attendance. Payments are made in two installments per month (on the 1st and 15th of each month for services provided during that month). This program replaced the previous retroactive, attendance-based payment system to provide faster cash flow to child care providers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MSDE pays licensed child care providers advance monthly payments based on enrollment of children with active scholarships. The payment amount is determined by the number of children with active, receipted vouchers assigned to a provider as of the end of the previous month. Monthly payments are divided into two equal installments, processed on the 1st and 15th of each month, with payments typically received by providers on the 6th and 21st of each month via direct deposit. Payment amounts are calculated based on daily rates to account for months with different numbers of calendar days. Payments include coverage for up to 60 days of absence per child per calendar year. True-Up reconciliation occurs monthly (beginning in April 2023 for January services) to adjust for changes in enrollment status, early scholarship endings, mid-month voucher assignments, provider eligibility changes, EXCELS tier payments, registration fees, union dues, and adverse actions. Informal providers are not paid for absences and holidays beyond the 60-day annual allowance. If a child is absent more than 60 days in a calendar year without a medical waiver, an overpayment is established for the excessive absences.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This is an ongoing subsidy program for existing child care scholarship providers. There is no formal application process for advance payments; providers who are already participating in the Maryland Child Care Scholarship Program automatically receive advance payments. Providers submit signed invoices and attendance records biweekly (or as requested) through the Child Care Provider Portal at https://provider.childcareportals.org/. Portal registration requires completion of a User Registration Form with required fields including first name, last name, date of birth, gender, email, phone number, and preferred language. After email verification and password creation, providers can log in to manage their programs. MSDE automatically processes Advance Payments monthly (on the 1st and 15th) based on enrollment data from receipted vouchers assigned as of the end of the previous month. Providers receive an individualized notification email at the start of each month showing enrollment used for calculation, base amount, additional funds from previously receipted vouchers, and any offsets based on scholarship students who left or were unassigned. Providers also receive an Advance Payment Invoice Detail Report in the portal the next business day after each payment is issued. True-Up reconciliation adjustments are processed one month after the advance payment (beginning April 2023 for January services). Payment disputes or disagreements with advance payment or true-up calculations can be submitted through the Provider Inquiry Link on the MSDE website within 90 days of receipt of the payment, and responses are provided within 3 business days. Informal appeals for repayment or Program Integrity Audit disputes can be submitted through the Provider Portal within 90 days, with a final decision issued within 90 calendar days.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care Scholarship (CCS) Program (formerly Child Care Subsidy) helps eligible Maryland families pay for high-quality child care and early education programs. The program provides scholarships (vouchers/subsidies) to families who are working, attending school, or in approved training programs, as well as recipients of Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), Supplemental Security Income (SSI), or TANF. Scholarships cover a state-assigned portion of child care costs, with families paying a co-payment; families receiving TCA or SSI have a $0 co-payment. Scholarships can be used at Maryland licensed child care centers, registered family child care homes, or with informal in-home providers (relatives or non-relatives). The program also fosters quality child care and promotes coordination among early childhood development and afterschool programs. As of May 1, 2025, the program temporarily stopped issuing scholarships to new families (enrollment freeze); however, applications continue to be accepted and approved families are placed on a waitlist. Currently enrolled families continue to receive benefits provided they meet eligibility requirements and complete recertification on time. Families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI are exempt from the freeze and can receive scholarships immediately upon approval.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible families receive payment scholarships from the state to cover part of their child care costs. The scholarship shows the state-assigned rate (the portion of child care costs the state pays) and the family co-payment (the amount the family pays). Families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), Supplemental Security Income (SSI), or TANF have a $0 co-payment. The assigned co-payment ranges from $0 to $3 per week and varies by the Unit of Care authorized on the scholarship (3-Unit scholarships have maximum $3.00/week, 2-Unit scholarships have maximum $2.00/week, 1-Unit scholarships have maximum $1.00/week). Three types of scholarships are available: (1) a temporary 60-day Fast Track scholarship for regulated child care, issued within three business days of application; (2) a full 52-week formal scholarship for regulated child care; and (3) an informal scholarship for relative care or non-relative care in the child's home. Families take the scholarship to a participating child care provider; once the child begins care, the provider submits an invoice and is reimbursed by the state for the scholarship portion. Advance payments are processed by the 1st and 15th of each month; providers receiving direct deposit can anticipate payment from the Maryland State Comptroller's Office within 7 days of payment processing completion. If a child care scholarship does not cover the full tuition, parents are responsible for paying the remaining amount. As of May 1, 2025, the program is in an enrollment freeze—new families are placed on a waitlist unless exempt (TANF, TCA, SSI recipients or existing enrolled families adding children).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program temporarily stopped issuing scholarships to new families starting May 1, 2025; applications are still accepted and placed on a waitlist. No hard application deadline for ongoing program. Fast-Track applications are processed within 3 business days. Full applications are determined within 30 calendar days from submission or 5 business days of receipt of all required documentation. Redetermination applications must be submitted 45 days before the end of current eligibility period; submit at least 15 days before end date to avoid payment interruption.
