structured_extraction.program_description: The ILOB program helps individuals who are 55 or older and are blind or have a vision impairment to live independently in their homes and communities. ILOB teaches independent living skills such as safe cooking techniques and management of personal care and household tasks, supporting older adults with vision loss in maintaining or improving their independence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: ILOB provides in-home training and assessment in independent living skills including: training in managing personal care and household tasks; labeling and organizing personal care items, clothing, appliances and medications; safe cooking techniques; orientation and mobility training; Braille instruction; use of assistive technology; referral to community peer support groups and other services; and introduction to community resources such as NFB-NEWSLINE and resources at the Maryland State Library for the Blind and Print Disabled. ILOB rehabilitation specialists come to your home to provide personalized assessment and training. The program serves individuals in all areas of the state, including rural counties, with specialists working as a team with ophthalmologists, low vision professionals, and community partners.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with vision loss (blind or visually impaired) age 55 and over seeking to maintain or improve independence in their homes and communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in independent living skills including management of personal care and household tasks, safe cooking, orientation and mobility training, Braille instruction, assistive technology use, and connection to community resources and peer support groups to support independent living at home and in the community
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide through DORS offices throughout Maryland. OBVS Regional Offices: Baltimore (410-261-2954) serving Baltimore City and Baltimore, Cecil, Howard, and Harford Counties; Wheaton (301-949-3750) serving Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Montgomery, and Washington Counties; Annapolis (410-974-7604) serving Anne Arundel, Calvert, Caroline, Charles, Dorchester, Kent, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico and Worcester Counties. The program reaches out to individuals in all areas of the state, including those living in rural counties.
requirements_list: Must have vision loss (be blind or have a vision impairment)
Must be age 55 or older
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office for Blindness & Vision Services or your local DORS regional office to inquire about ILOB services. ILOB rehabilitation specialists will come to your home to provide assessment and training.

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Support Services Program Grant (IECMHSS)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Support Services (IECMHSS) program improves the ability of staff, programs, and families to prevent, identify, treat, and reduce the impact of social, emotional, and other mental health problems among children from birth through 5 years old. Using a hybrid consultation model that is both child/family and classroom/program focused, the program allows consultants to address specific child behaviors while simultaneously working with teachers to improve overall classroom quality. It builds the capacity of early care and education providers and family members to promote healthy social-emotional development, and builds partnerships with local community resources including Judy Centers, Head Start Centers, health departments, and other early childhood support services. The program also administers state grant funding to support non-profit and public agencies providing these mental health services across Maryland. Originally piloted in Baltimore City and the Eastern Shore in 2002, the program expanded to statewide coverage across 12 child care licensing regions by 2006.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grant funding to eligible non-profit and public agencies, as well as direct consultation services, training, coaching, and mentoring to child care providers and teachers to help prevent and identify mental health problems in children. Consultants work directly with programs, staff, and families to improve classroom environments and child outcomes. The program also refers children and families in need of more intensive mental health services to appropriate support and clinical programs. Specific grant amounts are not stated on the program page. Three customer service support sessions were offered in June and July 2023 to explain program requirements and the proposal process.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Proposals are due no later than 5:00 p.m. on Wednesday, August 9, 2023.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and public agencies licensed to do business in Maryland that provide infant and early childhood mental health services, as well as child care staff, teachers, programs, families, and children birth through 5 years old in child care settings across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting positive mental and behavioral health practices for young children through referrals and services. Consultation, training, coaching, and mentoring services to address social, emotional, and mental health challenges in early childhood settings. Funds support specialist consultants who work with classrooms and individual children, and build the capacity of early care and education providers and family members to promote healthy social-emotional development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program operates statewide across 12 child care licensing regions in Maryland. Applicants must be licensed to do business within the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Serve children birth through 5 years old
Be a child care program, classroom, or related early childhood setting
Non-profit or public agency status
Licensed to do business within Maryland
Proven capacity to provide Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Services
Must operate 12 months per year except for federal holidays
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a written proposal using the provided application form by the deadline. Three customer service support sessions were offered in June and July 2023 to explain program requirements and the proposal process. Applicants should contact the program through the Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Grant Opportunity link for grant application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program for individuals who provide informal child care services. Informal providers may apply for initial approval or renewal of their informal provider status to participate in the child care subsidy program. The program includes health and safety inspections and adherence to Informal Inspection Standards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Informal child care providers can apply for initial approval or renewal of their status to participate in the Child Care Scholarship Program. There is no direct financial assistance provided by this program to the providers themselves; rather, it enables providers to serve families who receive child care subsidies. The program includes comprehensive health and safety inspections, compliance with Informal Inspection Standards (governed by COMAR 13A.14.06.11.F.12(b)), and ongoing monitoring visits. Providers must maintain current health and safety certifications at all times. Initial approval can take up to 60 days provided all background clearances have been received. Providers will not receive back payment for care provided prior to MSDE approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who provide informal child care services in Maryland, including relatives and non-relatives who care for children in their own homes or the child's home
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable - this is a certification/approval program, not a financial assistance program. Providers must comply with health and safety standards and maintain required certifications and documentation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Criminal background check via fingerprinting at CJIS-supported facility for provider and any individual 18+ residing in or with regular presence at the care location
Notarized Release of Information form for Child Protective Services review (child abuse and neglect records) for provider and any individual 18+ residing in or with regular presence at care location
Health & Safety Standards and Child Care Provider Agreement Form signed by provider and parent
Emergency Preparedness Plan (EPP) and Emergency Preparedness Kit (Ready-to-Go Pack) with completion of Emergency Preparedness Form
Emergency Care & Medication Authorization (ECMA) Form signed by provider, parent, and child's healthcare provider (one per child)
Proof of Residency (Maryland driver's license, mortgage contract, lease, or utility bill)
Social Security Number (SSN) card or Individual Taxpayer Identification (ITIN) documentation for payment eligibility
Valid photo ID (driver's license or government-issued)
Current MDH Immunization Certificate (MDH 896) or acceptable alternative for children not attending public school or licensed/registered child care program
Current MDH Blood-Lead Testing Certificate (MDH 4620) or acceptable alternative for children under 6 years old not attending public school or licensed/registered child care program
Proof of Relatedness documents if applying as Relative Informal Care Provider (birth certificate, marriage license, passport, adoption papers, or other proof)
Basic Health & Safety Training Certificate (3 hours, must pass with 80% or higher score)
Basic Health & Safety Training Annual Update Certificate (1.5 hours)

Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and First Aid Certification from American Heart Association or equivalent, including in-person skills training, appropriate for all child age groups (Adult, Child and Baby First Aid/CPR/AED)
Injury/Incident Report (Reportable Incident Report Form) if incident occurs during care hours
Care Location Inspection (initial inspection must be passed; onsite or virtual; unannounced monitoring visits may occur at any time)
All health and safety certifications must be current at time of application and remain current for continued approval
Renewal fingerprinting required every 5 years if there has been no break in active approval status
If break in approval status exceeds 90 days, must submit Initial Informal Provider Application with new fingerprinting for all individuals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Review definitions to determine eligibility as Relative or Non-Relative Informal Care Provider. Step 2: Submit application by uploading all required forms and supporting documentation to the Provider Portal at https://provider.childcareportals.org. Use the checklist provided to ensure all items are complete, signed, and dated. To obtain actual application paperwork (not just sample forms), applicants must contact CCS Central 2 at 877-227-0125 or email CCS.InformalProviders@maryland.gov. Step 3: If all items are accepted and all background clearances are received, a Care Location Inspection will be scheduled (onsite or virtual). Provider must sign, date, and upload the inspection form. Step 4: Informal provider will be approved for payment if all requirements are met and the parent is eligible for the Child Care Scholarship Program. Application processing can take up to 60 days for eligibility determination if all background clearances have been received. Providers will not receive back payment for services prior to MSDE approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Judy Center Early Learning Hub Expansion Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that provides funding for the expansion of Judy Center Early Learning Hubs across Maryland. Judy Centers are comprehensive early childhood education facilities that serve young children from prenatal stages through age 5 and their families. The program enables communities to access early childhood services and family support by establishing or expanding Judy Center locations statewide. The Fiscal Year 2026 expansion grant application is currently available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding available for Fiscal Year 2026 to support the expansion of Judy Center Early Learning Hubs. Grants are provided to eligible organizations to establish or expand Judy Center locations and services across Maryland. Specific award amounts and terms are to be confirmed with the program manager.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kaymi Plank, Judy Center Program Manager; Nancy Garcia, Judy Center Specialist (Spanish language assistance)
structured_extraction.program_audience: School systems, government entities, and organizations seeking to establish or expand Judy Center Early Learning Hubs in Maryland, serving children from prenatal stages through age 5 and their families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expansion of Judy Center Early Learning Hub programs, locations, and services, including establishment of new Judy Center sites and enhancement of existing early childhood and family support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Judy Center Expansion Grant Application for Fiscal Year 2026 is now available. Interested applicants should contact Judy Center Program Manager Kaymi Plank at kaymi.plank@maryland.gov or 410-767-0675 for application details, requirements, and submission information. Spanish language assistance is available through Nancy Garcia at nancy.garcia1@maryland.gov or 410-767-0785.

structured_extraction.program_name: Judy Center Early Learning Hubs (Judith P. Hoyer Early Learning Hubs)
structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive early learning hubs located in elementary schools across Maryland that serve families with children from prenatal stages through age 5, with a focus on Title I school communities. Using a multigenerational approach, Judy Centers provide families with learning experiences, developmental support, and connections to community services to prepare children for school success and life. The program empowers families as their children's most important teachers by offering a central location for early childhood education programs and comprehensive support services for children from birth through kindergarten and their families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Judy Centers are grant-funded programs providing comprehensive family support and early care and education services to children aged birth to five years old and their families within a school's catchment area. Services include: full-day/full-year services (not less than seven hours or more than 12 hours per day, year-round operations); meals for children and families during school day, breaks, weekends, and after-school hours; case management (confidential, comprehensive process connecting families to services and resources); integration of early education services across prekindergarten, kindergarten, Early Head Start, Head Start, and child care programs; family engagement using a multigenerational approach; early identification and intervention for all children birth through five years; services for children with disabilities (fully included in all services as part of IEP and IFSP); health-related services including developmental screenings, referrals for dental, vision, and hearing screenings, mental health assessments, and health insurance access; professional learning for partner staff; adult education and career services connecting adult family members to colleges, universities, and workforce development programs; support for accreditation of early care and education programs; and community partnerships with Early Head Start, Head Start, child care providers, family literacy programs, workforce development, and other family support services.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kaymi Plank, Judy Center Program Manager; Nancy Garcia, Judy Center Specialist (Spanish assistance)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children from prenatal stages through age 5 (birth through kindergarten) who live within the school zone where a Judy Center is located, particularly in Title I school districts across Maryland. Program uses a multigenerational approach serving families from historically underserved communities in Title I and high-needs schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for comprehensive child development and family support services including full-day/full-year early care and education, developmental screenings, family learning and engagement activities, parenting classes and training workshops, connections to adult education and workforce development, evidence-based family and child playgroups, service referrals, early intervention identification, evidence-based home visiting, case management, service coordination with community partners, health-related services (dental, vision, hearing, mental health referrals), meals, and professional learning opportunities for partners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Judy Centers are located in elementary schools across the state of Maryland in all 24 jurisdictions, primarily in Title I school districts. As of FY2024, there are 86 Judy Center sites across Maryland. Eligible families must live within the school zone where the Judy Center is located. The program is expanding by nine sites annually until 2025, then 18 sites annually from 2026-2030 as part of the Blueprint for Maryland's Future.
requirements_list: Children must live within the school zone where the Judy Center is located
Children must be prenatal through age 5 (birth through kindergarten)
Children who live in this zone will attend Pre-K and Kindergarten at the school where the Judy Center is located
Residence in a Title I school district

Families and children are considered served by the Judy Center if they engaged with the Judy Center at least 12 times during the fiscal year or were enrolled in formal partner programs such as Kindergarten, Prekindergarten, Early Head Start, Head Start, Patty Centers, family child care providers, or child care centers
Children with disabilities and their families are fully included in all services as part of the Individualized Education Program (IEP) and Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families interested in Judy Center services should contact their local Judy Center directly. Contact information and locations for each Judy Center can be found at marylandfamiliesengage.org/judy-center-hubs-map/ or by visiting marylandjudycenters.org. A map of Judy Center hub locations showing all 86 sites across Maryland's 24 jurisdictions is available at https://marylandfamiliesengage.org/judy-center-hubs-map/. Each Judy Center has a coordinator and steering committee that meets at least six times annually to coordinate services and partnerships. Enrollment is ongoing with rolling admissions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants supporting library partnerships as part of PDG B-5 grant activities to build local capacity in early childhood services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants supporting library partnerships for early childhood capacity building.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Libraries and early childhood organizations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Library partnership activities to support early childhood services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide

structured_extraction.program_name: Licensing Compliance Grant for Family Child Care Providers (LCGFCCP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that helps registered family child care providers offset the costs of opening their child care programs and achieving or maintaining compliance with family child care regulations. Eligible providers who meet income requirements can receive reimbursement of up to $1,000 in eligible expenses incurred in pursuit of regulatory compliance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $1,000 to reimburse eligible expenses incurred to achieve or maintain compliance with family child care regulations. Reimbursement is provided as a grant award to registered providers who meet income eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family child care providers in Maryland whose annual income does not exceed 60% of Maryland's current State Median Income (SMI) for their family size.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible expenses include safety supplies, provider medical examination fees, criminal background check fees, small household repairs in approved child care areas, approved child care training course fees, expenses related to local water, sewer, fire, and health requirements, program materials and equipment, and other costs necessary for completion of the registration process or for meeting the requirements of the family child care regulations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a registered family child care provider
Annual income must not exceed 60% of Maryland's current State Median Income (SMI) for the applicant's family size
Expenses must be incurred to achieve or maintain compliance with family child care regulations
Must meet income eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are processed in accordance with regulations set forth at COMAR 13A.14.07, which specifies eligibility requirements, application procedures, and the method by which awards are made. More information about the application process is available on the program webpage.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Early Childhood Advisory Council System Improvement Grant FY26
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that supports local early childhood advisory councils in establishing school readiness benchmarks, conducting needs assessments, developing action plans to increase program participation, coordinating early childhood initiatives, and reporting progress to the state. Funding supports council operations including benchmarking school readiness, assessing local early childhood program quality and availability, coordinating early childhood reforms, and reporting outcomes to state leadership.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support local early childhood advisory councils in their core functions including benchmarking school readiness, assessing local early childhood program quality and availability, developing action plans to increase participation in programs, coordinating early childhood initiatives, and reporting to state leadership. Funding supports council operations and activities such as establishing annual benchmarks of school readiness skills for children entering kindergarten, conducting periodic local needs assessments, identifying collaboration and coordination opportunities, developing action plans for increasing program participation and outreach to underrepresented populations, developing professional development and career advancement recommendations for early childhood educators, aligning local family engagement practices, and coordinating Race to the Top Early Learning Challenge projects and other early childhood initiatives locally.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Early Childhood Advisory Councils in Maryland counties. Each jurisdiction has an established Local ECAC with designated chairs, co-chairs, and council coordinators.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting council operations to establish school readiness benchmarks, conduct needs assessments of early childhood programs, develop action plans for program participation and quality improvement, coordinate early childhood reforms, report outcomes to state leadership, support professional development initiatives, align family engagement practices, and coordinate early childhood initiatives at the local level.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties with local early childhood advisory councils. Active councils exist in Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester counties. Note: Baltimore County council was disbanded as of 2/24/25.
requirements_list: Local Early Childhood Advisory Council must be officially established in the jurisdiction
Formal Memorandum of Agreement must be written and submitted to MSDE Division of Early Childhood Development for approval
Council must meet at least four times per calendar year
Council must maintain minutes and attendance rosters of all meetings
Council must provide quarterly submission of attendance rosters and meeting minutes to state
Council must submit annual report on local council action plans and progress on core responsibilities
Council must have designated leadership including chair and coordinator
Members must maintain at least 50% attendance rate during any consecutive 12-month period to remain active
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local Early Childhood Advisory Councils submit applications through the MSDE Grants website. Councils must develop and submit a formal Memorandum of Agreement to the Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Childhood Development for approval. Upon approval, MSDE provides funding as specified. Councils are required to submit quarterly attendance rosters and meeting minutes, and an annual report documenting action plans and progress on established benchmarks, needs assessments, collaboration opportunities, professional development recommendations, family engagement alignment, and coordination of early childhood initiatives.

structured_extraction.program_description: A certification program for licensed child care centers and public pre-kindergarten programs to demonstrate their commitment to providing high-quality early learning. Programs work through a 24-month process using Maryland Accreditation Standards, self-appraisal, program improvement planning, and validation visits to earn accreditation status valid for five years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Programs receive optional support through remote virtual technical assistance sessions for Program Administration and Home and Community Partnerships, and onsite technical assistance visits for Program Operation. Programs also access the Maryland Accreditation Online System for guidance and support throughout the 24-month accreditation process. Virtual TA is a phone call between a validator and program representative to discuss questions about Section 1 (Program Administration) and Section 3 (Home and Community Partnerships) indicators. Onsite TA includes validator observation of indoor and outdoor environments for all indicators in Section 2 (Program Operation) with feedback provided within three business days. Each program may accept or decline Virtual TA and Onsite TA one time during the accreditation cycle. Programs may also apply for Maryland Accreditation Support Funds to assist with the accreditation process.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing - applications accepted at any time; programs must complete orientation within 12 months of starting
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and public pre-kindergarten programs in Maryland. Family child care programs are not currently eligible. Head Start programs are also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The accreditation process supports programs in meeting Maryland Accreditation Standards across program administration, operation, and community partnerships. Support funds can be used for purchasing instructional materials and supporting the accreditation process. Programs work to address indicators rated as Partially Met or Not Met during initial self-appraisal.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to programs statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Program must be a licensed child care center, public pre-kindergarten program, or Head Start program
Family child care programs are not eligible
Program must complete self-paced Maryland Accreditation Orientation
Program must complete Initial Self-Appraisal within 12 months of finishing orientation; submit comments and required documentation for each indicator
Program must develop a Program Improvement Plan for indicators rated as Partially Met or Not Met
Program may request Virtual Technical Assistance for Section 1 and Section 3 questions
Program may request Onsite Technical Assistance for Section 2 (Program Operation) observation and feedback
Program must complete Final Self-Appraisal with comments and required documentation
Program must request Validation Visit at least 90 days before accreditation cycle expires
Program must participate in Validation Visit at least 30 days before expiration
Within 3 days of binder reopening, program must upload comments, required evidence and pictures in response to validator's ratings
If awarded accreditation, program must submit Annual Updates for years 1-3 of the 5-year accreditation cycle, submitted up to 60 days before Annual Update due date
Years 4-5: Program must begin re-accreditation process 24 months before expiration by completing the orientation again

Staff must meet qualification requirements: Early Childhood Educators must have Associate's degree or higher in Early Childhood Education/Child Development or related field and Maryland Child Care Credential Level 5 (for centers/Head Start) or State Teaching Certificate (for public schools)
Assistant Teachers must have high school diploma and Maryland Child Care Credential Level 2 or higher (for centers/Head Start) or high school diploma/CDA/Associate degree (for public schools)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Apply to participate in Maryland Accreditation. Step 2: Complete the self-paced Maryland Accreditation Orientation. Step 3: Within 12 months of finishing orientation, select 'Begin Accreditation' in the Maryland Accreditation Online System. Step 4: Form a Self-Appraisal Team and complete the Initial Self-Appraisal, submitting comments and required documentation for each indicator. Step 5: Apply for Maryland Accreditation Support Funds. Step 6: Develop a Program Improvement Plan for indicators rated as Partially Met (P) or Not Met (N). Step 7: Request or decline Virtual Technical Assistance for Program Administration and Home and Community Partnerships questions. Step 8: Request or decline Onsite Technical Assistance for Program Operation observation and feedback. Step 9: Complete the Final Self-Appraisal with comments and required documentation. Step 10: Request a Validation Visit at least 90 days before the accreditation cycle expires. Step 11: Participate in the Validation Visit at least 30 days before expiration. Step 12: Within 3 days of binder reopening, upload comments, required evidence and pictures in response to validator's ratings. Step 13: Receive Accreditation Decision from MSDE. Once awarded: During the first 3 years of the 5-year accreditation status, submit Annual Updates up to 60 days before the Annual Update due date (determined by accreditation expiration date). Years 4-5: Focus on re-accreditation; begin the re-accreditation process 24 months before expiration by completing the orientation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Low-interest loans that help Maryland residents with disabilities and their families purchase assistive technology equipment, devices, adapted and non-adapted vehicles to live, work, and learn more independently and support employment goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans available from $500 to $60,000. Applicants first have their application reviewed by MDOD staff. If complete, the application is submitted to a lender for approval on its own merit. If approved by the lender, applicants receive a preferred/discounted interest rate through the ATLP process. If the lender declines the application, the ATLP Board of Directors reviews the application for consideration of a loan guarantee. Approval time is 30-45 days. If the ATLP Board declines a loan guarantee, applicants have the right to appeal the decision in writing with additional documentation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents with disabilities and their families
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of assistive technology equipment, devices, adapted and non-adapted vehicles to support living, working, and learning independently and employment goals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Applicant or family member must have a disability
Must be a Maryland resident
Must intend to use the loan to purchase assistive technology for a Maryland resident with a disability
Must qualify for the loan or meet board approval criteria
Must have a good likelihood of repaying the loan
Must provide photo ID (passport, driver's license, or state-issued ID) with application
Must create and register a OneStop account to submit application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Create a OneStop account and log in to the online application. 2. Complete the MDOD Assistive Technology Loan Program application form and upload photo ID (passport, driver's license, or state-issued ID). 3. Submit the application to ATLP staff for review. 4. MDOD staff reviews the application for completeness and requests corrections if needed. 5. Once complete, the application is submitted to a lender for review. 6. If approved by the lender, the applicant receives a preferred/discounted interest rate and can close the loan at a convenient branch office or by mail. 7. If declined by the lender, the ATLP Board of Directors reviews the application for loan guarantee consideration and notifies the applicant by phone and in writing. 8. If the ATLP Board declines the loan guarantee, the applicant may appeal in writing with additional documentation to the ATLP address or email. Typical completion time is 20-60 minutes; approval time is 30-45 days.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind (BEP)
structured_extraction.program_description: BEP prepares individuals whose primary disability is vision loss to operate successful retail concession and food service operations in public facilities. The program is authorized by the Federally mandated Randolph-Sheppard Act and provides training, licensing, and oversight to manage vending facilities on Federal, Military, DOD and State property and at business partner locations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: BEP provides a three-phase training program to prepare individuals with vision loss to become licensed business managers. The program consists of: (1) an eight-week New Manager Training course conducted by BEP staff at DORS' Workforce & Technology Center in Northeast Baltimore; (2) formal food service training with certified instructors and chefs where prospective managers learn all aspects of food service operations and become certified by the National Restaurant Association in food service sanitation; and (3) on-the-job training consisting of three to six months of extended internship at various BEP facilities under an experienced manager. BEP-licensed operators manage approximately 50 long-term successful businesses in Maryland State, county, and federal agencies. Additionally, many BEP managers use adaptive technologies including laptop computers with adaptive software, digital talking cash registers, talking bill identifiers, scales, thermometers, and Braille note takers to perform daily job duties.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals whose primary disability is vision loss and who wish to operate retail concession and food service operations in public facilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and support for establishing and operating retail concession and food service businesses in Federal, Military, DOD, State, county, and partner facility locations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Federal, Military, DOD, and State facilities, as well as business partner locations throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Primary disability must be vision loss (legally blind)
Must be a U.S. Citizen
Must have at minimum a high school diploma or GED equivalent
Must have an aptitude for business management
Must have practical skills and meet legal criteria for operating a business supported by federal law
Must be referred by a DORS OBVS counselor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, individuals can either ask their existing DORS counselor about BEP participation, or get started by requesting DORS services. Go to dors.maryland.gov and select 'Request DORS Services'. The form can be completed by the job seeker, a family member, medical provider, social worker, or other representative. You will be contacted to set up an intake meeting where a DORS counselor will gather and provide information regarding your eligibility for DORS services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary professional recognition and development program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that recognizes and rewards individual child care providers who exceed state licensing and registration requirements for training, education, and experience in child care and early learning. Participants advance through seven staff credential levels or four administrator levels by completing approved training, gaining work experience, and participating in professional activities. The program improves the quality and stability of the child care workforce and provides a structure for provider growth and career advancement. Incentives include achievement bonuses, training vouchers and reimbursements, and tuition assistance through the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants earn achievement bonuses upon achieving a credential level. Staff bonuses are paid one-time at Levels 2, 3, and 4 and range from $200-$1,000, and paid annually at Levels 4 Plus, 5, and 6. Administrator bonuses are paid one-time only at Level 1 ($600) and annually at Levels 2, 3, and 4, ranging from $750-$1,500. Participants with Credential Level 2 or higher are eligible for up to $400 per year in training vouchers and reimbursements as funds are available. Training Vouchers are issued before training and submitted by the provider to the trainer as payment. Training Reimbursement is paid to the provider after successful completion of training. Eligible expenses include Core of Knowledge training (minimum 2 clock hours), pre-service training, registration at statewide and national child care conferences, and approved college coursework. All participants are also eligible to receive tuition assistance for enrolling in approved college or university programs through the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Training vouchers must be submitted at least 60 days before the conference or training. Training reimbursements must be submitted within 180 days of training completion. New applications coming soon. Applicants will receive a notification of approval or denial via email within 30 days of application submission.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family child care providers and operators, directors, teachers, assistants, or aides in licensed child care centers or Letter of Compliance programs in Maryland. Providers must hold a Level 2 or higher Maryland Child Care Credential (or have held a Level 2 or higher credential that expired between July 1, 2024 and August 30, 2025) to be eligible for training vouchers and reimbursements. Not eligible if sanctioned by the Office of Child Care, if a substitute or volunteer, or if a center employee who does not work directly with children on a daily basis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development through approved Core of Knowledge training in six key areas (Child Development, Curriculum, Health/Safety/Nutrition, Special Needs, Professionalism, and Community), pre-service training (45-hour Child Growth and Development, 45-hour Methods and Materials, 45-hour Directors/Administrator Course), registration at statewide and national child care conferences, and approved college coursework related to child development, early childhood methods, special education, program administration, infant and toddler care, school-age care, health and safety, and language and literacy. Also supports career advancement through credential-level achievement bonuses and tuition assistance for Associate's, Bachelor's, or Master's degrees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland, available to all eligible Maryland child care providers in licensed child care centers, Letter of Compliance programs, and registered family child care homes.
requirements_list: Must be a registered family child care provider or an operator, director, teacher, assistant, or aide in a licensed child care center or Letter of Compliance program in Maryland
Cannot have been sanctioned by the Office of Child Care
Cannot be a substitute or volunteer
Cannot be a center employee who does not work directly with children on a daily basis (e.g., regional/district manager, administrative, maintenance, food service, transportation staff)
Must complete approved training appropriate for the credential level sought, including Core of Knowledge training in six key topics
Must gain work experience in a registered or licensed child care program for a specified number of years according to credential level
Must participate in professional activities related to child care through Professional Activity Units (PAUs)
Must continue working in a child care setting for at least one year after acceptance
Must renew credentials annually if continuing to work in a registered or licensed child care program and completing continued training and professional activities

Must hold a Maryland Child Care Credential at Level 2 or higher (or have held a Level 2 or higher credential that expired between July 1, 2024 and August 30, 2025) to be eligible for training vouchers and reimbursements
For training vouchers: must submit application at least 60 days before conference or pre-service training
For training reimbursements: training must have taken place less than 181 days before application date
Training must be approved by MSDE according to COMAR 13A.14.09
Must provide documentation of successful completion including transcript, grade slip, or certificate of successful completion
Reimbursement can only be issued to the individual credentialed child care provider, not to a center or organization
Must provide receipt showing amount paid for training when requesting reimbursement
National conference documentation must include written workshop titles on back of certificate with trainer signatures and conference booklet descriptions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register for an individual account on the Maryland OneStop platform at tinyurl.com/md-credential. 2. Map out a professional development plan, choosing from training options including Core of Knowledge training, Child Development Associate training, or a college degree. 3. Complete the application form with required documentation and submit via Maryland OneStop (faxed, scanned, or mailed applications will not be processed). 4. For training vouchers: submit application at least 60 days before training or conference. 5. For reimbursement: submit within 180 days of training completion. 6. Approved applicants will receive an approval/denial notification via email within 30 days of application submission. 7. If approved, log into Maryland OneStop, navigate to My Dashboard, click into the application submission, scroll to the bottom and locate the 'MSDE Approved Training Voucher' section to download the PDF voucher. 8. Sign and forward the voucher to the Trainer/Training Organization to complete training registration. 9. After training completion, log back into Maryland OneStop, click My Dashboard, select the application, scroll to the 'Verification of Training Completion' section, click 'Choose File' to upload your certificate of completion, and press Submit. 10. The Office of Child Care-Workforce Advancement Branch will verify training completion. Applications for renewals will open soon.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland EXCELS is a Quality Rating and Improvement System (QRIS) that awards child care and early education programs quality ratings from 1 to 5 stars based on meeting standards in areas like developmentally-appropriate practice, professional development, and family engagement. Participating providers receive guidance from a regional Quality Assurance Specialist, training, and incentives to improve their practices. The goal is to increase the number of high-quality early childhood and school-age care options in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating providers receive a road map, training, and incentives to improve their practices. Support includes guidance from a regional Quality Assurance Specialist and opportunities to learn from other providers. Providers publish and improve their Quality Rating by uploading evidence of meeting Maryland EXCELS Standards into an online system, which is then reviewed by staff. Providers receive ratings for each standard area and an overall rating. Regional Quality Assurance Specialists provide assistance with increasing quality ratings and share information about available training, work groups, and resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care and early education program providers, including early childhood and school-age care programs, who want to improve the quality of services they provide to families and children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participating providers use support to improve quality standards in developmentally-appropriate practice, professional development, and family engagement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Meet Maryland EXCELS Standards in specified areas
Upload evidence of meeting Standards into the online system
Work with a regional Quality Assurance Specialist
Must operate an early childhood or school-age child care program
Must be committed to providing high-quality care and education that exceeds basic licensing requirements
Providers using Child Care Scholarships are required to use a Maryland EXCELS participating program or provider
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers sign up through the Maryland EXCELS website to create an account and get started. A Quality Assurance Specialist supports them in creating and uploading evidence of meeting Standards into an online system. Evidence is reviewed by Maryland EXCELS staff, and providers receive ratings for each Standard area and an overall rating. For assistance with increasing quality ratings and to learn more about available training, work groups, and resources, providers should contact their regional Quality Assurance Specialist.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education distributes financial bonuses to child care programs participating in Maryland EXCELS, a quality rating system for child care providers. Programs receive bonuses based on their quality rating level and program type.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bonuses are distributed to eligible child care programs based on quality rating and program type. Bonus amounts range from $1,000 to $13,500 and vary by program type and capacity: Child Care Centers with capacity 1-50 receive $1,000-$4,500; capacity 51-100 receive $1,000-$9,000; capacity 100+ receive $1,000-$13,500. Family Child Care homes receive $1,000-$4,300, and Large Family Homes receive $1,000-$4,500. Bonuses are paid by check or direct deposit and are typically processed within 60 days of the quality rating publication date. Programs receive bonuses each time they publish a first-time quality rating or re-publish a quality rating of 4 or 5 between July 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care centers, family child care homes, and large family child care homes participating in Maryland EXCELS
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bonuses may be spent at the discretion of the program with no restrictions specified. Programs have used bonuses for purchasing high-quality learning materials, supporting salary increases, hiring additional qualified staff, purchasing new furniture and equipment, and improving the overall quality of care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; available to all eligible Maryland EXCELS participating programs
requirements_list: Program must be participating in Maryland EXCELS
Program must be in compliance with all Maryland EXCELS regulations
Program must participate in scheduled Continuous Quality Improvement visits
Program must publish a first-time quality rating or re-publish a quality rating of 4 or 5 between July 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application or forms are required. Eligible programs automatically receive bonus payments by check or direct deposit once they meet the eligibility criteria. Payments are typically processed within 60 days of the quality rating publication date. Program operators can check payment status on the General Accounting Division (GAD) website. Contact a Quality Assurance Specialist for assistance with increasing your quality rating and to learn more about available training, work groups, and resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: A mentoring pilot program that provides training and support for mentors working with children. Participants complete a mandatory self-paced Introduction to Mentoring training and receive 2 Clock of Knowledge (COK) hours upon successful completion.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A self-paced online Introduction to Mentoring training course. Participants who successfully complete the training receive 2 Clock of Knowledge (COK) hours.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Mentors and individuals interested in mentoring children through the Maryland EXCELS program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and professional development in mentoring practices.
requirements_list: Must complete the self-paced Introduction to Mentoring training
Must be interested in working with children as a mentor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enroll in and complete the self-paced Introduction to Mentoring training course available on the website at https://marylandexcels.org/wp-content/uploads/articulate_uploads/Introduction-to-Mentoring/index.html. Upon successful completion, you will receive 2 COK hours.

structured_extraction.program_description: A quality-based reimbursement program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that rewards child care providers for delivering high-quality services to families using the Child Care Scholarship program. Providers at Maryland EXCELS Quality Ratings 3, 4, and 5 receive increased reimbursement amounts ranging from 10% to 44% above standard reimbursement based on the child's age group (under 2 years or 2 years and over), type of care provided (family child care home or child care center), and the program's quality rating level. Payments are shown separately as 'EXCELS' payments on the Invoice Detail Report for each child served.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Providers participating in the Child Care Scholarship program and maintaining a Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating of 3, 4, or 5 receive increased reimbursement payments. For family child care homes, increases range from 10% to 29%; for child care centers, increases range from 10% to 44%. The specific percentage depends on the rating level (3, 4, or 5), the age group of children served (under 2 years or 2 years and over), and the type of care provided. Payments are shown separately as 'EXCELS' payments on the Invoice Detail Report for each child.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers and family child care homes participating in the Maryland EXCELS quality rating system and the Child Care Scholarship program who have achieved a Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating of Level 3, 4, or 5.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Increased reimbursement payments for providing high-quality child care services to scholarship-eligible families. Funds support operating costs of quality child care programs serving children in the Child Care Scholarship program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for all licensed programs participating in Maryland EXCELS.
requirements_list: Program must be licensed and participating in Maryland EXCELS
Currently participate in the Child Care Scholarship program
Program must achieve and maintain a Maryland EXCELS quality rating of at least Level 3
Provide documentation of rating level for accurate payment calculation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers participating in Maryland EXCELS and serving families with Child Care Scholarship automatically receive the tiered reimbursement payments based on their quality rating level. No separate application is required; increased payments are applied based on the child's age group and provider type. Payments are shown on the Invoice Detail Report as 'EXCELS' payments for each child.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Hearing Aid and Language & Communication Video Loan Bank
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide resource that provides hearing aids and educational materials to families of children who are deaf or hard of hearing. Families without insurance coverage or those experiencing delays in acquiring hearing aids can borrow hearing aids for up to one year at no cost. The program also offers videos and resources to help families learn communication methods such as American Sign Language, Cued Speech, and spoken language development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Families may borrow hearing aids for up to one year at no cost. The program also provides access to DVDs and other educational materials about language and communication options. All resources are provided free to eligible families.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Zella Shabasson, Au.D. or Dr. Paige Bradford
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families of Maryland children who are deaf or hard of hearing, from birth to age 21 who have not yet graduated from high school.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hearing aids for trial or temporary use while families acquire or replace their own aids, and educational materials about communication methods and language development options.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents only. Statewide program.
requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident
Have a child diagnosed by an audiologist or other medical professional as Deaf or Hard-of-Hearing from birth to age 21 who has not yet graduated from high school

For hearing aids: do not have insurance coverage for hearing aids, are experiencing delays or difficulties acquiring or replacing hearing aids, and/or need a hearing aid trial before purchasing personal aids or receiving a cochlear implant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families can request materials and hearing aids through the program's online portal using the provided links for Hearing Aids, Language and Communication Videos, or Other Resources for Families of Children who are Deaf or Hard-of-Hearing. Families may contact the Division of Special Education audiologist or section chief for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Infants & Toddlers Program (MITP) Consolidated Local Implementation Grant (CLIG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant mechanism through which local jurisdictions receive federal and state funds to implement local early intervention programs for infants and toddlers with disabilities, in compliance with federal and state regulations, policies, and procedures. The program provides financial assistance to local governments to create and operate systems of early intervention services for infants and toddlers with disabilities across all Maryland jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Consolidated Local Implementation Grant (CLIG) provides federal and state funds (including formula and project grants) to local jurisdictions designated as Local Lead Agencies (LLA) of Local Infants & Toddlers Programs (LITP). Each LLA aggregates information from LITP partner agencies to complete grant applications and required submissions throughout the grant period to implement early intervention services. Submissions include grant applications, amendment requests, semi-annual program reports, annual program reports, annual LICC reports, interim and final cumulative variance reports, Forms 400 and 500, and invoices. Technical assistance and regulatory guidance are also provided. All submissions must be uploaded to the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website (MMSFTW) at https://msde.sftp.md.gov/ with proper file naming conventions and accompanied by email notification to the assigned fiscal grants liaison.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing with specific submission deadlines for budget amendments and reporting throughout the fiscal year; applications submitted annually
structured_extraction.contact_name: Daniele Redivo, Management Associate; Glenn Graymen, Lead Fiscal Grants Liaison; Nancy Vorobey, Fiscal Liaison; Brian Morrison
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Lead Agencies (LLA) of Local Infants & Toddlers Programs (LITP), local governments, and non-profit organizations that implement early intervention services for infants and toddlers with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to implement local early intervention programs in compliance with federal and state regulations, policies, and procedures, including the creation and operation of local systems of early intervention services for infants and toddlers with disabilities. Specific uses are detailed in the CLIG Grant Information Guide.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland local jurisdictions with designated Local Lead Agencies for Local Infants & Toddlers Programs.
requirements_list: Must be a designated Local Lead Agency (LLA) of a Local Infants & Toddlers Program (LITP)
Must aggregate information from LITP partner agencies to complete grant application
Must comply with federal and state regulations, policies, and procedures
Must submit all required forms and documentation
Must use current forms downloaded just before completion
Must upload all submissions to the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website (MMSFTW) at https://msde.sftp.md.gov/
Must follow submission requirements and file naming conventions
Each GSC (Grants Submission Coordinator/program director/project manager) must be assigned an Entity Code and log-on credentials
Separate access must be provided for each individual user with no shared accounts
Program director/project manager must ensure only authorized individuals have MMSFTW access
GSC must immediately notify the designated fiscal grants liaison to deactivate access for employees who leave employment
Each submission must be uploaded separately and labeled according to file naming specifications
Grant applications must be named: FileCode_EntityID_SFY_GrantNameCode_APP.pdf
Amendment requests and reports must be named: FileCode_EntityID_SFY_GrantNameCode_Grant#_TypeCode.pdf
Email notification must be sent to the fiscal grants liaison upon uploading submissions specifying document names
Screen shot of time-stamped upload should be saved as proof of submission
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local Lead Agencies must complete the CLIG grant application using the SFY 2026 CLIG Application form, SFY 2026 CLIG Budget Submissions Workbook, and other required documents including the CLIG Grant Information Guide, Linking Funds to Program Improvement Chart, Recipient Assurances, Federal Certifications, and State Systemic Improvement Plan Template. The designated Grants Submission Coordinator (GSC) or program director/project manager logs into the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website (MMSFTW) at https://msde.sftp.md.gov/ using Entity Code and credentials. All submissions must be uploaded to the program's designated 'ToMSDE' folder following specified file naming conventions. Documents are received by MSDE in the 'FromMSDE' folder. Upon uploading, the file name will display with a time-stamp; grantees should save a screenshot as proof of submission. An email notification must be sent to the assigned fiscal grants liaison specifying the name(s) of uploaded document(s) to ensure timely processing. The MMSFTW is intended for file transfer only, not file storage; files posted by MSDE are subject to deletion 30 days after posting, so documents should be immediately downloaded and saved. Budget amendments and final reports must be submitted on established timelines throughout the grant period. Applications are submitted annually.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Meals for Achievement provides state funds to supplement federal meal reimbursements, ensuring that all children in participating schools have access to nutritious breakfast at the start of each school day. Meals are consumed in the classroom. The program increases students' access to and participation in breakfast and has been credited with improving students' test scores, behavior, attendance, and overall well-being. Currently, 581 schools across Maryland participate in the program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides state funds to supplement federal meal reimbursements to participating schools, ensuring all children have access to nutritious breakfast consumed in the classroom. Currently, 581 schools participate in the program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: K-12 students, particularly children in participating schools that serve economically disadvantaged students throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free, nutritious breakfast served in the classroom to increase student access to and participation in breakfast meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland. Currently 581 schools participate in Maryland Meals for Achievement.
requirements_list: School must meet the economically disadvantaged criteria to qualify
Meals must be consumed in the classroom
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools meeting economically disadvantaged criteria apply through the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs. Currently, 581 schools participate in the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services Waiver for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (Autism Waiver)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicaid waiver program that provides community-based, long-term, person-centered therapeutic services and support to eligible children and youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder to enable them to live in their homes and communities as an alternative to institutional care. The program coordinates services for children ages 1 through the end of the school semester when the child turns 21, providing respite care, environmental accessibility adaptations, family training and consultation, supported adult life planning, intensive individual support services, therapeutic integration, residential habilitation, and service coordination. Families can join the Autism Waiver Registry to access available slots on a first-come, first-served basis. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland State Department of Education, with local administration in Montgomery County provided by the Department of Health and Human Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The waiver covers seven core services provided by approved Medicaid providers: Intensive Individual Support Services (IISS) - one-on-one assistance to help children acquire and improve self-help, socialization, communication, daily living, functional living, behavior management, and adaptive skills; Therapeutic Integration (Regular or Intensive) - structured programs available outside of school hours that provide therapeutic activities and expressive therapies for children with socialization, isolation, hyperactivity, impulse control, and behavior problems; Respite Care - short-term supervision and assistance with activities of daily living to provide relief to caregivers; Environmental Accessibility Adaptations (EAA) - funding for physical home modifications necessary to ensure health, welfare, and safety; Family Consultation (FC) - individualized consultation and training provided to the child's family; Adult Life Planning (ALP) - family-centered support to access adult community services; and Residential Habilitation (Regular or Intensive) - community-based residential placement for children who cannot live at home, with the goal of returning the child to the home. Additionally, participants receive full Medical Assistance benefits including health insurance, prescription coverage, dental care, physician and hospital care, home health, laboratory services, disposable medical supplies, durable medical equipment, and mental health services. Service coordination support is provided through the local education agency. Service coordination is available through available waiver slots offered on a first-come, first-served basis via a registry. Participants must use at least one participant-focused Autism Waiver service per month or 5 hours per month to maintain eligibility. There are no fees to participants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline specified; enrollment occurs when slots become available on a first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and youth ages 1 through the end of the school semester when the child turns 21 years old with Autism Spectrum Disorder living in Maryland who meet institutional level of care requirements and financial eligibility criteria, and their families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based therapeutic services and support for children and youth with autism, including intensive individual support services (one-on-one assistance), therapeutic integration programming, respite care, environmental accessibility adaptations (home modifications), family consultation and training, adult life planning, residential habilitation, and service coordination.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; families must reside in Maryland. Statewide there are over 60 approved waiver provider agencies. The program is administered locally by regional education agencies and early intervention programs in each Maryland county. Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services administers this program locally for Montgomery County residents.
requirements_list: Have a current educational classification of Autism or a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (diagnosed within the last 3 years by a qualified diagnostician)
Be ages 1 through the end of the school semester when the child turns 21 years old
Reside in Maryland

Receive early intervention or special education services identified through an Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP) for ages 1-5, an IEP in an early childhood or Kindergarten setting for ages 3-5, or an IEP with 15 or more hours of special education and related services and/or 1:1 adult supports per week for first grade through high school exit

Meet eligibility requirements for an Intermediate Care Facility for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities (ICF-IID) institutional level of care and choose to receive Autism Waiver services as an alternative
Be able to be served and safely maintained in the home and community with waiver services

Meet financial eligibility for Medical Assistance with monthly income not exceeding 300 percent of Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits and countable assets not exceeding $2,000 or $2,500 depending on eligibility category
Choose the Autism Waiver as the best option to meet the child's needs if enrolled in another Home and Community-Based Services Waiver or other Medicaid Waiver program
Register on the Autism Waiver Registry by calling (866) 417-3480 to be eligible to apply when a vacancy occurs
IEP must be approved by Maryland State Department of Education

Military Exception: Dependents of US Military Service members invited to apply to the Autism Waiver while the family is out of state for military services shall be offered an opportunity to apply upon request when they return to Maryland and meet all technical eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact the Autism Waiver Registry Helpline at (866) 417-3480 to register the child's name on the waiting list. Provide child's name, date of birth, address, county of residence, and contact information. 2. MDH vendor conducts initial screening during intake call based on parent self-report to verify technical eligibility criteria (Maryland residency, age under 21, Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis, IFSP or IEP with 15 hours of special education/health-related services). 3. If technical eligibility is met, the child's name is added to the Autism Waiver Registry and MSDE is notified; family receives confirmation letter. 4. If technical eligibility is not met or additional information is needed, family receives letter with 30-day deadline to provide updated/additional information or faces removal from registry. 5. When a waiver slot becomes available, family receives invitation letter giving a 45-day deadline to accept the invitation, establish contact with the Autism Waiver contact at their local education agency (LEA), complete the technical eligibility checklist, and submit financial application. Enclosures include Medical Assistance (MA) Financial Application, Parental Rights and Responsibilities, AW Contact List, and Application Documentation Checklist. 6. Family works with the Autism Waiver contact at their local education agency to confirm technical, financial, and medical eligibility through Level of Care assessment (signed by Maryland licensed psychologist or certified school psychologist). 7. Family completes financial eligibility application within 45 days from date of application letter from MDH. 8. Family attends multidisciplinary team meeting to develop a Plan of Care. 9. State sends final eligibility notification. If eligible, letter includes start date to begin Autism Waiver services. 10. Maintain eligibility by using at least one participant-focused Autism Waiver service per month or 5 hours per month. Application progress is tracked by LEA/MSDE. If financial application and technical eligibility checklist are not submitted within 30 days, a Final Notice is sent with 15-day deadline to submit information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) Outdoor Nature-Based Child Care License Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An innovative pilot initiative administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that expands high-quality child care options in Maryland by allowing early education providers to operate outdoor, nature-based early childhood programs. The program supports child care providers in establishing and operating outdoor-based child care services under a pilot license model, offering grant and technical assistance support statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grant funding and technical assistance support for child care providers to establish and operate outdoor, nature-based child care programs under a pilot license model issued by MSDE.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers and facilities — including non-profit, for-profit, and government entities — seeking to operate outdoor, nature-based early education programs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs associated with establishing and operating outdoor, nature-based child care programs under the pilot license model.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are now open. Interested providers should contact MSDE for application procedures and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A required pre-service training course for individuals seeking to acquire a Child Care Center License or a Family Child Care Registration in Maryland, provided by licensed Maryland Registered Nurses. This 6-hour Health, Safety, and Nutrition course covers theory and practice in medication administration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A six-hour classroom training course in Health, Safety, and Nutrition covering theory and practice in medication administration. Participants receive a certificate upon completion after passing content and skill tests. Some trainers also offer Special Needs Support Services for children with individualized medical management needs (Type 1 Diabetes DMMP, Seizure management, Tube Feeding, Urinary Catheter, Oxygen Mask/Cannula) and Spanish-language instruction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking to acquire a Child Care Center License or a Family Child Care Registration in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in medication administration procedures
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland via licensed trainers in various regions. Multiple trainers serve each county and region across all 24 Maryland counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be seeking a Child Care Center License or Family Child Care Registration
Must be able to attend six-hour classroom training
Must pass content and skill tests to receive certificate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a Medication Administration Trainer in your region using the approved trainers list available from the Division of Early Childhood - Office of Child Care. Trainers are listed by county/region coverage. Register directly with the licensed Registered Nurse trainer of your choice to schedule training.

structured_extraction.program_description: Twice-annual administrative meetings providing updates on USDA regulations and guidance and professional development for residential child care institutions and nonprofit private schools.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Twice-annual administrative meetings required for residential child care institutions and nonprofit private schools to receive updates on USDA regulations and guidance and professional development.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and professional development on USDA regulations and guidance

structured_extraction.program_description: Twice-annual administrative meetings providing updates on USDA regulations and guidance and professional development for public school systems.
