structured_extraction.program_description: The State aid program that reimburses the cost of tuition for students with disabilities placed in nonpublic special education schools through their Individualized Education Program (IEP) process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State's share of the cost of nonpublic special education tuition is calculated in accordance with Education Article §8-415 of the Annotated Code of Maryland. Children placed in nonpublic special education schools are included in the September 30th enrollment count with a code indicating their nonpublic placement. Reimbursement covers standard education and related services, extended school year services, residential services (when applicable), and supplementary aids and program modifications as outlined in the student's IEP. Related services may include audiology, counseling, medical services, occupational therapy, orientation and mobility services, parent counseling and training, physical therapy, psychological services, recreation, rehabilitation counseling, school health services, social work services, speech-language pathology services, classroom aides, intensive behavior modification, and extended day services as specified in the IEP.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis with specific timelines: ESY or entry dates in July/August submit by September 30; entry dates September 1 to June 2 submit within 30 calendar days of entry date; entry dates June 3-30 submit by July 7; discharge applications within 30 calendar days of discharge date; service revision applications within 30 calendar days of revision date
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local school systems and school districts placing students with disabilities in nonpublic special education schools through the IEP process.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition costs for students placed in nonpublic special education day or residential programs, including standard education and related services, extended school year services, residential services, and supplementary aids and program modifications as outlined in the student's IEP.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Student must be placed in a nonpublic special education school through the IEP process
Nonpublic school must be MSDE-approved or justification provided for non-approved or out-of-state programs
Student must be included in the September 30th enrollment count
Placement must be consistent with federal and state special education laws and in the least restrictive environment
Application must be submitted by local school system with IEP team approval
For residential placements, must include documented need and agency/funding source information

For individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state programs, must include IEP team minutes supporting placement, letter from school stating ability to implement FAPE, and agreement/decision documentation for mediated or due process cases
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: School districts submit NTAP applications to MSDE for MSDE-approved day and residential programs, or request individual placement applications for non-approved or out-of-state programs as needed. Applications must include: (1) completed NTAP application form indicating whether it is a New, Renewal, Re-Entry, Discharge, Service Revision, or Correction submission; (2) approved cost sheet with the application; (3) for individual placements, supporting documentation including IEP team minutes, school letter confirming FAPE capability, and mediation/due process agreement if applicable. All information must be typed or printed legibly. Applications are reviewed in accordance with Education Article §8-415. MSDE may audit and investigate applications and supporting documentation. Discrepancies or noncompliance findings may result in requirement for refund of State funds. Failure to submit applications within timely fashion may also result in refund requirement. Written notice and expected submission date should be provided if unable to meet submission timeline.

structured_extraction.program_description: OBVS provides vocational rehabilitation, transition services, independent living programs, and deaf-blind services for individuals whose primary disability is vision loss. Services include career guidance, assistive technology, training, independent living skills, orientation and mobility instruction, and job placement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: OBVS provides specialized training and technical assistance to individuals who are blind, vision impaired, or deaf-blind. Services include career guidance and exploration, assistive technology such as screen reading software and magnifiers, career training or academic education, independent living skills training such as safe cooking techniques and personal care, orientation and mobility instruction for safe travel, and job placement assistance. Four service areas are available: Employment/vocational rehabilitation services to help obtain competitive employment, transition services for students with disabilities to prepare for post-school life, Independent Living Older Blind (ILOB) programs for individuals age 55 and over, and Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind (BEP) to operate retail concession, food service, and vending operations in federal and State facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who are blind, vision impaired, or deaf-blind seeking vocational rehabilitation, transition services, independent living support, or employment assistance
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services support employment and vocational rehabilitation, school-to-work transition, independent living for older individuals age 55 and over, and business enterprise operations for individuals with vision loss
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services available statewide through DORS offices throughout Maryland. Regional offices serve: Baltimore (410-554-9217) serving Baltimore City and Baltimore, Cecil, Howard & Harford Counties; Wheaton (301-949-3750) serving Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Montgomery & Washington Counties; Annapolis (410-974-7604) serving Anne Arundel, Calvert, Caroline, Charles, Dorchester, Kent, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico & Worcester Counties.
requirements_list: Primary disability must be vision loss or deaf-blindness
Must be eligible for DORS services as determined through intake assessment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Go to dors.maryland.gov and select Request DORS Services to complete the Request DORS Services form. The form can be completed by the individual, a parent or family member, a medical provider, a teacher, or other referral source. You will be contacted to set up an intake meeting where a DORS counselor will gather information and provide details regarding eligibility. If eligible, you will be assigned a counselor or teacher who works in your community. You may also contact your local DORS office directly to request services.

structured_extraction.program_description: An educational support program for people with Autism that provides college enrollment assistance and support services in collaboration with community colleges throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The DORS Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) Pathways Program provides educational support services for job seekers with Autism. Students enroll in credit and certificate classes and register with the Disability Support Services (DSS) office at their college. The DORS Pathways coordinator works with students, families, DORS counselors, DSS staff, and college faculty. Program services include adjustment to college life, assessment services, career guidance and counseling, employment and communication skills training, and individual and group sessions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with documented Autism diagnosis pursuing post-secondary education at participating community colleges in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational support services including adjustment to college life, assessment services, career guidance and counseling, employment and communication skills training, and individual and group sessions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at Anne Arundel Community College, Community College of Baltimore County, Howard Community College, Prince George's Community College, College of Southern Maryland, and Montgomery College.
requirements_list: Have a documented diagnosis of Autism
Have a DORS Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) that supports college as part of the employment plan
Register with the Disability Support Services (DSS) program at the college
Attend weekly group sessions and schedule classes around this standing appointment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals must have a documented Autism diagnosis and obtain a DORS Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) that supports college as part of the employment plan. Contact your DORS Counselor or local office to request DORS Services. Once approved, register with Disability Support Services (DSS) at your chosen community college, enroll in credit and certificate classes, and attend weekly group sessions coordinated by the DORS Pathways coordinator.

structured_extraction.program_name: Patty Centers/Family Support Center Network (Family Support Centers)
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide network of centers offering free, comprehensive educational and health-related services to parents and their children from birth through age three. Services include infant/toddler care assessment, parent education, adult education, family literacy, job readiness training, health education and referrals, home visits, peer support groups, and coordination of services between agencies. The program targets families to promote child development, strengthen parenting skills, and connect families to community resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services provided either on-site or through referral, including infant/toddler care assessment, parent education classes, adult education and family literacy programs, job readiness training, health education with referrals to community resources, home visits, peer support groups, and coordination of services between agencies. Available through 24 Patty Centers across 14 counties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents and their children from birth through age three.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services designed to promote child development, help adults develop parenting skills and fulfill aims related to school/employment/family life, provide supportive networks among parents, and connect families to community resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide, with 24 Patty Centers operating in 14 counties including Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Talbot, Montgomery, Prince George's, Howard, Frederick, Washington, Charles, St. Mary's, and Wicomico. Specific locations include Southern Anne Arundel County, seven communities in Baltimore City, and Early Head Start programs in Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, and Talbot counties.
requirements_list: Child must be from birth through age three
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Family Network or visit a local Patty Center to access services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pre-employment program that provides instruction in self-advocacy and social skills training to Pre-ETS students with Autism to help them develop soft skills needed for employment. Students participate in activities that introduce them to education, training and employment options available after high school, including apprenticeships, career training, job placement, and college, with college tours included.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Classroom and other activities providing Pre-ETS students with Autism exposure to soft skills needed to obtain and maintain employment, including self-advocacy and social skills training. Students participate in the Counseling on Post-Secondary Education Opportunities (CPSEO) program to learn about education, training and employment options after high school, including apprenticeships, career training, job placement, and college opportunities. College tours are included as part of the program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-ETS students with documented Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis seeking employment preparation. Students must be currently enrolled in high school (including home school or alternative secondary education program), post-high school education program such as college, or another recognized educational program like a trade school.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in self-advocacy and social skills to prepare for employment, and counseling on post-secondary education opportunities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through DORS Pre-ETS programs in Maryland.
requirements_list: Be enrolled in Pre-ETS
Have a documented diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder

Be currently enrolled in high school (including home school or alternative secondary education program), post-high school education program such as college, or another recognized educational program like a trade school
Be at least 14 years old but less than 22 years old
Have an Individualized Education Program (IEP), 504 plan, or medical records that document disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible Pre-ETS students with Autism participate in classroom and other activities focused on developing soft skills for employment. Students should contact their DORS Counselor or local office for more information or request DORS Services.

structured_extraction.program_description: Five specific services designed to help students with disabilities—including those who are blind or visually impaired—identify their career interests and enhance their awareness of the world of work. Services include job exploration counseling, instruction in self-advocacy, counseling on post-secondary education opportunities, workplace readiness training, and work-based learning experiences. These are generally short-term services covering introductory topics that emphasize exploration and preparation for employment and post-secondary education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Five specific services are provided at no cost to students: (1) Job Exploration Counseling to explore skills, interests and career opportunities through interest inventories, labor market information, and sessions about specific in-demand occupations; (2) Instruction in Self-Advocacy to learn strategies for effective communication, including knowledge of rights and responsibilities, self-awareness, problem solving, and programs like the Youth Leadership Forum; (3) Counseling on Post-Secondary Education Opportunities to gain awareness of career pathways and training options after high school, guidance on how to choose the right type, and how to access disability supports; (4) Workplace Readiness Training to learn knowledge, skills and abilities valued by employers including peer and supervisor interaction, punctuality, appropriate dress and behavior, and strategies to get to work on time; and (5) Work-Based Learning Experiences to complete learning objectives through work opportunities outside traditional school settings, such as work experiences at local participating employers. Services are tailored to individual needs and vary by location, including specialized services for students who are blind or visually impaired.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jessica Markum (Staff Specialist for Students and Transitioning Youth); Muttasim Fadl (Employment Services Specialist for Students with Blindness or Vision Impairments); MSDE Division of Rehabilitation Services Headquarters
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with documented disabilities—including those who are blind or visually impaired—who are at least 14 years old and no more than 21 years old and are currently in school, homeschool, or other approved educational program (including post-secondary education programs and other recognized educational programs) who have not graduated or withdrawn.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services cover job exploration counseling, self-advocacy instruction, post-secondary education counseling, workplace readiness training, and work-based learning experiences. Services are designed to help students explore careers and prepare for employment or post-secondary education, including specialized services for students who are blind or visually impaired.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through local DORS offices throughout Maryland (located in more than 20 offices around the state). Services are also available virtually. Specific services vary based on needs and opportunities in each area.
requirements_list: Must be at least 14 years old and no more than 21 years old

Must be enrolled in a secondary school (including home school or other alternative secondary education program), post-secondary education program, or other recognized educational program, and have not graduated or withdrawn
Must have a documented disability (on an Individualized Education Program (IEP) or 504 plan, or have medical documentation of a disability)
Must complete the Request DORS Services form
Must provide Social Security Number
Must provide documentation of disability
Must provide proof of current school enrollment
Must provide proof of age
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Request DORS Services by completing the Request DORS Services form found at dors.maryland.gov (can be completed by student, parent, medical provider, school staff, or others). You can also call your local DORS office for assistance with the form over the phone. Step 2: Await contact from DORS staff. Allow 10 business days for a DORS representative to get back to you to schedule a virtual or in-person intake meeting and determine next steps. After submitting the form, in about 10 business days you will receive a text message and email introducing Sara (DORS client communication software). Text messages will come from 34459 and emails from sara@sara.digital. You can also connect directly to your DORS counselor by texting 95424. Step 3: Pre-ETS Qualification Review where DORS staff review submitted information and forward qualifying student information to local DORS office. Step 4: Pre-ETS Service Agreement Meetings where a counselor from the local DORS office contacts student and family to meet and plan Pre-ETS services. Student discusses career interests, service needs, and transition services with counselor.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that provides funding to local education agencies and private providers to deliver high-quality full-day prekindergarten and school readiness services to three- and four-year-old children from families earning at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level, at no cost to families. The program supports program operations, staff salaries according to professional salary schedules, and educational services aligned with The Blueprint for Maryland's Future.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding awarded to local school systems and private providers (including qualified vendors and Head Start programs) to administer high-quality prekindergarten programs. Funding supports program operations, staff salaries according to professional salary schedules, and school readiness services. The program provides free full-day Pre-K education for eligible children from low-income families earning at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level. The estimated grant award amount is $400,000 (average), with approximately 50 grants available. Total funding available is $26,644,000. Funding is approximately $19,950 per full-day slot for three- and four-year-olds. Programs must deliver a minimum of 180 instructional days per year with at least 6.5 hours per day of instruction. Funds may be used for: staff salaries and fringe benefits paid commensurate with local school system salaries; equipment, materials, and supplies (classroom furniture, instructional materials aligned with Maryland Early Learning Standards); reasonable rental/mortgage and utility costs (prorated by square footage); technology costs (not to exceed 10% of total request); costs for maintaining accreditation status or Maryland EXCELS rating; screening and intervention services; program evaluation and monitoring costs (not to exceed 5%); meals meeting CACFP requirements; academic field trips; and professional learning activities for instructional staff. Indirect costs may not exceed 15% for non-profit organizations or 10% for other grantees. Funds may NOT be used for supplanting existing program funds, capital improvements, costs incurred before grant approval, or transportation (except field trips).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, March 11, 2026. No later than 5:00 pm EDT.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dr. Nykia Washington, Prekindergarten and Mixed Delivery Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies, local school systems, qualified vendors, Head Start programs, and private providers (including center-based and family child care programs) that deliver prekindergarten services to eligible children; as well as three- and four-year-old children from families earning at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support the administration and delivery of high-quality full-day prekindergarten and school readiness services, including staff compensation according to professional salary schedules, program operations, educational programming aligned with Maryland Early Learning Standards and the Maryland College and Career Ready Standards, equipment and materials, professional development, accreditation costs, health screenings and referrals, and comprehensive services for children and families. At the family level, funds enable free Pre-K education services for eligible children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland; all counties are eligible.

Professional staff must be compensated according to state salary schedules

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete a grant application through the online Qualtrics form (https://msde.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0qxUC1IT7xwk08C) by March 11, 2026 at 5:00 pm EDT. The application is divided into four sections: (1) Applicant Information, (2) Slots Requested, (3) Application (Full or Modified based on eligibility responses), and (4) Appendices. Applicants must first answer initial eligibility questions confirming: valid license/registration (if applicable), current Maryland EXCELS rating (Level 3+ for private providers; Level 4+ for public providers), and organizational status. Based on responses, applicants are directed to either a Full Application or Modified Short Form Application. Full applications are required for all new applicants and existing grantees without a demonstrated track record of success. Modified short forms are available for existing grantees seeking renewal or expansion who demonstrate: maintained qualified lead teacher, maintained EXCELS Level 3+, remained in compliance with reporting/fiscal guidelines, not under corrective action, and filled 85% of seats by December 31, 2025. Full applications require minimum 80 points; modified applications require minimum 45 points. Application sections include: Program Eligibility (Maryland EXCELS/Accreditation), Evidence of Need (Market Analysis), Measurable Goals (4 SMART goals addressing standards alignment, instructional practice, quality improvement, child outcomes), Program Quality and Curriculum, Plan of Operation, Staffing and Key Personnel, Project Timeline, Collaboration and Sustainability, Fiscal Systems and Controls, and Budget/Budget Narrative. Applicants can save progress within a browser session on the same device; the application grows as text is entered. Applicants should review Completing the Pre-K Expansion Grant Application in Qualtrics document for detailed navigation tips. Before final submission, applicants must review all responses, check for missing information, and download a PDF copy for records. Once submitted, changes cannot be made. MSDE provides customer service support sessions and office hours to assist applicants. All required appendices must be uploaded within Qualtrics, including: Works Cited page, documentation of income eligibility policy per Federal Poverty Guidelines, Head Start letter of support (if applicable), resumes of key personnel, Maryland EXCELS verification, plan to achieve/maintain Level 5, professional learning plan (minimum 20 hours), job announcements for unfilled positions, MSDE Grant Budget C-1-25 form, and Grant Recipient Assurances form. Questions should be directed to prekexpansiongrant.msde@maryland.gov with subject line: Pre-K Expansion Application.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to help child care providers expand their business and access state prekindergarten funding. The initiative provides guidance on meeting requirements for Pre-K grants and simplifies the grant application process.

Providers receive support in understanding eligibility criteria, preparing grant applications, and meeting the technical, personnel, and financial capacity requirements outlined in the Grant Information Guide.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expanding child care services to provide state-funded prekindergarten programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: The School Breakfast Program provides children with nutritious breakfast meals in participating public and private nonprofit schools and residential childcare institutions. Studies show participation is correlated with higher test scores, decreased emotional and behavioral problems, reduced food insecurity, less frequent visits to the nurse, and fewer school absences. The program reimburses schools with federal dollars for meals that comply with USDA nutrition standards and Dietary Guidelines for Americans. Students may qualify for free or reduced-price meals based on family income.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses participating schools with federal dollars for nutritious breakfasts served to students that comply with USDA nutrition standards and Dietary Guidelines for Americans. Over 898,000 students across all 24 Maryland public schools, 17 non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions receive breakfasts. Students from families with incomes at or below 130-185% of the poverty level may receive meals at a free or reduced price. Students in families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and/or food stamp benefits are eligible for free meals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: K-12 students in Maryland public schools, participating non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions. Schools and residential childcare institutions serving school-age children are eligible to participate.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Breakfast meals that meet USDA nutrition standards and Dietary Guidelines for Americans. Funds help offset the costs of producing breakfast meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All 24 Maryland public school systems and 17 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions participate.
requirements_list: School must be public, private nonprofit, or residential childcare institution
Breakfast must meet USDA nutrition guidelines and Dietary Guidelines for Americans
Family income at or below 130-185% of the poverty level for free or reduced-price meals
Students in families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and/or food stamp benefits are eligible for free meals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and institutions participate in the SBP through the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs. Each school district determines the cost of school breakfast for students and administers eligibility determinations based on family income.

The program encourages the consumption of fluid milk by children in public and private nonprofit schools, summer camps, and other eligible nonprofit sites, reimbursing institutions for the cost of the half-pint of milk served to children.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimburses schools and institutions for the milk they serve to children through direct payments to offset the cost of milk. Schools with half-day pre-kindergarten and kindergarten programs where children do not have access to other school meal programs may also participate.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Milk served to children; funds offset the cost of milk provided to children at participating institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland

School with half-day pre-kindergarten and kindergarten programs may participate if children lack access to school meal programs

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education provides annual grants to qualified non-profit organizations that offer enriching educational programs to Maryland students. These programs provide learning experiences aligned with the state's curricular and educational priorities that cannot be replicated in a classroom. Programs emphasize experiential learning and one-on-one support services including free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, tutoring, and professional development for teachers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants are provided to qualified 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations for educational programs. Approximately $6,706,449 is available with an estimated 60-65 grants to be awarded for Fiscal Year 2027. Funds must be used for direct services to students and teachers within the fiscal year for which they are granted. Eligible uses include: salaries, wages, and stipends for direct service to students and educators; supplies and materials to implement the educational program; outreach, engagement, informational, and marketing tools to expand reach; equipment necessary for direct service to students and teachers; and contractual expenses. Funds may NOT be used for: construction or capital improvements, transportation of students, utilities or operating costs, or food.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, June 13, 2025, no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified non-profit organizations that are 501(c)(3) entities in good standing and provide direct service to Maryland students and teachers through enriching, educational programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports enriching educational programs including free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, tutoring, pre- and post-visit activities for teachers, and professional development opportunities for teachers that link programs to classroom curriculum. Funds support salaries and wages for direct service, supplies and materials, outreach and marketing tools, and equipment necessary for educational service delivery.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Currently, 57 organizations are in the SAI program. In fiscal year 2024, approximately 440,000 Maryland students and teachers were served through this program. Eligible organizations must be based in Maryland and incorporated or registered under Maryland laws.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are available for download on the SAI webpage starting May 1, 2025. Applicants must complete the electronic SAI application with all attachments and save as one PDF file. Grant applications must be submitted by email to sai.applications@maryland.gov no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT on June 13, 2025. MSDE will review applications on a rolling basis. Customer service support sessions are offered on May 5 and May 23, 2025 to review program requirements and provide a walk-through of the application process. After submission, a review committee at MSDE evaluates applications using a scoring rubric. For any section scored as Level 1 (does not meet criteria), written feedback is provided and an opportunity to revise and resubmit is offered. Results are communicated to the State Superintendent in July, then provided to the State Board of Education for review in August. The Governor releases the draft budget bill in January of the following year, which is voted on and published around April when funding decisions are revealed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive vocational rehabilitation services that help students with disabilities obtain meaningful employment and pursue successful careers, including Pre-ETS and a broad range of additional employment preparation and job placement services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Comprehensive vocational rehabilitation services available through two programs: (1) Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) covering job exploration counseling, counseling on opportunities for enrollment in comprehensive transition or post-secondary education programs, work-based learning experiences, workplace readiness training, and self-advocacy through activities, lessons, and workshops; and (2) VR Employment Services providing individualized plan of services to support students with most significant disabilities in obtaining competitive integrated employment. Services are determined through development of an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) that lists the employment goal, needed services, service providers, payment responsibility, evaluation methods, and expected employment timeline. DORS counselors participate in IEP meetings and coordinate services with school and family. Students with the Most Significant Disabilities receive priority for VR Employment Services. Some students may be placed on a waiting list for additional services beyond Pre-ETS based on disability significance, with those on the waiting list longest served first.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with disabilities enrolled in secondary school, post-secondary education, or recognized educational programs who are at least 14 years old but less than age 22, have a disability documented with an IEP, 504 plan, or medical record, and are interested in obtaining meaningful employment and a successful career. All students at least 14 years of age and up to their 22nd birthday with a documented disability who are enrolled in secondary school or approved post-secondary education are qualified to receive available Pre-ETS services. Students with most significant disabilities receive priority for VR Employment Services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment preparation, job training, vocational services, and career development services including job exploration counseling, work-based learning experiences, workplace readiness training, self-advocacy activities and workshops, and services outlined in the student's Individualized Plan for Employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland. DORS has a counselor assigned to every public high school in Maryland.
requirements_list: Be enrolled in secondary school (including home school or alternative program), post-secondary education program, or recognized educational program and have not graduated or withdrawn
Be at least 14 years old but less than age 22
Have a disability documented with an Individualized Education Program (IEP), 504 plan, or medical record
Be determined eligible for services through DORS review of available documentation and assessments
Students with Most Significant Disabilities receive priority for VR Employment Services; other eligible students are placed on waiting list
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students, families, or schools can submit an online referral to DORS (with parent/guardian consent if submitted by schools). Schools should provide documentation such as IEP, 504 plan, and/or psychological assessment. DORS reviews available documentation from schools or doctors and arranges assessments as necessary to determine eligibility. There is no wrong door to DORS services; regardless of referral type, DORS transition counselors will discuss both Pre-ETS and VR Employment Services programs with students and families. If eligible, DORS makes a priority determination based on the significance of the student's disability. Students with most significant disabilities receive an individualized plan of services. Eligible students complete an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) in consultation with their DORS counselor, family, or school personnel. The IPE is approved by DORS before Student Employment Services begin. Students who do not have most significant disabilities are placed on a waiting list, with those on the list longest served first.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded, state-administered program that provides free, nutritious meals (breakfasts and lunches) to children and teens 18 years and younger in low-income and economically disadvantaged areas during the summer months when school is not in session. The program reimburses approved meal service providers for serving meals that meet federal nutrition standards. Two service models are available through Maryland: SUN Meals (meals consumed on site, often combined with enrichment activities) and SUN Meals To-Go (multi-day meal boxes available for pickup with registration). The program helps children stay healthy, active, and well-nourished over the summer months. Baltimore City operates its own local implementation administered by the city.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses approved meal service providers for serving free, nutritious meals (breakfasts and lunches) to eligible children and teens ages 18 and younger. Each meal meets 1/3 of the minimum daily nutritional requirements as devised by the USDA and is prepared by a food service management company, with meals delivered daily to site locations. Two service models are available: SUN Meals (meals consumed on site with enrichment activities) and SUN Meals To-Go (multi-day meal boxes for pickup with registration). Breakfast consists of cold cereal or bread/bread alternate, fruit juice, and milk. In Baltimore City, organizations can apply to become meal serving sites and receive meals for a minimum of two weeks while serving a minimum of ten eligible youth. Operating dates for Baltimore City: Monday through Friday, June 17 through August 22 (pending verification of Baltimore City Schools' calendar).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and teens 18 years and younger in low-income and economically disadvantaged areas throughout Maryland. Organizations such as non-profits, churches, day camps, community groups, government agencies, and city agencies that wish to serve as meal distribution sites. In Baltimore City, interested organizations include non-profits, churches, day camps, and community groups seeking to serve as meal serving sites.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Serving federally-approved nutritious meals (breakfast and lunch) to eligible children during summer when school is not in session. Meals must meet federal, state, and local nutritional and regulatory standards. Breakfast consists of cold cereal or bread/bread alternate, fruit juice, and milk. Refrigeration is required for perishable components if meals are not served within one hour of delivery. Programs may be combined with summer activity and enrichment programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all Maryland counties in economically disadvantaged and low-income areas. Each county has a designated sponsoring organization (typically the county public schools or a specific county department) that administers the program locally. Baltimore City operates its own local implementation; meal serving sites in Baltimore City must be located within the city — private homes and public school buildings are not eligible in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Children must be 18 years old or younger
Meals must be served in low-income or economically disadvantaged areas
Meals must meet federal nutrition requirements (1/3 of minimum daily USDA requirements)
Organizations must apply through their county's sponsoring organization or through the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs
Site must plan to receive meals for a minimum of two weeks (Baltimore City)
Site must serve a minimum of ten eligible youth ages 18 or younger; youth workers may be included in the count (Baltimore City)
Private homes and public school buildings are not eligible to participate (Baltimore City)
Sites requesting breakfast must have adequate refrigeration to store perishables overnight (Baltimore City)
Refrigeration is also required for perishable lunch components if the meal is not served within one hour of delivery
Sites are subject to a pre-operational inspection and must be approved by program staff (Baltimore City)
Site supervisor and at least one alternate must attend a mandatory three-hour training session (Baltimore City)
All meals must be served in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations
All site supervisors and alternates must agree to serve all meals in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sponsors and organizations apply to participate through the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs at the Maryland State Department of Education. Organizations interested in becoming a SUN Meals site should contact the sponsoring organization designated for their county. In Baltimore City, organizations can apply online via the program website (cityservices.baltimorecity.gov/summerfood/) by downloading and reviewing the Program Description and Requirements, then completing the 2026 SFSP Site Application form. Paper applications may also be mailed to: Summer Food Service Program, 1135 N. Gilmor Street - 2nd Floor, Baltimore, MD 21217. Baltimore City applicants must attend a mandatory three-hour training session and undergo a pre-operational inspection before approval. Eligibility is determined by geographic location.

structured_extraction.program_description: Required annual training for participating agencies providing updates on USDA regulations and guidance and professional development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Required annual training for participating agencies providing updates on USDA regulations and guidance and professional development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agencies participating in the Summer Food Service Program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Annual training on USDA regulations and professional development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an agency participating in the Summer Food Service Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs for dates and locations.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding for Local Education Agencies (LEAs) participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during School Year 2021-2022 to support staff training on recipe preparation, recipe tasting events, and food purchases. The goal is to create new, high-quality, appealing standardized recipes for Maryland schools using local agricultural products in partnership with Prince George's Community College's Department of Wellness, Culinary Arts, and Hospitality. Feedback from tasting events is used to modify recipes to align with students' flavor preferences and school implementation capacity. Training and nutrition education resources are developed by Maryland SNAP-Ed and the Maryland Department of Agriculture.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MSDE provides subgrant funding to Local Education Agencies for the period May 1, 2022 – September 30, 2023. Funds support: (1) Salaries/wages to hire substitute school nutrition staff to allow regular staff to attend training; (2) Stipends for staff time to attend training activities outside normal work hours; (3) Food and nutrition equipment and smallware (crinkle cutters, peelers, food processors, knives, roasting pans, utensils) with total equipment value not exceeding 5% of subgrant total; (4) Food costs for grant-related training and taste tests, not exceeding 20% of subgrant total, purchased in accordance with Buy American Provision; (5) Consumable costs for grant-related training and taste tests. MSDE anticipates awarding approximately ten (10) grants, with additional grants possible if funds are available. Funds cannot be used for: child nutrition program costs outside this grant scope, purchasing meals/snacks for training participants, foods for reimbursable meals, foods as incentives/prizes, foods provided to students/families for home preparation, foods unrelated to standardized recipes, prize or incentive items, gardening tools/materials, or clothing (chef hats, aprons, shirts).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than 5:00 pm EST on April 22, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (LEAs) participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during School Year 2021-2022 that are in good standing and commit participation of up to three schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salaries and wages for substitute staff to allow nutrition professionals to attend training; stipends for staff time to attend training outside normal work hours; food and nutrition equipment and smallware (up to 5% of total grant); food costs for training and taste tests (up to 20% of total grant); consumable costs for training and taste tests. Funds support development and preparation of four standardized recipes: Vegetable Side Dish, Chicken or Fish Bowl, Vegetarian Bowl, and Entrée Salad.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties. Selection preferences include schools with high free and reduced-price meal percentages (over 75% receives 3 points, 50-75% receives 2 points), schools located in USDA-defined rural zones (1 point each, max 3 per LEA), and schools in IRS-designated Qualified Opportunity Zones (1 point each, max 3 per LEA).
requirements_list: Must be a Local Education Agency (LEA) participating in NSLP or SSO during 2021-2022 and in good standing

Must commit participation of up to three schools; if more than one school selected, at least two must serve different grade levels (with certain exceptions approved to maintain grade-level distribution)
Selected schools must be enrolled and registered as Team Nutrition Schools prior to application submission
LEA must designate a Grant Coordinator to serve as primary liaison with MSDE and grant partners, manage subgrant funds, and ensure grant activities are implemented at all participating schools
Each participating school's nutrition staff must attend required training events hosted by MSDE and/or grant partners
Each school must prepare at least one chef-designed recipe and host two or more student taste tests per recipe between Spring 2022 - Spring 2023
Grant Coordinator must collect feedback from students and school nutrition staff after each tasting event and submit to MSDE
Schools must use provided nutrition education resources to implement nutrition education for local products used in recipes
LEA must menu (serve) at least one of the final new recipes in a reimbursable meal at participating schools by end of grant
Grant Coordinator must submit quarterly reports on utilization of subgrant funds and grant activities
Grant Coordinator must secure photographs, training attendance records, data, and success stories for MSDE quarterly progress reports to USDA
Grant Coordinator must participate in periodic virtual meetings with grant partners
Food purchases must comply with Buy American Provision
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: (1) Identify participating schools that are registered as Team Nutrition Schools and participate in NSLP or SSO. (2) Complete a School Agreement Form for each participating school (up to three total) requiring signatures from School Principal, Kitchen Manager/Cafeteria Supervisor, and a third school staff member (such as School Health Council member, Title 1 Coordinator, or Community Coordinator). (3) Complete the Team Nutrition Grant Application including: school listing, recipe selection (choose from Vegetable Side Dish, Chicken or Fish Bowl, Vegetarian Bowl, Entrée Salad), budget, and school agreements. (4) Obtain required signatures on printed application from Local School System Superintendent, Food and Nutrition Services Director, and LEA Grant Coordinator. (5) Prepare required attachments: signed MSDE Assurances Page, signed LEA and School Agreement Forms, and completed Team Nutrition Budget (Excel file). (6) Save completed application as PDF. (7) Email complete application and all attachments to NutritionTraining.MSDE@maryland.gov, Attention: Sara Booker. An optional informational webinar was held March 31, 2022 from 2:00-3:00 pm. MSDE reviews applications for eligibility, scores using specified criteria, and notifies LEAs of award status by late April. Award processing begins May 1, 2022 and can take 4-6 weeks. Grantees must submit quarterly reports on June 30, September 30, December 30, March 31, and June 30, with final report due September 30, 2023. Final invoices must be submitted no later than 60 days after grant period ends.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Ticket to Work program connects people with disabilities who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) with the Department of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) or community Employment Networks (EN). Participants work with DORS to develop an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) and receive services including job training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation, job placement, job coaching, benefits counseling, and ongoing support services to help achieve and maintain employment. The program provides protections such as exemption from Continuing Disability Reviews as long as the Ticket remains in use and timely progress requirements are met.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Services are provided at no cost to participants. DORS works with eligible individuals to develop an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) based on their employment goals and provides job training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation services, job placement assistance, job coaching, benefits planning, and ongoing support services necessary to achieve employment goals. Participants receive protection from Continuing Disability Reviews while their Ticket is in use with DORS and they are making timely progress. After employment is achieved and the DORS case closes, the Ticket is no longer in use with DORS, and Social Security will send a letter explaining how to assign the Ticket to another agency if continued support is desired. Built-in work incentives help participants try working without immediately losing benefits, earn more money, keep health insurance (Medicare may be kept for at least 93 months after earning more; Medicaid can be maintained through continuation programs or the Employed Individuals with Disabilities (EID) program), and get cash benefits back if they must stop working due to disability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with disabilities aged 18-64 who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) and are interested in pursuing employment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services support employment planning and achievement including job training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation, job placement, job coaching, benefits planning, and ongoing employment support services. Work incentives help participants maintain health benefits and income while working.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Must be between 18 and 64 years old
Must be a recipient of Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
Must have an assignable Ticket from Social Security Administration
Must sign an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) with DORS for the Ticket to be considered in use with the agency
Must demonstrate timely progress toward employment or educational goals as defined by Social Security Administration requirements
Must reply to letters sent by Social Security Administration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the DORS Ticket Coordinator at 410-554-9460 or email Ticket.DORS@maryland.gov to begin the process. DORS will work with Social Security Administration to verify that your Ticket is available and assignable for use with the agency. You will work with a DORS counselor to develop an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) based on your employment goals. When you sign your IPE, your Ticket becomes 'In Use' with DORS and services begin. Services are provided free and participation is voluntary. If you are already using your Ticket with an Employment Network (EN), DORS will coordinate with that organization. After you obtain employment and your DORS case closes, your Ticket will no longer be in use with DORS, and Social Security will send information on reassigning your Ticket if additional support is desired.

structured_extraction.program_description: Supports domestic nutrition programs and American agricultural producers through purchases of 100% American-grown and -produced foods for use by schools participating in the National School Lunch Program. Reduces food expenses in schools by an average of twenty percent. Also provides cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods to Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) sponsors with their meal reimbursements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools can choose from a catalog of over two hundred choices of domestically grown fruits, vegetables, grains, poultry, dairy, and meat products to incorporate into their menus. Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) sponsors receive cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods with their CACFP meal reimbursements. Reduces food expenses in schools by an average of twenty percent.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland schools participating in the National School Lunch Program and Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) sponsors
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of domestically grown fruits, vegetables, grains, poultry, dairy, and meat products for school meals and nutrition programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to schools participating in the NSLP throughout Maryland
requirements_list: School must participate in the National School Lunch Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools participating in the NSLP receive USDA Foods through the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs

structured_extraction.program_description: A virtual mentoring and support service for college students on the autism spectrum who are not participating in the Pathways program. The program helps students transition into college, navigate the college environment, and develop self-advocacy and social skills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Remote mentoring and support services provided virtually to college students on the autism spectrum. The program focuses on college transition assistance, self-advocacy skill development, and social skills training to support success in the college environment. Students participate in weekly online sessions with DORS Autism Services staff and attend weekly VCAMP online group sessions. The program covers topics including transition from high school to college, navigating two-year to four-year college transitions, accessing campus supports like Disability Support Services (DSS) and academic tutoring, time management and organizational skills, self-advocacy and social skills, grooming and hygiene skills, and other skills needed to successfully navigate the college environment.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: Contact your DORS Counselor or local office for more information
structured_extraction.program_audience: College students on the autism spectrum attending in-state or out-of-state two- or four-year colleges who are not participating in the Pathways program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Virtual mentoring and support services focused on college transition, self-advocacy, and social skills development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students attending in-state or out-of-state two- or four-year colleges where the in-person DORS Pathways program is not available.
requirements_list: Be a DORS participant on the autism spectrum
Have an approved Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) that includes college
Work towards an industry-recognized college degree or certification from a two-year or four-year college where the in-person DORS Pathways program is not available
Meet with DORS Autism Services staff for weekly online sessions
Attend weekly VCAMP online group sessions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible DORS participants on the autism spectrum should contact their DORS Counselor or local office to request VCAMP services. The QR code on program materials can also be used to request DORS Services. Once approved, students participate in weekly online sessions with DORS Autism Services staff and attend weekly VCAMP online group sessions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that reimburses businesses for employee wages while they train qualified job seekers hired from the Department of Rehabilitation Services (DORS). Businesses can participate in short-term training (one month) with up to 100% salary reimbursement, or long-term training (up to four months) with gradually decreasing reimbursement as the employee becomes more skilled and independent.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses receive wage reimbursement for hiring and training qualified DORS job seekers. Short-term on-the-job training (one month) provides up to 100% salary reimbursement. Long-term on-the-job training (up to four months) provides gradually decreasing reimbursement as the employee becomes more skilled and independent. Businesses must complete the DORS Provider/Vendor Application to participate. Payment is processed by DORS and typically takes approximately 30 days after invoice receipt.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses interested in hiring and training qualified job seekers from DORS.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wage reimbursement for employees undergoing on-the-job training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. DORS operates six regional offices covering all counties in the state.
requirements_list: Must hire a qualified DORS job seeker
Must complete the DORS Provider/Vendor Application form and attach required credentials and documentation
Must work with a local DORS Business Services Representative
Must obtain written authorization from a DORS representative before providing services
Must provide invoices containing required information: DORS office billing information, remit-to address, Federal Tax ID, invoice date, description of services/goods, and costs
Goods or services must not be provided unless authorized by DORS in writing or with a preauthorized credit card
Provider/vendors may not require or accept payment from consumers or families unless preauthorized by DORS, agreed to in writing by the consumer, and approved by the DORS counselor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the DORS Provider/Vendor Application form. 2. Attach required supporting documentation including IRS Form W-9, copies of any required licenses/certifications, and insurance certificates if applicable. 3. Submit the application and attachments to the Director, DORS Business Support Services, 2301 Argonne Drive, Baltimore, MD 21218-1696, by phone at 410-554-9415 or fax at 410-554-9413. 4. DORS will contact the applicant within 30 days of receiving a complete application. 5. Once approved, work with your local DORS Business Services Representative to hire qualified job seekers and arrange wage reimbursement terms. 6. Submit invoices with required information for payment processing, which typically takes approximately 30 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: A two-part training program for individuals with disabilities who have little or no work experience or those who have been out of the workforce for an extended period. The program develops workplace skills through community-based activities and classroom sessions at the DORS WTC campus in Baltimore, helping job seekers prepare for competitive employment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers two six-week courses that can be taken together or separately. Work Readiness 1 includes career exploration, soft skills development, financial management, organizational skills, self-determination and self-awareness, interpersonal skills and teamwork, workplace preparation and communication, and job retention through videos, lectures, guest speakers, worksite tours, and job shadowing. Work Readiness 2 focuses on customer service, workplace ethics, conflict management, resume writing, job descriptions, mock interviews, and managing your online footprint, with real-world work experience through volunteer work at community worksites. Both courses are held at the DORS WTC campus in Baltimore and include community-based activities and classroom sessions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities who have little or no work experience or have been out of the workforce for an extended period and are seeking competitive employment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants gain skills and real-world work experience through volunteer work at community worksites and internships at the Workforce Training Center to prepare for competitive employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is held at DORS WTC campus in Baltimore.
requirements_list: Eligibility for DORS Services
Work Readiness 1: Must be able to function in a classroom setting and be able to fully participate in all individual and group activities.
Work Readiness 2: Must demonstrate capability and desire to participate in competitive employment and be able to spend half of each day volunteering at a community worksite with drop-in support only.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals contact their DORS Counselor or local DORS office to apply and request DORS Services. The program offers both six-week courses that can be taken together or as stand-alone programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides nutritious lunches and snacks to students in participating public and private nonprofit schools and residential childcare institutions. The program helps schools and residential child care facilities offset the cost of producing meals for students, ensuring meals meet USDA nutrition guidelines and Dietary Guidelines for Americans.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimburses and provides direct payments to participating schools to help offset the cost of producing nutritious lunches and snacks served to students. Over 900,000 students across all 24 Maryland public school systems and 22 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions receive meals. Non-financial assistance includes regulatory guidance, services, and technical assistance/information.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in participating public and private nonprofit schools, residential childcare institutions, and state colleges/universities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Nutritious lunches and snacks that meet USDA nutrition guidelines and Dietary Guidelines for Americans; funds help offset the cost of producing meals for students

requirements_list: School must be public, private nonprofit, or residential childcare institution
Meals must meet USDA nutrition guidelines
Eligible entities include county governments, municipalities/towns, non-profits, state colleges, state universities, and state government
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and institutions participate through the NSLP as administered by the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs. Applications are submitted annually.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified disability-related expenses

structured_extraction.program_name: ALERT / Alcohol Law Education Regulatory Training
structured_extraction.program_description: ALERT (Alcohol Law Education Regulatory Training) is an educational program administered by Montgomery County designed to educate servers, sellers, managers, and owners of alcohol beverage establishments in alcohol beverage regulatory compliance. Participants learn how to develop responsible alcohol policies, review issues identified by County and State enforcement agencies, and network with peers and county officials. The training is free, held online via Zoom, and available in English, Spanish, Amharic, Chinese, French, Korean, and Vietnamese. It complements but does not replace state-certified training.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training held from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM on the 2nd and 4th Monday of every month (except holidays). No cost to attend. Participants must register in advance as space is limited. Attendees must join the online Zoom session by 10:15 AM or will not be admitted. It is recommended to sign in 10 minutes early (by 10:05 AM) to allow time for troubleshooting. Those who join by 10:15 AM receive a letter of attendance via link provided at end of class. Registration is available in English, Spanish, Amharic, Chinese, French, Korean, and Vietnamese. Training complements but does not replace state-certified training required by Maryland law.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling registration; trainings held monthly on 2nd and 4th Monday (except holidays)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Servers, sellers, managers, and owners of alcohol beverage establishments in Montgomery County, Maryland. Training is designed for employees and operators of on-premise and off-premise alcohol retail establishments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational training covering: alcohol beverage regulatory compliance; responsible alcohol policies; blood alcohol concentration (BAC) and intoxication signs; alcohol absorption factors; Maryland alcohol rules and regulations; inspection requirements; underage drinking prevention and ID verification; responsible beverage service practices; civil liability and legal requirements; Board of License Commissioners hearing preparation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to alcohol beverage establishment servers, sellers, managers, and owners in Montgomery County, Maryland. Training is held online via Zoom and is accessible to participants in Montgomery County and surrounding areas.
requirements_list: Must be a server, seller, manager, or owner of an alcohol beverage establishment or prospective licensee in Montgomery County
Must register online in advance as space is limited
Must join the online Zoom session by 10:15 AM or will not be admitted and will not receive letter of attendance
Recommended to sign in 10 minutes early (by 10:05 AM) to allow time for technical troubleshooting
Training complements but does not replace state-certified Alcohol Awareness training required by Maryland law for certain positions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Access the program webpage at https://www.montgomerycountymd.gov/ABS/education/training/index.html#Section1. 2. Locate the Zoom webinar registration link provided on the program page. 3. Register online through the Zoom link in your preferred language (English, Spanish, Amharic, Chinese, French, Korean, or Vietnamese). 4. Space is limited so early registration is recommended. 5. Training sessions are held monthly on the 2nd and 4th Monday of the month from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM (except holidays). 6. Join the Zoom session by 10:05-10:10 AM for setup; class begins promptly at 10:00 AM. 7. Attendees must join by 10:15 AM to receive a letter of attendance. 8. At end of class, a link will be provided to complete information form to receive your letter of attendance via email.

structured_extraction.program_name: Ad Valorem Tax Exemption for Parking Lot Districts
structured_extraction.program_description: Property owners or lessees in Montgomery County Parking Lot Districts can apply for an exemption from paying an annual Ad Valorem (property-value-based) tax if they meet minimum parking space requirements defined in the County Zoning Code. This tax normally funds shared public parking resources in Bethesda, Silver Spring, Wheaton, and Montgomery Hills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners or lessees who provide the minimum number of parking spaces as defined by Article 59-6 of the County Zoning Code can apply for exemption from paying the annual Ad Valorem tax on their property value. The tax is assessed by the County and funds the Parking Lot District program. Exemptions are available for properties that meet minimum on-site parking space requirements and are located within one of the four Parking Lot Districts. Under Chapter 60, applicants may also reduce parking requirements through alternative compliance plans or make payments in lieu of providing minimum parking spaces.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and lessees in Montgomery County Parking Lot Districts (Bethesda, Silver Spring, Wheaton, and Montgomery Hills)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from Ad Valorem tax payment for property owners who meet minimum on-site parking space requirements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applies only to properties located within one of the four Parking Lot Districts: Bethesda, Silver Spring, Wheaton, or Montgomery Hills in Montgomery County. The districts are defined by specific geographic boundaries in the Montgomery County Code Chapter 60.
requirements_list: Property owner or lessee must be located in a Parking Lot District (Bethesda, Silver Spring, Wheaton, or Montgomery Hills)
Must provide the minimum number of parking spaces as defined by Article 59-6 of the County Zoning Code
Application must be submitted on or before April 1 of the application year
Must submit a completed application form with cover sheet
Must submit a list of all tenants located on the property (including square footage of each)
Must submit a site plan of the complete property
Must submit detailed plans of all parking spaces
All required supplemental documents must be submitted with a fully executed application to qualify for review
Incomplete applications will be rejected in their entirety and cannot be resubmitted until the following fiscal year application deadline
Property may be used for various commercial, residential, or mixed-use purposes per zoning code requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a complete exemption request application on or before April 1 of the application year to the Department of Transportation, Division of Parking Management, Management Services & Property Development, 100 Edison Park Drive, 4th Floor, Gaithersburg, Maryland 20878. Applications must include: (1) completed cover sheet with property information and contact details, (2) completed application form with property details and use information, (3) list of all tenants with square footage, (4) site plan of complete property, and (5) detailed plans of all parking spaces. Applicants should indicate the appropriate Parking Lot District (Silver Spring, Bethesda, Wheaton, or Montgomery Hills) and provide information about the property usage from the provided usage categories. All required supplemental documents must accompany the fully executed application. Applications can be submitted via mail or fax to the Division of Parking Management.

structured_extraction.program_description: The ACCU helps Maryland Medicaid members understand and use their HealthChoice benefits. Each Administrative Care Coordinator (ACC) is a local contact who connects residents with the care and services they need. The program provides navigation assistance, benefits explanation, provider selection support, and ombudsman services to resolve complaints and coordinate care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free navigation and advocacy services for Medical Assistance/HealthChoice beneficiaries. Services include: explaining HealthChoice benefits and how to use them; explaining out-of-network services and services available without referral; helping choose or change a Managed Care Organization (MCO); helping find or change primary care providers or specialists; helping renew Medicaid benefits; finding dentists through Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental Program; updating information or replacing lost/stolen Medicaid cards; obtaining Medicaid transportation; fixing billing problems; getting prescriptions filled; explaining appeal and grievance rights. Ombudsman services address complex medical or care coordination issues and help resolve complaints about care or MCOs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents enrolled in Medical Assistance/HealthChoice, with special support for children, pregnant and postpartum women, individuals with physical, mental or developmental disabilities, and individuals experiencing homelessness
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Guidance on navigating the managed care system, selecting providers, accessing medical transportation and community resources, renewing benefits, finding dental care, obtaining prescriptions, and resolving health care disputes, complaints, and appeals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County. Contact the HealthChoice Help Line at 800-284-4510 or your local health department ACC or ombudsman program for services.

Must be enrolled in Medical Assistance/HealthChoice
