structured_extraction.program_description: Provides matching grant cost-share assistance to farmers and agricultural entrepreneurs for agricultural business projects that improve, expand, and increase the profitability of farming operations. Created through a partnership between the Montgomery County Office of Agriculture and the Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO), the program matches applicant investments up to specified limits.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grant cost-share assistance where MARBIDCO contributes up to $3,000 per project and the ACRE program matches up to an additional $3,000 per project (maximum $6,000 combined from both sources), with an additional $1,000 available for projects totaling more than $14,000. Farmer or agricultural entrepreneur must invest at least half of the total project cost. Maximum lifetime limit of $15,000 in MARBIDCO funding per agricultural enterprise. Maximum $25,000 in total grants awarded to Montgomery County per fiscal year. Funding is a reimbursement program requiring original receipts as proof of payment. Agricultural enterprises may apply up to twice per fiscal year for different projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified Montgomery County-based agricultural entrepreneurs, including table crop farmers, vineyards, commodity farmers, vertical farmers, horticulture businesses, and other non-traditional types of agriculture. Both new and existing agricultural enterprises are eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible uses include infrastructure improvements such as deer fencing, agricultural wells, vertical racks for microgreens, farm equipment and tools, hydroponics equipment, aquaponics equipment, refrigeration, greenhouses, irrigation systems, composting equipment, farm mechanization equipment, and other agricultural infrastructure improvements that contribute to startup or expansion of an agricultural enterprise.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to agricultural enterprises headquartered in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a registered agricultural business in good standing with the MD Department of Assessment and Taxation
Agricultural enterprise must be headquartered in Montgomery County
Farmer or agricultural operator must pay at least half of the total project cost
Applicant must apply and receive approval from both the Montgomery County Office of Agriculture and MARBIDCO before making any purchases or beginning any phase of the project
Maximum $15,000 lifetime per agricultural enterprise (MARBIDCO funding)
Maximum $25,000 total for all Montgomery County projects per fiscal year
May apply up to twice per fiscal year for different projects

Project must enhance the agricultural economy by contributing to startup or expansion of an agricultural enterprise, or be associated with infrastructure improvement or equipment purchase that will enable future revenue and/or employment growth
Applicant must provide original receipts (proof of payment) as condition of receiving reimbursement funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Interested agricultural enterprises submit an application to Montgomery County Office of Agriculture (OAG) providing project information including applicant contact information, project description, type of project, total project cost, estimated employment data, and written proposal for total project cost. Step 2: OAG reviews the application to determine if it fits within MARBIDCO's economic development profile and project criteria. If approved at this stage, OAG submits the application with a cover letter to MARBIDCO for consideration. Step 3: MARBIDCO Review Committee reviews and approves the project. Applicant is notified and may begin the project; OAG and MARBIDCO enter into an agreement to provide cost-shared grant funding for the specified project. Step 4: Upon project completion, applicant notifies OAG and provides paid receipts showing total project cost has been paid in full. Agreed upon grant amount is reimbursed to applicant. ACRE projects are approved at the sole discretion of the OAG. Award recipients must provide information related to project outcomes, including increased revenue amounts and number of additional full-time and part-time employees.

structured_extraction.program_description: A farmland preservation initiative administered by Montgomery County that permanently extinguishes residential development rights—including associated septic capacity—by purchasing easements that retire approved on-site waste disposal systems and eliminate the development potential of individual lots. The program protects Montgomery County's Agricultural Reserve, reduces land fragmentation, and prevents future commercial, residential, or industrial development. The County may purchase BLT easements directly, or BLTs may be sold by landowners to developers for use in designated receiving areas. Because the landowner has already proven the lot is capable of supporting a residence, the price paid for a BLT easement is typically higher than that of a Transfer of Development Rights (TDR).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases BLT easements that permanently retire an approved on-site waste disposal system associated with a lot, eliminating the development potential of individual lots while allowing continued agricultural use. Easement values are determined annually on July 1st by the County Executive based on recent prices paid for agricultural easements, TDR prices, and fair market value prices for agricultural land. Because the landowner has already proven the lot is capable of supporting a residence, the price paid for eliminating the potential lot through a BLT easement is higher than that of a TDR. The County calculates offers using the BLT Valuation Formula with a Base Value (minimum price set annually), Added Value (based on property characteristics), and Maximum Value (highest price allowed). Offers cannot exceed the Maximum Value. Landowners must have a sewage disposal area(s) approved on a final well and septic plan and obtain a Well and Septic Approval Letter from the Department of Permitting Services. The County's ability to purchase BLT Easements is subject to available funding; if funds are insufficient, some eligible applications may not be accepted during a purchase period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Montgomery County with property in the Agricultural Reserve who have approved on-site waste disposal systems and intend to permanently preserve farmland by eliminating the development potential of individual lots.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to purchase BLT easements that permanently retire approved on-site waste disposal systems and eliminate the development potential of lots, protecting agricultural land from future commercial, residential, or industrial development while allowing continued agricultural use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in the Agricultural Reserve (AR Zone) in Montgomery County, Maryland, and must lie outside water and sewer categories 1, 2, and 3.
requirements_list: Property must be in the Agricultural Reserve (AR Zone)
Minimum 50 acres (smaller properties may be considered if contiguous to other lands protected by State/County agricultural and conservation easements)
At least 50% of land must be USDA Soil Classes I–III or Woodland Classifications 1 and 2
Must be outside water/sewer categories 1, 2, and 3
Must have a sewage disposal area(s) approved on a final well and septic plan
Must obtain a Well and Septic Approval Letter from the Department of Permitting Services (DPS) by emailing Heidi.Benham@montgomerycountymd.gov
Land must not be encumbered by Federal/State/County agricultural or conservation easements (except land protected by TDR Easements may still be eligible)

Land must be able to achieve a percolation rate sufficient to support an individual on-site waste disposal system as evidenced by septic system site plan approved by the Department of Permitting Services
Any TDRs retained with a parcel above the threshold of 1 TDR per 25 acres must be created/severed from the land prior to or simultaneously with settlement of the BLT easement
Applications must include the Well and Septic Approval Letter before they are reviewed
Total number of approved septic areas and number of approved septic areas planned for termination must be clearly identified
Properties with existing TDR easements must disclose how many TDRs remain
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners must submit a completed BLT Easement Application Form with all required documentation by February 13, 2026. All applicants must obtain a Well and Septic Approval Letter from the Department of Permitting Services (DPS) by emailing Heidi.Benham@montgomerycountymd.gov, even if they already have prior septic approval, to verify the number and locations of approved septic areas before proceeding. Applications should be submitted by email to Mike Weyand at Michael.Weyand@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov. Required documentation includes copy of property deed(s), property map(s), survey or plat if available, approved Well and Septic Plan, and disclosure of any existing encumbrances or easements. The Office of Agriculture reviews applications for completeness and eligibility (March-April). Eligible applications are forwarded to the Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board (APAB) for ranking using the BLT Ranking Formula based on size (up to 5 points), soil quality (up to 10 points), land tenure (up to 5 points for active farming or long-term lease), and additional factors such as proximity to preserved land or subdivision approvals. The County Executive determines the Base Value and Maximum Easement Value for the BLT Ranking Formula annually on July 1st. The County and Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board prioritize multiple properties to achieve program objectives (May-July). Formal offers are made to selected landowners. Title searches and legal documentation are completed, and easements are recorded in land records with payments issued (August-November). Properties are monitored at least biannually for compliance. Landowners without an updated Soil Conservation Plan must implement one within one year of settlement. Participation in the BLT Program is voluntary, and acceptance is not guaranteed. If an applicant rejects the County's offer, they cannot reapply for 24 months.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides subsidized taxi trips for low-income older adults aged 65 and older and low-income individuals with disabilities aged 18 to 64 who are Montgomery County residents. The program helps participants get to medical and personal appointments via a subsidized taxi service, with fees determined on a sliding scale based on total household income. Participants with current MetroAccess identification cards may also benefit from the Same Day Access Program, which provides a $60.00 value on their Call-n-Ride swipe card when they pay $30.00, with no income requirement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subsidy assistance is provided on a sliding fee scale determined by total household income. For a household of one with yearly income up to $15,856, the monthly cost per $60 value is $5.25. For income $15,857–$21,403, the cost is $10.00. For income $21,404–$26,951, the cost is $20.00. For income $26,952–$39,000, the cost is $30.00. Participants with current MetroAccess identification cards can receive a Same Day Access Program benefit of $60.00 value on their Call-n-Ride swipe card when they pay $30.00, with no income requirement. Participants add money to their Call-n-Ride swipe card account in monthly increments (choice of $60 or $120 subsidy value). Payments may be made by check or money order mailed to Montgomery County Maryland, P.O. Box 824871, Philadelphia, PA 19182-4871, or via credit card online. Allow 5-7 business days for payment processing. Participants can schedule unlimited trips by calling participating taxicab companies. Taxi fares are charged at meter rates set by Montgomery County Division of Transit Services with initial charge of $4.00, $2.00 per mile, $28.00/hour traffic delay time, and additional fees for extra passengers ($1.00) or personal loading service ($1.00). The maximum trip limit for each one-way trip is $60.00 including tip. Trips to approved medical facilities in Designated Service Areas (Baltimore, Prince George's County, Northern Virginia, and Washington DC) require pre-authorization if fare exceeds $60.00. Money placed on the CNR swipe card never expires. Maximum accumulated balance that can be carried on card is $360.00. Remaining monthly balance rolls over to the following month. There is a $5.00 replacement fee for lost, stolen, or damaged cards.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income older adults at least 65 years of age, or low-income individuals 18 to 64 years of age with a disability, who are Montgomery County residents. Also open to MetroAccess cardholders (with no income requirement) under the Same Day Access Program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subsidized transportation via taxi to medical and personal appointments within Montgomery County or to approved medical facilities in Designated Service Areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County. Special exceptions have been made to allow transportation to approved medical facilities in Designated Service Areas located in Baltimore, Prince George's County, Northern Virginia, and Washington DC. A complete list of approved medical facilities is available in the Designated Service Areas (DSA) List.
requirements_list: Must be at least 65 years of age (for seniors) or 18 to 64 years of age with a disability (for persons with disabilities)
Must be low-income as determined by total household income
Must be a Montgomery County resident (proof of current residence required within last six months)
Must complete application and provide proof of eligibility and relevant supporting documentation
Must register as a participant
For Same Day Access Program: must have a current MetroAccess identification card (no income requirement applies)
Applicants ages 18-64 claiming disability must have disability certification completed by a licensed physician, physician's assistant, certified registered nurse practitioner, or psychologist
All participants are required to re-certify every two years to remain in program
Proof of age required (Maryland Driver's License, Birth Certificate, Social Security Statement, Permanent Resident Card, Passport, or other government-issued identification)

Proof of household income required from all adult household members (Social Security checks/stubs/award letters, pension letters, annuity statements, IRA distributions, paystubs, bank statements, or tax returns)
Recent wallet-size photograph recommended but not required for swipe card
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 301-948-5409 Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. to inquire about applying for program participation and request application materials. Alternatively, contact Connect-A-Ride Transportation Resource Center at 301-738-3252 or email ConnectARide@AccessJCA.org. Complete the CNR Application Form (including all sections clearly and legibly) and submit with required supporting documents. For applicants ages 18-64 claiming disability, request and submit a CNR Disability Certification Form completed by a licensed physician, PA, CNRP, or psychologist. Proof required includes: (1) Montgomery County residence (utility bill, mortgage statement, lease agreement, property tax bill, or Social Security statement - documents must be current/within last six months); (2) Age (government-issued ID or birth certificate); (3) All household income sources (pay stubs, benefit statements, tax returns, bank statements, or certification forms for zero income or support from others). Submit documentation by fax (240-556-0999), email (cnrorder@montgomerycountymd.gov), or mail/hand-deliver to: Call-n-Ride, 101 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850. Upon approval, register as participant and add money to CNR swipe card account online at www.eztransport.net/mococnr/members or through the mail. Begin using the program by calling participating taxicab company dispatchers to schedule trips.

structured_extraction.program_name: Certified Agricultural Producers Energy Tax Relief Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax relief program for qualified agricultural producers in Montgomery County that allows them to pay the county's energy tax at a lower residential rate instead of the industrial rate, reducing their fuel, propane, and electricity costs. The program is available to those engaged in the production of livestock, horses, poultry, field crops, nursery stock, bulbs, flowers, or other agricultural commodities in Montgomery County, including equestrian facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified agricultural producers pay the county's fuel and energy tax at the lower residential rate rather than the industrial rate. Eligible energy sources include: dyed diesel fuel delivered to the farm for off-road use, liquid petroleum (LP) gas delivered to the farm for non-residential use, and electricity used for agricultural purposes that is metered separately from residential meters. To qualify, applicants must be enrolled in at least one of the following: Montgomery Soil Conservation District, Maryland Nutrient Management Program, USDA Farm Service Agency, Montgomery County Extension, Montgomery County Farmers Market, Maryland Department of Agriculture Certified Organic Growers, or farmland preservation programs (AEP, MALPF, BLT, RLP, or MET). Applicants may also qualify through individual consideration if they operate a bona fide farming operation not falling into these categories. The certification provides a lower tax rate per kilowatt-hour or per unit of fuel, which does not affect the base utility rate charged by the power company.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers operating in Montgomery County who are engaged in the production of livestock, horses, poultry, field crops, nursery stock, bulbs, flowers, or other agricultural products, including equestrian facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces energy costs by lowering the tax rate on fuel, propane, and electricity used for agricultural purposes. Savings apply to dyed diesel fuel for off-road use, LP gas for non-residential use, and separately metered electricity for agricultural operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County only. Applicants must own agricultural property in the county or be tenant farmers. Energy must be delivered to and used on the farm as part of the agricultural operation.
requirements_list: Must be engaged in the business of agriculture in the production of an agricultural commodity in Montgomery County
Must own property assessed as agricultural in Montgomery County or be a tenant farmer

Must be enrolled in at least one of the following programs or services: Montgomery Soil Conservation District, Maryland Nutrient Management Program, USDA Farm Service Agency, Montgomery County Extension, Montgomery County Farmers Market, Maryland Department of Agriculture Certified Organic Growers, or farmland preservation programs (AEP, MALPF, BLT, RLP, or MET)
May qualify for individual consideration if operating a bona fide farming operation not falling into the above categories
Applicant's eligibility must be verified by the Department of Finance
For electricity: meter must be separate from residential meter and used for agricultural purposes
For fuel: must be dyed diesel fuel for off-road use or LP gas for non-residential use
Enrollment records are updated biannually
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Department of Economic Development mails a one-page application to owners of agriculturally assessed property and provides an opportunity for non-landowner producers (such as tenant farmers) to apply. Applicants must indicate at least one agricultural program or service they are enrolled in. The Department of Finance verifies eligibility based on enrollment in specified agricultural programs and services. Once approved, applicants receive Certification as an Agricultural Producer with a Certification Number, and this certification is transmitted to fuel and energy suppliers in the county. Applicants should contact their fuel-energy suppliers to inform them of certification status and provide the Certification Number. To verify correct tax rates are being charged, applicants should review monthly billing statements and divide the Montgomery County Tax Amount by the actual usage to calculate the tax rate, then compare to the residential rate specified in the County Code resolution. If incorrectly charged, contact the utility company with the Certification Letter and resolution to request a credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: A guidance service provided by a Child Care Business Counselor who helps entrepreneurs navigate the process of opening and operating a home or center-based child care program in Montgomery County. structured_extraction.program_description: Free onsite consultation, teacher coaching, classroom modeling, and reflection services for early childhood educators. Services include infant and early childhood mental health consultations, early childhood coaching, and health consultation from a registered nurse to support the social and emotional development of young children and improve teaching practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free onsite coaching and consultation services provided by trained consultants and coaches. Services include one-on-one coaching, strength-based assessments, action planning, classroom modeling, reflection and discussion of strategies, and resource identification and referrals. A registered nurse is available for health and safety consultation, observation, training, and referrals.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free or low-cost training opportunities for early childhood workers to advance their skills and knowledge. Offers MSDE approved Core of Knowledge classes in multiple languages and formats, guidance on career pathways, and financial support for credentials and higher education.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Child Care in Public Space (CCIPS) program oversees dedicated child care spaces in public facilities across Montgomery County to expand affordable and quality child care in underserved communities. The program provides licensed child care center space—including ground-level and modular centers with classrooms, offices, kitchens, storage, and outdoor play areas—available for qualified child care operators to lease and operate. County-subsidized programs are required to meet high-quality standards including accreditation and Maryland EXCELS levels 3-5, and receive ongoing support through monitoring to maintain quality benchmarks. Spaces are awarded through a competitive bid/application process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County provides subsidized and licensed child care facility space on a lease basis in public facilities across Montgomery County. Two specific locations include: the UpCounty Regional Services Center (12900 Middlebrook Road, Germantown, MD), offering approximately 2,400 square feet of classroom space licensed for 68 children; and the Shady Grove Life Sciences Center (14910 Broschart Road, Rockville, MD), offering approximately 3,500 square feet (1,900 square feet usable classroom space) licensed for 42 children. Lease terms include a seven-year initial term with one four-year renewal option and one three-year renewal option. The county rental rate is $11.35 per square foot per year and includes utilities (except phone and internet), janitorial services, building and grounds maintenance, snow and trash removal, and pest control. In total, 29 dedicated child care spaces are available across county public facilities. Providers receive continual support through the monitoring process to ensure continued achievement of quality benchmarks. Programs must operate at least 6:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday-Friday, year-round. All directors and teachers working directly with children must complete 12 hours of OCC approved training annually. Assistant teachers and aides must complete 6 hours annually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care operators, providers, and organizations seeking to operate licensed child care centers in Montgomery County public facilities, particularly those serving underserved communities including infants, toddlers, preschoolers, and before- and after-school age children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lease of county-owned child care facility space to operate licensed child care programs, including operating subsidized child care spaces in public facilities. Programs must achieve accreditation and Maryland EXCELS levels 3-5, and serve infants, toddlers, preschoolers, and before- and after-school age children. Facilities can accommodate part-time and occasional care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, with priority for underserved communities. Specific facility locations include UpCounty Regional Services Center at 12900 Middlebrook Road, Germantown, MD and Shady Grove Life Sciences Center at 14910 Broschart Road, Rockville, MD.
requirements_list: Must meet high-quality standards including accreditation
Must reach Maryland EXCELS levels 3-5
Must operate through competitive bid/application process
Must maintain quality benchmarks throughout operation
Must be licensed by State and County agencies and maintain compliance with all applicable rules and regulations
Applicants must complete a full application (Parts A through J with attachments)
Applicants must submit two complete copies of the application in a spiral or notebook bound format no larger than a 1-inch binder
Applications must be submitted by mail or dropped off in person by the deadline
Applications must include all required components to be considered
Applicants scoring 85 or above out of 110 on Parts A-F will advance to external committee review
Applicants scoring 110 or above out of 140 will be invited for interviews

Applicants must be able to demonstrate how their program will meet Maryland State Department of Education Prekindergarten Expansion Quality Benchmarks and Programmatic Plan Requirements (for UpCounty location)
Final capacity determination is made by the Maryland State Department of Education Office of Child Care
All pages of application must be numbered
Must provide three signed current letters of professional reference, including at least one from a parent-client
Must achieve NAEYC or MSDE accreditation within three years and maintain accreditation at all times
Must enroll in MD EXCELS and publish at Level 3 or higher
All directors and teachers working directly with children must complete 12 hours of OCC approved training annually
Assistant teachers and aides must complete 6 hours of OCC approved training annually

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants attend a pre-application meeting and facility tours. Applicants then prepare and submit two complete application copies (Parts A-J with attachments) bound in a spiral or notebook format no larger than a 1-inch binder with all pages clearly labeled, sequenced, and numbered by the deadline. The program manager reviews applications for completeness. Complete applications are scored by an internal Early Childhood Services committee on Parts A-F (maximum 110 points). Applications scoring 85 or above out of 110 advance to an external selection committee comprised of county personnel, Montgomery County Public Schools staff, parents, and community representatives. The external committee scores the full application on Parts A-J (maximum 140 points) and interviews top-scoring applicants (those scoring 110 or above out of 140). The external committee makes a final recommendation based on application score, interview score, and other relevant information. Selected applicants are notified and unsuccessful applicants are informed of the decision. Contact Tamieka Thomasson at tamieka.thomasson@montgomerycountymd.gov or 240-777-1732 for more information or to schedule a pre-application meeting and facility tour.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that invests in Montgomery County's young people by allocating funds into interest-bearing accounts based on the number of babies born each year. Once a child turns 18 years old and is a resident of the county, they become eligible to withdraw funds to support vocational or educational expenses, investment in a business in the county, purchasing property in the county, or retirement investments. Payments are made progressively based on wealth and income at the time of application.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual allocation of $1,800 per child expected to be born that year, subject to appropriation. Funds grow in an interest-bearing account over time. Eligible residents age 18 and older (up to age 36) who are Montgomery County residents can withdraw funds for vocational or educational expenses, business investment in the county, property purchases in the county, or retirement investments. Payments are made progressively based on wealth and income at the time of application, with distribution criteria to be outlined by the Child Investment Fund Committee to ensure adults with the least amount of personal wealth benefit most from the fund.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Will Jawando, Councilmember; Gabe Albornoz, Councilmember
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who were born in the county on or after January 1, 2024 and turn 18 years old.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vocational or educational expenses, investment in a business in the county, purchasing property in the county, or retirement investments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Applicants must be born in Montgomery County on or after January 1, 2024 and must be residents of Montgomery County at the time of withdrawal. Applicants may apply for funds once they turn 18 years old, up to age 36.
requirements_list: Must be born in Montgomery County on or after January 1, 2024
Must be 18 years old or older (up to age 36) to withdraw funds
Must be a resident of Montgomery County at time of withdrawal
Eligibility for fund disbursement is based on the applicant's income and wealth at the time of application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible individuals born in Montgomery County on or after January 1, 2024 can apply for funds once they turn 18 years old. Applications will be evaluated based on wealth and income criteria at the time of application, with progressive payments designed to benefit those with the least amount of personal wealth. The Child Investment Fund Advisory Committee will oversee the fund and outline specific disbursement criteria.

A Care Coordinator works with families to coordinate care and locate services, including specialists at Children's Hospital in Washington D.C. when needed.

Child must not qualify for any other health insurance or have insurance that does not meet the child's special medical needs

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Water Montgomery Watershed Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program funded through Montgomery County's Water Quality Protection Charge that supports public outreach, stewardship, and community-based restoration projects aimed at reducing pollutants and improving water quality in Montgomery County's local streams and waterways. Eligible projects include tree planting, rain gardens, trash cleanup, litter reduction in the Anacostia watershed, water quality monitoring, and public education initiatives that engage residents in watershed improvement and achieve measurable water quality impacts and sustainable behavior change. The program is administered in partnership with the Chesapeake Bay Trust and targets community groups, nonprofits, and faith-based organizations operating in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grant awards funded through the County's Water Quality Protection Charge. Award amounts are set each year based on available funds, with individual grants of up to $100,000 available. Match is encouraged but not required; preference is given to projects with match and/or in-kind services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Typically, the fall of each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations such as local watershed groups, community associations, service and civic groups, faith-based organizations, and community groups operating in Montgomery County, Maryland, with at least one partner representing a stakeholder group based in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public outreach and stewardship projects, community-based restoration water quality implementation projects, tree planting, rain gardens, trash cleanup, litter reduction in the Anacostia watershed and countywide, water quality monitoring projects, and public education initiatives that educate and engage residents in watershed improvement while achieving measurable water quality impacts and sustainable behavior change.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Applicants must include at least one partner that represents a stakeholder group based in Montgomery County, Maryland.

Applicant must include at least one partner representing a stakeholder group based in Montgomery County, Maryland
Projects should educate and engage residents in watershed improvement
Projects should achieve measurable impacts and sustainable behavior change
Match is encouraged but not required; preference given to projects with match and/or in-kind services

Applicants should visit the Chesapeake Bay Trust website for application details, to submit their proposal, and for any questions regarding the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides free colorectal cancer screenings including colonoscopy and follow-up care to eligible Montgomery County residents. It includes care coordination, links to further diagnosis and treatment if needed, and health education about cancer awareness and the importance of screenings.

The program covers the cost of screening services, care coordination, referrals to further diagnosis and treatment if needed, and patient navigation services. All services and materials are provided at no cost to eligible applicants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Uninsured or under-insured Montgomery County residents age 45 and older with family income no higher than 250% of federal poverty guidelines and no current diagnosis of colorectal cancer.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Colorectal cancer screenings via colonoscopy, follow-up care, care coordination, patient navigation services, and referrals to diagnosis and treatment services. The program provides free screening, case management, and assistance accessing additional medical care if needed.

A nurse case manager will follow up if needed to explain results and provide instructions and assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax deduction program significantly expanded starting January 1, 2023, that allows businesses to deduct energy efficiency expenditures for commercial buildings. The deduction has increased from $1.80 per square foot to a sliding scale of $2.50 to $5.00 per square foot, with a new pathway for existing building retrofits to access the deduction.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal tax deduction of $2.50 to $5.00 per square foot for commercial building energy efficiency improvements. New construction must achieve 25% to 50% savings relative to the most recent ASHRAE 90.1 standard. Retrofits must demonstrate 25% to 50% improvement over existing building performance measured by Energy Use Intensity (EUI). The deduction can be taken on a specific commercial building every 3 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and commercial property owners who have made energy efficiency construction expenditures
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax deduction for energy efficiency expenditures in commercial buildings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide

Retrofits must demonstrate 25% to 50% improvement over existing building performance (EUI)
Deduction can be taken on specific commercial building every 3 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Taxpayer reports the deduction on their federal income tax return. Consult with tax professional for specific filing requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) is an innovative financing program that allows qualified commercial property owners to receive lower-cost, long-term flexible financing for building upgrades. Funding can cover up to 100 percent of eligible property improvements and is repaid as a surcharge on the property tax bill for up to 20 years.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Long-term, flexible financing for up to 100 percent of eligible property improvements. Loan terms extend up to 20 years and are repaid as a surcharge added to the property tax bill. The financing is lower-cost compared to traditional commercial loans. Starting in 2024, the Montgomery County Green Bank became a small C-PACE capital provider to help stimulate the market and close gaps for smaller-sized transactions of $2.5 million or less. Financing can support energy efficiency measures such as LED lighting upgrades, heat pumps, insulation, window replacements, renewable energy systems including solar photovoltaic (PV) systems, climate resilience upgrades, water conservation improvements, and environmental health and safety upgrades. Projects completed within the last 12 months are eligible for retroactive financing.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Nancy Feldman, Chief, Division of Fiscal Management; Lindsey Robinett Shaw, Section Chief, Buildings and Transportation Programs
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified commercial property owners in Montgomery County, including for-profit businesses and nonprofits (including faith-based organizations), seeking to finance energy efficiency, renewable energy, climate resiliency, water conservation, and environmental health and safety building upgrades. The program also targets minority-owned businesses and properties in Low Income/Disadvantaged Communities (LIDAC) and Equity Emphasis Areas (EEA).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements, renewable energy improvements, climate resiliency and climate adaptation upgrades, water conservation improvements, and environmental health and safety upgrades. Funds can be used for planned renovations, completed renovations that occurred within the last 12 months, and new construction projects. Eligible measures include LED lighting upgrades, heat pump installations, building insulation, window replacements, solar photovoltaic systems, and other clean energy and resilience measures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. The C-PACE financing program applies only to commercial properties, not residential properties.
requirements_list: Property must be a qualified commercial property in Montgomery County
Property owner must be ready to undertake or have undertaken eligible improvements
Improvements must be eligible: energy efficiency, renewable energy, climate resiliency, climate adaptation, water conservation, or environmental health and safety upgrades
For existing buildings, renovations must be planned or completed within the last 12 months
Project must demonstrate measurable energy savings, cost savings, environmental benefits, or climate resilience improvements
Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS) compliance may drive additional financing interest as standards establish energy performance targets for existing buildings
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Building owners interested in the C-PACE program should contact the Montgomery County Green Bank at mcgreenbank.org/mc-pacer/ or MCGreenBank.org to learn more about getting started. The Green Bank provides technical assistance, conducts one-on-one consultations, and works with property owners to assess eligibility and project readiness. The Green Bank coordinates with capital providers, lenders, developers, and energy service contractors throughout the application and financing process. Technical assistance is available to help property owners assess their properties and identify C-PACE-eligible building upgrades. The Green Bank has established relationships with multiple C-PACE lenders and capital providers to facilitate financing. For application forms and guidance documents, building owners should visit the Montgomery County Green Bank website.

The program runs October through May and includes monthly workshops on topics such as working with elected officials, storytelling, research, developing testimony, and key advocacy issues in the county. The program is bilingual in English and Spanish.

The program is bilingual in English and Spanish and is designed for economically-disadvantaged residents with modest household incomes.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicaid program that provides supports planning (case management) and community-based services to enable older adults and individuals with disabilities to live independently in their own homes in the community. The program offers enhanced home-based services to Maryland residents who receive Community Medicaid benefits and meet an institutional level of care based on their need for assistance with activities of daily living. Available statewide, with specific implementation in Montgomery County and Prince George's County, the program encompasses multiple related programs including Community Personal Assistance Services (CPAS) and Increased Community Services (ICS).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides Medicaid-funded personal assistance services with activities of daily living (bathing, grooming, dressing, mobility, meal preparation, and light chores); supports planning (case management) to help participants plan for their needs and access appropriate services; nurse monitoring of health and well-being; personal emergency response systems; assistive technology; environmental assessments; accessibility adaptations; consumer training; transition services; home delivered meals; and medical day care. Services are funded through Medicaid and vary based on assessed need. Participants choose an approved Supports Planning Agency to guide them through service planning.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults and individuals with disabilities who qualify for community Medicaid or a Medicaid waiver and need help with activities of daily living, and who wish to live independently in their own homes and communities rather than in an institution
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal assistance services with activities of daily living (bathing, grooming, dressing, mobility, meal preparation, light chores); supports planning (case management); nurse monitoring; personal emergency response systems; assistive technology; environmental assessments; accessibility adaptations; consumer training; transition services; home delivered meals; and medical day care
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; must reside in the community (not in an institution). Specific county programs available in Montgomery County and Prince George's County.
requirements_list: Must reside in the community (not in an institution)
Must qualify for community Medicaid or a Medicaid waiver
Must meet the level of care required for services in an institution (institutional level of care criteria)
Must need help with activities of daily living such as bathing, grooming and dressing
Must meet the program's medical level of care
Must meet both medical and financial criteria for community Medicaid eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Aging and Disability Resource Unit (ADRU) at 240-777-3000 (Montgomery County), 410-767-1739 (state), or 301-265-8450 (Prince George's County) to apply. Eligibility is determined based on both financial and medical requirements. Participants choose an approved Supports Planning Agency to guide them through service planning.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to 501(c)(3) nonprofit food assistance provider organizations in Montgomery County to support the purchase and distribution of shelf-stable food, fresh food, and prepared meals to residents experiencing food insecurity. Eligible organizations must deliver regularly scheduled, no-cost food services at county-based sites at least once per month for a minimum of one year. The program also funds food recovery operations — including the recovery, handling, and redistribution of surplus food — and prioritizes under-resourced ZIP codes, home delivery models, services to immigrant and unhoused residents, and high-performing returning grantees. Awards may be issued as direct cash grants or as credits through bulk-food purchasing partnerships with organizations such as Manna Food Center and the Capital Area Food Bank.
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to food assistance provider organizations and food recovery organizations. In FY25, $3,699,500 was awarded across 49 organizations — either as direct cash grants to purchase food from wholesale or retail outlets, or as credits to order produce, shelf-stable products, and other nutritious food items through bulk-food purchasing partnerships. In FY26, $3.5 million was awarded to 56 active organizations for community-based food distribution, and an additional $428,202 was awarded to six organizations for food recovery services ($290,785 in renewable CFA funding and $137,417 through a Special Appropriation). A Special Appropriation also distributed approximately $1.9 million in expanded grants to 53 nonprofit providers, prioritizing under-resourced ZIP codes, home delivery models, services to immigrant and unhoused residents, and food recovery operations. Recipients of food recovery funding are expected to recover and redistribute more than 10 million pounds of food annually. Grant awards range from under $20,000 to over $100,001. Grantees are required to submit monthly service data reports (12 total) and quarterly narrative and financial reports (4 total) through the OFSR online reporting platform. Reporting requirements vary by award amount and include metrics such as number of households served, food types and quantities distributed, financial expenditures, and for larger awards, demographic breakdowns by household size and age, local sourcing information, and in-kind resource valuations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Launching July 2025 (community-based food distribution); Coming fall 2026 (food recovery)
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit food assistance provider organizations and food recovery organizations serving Montgomery County residents experiencing food insecurity, including organizations providing home delivery, services to immigrant and unhoused residents, and surplus food recovery and redistribution
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and distribution of shelf-stable food, fresh food, and prepared meals to Montgomery County residents on a monthly or more frequent basis; food recovery operational costs including sourcing, handling, storage, and redistribution of surplus food; services to immigrant and unhoused residents; and home delivery food assistance models
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland; services must be provided at county-based sites throughout ZIP codes in the County, with priority given to under-resourced ZIP codes
requirements_list: Applicant must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization

Organization must provide regular food distribution or food recovery services

Grant recipients must submit quarterly narrative and financial reports (4 total) throughout the grant performance period
Reports must be submitted through the OFSR online reporting platform by the 30th or end of the month following the end of each quarter
Grantees must track receipts, proof-of-payment, and other relevant proof of program costs incurred
Grantees must distribute a satisfaction survey to participants on a once-annual basis (minimum)
Grantees must demonstrate in performance reports how they are adapting services to address participant feedback
Reporting requirements vary based on award amount, ranging from basic household counts for awards $20,000 or less to detailed demographic and sourcing data for awards over $100,001
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit applications for funding through the county grants portal; awards are announced for project implementation. The FY26 community-based food distribution application is launching July 2025 and the food recovery application is coming fall 2026. Successful applicants will be required to submit monthly service data reports and quarterly narrative and financial reports through the OFSR online reporting platform following the established reporting schedule.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training covers ethics, roles and responsibilities of board members and homeowners, governing documents, financial management, meeting rules, and general administration of common ownership communities.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County provides hot meals at lunchtime to seniors ages 60 and over at 13 senior program locations around the county. The program is funded under the Older Americans Act and promotes better health through improved nutrition while reducing isolation through socialization. A voluntary donation is requested for seniors ages 60 and over; for those under 60, the full price of the meal is required. Advanced registration is required at least one week in advance. Most locations offer meals five days a week, with some locations offering meals on select days. Some centers also offer a stand-by or waiting list for individuals who wish to have a meal at the last minute if extra meals are available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hot meals provided at lunchtime at 13 participating senior program locations throughout Montgomery County (Benjamin Gaither Center, Damascus Community Center, East County Community Center, Germantown Community Center, Holiday Park Senior Center, Long Branch Community Center, Margaret Schweinhaut Senior Center, Montgomery Village Foundation at Stedwick Community Center, North Potomac Community Center, Rockville Senior Center, Silver Spring Recreation & Aquatic Center, Wheaton Community Center, and White Oak Community Center). Most locations serve meals Monday through Friday at 12:00 PM, with some variation in days and times. Meals include hot, cold, and vegetarian options. All meals are served with milk or yogurt and 100% fruit juice. For seniors ages 60 and over, a voluntary donation is requested (recommended $3 per meal, but smaller donations are accepted). For those under 60, the full price of the meal is required. Donations may be made in cash, check, or credit card. Advanced registration is required at least one week in advance so staff can determine the number of meals to order. Some centers also offer a stand-by or waiting list for individuals who wish to have a meal at the last minute if extra meals are available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors ages 60 and over in Montgomery County (donation requested), spouses of any age of registered participants age 60+, SNP volunteers of any age for two hours per month, persons with disabilities under age 60 living with a parent or grandparent who is a registered participant, persons with disabilities under age 60 living in a building where a nutrition site is located, and those under 60 who can pay the full meal price, served at 13 senior program locations around Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hot meal nutrition at participating senior centers and recreation facilities at lunchtime. Meals provide balanced nutrition supporting better health and independence for older adults.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at 13 senior program locations throughout Montgomery County: Benjamin Gaither Center (Gaithersburg), Damascus Community Center (Damascus), East County Community Center (Silver Spring), Germantown Community Center (Germantown), Holiday Park Senior Center (Wheaton), Long Branch Community Center (Silver Spring), Margaret Schweinhaut Senior Center (Silver Spring), Montgomery Village Foundation at Stedwick Community Center (Montgomery Village), North Potomac Community Center (Rockville), Rockville Senior Center (Rockville), Silver Spring Recreation & Aquatic Center (Silver Spring), Wheaton Community Center (Silver Spring), and White Oak Community Center (Silver Spring).
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or older, OR spouse (any age) of registered 60+ participant, OR SNP volunteer (any age) contributing at least two hours per month, OR person with disabilities under 60 living with registered parent/grandparent participant, OR person with disabilities under 60 living in building where nutrition site is located
Must complete SNP registration form annually (available in multiple languages: Chinese, English, French, Korean, Spanish, Vietnamese)
Must receive SNP meal card for meal transactions
Must call or contact the nutrition site manager at least one week in advance to reserve a meal
Must provide reservation by deadline: Wednesday for Monday meals, Thursday for Tuesday meals, Friday for Wednesday meals, Monday for Thursday meals, Tuesday for Friday meals (all by 10:00 AM)
For seniors 60+: voluntary donation requested (recommended $3 per meal)
For those under 60: full price of the meal required
Must cancel meals within notice period; cancellations on day of meal are considered no-shows
May only reserve one meal type of choice per reservation
May reserve a single meal at only one location per day

Must follow SNP rules and regulations including courteous behavior, no bullying or harassment, no removal of perishable food from dining areas, compliance with meal ordering and cancellation timelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To register: Complete the SNP registration form (available in multiple languages) and submit to the Nutrition Site Manager at your preferred meal location. The registration form must be completed annually. You will receive an SNP meal card to be used for each meal transaction. The SNP meal card can be used at any meal location in Montgomery County. To reserve meals: Fill out a monthly reservation menu indicating your meal choice (hot, cold, or vegetarian option) and submit to the Nutrition Site Manager at your preferred location. Reservations must be made by the deadline at 10:00 AM (Wednesday for Monday meals, Thursday for Tuesday meals, Friday for Wednesday meals, Monday for Thursday meals, Tuesday for Friday meals). Menus are available from the Nutrition Site Manager or on the Recreation Department's Senior Programs website. Monthly menus are available in Chinese, English, French, Korean, Spanish, or Vietnamese. To cancel: Contact the Nutrition Site Manager at your location's phone number or email. Cancellations should be made within the notice period when possible. Stand-by option: Registered participants without a reservation or who have lost advance reservation privileges for two weeks may request to be added to the stand-by list. Must be present in person at the center on the day of the meal. Meals on stand-by are not guaranteed.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides technical and financial support to property and business owners to improve the exteriors of older commercial properties. The program reimburses eligible applicants up to 50% of eligible costs for design and construction of approved facade improvement projects. Participants must maintain improvements for a negotiated term through a facade easement agreement with the County.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible property and business owners are reimbursed up to 50% of the total eligible project costs, up to $500,000. County reimbursement amounts above $500,000 may be available at the discretion of the DHCA Director on a per-project basis, based on the availability of program funds and evaluation of the overall scope of improvements. The easement term correlates with the total project cost: $150,000-$300,000 requires a three (3) year easement term; $300,001-$700,000 requires a five (5) year easement term; and $700,001-$1,000,000 requires a seven (7) year easement term with lien subordination required if applicable. Improvements may include facade renovation and treatments, building and pylon signage, LED lighting, streetscape elements, landscape installation, art and mural installation, and other exterior amenities. All approved projects must provide for the installation of new facade materials (not including paint), canopies/awnings and building signage on at least 50% (excluding window and door areas) of the main face or front of the building. Site improvement expenses cannot exceed 15% of the building facade improvement costs. Participants are required to maintain improvements for the negotiated term via a facade easement agreement with the County and must register in the County's Central Vendor Registration System (CVRS) to receive payment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications will not be reviewed for full submission and approval until July 1, 2025, at the earliest. Program Interest Forms are accepted on an ongoing basis and are reviewed and evaluated on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County property and business owners interested in making improvements to the exterior of commercial properties that are 10 or more years old. Applicants can be property owners or lessees (with written property owner consent).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Facade renovation and treatments, building and pylon signage, LED lighting, streetscape elements, landscape installation, art and mural installation, demolition of existing facade, cleaning and/or painting of building exterior, installing new windows/doors, canopies/awnings, exterior site lighting, exterior electrical work, parking lot and/or sidewalk repaving/replacement, landscape plant material, parking lot reconfiguration and restriping, dumpster enclosures, convenience features including affixed benches or outdoor seating, and new or refurbished exterior wall murals and/or permanent public art sculptures/features for commercial properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available countywide in Montgomery County, Maryland. Priority consideration is given to projects located in program priority areas of Glenmont, Hillandale, Layhill, Long Branch, Montgomery Village or Wheaton; located in an Equity Focus Area within the County; mixed-use properties (but not exclusively used for or converted to housing); or properties with significant first floor retail.
requirements_list: Property or business must be in Montgomery County
Commercial property must be more than 10 years old at time of application
Property must be a commercial building or mixed-use building with a retail component
Property must be an existing building four or less stories tall
Applicant must be the owner of the commercial or mixed-use property OR a lessee with written property owner agreement
All documentation for agreements and easements must be signed and executed by the owner(s) of the property
Property owner name, business name, phone number and email address required in Program Interest Form
If lessee is the applicant, lessee's name, business name, phone number, email address, and lease expiration date required
General description of planned, eligible project improvements required
Estimated budget for project improvements required
Property Tax ID number required
Certificate of insurance for the property's casualty and liability insurance naming Montgomery County as an additional insured required
If program participant is a business entity with Board of Directors or Managing Member, resolution from Board or Managing Member required
Letter from construction contractor indicating anticipated start and completion dates required
Current title report for the property paid for by the owner required

Proposed projects must achieve the program's objective to provide significant improvements to the facade and improve the overall physical appearance of the building as determined by the Architectural Review Committee
If property is located within a historic district and/or is on the historical register, program participants must obtain approval of the Historic Preservation Commission
Participants must maintain improvements for the negotiated term via facade easement agreement with the County
All invoices and receipts for eligible project costs must be submitted within 45 days of project completion

Employees of DHCA and their family members are NOT eligible to apply; participation of other County employees may require review and approval by the County's Chief Administrative Officer and the County's Ethics Commission
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete Program Interest Form available at www.montgomerycountymd.gov/DHCA/community/neighborhood/facade.html. Program Interest Forms are accepted on an ongoing basis and reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis. DHCA staff will follow-up via email verifying receipt. 2. Proposed projects/applicants meeting requirements for Program Participation will be emailed requesting submittal of project concept designs and other materials including existing photos of the building(s), concept design drawings of all sides of the building to be improved, concept design plans for any site improvements if applicable, material samples/color selections/manufacturer information, detailed line-item cost estimates for construction project elements, and estimated architectural and engineering service fees. 3. Applicant and/or their architectural and engineering firm may mail, hand deliver or email materials to DHCA staff who will schedule a date to present the proposed project and plans to the Architectural Review Committee (in-person or online via TEAMS/ZOOM) for feedback and suggestions. 4. Following presentation meeting, the Committee will make a recommendation to the DHCA Director to approve the project with or without contingencies, or disapprove the project. Applicants of disapproved projects will be notified via email regarding the basis for the decision. 5. After reviewing the Committee's recommendation, the DHCA Director has absolute and sole discretion on whether to approve the project for funding. The Director's decision is final. All project approvals are subject to funding availability. 6. Program Offer Letter will be provided by DHCA Director detailing project funding amount offered by the County (in the form of easement purchase) along with easement purchase terms and conditions. This letter must be signed by the property owner and returned by email to DHCA within ten (10) business days of receipt. 7. Program participant must provide DHCA with property Tax ID number, certificate of insurance, board resolution if applicable, letter from construction contractor, and current title report. 8. Following return of executed Offer Letter, a public notice for projects with easement terms of five (5) or more years shall invite written comment with a deadline of no more than 30 days after public notice dissemination. Notice shall be posted on DHCA's website, at the project site, in online community news/social media platforms, emails or newsletters sent by Regional Services Centers, and/or in-person notice at community meetings. Notice of the proposed easement purchase shall be mailed to all property owners within 500 feet of the project property/site. 9. At conclusion of 30-day public notice period, DHCA will email a Notice to Proceed for completion of the project's design and construction activities. Design and construction should be completed within a reasonable timeframe based on project scope. Requests for project extensions will be granted on a case-by-case basis. 10. During project construction and/or at completion, DHCA may request that the property owner allow the County/DHCA to display banner signage acknowledging County and program support. 11. Program participants must submit all invoices and receipts for eligible project costs within 45 days of project completion. 12. Upon review and approval of submitted invoices and payment receipts, DHCA will issue a reimbursement check within 30 days, after which DHCA will record the easement granted by the property owner to the County and any required subordination agreement among County land records. 13. Program participants must register in the County's Central Vendor Registration System (CVRS) to receive payment. 14. Each completed project will be inspected periodically by DHCA during the easement term to ensure project elements are maintained and unaltered based on submitted and approved design plans. Within 15 days of inspection, DHCA will provide written notice if needed of any observed damage, deterioration (other than normal wear and tear) and/or unapproved alterations. Noted damage and/or unapproved alterations must be remedied within the timeframe provided in DHCA's written notice.

structured_extraction.program_name: Design for Life (DFL) Tax Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary tax incentive program administered by Montgomery County that increases the stock of visitable and livable housing by providing property tax credits and Development Impact Tax for School Improvements credits to homeowners, builders, and developers who construct or renovate single-family attached and detached homes meeting Design for Life accessibility standards. The program promotes universal design principles so homes are accessible to people of all ages and abilities, helping County residents remain in their homes as physical needs change. Three tiers of tax credits are available: (1) individual accessibility features installed in existing residences, (2) Level I (VISITable) Accessibility Standard homes meeting basic visitability thresholds, and (3) Level II (LIVEable) Accessibility Standard homes meeting higher liveability standards. Builders of new construction may also qualify for Development Impact Tax for School Improvements credits. The program covers both new construction and renovation of single-family attached and detached homes, townhomes, duplexes, and condominium units in Montgomery County, and includes a builder and homeowner certification process, permit fast-tracking, and increased marketability of certified properties.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description:
The program provides three tiers of property tax credits that run with the property and carry forward to future years if the credit exceeds the county property tax owed in any single year. The maximum credit that may be applied in any single tax year is $2,000, with excess carrying over to subsequent years. Credits transfer to subsequent owners if the property is sold. An annual limit of $100,000 is allocated for Individual Accessibility Features credits, and $500,000 for Level I and Level II Accessibility Standards credits.

1. Individual Accessibility Features: A property tax credit equal to the lesser of 50% of eligible costs or $2,500 per property owner per tax year, minus any subsidy received from governmental, quasi-governmental, or non-profit entities. Eligible costs must exceed $500 and be incurred within 12 months prior to application. Applies to condominium units, attached or detached single-family dwellings, townhouses, and duplexes.

2. Level I (VISITable) Standard: A property tax credit of up to $3,000 (less other subsidies including school impact tax credit) for homes meeting all four Level I design elements: at least one no-step entrance, an accessible route to a place to visit on the entry level, a usable powder room or bathroom, and at least one 32-inch nominal clear width interior door. Applies to attached or detached single-family dwellings, townhomes, and duplexes.

3. Level II (LIVEable) Standard: A property tax credit of up to $10,000 (less other subsidies including school impact tax credit) for homes meeting all eight Level II design elements, which include all Level I elements plus an accessible circulation path, accessible kitchen, accessible bedroom, and an accessibility-enhanced full bathroom. Applies to attached or detached single-family dwellings, townhomes, and duplexes.

Development Impact Tax for School Improvements Credits (for builders of new single-family residences meeting Level I or Level II standards): $500 per Level I house for projects where 5% of units meet Level I; $1,000 per house for 10%; $1,500 per house for 25%; $2,000 per house for 30%. A separate School Impact Tax Credit Certification Agreement must be entered into before issuance of building permits. School impact tax credit applies only where there is no bonus density for Design for Life units.

The tax credit is assessed by the Montgomery County Department of Finance and appears as a line item on the property tax bill. Credits are granted in the order in which the Department certifies the amount of the credit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing program; applications accepted throughout the year on or after March 1, 2014
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, builders, contractors, and developers in Montgomery County who own or are constructing new or existing single-family attached or detached homes, townhomes, duplexes, or condominium units as their principal residence, and who wish to incorporate accessibility features meeting Design for Life standards. Eligible applicants include first-time homebuyers, young families, active adults, and people living with temporary or permanent impairments, as well as commercial builders and developers constructing multiple single-family dwellings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation or construction of permanent accessibility features including but not limited to: no-step entrances; ramps; exterior and interior doorways with specified clear widths (32-inch nominal); elevators or lifts; stair glides or chair lift devices; accessible bathrooms including grab bars, accessible shower/tub, and chair-height toilets; accessible kitchens with maneuverable layouts; accessible bedrooms; accessible circulation paths; accessible closets; relocation of controls, switches, doorbells, and electrical receptacles to accessible heights; lever door handles; alternative sensory alarms; and other features meeting Design for Life Level I (VISITable) or Level II (LIVEable) Accessibility Standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. Applies to single-family attached and detached homes, townhomes, duplexes, and condominium units located in Montgomery County. Property owners whose properties are located in the City of Rockville or City of Gaithersburg must also submit a signed affidavit from their respective city verifying that all necessary inspections have been completed and features have been installed according to permit.
requirements_list: Property must be the owner's principal residence (occupancy box on real property tax bill must read 'Principal Residence')
Property must be a new or existing residential dwelling: condominium unit, attached or detached single-family dwelling, townhouse, or duplex
For individual accessibility features: applicable to condominium units, attached or detached single-family dwellings, townhouses, and duplexes
For Level I (VISITable) and Level II (LIVEable) standards: applicable to attached or detached single-family dwelling units (including townhomes and duplexes)
Eligible costs must be incurred within 12 months prior to submitting the application
Eligible costs must exceed $500
Costs must be documented by contracts, receipts, or invoices
Any subsidy received from governmental, quasi-governmental, or non-profit entities must be deducted from eligible costs

For Level I (VISITable) standards: all four required design elements must be completed at the same time and prior to final approved inspection
For Level II (LIVEable) standards: all eight required design elements must be completed prior to final approved inspection

Only one application for property tax credit may be submitted per property per tax year
