Exterior doorways must provide 32-inch clear opening and include exterior lighting controlled from inside, automatic, or continuous
structured_extraction.application_process_overview:
The application process is a two-part process:

Part 1 – Building Permit (before work starts):
Apply for a Residential or Commercial Building Permit before beginning any work. Apply online through Montgomery County eServices at https://eplans.montgomerycountymd.gov (check the DFL application box on the residential or commercial permit application) and upload all electronic plans and documents showing the accessibility features; alternatively, submit paper documents in person at the Montgomery County Department of Permitting Services (2425 Reedie Drive, 7th Floor, Wheaton, MD 20902), including the Building Permit – Supplemental Design for Life Application (form DesignForLifeSupplementalApplication.pdf) along with architectural and/or engineering plans documenting the renovations. For existing homes, apply for an Alteration Permit and indicate the specific accessibility features on the application with required plans. For School Impact Tax Credits, submit a separate School Impact Tax Credit Certification Agreement before building permits are issued. Plans must conform to Design for Life Technical Guidelines and include a 3" x 4" area at the top center for DPS electronic approval stamp.

Part 2 – Tax Credit Application (after work is completed and inspected):
After all work is completed and the final inspection is approved, submit a separate Application for Design for Life Tax Credits (Design for Life Application for Tax Credit form) to the Department of Permitting Services at DPS.DesignforLife@montgomerycountymd.gov or by paper mail to 2425 Reedie Drive, 7th Floor, Wheaton, MD 20902. Include: a copy of the building permit, cost documentation (contracts, receipts, invoices) documenting eligible costs, copies of applications and receipts for any other subsidies received, a signed affidavit stating that neither the previous owner nor the applicant has received other subsidies for modifications, and a list of features and costs for each feature. Applicants in the City of Rockville or City of Gaithersburg must also include a signed affidavit from their respective city verifying inspections and installation. DPS confirms receipt, certifies all requirements have been met, and forwards the certification to the Department of Finance. The Department of Finance reviews the application, assesses the tax credit amount, notifies the applicant, and the credit appears as a line item on the next property tax bill, applied in amounts up to $2,000 per tax year with any balance carried over to following years. Credits are granted in the order received by DPS.

structured_extraction.program_name: Design for Life - Level II (LIVEable) Accessibility Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program administered by Montgomery County that provides incentives to homeowners and builders who construct or retrofit single-family homes meeting the Level II (LIVEable) accessibility standard. These comprehensive accessibility standards include a no-step entrance, accessible route to a visitability space on the entry level, usable powder room or bathroom, at least one 32-inch nominal clear width interior door, accessible interior circulation path, accessible kitchen, at least one accessible bedroom, and an accessibility-enhanced full bathroom with walk-in or roll-in shower or tub. The program aims to promote accessible and inclusive housing design for residents of Montgomery County.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners receive a property tax credit that runs with the property for up to $10,000 (less other subsidies including school impact tax credit) for homes meeting Level II (LIVEable) accessibility standards. The maximum credit applied in any single tax year is $2,000, with any excess credit carrying over to future years. Improvements must exceed $500 and be completed within 12 months of application. Builders or developers receive variable credits against school impact taxes depending on the percentage of homes built to the Level II standard: 5% of homes = $500 per Level II house; 10% = $1,000 per Level II house; 25% = $1,500 per Level II house; 30% = $2,000 per Level II house. The school impact tax credit applies only where there is no bonus density for Design for Life units. The credit runs with the property for future tax years if not fully used in the initial year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling application process - no specific deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners and builders/developers in Montgomery County who own or are constructing attached or detached single-family dwellings and wish to meet comprehensive Level II (LIVEable) accessibility standards. Builders or developers building multiple homes to these standards are also eligible for school impact tax credits based on the percentage of homes built to Level II standard. Property owners must be building new residences or retrofitting existing residences to meet the standards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs of implementing the seven required design elements of Level II (LIVEable) accessibility standards: at least one no-step entrance, an accessible route to a visitability space on the entry level, a usable powder room or bathroom, at least one 32-inch nominal clear width interior door, an accessible interior circulation path that connects the accessible entrance to an accessible kitchen, at least one accessible bedroom, and an accessibility-enhanced full bathroom with walk-in or roll-in shower or tub. Eligible costs include purchase and installation of accessibility features, required permit fees, and inspection fees. Costs must exceed $500 and be incurred within 12 months of application submission.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, including properties within Montgomery County, the City of Gaithersburg, and the City of Rockville.
requirements_list: Property must be an attached or detached single-family dwelling (single-family dwellings, townhouses, and duplexes)

Home must meet all seven Level II (LIVEable) accessibility design elements: no-step entrance, accessible route to visitability space on entry level, usable powder room or bathroom, 32-inch clear width interior door, accessible circulation path to kitchen, at least one accessible bedroom, and accessibility-enhanced full bathroom with walk-in or roll-in shower or tub
Expenditures must exceed $500
Expenditures must be incurred within 12 months of application submission
Work must be completed and certified by Department of Permitting Services after building permit is issued and final building inspection is approved
After final building inspection, property owner must submit the Design for Life Application for Tax Credit
Property owner must have paid eligible costs (not reimbursed by other entities) and documented costs with contracts, receipts, or invoices
For existing residences, the property must be the owner's principal residence (marked as such on property tax bill)
Credits received from other subsidies must be deducted from the property tax credit amount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Homeowner or builder implements the seven required Level II (LIVEable) design elements. 2. After work is completed, the Department of Permitting Services issues building permit and conducts final building inspection to certify that accessibility features are installed in accordance with the permit. 3. Once final inspection approval is granted, the property owner submits the Design for Life Application for Tax Credit form to the Department of Permitting Services, including contracts, receipts, or invoices demonstrating costs and a complete list of features and costs for each feature. 4. The Department of Permitting Services reviews the application and provides an affidavit certifying eligibility. 5. The property tax credit is applied to the owner's property tax bill, with amounts up to $2,000 applied per tax year, and any balance carried over to following years. Builders and developers receive credits against school impact taxes based on the percentage of homes built to Level II standard per an Impact Tax Credit Certification Agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that solves drainage problems where there is no storm drain system or the existing system is failing or is inadequate. The program addresses requests for assistance to correct drainage problems where runoff water originates from the public right-of-way.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program investigates drainage problems, determines if they qualify as a Drainage Assistance Request (DAR) project, calculates watershed size and water flow characteristics, verifies affected properties and damage extent, reviews existing drainage systems, determines availability of right-of-way or easements, determines if a spot solution or comprehensive capital improvement project (CIP) is needed, develops designs, schedules construction work with HMS Contracts Unit, or prioritizes projects for county approval and recommendation to the County Executive and County Council. Assistance includes design services and coordination of improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents and property owners experiencing drainage problems from surface runoff originating from public rights-of-way.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Drainage system design, planning, and construction improvements to address inadequate or failing drainage systems and surface runoff issues from county-maintained property and roads.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Assistance applies where runoff water originates from the public right-of-way or county-owned and maintained property. For drainage issues within City of Rockville, contact City of Rockville DPWT at 240-314-8567. For drainage issues within City of Gaithersburg, contact City of Gaithersburg DPWT at 301-258-6370.
requirements_list: Drainage problem must be related to surface runoff from roads or property owned and maintained by Montgomery County
Runoff water must originate from the public right-of-way
Problem must involve either absence of a storm drain system, failure of existing system, or inadequacy of existing system
Must provide location where drainage problem is occurring
Must provide brief statement describing the drainage problem and where water originates and where it goes (photographs are helpful)
Must provide name, home address, and telephone number where applicant can be contacted
Must authorize site visit by County staff on property, if applicable
Must indicate availability to meet County staff at site during site visit, if necessary
Should provide Community or Homeowner Association name, representative name, and telephone number, if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a request for assistance by telephone call, email, FAX, or letter to the Design Section of the Division of Transportation Engineering (DTE). Address: 100 Edison Park Drive, 4th floor, Gaithersburg, Maryland 20878, ATTN: Program Manager, Drainage Assistance Request Program. Phone: 240-620-9115. FAX: 240-777-7277. Email: matt.spielman@montgomerycountymd.gov. A County staff member knowledgeable in surface runoff issues will review the request in a timely manner. The evaluation process includes investigation of the nature and cause of the problem; determination if it should be included as a DAR Project or referred to another agency; if a DAR project, calculation of watershed size and water flow characteristics; verification of affected properties and damage extent; review of existing drainage system and upgrade needs; determination of right-of-way or easement availability; determination if a spot solution or comprehensive Capital Improvement Project (CIP) is needed; scheduling of work or prioritization for County Executive and County Council approval; and notification to residents of action being taken. After review is completed, applicants will receive an explanation of the review findings and proposed action.

structured_extraction.program_description: A maintenance assistance program for existing storm drain systems that require upkeep such as clearing debris from inlets and pipes, re-establishment of eroded or silted drainage channels, fixing water ponding on roads, and reconstruction of roadside curbs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides maintenance assistance for existing storm drain systems including debris clearing from inlets and storm drain pipes, drainage channel re-establishment where channels have eroded or silted up, fixing water ponding issues on roads, and reconstruction of roadside curbs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents and property owners with drainage concerns on existing storm drain systems requiring maintenance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Maintenance of existing storm drain systems including debris removal, drainage channel maintenance, road ponding fixes, and roadside curb reconstruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Applies to existing storm drain systems within the county.
requirements_list: Drainage concern must involve existing storm drain systems
Maintenance must be needed for issues such as debris in inlets or pipes, channel erosion or silting, water ponding on roads, or damaged roadside curbs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Transportation via email at mcdot.highway@montgomerycountymd.gov to report drainage maintenance needs on existing storm drain systems.

structured_extraction.program_description: Participating dealerships in Montgomery County offer deals, special offers, and promotions on new or used electric vehicles to members of the EV Purchasing Cooperative. The cooperative uses combined purchasing power of county residents and businesses to negotiate discounts with local dealerships.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly deals, special offers, and promotions on new or used electric vehicles from participating local dealerships. Specific offers vary by dealership and change monthly.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents and businesses seeking to purchase or lease new or pre-owned electric vehicles.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase or lease of new or pre-owned electric vehicles
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Check the EV Purchasing Co-op website monthly to view available dealer offers and promotions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Early Head Start Community Based Model
structured_extraction.program_description: A full-year, full-day early childhood education and childcare program for infants and toddlers from birth to age 3. The program provides comprehensive services through a network of registered family childcare homes and licensed center-based childcare programs, with wrap-around support including training, technical assistance, coaching support, and family engagement services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Early Head Start provides $17,965 per child annually for a full-year (1,380 annual hours), full-day (9-hour) program. Programs receive monthly payments of $1,497 for 12 months based on enrollment. Minimum enrollment slots required are 2 for family childcare providers and 4 for childcare centers. Registered family childcare homes and licensed center-based programs with a minimum of Level 3 EXCELS rating are eligible to apply. Childcare programs receive wrap-around services including training, technical assistance, early childhood education (ECE) coaching support, family engagement services, health services for children, administrative support, and education supplies and equipment from the County's Early Childhood Services program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications available November 1st - 15th. Application closes November 14, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family childcare homes and licensed center-based childcare programs serving infants and toddlers ages birth to 3 in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Early Head Start childcare services, staff training, technical assistance, early childhood education coaching support, mental health consultation, family engagement services, health services for children, administrative support, and education supplies and equipment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Throughout Montgomery County
requirements_list: Licensed through Maryland State Department of Education
Registered and published as a Level 3 or higher in Maryland EXCELS
Minimum of Level 3 EXCELS rating required
Programs must attend orientation session in October to be considered
Program must collaborate as an Early Head Start childcare hub
Responsible for the early childhood education component of the program
Provide families with the option to access the Maryland State Childcare Scholarship and the County's Working Parents' Assistance (WPA) programs for extended day program options
Full participation in comprehensive services including site visits by county staff, parent engagement activities, coaching and professional development
Agree to county's review of last MSDE-OCC inspection report
Submit two letters of recommendations from current or past parents of the program
Childcare centers require minimum of two teachers with Infant & Toddler CDA
Family childcare providers require minimum of FCCP CDA
Childcare programs with multiple locations must submit separate application for each location
Families served must meet 100% Federal Poverty Level (FPL) income eligibility requirement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Programs must attend one of the orientation sessions held in October. Programs that do not attend an orientation session are not eligible. Early Head Start applications are available from November 1st to November 15th and are submitted through the online application portal at https://forms.montgomerycountymd.gov/ng/fa/089pezv0rure. The link to the application is posted on the Montgomery County Community Action Agency Website. Programs must submit the Childcare Provider Application Form along with required documentation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Economic Development Fund Grant & Loan Program (EDFGLP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A discretionary strategic attraction and retention program providing financial assistance to private employers in Montgomery County who retain jobs or stimulate new job creation. The program supports projects in targeted industry sectors that generate significant economic development impact, including job growth and retention, capital expenditure, and other measurable benefits. Priority is given to high technology companies, manufacturing companies, businesses located in urban revitalization areas, and other private employers providing the greatest public benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Typical assistance ranges from $5,000 to $100,000, with higher amounts possible for businesses involved in large projects. Project awards stipulate conditions for disbursement and minimum performance measures, and include clawback provisions to recapture funds if a business fails to achieve the expected economic output.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private employers and businesses in targeted industry sectors in Montgomery County that can generate significant economic development impact, including high technology companies, manufacturing companies, and businesses located in urban revitalization areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that generate job growth, job retention, capital expenditure, and other significant economic development impact in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, with priority for businesses in urban revitalization areas.
requirements_list: Must be a private employer
Project must be in a targeted industry sector
Project must generate significant economic development impact such as job growth, job retention, or capital expenditure
Must demonstrate projected employment growth and capital investment or other positive economic impacts
Business must meet minimum performance measures
Funds subject to clawback provisions if business fails to achieve expected economic output
Must provide financial history and projections including balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow statements
Must demonstrate background of the company and its management
Must demonstrate present and future market outlook for the business
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through the Montgomery County Business Portal with financial documentation (balance sheets, income statements, cash flow statements), company background, and market outlook information. Applications are evaluated based on employment growth projections, capital investment, financial history, company background, market outlook, and priority criteria.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax-exempt financing program that provides bond financing to non-profit organizations and selected for-profit businesses seeking to locate or expand operations within Montgomery County. Bonds are issued to help businesses and organizations finance facilities, equipment, and other capital projects including construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt revenue bonds issued to finance capital projects. Applicants pay a non-refundable application fee of $5,000 at filing and an annual administrative fee of 10 basis points at closing and on an annual basis thereafter based on the original issue amount while bonds are outstanding. Applicants also bear all legal and administrative costs incurred during review and financing. The typical process takes approximately six weeks or longer depending on County Council agenda.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations qualified under Section 501(c)(3) and selected for-profit businesses seeking to locate or expand in Montgomery County, seeking capital financing for facilities, equipment, or other project costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects including construction and acquisition of facilities, purchase of equipment, rehabilitation of existing structures, medical facilities, educational facilities, low-income housing, small manufacturing facilities, solid waste disposal facilities, and other qualifying project costs including architectural, engineering, financing, and legal fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Montgomery County, Maryland. Applicants must be located in the County or be a start-up or relocating to the County.
requirements_list: For non-profits: must be tax-exempt entity qualified under Section 501(c)(3) with IRS Determination Letter
For non-profits: project must be non-speculative (developed for specific occupant)
For non-profits: project must further charitable purposes
For non-profits: underwriter must provide letter deeming project financially feasible
For non-profits: schools must hold Certificate of Approval from State Board of Education
For non-profits: medical/health organizations must be properly licensed by County, State, or Federal government
For non-profits: religious organizations must obtain letter of preliminary advice from County bond counsel regarding separation of church and state

For for-profits: project must be non-speculative (developed for specific occupant)
For for-profits: business/landlord must pay County property taxes and be current on all taxes owed
For for-profits: must submit letter of good standing from Maryland Department of Assessment and Taxation
For for-profits: project should have positive economic and fiscal impact on County
Organization must provide background information including description, recent annual reports, and three years of financial statements (audited statements preferred)
Current and projected three-year payroll information required
Detailed project description including purpose, amount and term of financing requested, and financing structure
Site map, plat, and itemized project cost schedule required
Description of new equipment to be acquired and estimated costs
Status of other government approvals and disclosure of legal issues related to project
Projected employment information for current and new positions by occupational category and salary
Statement of benefits to Montgomery County including projected tax benefits and employment opportunities
Percentage of gross revenue resulting from federal contracts if any
Breakdown of in-County employment by occupational category
Average salary by occupational category
Number of present employees living in Montgomery County
Estimate of new hires from Montgomery County
Willingness to participate in County-sponsored employment-training programs
Summary of other unquantifiable or intangible benefits to local economy and community
Relationship of company products or services to existing County businesses or County departments
Community activities of corporation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Borrower completes application with all required materials and submits to Montgomery County Department of Finance along with $5,000 non-refundable application fee. Checks should be made payable to Montgomery County and remitted to the Director, Department of Finance. A copy of the application is also submitted to the County's bond counsel. Department of Finance reviews the application and requests a Letter of Intent from the Borrower. County bond counsel drafts County Council Resolution. Department of Finance holds a TEFRA public hearing. Following the hearing, Department of Finance forwards its recommendation to the County Executive with the relevant Letter of Intent and Resolution. If the County Executive accepts the Letter of Intent and Resolution, it is forwarded to the County Council for action. County Council takes action on the Resolution. The typical process takes approximately six weeks or longer depending on County Council agenda.

structured_extraction.program_name: Electric Leaf Blower Rebate Program (Incentive Program for Electric Leaf Removal Equipment)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County rebate program that provides financial incentives to help residents and businesses transition from gas-powered to electric leaf blowers and leaf removal equipment. Residents receive a $100 rebate per electric leaf blower purchase (up to one rebate). Small landscaping businesses with annual revenue under $250,000 or five or fewer employees can receive rebates up to $1,500 per 12-month period. Larger landscaping businesses with revenue over $250,000 or six or more employees can receive rebates up to $1,000 per 12-month period. Equipment must be purchased after pre-approval to qualify.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residents receive a $100 rebate limited to one rebate per applicant. The rebate must not exceed the cost of the eligible equipment. Revenue qualifying businesses (annual revenue less than $250,000 or employing 5 or fewer employees) can receive rebates up to $1,500 per 12-month period. Non-revenue qualifying businesses (annual revenue of $250,000 or more or employing 6 or more employees) can receive rebates up to $1,000 per 12-month period. Rebates are subject to appropriation and availability of funds. Electric leaf removal equipment is defined as handheld, backpack, or walk-behind devices powered by only electric means (battery-powered and corded leaf blowers, leaf vacuums, and required batteries and chargers). All rebates are subject to pre-approval by the Director prior to purchase.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be submitted not later than December 31, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents and leaf removal businesses (individuals or entities that earn income using leaf removal equipment to perform paid work) seeking to replace gas-powered leaf blowers with electric alternatives.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of electric leaf removal equipment (handheld, backpack, or walk-behind devices powered by electric means, including battery-powered and corded leaf blowers, leaf vacuums, and batteries and chargers required to power such equipment) to replace gas-powered leaf removal equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must have a Montgomery County street mailing address. Montgomery County residents or leaf removal businesses with a business mailing address located in Montgomery County are eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident or leaf removal business with a Montgomery County street mailing address

Equipment must be electric leaf removal equipment (handheld, backpack, or walk-behind device powered by only electric means, including battery-powered and corded leaf blowers, leaf vacuums, and batteries and chargers)
Application must be pre-approved by the Director prior to purchase of eligible equipment
Residents may receive only one rebate per applicant
For residents: rebate limited to $100 and cost of eligible equipment, whichever is less
For revenue qualifying businesses (revenue less than $250,000 or 5 or fewer employees): rebate limited to $1,500 per 12-month period and cost of eligible equipment, whichever is less
For non-revenue qualifying businesses (revenue of $250,000 or more or 6 or more employees): rebate limited to $1,000 per 12-month period and cost of eligible equipment, whichever is less
Applicant may only submit one application and receive a rebate once per 12-month period as designated by the Department
Equipment must be designated by the Department as eligible equipment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must apply to the Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection in a form prescribed by the Director. The application must be pre-approved by the Director prior to the purchase of eligible equipment. Applications must be submitted not later than December 31, 2026. The Director will make the application available online via the Department's website. The Director may deny applications if multiple applications are received from the same applicant or address, or if the applicant requests a rebate for items not designated as eligible equipment by the Department. Contact Mary Travaglini at LeafBlowerRebateProgram@montgomerycountymd.gov or 240-777-7700 for further information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot project that helps Montgomery County residents transition from fossil fuels (oil, gas, and propane) in their homes by providing a one-stop option for home electrification. The program offers outreach, technical support, home energy audits, electrification recommendations, and direct installation services using financial incentives. It is designed to help residents reduce monthly utility bills while improving indoor air quality, home comfort, and reducing carbon emissions.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct incentives applied at point of sale for eligible electrification work. Incentives vary by appliance: $250 for electric clothes dryer and electrical circuit installation; $500 for electric range/cooktop and electrical circuit; $500-$2500 for heat pumps depending on type and efficiency; $500 for heat pump water heater when using Elysian Energy; $165 for natural gas permit; $500 for oil tank removal; $200 for whole house surge protector; $100 for single-appliance surge protector. Additional rebates available through EmPOWER Maryland utility programs. Energy audit costs $100. The program also works in combination with IRA savings calculator and other incentives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who want to replace fossil fuel heating, water heating, cooking, and laundry appliances with electric alternatives, including homeowners interested in transitioning from fossil fuel heating and water heating to electric systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Incentives cover installation of electric heat pumps (ducted, mini-split, cold-climate, geothermal, or air-to-water models), heat pump water heaters, electric ranges and cooktops, electric clothes dryers, electrical circuit installation, surge protectors, natural gas line capping permits, and oil tank removal. Also supports planning and transitioning to all-electric home systems including heating, cooling, and water heating.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Residences located in Montgomery County, Maryland with individually metered utilities. Eligible for Pepco, BG&E, and Potomac Edison (coming soon) Home Performance with ENERGY STAR programs.
requirements_list: Residence must be located in Montgomery County, Maryland
Utilities must be individually metered
Must replace a fossil-fueled equivalent appliance (effective July 16, 2024)
All combustion appliances must be removed from kitchen when installing electric range/cooktop
Heat pumps must meet minimum efficiency standards (CEE Tier 1 or ENERGY STAR)
Work must be coordinated and completed by Elysian Energy to qualify for Electrify MC incentives
Mini-split heat pumps must provide 50% or more of total heating load
Fossil fuel heating cannot be retained when installing ducted heat pump, mini-split heat pump, cold-climate heat pump, or geothermal heat pump
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Electrify MC Help Desk by phone at 301-830-5767 or email electrifymc@elysianenergy.com. Sign up through the online form or by signing the Montgomery County Electrify Everything Pledge. A member of the Electrify MC team will contact you by phone and email. Schedule a Home Performance with ENERGY STAR energy audit (costs $100). Audit and electrification assessment are completed. Choose improvements including insulation, air sealing, and electrification of HVAC, water heater, stove, and dryer. Have work completed through Elysian Energy. Receive Electrify MC direct incentives at point of sale, with utility rebates for insulation work arriving in 6-8 weeks.

structured_extraction.program_name: Emergency Assistance for Eviction Prevention (Housing Stabilization Services)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides case management and limited financial grants to Montgomery County residents at risk of homelessness due to eviction, foreclosure, or utility disconnection. Assistance includes emergency financial support to prevent eviction, help obtaining or keeping housing, prevention of utility shut-offs, restoration of disconnected utilities, burial assistance grants, and case management to stabilize housing and prevent future crises. Residents of the City of Gaithersburg, City of Rockville, or City of Takoma Park may be eligible for services through those municipalities instead.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Limited financial grants are provided to eligible households to prevent eviction, foreclosure, and utility disconnection. Assistance covers emergency needs such as back rent owed, utility bills, security deposits, first month's rent, and other housing-related expenses to maintain current housing or obtain new housing. Case management services are also provided to help households stabilize housing and prevent future crises. Burial assistance grants are also available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents at risk of homelessness who have received a court judgment for eviction, a put-out notice from their landlord, or are facing foreclosure or utility disconnection. Residents of the City of Gaithersburg, City of Rockville, or City of Takoma Park may be eligible for services through those municipalities instead.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency financial assistance to prevent eviction, foreclosure, or homelessness, including back rent, utility bills, security deposits, first month's rent, mortgage assistance, and other housing-related expenses to maintain current housing or obtain new housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Residents of the City of Gaithersburg, City of Rockville, or City of Takoma Park may be eligible for services through those municipalities instead.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Montgomery County resident
Household income must be at or below 60% of the area median income (AMI)
Household must not have received an eviction prevention grant in the past 12 months
Must have a court summons, judgment, or red and white notice from the Sheriff's Office related to an eviction, or a landlord-issued put-out notice
Must provide photo identification for all adults in the household
Must provide last 30 days of bank and financial statements for all accounts
Must provide last 30 days of income documentation for all adults
Must provide proof of expenses such as utility bills, rent, or mortgage statements
Must provide emergency court or legal documentation related to the eviction
Must provide current rental ledger for eviction prevention cases
Must sign a Release of Information Form authorizing HSS to contact third parties
Must meet program guidelines for eviction prevention assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit one of three office locations (Germantown, Rockville, or Silver Spring) to apply in person, or request a telephone interview by calling 311 or 240-777-0311. Submit all required supporting documentation at the time of application, including photo identification, bank statements, income documentation, proof of expenses, emergency court or legal documentation, and a signed Release of Information Form. Document drop-off stations are also available at the Germantown, Rockville, and Silver Spring offices. HSS staff will assess your needs and determine eligibility. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with sign-in available until 4:30 p.m. You may also email HSS@montgomerycountymd.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County engages a contractor to examine one or more buildings and implement improvements to reduce energy usage. The contractor funds capital costs through borrowing, and the County repays the costs through the energy savings generated by the project over a period of 15 years or less. The contractor guarantees the projected savings and must reimburse the County for any shortfall.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County contracts with an Energy Savings Contractor to provide evaluation, design, implementation, and verification of energy-saving improvements to county buildings. Capital costs are funded through borrowing and repaid from the energy savings generated. Payback is generally achieved in 15 years or less. The contractor guarantees savings and must reimburse the County for any shortfall. Actual savings are reconciled annually per the contract terms.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County Government facilities and agencies seeking to reduce energy usage and upgrade building systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements to buildings, including upgrades to equipment and systems to reduce energy and operational costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to Montgomery County Government buildings and facilities.
requirements_list: Building or group of buildings must be county-owned and operated
Project must result in measurable energy savings
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Montgomery County engages Energy Savings Contractors through a procurement process. The selected contractor performs an evaluation of the facility, designs the project, implements improvements, and verifies savings.

structured_extraction.program_description: A two-tiered property tax credit program for owners of commercial and multi-family buildings in Montgomery County. Existing building owners can receive up to 100% property tax credit against County taxes for two years after making major energy efficiency improvements. The first tier for existing buildings is based on measurable energy use reduction (using ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager), and the second tier provides additional credits for achieving LEED, BREEAM, or equivalent certifications. Newly constructed building owners can receive up to 100% property tax credit against County taxes for four years (or five years for Living Building Certification) if their new building exceeds current building code requirements by at least 10%. Buildings located in Equity Emphasis Areas receive an additional 10% credit. Both tiers can be combined but cannot exceed 100% per year.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credits of up to 100% against Montgomery County taxes. For existing buildings: up to two years of tax credits following energy efficiency improvements. First tier credit calculated by subtracting baseline ENERGY STAR score from improved score and multiplying by a tier-based multiplier (ranging from 1.0 to 2.5). Second tier credit provides up to 50% additional credit for LEED Platinum or BREEAM In-Use Outstanding certification. For newly constructed buildings: up to four years of tax credits (five years for Living Building Certification). First tier credit based on percentage above building code: buildings 10-20% above code receive 5-10% credit, 21-30% above code receive 21-30% credit, 31-40% above code receive 46.5-60% credit, and above 40% receive 82-100% credit. Second tier provides 25% for LEED Gold or equivalent, or 75% for LEED Platinum, Living Building Certification, or equivalent. Buildings in Equity Emphasis Areas receive an additional 10% credit. Maximum combined credit cannot exceed 100% per year. As of October 2018, the program has distributed nearly $33.4 million in property tax credits since establishment in March 2008, with a maximum annual allocation of $5 million.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of existing and newly constructed commercial and multi-family buildings in Montgomery County with at least 10,000 square feet of gross floor area, including developers and property owners constructing new energy-efficient buildings. Core and Shell buildings with full mechanical systems and weather-sealed thermal envelopes are eligible under the New Construction program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credits applied against Montgomery County taxes for buildings that make major energy efficiency improvements (existing buildings) or are newly constructed to exceed current building code energy efficiency requirements by at least 10% (new construction). Credits support investments in energy performance improvements, sustainable building certifications, and whole-building sustainability features.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Additional 10% credit available for buildings located in Equity Emphasis Areas.
requirements_list: At least 10,000 square feet of gross floor area
Property must be located in Montgomery County
For existing buildings: Certificate of Occupancy from Department of Permitting Services
For existing buildings: at least 50% occupancy rate for at least 12 consecutive months
For existing buildings: demonstrated energy improvements consistent with Montgomery County Code Section 52-103A
For existing buildings Tier 1: measurable reduction in energy use demonstrated through ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager baseline and improved scores
For existing buildings Tier 2: LEED O+M Gold or Platinum, BREEAM USA In-Use Excellent or Outstanding, or equivalent certification
For existing buildings: ENERGY STAR Data Verification Checklists must be verified by licensed Professional Engineer or Registered Architect in good standing
For existing buildings: baseline and improved ENERGY STAR time periods must not overlap, not include installation period, and not be more than 6 calendar years apart
For existing buildings: Improved ENERGY STAR score cannot be issued more than 12 months before application date
For existing buildings: Baseline ENERGY STAR score 12-month period must not begin earlier than August 26, 2018
For existing buildings: Maximum of 3 applications per building (one initial and two reapplications)

For newly constructed buildings: certification from Department of Permitting Services within last 12 months indicating percentage performance above current Building Code requirements at time of application
For newly constructed buildings: minimum 10% better than Building Code required
For newly constructed buildings: buildings demonstrated code compliance via performance pathway with DPS-stamped energy model (buildings using prescriptive pathway not eligible)
For newly constructed buildings: modeled energy performance consistent with Montgomery County Code Section 52-103B
For newly constructed buildings: energy model must validate performance pathway
One application per single property for first tier credit (new construction)
Core and Shell buildings must include complete thermal enclosure system with primary-backbone HVAC and electrical distribution infrastructure
For Core and Shell buildings: primary HVAC system and capacity must be fully designed, purchased, and operational to serve occupied future tenant spaces
For Core and Shell buildings: only equipment purchased by owner as part of base building project can be included in analysis
For Core and Shell buildings: all non-purchased equipment, lighting and process energy must be assumed to be current energy code compliant in baseline and proposed case analysis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For existing buildings: 1. Establish a 12-month baseline ENERGY STAR score in Portfolio Manager. 2. Complete energy efficiency improvements and document with finalized DPS permit and vendor installation invoices. 3. Measure improved energy performance using Portfolio Manager after improvement period. 4. Have ENERGY STAR Data Verification Checklist verified by a licensed Professional Engineer or Registered Architect. 5. Submit application through the online portal (https://montgomerycountymd.seamlessdocs.com/f/EnergyEfficientExistingBuildingsTaxCredit). 6. For second tier credit, obtain LEED, BREEAM, or equivalent certification and submit additional application. For newly constructed buildings: 1. Design new building to exceed current Building Code requirements by minimum 10% using performance pathway. 2. Obtain DPS-stamped energy model demonstrating performance above code. 3. Receive certification from Department of Permitting Services within last 12 months of application. 4. Submit first tier application through online portal (https://montgomerycountymd.seamlessdocs.com/f/EnergyEfficientNewBuildingsTaxCredit). 5. For second tier credit, obtain LEED, BREEAM, NGBS, PHIUS+/Passive House, Living Building Certification, or equivalent certification. 6. Submit second tier application combining both credit percentages. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis through the online portal.

Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_prioritized_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County tax credit at 58.5% of additional local tax liability for 24 years. Businesses have six years from notification to create and fill required jobs and acquire new space. State credit available at 31.5% annually against State income taxes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses in qualified industries planning major expansion projects with significant job creation and real estate investment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit against local real and personal property taxes and State income taxes resulting from qualified business expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Montgomery County for businesses in qualified industries.
requirements_list: Must be in a qualified industry
Option 1: Increase space by 250,000+ square feet, create 500+ new permanent full-time jobs if company has 2,500+ existing jobs, pay employees at least 150% of federal minimum wage
Option 2: Increase space by 250,000+ square feet, create 1,250+ new permanent full-time jobs, pay employees at least 150% of federal minimum wage

Option 3: Expend at least $150 million, increase space by 700,000+ square feet, create 500+ new permanent full-time jobs if company has 1,100+ existing jobs, pay employees at least 150% of federal minimum wage and provide subsidized health care benefits
Must notify County before expanding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application showing expansion plans. Business has six years from notification date to create required jobs and acquire new space. Once accomplished, notify County Department of Finance to begin receiving credits.

structured_extraction.program_description: The FJC Training Institute provides free training programs to organizations, agencies, groups, and the general public on topics related to domestic violence and teen dating violence. The institute offers multiple training modules ranging from 45 minutes to 4 hours covering dynamics of domestic violence, bystander intervention, effects on children, workplace impacts, healthcare response, and teen dating violence awareness. Staff can also create personalized trainings on domestic violence topics.

Topics include domestic violence dynamics, bystander intervention, workplace impacts, healthcare response to intimate partner violence, pregnancy and intimate partner violence, strangulation response, and teen dating violence. Customized trainings on domestic violence topics can also be created upon request. The 'Expect Respect' teen dating violence workshop is available to schools for students ages 12-18.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations, agencies, groups, and the general public. Training is not available to individuals; requests must be from groups, organizations, or agencies. Specific audiences include faith-based institutions, workplace employees and managers, healthcare providers, first responders, legal professionals, victim advocates, parents, youth-serving professionals, and students ages 12-18 (for teen dating violence trainings).

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Requests must be for groups, organizations, or agencies (training cannot be provided to individuals)
For school-based teen dating violence trainings, schools must submit a request through the provided form for the 'Expect Respect' workshop
Groups should contact the FJC Training Institute to schedule a training

Schools requesting the 'Expect Respect' teen dating violence training for students should submit a request form using the provided Google Form link. The institute will work with organizations to schedule trainings at convenient times and locations.

Reimbursement is limited to $5,000.00 over the course of the collective bargaining agreement. The volunteer must use the provider recommended by FROMS, if any.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the following documents to michael.kelley@montgomerycountymd.gov and CC satchel.kornfeld@montgomerycountymd.gov: a document from FROMS stating that a specialist is needed, a copy of the medical invoice or statement showing the amount and proof of payment, and a statement from the member attesting that the amount paid is not covered by insurance or that they have no insurance. structured_extraction.program_name: FY25 Food Recovery Network Infrastructure Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to non-profit organizations to expand and strengthen Montgomery County's Food Recovery Network capacity to transport, store, and distribute recovered food to residents experiencing food insecurity. The program funds projects that reflect collaborative, shared-use approaches for infrastructure capacity building, establish recovery relationships with new donors, increase access to higher-value and limited-availability products, reduce climate impacts of food recovery and assistance operations, and leverage external investment and resources. Specific infrastructure investments include refrigerated vehicles and shared cold storage units that increase the network's ability to recover, store, and distribute fresh, perishable foods.
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $306,000 was awarded in FY25 to four organizations (AfriThrive, Nourish Now, Rainbow Community Development Center, and So What Else) for projects that build capacity of the food recovery network, establish recovery relationships with new donors, increase access to higher-value and limited-availability products, reduce climate impacts of food recovery and assistance operations, and leverage external investment and resources. Funded infrastructure includes refrigerated vehicles and shared cold storage units. Grant funds may be spent on infrastructure purchases (capital or durable goods such as refrigeration, shelving, vehicles for food transport, pallet jacks, etc.), staff costs for program coordination, logistics, or administration, indirect costs (shared administrative expenses such as accounting, insurance, IT systems, or general office expenses), and other operational costs such as fuel, vehicle maintenance, packing materials, maintenance and repairs, training activities, and food-safety supplies. Grantees are required to submit financial and performance reports at mid-cycle (6 months) and end-cycle (12 months), with mid-cycle reports due 01/31/2026 and end-cycle reports due 07/31/2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations involved in food recovery, rescue, and distribution in Montgomery County, including those focused on food recovery network capacity building, donor relationship development, and reducing climate impacts of food assistance operations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure improvements for transporting, storing, and distributing recovered food, including purchase of refrigerated vehicles and shared cold storage units; capacity building of the food recovery operator network; establishing recovery relationships with new donors; increasing access to higher-value and limited-availability products; reducing climate impacts of food recovery and assistance operations; leveraging external investment and resources; and supporting food recovery operational costs and collaboration efforts. Specific allowable uses include infrastructure purchases (refrigeration, shelving, vehicles, pallet jacks, etc.), staff costs for program coordination and logistics, indirect administrative costs, and operational costs such as fuel, vehicle maintenance, packing materials, training, and food-safety supplies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization
Organization must focus on food recovery and distribution
Projects must reflect collaborative, shared-use approaches
Projects must allow for capacity building of the food recovery network
Projects must establish recovery relationships with new donors or increase access to higher-value and limited-availability products
Projects must reduce climate impacts of food recovery and assistance network
Projects must leverage external investment and/or resources
Grantees must participate in the Montgomery County Food Recovery Network and attend 75% or more of FRN meetings
Grantees are required to submit mid-cycle performance and financial reports by 01/31/2026 and end-cycle reports by 07/31/2026
Grantees must track and report financial data including infrastructure purchases, staff costs, indirect costs, and other operational costs, as well as in-kind resource contributions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submitted applications for infrastructure funding to support food recovery operations. FY25 awards have been completed. Awarded grantees are required to participate in the Montgomery County Food Recovery Network, attend 75% or more of FRN meetings, and submit financial and performance reports at two points during the grant performance period: mid-cycle (6 months) due 01/31/2026 and end-cycle (12 months) due 07/31/2026. All reports must be submitted through the OFSR online reporting platform.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Food as Medicine Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program funds innovative initiatives that screen pediatric patients for food insecurity and provide nutritious food and food education services. It supports healthcare and clinic-led programs that increase access to culturally diverse, medically-relevant, nutritious, and locally produced food for Montgomery County households with at least one child aged 0-18 that screen positive for food insecurity and include a parent and/or child with a current diagnosis of diet-related disease. The program also supports broader healthcare and clinic-based approaches that deliver medically tailored food assistance to residents experiencing food insecurity and diet-related health conditions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $750,000 in total grant funding is available to support healthcare and clinic-led Food as Medicine programs that screen pediatric patients for food insecurity and provide medically tailored, nutritious, and locally produced food assistance and food education services to eligible Montgomery County households. Individual awards are expected to range from $100,000 to $300,000, with final award amounts potentially lower than $100,000. The grant performance period is anticipated to be twelve (12) months, from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027, with the opportunity for renewal for one additional year contingent on performance, continued need, and availability of funds. Applicants must meet graduated match requirements: Year 1 minimum 15% match (up to 10% in-kind) and Year 2 minimum 25% match (15% in-kind).
structured_extraction.contact_name: Greg Weissman, Program Manager II, OGM and Catherine Nardi, Program Manager, OFSR
structured_extraction.program_audience: Healthcare providers, clinics, federally qualified health centers (FQHCs), hospital systems, community clinics, nonprofit organizations in formal partnership with healthcare providers, and organizations that serve Montgomery County households with children aged 0-18 who screen positive for food insecurity and have diet-related disease, as well as healthcare and clinic-based organizations providing food assistance to residents experiencing food insecurity and diet-related health conditions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports clinical screening for food insecurity and diet-related disease among pediatric patients; food purchasing and distribution of medically relevant foods through choice markets, pre-packaged boxes or bags, retail vouchers, or hybrid models; recurring access to medically relevant food on a minimum biweekly basis; evidence-based nutrition education aligned with clinical goals; structured transitions and warm handoffs connecting households to ongoing food assistance and nutrition benefit supports; enrollment and referral coordination; data collection, tracking, and reporting; and program coordination with food partners, educators, and clinical staff. Programs should provide meaningful quantities of food intended to supplement household nutrition needs during a defined enrollment period of approximately three to nine months per family.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. All activities and expenditures under this grant program must be provided in Montgomery County and/or be exclusively for Montgomery County residents. The organization's principal place of business must be located in Montgomery County; if a national or regional organization, it must have a location in Montgomery County through which it provides related services.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted through the Montgomery County Office of Grants Management Grants Application Platform (https://gn.ecivis.com/GO/gn_redir/T/17b6541nxefcw) using the Euna (eCivis) Portal. To apply: (1) Log into the eCivis Portal and create an application profile; (2) Access the FY26 Food as Medicine Grant Program Solicitation Page and click the Apply button; (3) Complete all required application sections; (4) Submit before the deadline. Applicants should review the Euna applicant user guides and instructional videos available on OGM's Resources for Applicants Webpage. An informational session is scheduled for Tuesday, February 24, 2026 from 12:00 PM to 1:00 PM EST via MS Teams meeting. Applications received after the deadline will be disqualified. OGM will conduct an Administrative Review assessing Montgomery County Eligibility Conditions and application completeness. OFSR will conduct a Programmatic Eligibility Review. An independent Subject Matter Expert Review Committee composed of neutral, qualified individuals will review and score proposals based on established criteria and submit recommendations for funding. Final decisions will be made based on scores and other factors deemed relevant by the County. Award notification letters are expected approximately three weeks after the deadline. Successful applicants will receive a Grant Agreement containing the total amount awarded, funding restrictions, programmatic and administrative requirements, and payment terms. Award winners must submit semi-annual programmatic and financial reports during grant implementation and participate in regular check-ins with the Grantor.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Resident and Community Gardening Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program provides funding to support resident and community gardening projects that increase the volume of fresh, edible food available to Montgomery County residents experiencing food insecurity. The program expands the capacity of eligible nonprofit organizations to provide residents with access to yard, patio, and community gardening supplies, space, and education. It supports initiatives that expand resident and community food production capacity as a means of increasing local food security, including access to land, education, and resources to grow their own food. The program supports scalability and sustainability of projects with demonstrated success in resident and community gardening program design and implementation that are rooted in research and best practices.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $200,000 in total grant funding is available. Individual awards are expected to range from $25,000 to $100,000, with final award amounts potentially lower. The grant performance period is anticipated to cover 17 months from on/about June 30, 2026 to November 1, 2027, with opportunity for renewal for one additional year (12 months) contingent on performance, continued need, and availability of funds. Historically, the FY24 program awarded $210,559 to 7 grantees for a 15-month grant period. The funded projects engaged more than 2,000 County residents and produced more than 4,000 pounds worth of crops for donation to the County's food assistance network. Applicants must provide a minimum 25% match (up to 10% in-kind) for the initial grant performance period. For a renewal year, applicants may be funded at 25% of the initial grant award and must meet an increased match requirement of 75% (not including in-kind).

Organizations must be registered and in Good Standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and have Current standing with Maryland Secretary of State OneStop – Charities Public Registry.

Grant funding cannot be used for any purchase already made, purchases or activities unnecessary to accomplish grant purposes, prior obligations or fines, debts and penalties, lobbying expenses, alcoholic beverages, pet food, or supplanting other funds.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) and program requirements. 2. structured_extraction.program_description: A commuter benefits program administered by Montgomery County that encourages private employers to provide transit and vanpool subsidies to their employees. The county reimburses employers for contributions made above a minimum threshold, up to the federal maximum of $325 per month per employee (effective January 1, 2025), to help reduce traffic congestion, lower pollution, and support clean air goals. Employees receive enhanced commuting benefits at a lower cost, including tax-free transit subsidies. Employers can also receive a Maryland state tax credit for their contributions. Benefits are also available for bikers and walkers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county reimburses employers for transit benefit contributions made to employees. Employers must contribute at least $25 per month per employee. Montgomery County will contribute toward the benefit up to $325 less the $25 required by the employer per employee per month (effective January 1, 2025), with a maximum reimbursement of $40,000 per year to any single employer. Employers are also eligible for a Maryland state tax credit of 50 percent of their contribution, up to a maximum of $100 per employee per month. Employees receive transit subsidies up to $325 per month tax-free (effective January 1, 2025) to help pay commuting costs. The program is offered on a first-come, first-served basis and is contingent upon the availability of funds. FareShare is not intended to provide an ongoing County subsidy, but to help employers with start-up costs and incorporating commuter benefits costs into their budgeting.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private employers in Montgomery County and their employees. Public sector employers are not eligible. Employees can live anywhere and still participate. Program supports employers with recruitment and retention of employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transit and vanpool commuting costs for employees. Benefits also available for bikers and walkers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Employers must have a business location in Montgomery County or employees working in Montgomery County. Employees can live anywhere and still be eligible.
requirements_list: Employer must be a private sector employer (public sector employers are ineligible)
Employer must be located in or have a business location in Montgomery County
Employer must offer a minimum transit benefit contribution of $25 per employee per month
Employer must complete the FareShare Employer Enrollment Form
Total benefit provided to any employee cannot exceed their actual commuting cost
Employers must be able to sustain the benefit level once the county match ends
Employers must conduct a pre-program survey of employees at the worksite prior to implementation of the FareShare program
Employers are expected to participate in subsequent Commuter Surveys every other year to evaluate impact on employee commuting choice
Employers must use best efforts to achieve a survey response rate acceptable to the County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Employer contacts MCDOT Commuter Services at 240-773-2989 or mcdot.CommuterServices@montgomerycountymd.gov to set up the program. If the employer does not currently offer a direct transit/vanpool benefit, Commuter Services will assist them in starting a commuter benefits program. Marketing specialists will visit the office free of charge to help tailor a commuting benefits program to the company's needs. 2. Employer completes the FareShare Employer Enrollment Form. 3. Employer conducts a pre-program survey of employees at the worksite prior to implementation. 4. After enrollment, employer submits the Montgomery County Employer Worksheet Invoice and WMATA SmartBenefits Order Confirmation Form to the Commuter Services representative. 5. Employer receives reimbursement from the County. 6. Employers participate in subsequent Commuter Surveys every other year to evaluate impact on employee commuting choice. Employees can ask their employer to download the FareShare brochure or contact MCDOT for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Fiscal Year 2022 Community Services Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services provides grants to community organizations to support health and human services in the county. The program provides one-time only grants to non-profit organizations serving Montgomery County residents for approved equipment and other capital purchases, with a priority focus on COVID-19 or COVID-19 recovery related projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $10,000 are provided to support health and human service projects. The program provides one-time only reimbursement grants to non-profit organizations for approved equipment and other capital purchases, including capital improvements, equipment, and associated delivery and setup costs. Grant awards are distributed via reimbursement upon receipt of proof of payment and required documentation verifying the purchase of approved items. Funded projects and expenditures must occur between July 1, 2021 and June 30, 2022. Eligible expenses include capital expenditures (renovations, equipment, technology improvements), purchase of goods, and staff training related to COVID-19 or COVID-19 recovery. Ineligible expenses include vehicles, salaries, conferences, training costs not related to equipment purchases, and funds to apply to deficits or losses in other funding sources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations incorporated under 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code providing health and human services activities in Montgomery County. Organizations who have not received funding for the last three years will be given priority.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements and equipment purchases for health and human service programs, with preference given to COVID-19 or COVID-19 recovery related projects. Funds can be used for renovations, equipment, technology improvements, and purchase of goods. Funds may not be used for vehicles, personnel salaries, non-local travel, or replacement of lost or reduced Federal, State, United Way or other funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County. Organizations must operate in and provide direct service to residents of Montgomery County. Organizations may have headquarters and/or administrative offices outside of Montgomery County if they demonstrate that client populations served by the award reside in Montgomery County. Grant-funded projects must be implemented in Montgomery County only.
requirements_list: Must be a not-for-profit agency, organization, institution, or association incorporated under 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code
Must provide services in Montgomery County
Must provide health and human services activities
Must submit IRS not-for-profit designation proof
Must submit proof of incorporation from State Department of Assessment and Taxation
Must provide complete project budget with all needed equipment, quantities, specifications, manufacturer details, drawings, photographs or renderings
Must provide complete organizational budget for current fiscal year
Must provide current list of Board of Directors
Must submit Grant Application Checklist as cover page
Must include narrative clearly listing all proposed items, explaining nature and purpose, and demonstrating contribution to stated outcomes
May submit only one application per grant period per organization
Organizations that have not received funding for the last three years will be given priority
Project must not duplicate or supplant funding for any existing activities or efforts
Cannot fund projects with existing deficit from previous year or previous project
Cannot fund organizations that received previous awards and did not comply with award terms including submission of project reports and participation in monitoring visits
Cannot fund projects requiring more than one-time grant award
Cannot fund projects implemented before July 1, 2021 or after June 30, 2022
Cannot fund organizations with outstanding dispute with Department and/or County
Item(s) must be used solely for purpose outlined in application for period up to two years following award of funds
Awardees must acknowledge Montgomery County in all publicity and promotional materials
Awardees must submit within 30 days of project completion a brief summary (not more than 3 pages) of how grant was used and how it contributed to stated outcomes
Awardees must be in compliance with Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit typed applications on appropriate forms with required attachments electronically to Community.ServicesGrants@montgomerycountymd.gov by 3:00 p.m. on Wednesday, April 7, 2021. All applications are subject to an initial acceptance review including completeness, legibility, compliance with guidelines, and fiscal accuracy. Incomplete applications will be returned without consideration. Complete applications are reviewed by a Grants Review Panel including public and private representatives, chaired by the Director of DHHS or designee. The Panel reviews applications based on evaluation criteria. The Review Panel presents recommendations to the Montgomery County Executive, who determines final approval based on availability of funds. Final determination of awards is subject to County Council approval during annual budget review. Grant applications will be reviewed and grants announced by July 1, 2021. Awardees are required to submit organizational invoices with documentation confirming payment and receipt of approved items for reimbursement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that provides funding to states, local communities, federally recognized tribes, and territories to reduce or eliminate the risk of repetitive flood damage to buildings insured by the National Flood Insurance Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal competitive grant funding for flood mitigation projects. FMA provides up to 75% federal funding for eligible activities, with a 25% non-federal cost share requirement. For repetitive loss (RL) properties, up to 90% federal funding may be available. For severe repetitive loss (SRL) properties, up to 100% federal funding may be available. The program prioritizes repetitive loss and severe repetitive loss projects. Communities must be in good standing with the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP), and properties must have active NFIP policies. Projects are ranked by the applicant and FEMA selects recipients based on eligibility, cost-effectiveness, and benefit-cost analysis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Notices of Interest due in August; deadline varies based on federal Notice of Funding Opportunities (NOFO) announcement
structured_extraction.program_audience: State agencies, local governments (county agencies and municipalities), tribal governments, tribal agencies, private nonprofit organizations, and federally recognized tribes in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that reduce or eliminate the risk of repetitive flood damage to buildings insured by the National Flood Insurance Program, including property acquisition and demolition, structure elevation, mitigation reconstruction, floodproofing of historic residential structures, localized and non-localized flood risk reduction, structural and non-structural retrofitting, and other eligible mitigation activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland and participating jurisdictions nationwide. Applications must be submitted through the State of Maryland (MDEM). Communities must be in good standing with the National Flood Insurance Program.
requirements_list: Must be a state agency, local government, tribal government, private nonprofit organization, or federally recognized tribe
Must be in good standing with the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP)
Property must have an active NFIP policy (for structure projects)
Must provide 25% non-federal cost share (exceptions: RL properties may be eligible for 90% federal share; SRL properties may be eligible for 100% federal share)
Cannot use federal funds for the 25% non-federal cost share
Project cannot be started or completed before the kick-off meeting with MDEM
Project must align with an approved FEMA Hazard Mitigation Plan compliant with 44 CFR Part 201
Project must reduce or eliminate risk of repetitive flood damage to NFIP insured buildings
Hazard Mitigation Plan must be current (not expired)
Must comply with environmental and historic preservation requirements
Must meet technical feasibility and effectiveness standards
Must demonstrate cost-effectiveness through benefit-cost analysis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a Notice of Interest (NOI) to OEMHS by August deadline. The NOI should indicate HMA program preference, activity type, project location, hazard mitigation plan alignment, cost estimates, and non-federal funding sources. 2. OEMHS reviews NOIs for basic applicability across the three HMA programs (BRIC, FMA, HMGP). 3. Upon preliminary approval, OEMHS provides technical assistance to develop the project. 4. Approved subapplicants submit complete subapplications to FEMA through MDEM, including scope of work, budget, cost-effectiveness documentation (benefit-cost analysis), environmental and historic preservation documentation, and required certifications. 5. FEMA reviews subapplications for eligibility and cost-effectiveness using the Benefit-Cost Analysis Toolkit or streamlined methodologies. 6. FEMA selects recipients based on project ranking, eligibility criteria, cost-effectiveness, and availability of funding. 7. Selected subapplicants receive an award package and enter into a grant agreement with FEMA.
attachment_urls: https://www.montgomerycountymd.gov/OEMHS/Resources/Files/Hazard Mitigation Assistance Program and Policy Guide (2024).pdf
