structured_extraction.program_description: A rebate program that provides financial incentives for property owners to install green roofs designed to hold special soil and plants. Green roofs treat stormwater runoff by capturing rainfall, helping conserve energy, reduce stormwater runoff, support pollinator populations, and extend roof lifespan. Studies show that 50-60% of annual rainfall can be captured by green roofs, significantly reducing runoff and environmental impact.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebate of $9 per square foot of green roof installed. Residential properties may receive a maximum rebate of $7,500; commercial and institutional properties may receive a maximum rebate of $20,000. Minimum installation size is 100 square feet for residential applications and 200 square feet for commercial/institutional applications. Only extensive green roofs constructed on existing buildings (retrofits) are eligible; green roofs for new construction are not eligible at this time.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential and commercial property owners in Montgomery County outside the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park who want to install extensive green roofs on existing buildings to reduce stormwater runoff and conserve energy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of extensive green roofs with 4 inches of growing media on existing roofs. Green roofs must include waterproof membrane, filter fabric, drainage layer, root barrier, growing medium (soil), and drought-tolerant plants. Soil depth must be 4 inches and not exceed 28 lbs per square foot when saturated.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, but outside the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park. Property must be on private land with a structurally sound, existing roof.
requirements_list: Minimum 100 square feet for residential applications; 200 square feet for commercial/institutional applications
Maximum green roof must not exceed one-quarter of total roof area
Green roof must replace existing roof area, not expand roof footprint
Growing media depth must be 4 inches, not exceeding 28 lbs per square foot when saturated
Structural analysis report from licensed structural engineer required, certifying roof can carry green roof load
Rooftop must be adequately waterproofed before green roof installation
Planting plan with graphic scale showing plant quantities and locations required
Installer must be certified green roof contractor with previous experience, approved by RainScapes staff
Minimum 2-year workmanship warranty from installer required
Green roof components must have minimum 5-year manufacturer's warranty
Pass preliminary inspection for site suitability before installation begins
Pass final inspection after project completion
Property must be located outside Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park municipalities
HOA approval letter if applicable
Project must be installed within six months of approval letter date
Installation must be performed by certified green roof contractor; do-it-yourself not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the Green Roof Project Manual and design manual on the website. 2. Complete the online RainScapes Rewards rebate application at rainscapes.org. 3. Submit application; confirmation email will be sent from RainScapes@montgomerycountymd.gov. 4. Schedule and attend mandatory preliminary inspection with Department of Environmental Protection before installation begins. 5. Submit all required supporting documents (structural analysis report, planting plan, HOA approval if applicable). 6. Receive approval letter with rebate funding details and property owner agreement. 7. Begin project installation within six months of approval letter date. 8. Schedule and complete final inspection after project completion. 9. Address any necessary adjustments identified at final inspection and photo-document corrections. 10. Submit itemized receipts (with sales tax subtracted) and electronically-signed property owner agreement. 11. Rebate check issued by Montgomery County Department of Finance after final inspection approval and receipt submission.

Participants pay a limited percentage of their income (generally 30% to 40%) as rent, and the housing subsidy is paid directly to the landlord by the Housing Opportunities Commission (HOC) on behalf of the family. The voucher is portable anywhere in the United States, including Guam, Puerto Rico, Alaska, Hawaii, and the Virgin Islands.

The voucher is portable anywhere in the United States, including Guam, Puerto Rico, Alaska, Hawaii, and the Virgin Islands.

structured_extraction.program_description: The HOME Investment Partnerships Program is a federal funding source designed to increase affordable housing choices for low-income households by supporting the development, acquisition, rehabilitation, and preservation of rental and homeownership housing. In Montgomery County, HOME funds are loaned or granted to non-profit and for-profit developers for a variety of affordable housing activities including new construction, acquisition, rehabilitation, and tenant-based rental assistance. The program requires deeply affordable rental units with 90% at or below 60% AMI, and mandates ongoing compliance monitoring for up to 20 years. In fiscal year 2026, Montgomery County received approximately $2 million in HOME funds.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HOME funds are loaned or granted to non-profit and for-profit developers for affordable housing activities including acquisition, rehabilitation, new construction, and tenant-based rental assistance. In FY2026, Montgomery County received approximately $2 million in HOME funds. For rental projects, 90% of units must be at or below 60% AMI; if more than five units are involved, 20% must be at or below 50% AMI. Homeownership projects can assist persons earning up to 80% AMI. Funds are tied to individual units monitored for up to 20 years, with an annual maximum subsidy per unit. Federal Davis-Bacon wage rates apply at 12 units or more. Property owners and managers of HOME-assisted units must maintain compliant tenant files documenting income eligibility for occupants and perform annual recertifications. Interest rates are typically set at 0-3%, though can range from 1% to prevailing market rates. Loan repayments can be structured as monthly amortization, deferred payments, or based on available cash flow. The period of affordability varies by project type: new construction requires 20 years of affordability restrictions; rehabilitation/acquisition periods depend on HOME cost per unit (under $15,000 = 5 years; $15,000-$40,000 = 10 years; over $40,000 = 15 years). Montgomery County may establish longer affordability terms extending for the life of the HOME loan, typically 30-40 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and for-profit housing developers and property owners/managers seeking to create, acquire, or rehabilitate multifamily affordable rental and homeownership housing in Montgomery County, as well as property managers of existing HOME-assisted units.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable housing production and preservation, including new construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of rental and homeownership units, and tenant-based rental assistance. Eligible direct costs include labor, materials, and construction costs; energy efficiency improvements; utility connections; inspection, testing, and abatement of lead-based paint; relocation costs; soft costs such as financing fees, credit reports, legal and accounting fees, appraisals, architectural and engineering fees, environmental reviews, and affirmative marketing; handicap accessibility improvements. HOME funds may not be used for operating costs, non-residential accessory structures, off-site infrastructure costs, or organizational costs such as partnership formation or syndication costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Montgomery County, Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible developers and owners submit applications to the Department of Housing and Community Affairs (DHCA). The Multifamily Loan Application requires information needed for a normal development project. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with no deadlines. DHCA staff conducts application review and underwriting analysis, evaluating cost reasonableness, market demand, developer capacity, and commitment of other funding sources. The Housing Loan Review Committee (HLRC), comprised of private citizens and designated county staff knowledgeable in affordable housing development and finance, reviews applications and makes recommendations to the Director of DHCA regarding allocation and funding conditions. The Director of DHCA reviews committee recommendations and determines which proposals will be funded and the loan terms based on project needs. Upon approval, developers receive funding via low interest or cash flow loans, typically at 0-3% interest, with funds available at closing or as needed. Environmental clearance must be obtained before committing or expending any HOME funds on physical improvements. Property owners and managers must maintain ongoing compliance documentation for HOME-assisted units, including annual tenant recertification forms, tenant file audits, and compliance reports.

structured_extraction.program_name: Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP) and HMGP Post Fire
structured_extraction.program_description: FEMA funding for state, local, tribal, and territorial governments to develop hazard mitigation plans and rebuild in ways that reduce future disaster losses in their communities. The program includes a Post Fire component that specifically addresses long-term secondary hazards such as floods, erosion, and mudflows created by wildfires. Funding is available after a presidentially declared disaster (including wildfire disasters) when requested by an authorized representative.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funding available after a presidentially declared disaster, including wildfire disasters. The program provides up to 75% federal cost share (with a 25% non-federal cost share required), though small impoverished communities may be eligible for up to 90% federal share under BRIC funding. Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA) funds may be used to pay up to 75% of eligible activity costs. Eligible applicants must provide a 25% non-federal cost share (federal funds cannot be used for this share) and cannot start or complete projects before the kick-off meeting with MDEM. MDEM is the pass-through agency and disburses grant awards. Non-federal cost share can be provided as in-kind donations or cash match from third parties or contributed by the agency, and must be provided and expended during the project period along with federal funds to satisfy matching requirements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Notices of Interest due in August; deadline varies based on federal Notice of Funding Opportunities (NOFO) announcement
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (county agencies and municipalities), tribal governments, state agencies, tribal agencies, and private nonprofit organizations in Montgomery County, including those affected by wildfire disasters. Federally recognized tribal governments also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Sustainable actions that reduce or eliminate long-term risk to people and property from future disasters, including wildfires and wildfire-related secondary hazards such as floods, erosion, and mudflows. Eligible activities include property acquisition and demolition, structure elevation, mitigation reconstruction, floodproofing, localized and non-localized flood risk reduction, structural and non-structural retrofitting, wind retrofit, infrastructure retrofit, soil stabilization, hazard mitigation planning, and capacity and capability building activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland and participating jurisdictions including cities and towns of Gaithersburg, Rockville, Takoma Park, Barnesville, Brookeville, Chevy Chase, Glen Echo, Kensington, Laytonsville, Poolesville, Somerset, Washington Grove, and villages.
requirements_list: Must be a local government, tribal government, state agency, tribal agency, or private nonprofit organization
Must provide 25% non-federal cost share (minimum)
Cannot use federal funds for the 25% non-federal cost share
Project cannot be started or completed before the kick-off meeting with MDEM
Project must align with an approved local or state hazard mitigation plan in accordance with 44 CFR Part 201
Entity must not be delinquent on any federal debt
For NFIP-related projects, community must be in good standing with the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP)
For flood insurance requirements, properties must have an active NFIP policy for structure projects
Funding is only activated following a Presidential Disaster Declaration (for HMGP and HMGP Post Fire)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a Notice of Interest (NOI) in August following a presidentially declared disaster (including wildfire disasters) to OEMHS. The NOI must indicate interest in one of the HMA programs (BRIC, FMA, or HMGP) and include project details, hazards addressed, mitigation actions, cost estimates, and potential funding sources for the non-federal cost-share. 2. OEMHS reviews NOIs for basic applicability and determines which HMA program is appropriate. 3. Upon determination of program applicability, OEMHS provides technical assistance to subapplicants. 4. Subapplicants develop detailed subapplications using FEMA's electronic grants management system, including scope of work, schedule, budget, cost-effectiveness analysis documentation, and environmental/historic preservation documentation. 5. OEMHS submits recommended sub-applications to FEMA through Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM). 6. FEMA reviews applications for eligibility and award determination. 7. Upon approval, MDEM is the pass-through agency and disburses grant awards to subrecipients. Subapplicants must attend a kick-off meeting with MDEM before starting or completing any project work.

structured_extraction.program_description: A sustainability-themed Artist-In-Residence project that invites community-based artists and arts collectives to engage with staff and community participants through hands-on art making activities over six months. The project focuses on skill sharing, collaboration, and creating visual artwork that explores themes of community climate resilience, to be displayed inside the Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services building. The project arose from a shared desire to strengthen community ties in the face of climate hazards, build social support and facilitate healing, promote environmental ethics, and promote a sense of agency on the part of DHHS clients.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Selected artist or team receives an all-inclusive honorarium stipend of $18,000 covering all artist fees, fabrication and production costs, art-making materials, meeting costs, documentation, transportation, insurance, and other residency-related costs. Up to four finalists also receive $500 each for developing proposals. The residency runs for a maximum of 6 months with an expected completion date in June 2024.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based artists and arts collectives residing in Montgomery County who are at least 18 years old and not enrolled as full-time students. Artists in underrepresented communities including Black, Indigenous, Native American, Latinx, Chicanx, Arab, MENASA, Asian, Pacific Islander, communities of color, socio-economically disadvantaged communities, differently abled individuals, and LGBTQ+ constituents are highly encouraged to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creation of environmentally themed visual artwork through collaborative art-making workshops with DHHS clients and staff, culminating in installation of 2-3 non-permanent artworks within the DHHS building at 1301 Piccard Drive. Artists may work in any visual media that engages and/or is a result of working with the collective staff and constituents (e.g., mural, mosaic, collage, etc.). The resulting artwork should beautify the space, represent its creators, encourage thoughtful engagement on themes of community climate resilience, and contribute to a positive environment for clients and staff.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must reside in Montgomery County, MD with a verifiable mailing address in Montgomery County. Artwork will be created and installed at 1301 Piccard Drive in Rockville, MD 20850.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Phase One: Submit application materials electronically via online form by November 6, 2023 at 5:00pm. Submissions must include CV/resume (up to 2 pages), current artist statement, narrative responses to three questions about artistic interests and community engagement experience, and up to 10 images of past work with detailed descriptions. A community-based selection panel reviews submissions and invites up to four finalists to Phase Two. Phase Two: Selected finalists have six weeks to develop and submit detailed proposals for community workshops and final artwork design process. Finalists are scheduled to tour the facility for deeper understanding and receive a $500 honorarium for their efforts. Finalists present proposals to the selection panel via Zoom. The selection panel awards the residency to one artist or team based on submitted materials using criteria including demonstrated community engagement, experience with similar budgets, experience presenting work publicly, collaborative skills, ability to meet timeframes, and clarity of proposal. The selected artist/team begins residency in January 2024 with a completion date of June 2024. Optional info session available Thursday, October 26, 3:00-4:00pm via Zoom. Optional facility tours available by request until October 27 (requests must be received at least 5 days in advance, limited to 15 people per tour).

Employers must submit proof of purchase of each new home computer or laptop, including the date of purchase and the cost of each computer or laptop.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Fire and Rescue Service provides complimentary home safety visits to residents. A trained representative checks working smoke alarms, replaces outdated or non-functioning alarms, changes backup batteries, identifies fire hazards, helps develop home fire escape plans, and provides fire safety education. The program prioritizes high-risk individuals including older adults, seniors, and people with disabilities or economic challenges.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free in-person or virtual home safety visits. MCFRS personnel check all smoke alarms for proper operation, replace backup batteries in hard-wired alarms as needed, recommend replacement of outdated alarms (over 10 years old) or non-functioning units, identify home fire hazards, assist with developing home fire escape plans, and provide fire safety education. Installation of free alarms is targeted to high-risk individuals including older adults, seniors, individuals with mobility, vision or hearing impairments, and residents with disabilities or economic challenges. Specialized smoke alarms are available for deaf and hearing impaired individuals. No cost to residents. Smoke alarm requirements vary by home construction date: homes built before July 1, 1975 may use battery-only alarms (must have sealed, tamper-resistant 10-year long-life batteries with silence button); homes built July 1, 1975 or later require hard-wired alarms with battery backup. All smoke alarms must be replaced after 10 years from manufacture date. Alarms must be located outside each sleeping area and on every level of the home, including basements. For new construction after July 1, 1997, at least one alarm must be inside each sleeping room.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Montgomery County, Maryland, particularly older adults, seniors, individuals with mobility, vision, or hearing impairments, and residents with disabilities or economic challenges.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free home safety visits including smoke alarm inspection, testing, battery replacement, and installation of complimentary alarms for eligible residents. Also includes fire hazard identification and fire escape plan development. Assistance with understanding Maryland smoke alarm code requirements based on home construction date.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home and Community-Based Services Waiver for Individuals with Brain Injury
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides home and community-based services for adults with brain injury to enable independent living in the community as an alternative to institutional care. The waiver enables individuals with brain injury to receive necessary services and support in the community instead of in institutional settings, funded through Medicaid.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid waiver providing residential habilitation, day habilitation, supported employment, individual support services, case management, and medical day care. Additional Medicaid State Plan services include physician and hospital care, pharmacy services, home health services, laboratory services, mental health services, disposable medical supplies, durable medical equipment, and payment of Medicare premiums, co-payments, and deductibles.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults with brain injury requiring specialty hospital or nursing facility level of care
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Residential habilitation, day habilitation, supported employment, individual support services, case management, medical day care, physician and hospital care, pharmacy services, home health services, laboratory services, mental health services, disposable medical supplies, durable medical equipment, and payment of Medicare premiums, co-payments, and deductibles
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Diagnosis of brain injury requiring specialty hospital or nursing facility level of care
Brain injury occurred after the age of 17

Currently or formerly inpatient in a State Behavioral Health Administration facility, state-owned and operated nursing facility, Maryland licensed Special Hospital for Chronic Disease accredited by CARF for Brain Injury Inpatient Rehabilitation, or placed by Medicaid in an out-of-state facility
Must meet financial eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Maryland Department of Health, Behavioral Health Administration at 410-402-8476 or 1-877-463-3464 (Toll Free) for application and eligibility determination.

structured_extraction.program_description: A specialized post-arrest diversion program for individuals experiencing homelessness who have been accused of specific nonviolent misdemeanors or who have outstanding warrants for misdemeanors and transit or traffic offenses. The program resolves open misdemeanor criminal, traffic, and transit matters for persons who are homeless or have been homeless, using a voluntary engagement model. Participants work with service providers to develop and complete action plans, with successful completion resulting in charges being dropped and records expunged.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides post-arrest diversion services for individuals experiencing homelessness who have been accused of specific nonviolent misdemeanors or have outstanding warrants. Participants are referred to the program and, if approved by the State's Attorney's Office, meet with a legal representative and service providers at a monthly meeting (held the second Wednesday of each month from 2-4 p.m. at Progress Place in Silver Spring). Together they develop an action plan addressing their needs in areas such as housing, healthcare, behavioral health, benefits, and employment. Charges are placed on the STET docket for up to 90 days while the participant engages with services. Upon satisfactory completion of the service plan, the State's Attorney's Office will nolle prosequi the charges, and the Homeless Persons Representation Project will file for expungement of the criminal record. Participation is entirely voluntary, and participants retain all due process rights.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals experiencing homelessness who are on the street, in a shelter, doubled-up in another person's household, in a motel, or in a place unfit for human habitation, and who have been accused of specific nonviolent misdemeanors or have outstanding warrants for misdemeanors and transit or traffic offenses in Montgomery County District Court.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program does not provide direct financial assistance. It provides post-arrest diversion services to help resolve criminal matters outside traditional prosecution. Service providers connected through the program may offer assistance with first month's rent, security deposits, housing location, mental health treatment, substance use treatment, vocational services, case management, benefits enrollment, and civil legal services including expungement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Eligible individuals must have pending cases or warrants issued in Montgomery County District Court and cannot have pending criminal cases in Montgomery County Circuit Court.
requirements_list: Must be experiencing homelessness in Montgomery County using the broadest definition possible (on the street, in a shelter, doubled up with friends or family, in a motel, or in a place unfit for human habitation)

Must have been charged with a nonviolent misdemeanor or have an open warrant for a transit or traffic offense, including but not limited to: alcohol offenses (not DUI), drug possession/paraphernalia, disorderly conduct, panhandling, solicitation/prostitution, traffic offenses (not DUI), public urination, destruction of property, rogue and vagabond, theft, trespass, and Metro citations
Must have pending case(s) or warrant(s) issued in Montgomery County District Court
Cannot have pending criminal cases in Montgomery County Circuit Court
Voluntary participation required
Other misdemeanors not listed will be subject to case-by-case consideration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Referrals can be made by service/shelter providers, the Homeless Persons Representation Project, Office of the Public Defender, State's Attorney's Office, Montgomery County Police Department, Sheriff's Office, or by self-referral. Submit a referral form (available in English and Spanish) to hpcdp@montgomerycountymd.gov. Service providers can check the Maryland Judiciary Case Search online to verify if clients have outstanding warrants or cases. Upon referral, the Program Coordinator screens for homeless status through HMIS and forwards approved referrals to the State's Attorney's Office. The SAO reviews the case, including National Crime Information Center search results, to determine eligibility. If approved, the participant meets with a legal representative and service providers at the monthly HPCDP meeting held the second Wednesday of each month from 2-4 p.m. at Progress Place in Silver Spring. The legal representative explains the program, and if the participant voluntarily agrees to participate, they develop an action plan with assigned service providers. The case is placed on STET docket for up to 90 days while the participant engages in services. At the conclusion of 90 days, if the participant has satisfactorily engaged with their service provider, the State's Attorney will nolle prosequi the charges. The Homeless Persons Representation Project then files for expungement of the participant's records.

structured_extraction.program_name: Homeowner Tax Credit (Montgomery County General Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Homeowners with modest income and assets can receive a tax credit on their property taxes. Qualified homeowners age 60 and older also receive a 50% matching tax credit from Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners with modest income and assets qualify for a tax credit. Those age 60 and older receive an additional 50% matching tax credit from Montgomery County on top of the state credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners age 60 and older with modest income and assets living in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax reduction
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County
requirements_list: Age 60 or older (for 50% matching credit)
Modest income and assets
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the state homeowner tax credit program by the October 1 deadline

structured_extraction.program_description: Rental assistance for very low and extremely low-income households, the elderly, and the disabled. Provides a rent subsidy so that eligible households pay no more than 40% of total household income on housing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides a rent subsidy to customers so that they pay no more than 40% of total household income on housing. Vouchers can be used at any home, apartment, or other private market residence that meets household requirements, safety standards, and rent reasonableness standards.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Very low-income households, extremely low-income households, elderly individuals, and disabled individuals
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance for housing
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County
requirements_list: Very low or extremely low-income household status
Elderly or disabled status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Housing Opportunities Commission. More details on the HCV process are available on their website.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides one-time financial assistance up to $25,000 and/or technical assistance to financially healthy small businesses in designated areas of Montgomery County that are adversely impacted by a redevelopment project initiated by the County, on County-owned property, or of a County facility. Eligible designated areas include Silver Spring (Studio Plaza Project), Bethesda (Metro Station South Entrance CIP Project), and Clarksburg (Square Road Extension Project) related to specific County-related projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time financial assistance up to a maximum of $25,000 and/or technical assistance provided to eligible financially healthy small businesses in designated areas adversely impacted by County redevelopment projects. Grants are given on a one-time basis. Since inception in 2018, the program has disbursed $350,000 across 14 awards.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Financially healthy small businesses in designated areas of Montgomery County (Silver Spring, Bethesda, and Clarksburg) adversely impacted by County-related redevelopment projects or County facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To assist small businesses impacted by redevelopment projects initiated by the County, on County-owned property, or of a County facility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated geographic areas in Silver Spring (Studio Plaza Project), Bethesda (Metro Station South Entrance CIP Project), and Clarksburg (Square Road Extension Project) related to specific County-related projects. Only businesses currently experiencing adverse impact due to redevelopment projects in these designated areas are eligible.
requirements_list: Business must be financially healthy
Business must be located in a designated area (Silver Spring around Studio Plaza Project, Bethesda around Metro Station South Entrance CIP Project, or Clarksburg near Square Road Extension Project)
Business must be currently experiencing adverse impact due to a County redevelopment project
Maximum assistance per business is $25,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For additional information or to apply for this program, visit the Montgomery County Business Portal or contact the Division of Fiscal Management at (240) 777-8860.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's program that grants residential property owners who own and live in their property a $692 annual tax credit on their county income tax bill. The credit is automatic each year once a one-time Homestead Tax Credit application is approved and on file with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible homeowners receive a $692 annual tax credit applied to their county income tax bill. The credit is automatic each year once a Homestead Tax Credit (HTC) application is approved and on file with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). To receive the credit, homeowners must have the HTC on file with SDAT by May 1st. The application is a one-time requirement; once approved, the $692 credit automatically applies to future years without needing to reapply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who own and live in their primary residential property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The $692 credit is applied as an offset to county income tax liability owed by eligible homeowners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. Applicants must be residents of Montgomery County who own and live in the property as their primary residence.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must own residential property in Montgomery County
Must live in the property as primary residence
Must have a Homestead Tax Credit (HTC) application on file with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) by May 1st
Application is one-time only; once approved, the $692 credit automatically applies to future years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Check if you already have a Homestead Application on file by visiting the SDAT Real Property search website and looking for your 'Homestead Application Status'. Step 2: If no application is on file, obtain your Real Property Account Number from your SDAT letter or the property search results. Then file a Homestead Tax Credit Eligibility Application either online through the Maryland SDAT website or by mailing a paper application form to the address provided on the form. Once approved and on file, the $692 credit automatically applies to future years without needing to reapply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Income Tax Offset Tax Credit (ITOC) Reinstatement
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for owner-occupied residential properties in Montgomery County. Property owners with approved Homestead Tax Credit applications from the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation can apply for reinstatement of the credit if it was removed from their property tax bill.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit that applies to owner-occupied residential property tax bills. Eligible property owners must have an approved Homestead Tax Credit application on file with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Under Maryland law, a person can have only one property listed as their principal residence, and the Income Tax Offset Credit is available only for properties that are the owner's principal residence. Property owners can apply for reinstatement if the credit was removed from their bill. The credit amount previously referenced was $692.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Division of Treasury - Excise Tax Unit
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of residential properties in Montgomery County who have an approved Homestead Tax Credit application on file with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation and occupy the property as their principal residence
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit applied to residential property tax bills
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be owner-occupied residential property
Property must be applicant's principal residence
Property owner must have an approved Homestead Tax Credit (HTC) application on file with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Applicant must provide a copy of an electric bill from the last 2 months with the property address and applicant's name as the party being billed

Applicant must provide at least one of the following with matching address: current valid driver's license or government-issued ID, first page of most recent Maryland income tax return, or first page of most recent Federal income tax return
All documents submitted must show the same address as the property in question
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners can apply for reinstatement by submitting an Application for Reinstatement of the Income Tax Offset Credit form. The application can be submitted online or by mail to: Montgomery County Division of Treasury - Excise Tax Unit, 27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, Maryland 20850. Required documents must be attached and all addresses on documents must match the property address. Applicants must certify that they own the property and occupy it as their principal residence.

structured_extraction.program_name: Individuals 65 and Above and Retired Military Services Members Tax Credit (Bill 42-16)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County property tax credit for residents age 65 and older who have owned and lived in their home for at least 40 consecutive years, or for military retirees age 65 and older. The credit provides a 20% reduction on Montgomery County property taxes for owner-occupied dwellings and is granted for 7 consecutive years. The credit also extends to surviving spouses of deceased military retirees who meet certain requirements. Established under Bill 42-16.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The tax credit provides a 20% credit on Montgomery County property taxes only for owner-occupied dwellings. The credit is granted for 7 consecutive years and is not available after that 7-year period. The credit appears as a line item deduction on the property tax bill. Eligible residents must be age 65 and above and either: (1) have owned and lived in their home for at least 40 consecutive years, OR (2) be retired from the U.S. Armed Forces (Army, Navy, Air Force, Marines, Coast Guard), the uniformed services of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), the Public Health Service, military reserves, or National Guard. Surviving spouses of deceased eligible military retirees may also qualify. Assessment limits apply: $700,000 or less for 40+ year owners and $550,000 or less for military retirees.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Department of Finance, Division of Treasury
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Montgomery County age 65 and older who own and occupy their home and have done so for at least 40 consecutive years, military retirees age 65 and older, and surviving spouses of eligible deceased military retirees who have not remarried
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax reduction (20% credit on Montgomery County property taxes) for owner-occupied dwellings for up to 7 consecutive years
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only
requirements_list: Must be at least 65 years old (for Levy Year 2026, birthday must be on or before June 30, 1961)
For 40+ year owners: must have owned and lived in the dwelling for at least 40 consecutive years with deed dated June 30, 1986 or earlier

For military retirees: must be retired from the U.S. Armed Forces (Army, Navy, Air Force, Marines, Coast Guard), the uniformed services of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), the Public Health Service, military reserves, or National Guard (veteran status alone is not sufficient)
Must be on the deed for the property
Property must be owner-occupied
For 40+ year owners: dwelling must have an assessment of $700,000 or less at time of application
For military retirees: dwelling must have an assessment of $550,000 or less at time of application
For surviving spouses: military retiree must have been at least 65 years old or retired at death and retired from an eligible service, and surviving spouse must not have remarried
If property is titled in a trust, must complete and submit an Affidavit Re Trust Ownership
Must provide proof of age (Driver's License or Certificate of Live Birth)
For 40+ year owners: must provide copy of original deed
For military retirees: must provide copy of Retired Military I.D.
For surviving spouses: must provide death certificate, proof of deceased military retiree's retirement status (DD-214 or Retired Military I.D.), and affidavit certifying non-remarriage
Application must be complete with all required attachments
Credit is granted for 7 consecutive years and is not available after that 7-year period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the appropriate tax credit application form (standard application for 40+ year owners or military retirees, surviving spouse application, or trust ownership affidavit as needed). Gather all required documentation including proof of age (Driver's License or Certificate of Live Birth), deed (for 40+ year owners) or Retired Military I.D. (for military retirees), and any affidavits required. Mail the completed application and all required documents to the Department of Finance, Division of Treasury, Attn: Bill 42-16 Tax Credit, 27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, Maryland 20850 on or before April 1 of the tax year beginning July 1. Incomplete applications will not be processed. Approved applications submitted by the April 1 deadline will be processed on the property tax bill issued in July of the same year. For information, call 311 (in County) or 240-777-0311 (outside County).

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Consultation Support Services
structured_extraction.program_description: Free consultation services to support healthy social and emotional development for children birth to age 5 enrolled in licensed child care programs. Consultants work with parents and child care staff to develop strategies to help children form secure relationships, regulate emotions, and explore their environment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free mental health consultation services provided by trained consultants who observe children and classrooms, gather information through conversation with parents and child care staff, and develop individualized strategies. Services include resource referrals to other professionals such as pediatricians, occupational therapists, and speech therapists as requested by families. No fees are charged.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents and child care providers in licensed child care programs serving children birth to age 5 in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mental health consultation services and technical assistance for licensed child care settings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Child must be birth to 5 years old
Child must be enrolled in a licensed child care program
Services are not provided in before and/or after school programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call Montgomery County Child Care Support Services at 240-777-4769 (4769) to apply. No documents required to bring. Participants will be asked to complete a survey at the end of services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant at Risk Home Visiting Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A home visiting program that provides public health nursing services to new mothers and babies identified as at risk due to various circumstances including teen pregnancy, lack of prenatal care, substance use, mental health issues, intimate partner violence, housing instability, previous infant loss, preterm birth, or very low birthweight.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Home visits by a public health nurse to provide support and services to new mothers and babies meeting risk criteria. Services include home visiting and case management referrals. Services are provided at no cost to eligible families.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New mothers and babies in Montgomery County with identified risk factors such as teen pregnancy, lack of prenatal care, substance use, mental health concerns, intimate partner violence, housing instability, previous infant death, preterm birth history, or very low birthweight.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides home visiting services from public health nurses to support at-risk new mothers and infants through case management, maternal and infant medical follow-up, breastfeeding support, safe sleep education, and referrals to community services including mental health, substance use treatment, immunizations, WIC, and other supportive services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Services are available through the Silver Spring Health Center and the Germantown Health Center.
requirements_list: Teen mother (age less than 18)
No prenatal care or late prenatal care
History of substance use or misuse
Mental or behavioral health concerns
Intimate partner violence
Unstable housing or homelessness
Previous infant death
Previous preterm birth
Very low birthweight (less than 1500 grams)
Gestational age less than 34 weeks
Apgar score less than 4 at 5 minutes
Small for gestational age (SGA)
Birth defect or syndrome
Congenital infection
Positive toxicology screen
Anemia
Asthma
BMI less than 18.5 or BMI greater than or equal to 30
Chronic hypertension
Diabetes (Type I or Type II)
Physical disability
Sickle cell disease
Gestational diabetes (insulin dependent)
Gestational hypertension
Pre-eclampsia or eclampsia
Sexually transmitted infection
Age 40 or older
Lack of social or emotional support
Maternal-infant attachment or parenting deficit
Smoking or tobacco use
Alcohol use
CPS case involving family
History of abuse or violence
Any other circumstance deemed to be a serious risk for the mother or infant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a referral using the Maryland Postpartum Infant and Maternal Referral Form by facsimile (fax) to either the Silver Spring Health Center (240-777-3054) or the Germantown Health Center (240-777-4648). The referral form should be completed by the maternal care provider, hospital, or health department. After the referral is received, a public health nurse from the Maternal-Child Health Program will contact you to schedule home visits. No patient authorization is required for the referral form submission under HIPAA regulations for public health purposes.

structured_extraction.program_description: A residential electrical training program where participants complete on-the-job training and classroom instruction over approximately 5 years to become licensed electricians.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants complete 10,000 hours of on-the-job training (approximately 2,000 hours per year), fulfill 8 modules, and take 10 classes through computer-mediated online learning. Pay increases as participants move through the program. Trainees can be accepted as apprentices during the process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young people seeking residential electrical apprenticeships with no high school diploma or GED requirement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants receive paid on-the-job training in residential electrical work and complete computer-mediated learning courses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Main location in Washington DC near Springdale. Participants must have access to a computer and WiFi for online courses.
requirements_list: No GED or diploma required
Access to a computer and WiFi for online courses
Application fee of $50
Subscription fee of $150 for 12 months of access to PTSI system for CML (Computer Mediated Learning) courses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants apply online through the JATC 26 website. A $50 application fee is required. Once accepted, participants are placed with a signatory contractor of Local Union 26 IBEW.

structured_extraction.program_name: Keeping it SAFE: Under Twenty-One Alcohol Prevention Coalition Student Video Contest
structured_extraction.program_description: A student competition where teams from Montgomery County public and private high schools and middle schools, as well as faith-based or service-based organizations, create 30-second public service messages about the risks and dangers of underage alcohol use. Student teams compete for cash prizes awarded to their affiliated schools or organizations. The contest is organized by the Montgomery County Alcohol Beverage Services and Police Department and is part of the Keeping it SAFE: Under Twenty-One Alcohol Prevention Coalition. Participants are also eligible to earn 5 Service Learning (SSL) hours. The 2025-2026 contest cycle deadline is March 31, 2026 by 4:00 PM.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cash prizes awarded to participating student teams' affiliated schools or organizations. Checks are payable to schools or organizations only, not individual students. High school prizes: 1st place $1,000, 2nd place $500, 3rd place $350, Honorable Mention $100. Middle school prizes: 1st place $500, 2nd place $300, 3rd place $250, Honorable Mention $100. Additional $150 prize for the video receiving the most 'likes' on social media. Prizes are awarded at a reception hosted by Montgomery County Alcohol Beverage Services and the Police Department in early May. Participants are also eligible to earn 5 Service Learning (SSL) hours for participation. All entries become the property of the KIS Coalition, and winning entries may be submitted to multiple media outlets.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Student teams of two or more students enrolled in Montgomery County public or private high schools or middle schools, or in faith-based or service-based organizations in Montgomery County. Students must be under age 21 and between ages 10 and 18. All entries must have a sponsoring teacher.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creation of 30-second public service videos addressing one of three specified topics: (1) standing your ground against peer pressure to drink, (2) how underage alcohol consumption affects your future, or (3) social media's impact on underage alcohol consumption. Videos must be original content; copyrighted materials (including images, music, materials from magazines, books, DVDs, websites, films, or YouTube) may not be used without permission. Documented permission must be included if using copyrighted materials. Videos should not include clothing, language, or music that glorifies alcohol, drugs, sex, violence, or gang-related paraphernalia. Branded products should not be featured.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Students must be enrolled in Montgomery County public or private schools or in faith-based or service-based organizations located in Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Teams must consist of two or more students
Students must be enrolled in Montgomery County public or private schools (high school or middle school) or in faith-based or service-based organizations in Montgomery County
Students must be under age 21 and between ages 10 and 18
All entries must have a sponsoring teacher; no individual entries will be accepted
Video must be exactly 30 seconds in length; slates and credits cannot be overlaid onto the PSA or included in the 30 second message allotment; entries over 30 seconds will be disqualified
Video must address one of three specified topics about underage alcohol risks and dangers
Videos must not include copyrighted images, materials from magazines, books, DVDs, websites, films, YouTube, or music without documented permission
Videos must not include clothing, language, or music that glorifies alcohol, drugs, sex, violence, or gang-related paraphernalia
Branded alcohol products should not be featured; cover, distort, or make your own labels
Background music or sounds should not interfere with spoken dialogue
Screen text must be readable
Videos must be submitted in 16x9 aspect ratio in 720p or higher definition
TikToks are not allowed; YouTube Shorts must be submitted via public shared drive
Only one entry per student group
Each participating student must complete and submit a consent and release form
Online application must be completed with a link to the video entry submitted via public shared file link (e.g., Dropbox, Google Drive)
Checks for prizes are payable to schools or organizations only, not individual students
Sources of information must be listed on the reflection page
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students form teams of two or more and create a 30-second public service video on one of the three approved topics about underage alcohol prevention. Teams must submit the video via a public shared file link (such as Dropbox or Google Drive) in 16x9 aspect ratio at 720p or higher resolution. Teams complete an online application form through the Formstack portal and provide the link to their video entry. Each participating student must complete a separate consent and release form. Both the application and all release forms are submitted through the online application portal by the March 31, 2026 at 4:00 PM deadline. All entries become the property of the KIS Coalition. Winners are selected by a judging panel and contacted via email or phone. Prizes are awarded at a reception hosted by Montgomery County Alcohol Beverage Services and the Police Department in early May. Participating students who submit entries following all contest guidelines and submit video documents prior to the contest deadline receive 5 SSL hours in May 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between the Office of Human Resources and the Department of Health and Human Services that provides employment opportunities for individuals with disabilities who have limited work experience. The program aims to develop skills and gain experience that may lead to continued employment after the two-year term ends.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full-time or part-time paid positions lasting two years. Positions include benefits and eligibility to participate in Montgomery County Government's retirement plan. Applicants apply through the iRecruitment portal (work4mcg.com) by searching for LEAP4MCG positions. Each job posting is open for a minimum of two weeks. Applicants must upload their resume in Adobe PDF or Microsoft Word (DOCX) format and submit a Schedule A letter certifying disability status from the Maryland Department of Rehabilitation Services or equivalent out-of-state vocational rehabilitation agency.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Minimum of two weeks from job posting
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with severe disabilities who have limited work experience and have not previously held merit positions with Montgomery County Government
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment in full-time or part-time paid positions with Montgomery County Government
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Meet eligibility criteria for certification by the Maryland Department of Rehabilitation or equivalent out-of-state agency

Be certified by the Maryland Department of Education Division of Rehabilitation Services or equivalent out-of-state vocational rehabilitation agency as meeting the definition of persons with severe disabilities with a Schedule A Letter
Meet the minimum requirements for the specific position and be able to perform essential job functions with or without reasonable accommodation
Provide proof of full COVID-19 vaccination prior to first date of employment (or contact OHR for possible accommodations)
Not be a current or prior County merit employee
Complete all required sections of the Qualification Assessment including education, relevant experience, licenses, and certifications
Submit resume in Adobe PDF or Microsoft Word (DOCX) format
Provide workforce demographic information, veteran information, and disability information as required in the application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Open the iRecruitment Portal at ex12.montgomerycountymd.gov/irec_home/irec_home.htm. 2. Login using either Active Employee Login (for County employees) or AccessMCG Extranet Login (for non-employees). 3. Select the Search Jobs tab, choose job category (optional), enter 'LEAP4MCG' as a keyword, and click Search. 4. Select a LEAP4MCG job posting to view the full job description and requirements. 5. Click Apply Now and confirm the Employment Application Process Agreement. 6. Complete the Qualification Assessment section by responding to questions about education, relevant experience, knowledge, skills and abilities (allow at least 30 minutes). 7. Complete the Education and Relevant Experience section, providing details on education, years of experience, licenses, and certifications. 8. Complete any additional required sections (Knowledge, Skills and Abilities; Preferred Criteria, Competencies, and Skills). 9. Review your account information and update contact information and address as needed. 10. Upload your resume (must be Adobe PDF or Microsoft Word DOCX format). 11. Enter workforce demographic information, veteran information, and disability information. 12. Review all information and agree to the job posting agreement. 13. Click Finish to submit your application. 14. Confirm receipt of the confirmation message 'Thank you for submitting your application.' 15. Track your application status by logging back in and checking the Status column. Submit your Schedule A letter according to instructions in the job announcement. Application status will generally be updated after 10 business days from the job's closing date. Average time to fill positions ranges from three to eight weeks.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides financial protection and incentives to landlords who partner with Montgomery County to rent units to individuals transitioning out of homelessness. The fund helps minimize landlord risks related to property damage and lease violations while ensuring consistent occupancy of rental units.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides financial incentives and risk mitigation protections to landlords who rent to individuals supported through the homelessness services program. Landlords receive an annual limit of up to $5,000 in financial coverage per participating tenant for property damages beyond normal wear and tear, unpaid rent, or vacancy losses. The lifetime limit of financial coverage per participating tenant is $10,000. New landlords receive a one-time sign-on bonus of $500, and referred landlords receive $250. Rent is paid by both Montgomery County and the tenant depending on the eligible program (SHARP, Rapid Rehousing, Housing Initiative Program, or Permanent Supportive Housing). Landlords must first attempt to collect financial losses from the tenant, and if the tenant does not make payment arrangements within 10 business days, a claim form can be submitted. Claims must be filed within 45 days of lease term ending or tenant vacating. The fund covers property damages beyond normal wear and tear as defined by DHCA OLTA guidelines and loss of rent where eligible. LRMF will consider minimum reimbursements of $100.00. Payment is contingent upon approved claim amount and available funds in the program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing program with no defined application deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed and registered Montgomery County landlords and property owners who are willing to rent to individuals transitioning from homelessness and participating in eligible housing programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial reimbursement for property damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, unpaid rent, and vacancy losses when renting to supported tenants participating in eligible SEPH programs (SHARP, Rapid Rehousing, Housing Initiative Program, or Permanent Supportive Housing).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Tenants must be participating in one of the following eligible programs: Short-term Housing and Resolution Program (SHARP), Rapid Rehousing (RRH), Housing Initiative Program (HIP), or an eligible Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH) program that provides ongoing case management services. Rents must comply with HUD Fair Market Rent standards.
requirements_list: Landlord must be licensed and registered in Montgomery County
Landlord must sign the Landlord Risk Mitigation Fund Program Agreement
Landlord must provide a copy of the signed lease agreement
Tenant must be participating in one of the eligible SEPH programs: SHARP, Rapid Rehousing, Housing Initiative Program, or Permanent Supportive Housing
Pre move-in inspection must be completed by a SEPH designated housing service provider or housing locator prior to tenant move-in
All required documentation must be submitted within 15 calendar days of lease signing
Landlord must attempt to collect financial losses from tenant prior to submitting claim; if tenant does not make payment arrangements within 10 business days, claim can be submitted
Tenant initially occupied unit on or after March 1, 2024 (with exception for previously enrolled participants through 9/15/2023)
Landlord must follow lease terms in accordance with federal, state, and local law
Landlord must first contact tenant directly and follow standard lease procedures; if conflict continues, contact tenant's housing service provider
Landlord must participate in mitigation efforts with housing service provider and/or Office of Landlord Tenant Affairs prior to starting eviction
Landlord must notify program via LRMF email if tenant breaches lease without proper notice and work with SEPH to provide another tenant within 45 days
Damage must be beyond ordinary wear and tear as defined by DHCA OLTA guidelines
Landlord must use security deposit and other available financial resources prior to accessing LRMF for unpaid rent

For property damage claims during lease term or within 45 days of tenant exit, must provide detailed inspection comparison and supporting documentation including receipts, repair invoices, and itemized charges
For unpaid rent claims at end of lease term, must provide notice to vacate, collection efforts documentation, rent payment ledger, and insurance claim information if applicable
Landlord must disclose and submit copy of insurance claim payout information if filing with insurance for same damages
Annual limit of $5,000 per participating tenant; lifetime limit of $10,000 per participating tenant
Minimum reimbursement consideration is $100.00
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Landlord registers to participate by signing the Landlord Risk Mitigation Fund Program Agreement. 2. Landlord provides a copy of the signed lease agreement with tenant. 3. SEPH designated housing service provider or housing locator completes pre move-in inspection of the unit at no cost to the landlord, free of charge prior to tenant move-in date. 4. All required documentation must be submitted within 15 calendar days of lease signing via email to LRMF@montgomerycountymd.gov. 5. If property damage occurs or tenant defaults on lease, landlord contacts housing service provider to inform them of concerns. 6. Landlord completes the LRMF Claim Form with all required supporting documentation. 7. For property damage claims, landlord must first pay for repairs and then submit claim for reimbursement consideration. 8. For unpaid rent claims, must be filed at end of lease term only. 9. Landlord attempts to collect from tenant within 10 business days; if unsuccessful, submits claim. 10. Claims are reviewed on a case-by-case basis by the LRMF team. 11. All communication and claim submissions must be sent directly to LRMF@montgomerycountymd.gov. Inspection forms, claim forms, and program agreements are available for download from the website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that requires contractors on large Montgomery County procurement contracts to award at least 10% of contract dollars to local businesses, increasing participation of local businesses in county contracts valued over $10 million. Provides that at least 10% of contracting dollars awarded should go to local businesses and 10% of the total dollar value in aggregate should be awarded to local businesses as subcontractors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program requires that at least 10% of contract dollars for each High Dollar Value Contract (contracts exceeding $10 million) be awarded to local businesses. Additionally, at least 10% of the total dollar value of all High Dollar Value Contracts in aggregate must be awarded to local businesses. Contractors must submit a Local Business Subcontracting Program Performance Plan (PMMD-192) that details the local business subcontractors they will use, the percentage of total contract dollars to be paid to each local business subcontractor, and the goods/services each will provide. The plan covers the life of the contract including modifications and renewals. Local businesses must be certified by the Montgomery County Office of Procurement, Division of Business Relations and Compliance. A local business must have its principal place of business in Montgomery County, either with all physical locations in the county or with the majority of employees or gross sales based in the county. Contractors must include binding arbitration language in subcontracts to resolve disputes with local business subcontractors. Businesses must be registered in the Montgomery County Vendor Registration System and can be searched on www.mcipcc.net.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local businesses with principal place of business in Montgomery County that can serve as subcontractors on large county procurement contracts. Prime contractors on High Dollar Value Contracts (estimated to exceed $10 million) must comply with the subcontracting requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Businesses may bid as subcontractors on county procurement contracts, including subcontracting opportunities with Montgomery County and prime contractors. Prime contractors must allocate at least 10% of contract dollars to local business subcontractors for goods and services provided.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must have their principal place of business in Montgomery County, defined as having all physical business locations in Montgomery County, or having the majority of employees or gross sales located in Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Business must have principal place of business in Montgomery County

Business must have physical business location(s) only in Montgomery County, OR have physical business locations both in and outside the county with the county-based location(s) accounting for over 50% of the business's total number of employees or over 50% of gross sales
Business must be certified by the Montgomery County Office of Procurement, Division of Business Relations and Compliance
Eligible to participate as subcontractor on High Dollar Value Contracts (contracts estimated to exceed $10 million)
Must be registered in the Montgomery County Vendor Registration System and searchable on www.mcipcc.net
Prime contractors must submit completed PMMD-192 Local Business Subcontracting Program Performance Plan
Prime contractors must commit to a specified percentage of contract dollars to be paid to local business subcontractors
Prime contractors must list specific local business subcontractors with percentages and goods/services to be provided
Prime contractors must include binding arbitration language in subcontracts with local business subcontractors
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For local businesses: Businesses must qualify as local businesses meeting the principal place of business requirements in Montgomery County, become certified by the Montgomery County Office of Procurement Division of Business Relations and Compliance, and register in the Montgomery County Vendor Registration System at www.mcipcc.net. They can then be identified as potential subcontractors on county procurement contracts. For prime contractors: When awarded a High Dollar Value Contract (estimated to exceed $10 million), contractors must complete and submit the PMMD-192 Local Business Subcontracting Program Performance Plan, which details the local business subcontractors they will use, specifies the percentage of total contract dollars to be paid to each local business subcontractor, identifies the goods and services each will provide, and includes binding arbitration provisions for dispute resolution. The plan must be approved by the Director of the Office of Procurement and covers the entire life of the contract including modifications and renewals. For assistance, contact the LBSP program manager at DBRC@montgomerycountymd.gov or call 240-777-9913.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Local Small Business Reserve Program (LSBRP) ensures that Montgomery County government departments award at least 25 percent of their procurements for goods, services, and construction to registered and certified local small businesses, including non-profits. Administered by the Department of Procurement and the Division of Business Relations and Compliance (DBRC), the program helps County departments identify solicitations appropriate for LSBRP competition and allows local small vendors an opportunity to compete with businesses of similar size and resources for County contracts. Eligibility is based on ownership type, principal place of business in Montgomery County, and size/revenue thresholds that vary by business type.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reserves at least 25 percent of Montgomery County procurement opportunities (goods, services, and construction) exclusively for competition among registered and certified local small businesses. DBRC staff work with County departments and agencies to identify procurement solicitations suitable for LSBRP competition and meet regularly with vendors. Eligibility size and sales thresholds vary by business type: Retail and Wholesale (30 employees or fewer OR prior 3 years' average sales of $5,000,000 or less), Services (100 employees or fewer OR prior 3 years' average sales of $10,000,000 or less), Construction (50 employees or fewer OR prior 3 years' average sales of $14,000,000 or less), and Manufacturing (40 employees or fewer OR prior 3 years' average sales of $14,000,000 or less). Registration and certification through the County Vendor Registration System (CVRS) is free.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Independently-owned local small businesses based in Montgomery County, including retailers, construction and trades companies, wholesalers, service firms, and non-profit organizations that meet size, ownership, and location requirements and seek Montgomery County government contracting opportunities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reserved Montgomery County government procurement contracts for goods, services, and construction that certified local small businesses can compete for.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must have its principal place of business in Montgomery County, defined as having physical business location(s) only in Montgomery County, or having physical business locations both in and outside the County where the County-based location(s) account for over 50 percent of the business's total number of employees or over 50 percent of the business's gross sales.

For Wholesale: 30 employees or fewer OR prior 3 years' average sales of $5,000,000 or less

Must register and obtain LSBRP certification through the County Vendor Registration System (CVRS)
Must qualify as a local small business
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Companies interested in providing goods and services to County agencies must register and apply for LSBRP certification through the County Vendor Registration System (CVRS) at no financial cost. The web-based system allows businesses to create and maintain their vendor registrations and apply for certifications online, ensuring County agencies have up-to-date vendor information. DBRC staff meet regularly with County department and agency staff to identify LSBRP procurement opportunities and connect certified vendors with appropriate solicitations. The program accepts applications on a rolling basis with no fixed deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: The MC Groceries Program is a nutrition benefit program administered by Montgomery County that provides monthly grocery purchasing power to households with children who are not eligible for SNAP due to income or citizenship restrictions. Eligible households receive monthly Fresh Funds codes through a partnership with Instacart Health to shop online from over 20 participating grocery retailers for home delivery or pickup. Benefits are $100 per month per child aged 0-18, up to $400 per month per household. The program supports food security by enabling access to fresh and shelf-stable food items through a convenient online shopping experience. Enrollment is limited and subject to availability; a waitlist is available for upcoming program cycles.
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible households receive $100 per month in Instacart Health Fresh Funds benefits for each child under age 18 who is not eligible for SNAP benefits, up to a maximum of $400 per month per household. Benefits are provided as dollar-value credits automatically loaded to the participant's Instacart Fresh Funds account on the 15th of each month or the following business day. Credits can be used to purchase any food or non-alcoholic beverage items, including fresh or frozen produce, seafood, dairy, eggs, meat and meat alternatives, bakery, deli, and pantry staples from participating Instacart retailers. Eligible fees including driver tips, delivery fees, and service fees can be covered with Fresh Funds benefits. Non-eligible items and amounts exceeding the Fresh Funds balance are charged to a backup payment method (debit card, credit card, Google Pay, Apple Pay, PayPal, or Klarna). Unspent funds do not roll over to the next month. Funds must be used by participants within the same benefit period to maximize use. Up to 700 families may be served in any given enrollment cycle. Participants must complete all orders (placed, delivered, and/or picked up) within the same benefit month.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program enrollment is not currently open to new participants. Waitlist available for upcoming cycle July 2026 – July 2027.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Heather Bruskin; Montgomery County Food Council and Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services Navigation Line
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 301-818-3614 or 240-777-4141; Instacart Senior Support Line: (844) 981-3433 (8 a.m. - 11 p.m. ET daily)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Households with at least one child under age 18 residing in Montgomery County who do not have an active SNAP case and whose post-tax household income is at or below 400% of the Federal Poverty Level (approximately $132,000/year for a household of 4). The program is intended for families seeking food security and convenient online grocery shopping options.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of fresh and shelf-stable nutritious food and non-alcoholic beverage items through participating Instacart retailers, including fresh or frozen produce, seafood, dairy, eggs, meat and meat alternatives, bakery, deli, and pantry staples. Eligible fees such as driver tips, delivery fees, and service fees can also be covered. Purchases must be for home delivery or local pickup. Use of funds is restricted to the household participating in the program and delivery addresses must match the address provided during enrollment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must reside in Montgomery County, Maryland throughout the program participation period. Delivery must be to the address provided during the enrollment process.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Contact a Nutrition Benefits Navigator by phone (301-818-3614 or 240-777-4141) or email SNAP@mocofoodcouncil.org, or submit a referral form to complete an eligibility pre-screening for MC Groceries and other nutrition assistance programs. Step 2: If pre-screening criteria are met, the Navigator assists with completing a waitlist form. Step 3: When openings become available, individuals on the waitlist are notified and asked to complete an application and submit required documentation including proof of income (pay stubs or employer letter), valid photo ID, proof of address, and government-issued identity proof for each child. Applications are processed first-come, first-served based on completion. Step 4: Once enrolled, households receive instructions to create an Instacart Fresh Funds account and a unique code to redeem monthly benefits. Funds are automatically loaded on the 15th of each month or the following business day. Step 5: Participants shop online through Instacart, selecting from over 20 participating grocery retailers for delivery or pickup. Fresh Funds credits are automatically applied at checkout. Step 6: All follow-up communications are sent to the email address provided on the application. DHHS staff including the Navigation Unit and CASCBS team provide outreach, technical assistance, and translation assistance in multiple languages. Instacart Senior Support Line (844-981-3433) is available for customers over age 60 from 8 a.m. to 11 p.m. ET daily.
