structured_extraction.program_name: Make Office Vacancy Extinct (MOVE) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Make Office Vacancies Extinct (MOVE) Grant Program is a Montgomery County initiative designed to attract new businesses, support startups, and encourage expansion of existing businesses within the county by reducing vacant Class A and B office or flex space. The program provides one-time financial grants to businesses signing their first commercial office lease (Inaugural Commercial Lease) or expanding their office space by at least 500 square feet (Expanded Commercial Lease) in Montgomery County. It supports startups locating in the county, companies relocating to Montgomery County, and businesses expanding operations within the county. The program has been codified via Executive Regulation 12-24, administered by the Montgomery County Department of Finance. The program is a sub-program of the Economic Development Fund and operates on a first-come, first-served basis subject to availability of funds.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses receive a one-time grant to help offset expenses related to their first commercial office lease or expansion of office space by at least 500 square feet. For Inaugural Commercial Leases (first-ever commercial lease in the County), eligible square feet equals the total square footage leased. For Expanded Commercial Leases, eligible square feet equals the new square footage minus the previous lease square footage. Award calculations are: Less than 7,500 sq ft: $8.00 per sq ft, max $60,000; 7,501-10,000 sq ft: $10.00 per sq ft, max $100,000; More than 10,000 sq ft: $12.50 per sq ft, max $150,000; Strategic Industries: $15.00 per sq ft, max $150,000. No single award may exceed $150,000. A business is limited to one award per County Fiscal Year (July 1-June 30) and a total of three awards across the business and its subsidiaries. Awards are funded on a first-come, first-served basis based on the date of receipt of a Completed Application and subject to availability of appropriated funds. If calculated awards exceed available funds, awardees receive awards based on remaining available appropriation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Completed Application must be submitted on or before 180 days of the execution date for the Inaugural Commercial Lease or Expanded Commercial Lease
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit businesses planning to sign their first commercial office lease in Montgomery County, startups locating in the county, companies relocating to Montgomery County, and existing businesses expanding their office space by at least 500 square feet within Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To offset rental expenses related to first commercial office lease, business relocation, or expansion of office space within Montgomery County in Class A or B office or flex space; to reduce vacant office space by attracting and retaining businesses in the county.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Office space must be located in Montgomery County and labeled as Office Space by third-party real property software.

Leased premises must have a real property address and cannot be a mobile trailer or similar non-permanent structure
Lease cannot be executed between a Business and its Subsidiary
Business sole proprietors cannot primarily sell products or services underwritten by a third party
Awardees must remain in Montgomery County for a minimum of 36 months following the award
Awardees must maintain the Eligible Square Feet for 36 months
Awardees must submit annual reports by January 15 for three years after receiving the award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can learn more and apply for a MOVE grant through the County's online portal at montgomerycountymd.gov/business/programs/move-grant.html or contact the Office of the County Executive, Business Center. Businesses must submit a Completed Application including an executed lease, Articles of Incorporation or equivalent, utility bill or equivalent document, and a complete business plan within 180 days of lease execution. Applications are time-stamped by the system and reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis. Upon verification of eligibility, the Director of Finance makes final determination on all applications. All applicants receive formal notification of award status. Awardees receive a conditional grant award letter stipulating the process to receive funds and post-award requirements. structured_extraction.program_description: Provides transportation services for Medical Assistance (Medicaid) recipients who reside in Montgomery County and need transportation to access medically necessary services. This is a last resort transportation program for ambulatory, wheelchair, and stretcher-bound recipients who have no other means of transportation. The program is administered by Montgomery County Department of Transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides transportation services to medical appointments and facility transfers/discharges covered by Medical Assistance (Medicaid). Transportation may be scheduled up to seven days in advance, and next-day service is available if requests are made by noon the working day before. Available for ambulatory, wheelchair-bound (regular, electric, electric scooter, extra-wide, or specialty), and stretcher-bound recipients as a last resort when no other transportation means are available. Transportation modes include paratransit vehicles, public transit, cab/sedan, wheelchair vans, geri chairs, and ambulances (BLS, ALS, SCT/P, SCT/N, or neonatal levels as medically justified). Forms are valid for one year from the date of provider certification unless medical condition changes warrant recertification.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 240-777-5899 for trip scheduling; 240-777-5890 for information; TTY: 240-777-5869; Connect-A-Ride Transportation Resource Center: 301-738-3252
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who are Medical Assistance (Medicaid) recipients and need transportation to medically necessary services, including ambulatory, wheelchair-bound, and stretcher-bound individuals. Applicant must have exhausted all possible alternative transportation resources.

Applicants must provide proof of Montgomery County residency such as utility bills, mortgage/lease agreements, state ID or driver's license, or home/cell phone bills.
requirements_list: Must have eligible Medical Assistance (Medicaid) with valid 11-digit MA number
Must be a Montgomery County resident with proof of residency (utility bill, mortgage/lease, state ID, or phone bill)
Must have medical certification from physician, physician assistant, certified nurse practitioner (CRNP), or dentist on approved Statewide Medical Assistance Provider Certification form
Must demonstrate no other available transportation or be physically unable to use existing transportation services, including public transit and paratransit
Ambulatory, wheelchair-bound (all types), or stretcher-bound
Must have valid medical appointment or facility transfer/discharge authorization
Must sign Authorization for Release of Information form to verify appointment details with healthcare providers
Must sign Notice of Privacy Practices form
For facility transfers/discharges: facility must provide sending facility contact information, authorization numbers if applicable, and specify whether stay is Medicare Part A reimbursed
Physician certification must clearly state diagnosis in plain language (no abbreviations, ICD or DSM codes) and explain why transport by other means is contraindicated

For out-of-area transports: must justify why service is needed outside of Montgomery County (procedure not available locally, no local specialist, local specialist does not participate with MCO or Medicaid, or other documented reason)
Must report any change in address or medical condition immediately to the Medicaid Transportation Office
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Applicant's healthcare provider completes the Statewide Medical Assistance Provider Certification form in its entirety, clearly stating diagnosis and how the medical condition prevents use of accessible public transportation. Provider must sign the form certifying medical necessity. 2. Applicant provides proof of Montgomery County residency (utility bill, mortgage/lease, state ID/driver's license, or phone bill). 3. Applicant completes and signs Authorization for Release of Information form and Notice of Privacy Practices form. 4. Mail completed application with all attachments to: Medicaid and Special Transportation, 101 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Rockville, Maryland 20850. Alternatively, contact Connect-A-Ride Transportation Resource Center at 301-738-3252 or ConnectARide@AccessJCA.org. 5. For trip scheduling after certification: call 240-777-5899 Monday-Friday (except holidays) 8:30 a.m. to 12:00 noon. Scheduling staff will ask screening questions to confirm eligibility. 6. Applicant will be notified in writing of certification status; determinations are not provided over the telephone. 7. For facility transfers/discharges: facility completes Transfer/Discharge form with medical information, facility details, and authorization information. For out-of-area transports: provider completes out-of-area certification form justifying why transport outside Montgomery County is medically necessary. 8. Periodic recertification required for all recipients. 9. Appeal rights available for denied applications under COMAR 10.04.01 and 10.09.24.

structured_extraction.program_name: Minority, Female and Disabled-Owned Businesses (MFD) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's MFD Program assists certified minority, female, and disabled-owned firms in gaining access to prime contractor and subcontractor opportunities with County government agencies. The program encourages MFD participation through outreach activities, workshops, and a forum for businesses to explore individual and joint contracting opportunities. Service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses are also eligible under the disabled category. Participation goals are set for each purchasing category based on contract value and life, effective January 1, 2025: Construction (22%), Professional Services (25%), Non-Professional Services (24%), and Goods (10%). The program also supports non-profit entities organized to promote the interests of persons with disabilities that can demonstrate at least 51% of personnel used to perform contracted services are persons with disabilities.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides access to prime contractor and subcontractor opportunities with Montgomery County government agencies, along with outreach activities, workshops, and a forum for MFD-certified businesses to explore individual and joint contracting opportunities. For contracts valued at $50,000 or more, prime contractors must subcontract a percentage of the total contract value (including all modifications and renewals) to certified MFD businesses, with participation goals by category: Construction (22%), Professional Services (25%), Non-Professional Services (24%), and Goods (10%) as of January 1, 2025. Contractors must submit an approved MFD Subcontractor Performance Plan identifying certified MFD subcontractors and the percentage of contract dollars to be paid to each. Contractors must include binding arbitration provisions in subcontracts with MFD businesses to resolve disputes, and must submit documentation of compliance before receiving final payment. Failure to comply results in liquidated damages equal to the difference between contracted MFD amounts and actual payments to MFD subcontractors, and may result in contract termination and the contractor being found non-responsible for future County procurement for three years. Eligible businesses must be at least 51% owned, controlled, and managed daily by individuals from designated categories: African American, Hispanic American, Asian American, Native American, Disabled Persons, or Women.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified minority-owned, female-owned, disabled-owned, and service-disabled veteran-owned businesses seeking contracting opportunities with Montgomery County government agencies. Also includes non-profit entities organized to promote interests of persons with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to prime contractor and subcontractor opportunities with Montgomery County government agencies, including participation in outreach activities, workshops, and a forum for exploring individual and joint contracting opportunities. Funds from MFD subcontracts can be used for goods and services as specified in individual subcontract agreements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Business must be at least 51% owned, controlled, and managed daily by a minority person(s), disabled person(s), or woman
Ownership categories include: African American, Hispanic American, Asian American, Native American, Disabled Persons, or Women
Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business certification from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs qualifies under the disabled category

Business must be certified by an approved certifying agency such as MDOT (MBE/DBE), SBA (8(a) or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business), WBENC, Capital Region Minority Supplier Development Council (MSDC), MD/DC Minority Supplier Development Council, or City of Baltimore (MWBOO)

For non-profit entities: must be organized to promote interests of persons with disabilities and demonstrate on a contract-by-contract basis that at least 51% of persons used to perform the contracted services or manufacture goods are persons with a disability
Prime contractors must subcontract a minimum percentage of contract value to certified MFD businesses for contracts valued at $50,000 or more
Contractors must submit an approved MFD Subcontractor Performance Plan identifying all MFD subcontractors and payment percentages
Contractors must include binding arbitration provisions in all subcontracts with MFD businesses
Contractors must submit documentation of compliance with the MFD Subcontractor Performance Plan before receiving final payment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain certification from one of the approved certifying agencies: Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) for MBE/DBE, Federal Small Business Administration (SBA) for 8(a) or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned certification, Women's Business Enterprise National Council (WBENC) for WBE, MD/DC Minority Supplier Development Council (MSDC) for MBE, Department of Veterans Affairs for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, or City of Baltimore for MWBOO. 2. Once certified, businesses are included in the County's MFD program and can participate in County procurement opportunities. 3. For prime contractors winning County contracts valued at $50,000 or more: submit a completed MFD Subcontractor Performance Plan (Form PMMD-65) identifying all certified MFD subcontractors, the percentage of contract dollars to be paid to each, and a statement of good faith efforts or waiver request justification. 4. Obtain Director of Procurement approval of the Performance Plan. 5. Include binding arbitration language in each subcontract with MFD businesses describing how dispute resolution costs will be apportioned. 6. During contract performance, MFD subcontractors submit monthly MFD Report of Payments Received forms to the Office of Business Relations and Compliance. 7. Before final payment, prime contractors must submit documentation demonstrating compliance with the approved Performance Plan, which may include invoices, copies of subcontracts, cancelled checks, affidavits from MFD subcontractors, waivers, and arbitration decisions. 8. The Director may conduct on-site inspections and require periodic compliance reports. For further information, contact the MFD Program Manager at 240-777-9912.

structured_extraction.program_description: A shared cold storage facility in a 20-foot by 10-foot container unit that helps small county farms store and aggregate their agricultural products after harvesting and before distribution to food assistance providers and schools. The program addresses food waste, spoilage, and cold storage shortages faced by local farmers in Montgomery County. It provides free or subsidized access to shared cold storage space, supporting agricultural microenterprises and small producers with resources to reduce post-harvest losses and connect with food pantries, schools, businesses, and farm-to-table programs.
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or subsidized access to shared cold storage space in a 20-foot by 10-foot container unit. The unit can hold approximately 10 standard pallets of product with an average estimated capacity of 8,750 pounds at any given time. Product is rotated every two weeks during peak growing and harvest seasons from mid-March through mid-November. Farmers can store and aggregate their products for distribution to food pantries, schools, businesses, and farm-to-table programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small county farms and local farmers in Montgomery County who experience refrigeration shortages and need space to store and aggregate agricultural products, as well as agricultural microenterprises and small producers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cold storage space for agricultural products after harvesting and before distribution to food assistance providers, schools, food pantries, and farm-to-table programs; agricultural business development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Farmers must participate in a brief training
Farmers must request space through the Food Corridor App
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Farmers participate in a brief training and request storage space through the Food Corridor App, which is coming soon.

structured_extraction.program_name: Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Program - Montgomery County
structured_extraction.program_description: The Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Program is an inclusionary zoning program administered by Montgomery County that requires residential developers to make a percentage of housing units available at affordable prices to low- and moderate-income households. Established in 1974, the program has produced over 17,836 total MPDUs, with approximately 5,858 units currently under control (1,833 for sale and 4,025 for rental) as of 2025. The program includes both a Purchase Program and a Rental Program. The Purchase Program helps first-time homebuyers with moderate household incomes purchase affordably priced homes at controlled prices significantly below market rates, subject to a 30-year control period with resale restrictions. The Rental Program offers affordable rental units in apartment communities throughout Montgomery County at regulated rates based on household income and size. Units are subject to resale and occupancy restrictions during their respective control periods (30 years for for-sale units, 99 years for rental units) to maintain long-term affordability. The Housing Opportunities Commission may acquire one-third of produced units to serve low-income tenants.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The MPDU Program provides two forms of assistance: (1) Purchase Program: Eligible first-time homebuyers may purchase MPDU homes at controlled resale prices significantly below market value. For-sale units typically range from $150,000 for a 2-bedroom condominium to approximately $220,000 for a 3-bedroom townhouse. Units are subject to a 30-year control period (or 10 years for units purchased before April 1, 2005), during which the resale price is capped at an MPDU-calculated maximum and can only be sold to another MPDU-certified household. After the control period expires, owners may sell at market value but must share 50% of the difference between the fair market sales price and the MPDU resale value (accounting for inflation, documented improvements, real estate commission, and transfer taxes) with the County. Buyers must obtain their own mortgage financing of at least $150,000 from a licensed lender. (2) Rental Program: Eligible tenants may rent MPDU units at regulated rates set by Executive Regulation and recalculated annually. For garden apartments, maximum income for new tenants is 65% AMI; for high-rise apartments (5 stories or more), maximum income for new tenants is 70% AMI. Renewing tenants may have income up to 130% of the applicable new-tenant limit. For example, a new tenant in a garden apartment with 1 person can have a maximum annual household income of $74,500; renewing tenants can have up to $96,850. The program does not provide rental subsidies directly, but MPDU rents are regulated below market rates. Tenants may use Housing Choice Vouchers or Housing Opportunities Commission assistance to help pay rent. Units are allocated through random selection drawings for purchase applicants. In 2025, the MPDU program approved 564 MPDUs with 521 new MPDUs built during the year. The program has successfully produced more than 17,800 affordable units since inception.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No specific deadline; applications accepted on rolling basis year-round after completing required training
structured_extraction.contact_name: MPDU Office; Greater Washington Urban League (GWUL); MPDU Rental Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers and renters with moderate household incomes seeking affordable housing in Montgomery County. For purchase: households earning up to 70% of Washington Metro Area Median Income (approximately $79,500 for a family of two or $99,500 for a family of four), with minimum annual household income of $40,000 and maximum ranging from $80,500 for a 1-person household to $133,000 for a 6-person household (effective April 11, 2025). For rental: income limits vary by household size and development type (65% or 70% AMI for new tenants). Priority is given to people who live or work in Montgomery County. Units are allocated through random selection drawings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase or rental of affordable housing units in residential developments throughout Montgomery County. For purchase: buyers own the property and can make improvements to their home, though only certain improvements (room additions, patios, fireplaces, deck/patio, landscaping up to $800, storm windows/doors, fencing, HVAC replacement up to 50%, flooring upgrades, appliances, etc.) can be credited toward the resale price, subject to a 10% limit of the original purchase price. For rental: tenants must use the MPDU unit as their primary residence and cannot sublet the unit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. The MPDU requirement applies to residential developments of 20 or more units in applicable zones. Apartment communities with MPDU units are located throughout the County. Note: The City of Rockville and City of Gaithersburg have separate MPDU programs. As of December 31, 2025, there are 89 apartment communities with MPDU rental units across the County.
requirements_list: Must be a first-time homebuyer (for for-sale units) — applicant and all household members must not have owned a home in the past 5 years
Applicant and all household members must not have owned any residential property during the previous 5 years and must never have owned an MPDU (for rental)
Minimum annual household income of $40,000 (for purchase)
Maximum annual household income based on household size: ranges from $80,500 for 1-person household to $133,000 for 6-person household (effective April 11, 2025, for purchase)
Income limit of up to 70% of Washington Metro Area Median Income (general program)
For new MPDU tenants in garden apartments: maximum income is 65% AMI; for high-rise apartments: maximum income is 70% AMI
For renewing MPDU tenants: maximum income is 130% of the amount for new tenants
Mortgage pre-qualification letter for at least $150,000 from a licensed lender (issued within last three months, for purchase)
Ability to document affordability of mortgage, utilities, and fees (for purchase)
Provide federal tax returns for all adult wage earners
Household size must be appropriate for the number of bedrooms in the MPDU property
Must complete three free online training courses in order: MPDU Orientation Seminar (2-2.5 hours), First-Time Homebuyer Class (8 hours, HUD-certified), and Application Tutorial (for purchase)
All classes must be completed within 2 years of applying
Must pass post-tests with score of 80% or higher for each class
Must maintain consistent name, last name, and email address across all class registrations
Owner occupancy requirement during control period (for purchase)
Priority given to County residents and those employed in the County
If purchasing during control period, must work with MPDU office and MPDU-trained realtor
If selling during control period, must sell at MPDU-calculated maximum resale price to another MPDU-certified household
If selling after control period expires, must pay shared profit to Montgomery County based on excess profit calculation
Must comply with MPDU covenants recorded on the property deed
Credit rating must be acceptable to apartment community management (for rental)
Income must be sufficient to meet monthly rent payments according to management company standards (for rental)
Unemployed participants must have other means of support such as child support, Housing Opportunities Commission voucher, retirement benefits, or interest from assets (for rental)
MPDU unit must be primary residence; unit cannot be sublet (for rental)
Number of people in household determines eligible number of bedrooms (1 person = 1 bedroom; 2 people = 1–2 bedrooms; 3–4 people = 2–3 bedrooms; 5+ people = 3+ bedrooms) (for rental)
Application fee should not exceed $25; any amount over $25 must be returned if applicant does not move in (for rental)
Valid government identification for all adult household members
Most recent federal income tax return (Form 1040 and W-2/1099)
Proof of income (two most recent pay stubs per wage earner, or four if paid weekly)
Proof of residence if current taxes do not show current address
Special documentation for dependent claims, newborns, or divorce/separation situations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: PURCHASE PROGRAM: 1) Complete pre-screening intake form and submit to Greater Washington Urban League (GWUL) at mpdu@gwul.org. 2) Attend virtual MPDU Orientation Seminar (2-2.5 hours, offered second and fourth Thursdays of the month), pass post-test with 80% or better, and receive certificate of completion. 3) Attend virtual First-Time Homebuyer Class (8 hours, HUD-certified, offered second Saturday of the month) from a HUD-approved housing counselor, pass post-test with 80% or better, and receive certificate of completion. 4) Receive email from MPDU office with an Orientation ID and instructions to access the MPDU Application Portal. 5) Validate class attendance using the Classes Validation Form. 6) Create a user account in Montgomery County's AccessMCG Extranet system. 7) Complete the online Application Tutorial in the portal (pass with 80% or better). 8) Submit completed application form with all required supporting documents (tax returns, pay stubs, proof of residency, pre-qualification letter, and verification of income forms) through the portal. 9) MPDU staff review application within 30 days; incomplete applications will be denied if requested information is not submitted within three months. 10) If eligible, applicant receives MPDU Certificate of Eligibility in the mail; certificate is valid for one year and must be renewed annually. 11) Certificate holder participates in Random Selection Drawings for available MPDU properties. 12) Upon selection, applicant works with MPDU-trained realtor to purchase unit at MPDU-calculated price. FOR RESALE DURING CONTROL PERIOD: (1) Homeowner requests MPDU Maximum Resale Price from MPDU office using the Resale Price Request Form; (2) Completes MPDU Marketing Form and provides documentation of improvements (receipts, cancelled checks, invoices showing payment); (3) MPDU is offered to County and Housing Opportunities Commission with right of first refusal; (4) If not purchased by County/HOC, property is marketed only to MPDU program participants through random selection drawing; (5) After random selection, if no interested participants, owner may request permission to sell to general public; (6) Real estate agent must provide required documents to MPDU office within 14 days of contract ratification, and settlement documents after closing. FOR SALE AFTER CONTROL PERIOD: (1) Owner submits Shared Profit Calculation Request Form and Calculation of Improvements Credit Request Form to MPDU office; (2) MPDU office calculates shared profit owed (allow 21 days); (3) Settlement company pays shared profit to County; (4) County terminates MPDU covenants once profit received. RENTAL PROGRAM: 1) Review the list of apartment communities with MPDU units at the online directory at https://apps.montgomerycountymd.gov/dhca-mpdu/Rental/List. 2) Identify apartment community properties of interest and check current MPDU unit availability, unit types, and rental rates. 3) Contact one or more apartment communities directly to apply for an MPDU unit using contact information from the directory. The management company at each apartment community will provide an application form, verify income and credit history, and determine eligibility. The MPDU office does not provide applications, does not accept applications, and does not issue Certificates of Eligibility for MPDU rentals. All rental applications must be submitted directly to the apartment community of interest. 4) Leasing office reviews application within timeframe set by management company. 5) If approved, tenant signs lease agreement at MPDU rent rate.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery Cares - Medical Care for Uninsured Adults
structured_extraction.program_description: A county health care program providing medical and dental services to uninsured adults in Montgomery County who have income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level. The program serves low-income adults regardless of immigration status who do not qualify for other insurance. Services include medical care, dental care, and prescription assistance through health centers located throughout the county, with no fees or payments charged to enrollees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No fees or payments are charged for Montgomery Cares health center services. Health centers set their own fees which vary by location, but enrollees receive medical care, dental care, and prescription assistance at no cost through the program. The program provides affordable health and dental coverage for eligible uninsured residents who do not qualify for other insurance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Uninsured adults age 18 or older who are residents of Montgomery County with income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level and who do not qualify for other health insurance. No immigration status requirement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical care, dental care, and prescription assistance services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services are available throughout Montgomery County, Maryland. Applicants must be residents of Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Be age 18 or older
Be uninsured
Have an income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level
Be a resident of Montgomery County
Not be enrolled in health insurance including Medicaid, Medicare, commercial insurance or employee-sponsored coverage
No immigration status requirement
Bring proof of income (paycheck stubs, tax returns, or letter from employer or family)

Bring proof of Montgomery County residency (mortgage, lease, property tax bill, utility bill, school records, driver's license, Maryland State ID Card, Federal tax return, W2, pay stubs, voter registration card, or letter from landlord)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 311 or 240-777-1003 for information about a Montgomery Cares health center near you or for questions regarding eligibility. Call the health center of your choice to enroll, or visit participating clinics for enrollment. Bring proof of income and proof of Montgomery County residency to your first appointment.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Access to medical clinic services for uninsured and low-income families who do not qualify for state and federal programs. Complete an application form for County Programs for the Uninsured and email it to OESS.MoCo@montgomerycountymd.gov. The application collects household member information, income details, employment history, and other income sources to determine eligibility.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Uninsured and low-income families who do not qualify for state and federal health programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical clinic services and healthcare provided through the Montgomery Cares program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be uninsured or low-income
Must not be eligible for state and federal programs
Must complete application form with household member information
Must provide Social Security numbers for household members applying for services
Must provide income and employment information
Must reside in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the County Programs for the Uninsured Application form (available in English and Spanish). The form requires information about all household members, their dates of birth, relationships, Social Security numbers, health insurance status, employment history, and income sources. Submit the completed form by email to OESS.MoCo@montgomerycountymd.gov. For eligibility questions or assistance, call 240-777-1003. Applicants may also apply for related programs including Care for Kids, Maternity Partnership, and Senior Dental through the same application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery Connects is a digital equity and inclusion program administered by Montgomery County that helps residents and businesses access computer devices, technology training, affordable home broadband services and subsidies, and public WiFi access points. A key component distributes free Chromebooks to Montgomery County and Maryland residents who do not have access to a personal computer. Over 50,000 computers have already been provided, with an additional 60,000 in distribution. Funding is supported by federal government grants. The program also addresses broadband infrastructure, including in the county's rural Agricultural Reserve.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free Chromebooks (one per person) to eligible residents at in-person appointments, along with technology training, affordable home broadband services and subsidies, and public WiFi access points. No U.S. citizenship is required. Applicants must have a library card and bring proof of ID and address to their scheduled appointment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County and Maryland residents who do not currently have access to a personal computer, particularly those who cannot afford to purchase one. Applicants must be at least 7 years old. Also open to businesses needing digital equity and inclusion support. U.S. citizenship is not required.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free Chromebook/laptop computer for personal use, technology training, affordable home broadband services and subsidies, and public WiFi access.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Specific focus on the county's rural Agricultural Reserve for broadband infrastructure. Maryland residency required for device distribution.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland or Montgomery County resident
Must not currently have a computer
Must be at least 7 years old
Must have a county library card
Must bring proof of ID and address
Must schedule an appointment at a local library or designated location
Limit one computer per person
Not eligible if received a computer from the County between May 2022 and April 2023
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for a free library account online at the Montgomery County Public Libraries website, then schedule an appointment to receive a free Chromebook at your local library branch or designated location. Appointment links are organized by date and time on the program website. For questions or additional help, email montgomeryconnects@montgomerycountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A County-run program that purchases agricultural land preservation easements to conserve farmland for future food and fiber production. The program places an easement on the property to prevent future commercial, residential, or industrial development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases agricultural land preservation easements. Easement values are determined using an Agricultural Value Formula (AVF) based on farm size, soil quality, road frontage, farm location, land tenure, and proximity to the agricultural zone edge. This formula-based system does not require appraisals and typically processes applications in 6 to 12 months.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with farms in Montgomery County's Agricultural Reserve or other zones with significant agricultural value who wish to preserve their land from development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to purchase development rights through an easement placed on the property. The easement prevents future commercial, residential, or industrial development while allowing continued agricultural use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Land must be located in the Agricultural Reserve (AR), Rural Cluster Zone (RC), Rural Zone (RZ), or other zones determined by the County's Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board to possess significant agricultural value. Land must lie outside water and sewer categories 1, 2, and 3.
requirements_list: Farm must be located in the Agricultural Reserve (AR), Rural Cluster Zone (RC), Rural Zone (RZ), or other zones with significant agricultural value
Minimum property size is 50 acres, or 10 acres or more of cropland adjacent to other protected land
One Transferable Development Right (TDR) for every 25 acres must be retained with the property prior to easement application to be eligible for maximum easement value
At least 50 percent of the land must meet USDA Soil Classification Standards I-III or Woodland Classifications 1 and 2
Land must lie outside water and sewer categories 1, 2, and 3
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application to the County. Applications are processed relatively quickly compared to State programs, typically within 6 to 12 months. The County's Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board reviews applications and determines easement values using the Agricultural Value Formula.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Community Food Rescue Mini-Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides mini-grants to support food rescue and food security initiatives in Montgomery County. Grants fund activities such as volunteer coordination, food storage equipment, refrigerated transport vehicles, and community food distribution efforts to reduce food insecurity. Funding is available to non-profit organizations, for-profit entities, government agencies, community groups, schools, and churches engaged in food rescue and food security work in Montgomery County.
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Mini-grants are provided to support food rescue operations and food security initiatives. Grant amounts have ranged from $2,000 to $10,000. Funds can be used to cover costs such as volunteer coordinator salaries, food storage and refrigeration equipment, refrigerated vehicles, signage, technology equipment, and other food distribution infrastructure. Applicants must complete an online application form to apply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, for-profit entities, government agencies, community groups, schools, and churches engaged in food rescue and food security work in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support food rescue and food security operations including volunteer coordination, commercial refrigeration and freezer equipment, refrigerated transport vehicles, food storage infrastructure, technology equipment for record-keeping, and community food distribution programming.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program serves Montgomery County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit an online application form describing their food rescue or food security project and the requested grant amount. Applications are reviewed and awarded organizations are announced in the fiscal year.

structured_extraction.program_description: A collaboration of public and private groups working to prevent and end homelessness in Montgomery County, Maryland through coordinated funding and support services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal, state, local and private funds totaling more than $7.5 million in U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) funding awarded through the Continuum of Care Funding Competition to support housing and services for homeless individuals and families. Funding supports Tier I projects (permanent supportive housing and supportive services) and Tier II projects (rapid re-housing and other innovations). Recent funding recommendations include projects such as HOC McKinney programs, MCCH housing initiatives, and rapid re-housing demonstrations, with individual project awards ranging from approximately $33,000 to $2.9 million.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private organizations and entities working to prevent and end homelessness in Montgomery County, including nonprofits, government agencies, and for-profit entities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating permanent supportive housing projects for chronically homeless persons and families, providing supportive services to prevent and end homelessness, rapid re-housing programs, and innovative housing solutions. Funds support both direct housing provision and support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Participation in the Continuum of Care collaborative application process
Public or private organization with focus on homelessness prevention or services
Alignment with CoC priorities and funding tiers
Capacity to implement and sustain funded programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services coordinates the application process on behalf of the CoC through the HUD Continuum of Care Competition. The CoC Allocation Committee reviews applications and makes funding recommendations based on established ranking criteria. Projects are categorized into Tier I (permanent supportive housing and supportive services) and Tier II (rapid re-housing and innovative projects).

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Dental Health Services (Dental Connections Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County provides comprehensive dental care services to eligible uninsured residents through a network of participating dentists and dental organizations. Services are offered at reduced fees based on a sliding scale adjusted for income and family size. The program encompasses multiple sub-programs including Care for Kids, Adult Dental, Senior Dental, and the Ryan White HIV Dental Program. The Dental Connections component connects enrolled patients to participating dental offices throughout the county. Services include oral examinations, radiographs, cleanings, fluoride applications, sealants, fillings, extractions, root canal therapy, emergency treatment, crowns, dentures, and oral health education. Program availability is subject to funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County-funded initiative that promotes housing opportunities for residents by providing financial assistance for the construction or acquisition of affordable housing units, rehabilitation of existing rental units at risk of losing affordability, and development of housing or mixed-use developments that include affordable housing units. The program supports multifamily housing development and rehabilitation projects in Montgomery County, serving both for-profit and non-profit developers. Since 1989, DHCA has provided flexible financing as loans to affordable housing developers. Program funds are available for production and preservation of affordable housing, with funding sources including the Montgomery Housing Initiative Fund (HIF), federal HOME funds, and Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Program funds are provided in the form of non-recourse, secured loans to support multifamily housing development and rehabilitation, including construction or acquisition of affordable housing units, buying and rehabilitating existing rental units at risk of affordability loss, and development of housing or mixed-use developments including affordable units. Loan terms are flexible and set by the Director based on project needs. Interest rates are generally 3% but can vary depending on project purpose and financing. Loan repayments can amortize monthly, be deferred for a period of time, or be based on a property's annual available cash flow. Loans are subject to annual monitoring fees. Affordable units must serve households at or below 70% of Area Median Income (AMI) and must remain affordable for the greater of 30 years or the term of the Program Loan. Developers can request county funds for projects with less than 10 county-funded units or less than $500,000 using a small project application, or for projects with 10 or more county-funded units with $500,000 or more in county funds using a large project application. Up to $28.0 million was available from the Fiscal Year 2021 Housing Initiative Fund beginning July 1, 2020; funding levels vary by fiscal year and are subject to appropriation.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling, continuous basis with no set deadline. Applicants are encouraged to discuss project proposals with DHCA staff prior to submission for eligibility and feasibility review. Developers submit either a small project or large project application with required forms including application, loan request summary form, financial forms, cost estimates, and tenant housing report for occupied rental properties. Applications are submitted by email to DHCA.Housing@montgomerycountymd.gov and DHCA staff will send an email receipt upon receipt. Complete, thorough applications should be provided with the applicant's most favorable terms. Applications are reviewed by a Selection Advisory Committee (SAC) appointed by the DHCA Director. DHCA staff will assess funding needs based on population served, reasonableness of projections, efficient use of local funds, and leveraging of other resources. If no clarification is needed, the application may be evaluated without further discussion. If DHCA requires clarification or additional information, applicants should submit such material in a timely manner. The SAC reviews applications and makes a recommendation to the DHCA Director on whether a project should be considered for funding. The Director has sole discretion to determine whether to use Program funds for a project. After the Director's decision, applicant will receive notification regarding funding. The County may withdraw funding and/or determine funding will not be provided at any time prior to closing.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Recreation's Financial Aid Program (Rec Assist)
structured_extraction.program_description: Rec Assist is a financial assistance program administered by Montgomery County Recreation that provides subsidies to eligible Montgomery County residents who receive public assistance, allowing them to pay reduced fees for recreation activities, classes, programs, and memberships. The program distributes $400 per eligible family member placed on their Recreation account, valid January 1 through December 31, 2026, or until funds are depleted. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis and can be applied to Montgomery County Recreation classes and programs including yoga, summer camps, swim lessons, sports, art, dance, and other recreation activities, as well as swim passes. A minimum 20 percent co-payment per activity or membership is required at registration, and funds can only be applied to activities costing $25 or more. Applications are available in multiple languages including English, Spanish, Amharic, Chinese, French, Korean, and Vietnamese.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible applicants receive $400 per eligible family member placed on their Recreation account. Funds are valid January 1 through December 31, 2026, or until the fund is depleted. Rec Assist funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. A minimum 20 percent co-payment per activity or membership per participant is required at the time of registration. If the applicant does not have enough Rec Assist funds remaining on their account to cover 80 percent of the activity/program fees, the co-payment will be higher. Funds can only be applied to activities costing $25 or more. Funds may be used for Montgomery County Recreation classes and programs including yoga, summer camps, swim lessons, sports, art, dance, and other recreation activities, as well as toward swim passes including Family Pool Passes. Only one swim punch pass per eligible family member per calendar year may be purchased using Rec Assist funds. Funds cannot be used for activities costing less than $25, previous registration adjustments, previous account balances, sports team league fees, facility rentals, recreation gift cards, daily pool admissions, supplemental fees (including security deposits, withdrawal fees, materials fees, late pick-up fees), aquatic merchandise, or out-of-school time programs. All Montgomery County Recreation withdrawal, transfer and refund guidelines apply. Once the Rec Assist fund is depleted, applicants must pay full price for all registrations, even if they still have Rec Assist dollars on their account.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Senior Property Tax Deferral Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program allows senior property owners aged 65 and older to defer increases in their Montgomery County property taxes if they meet income and residency requirements. Eligible seniors with combined household income less than $80,000 can postpone paying increases in the county property tax portion of their bill. The deferred taxes become a lien on the property and must be repaid when the property is sold, transferred, or no longer used as the owner's principal residence. The accumulated deferred taxes cannot exceed 50 percent of the fair market value of the property.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners who qualify can defer the amount by which their current county property tax exceeds their previous county property tax. The deferred taxes accrue as a lien on the property and do not charge interest during the deferral period. The deferral ends when the property is transferred, the applicant no longer occupies it as their principal residence, the property becomes subject to tax sale, or the property's use changes. The accumulated deferred taxes cannot exceed 50 percent of the assessed value of the property. A lien shall attach to the property in the amount of deferred tax and interest (if any) and shall remain until the deferred tax is paid. The lien shall be recorded in the land records of Montgomery County and all costs of recording the document will be paid by the applicant. Any mortgagee or beneficiary under a deed of trust will be notified of the deferral and the amount of tax being deferred. All county real property tax not deferred is due and payable subject to the same interest rate and penalty as all other county property taxes. The annual tax bill shall show the cumulative amount of the deferral and accrued interest as of the date of the billing. A homeowner may end a deferral at any time by giving written notice to the Director of Finance and paying the deferred tax.

requirements_list: At least one applicant must be at least 65 years old (provide copy of birth certificate, driver's license or other proof of age)

At least one applicant must have resided in the dwelling as their principal residence for five consecutive years and must continue to occupy it as their principal residence

The combined gross income of all individuals who actually reside in the dwelling must not exceed $80,000 (does not include dependents of the homeowner or any individual residing in the home who pays a reasonable amount for rent or room and board)
The accumulated deferred taxes cannot exceed 50 percent of the assessed value of the property

Gross income must be reported for the applicant, spouse or co-owner and all other occupants of the dwelling unless such other occupants were claimed as dependents on the applicant's federal income tax return or unless they are paying reasonable fixed charges such as rent or room and board
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be received by September 1st of the current taxable year. Applicants must complete the application form and submit it with the following required documentation: proof of age (birth certificate, driver's license, or other proof), a copy of the completed federal income tax return with all accompanying schedules and forms, and the completed Tax Deferral and Lien Agreement. If income was derived from a partnership or corporation, a copy of the partnership return (Form 1065 including Schedule K-1) and/or corporate return (Form 1120 or 1120S including Schedule K-1) must also be included. If married filing separately, a copy of each spouse's return must be included. Applications are available in printed form at the Division of Treasury (27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, MD 20850) or as an electronic version at montgomerycountymd.gov/seniordeferral. For the property tax year beginning July 1st, pay the full first installment in a timely manner to avoid interest charges. Once approved, the deferral will be applied toward the second installment or refunded if the bill has been paid in full. Applications must be mailed to: Montgomery County Maryland Department of Finance, Division of Treasury, Attn: Tax Deferral, 27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, MD 20850. Incomplete applications will be returned and must be completed and re-submitted. Note: In certain individual cases only, a secondary request may be made to submit additional documentation or other items of evidence in an effort to verify income. Applications are always subject to an audit at any time.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Supplemental Homeowners' Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides additional county-level tax credits for homeowners who qualify for the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit. The credit amount is based on the homeowner's household income compared to their property tax bill, and is designed to supplement the state credit. A special property tax credit is also available for eligible senior residents age 65 and older. The county supplement is applied only against General County and Special Service Area real property taxes, with eligibility thresholds and credit amounts updated annually.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County Supplement provides a tax credit applied only against General County and Special Service Area real property taxes. For the July 1, 2026 tax billing, the assessed value on which the credit applies is $383,100, the combined income eligibility level is $76,620, and net worth criteria is $255,400. The credit amount is calculated on a progressive scale based on income levels, ranging from 0% to 8% of eligible income. No additional application is required beyond the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit application. In a recent year, the average credit benefited 4,486 County residents with an average value of $1,276. Taxpayers age 70 or older may submit retroactive applications for the current and 3 prior levy years at any time.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1st to be applicable for that tax year, except taxpayers age 70 or older may submit retroactive applications for the current and 3 prior levy years at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Montgomery County who qualify for the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit, including senior residents age 65 and older, with household income not exceeding $76,620
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credits applied against General County and Special Service Area real property taxes, reducing property tax obligations for eligible low-income homeowners
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must qualify for the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit
Must be a homeowner of principal residence
Household income must not exceed $76,620 (as of July 1, 2026)
Net worth must not exceed $255,400 (as of July 1, 2026)
Assessed property value must not exceed $383,100 (as of July 1, 2026)
No separate application required; included in the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit application
Must apply for the State HOTC through SDAT to be considered for the County Supplement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Taxpayers must apply for the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit through the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) by October 1st. Only the State HOTC application must be completed — there is no separate application for the County Supplement. Applications can be submitted online or by mail to SDAT. Contact SDAT at 800-944-7403 or visit https://dat.maryland.gov/realproperty/pages/homeowners'-property-tax-credit-program.aspx. Taxpayers age 70 or older may submit retroactive applications for the current and 3 prior levy years at any time.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Transfer of Development Rights Program (TDR)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows landowners in the Agricultural Reserve to sell development rights to areas designated for growth elsewhere in the County. When landowners create and sell TDRs, a TDR easement is placed on the property that permanently restricts development to a maximum of 1 unit per 25 acres.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners in the Agricultural Reserve can sell development rights (TDRs) to designated receiving areas in the County. The sale generates private funds for the landowner while placing a TDR easement on the property that permanently restricts development to 1 unit per 25 acres. To date, over 52,000 acres of farmland have been preserved through this program, generating over $117 million in private funds through TDR purchases.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in Montgomery County's Agricultural Reserve who wish to preserve their land and potentially recapture equity through the sale of development rights.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Landowners recapture some of the lost property value resulting from the 1980 down-zoning of the Agricultural Reserve by selling development rights to areas designated for growth. The TDR easement placed on the property permanently restricts development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Agricultural Reserve (AR) is the primary area where landowners can create and sell TDRs. Development rights can be sold to designated receiving areas elsewhere in Montgomery County that are designated for growth.
requirements_list: Property must be located in the Agricultural Reserve
Development rights are based on previous zoning designation of 1 unit per 5 acres
A TDR easement is placed on the property when TDRs are created and sold
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners create TDRs from their land and sell them to designated receiving areas. The process involves severing development rights and placing a TDR easement on the property.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides assistance with past due heating and electricity bills and ongoing benefits to help residents avoid utility shut-off.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Volunteer Income Tax Assistance Partnership (VITA)
structured_extraction.program_description: The VITA Partnership delivers free tax preparation and filing services to low- and moderate-income families and individuals in Montgomery County. IRS-certified volunteer tax preparers prepare and electronically file federal and state income tax returns, help taxpayers claim special credits including the federal Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC, up to $8,046), Maryland EITC, Child Tax Credit, and the Montgomery County Working Families Income Supplement (WFIS). The program also assists with ITIN (Individual Taxpayer Identification Number) applications and renewals, promotes banking and asset building (including opening free or low-cost bank accounts and purchasing U.S. Savings Bonds), provides financial education, and offers referrals to public and community resources. Services are available in-person at multiple locations (Gaithersburg, Rockville, Wheaton, Silver Spring) and virtually. The program operates during tax season (late January through April) for current-year returns and June through November for amended and prior-year returns.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free tax preparation and electronic filing of income tax forms by IRS-certified volunteer tax preparers. Eligible Montgomery County households with combined household income of $69,000 or less can receive free tax help. The program helps filers claim the federal EITC (up to $8,046), Maryland EITC, Child Tax Credit, and the Montgomery County Working Families Income Supplement (WFIS). Filers with an ITIN can qualify for Maryland EITC and WFIS. Volunteers also assist with ITIN applications and renewals, direct deposit setup, opening free or low-cost bank accounts, purchasing U.S. Savings Bonds, financial education, and referrals to public and community resources. Tax season appointments run January 20 – April 9, 2026; amended and prior-year returns are served June through November. All VITA sites serve taxpayers filing with ITINs. Staff are available to help submit ITIN applications at Community Action Agency VITA and at CASA.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 9, 2026 for current tax year; June through November for amended and prior year returns
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- and moderate-income Montgomery County residents and families with combined household income of $69,000 or less, including those who file with an ITIN. The program ensures access for individuals with disabilities through public and community provider partnerships.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free income tax preparation and electronic filing; claiming federal EITC, Maryland EITC, Child Tax Credit, and Montgomery County Working Families Income Supplement; ITIN application and renewal assistance; direct deposit setup; opening free or low-cost bank accounts; purchasing U.S. Savings Bonds; financial education; referrals to public and community resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. In-person services available at multiple locations: Casey Community Center (Gaithersburg), TESS Community Action Center (Silver Spring), Community Action Agency (Rockville), and WorkSource Montgomery (Wheaton). Virtual appointments also available.

Must be a Montgomery County resident

Must bring government-issued photo ID (valid Driver's License, Passport, or Age of Majority Card) for each filer
Must bring original Social Security Card and/or ITIN notice for each family member

Must bring Forms 1098, 1099, and other income documentation

Must bring child care provider information if applicable

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schedule a free tax filing appointment online through the AppointmentPlus scheduling system at montgomerycountymd.gov/cashback/schedule.html, or call 240-777-1123. Appointments are available January 20 – April 9, 2026 at multiple locations with the following hours: Mondays 2–8 pm (Casey Community Center, Gaithersburg); Tuesdays 2–8 pm (TESS Community Action Center, Silver Spring) and 11 am–5 pm (Community Action Agency, Rockville); Wednesdays 12–8 pm (Community Action Agency, Rockville); Thursdays 11 am–5 pm (WorkSource Montgomery, Wheaton and Community Action Agency, Rockville); Fridays 11 am–5 pm (virtual appointments). Walk-in appointments are available Tuesday through Thursday from 2–4 pm at Community Action Agency in Rockville on a first-come, first-served basis. For amended and prior-year returns, contact a VITA site between June and November. Certified tax preparers will complete and file taxes for free.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Working Families Income Supplement (WFIS) / Refundable Earned Income Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A local tax credit offered by Montgomery County that supplements the Maryland State Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC). The program provides a 56% match of the State Refundable Earned Income Credit for eligible low-income working residents of Montgomery County, including eligible ITIN filers. The County provides a separate refund check in addition to the State credit, issued by the Maryland Office of the Comptroller on Montgomery County's behalf.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Montgomery County matches 56% of the State Refundable Earned Income Credit. Eligible residents receive a separate check from the Comptroller paid for by Montgomery County. Eligible ITIN filers may also receive this credit. Checks are mailed on a schedule based on when tax returns are filed: returns filed through June result in checks mailed by end of July; returns filed July through September result in checks mailed by end of October; returns filed through December result in checks mailed by end of January. This schedule pertains to tax returns filed for the prior year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income working residents of Montgomery County who are eligible for the federal and state Earned Income Credit, including eligible ITIN filers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit is provided as a refund check to eligible individuals, applied to supplement their Montgomery County tax liability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to residents of Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must have filed taxes as a Montgomery County resident for the tax year in which the credit is claimed
Must have earned income in the tax year
Must be eligible for the federal Earned Income Credit
Must claim the Maryland Earned Income Credit
Must file a Maryland tax return
Must have at least one dependent
Eligible ITIN filers may receive the credit
Eligibility determined by Maryland Office of the Comptroller
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents apply for the federal and state Earned Income Credit on their federal income tax return and file a Maryland tax return as a Montgomery County resident. The Maryland Office of the Comptroller verifies eligibility. If eligible for the State Refundable EIC and filing as a Montgomery County resident, the County automatically provides a matching 56% credit. The Comptroller issues both state and county checks separately.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County's Pet Waste Management Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that collaborates with homeowner associations to reduce bacteria levels in local rivers and streams by installing and maintaining pet waste stations in common areas. The program provides onsite evaluation, outreach materials, and pet waste station installation and maintenance at no cost for up to one year, helping HOAs address pet waste contamination and protect local water quality.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible homeowner associations receive an onsite evaluation, outreach materials, a number of pet waste stations (determined with the HOA based on the extent of the issue), and maintenance of the stations for up to one year at no cost. After the year, the HOA can choose to adopt and maintain the stations themselves.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowner associations and condominium associations located in Montgomery County that are interested in managing pet waste issues and reducing pet waste contamination in their communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation and maintenance of pet waste stations in common areas managed by homeowner associations to collect pet waste and reduce water pollution in local rivers and streams.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Homeowner associations located in Montgomery County are eligible. One exception applies: HOAs located within municipalities such as the City of Rockville, City of Gaithersburg, and City of Takoma Park are not eligible.
requirements_list: Located in Montgomery County (with noted exceptions for certain municipalities such as the City of Rockville, City of Gaithersburg, and City of Takoma Park)
Currently do not have an existing pet waste management program
Interested in having a pet waste management program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Homeowner associations or condominium associations interested in participating should send an email to AskDep@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov or call customer service at 311 (240-777-0311) to express interest, ask questions, and begin the process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County program providing nurse case management, community health worker services, and home visiting for pregnant women and postpartum mothers. The program offers prenatal care for low-income pregnant women regardless of immigration status. Services include supportive health education, care coordination, prenatal classes, home visiting, and referrals to community resources.

Services include individual supportive health education, care coordination, home visiting services, and prenatal classes. Care coordination includes phone calls and referrals to community resources. Prenatal care services are provided to low-income pregnant women without regard to immigration status.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services cover nurse case management, community health worker support, health education about pregnancy and childbirth, infant care instruction, home visiting, prenatal classes, and prenatal care services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Residents of Montgomery County, Maryland

Must live in Montgomery County

Must have Medicaid or Managed Care Organization Insurance Card
Low-income
No immigration status requirement

Contact Silver Spring Health Center at 240-777-3160 or Germantown Health Center at 240-777-3380 to enroll. list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Gap financing provided through a conditional commitment letter detailing terms and conditions of DHCA's participation in the project. The amount of appropriate financing is determined based on existing requests and priority considerations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Experienced rental housing developers with multifamily rental housing projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Gap financing for multifamily rental housing developments to increase or preserve affordable rental housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Projects must have more than four units
Developers must be experienced in rental housing development
Project must comply with stated development and applicant requirements
Project must meet one or more County and DHCA preferred criteria to increase or preserve affordable rental housing
Applicants must complete an Intake or Inquiry form before submission
Applicants are encouraged to discuss proposals with DHCA staff before inquiry form submission
Developers must finalize development plan including land use approvals, entitlements, and financing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Begin by completing an Intake or Inquiry form. DHCA staff will contact the applicant to provide next steps. For HIF and Federal Funding: developer submits Inquiry Form to identify future projects, then submits detailed Intake Form with project details. Meeting with DHCA staff follows to discuss the proposal. Staff reviews the application and seeks quarterly updates. DHCA provides a general support letter documenting support for the project. Developer finalizes development plan. Final application is submitted to DHCA and underwritten. Project is presented to DHCA Selection Advisory Committee (SAC) for review and recommendation. DHCA Director reviews SAC recommendation and determines approval. Final approval is evidenced by a conditional commitment letter.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County program that provides funding and support for recreational activities and summer camps for children ages 3 to 18 with developmental disabilities who are not connected with State of Maryland resources. Funding supports community activities like swimming and horseback riding, as well as summer camp experiences. The program also provides outreach, assistance with summer camp placements, and other programmatic and financial assistance to eligible families.

Funding is limited and covers community activities such as swimming, horseback riding, and summer camps. Therapeutic services (occupational therapy, physical therapy, speech therapy) are not covered. Additionally, programmatic support including outreach, summer camp placement assistance, and other financial assistance is provided to eligible families.

Condition results in inability to live independently

structured_extraction.program_description: A national community health program administered through the National Association of Counties (NACo) that Montgomery County participates in. It provides residents with free prescription discount cards and low-fee dental, vision, and health discount programs to help save money on prescription medications, dental care, vision services, hearing aids, diabetic supplies, and other health-related expenses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers three components: (1) Montgomery RX - free prescription discount cards with no annual fees that save an average of 24% off the retail price of prescription medicines, good at over 68,000 retail pharmacies nationwide, with discounts available for county residents and their pets; (2) Dental Discount program - low-fee membership ($6.95 monthly individual, $8.95 monthly family, $69 annual individual, $79 annual family) providing 15% to 50% discounts off most dental procedures at over 110,000 providers nationwide with no deductibles or benefit maximums, covering check-ups, cleanings, fillings, crowns, x-rays, and root canals; and (3) Health Discount program - low-fee membership ($6.95 monthly individual, $8.95 monthly family, $69 annual individual, $79 annual family) providing 15% to 75% discounts at a national network of providers, including 35% discounts on eyeglass frames with purchase of a complete pair, discounts on exams, lenses, accessories, and contact lenses, 15% off retail prices for Lasik and PRK vision services through the U.S. Laser Network, 35% discounts on hearing aids with complimentary screenings, and discounts on diabetic supplies and prepaid lab work.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 1-877-321-2652 for prescription discounts; 1-877-573-2395 for health and dental discounts
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents seeking to save money on prescription medications, dental care, vision services, hearing aids, and other health-related expenses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prescription medications at participating pharmacies, dental procedures including check-ups, cleanings, fillings, crowns, x-rays, and root canals, vision services including eyeglasses, exams, lenses, contact lenses, and laser vision correction (Lasik/PRK), hearing aids and screenings, diabetic supplies, and prepaid lab work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Montgomery County resident
This is not insurance and is a discount program, not a health insurance policy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can pick up a free prescription discount card (Montgomery RX) at all Montgomery County libraries, regional service centers, and senior centers, or download and print their own card from www.nacorx.org. To enroll in dental and health discount programs, visit www.nacohealth.org or call toll-free 1-877-573-2395. Program includes a 30-day cancellation provision for dental and health memberships. Call toll-free for more information or assistance.

Must be concerned about someone with opioid addiction or seeking overdose prevention knowledge
