structured_extraction.program_name: Neighborhood Events Matching Funds (NEMF) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by Montgomery County that provides matching funds to neighborhood organizations, block groups, tenant associations, and civic clubs to hold events and activities that engage the community, build capacity, encourage networking, and stimulate the local economy. The program encourages community involvement and local growth by matching dollar-for-dollar donations or money raised by the applicant group. It is managed by five Regional Service Offices: Bethesda-Chevy Chase, East County, Mid-County, Silver Spring, and UpCounty.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $1,000 per applicant per funding cycle for events occurring between July 1, 2024, and June 30, 2025. The county matches donations or money raised by the group on a dollar-for-dollar (1:1) basis with cash or in-kind donations. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. Due to increased demand and limited budget, funding priority is given to first-time applicants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; events must occur between July 1, 2024, and June 30, 2025
structured_extraction.contact_name: Thomas C. Dant (Bethesda/Chevy Chase), Ayanna King (East County), Talia Beaulieu-Hains (Mid-County), Nahom Tekle (Silver Spring), Jake Adler (UpCounty)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Neighborhood organizations, block groups, tenant associations, and civic clubs that are active and in good standing in Montgomery County, across five regional service areas: Bethesda-Chevy Chase, East County, Mid-County, Silver Spring, and UpCounty.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Events and activities that are open to all residents and create sustainable and lasting impacts for the neighborhood, including educational community gatherings. All events must comply with Montgomery County Law.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, managed by five Regional Service Offices: Bethesda-Chevy Chase, East County, Mid-County, Silver Spring, and UpCounty. Events must take place in Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a neighborhood organization, block group, tenant association, or civic club
Organization must be active and in good standing
Events must be open to the public
Events must create sustainable and lasting impacts for the neighborhood
Events must comply with Montgomery County Law
Applicant must provide matching funds or raise donations equal to the grant amount requested (1:1 match with cash or in-kind donations)
Applicant must provide proof of payment (receipts) for all expenditures from the eligible activity before funds are released
Applicant must be registered in the County Central Vendor System
A final report must be submitted after the event
Organization must be able to provide mission/purpose statement and list of leaders/current officers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the NEMF application form (available online or in PDF from your regional office). 2. Include applicant and event information, estimated expenses, and matching funds pledge form. 3. Submit the application to your regional service office contact. 4. The county reviews the application to verify the event qualifies (typically 1-2 weeks processing time). 5. If approved, you receive notification of the grant amount (up to $1,000). 6. Approved applicants must agree to program conditions and requirements. 7. Once approved and registered in the County Central Vendor System, provide proof of payment (receipts) for all expenditures. 8. Submit a final report after the event. 9. Funds are released after all requirements are met. Applications are accepted on an ongoing, first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: The New Farmer Program provides mentoring and specialized business training in marketing, accounting, business planning, and advanced sustainable farm practices to new farmers. Unlike traditional farm incubators that place farmers on shared space for limited time, this program matches new farmers with private landowners for long-term leases from the start, allowing farmers to focus on growing their businesses rather than finding real estate. Participants receive business planning resources, access to shared equipment, and mentor matching with experienced farmers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides mentoring, specialized business training, and business consulting services. Training occurs from January through March each year, held approximately weekly in the evenings, covering topics including customer validation, marketing, business planning, soils and composting, agritourism, value-added products, equipment and infrastructure, farm accounting and taxes, foodborne illness prevention, organic certification, season extension techniques, and integrated pest management. Participants are matched with experienced mentors who provide advice and counseling for a minimum of one year. Equipment training occurs as weather permits. The program also provides business planning resources, land matching services with private landowners for long-term leases (when available), and access to shared farm equipment. UMD Extension partners to coordinate training programs and provide business consulting services. No direct financial assistance is provided.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New farmers seeking to establish agricultural businesses in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program does not provide direct funding. It provides mentoring, business training, land matching with private owners for long-term leases (when available), access to shared farm equipment, and technical assistance with business planning and sustainable farming practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, specifically farmers matching with landowners throughout the Agricultural Reserve.
requirements_list: New farmer status
Interest in sustainable farming practices
Willingness to work with private landowners on long-term leases
Thoughtful enterprise concept demonstrating good market opportunity
Demonstrated farming or horticultural experience
Work history and references
Personal capacity to take risk with resources to cover living expenses
Awareness of sustainable farming principles

structured_extraction.program_name: Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH) & Housing Initiative Program (HIP) / Supportive Housing Rental Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides long-term rental assistance and supportive housing to eligible individuals and families in Montgomery County with special housing needs, including those exiting homelessness. Formerly known as the Supportive Housing Rental Assistance Program, the Housing Initiative Program (HIP) offers rental subsidies where participants pay 30% of their adjusted gross household income directly to the landlord, with the housing provider covering the remainder. Both PSH and HIP programs include comprehensive case management with in-home visits provided 3 to 4 times monthly. The program operates under eligibility standards and administrative procedures established by Executive Regulation 17-06AM. HIP is a permanent supportive housing program with ongoing participation as long as participants qualify and remain eligible.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants pay 30% of their adjusted gross household income directly to the landlord. HIP pays the remaining 70% of rent directly to the landlord via check or ACH/direct deposit. The program covers application fees and security deposits (up to 2 months rental amount). A utility allowance is provided to eligible participants to assist with utility costs. Participants receive monthly supportive services and case management based on their level of need, with case managers meeting with participants in their unit and in the community. Rental assistance is provided according to program eligibility standards and administrative procedures established by Executive Regulation 17-06AM. HIP is permanent supportive housing with ongoing participation as long as participants qualify and remain eligible.

Also relevant to landlords with available rental units.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing subsidy including rental assistance (70% of rent), application fees, security deposits (up to 2 months rental amount), utility allowance, and case management services including in-home visits and community-based support.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program that makes funds available to state, local, tribal, and territorial governments to plan for and implement sustainable, cost-effective measures designed to reduce the risk to individuals and property from future natural hazards, while reducing reliance on federal funding from future disasters. The program includes multiple HMA grant programs: Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC), Flood Mitigation Assistance (FMA), Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP), and HMGP Post Fire.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funding for pre-disaster mitigation projects through three main programs: (1) Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC) - nationally competitive grant designed to promote mitigation measures to reduce community disaster risk and disaster risk awareness; (2) Flood Mitigation Assistance (FMA) - nationally competitive grant for flood-prone communities registered in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP), prioritizes repetitive loss (RL) and severe repetitive loss (SRL) projects; (3) Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP) - funds plans and projects to reduce long-term community disaster risk, activated only following a Presidential Disaster Declaration. Eligible applicants must provide a minimum 25% non-federal cost share (except for small impoverished communities eligible for up to 90% federal share under BRIC, FMA and SRL properties eligible for up to 100% federal share, and RL properties eligible for up to 90% federal share). Non-federal cost share cannot consist of federal funds. Projects cannot be started or completed before the kick-off meeting with MDEM. FEMA provides 100% federal funding for subrecipient management costs for BRIC program activities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Notices of Interest due in August; deadline varies based on federal Notice of Funding Opportunities (NOFO) announcement
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (county agencies and municipalities), tribal governments, state agencies, tribal agencies, and private nonprofit organizations in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Sustainable, cost-effective measures designed to reduce the risk to individuals and property from future natural hazards. Eligible activities include: property acquisition and demolition, structure elevation, mitigation reconstruction, floodproofing of historic residential structures, generator/emergency power backup, localized and non-localized flood risk reduction, structural and non-structural retrofitting, wind retrofit, infrastructure retrofit, soil stabilization, hazard mitigation planning, capacity and capability building (project scoping, building codes, partnership building), and other measures that align with approved hazard mitigation plans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland and participating jurisdictions. Communities must be registered in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) for FMA projects and must be in good standing with NFIP.
requirements_list: Must be a state agency, local government, tribal government, private nonprofit organization, or federally recognized tribal government

Must provide minimum 25% non-federal cost share (exceptions: small impoverished communities may qualify for 90% federal share under BRIC; FMA and severe repetitive loss properties may qualify for 100% federal share; repetitive loss properties may qualify for 90% federal share)
Cannot use federal funds for the non-federal cost share
Project cannot be started or completed before the kick-off meeting with MDEM
Project must align with a current FEMA-approved hazard mitigation plan
Project must be included in an approved local hazard mitigation plan or may be considered ineligible
For NFIP-related projects, property must have an active NFIP policy and community must be in good standing with NFIP
Project must be technically feasible and cost-effective with a benefit-cost ratio demonstrating project benefits exceed costs
Activity must address eligible hazards (earthquake, flooding, severe storm, landslide, wildfire, tornado, hurricane, etc.)
Local Emergency Management Office must be made aware of the project application
No delinquency on federal debt
Environmental and historic preservation compliance required
Compliance with non-discrimination, accessibility, and procurement requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a Notice of Interest (NOI) to OEMHS in August indicating interest in pursuing an activity under one of the FEMA Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA) grant programs. 2. Select HMA program preference (BRIC, FMA, or HMGP) and provide project details including activity type, hazard mitigation activity title with location, approximate project address, total cost estimate, timeframe in months, and proposed non-federal cost share funding sources. 3. OEMHS reviews NOIs to determine basic applicability for the three HMA programs and provides technical assistance. 4. Upon State (MDEM) approval of NOI, OEMHS provides additional technical assistance for subapplication development. 5. Submit complete subapplication including scope of work, schedule, budget, cost-effectiveness documentation, environmental and historic preservation documentation, and required certifications and assurances. 6. OEMHS submits recommended sub-applications to FEMA through MDEM (Maryland Department of Emergency Management). 7. MDEM is the pass-through agency and disburses grant awards to successful subapplicants. 8. Submission of an NOI does not guarantee future approval of awards.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program administered by the Montgomery County Police Department that provides rebates to incentivize the installation of private security cameras at residential, commercial, and nonprofit properties throughout Montgomery County. The program aims to deter and solve crime, with particular focus on geographic areas experiencing relatively high crime incidents. Property owners and tenants — including residents, businesses, and nonprofit organizations — can apply for rebates to help cover the cost of purchasing and installing eligible security camera systems. The program has been expanded to include more communities around downtown commercial centers, and further expansion to additional geographic areas has been requested. Camera footage is not automatically shared with police; the Department may only access video with the express permission of the applicant or through other legal mechanisms.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A rebate of up to $250 per security camera covering the cost of the camera only. Residents can receive one rebate per qualifying residence (up to $250), while businesses and nonprofit organizations can receive up to five rebates for a maximum of $1,250. The rebate amount shall not exceed the actual cost of the camera purchase. Installation, accessories, recording subscriptions, and video storage costs are not covered. Rebate amounts are subject to availability of funds and are provided on a first-come, first-served basis by the Montgomery County Government Department of Finance. Cameras must be purchased on or after November 15, 2023. In FY24, the Council approved $255,000 for the program, which could provide reimbursement for approximately 1,020 cameras.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing basis while funds remain available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and tenants in Montgomery County — including residents, businesses, and nonprofit organizations — who wish to install security cameras at their properties, with priority given to those in geographic areas experiencing relatively high crime incidents and priority zones designated by the Police Chief.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of security cameras that meet minimum technical specifications. Cameras must be installed on the exterior of a building, be weatherproof, retain video footage for at least seven days, have a minimum resolution of 1 megapixel, and meet other specified requirements. Installation costs, accessories, recording subscriptions, and video storage are not covered.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Priority areas are one or more police districts identified by the Police Chief as needing additional security cameras based upon public safety indicators, including crime levels. Priority zones are designated geographic areas within Montgomery County experiencing relatively high crime incidents, particularly around downtown commercial centers and surrounding communities. Priority areas will be evaluated annually. Expansion to additional areas has been requested.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants register online and can determine whether their property is located in a Priority Area through the Police Department's camera application website. If installed by the property owner or another person without a valid Business License, a police officer conducts an on-site visit to verify installation. Upon approval and compliance with all requirements, and subject to the availability of funds, the applicable rebate amount is processed by the Montgomery County Government Finance Department and funds are sent to the applicant at the address provided on the application form. Applicants can also contact the Montgomery County Police Department at 240-773-6120 or email pol.camera.rebate@montgomerycountymd.gov for more information.

Developers must execute a written agreement with the Department of Housing and Community Affairs prior to issuance of building permits, specifying the affordable housing units and construction staging plan. Affordable housing units are subject to price controls and income restrictions for specified control periods (10 years for for-sale units, 20 years for rental units).

structured_extraction.program_description: An education and training program for young adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Participants complete three 10-week intensive worksite internships supported by job coaches, working approximately 25 hours per week while attending one hour of daily classroom instruction. The program runs from September to June.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Unpaid volunteer internships with three 10-week intensive worksite placements supported by job coaches. Participants work approximately 25 hours per week and receive one hour of classroom instruction daily. Program hours are 8:30 am to 2:30 pm, running from September to June. A four-week trial period is required for all accepted enrollees. Program begins late August to early September.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities between ages 18 and 30
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants receive training, career development, and work experience through internship placements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland residents only. Must have DDA funding in place prior to start date of program or have private pay agreement established with Ivymount.
requirements_list: Between ages 18 and 30
Have an intellectual and/or developmental disability
Eligible for DDA funding or able to do Private Pay
Must be a Maryland resident
High school diploma or certificate of completion required
Attendance at one Information Session is required for acceptance into the program
Current IEP for applicants currently in school
Person Centered Plan (PCP) for applicants receiving DDA/DDS supports
Most recent psychological evaluation/report (school or private therapist/counselor)
Resume of applicant's work/volunteer history
Proof of funding (eligibility letter from DDA or service funding plan for DORS/RSA)
Parent Questionnaire completed
Some sites require passing a criminal background check and drug screen
NIH program only requires documentation of negative TB test within 6 months of program start date
Must be able to pass background check
Must use public transportation or make private arrangements to and from program
Must attend required Open House in summer at host business site
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Attendance at one Information Session is required. 2. Download and complete the Project SEARCH Montgomery Application form from SEEC. 3. Gather required documents: current photo, high school diploma or certificate of completion, current IEP (if in school), Person Centered Plan (if receiving DDA/DDS supports), most recent psychological evaluation/report, resume of work/volunteer history, proof of funding, and completed Parent Questionnaire. 4. Provide three references other than family. 5. Email or mail completed application and all supporting documents to PSRecruitment@seeconline.org. 6. Selection Committee will review application and documents for compatibility with program requirements. 7. Vocational Rehabilitation Counselors will complete eligibility and develop Individual Plan of Employment in summer before program starts. 8. If accepted, attend required Open House in summer at host business site. 9. All accepted applicants will begin with a four-week trial period.

structured_extraction.program_description: A rental assistance program where vouchers are tied to specific units in designated buildings or developments. Eligible low-income households must reside in the assigned property to receive assistance. The program is administered both through the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County and Rockville Housing Enterprises for properties within their respective jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Vouchers are tied to specific units in designated buildings or developments, providing rental assistance to eligible households who reside in those properties. The subsidy stays with the unit, so participants must live in the assigned property to receive assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income individuals and families seeking rental assistance in designated buildings or developments in Montgomery County, including properties administered by the Housing Opportunities Commission and Rockville Housing Enterprises
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance for housing in designated buildings or specific developments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, including the City of Rockville
requirements_list: Residency in the assigned building or participating development
Household must meet income eligibility requirements for low-income assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County or Rockville Housing Enterprises, depending on the specific property or development where assistance is sought.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit for Public Safety Officers and Emergency Communications Specialists
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit applied to Montgomery County property taxes for eligible public safety officers, public safety emergency communications specialists, deputy sheriffs, correctional officers, and volunteer fire and rescue department members who are legal owners of their principal residence in Montgomery County. The credit equals the lesser of $2,500 or the amount of County property tax due on the property, and must be applied for annually by April 1 prior to the tax levy year in which the credit is sought.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An annual property tax credit of up to $2,500 or the full amount of County property tax due on the owner-occupied principal residence, whichever is less. Applicants must reapply each year by April 1 prior to the tax levy year for which the credit is sought.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1 of the year prior to the Tax Levy Year that the credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active public safety officers, public safety emergency communications specialists, deputy sheriffs, correctional officers, and volunteer fire and rescue department members employed by Montgomery County, M-NCPPC, WSSC, WSTC, county municipalities, or assigned to the Department of Health and Human Services Crisis Center, who own and occupy their principal residence in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit applied to Montgomery County property tax liability on an owner-occupied principal residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in Montgomery County and must be the principal residence of the owner.
requirements_list: Must be an active public safety officer, public safety emergency communications specialist, deputy sheriff, correctional officer, or active volunteer fire and rescue department volunteer/firefighter
Must be employed by Montgomery County, M-NCPPC, WSSC, WSTC, a County municipality, or the Department of Health and Human Services Crisis Center (for certain positions)
Employees of M-NCPPC, WSSC, WSTC, county municipalities, or the Crisis Center must be certified as meeting the definition of public safety officer
Must be the legal owner of an owner-occupied property in Montgomery County
Property must be the principal residence of the owner
Must apply annually by April 1 prior to the tax levy year for which the credit is sought
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application by April 1 prior to the tax levy year for which the credit is sought. Different application forms are available depending on employer: Active County Employee, Fire Rescue Services Volunteers, M-NCPPC Public Safety Officers, WSSC Public Safety Officers, Gaithersburg Public Safety Officers, Rockville Public Safety Officers, Takoma Park Public Safety Officers, or Chevy Chase Village Public Safety Officers. An automatic confirmation email is sent to the email address provided within 24 hours of submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides a reduction in County property taxes for qualified disabled veterans or their surviving spouses based on the percentage of their service-connected disability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The tax credit equals 50% of the County property tax for veterans with a service-connected disability of 75% or more, or 25% of the County property tax for veterans with a service-connected disability between 50% and 74%. The disabled veteran's property must be their principal residence and must not be occupied by more than 2 families. Veterans who qualify for a property tax exemption under Maryland Tax Property Article Section 7-208 are not eligible for this credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified disabled veterans or their surviving spouses who own property in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit reduces the amount of property tax owed to Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be a qualified disabled veteran or surviving spouse of a qualified disabled veteran
Applicant must own property in Montgomery County as their principal residence
Property must not be occupied by more than 2 families
Veteran must have been discharged under honorable conditions from active service in the U.S. Armed Forces
Veteran must have a service-connected disability rated at 50% or higher, either permanent or non-permanent (100%)
Federal adjusted gross income of the disabled veteran for the preceding taxable year must not exceed $100,000
Applicant cannot qualify for a property tax exemption under Maryland Tax Property Article Section 7-208
Applicant must submit application on or before April 1 before the tax year seeking the credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Property Tax Credit – Disabled Veterans application form by April 1 before the tax year seeking the credit. Applicants must include with the application: (1) a copy of the disabled veteran's DD-214 discharge document indicating discharge under honorable conditions, (2) certification of the disabled veteran's disability from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (must indicate percentage of disability), and (3) a copy of the most recent federal income tax return (SSN may be redacted). All three required documents must be submitted or the application will not be processed.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows homeowners to defer payment of County property taxes on their principal residence. Eligible homeowners can postpone paying the amount by which their current year County taxes exceed the prior year's taxes, with interest accruing annually.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners can defer payment of the portion of County property taxes that exceed the prior year's amount. Interest accrues annually at a rate set by the County that does not exceed the prime lending rate (approximately 3%). The accumulated deferred taxes and interest cannot exceed 50% of the property's full cash value.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Montgomery County whose principal residence is a single-family home or residential property they own and occupy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax payments on the owner's principal residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County residential properties used as the owner's principal residence.
requirements_list: Gross income or combined gross income of all residents in the dwelling did not exceed $120,000 in the preceding calendar year
Owner or at least one owner must reside in the dwelling as their principal place of residence
Owner must have resided in the dwelling for at least 5 years
Property must be residential real property used as the owner's principal residence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The page does not provide specific application process steps.

structured_extraction.program_description: A conditional grant program administered as a sub-program of the Economic Development Fund that provides financial assistance to eligible for-profit small businesses and non-profit organizations in Montgomery County experiencing significant adverse impacts from a communicable disease outbreak that resulted in a Federal, State, or County Public Health Emergency order restricting business operations. Originally established in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, the program provides grants of up to $75,000 for businesses suffering financial loss, as well as micro-grants to assist with transitioning to telework. Total program allocation was $25 million. Grants are awarded through a formal process and criteria established in temporary regulation 9-20T.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and conditional grants awarded in multiple potential disbursements. Initial disbursement up to $10,000 for businesses demonstrating significant financial loss (50% or greater revenue decline). Maximum aggregate assistance per business: $75,000 for revenue loss recovery. Separate assistance up to $2,500 available for technology equipment and software to facilitate employee teleworking. Additional disbursements available subject to appropriation and availability of funds, based on demonstrated loss of additional revenue since most recent prior disbursement. Assistance calculated based on difference between historical monthly/quarterly average revenue and adjusted revenue during public health emergency period. Conditional grants remain as grants upon satisfactory adherence to grant agreement terms; non-compliance results in partial or full repayment to County. Total program allocation: $25 million, with $10 million reserved for initial $10,000 disbursements and one-quarter of funds reserved for restaurants and retail storefront establishments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Privately owned local for-profit small businesses (100 or fewer full-time equivalent employees) and non-profit organizations located in Montgomery County that have experienced significant adverse impacts from a public health emergency (including COVID-19) that resulted in a Federal, State, or County Public Health Emergency order restricting business operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance covers actual loss in revenue due to public health emergency restrictions on business operations. Grant funds cannot be used for: (1) expenses reimbursed by COVID-19 related Federal or State government assistance programs, which must be repaid; (2) losses reimbursed through business insurance policies; (3) wages paid to employees during periods the employee is eligible for unemployment insurance benefits. Separate technology assistance (up to $2,500) may be used for purchasing technology equipment and software to facilitate employee teleworking during a public health emergency.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. Business must have its principal place of business in Montgomery County, defined as either: (1) physical business location(s) only in the County, or (2) physical business locations both in and outside the County where County-based location(s) account for over 50% of total employees or over 50% of gross sales.
requirements_list: Business or organization must be a privately owned local for-profit business or non-profit organization
Must have principal place of business in Montgomery County, Maryland
Must employ 100 or fewer full-time or full-time equivalent employees
Must be in existence prior to March 5, 2020 and in good standing with the State of Maryland (registration with SDAT sufficient for sole proprietorships and general partnerships)

Must demonstrate significant financial loss (adjusted revenue decline of 50% or greater) for a financial period caused directly or indirectly by the public health emergency when compared to a financial period of equal duration prior to March 5, 2020
Must provide documentation such as federal income tax returns and Profit and Loss Statements demonstrating revenue before and after the public health emergency
All grants and conditional grants are subject to appropriation and availability of funds

Must enter into a grant agreement with the County including authorization for County to audit financial records, reporting obligations to Director of Finance, obligation to remit unused or improperly used funds, and certification under penalty of perjury that all application statements are true and correct
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted online. Applicants must provide documentation including federal income tax returns and Profit and Loss Statements demonstrating revenue for a financial period immediately prior to the Public Health Emergency and corresponding financial documentation demonstrating significant loss of revenue. The County calculates eligibility and grant amounts using the following process: (1) Determine Annual Historical Average revenue prior to Public Health Emergency; (2) Calculate Monthly or Quarterly Historical Average as baseline; (3) Determine PHE Revenue for reported financial period; (4) Adjust PHE Revenue by adding back any deferred payroll expenses or rent to create Adjusted Revenue; (5) Calculate Percentage Decline by subtracting Adjusted Revenue from Historical Average and dividing by Historical Average; (6) If Percentage Decline exceeds 50%, applicant qualifies for Significant Financial Loss and initial disbursement up to $10,000; (7) Recommended Grant Amount calculated by subtracting Adjusted Revenue from Historical Average, up to maximum of $75,000 aggregate. Initial $10,000 disbursements prioritized from $10 million reserve. Additional disbursements evaluated once initial reserve is committed, subject to availability of funds. For technology assistance, applicants may separately apply for up to $2,500 for equipment and software purchases. Grant recipients must adhere to conditional grant terms; Director establishes closing documents and requires compliance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Purple Line Small Business Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides grants to small businesses that have been affected by construction impacts from the Purple Line transit project. Eligible businesses can receive up to $50,000 in compensation for the impact of Purple Line construction.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $50,000 for small businesses impacted by Purple Line construction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses in the Purple Line project area affected by construction.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To compensate for the impact of Purple Line construction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Purple Line construction project area in Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Small business status
Located in area impacted by Purple Line construction
Meet program eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit applications through the program website by the first round deadline of March 14.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free technical assistance and coaching program to help licensed child care centers, letter of compliance programs, and registered family child care providers improve the quality of their services. The program provides expert coaches, group sessions, peer mentors, and multilingual support to guide providers toward quality improvement goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free coaching and technical assistance from Quality Enhancement Coordinators and business coaches. Services include guidance for reaching Maryland EXCELS levels 3 to 5, support for obtaining and maintaining National and State accreditation, leadership development for practitioners, business coaching on marketing and operations, and reimbursement for accreditation materials. Services are available both onsite and virtually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers, letter of compliance programs, and registered family child care providers in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Quality improvement coaching, accreditation support, leadership development, business operations coaching, and accreditation materials reimbursement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County only.
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care center, letter of compliance program, or registered family child care program in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Quality Enhancement program to work with coordinators who will develop and implement an individualized action plan for your program. Reimbursement requests for accreditation materials and NAFCC membership can be submitted through the provided online forms.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program where Montgomery County Public Schools (MCPS) high school horticulture and environmental science classes receive plants, pots, soil, and guidance to propagate native plants in their greenhouses. Plants are grown in the second semester and used in watershed restoration projects. Schools return a portion of plants to the Department of Environmental Protection for outreach and stormwater management, and can use the remaining plants for native plant sales or other environmental projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides native plants (plugs/seedlings), pots, potting soil, and technical guidance at no charge to participating schools. Native plant seeds are harvested, germinated, and grown at Pope Farm Greenhouses, then provided to schools as plug seedlings in trays. High school horticulture and AP environmental studies classes transplant plugs into 1-quart pots and grow the plants during the second semester. Schools are required to return approximately 33 percent of the plants produced to RainScapes by mid-spring (typically before Spring Break but no later than the first week of May) for use in watershed restoration and stormwater management projects throughout the county. Schools retain the balance of plants for use in community-based projects or native plant sales.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 30th for the following academic year
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school horticulture and AP environmental studies teachers and students in Montgomery County Public Schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Native plant plugs/seedlings, growing media (potting soil), pots, and technical guidance for propagating native plants in school greenhouses for educational purposes and watershed restoration projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County Public Schools only
requirements_list: High school must be part of Montgomery County Public School System (MCPS)
School must have horticulture and/or AP environmental studies programs
School must have greenhouse access
Participation is by invitation based on previous participation or by teacher request
School must return at least 33 percent of plants provided to RainScapes by mid-spring (typically before Spring Break but no later than the first week of May)
School must submit a one-page assessment survey of the project
Plants must be properly transplanted from plugs to 1-quart pots following provided planting guidelines
Plant tags must be maintained with transplanted plants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participation is by invitation based on previous participation, or teachers can request participation by sending an email to rainscapes.application@montgomerycountymd.gov by March 30th for the following academic year. After approval, schools coordinate pickups of native plant plugs, pots, and potting soil from Pope Farm Greenhouses. Teachers are responsible for collecting materials and coordinating pickup details. Detailed plug planting instructions are provided to guide transplanting into 1-quart containers. RainScapes staff picks up the mature plants from schools in the spring, typically before Spring Break but no later than the first week of May. Plants are then transported to Pope Farm and distributed to various watershed restoration and stormwater management projects throughout Montgomery County.

structured_extraction.program_description: A rebate program that pays property owners to install permeable pavement on their property. Permeable paving allows stormwater to seep into the ground while maintaining a durable surface for cars and people. Specially engineered layers under the permeable paving surface clean and soak in stormwater.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebate of $14 per square foot for permeable pavement installation. Residential projects: 100 square foot minimum with maximum rebate of $7,500. Commercial/Institutional projects: 200 square foot minimum with maximum rebate of $20,000. Applications are accepted on a first come, first served basis. Rebate is processed for payment after project passes final inspection and receipts and property owner agreement are submitted.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications currently closed but program is recurring
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County property owners located outside the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of permeable pavement (permeable interlocking concrete pavers) to replace existing impervious surfaces such as driveways, walkways, patios, and sidewalks. Runoff from adjacent impervious surfaces such as roofs may also be directed to the permeable pavement system.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, but excluding properties within the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park. Properties must be on private property and cannot be installed in the County's right-of-way.
requirements_list: 100 square foot minimum project size for residential; 200 square feet minimum for commercial/institutional
Permeable pavement must meet county requirements and specifications and be installed according to RainScapes Permeable Paver Manual or PICP specifications
Project must be new, not fulfilling a county-required stormwater permit
Soil must pass a percolation test with drainage within 36 hours
Driveway slope cannot exceed 5% and must slope away from house
Cannot be installed on slopes greater than 10%
Waterproof liner required within 10 feet of house foundation and 5 feet from slab
Cannot be installed over water, sewer, or gas mains; maintain 5-foot setback from sanitary sewer or water mains
Maintain 100-foot setback from water supply wells
Maintain 50-foot setback from septic system components
Do not disturb more than 25% of critical root zone for trees with diameter at breast height of 8 inches or greater
Residential installations: must be installed by certified ICPI contractor with PICP training or experienced contractor with portfolio of 5 permeable paver projects
Commercial installations: must be installed by contractor with PICP Specialist designation
Contractor must have attended PICP training through ICPI or submit portfolio of at least 5 permeable projects
Use only washed natural stone aggregates; recycled construction materials not allowed
Aggregates used must be washed natural stone
Geotextiles should only be used on sidewalls
Choker course of pea gravel (2-4 inches) required between aggregate and subsoil
Downspout connection to system required where possible
Underdrain required if perc rate exceeds 36 hours
Projects must be installed within 6 months of approval letter date
Preliminary inspection required before installation begins (mandatory)
Final inspection required after installation completion
Receipts must be itemized with sales tax subtracted
Property owner agreement must be electronically signed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review RainScapes website and design manual for permeable pavement. Review the Application Process document. 2. Complete and submit the online RainScapes rebate application. Applicant will receive confirmation email from RainScapes@montgomerycountymd.gov if application is complete. 3. Department of Environmental Protection will contact applicant to schedule a mandatory preliminary inspection to ensure site suitability. No preliminary inspection is required for rain barrels. 4. Submit supporting documents specific to permeable pavement rebate type (contractor qualifications, Right of Way permit if applicable). This can happen before or after preliminary inspection. 5. Once preliminary inspection is passed and all supporting documents are approved, applicant receives an approval letter with approval details and rebate funding level, plus property owner agreement. 6. Installation can begin after receiving approval letter. Projects must be installed within 6 months of the approval letter date. 7. After project installation is complete, contact Department of Environmental Protection to schedule a final inspection. 8. At final inspection, applicant may receive a list of necessary changes/adjustments. Photo-document completion of any adjustments and email to RainScapes@montgomerycountymd.gov. A second final inspection may be necessary depending on number of adjustments. 9. Submit itemized receipts (with sales tax subtracted) and electronically-signed property owner agreement. 10. Rebate is processed for payment after project passes final inspection and all required documents are submitted. Rebate check is issued by Montgomery County Department of Finance. Application status can be checked online.

structured_extraction.program_name: RainScapes Rewards Rebate Program - Pavement Removal
structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides rebates to property owners who remove pavement, decompact soil, and plant vegetation to replace hard surfaces with natural surfaces such as rain gardens, conservation landscaping, or lawn. This helps reduce stormwater runoff and provides environmental benefits to the community.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates are provided based on the type of replacement material: $3 per square foot if replacing pavement with sod; $6 per square foot if replacing pavement with conservation landscape with less than 3 inches of temporary ponding; $7 per square foot if replacing pavement with conservation landscape with 3 inches of temporary ponding and berms or stone check dams. Maximum rebate amounts are $7,500 for residential properties and $20,000 for commercial/institutional properties. Minimum project sizes are 100 square feet for residential properties and 200 square feet for commercial/institutional properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Montgomery County (outside the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park) who want to remove pavement and replace it with natural vegetation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used to remove pavement, decompact soil, and plant vegetation to create natural surfaces such as rain gardens, conservation landscaping, or lawn. Rebates can cover project costs including pavement removal, soil amendment, and planting materials.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, but outside of the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park. Properties must be on private property and not in the County's right-of-way. These jurisdictions collect their Water Quality Protection Charge separately.
requirements_list: Minimum project size: 100 square feet for residential properties, 200 square feet for commercial/institutional properties
Replaces existing impervious surface (driveway, walkway, patio, etc.)
Must be on private property and not in County's right-of-way
Does not redirect existing flow of water to a paved surface or neighbor's property
Does not back up water onto neighbor's property
Projects within close proximity of large canopy trees approved on case-by-case basis
Planting plan with graphic scale required if installing conservation landscape
HOA approval letter required if applicable
For conservation landscaping: at least 50 percent of plants must be native species
Soil must be decompacted at least 9 inches and amended with at least 2 inches of compost
Project must be installed within six months of approval letter date
Only new projects eligible; cannot fulfill county-required stormwater permits
Proper sediment control procedures must be utilized during installation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Read the RainScapes website and design manual for pavement removal project. 2. Review the Application Process document. 3. Complete and submit the online application. Confirmation will be sent via email to RainScapes@montgomerycountymd.gov. 4. Department of Environmental Protection will contact you to schedule a mandatory preliminary inspection before project installation begins. 5. Submit supporting documents specific to pavement removal (planting plan with graphic scale if applicable, HOA approval letter if needed). 6. Once preliminary inspection is passed and supporting documents are approved, you will receive an approval letter with rebate funding level and property owner agreement. 7. Installation must occur within six months of approval letter date. 8. After project installation, schedule a final inspection with the Department of Environmental Protection. 9. At final inspection, you may receive a list of necessary adjustments. Photo-document and email any adjustments to RainScapes@montgomerycountymd.gov. 10. Submit itemized receipts (with sales tax subtracted) and electronically-signed property owner agreement. 11. Rebate check will be issued by Montgomery County Department of Finance after project passes final inspection and receipts/agreement are submitted.

structured_extraction.program_description: A cost-share rebate program administered by Montgomery County that helps residential, commercial, institutional, and community property owners install stormwater management landscape techniques on their properties to reduce stormwater runoff and prevent pollution from flowing into storm drains and streams. Eligible project types include rain gardens, conservation landscapes, water harvesting systems (rain barrels and cisterns), green roofs, permeable pavement, and pavement removal. The program also supports community properties such as HOAs, congregations, multi-family properties, institutional properties, private schools, and community pools. Rebates are funded by the Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) and are issued after project completion and final inspection. Completing a RainScapes project may also make property owners eligible for a Water Quality Protection Charge credit on their property tax bill.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides cost-share rebates to offset the cost of installing eligible stormwater management projects. Rebate amounts vary by project type: Rain Garden — $10 per square foot (maximum $7,500 for residential, $20,000 for commercial/institutional; minimum 75 sq ft for residential, 100 sq ft for commercial/institutional). Conservation Landscape — $5 per sq ft (no ponding) or $6 per sq ft (with 3 inches of ponding; minimum 250 sq ft for residential, 350 sq ft for commercial/institutional). Rain Barrels — $1 per gallon, maximum $250 (minimum 200 gallons for residential, 100 gallons for townhomes, 50 gallon minimum per individual barrel). Cisterns — $1 per gallon, maximum $500 for residential and $2,000 for commercial/institutional (250–500 gallon range for residential; up to 2,000 gallons for commercial/institutional; exceptions possible). Properties using both rain barrels and cisterns can receive a combined maximum of $750. Property owners pay the full upfront cost; rebate is issued based on submitted itemized receipts (sales tax excluded) after final inspection. Rebate checks are typically issued within 8–12 weeks after final inspection. Rebates are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. Projects must be completed within 6 months of approval. For all projects except rain barrels, a preliminary inspection is required after application submittal to ensure site suitability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No fixed deadline; rolling admissions on a first-come, first-served basis. Application period may be periodically closed. Processing time 8–12 weeks for planner response; 6 months to complete project after approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Montgomery County outside the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park, including residential homeowners, commercial property owners, multi-family properties, homeowner associations, congregations, private schools, community pools, institutional properties, and community organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of stormwater management landscape techniques and retrofits including: rain gardens, conservation landscapes (native plants replacing lawn or invasive species), water harvesting systems (rain barrels and cisterns), green roofs, permeable pavement, and pavement removal. Eligible expenses include purchase of approved native plants, materials (mulch, compost), hardware (pipes, connectors), equipment rental, design fees, and labor directly related to the project. Tools and equipment for personal use (shovels, wheelbarrows) are not eligible. Sales tax is excluded from eligible costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, excluding properties within the incorporated city limits of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park (which have their own separate rebate programs). Property must not be within a right-of-way or easement to qualify. Projects must be located on private property. For ponding gardens (rain gardens and 3-inch ponding conservation landscapes), must be at least 10 feet away from building foundations and downhill from structures.
requirements_list: Property must be located in Montgomery County outside the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park
Project must be one of the eligible RainScapes project types: rain garden, conservation landscape, water harvesting (rain barrel or cistern), green roof, permeable pavement, or pavement removal
Project must receive runoff from an impervious surface
Project cannot have been installed prior to RainScapes approval
Project site cannot have already received a RainScapes rebate for the same project
Project cannot require a permit or be installed due to a stormwater permit requirement
Project cannot be grant-funded
Project cannot be re-landscaping of current healthy, non-invasive landscaping
Native plants must comprise at least 75% of planted projects (both in plant quantity and coverage); invasive or sterile cultivars are not permitted
Rain garden must be at least 75 square feet and 6 inches deep, designed to drain within 24–48 hours, and must pass a percolation test (drain time 0–36 hours)
Rain garden must be at least 10 feet away from all building foundations and downhill from structures

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Read the RainScapes website and design manual for the specific project type. Review the Application Process document. 2. Submit an online application through the RainScapes Rewards portal at RainScapes.org, including your Property Tax ID. 3. Submit your application; you will receive a confirmation email from RainScapes@montgomerycountymd.gov. If you do not receive an email, your application was not completed successfully. 4. For most projects (except rain barrels), within 2–4 weeks of application submittal, the Department of Environmental Protection will contact you to schedule a mandatory preliminary inspection to ensure site suitability. Preliminary inspections are required before project installation begins. Overall processing time is 8–12 weeks for planner response. 5. Submit project-specific supporting documents (within 3 months of receiving site assessment report). Required documents vary by project type but include: planting plan with graphic scale (for planted projects), plant list with varieties/quantities/sizes, location plan indicating foundation area, and HOA approval letter if applicable. 6. Once you have passed the preliminary inspection and all supporting documents are approved, you will receive an application response letter via email with approval details and the approved rebate funding level. A Property Owner Agreement will also be sent at this time. Do not begin installation before receiving this approval letter. 7. Complete installation within 6 months of the approval letter date. Planted projects typically installed April through November; permeable pavement year-round (except frozen ground); water harvesting in spring, summer, or fall. 8. Schedule and complete a final inspection with your assigned planner. Cistern projects also require a preliminary inspection after application submittal. 9. At final inspection, you may receive a list of necessary changes or adjustments to make before a rebate can be issued. Photo-document completion of any adjustments and email to RainScapes@montgomerycountymd.gov. Depending on the number of adjustments, a second final inspection may be necessary. 10. After passing final inspection, submit all required documents: copies of itemized receipts with sales tax subtracted, photos and measurements of completed project, and electronically sign and submit the Property Owner Agreement. 11. The Department of Finance will process your rebate after your project passes final inspection and all required documents are received. Rebate checks are typically issued within 8–12 weeks after final inspection. 12. After project completion, you become eligible to apply for a Water Quality Protection Charge credit on your property tax bill. Visit MontgomeryCountyMD.gov/water/WQPC to learn more and apply. Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis; check the online portal for current application period status.

structured_extraction.program_name: Resilient Infrastructure- Local Food Aggregation Grant (Food Aggregation Grant Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: A multi-year single-award competitive grant opportunity providing funding for operating and build-out costs to establish a local food aggregation facility in Montgomery County. The program supports the aggregation, distribution, and marketing of food grown by regional and County-based farmers to wholesale and institutional markets, with the goal of meeting current and future market demand. The grant is awarded to one successful applicant through a two-stage application process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A competitive single-award grant with up to $550,000 in multi-year funding for operating and build-out costs to establish a local food aggregation facility. Year 1 funding ($550,000): $250,000 in flexible grant funding for operational activities and startup costs (up-front payment) plus $300,000 in capital/construction grant funds (reimbursable). Minimum 50% matching funds required ($275,000), with no more than 20% in-kind ($55,000). Year 2 funding ($500,000, contingent on appropriation and Year 1 compliance): $200,000 in operational grant funding plus $300,000 in County committed purchases. Years 3-4 funding ($300,000 each year, contingent on appropriation and compliance): $300,000 in County committed purchases. The grant supports aggregating, distributing, and marketing food grown by regional and County-based farmers to wholesale and institutional markets including schools, hospitals, senior centers, food banks, and correctional facilities. The application process consists of two stages: Stage One assessed eligibility for grant funding, and Stage Two assesses program alignment and viability of success.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Catherine Nardi for program scope and requirements; Greg Weissman for technical application questions
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit organizations with demonstrated experience in food aggregation, distribution, and wholesale/institutional sales seeking to establish or expand a local food aggregation facility to aggregate, distribute, and market food grown by regional and County-based farmers to wholesale and institutional markets in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating and build-out costs to establish an aggregation facility for locally produced food, including: construction and retrofitting of facilities; startup costs; facility planning and management; technology systems for managing buyer and seller relationships; farmer outreach and capacity building; inventory management; logistics and fleet management; staffing; and aggregating, distributing, and marketing food grown by regional and County-based farmers to wholesale and institutional markets.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. The organization's principal place of business must be located in Montgomery County; if a national or regional organization, it must have a location in Montgomery County through which it provides the grant-funded services. All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and/or exclusively for Montgomery County residents. While the aggregation facility must be located in Montgomery County, the project is designed to support regional food value-chains and can source from producers in the Mid-Atlantic region (DC, Maryland, Virginia, Delaware, PA, NJ, West Virginia).

Activities must not be provided in promotion of particular religion or political party

Activities must be open and available to all Montgomery County residents regardless of race, color, religious creed, ancestry, national origin, age, sex, marital status, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, family responsibility, genetic status, presence of children, or source of income
Organization may only submit one application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This is a two-stage application process. Stage One assessed eligibility for grant funding, and applicants who received notification from OFSR and OGM that they passed Stage One are invited to participate in Stage Two. Stage Two assesses program alignment and viability of success. NOFO available and applications open March 18, 2026. MS Teams Live Grant Information Session will be held (details to be sent to applicants). Applications must be submitted through the Online Grants Application Platform by April 22, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST. Applications that are incomplete, do not meet legal requirements, or are submitted after the deadline will not be accepted. OGM will conduct an Administrative Review assessing Montgomery County Eligibility Conditions and application completeness. Applications will then undergo panel review scoring based on published criteria. Award notification will follow the review process. Applicants requiring ADA accommodations should contact OGM to discuss alternative submission options.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides short-term temporary relief to primary unpaid full-time live-in caregivers who are caring for frail elderly adults, functionally disabled adults (including those with Alzheimer's disease and other dementias), children with challenging behaviors, children and adults with developmental disabilities, and children with severe medical conditions. Care is provided by trained, certified care workers in the family's home, adult medical day programs, or approved respite care facilities. The program coordinates with families to locate appropriate providers and may provide a subsidy to pay for respite care services, though funding is limited and not guaranteed for every respite occasion requested.

Families can choose from many respite care venues, including the family home, adult medical day programs, and approved respite facilities. Respite staff work with families to locate appropriate providers for direct services after the applicant completes an orientation. Respite may provide a subsidy but it is not an entitlement — eligibility for a subsidy does not guarantee funds for each respite occasion requested due to limited funding. Short-term relief may range from a few hours to a day, a weekend, or sometimes longer.

Patients must bring proof of income to each visit. Services cover routine dental care but do not include specialty care such as dentures.

The maximum length of stay is thirty days. All cats and dogs must be spayed or neutered; if not already altered, OAS performs the procedure at the shelter.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program covers temporary care and housing of eligible pets, including intake assessments, required vaccinations, heartworm or FELV/FIV testing, and spay/neuter procedures if needed.
