structured_extraction.program_description: Same Day Access is a subsidized transportation program for certified MetroAccess participants who reside in Montgomery County. There is no income requirement. Participants receive $60 value on their Call-n-Ride swipe card when they pay $30.00, representing a 50 percent discount on transportation value. The benefit is provided once per month and can be used for medical and personal appointments within Montgomery County, with special exceptions for approved medical facilities in designated service areas outside the county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants with current MetroAccess identification cards receive a $60 subsidy value on their Call-n-Ride swipe card when they pay $30.00 out-of-pocket, representing a 50 percent discount on transportation value. This benefit is provided once per month with no income requirement. The maximum trip limit per one-way trip within Montgomery County is $60.00 including tip. Participants can accumulate and carry a maximum balance of $360 on their CNR swipe card. Money placed on the card never expires. Participants may also choose to add $60 per month in subsidy value. The subsidy helps offset the cost of fares charged by participating taxicab companies at meter rates set by Montgomery County. Fares include an initial charge of $4.00, $2.00 per mile, $1.00 per extra passenger, $1.00 for personal service loading items, and $28.00 per hour for traffic delay time. Tips not to exceed 15% of the fare are allowed. Participants are responsible for all tolls.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who are certified MetroAccess participants with current MetroAccess Identification cards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subsidized taxi transportation for medical and personal appointments within Montgomery County. Trips to approved medical facilities in designated service areas outside Montgomery County are allowed with pre-authorization. Designated service areas include Baltimore, Prince George's County, Howard County, Northern Virginia, and Washington D.C.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County. Special exceptions have been made to allow transportation to approved medical facilities in Designated Service Areas located in Baltimore, Prince George's County, Howard County, Northern Virginia, and Washington D.C. Pre-authorization is required for trips exceeding the $60 maximum trip limit or to designated medical facilities.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident (PO Box not acceptable)
Must have a current MetroAccess identification card
Must complete SDA Application Form with supporting documentation to verify eligibility

Must provide proof of Montgomery County residence (recent Social Security/SSI Statement, Utility Bill, IRS W-2, Property Tax Bill, Homeowner's/Auto/Renter's Insurance Bill, Monthly Mortgage Statement, or Residential Rental/Lease Agreement)
Must provide photocopy of government issued photo identification
Passport photo (2 inch x 2 inch) recommended but not required
No income requirement
Must recertify upon renewal of Metro Access ID card by providing photocopy of renewed Metro Access ID card
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To become a new Same Day Access participant, complete the SDA Application Form with all required supporting documentation. Application must be completed in its entirety. Submit required documents including proof of Montgomery County residence and current Metro Access Identification card. Applications take approximately 10 business days to process. Upon approval, participants receive a welcome packet with membership information. Submit completed applications by fax to 240-556-0999, email to cnrorder@montgomerycountymd.gov, or mail to Call-n-Ride Program, 101 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850. To schedule trips, call a participating taxicab company dispatcher in advance and identify yourself as a CNR participant. Provide your name, CNR swipe card number, exact pick-up and destination addresses, and pick-up time. Get a confirmation number for your trip. Present your valid CNR swipe card to the driver at the beginning and end of the trip. Upon arrival at destination, verify the meter amount is accurate, provide a tip if desired (not to exceed 15% of fare), and sign the receipt provided by the driver. Keep receipts for six months.

structured_extraction.program_description: On-site dental services provided to students at select Montgomery County public schools during normal school hours. Offers preventive dental care including screenings, exams, cleanings, fluoride treatments, sealants, and restorative treatments at no cost to eligible students. Available at participating schools throughout Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free dental services provided on school premises during school hours at no cost to eligible students. Services include dental screenings and assessments, periodic dental examinations, x-rays, dental cleanings, fluoride applications and varnish, dental sealants, and restorative treatments including stainless steel crowns and fillings as needed. Silver Diamine Fluoride (SDF) treatment is also available to help stop tooth decay. Medicaid may help cover the cost of services; the Health Department will seek reimbursement for services if the child has dental coverage through Medicaid.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students attending select Montgomery County public schools. Parents and guardians of eligible students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Dental services including screenings, exams, x-rays, cleanings, fluoride treatments and varnish, sealants, restorative treatments (stainless steel crowns and fillings), and Silver Diamine Fluoride treatment provided at school locations during normal school hours.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Select Montgomery County public schools throughout the county.
requirements_list: Be a student at a select Montgomery County public school that participates in the program
Student enrollment at participating school
Parent or legal guardian must complete and sign informed consent forms
Parent or legal guardian must provide medical history information including allergies, current medications, and past medical conditions
Photo identification required for authorized persons picking up child at appointments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for the program by completing and submitting the School-Based Dental Program Registration Packet. The registration packet includes: (1) Dental Sealant Program Informed Consent and Medical History Form requesting child demographics, medical history, allergies, medications, and dental insurance information; (2) Dental Treatment Informed Consent for Minors form authorizing specific dental procedures and behavior management techniques; (3) Attestation of Parentage or Legal Guardianship form; (4) HIPAA Acknowledgement and Designation Disclosure form for privacy practices and communication preferences; and (5) Silver Diamine Fluoride consent form if SDF treatment is anticipated. Registration forms are available in English and Spanish. All forms must be completed by parent or legal guardian and returned to the child's school. Contact the Dental Kids program via email or phone for additional information or to request forms.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to non-profit organizations to establish, expand, and maintain school-based food assistance programs in partnership with Montgomery County Public Schools (MCPS). It supports projects that address critical gaps in healthy food access for children and families by co-locating food assistance services at MCPS school sites. Innovative approaches include food pantries, pre-packed meals and snack bags, grocery gift cards, and locally grown produce distribution. In FY26, $2.3 million was awarded to 13 organizations supporting 99+ MCPS school sites serving an estimated 50,000 students, with an additional $300,000 added to expand reach to over 80 sites — an increase of more than 30 percent over prior years.
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program awards grants to non-profit organizations to establish, expand, and maintain school-based food assistance programs in partnership with MCPS. Grant amounts range from a minimum of $40,000 to a maximum of $300,000, though final award amounts may be lower. FY25 had $1,250,000 in total funding available; FY26 provided $2.3 million with an additional $300,000 to expand reach. Grants support food pantries, pre-packed meals and snack bags, grocery gift cards, and locally grown produce distribution at school sites. Funds may be used for staffing costs, food purchases, infrastructure (refrigeration, storage, shelving), transportation, and operational costs. Indirect costs up to 15% are allowed (or applicant's federal Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement if applicable). Funds cannot be used for lobbying, expenses made prior to grant award, or to supplant other funding. The performance period for FY26 grants is approximately August 25, 2025 through June 30, 2026, requiring mid-cycle and end-of-cycle financial and programmatic reporting.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY26: Applications Closed 7/14/25; FY25: Deadline was Friday, July 26, 2024 at 12:00 PM
structured_extraction.contact_name: Heather Bruskin (FY26); Catherine Nardi (Program Manager, OFSR); Ali Hoy (Program Manager II, OGM)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and food assistance providers currently offering or seeking to offer school-based food assistance services in partnership with Montgomery County Public Schools. Organizations must have provided food assistance services over the past calendar year in at least one MCPS site. Programs serve students and families experiencing food insecurity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing, expanding, and maintaining school-based food assistance programs including food pantries, pre-packed meals, snack bags, grocery gift cards, and fresh produce distribution co-located at MCPS school sites. Funds may support staffing and fringe costs, food purchases (with recommended cost ranges provided), transportation, onsite infrastructure (refrigeration, storage, shelving), and operational costs including indirect costs. Programs may support new initiatives or expansion of existing programs at current or additional school sites.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Programs must be co-located at Montgomery County Public School sites. Organizations' principal place of business must be located in Montgomery County; if a national or regional organization, must have a location in Montgomery County. All activities and expenditures must occur in Montgomery County and exclusively benefit Montgomery County residents.
requirements_list: Organizations must be food assistance providers based in Montgomery County with documented experience providing services at MCPS sites over the past calendar year
Organizations must be registered and in Good Standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Principal place of business must be in Montgomery County; national/regional organizations must have a Montgomery County location
All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County exclusively for Montgomery County residents
Proposed projects must not exclude beneficiaries based on race, ethnicity, gender, or other protected class
Current Montgomery County contract/grant award winners must be current on all reporting obligations and demonstrate substantial progress
Organizations must partner with Montgomery County Public Schools
Programs must address food resource needs within the school community as identified by school personnel
Organizations must develop program models for successful services at school sites
Project must address food access gaps for families
Services must be co-located at eligible MCPS school sites
Lead applicants may only submit one application
Proposed expenses must be for new activities, expansion of existing activities, or a combination (not supplanting)
Organizations must demonstrate past experience with successful operation of school-based food assistance programs in partnership with MCPS
Organizations must describe a quickly actionable program model for services at new schools
Organizations must identify potential zip codes, capacity, resource needs, and format for expanded services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Montgomery County Online Grants Application Platform (SM Apply). For FY25, applications opened Wednesday, July 3, 2024 with an information session on Tuesday, July 9, 2024 at 12:00 PM, and deadline was Friday, July 26, 2024 at 12:00 PM. Applicants must provide organizational information (legal name, SDAT ID, Federal Tax ID, CVRS Vendor ID, mission statement, contact information), documentation (IRS tax-exempt letter, most recent 990 form, board list, audit report), project strategy with narrative describing service delivery and community engagement, detailed budget (preferably MS Excel), budget narrative/justification, staffing plan, work plan/timeline, and performance plan. An independent Review Committee of neutral, qualified individuals scores applications based on specified criteria and racial equity lens. Review Committee recommendations are submitted to County decision-makers. Award notifications are expected approximately one month after the deadline. Successful applicants are matched with specific MCPS schools based on alignment of school needs with provider programs, experience, and capacity. Grant agreements specify awarded amount, funding restrictions, programmatic and administrative requirements, reporting requirements, and payment terms. Grantees must submit mid-cycle (due 2/20/2026 for FY26, covering 08/25/2025-1/31/2026) and end-of-cycle (due 7/21/2026 for FY26, covering full 08/25/2025-06/30/2026 period) programmatic and financial reports with specific required metrics including participation data, service format details, food types offered, budget breakdown, in-kind resources, and narrative feedback on implementation, cultural proficiency, nutrition quality, and satisfaction survey incorporation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows eligible owner-occupied residential property taxpayers in Montgomery County to pay their real property taxes in two installments instead of one annual payment. The first half of taxes is due by September 30th, and the second half is due by December 31st.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible owner-occupied residential property owners can elect to pay real property taxes in two installments: one-half by September 30th and one-half by December 31st, instead of paying the full amount annually by September 30th. Taxpayers who escrow payments with their lender must notify the lender by May 1st if they want to pay annually instead. Personal property taxes, residential rental unit taxes, and commercial real property taxes are not eligible for this program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupied residential property owners in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real property tax payments for principal residence
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland - applies only to owner-occupied residential property where the owner's mailing address matches the premise address
requirements_list: Must own and live in a residential property as principal residence
Must have a mailing address that matches the property address
Cannot have residential rental property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program is automatically available to eligible taxpayers. Tax bills indicate semi-annual and optional full payment amounts. Taxpayers paying themselves can choose either payment option. Those escrowing taxes with a lender must notify the lender by May 1st if they want to pay annually; otherwise the lender will pay semi-annually.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Senior Assisted Living Subsidy Program (SALS) helps qualified seniors age 62 and older afford care in state-licensed and Montgomery County-licensed assisted living facilities by providing monthly subsidies toward the cost of care. The program is administered by Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services and is designed for seniors who require 24-hour supervision and meet income and asset eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a monthly subsidy to help pay for care in state-licensed and Montgomery County-licensed assisted living facilities that are enrolled as program participants. The maximum subsidy is currently $1,056.00 per month. The total monthly care rate for subsidy participants cannot exceed $3,300 per month. Subsidy amounts may be partial depending on the applicant's calculated monthly payment. The subsidy does not typically cover the full cost of care; applicants are responsible for paying the difference, which family, friends, or others may help cover or which may be negotiated directly with the facility.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors age 62 and older who are Maryland residents requiring 24-hour supervision, meet income and asset limits, and are seeking care in licensed assisted living facilities in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly assisted living facility care costs, including room, board, and personal care services at state-licensed and Montgomery County-licensed assisted living facilities enrolled in the program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents; program administered in Montgomery County. Assisted living facilities must be licensed by the state and Montgomery County and enrolled in the subsidy program.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be 62 years or older
Must require 24-hour supervision as documented by a nurse from the Department of Health and Human Services
Income must not exceed $4,350 per month for an individual (as of July 14, 2023)
Assets must not exceed $20,064 for an individual or $20,064 for a couple (as of July 14, 2023)
For couples, income is evaluated individually but combined assets cannot exceed $20,064
Assisted living facility must be licensed by the state and Montgomery County and enrolled in the subsidy program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Senior Assisted Living Subsidy program at 240-777-1138 to request an application. Submit the completed application along with photo ID and proof of income, assets, benefits, and medical expenses. A Department of Health and Human Services nurse will conduct an in-home assessment at no cost to determine if you meet eligibility requirements. Applications are date-stamped and placed on a waiting list to be processed on a first-come, first-served basis according to funding availability. The assisted living facility must be enrolled in the subsidy program.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Covers security deposit (up to double the monthly rental amount) and rental subsidy for up to 12 months. Supportive and financial services are also included. For tenants with income over $1000/month, the tenant pays 40% of their income toward rent and SHaRP pays the remainder directly to the landlord. For tenants with income below $1000/month, SHaRP pays the full rent for twelve months. Each tenant receives a Case Manager who provides ongoing support including income recertification to ensure affordability. Payments are made directly to landlords via check or ACH deposit. After 12 months, tenants exiting SHaRP are connected to the Rental Assistance Program and other available services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County program that provides financial assistance up to $125,000 and/or technical assistance to financially healthy small businesses located in identified geographic areas that are adversely impacted by a County-funded redevelopment project or a redevelopment project on County-owned property. The program was created by Montgomery County Council under Bill 6-12 in April 2012. The program operates through the Economic Development Fund and may award loans, grants, and technical assistance based on criteria and processes established in applicable regulations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial and/or technical assistance up to a maximum of $125,000 per business may be provided periodically over the duration of the County-related project. Businesses may receive multiple disbursements, with the total cumulative assistance not to exceed $125,000 throughout the entire project period. Assistance is awarded in the form of loans and/or grants through the Economic Development Fund, with specific award amounts, terms, and conditions determined through the award process and criteria established in Executive Regulation 24-12AM.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Financially healthy small businesses in Montgomery County located in identified geographic areas adversely impacted by a County-funded redevelopment project, a redevelopment project on County-owned property, or a County facility project.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To maintain small business viability during adversely impactful County-funded or County-related redevelopment projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Identified geographic areas in Montgomery County, Maryland affected by County-funded redevelopment projects, redevelopment projects on County-owned property, or County facility projects. Currently, the primary focus is on businesses affected by the Wheaton Revitalization Project.
requirements_list: Business must be financially healthy
Business must be located in an identified geographic area in Montgomery County
Business must be adversely impacted by a County-funded redevelopment project, a redevelopment project on County-owned property, or a County facility project

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Business Innovation Research and Small Business Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) Matching Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County provides matching grants to small businesses conducting research in biotechnology, medicine, or life sciences that have received federal SBIR (Small Business Innovation Research) or STTR (Small Business Technology Transfer) awards. The program offers three phases of funding to help companies advance their technologies toward commercialization: Phase 0 for technical assistance costs related to applying for a first SBIR/STTR award, Phase 1 for companies that have received their first federal award, and Phase 2 for companies advancing technologies toward commercialization. Companies must conduct at least 51 percent of their research and development operations in Montgomery County. The program is administered through the Montgomery County Economic Development Fund and establishes policies and procedures for administration of matching grants. Established in 2018, the program was updated to enable more young biotech companies to secure non-dilutive funding. This is the only County SBIR/STTR match program of its kind in the country.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Phase 0: Up to $5,000 reimbursement for qualified reimbursable expenses (technical assistance costs) related to applying for a first SBIR/STTR Phase 1 award. There is a limit of two (2) Phase 0 grants per company. The Phase 1 application must be submitted to the relevant federal department or agency for reimbursement. Phase 1: Up to $25,000 matching grant (25% of the federal award) to companies that have received no more than 2 prior Phase 1 awards and zero prior Phase 2 awards. Phase 2: Up to $50,000 matching grant (25% of the federal award) to companies that have received no more than 4 prior Phase 1 awards and no more than 1 prior Phase 2 award. For Phase 1 and Phase 2 grants, 50% of the matching grant amount must be used for reimbursement of technical assistance, investment assistance, or commercialization assistance expenses; the remaining 50% can be used for other business research related expenses. Funds cannot be used for expenditures already reimbursed by other federal, state, or county funding sources. All grants are subject to annual appropriation and availability of funds. Program funds are allocated with 20% for Phase 0 grants, 40% for Phase 1 grants, and 40% for Phase 2 grants, though funds may be reallocated based on applicant demand and director discretion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a first-come-first-served basis beginning February 15, 2023 at 9:00 a.m. EST. There are two application periods per calendar year commencing August 11 and February 15, though dates may change after adequate public notice due to applicant demand and/or director discretion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses in Montgomery County conducting research in biotechnology, medicine, or life sciences that have received or are preparing to apply for federal SBIR or STTR awards. Businesses must have a maximum of 20 employees at the time of application. For Phase 0: businesses preparing to apply for their first SBIR/STTR Phase 1 award. For Phase 1: businesses that have received a maximum of 2 prior Phase 1 awards and zero prior Phase 2 awards. For Phase 2: businesses that have received a maximum of 4 prior Phase 1 awards and 1 prior Phase 2 award.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Phase 0: Reimbursement of qualified reimbursable expenses (technical assistance costs) associated with completing and filing a SBIR/STTR Phase 1 or Fast Track grant application. Phase 1 and Phase 2: 50% of the matching grant must be used for reimbursement of technical assistance, investment assistance, or commercialization assistance expenses; remaining 50% for other business research related expenses that advance the technology toward commercialization through the SBIR/STTR research project. Funds must relate to the SBIR/STTR grant awarded and cannot reimburse expenditures covered by other federal, state, or county funding sources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Businesses must conduct at least 51 percent of their research and development operations in Montgomery County. Awardees must continue to conduct at least 51% of research and development operations within Montgomery County for a minimum of two years from the date of disbursement of the County's conditional matching grant.
requirements_list: Business must be located in Montgomery County
Business must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Research must be in biotechnology, medicine, or life sciences
At least 51 percent of research and development must be conducted in Montgomery County
Business must have a maximum of 20 employees at the time of application

Phase 0: Business must have been in operation for five years or less, must have received no prior SBIR/STTR awards, must have qualified reimbursable expenses related to a submitted SBIR/STTR Phase 1 proposal, must have retained technical assistance after December 27, 2022, and there is a limit of two Phase 0 grants per company

Phase 1: Business must have been in operation for five years or less, must have received a maximum of 2 prior Phase 1 awards and zero prior Phase 2 awards, and must have been awarded an SBIR/STTR Phase 1 grant in the current calendar year

Phase 2: Business must have been in operation for seven years or less, must have received a maximum of 4 prior Phase 1 awards and 1 prior Phase 2 award, and must have been awarded an SBIR/STTR Phase 2 grant in the current calendar year
Company must have been awarded an SBIR or STTR Phase 1 or Phase 2 grant from the federal government
Phase 0 applicants must submit an SBIR/STTR Phase 1 application to the relevant federal department or agency to be reimbursed for qualified reimbursable expenses

All conditional grants are subject to formal written agreement with performance conditions including continued 51% county-based research operations for minimum two years and annual reporting requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be complete and submitted online via the County's Business Portal (SBIR/STTR Matching Grant Application at montgomerycountymd.gov). Applications will be automatically date and time stamped in order of submission and awards made to qualified applicants on a first-come-first-served basis. There are two application periods per calendar year commencing August 11 and February 15. Phase 0 applicants must submit documentation of retaining technical assistance after December 27, 2022, evidence of subsequent SBIR/STTR Phase 1 application submission to a federal agency, and related expenses through the application portal. Phase 1 and Phase 2 applicants must submit applications after receiving notification of their federal SBIR/STTR award through the application portal. Phase 0 and SBIR/STTR Phase 1 or Phase 2 matching grant awardees will receive a formal letter offering county funds as a conditional grant with specified performance conditions. Awardees must provide a proposed budget for how they plan to use County matching grant funds in relation to their SBIR/STTR grant, continue conducting at least 51% of research and development operations within Montgomery County for a minimum of two years from disbursement, and submit annual certified reports containing: expenditures of County matching grant funds, proof of county occupancy (lease payment or property tax bill), copies of progress reports required by SBIR/STTR grantor, and high-level company summary including leadership, contact info, employee count at grant application and report dates, funding history, and research progress. For additional information or to apply, contact Derese Bikila at Derese.Bikila@montgomerycountymd.gov or BusinessCenter@montgomerycountymd.gov, or visit the Montgomery County Business Portal.

structured_extraction.program_name: Standard PILOT (Payment in Lieu of Taxes)
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax abatement program that lowers or eliminates Montgomery County real property taxes on rental housing projects for a period of years in exchange for the property owner's commitment to provide affordable housing units to low-income residents. The tax abatement amount is based on the number of affordable rental units and is equal to the average County homeowner tax credit adjusted annually.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County's real property tax abatement is usually based on each affordable rental unit in the rental project. The tax abatement equals the average County homeowner tax credit adjusted annually. The term of the PILOT is tied to the affordability period desired by Montgomery County. The abatement is administered under a Regulatory Agreement signed by the property owner and the County and recorded in the land records. Standard PILOTs are not transferable. Property owners must still pay all State real property taxes, municipal taxes, front foot benefit charges, and other applicable fees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers of rental housing projects in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To support the construction and preservation of affordable multifamily rental housing through property tax abatement
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rental housing projects located in Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Legal description of the property
Project financial pro forma including evidence of financial commitments for total project costs and financial need for the PILOT
Project description including total number of units and number of affordable units with documentation demonstrating affordability (such as rent rolls or LIHTC Covenants)
Demonstrate site control equivalent to fee simple title, 99-year lease, or option to purchase with no contingencies except financing
Any other information or documentation reasonably required by the County to determine eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit required information electronically to DHCA.Multifamily@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov or by mail to Department of Housing and Community Affairs, 1401 Rockville Pike, 4th Floor, Attn: PILOT Request, Rockville, MD 20852. A request for a PILOT is analyzed to define the level of PILOT required using financial information from the property owner.

They work 200-350 hours depending on grade level (9th grade: 350 hours, 10th grade: 300 hours, 11th-12th grade: 200 hours). Employees complete three coaching sessions, attend 30 hours of workforce development training, develop and implement a capstone project, and earn a certificate of completion and letter of reference. Work schedules are flexible and can include weekdays, evenings, and weekends. Host sites provide structured work opportunities, onsite training and coaching, supervision, mentorship, and practical experiences to develop job-related skills.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Government offers tuition assistance funds to employees with merit system status on a first-come, first-served basis. The program provides financial support for employee education and training, with funding available each fiscal year beginning July 1st. Funding levels and eligibility vary by employee bargaining unit (FOP, IAFF, MCGEO, UNREP, MCVFRA), and reimbursements can be sent via electronic payment or paper check. The program also extends to active volunteers in fire and rescue services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employees and eligible volunteers receive tuition assistance funds on a first-come, first-served basis until annual funding is obligated. For FOP employees: maximum $1,730 (full-time) or $865 (part-time) per fiscal year; covers tuition and direct/compulsory costs (lab fees, registration, library services, technology fees). For IAFF employees: maximum $1,830 (full-time) or $915 (part-time); covers tuition and direct/compulsory costs. For MCGEO and UNREP employees: maximum $2,300 (full-time) or $1,150 (part-time); covers tuition only. For eligible volunteers: maximum $1,830 per fiscal year; covers tuition only. Funding levels vary by bargaining unit. Does not cover books, supplies, application fees, late registration, parking, travel, food, lodging, audit courses, credit by examination, exam fees, or courses outside the USA. Reimbursements can be sent via electronic payment (ACH) or paper check. Applicants may submit applications online through MCG ePortal with their MCG Computer Network login, or paper applications for those without email access.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY26 Program Application opens Wednesday, July 1, 2025 at 9 am. First-come, first-served until funding is obligated. All FY26 approved applications and required documents must be submitted to OHR by June 18, 2026 for payment processing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County Government employees with merit system status, employees of the State's Attorney's Office (excluding the State's Attorney), and active Montgomery County fire and rescue volunteers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and direct/compulsory training costs (such as laboratory fees, registration fees, library services, technology fees for some bargaining units) for employee education and professional development, including certificates, associate degrees, baccalaureate degrees, graduate degrees, credit courses, non-credit courses, and seminars. Training must be directly related to the employee's current job functions or career ladder in the same job series or profession, or prepare the employee to make a career change within the County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County Government employees and active Montgomery County fire and rescue volunteers only. Courses must be taken at accredited institutions as recognized by the United States Department of Education or Higher Education Accreditation Commission.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County Government employee with merit system status (or probationary employee approved for reimbursement upon merit status achievement)
Employees of the State's Attorney's Office (excluding the State's Attorney) are eligible
Active volunteers must appear on the most recent certified list of active volunteers and be qualified under the point system in Montgomery County Code Section 21-21

Training must be directly related to either: (a) the employee's current County job functions or career ladder in the same job series or profession, or (b) a field of study that will prepare the employee to make a career change within the County
Application submitted on first-come, first-served basis until annual funding is obligated
Funding varies by bargaining unit (FOP: $1,730 FT/$865 PT; IAFF: $1,830 FT/$915 PT; MCGEO: $2,300 FT/$1,150 PT; UNREP: $2,300 FT/$1,150 PT; Volunteers: $1,830)
Course must be taken at an accredited college, university, or institution recognized by the United States Department of Education or Higher Education Accreditation Commission
Courses must be taken during off-duty hours or on approved leave (not administrative leave or Professional Improvement Leave)
Course start date must be within the current fiscal year (July 1 through June 30)
Employee must complete course with passing grade or obtain course completion certificate
Employee must remain employed by the County for one to two years after course completion (depending on bargaining unit or personnel policy), or reimburse the County a prorated amount
For probationary employees: employee must pay tuition upfront and receive reimbursement only after achieving merit system status and providing evidence of successful course completion
Department director approval required prior to OHR submission
All required documents must be submitted within the fiscal year
Final grade or certificate of completion must be submitted to OHR upon completion of course
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Employee discusses educational goals with immediate supervisor. 2. Employee identifies degree program, course, or workshop and obtains course description including contact hours, cost, dates, and credits. 3. Employee completes online application form at https://ex02.montgomerycountymd.gov/ojn4/ijn36/ohr/ using Montgomery County username and password (available July 1 through June 30 each fiscal year), or submits paper application if without email access. 4. For MCGEO and UNREP employees: supervisor reviews and approves application online. 5. Employee receives approval notification email and uploads required documents (course description, itemized bill, grade reports from previous courses if applicable, leave request if needed, receipt if seeking reimbursement). 6. Department director reviews and approves submitted application and supporting documents online. 7. Application is forwarded to OHR (MCGEO and UNREP) or OHR reviews and makes recommendation. 8. If approved, OHR sends authorization letter (voucher letter) to employee addressed to the educational institution. 9. Employee submits voucher letter to educational institution. 10. County receives bill/invoice from institution and processes payment directly to vendor, or if employee paid upfront, payment is processed directly to employee via ACH or check. 11. Employee must submit final grades or certificate of completion to OHR upon course completion. Processing time is typically 7-14 days. All FY26 approved applications and documents must be submitted to OHR by June 18, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for residential properties used for urban agriculture. Property owners receive a credit equal to 80% of their Montgomery County property tax. The credit is available for up to 10 years (two 5-year periods with renewal option) if the property meets all eligibility requirements.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The tax credit equals 80% of the County property tax on the eligible property. The credit is available for a 5-year period (two tax years under the amended law) and may be renewed for another 5 years, for a maximum of 10 years total. The credit appears as a line item deduction on a revised property tax bill issued after the initial July bill. Property owners must reapply each year by April 1 and must have more than $5,000 in gross income from agricultural products each year to maintain the credit. Gross income includes revenue from the sale of products grown or raised on the property, as well as the fair market value of food products donated to a registered charitable organization.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1 annually, before the tax year that begins July 1 of the same calendar year. For 2017 taxes only, applications were accepted until September 1, 2017. Renewal applications must be filed no later than 90 days before the expiration of the current credit term.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Montgomery County who operate urban agricultural businesses on residential properties zoned for residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit reduces property tax liability for eligible urban agricultural properties. Funds cannot be directed to specific uses; the credit is applied against property taxes owed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within 1,000 feet of one of ten designated Metro Station Policy Areas: Bethesda Central Business District, Friendship Heights, Glenmont, Grosvenor, Rockville Town Center, Shady Grove, Silver Spring Central Business District, Twinbrook, Wheaton Central Business District, or White Flint.
requirements_list: Property must be between ½ acre and 1 acre in size
Property must be zoned residential (multiple contiguous parcels owned by the same person may be combined)
Property must be used solely for urban agricultural purposes, except an individual may also reside on the property

Owner must receive more than $5,000 in gross income annually from sale of products grown or raised on the property (or by donating more than $5,000 of agricultural products to a registered charitable organization)
Property must be within 1,000 feet of a Metro Station Policy Area
Urban Agricultural Purposes are limited to: cultivation of fruits, vegetables, flowers and ornamental plants; limited keeping and raising of fowl or bees; or practice of aquaculture
Property owner must file a timely application for the credit with proof of eligibility
Property must maintain continuous agricultural use throughout the credit term or the credit will be terminated and back taxes will be owed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners must complete the Urban Agricultural Property Tax Credit Application each year and submit it to the Montgomery County Office of Agriculture by April 1 before the tax year beginning July 1. Applications can be submitted online through SeamlessDocs or as a paper version mailed to the Office of Agriculture address listed on the application. A paper version is also available at the Department of Finance, Division of Treasury, 27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, Maryland 20850. The Director of Finance determines taxpayer eligibility for the credit based upon the recommendation from the Office of Agriculture. To renew the credit for another term, property owners must file a renewal application no later than 90 days before the expiration of the current credit. If a property is no longer used for agricultural purposes during the credit term, the credit must be terminated and the owner is liable for all property taxes that would have been due if the credit had not been granted for any year the property was not used for agricultural purposes. Taxpayers may appeal a final decision by the Director denying or terminating the credit to the Maryland Tax Court within 30 days after receiving notice of denial or termination.

The program aims to create approximately 8,600 new housing units and business space around metro stations, supporting transit-oriented development. Qualifying projects must include at least 50 percent rental housing and meet affordable housing requirements under Chapter 25A of the County Code.

The project must provide at least 25 percent of the MPDUs required under County law at affordability levels for households with income no greater than 50 percent of AMI. structured_extraction.program_name: Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) Stormwater Management Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A charge reduction program administered by Montgomery County that provides credits of up to 60% or 80% off the annual Water Quality Protection Charge (a stormwater fee) for property owners—including residential, multi-family, non-residential, and nonprofit organizations—who install and maintain stormwater management practices on their property, such as rain gardens, permeable pavement, green roofs, rain barrels, dry wells, grass swales, and stormwater ponds. Additional credits are available for offsite stormwater treatment. Hardship reductions and successful charge appeals may also qualify a property owner for a reduction. Credits must be renewed every 3 years. The program applies to all property types subject to the WQPC in Montgomery County, Maryland.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners receive a credit (reduction) on their annual Water Quality Protection Charge based on stormwater management practices installed and maintained on their property. For Single-Family Residential (SFR) properties, the credit can reduce the WQPC by up to 80% based on the volume of water captured compared to the Environmental Site Design Volume (ESDv) requirement. Credits are calculated using the formula: SFR WQPC Percent Credit = (Total Volume Captured / Environmental Site Design Volume) × 80%. For Non-Residential/Multi-Family Residential (NR/MFR) properties, credits of up to 60% or 80% are available depending on the stormwater treatment approach. The credit is calculated based on the sum of the volume of stormwater treatment provided by each stormwater management system practice at the site. Additional credits are available for offsite stormwater treatment. Hardship reductions and charge appeals are also available. The credit must be renewed every 3 years. Eligible stormwater management practices include: rain barrels and cisterns, rain gardens, permeable pavement, stormwater ponds, conservation landscaping, dry wells, green roofs, grass swales, swales, roof leader disconnection to pervious areas, non-roof area disconnection to pervious areas, micro-infiltration, micro-bioretention, and sheet flow to conservation areas. The volume of water captured is determined based on specific design information and calculations outlined in the WQPC Credit Procedures Manual.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications, submissions, and requests are due September 30
structured_extraction.program_audience: All property owners in Montgomery County subject to the Water Quality Protection Charge, including homeowners, multi-family residential property owners (where one or more dwelling units share a common entrance and are arranged in the same building), non-residential property owners (commercial, industrial, hotels, retail establishments), homeowner associations, non-profit entities, healthcare facilities, and government-owned properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit reduces the annual Water Quality Protection Charge (stormwater fee) only. It cannot be used for any other purpose. Eligible stormwater management practices include rain barrels and cisterns, rain gardens, permeable pavement, stormwater ponds, conservation landscaping, dry wells, green roofs, grass swales, swales, roof leader disconnection to pervious areas, non-roof area disconnection to pervious areas, micro-infiltration, micro-bioretention, and sheet flow to conservation areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Applies to all property types subject to the WQPC, including residential, multi-family residential, commercial, industrial, and government-owned properties.

Stormwater management practices must be maintained in accordance with Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection maintenance requirements

Engineer-certified plans must include: Total Impervious Area (buildings, parking lots, walkways, driveways, sheds), Year of Installation, Facility Size and Units, and Impervious Area Treated by the Stormwater Management System
Photograph of the stormwater management system must be included with the application

Owner Name as it appears on property tax bill
Property Address, City, State, and Zip Code
Mailing Address if different from property address
Telephone Number and Email address for contact
Applicants must specify if application is new or renewal
Credits must be renewed every 3 years

Privately installed practices may be required to submit specific information relating to their design for the County to establish credit amount

All residential practices must be maintained in accordance with maintenance requirements of Section 19-28 of the Montgomery County Code, unless facilities are part of a County-approved stormwater management participation project
For SFR properties: applicants must complete the Inspections and Maintenance Checklist confirming practices are functioning in accordance with maintenance requirements

For NR/MFR properties: applicants can directly input the design volume into the NR/MFR Credit Calculator if design plans are available; if no design data available, the calculator automatically calculates an Assumed Treatment Volume based on the practice's design era and contributing drainage area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners must submit a credit application through the WQPC forms portal by September 30 each year. Step 1: Select your property type (Residential & Agricultural, Multi-Family & Non-Residential, or Nonprofit Organizations) and access the appropriate application form. Step 2: The SFR credit application prepopulates initial application information including parcel area, impervious area, and other WQPC information once a property tax account is selected. When practices are permitted through the County, the application will pre-populate the list of practices on the property. Step 3: Complete the Inspections and Maintenance Checklist, answering questions on the maintenance performed on each stormwater facility. By completing the self-inspection form for each facility, property owners confirm the practices are functioning in accordance with Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection maintenance requirements. Step 4: Complete contact information and specify whether you are the owner or the owner's agent completing the application. Step 5: For SFR properties, proceed to the SFR Credit Calculator form and input the size and/or number of stormwater management systems on your property along with any date information. The calculator will compute a volume of water treated based on assumptions typical for each practice. Step 6: For NR/MFR properties, applicants can directly input the design volume into the NR/MFR Credit Calculator if design plans are available; if no design data are available, the calculator will automatically calculate an Assumed Treatment Volume based on the practice's design era and contributing drainage area. Step 7: Once completed, the Credit Calculator accumulates the volume treated by all practices on the site and prorates the WQPC credit up to 80% (or 60%-80% for NR/MFR). For condominiums, only one application is needed if the stormwater practice applies to all property owners, but a list of qualified tax accounts must be included. Applications can be submitted at https://ex11.montgomerycountymd.gov/extranetportal/water-quality-protection-charge. For questions or to create a service request, contact MC311 by calling 311 (in County), 240-777-0311, or 711 for MD Relay TTY. Email questions to AskDEP@montgomerycountymd.gov or visit montgomerycountymd.gov/stormwater.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to make homeownership and rental housing affordable to households with incomes at or below 120% of the area-wide median income. The program promotes housing construction affordable to moderate-income workers and public employees, increases housing choices, reduces commute distances, and helps employers address labor shortages.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides affordable housing through new construction and resale of homes to eligible households. Homes are sold at controlled prices established by DHCA and are subject to a 20-year Control Period with restrictive covenants. Owners must occupy the home as their primary residence and cannot rent it out during the Control Period without prior consent from DHCA. The controlled resale price is established by DHCA. Owners must contact DHCA to obtain a maximum resale price and receive further instructions prior to refinancing or selling. Upon sale after the Control Period expires, owners must pay half of the excess proceeds above the controlled price to the County's Housing Initiative Fund.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Households with incomes at or below 120% of the area-wide median income, including public employees and other workers whose incomes cannot support high housing costs near their workplace, and County employers seeking to address labor shortages.

Must occupy the home as primary residence during the 20-year Control Period
Cannot rent out the home during the Control Period without prior consent from DHCA
If relocating during Control Period, must sell to another WFH-eligible household
Cannot refinance for more than the DHCA-controlled resale price during Control Period
Refinancing must not reduce owner equity below $10,000 during Control Period
Upon sale after Control Period, must pay half of excess proceeds above controlled price to County Housing Initiative Fund
Must submit annual re-certification under penalty of perjury that the WFH Unit is owner's primary residence

Inducement resolution fee of 15 basis points (.15%) and commitment fee of 25 basis points (.25%) are credited toward the final financing fee. structured_extraction.program_audience: Private for-profit and not-for-profit developers and owners developing multifamily rental housing projects serving low- and moderate-income residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction and permanent financing for new construction, substantial rehabilitation, adaptive reuse of non-residential buildings, and preservation of existing multifamily rental housing units with at least 5 dwelling units. Developments must serve residents at 50% AMI (20% of units) or 60% AMI (40% of units) with rents not exceeding 30% of residents' adjusted gross income.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, including urban, suburban, and rural areas. Priority given to projects in: Inner Beltway Communities (older communities inside the beltway where acquisition/rehab projects are needed), Regional Transit Districts (within ½ mile of Metro stops at Largo Town Center, New Carrollton, Prince George's Plaza, Branch Avenue, and Suitland), Opportunity Zones (census tracts designated as Opportunity Zones), and Designated Development Areas (areas designated by County for future development such as Westphalia).
requirements_list: Complete CDA Form 202 application
Resumes and experience of key development partners (Sponsor, General Contractor, Architect, Property Manager)
Site location map showing proximity to schools, public transportation, shopping, and neighborhood amenities
Market data showing comparable rental developments including rent levels, amenities, vacancy rates
Evidence of applicable zoning or zoning approval actions
Title report disclosing all liens, easements, and encumbrances
Evidence of utility availability
Evidence of site control extending at least 6 months after application
Form of credit enhancement or private placement contemplated
Site, building, and unit plans
MAI appraisal performed within 6 months preceding application
Personal financial statements for principals of ownership entity
Non-refundable application fee of $5,000
Updated financial proforma at commitment stage
Appraisal not dated more than 6 months from submission; independent market study may be required
Credit reports for all principals
Phase I environmental report
Letters of commitment for any secondary or soft debt
Updated title report and survey
Demonstration of good faith efforts to use minority and women-owned businesses and meet Section 3 requirements
Financial statements for previous 3 years plus interim statements; balance sheets for previous 3 years plus current quarter
Partnership or corporate tax returns for past 2 years with all schedules
Schedule of income-producing real estate owned by each principal with vacancy rates and outstanding mortgage balances
Certification regarding involvement with defaulted loans, workouts, foreclosures, tax liens, or bankruptcy in past 5 years
General Contractor description of experience with similar projects in past 5 years with staff resumes
General Contractor audited financial statements and evidence of insurance and bonding capacity
Architect description of experience with similar projects in past 5 years with staff resumes
Detailed property management plan including lease-up, operations, maintenance, staffing, resident services, rent collection, income verification, and marketing with fair housing compliance
Property management contract and experience managing similar properties
Evidence of zoning compliance or planned compliance actions before closing
Evidence of utility availability or planned availability
Relocation plan if temporary or permanent relocation anticipated
Project plans and specifications at least 80% complete at commitment; final plans, specifications, and cost estimates before closing
Commitment from credit enhancement provider achieving AA or higher rating
Organizational documents and evidence of good standing
Minimum project size of 5 units in garden, mid-rise, high-rise, or scattered site configuration
Projects must meet public purpose: 20% of units at 50% AMI or 40% of units at 60% AMI with rents not exceeding 30% of adjusted income
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit complete CDA Form 202 application with required documentation including resumes, market analysis, title reports, appraisals, and $5,000 non-refundable application fee. 2. Credit Underwriting team reviews and underwrites the application to assess economic feasibility, creditworthiness, partner credentials, and site desirability. 3. Underwriting team submits Credit Memo to HAPGC Credit Committee with recommendations. 4. Credit Committee approves or declines and submits recommendations to Development and Finance Sub-Committee of HAPGC Board. 5. If approved, Sub-Committee directs staff to prepare Inducement Resolution for full HAPGC Board (allows recoupment of certain development costs at closing). 6. Upon Board approval of Inducement Resolution, staff prepares Resolution for Prince George's County Council approval and prepares for TEFRA public hearing. 7. Following Inducement Resolution passage, submit additional loan commitment documents including updated financial proforma, credit reports, environmental reports, updated appraisals, management plans, and evidence of credit enhancement. 8. Upon review and approval, Executive Director issues Commitment Letter detailing financing terms and requirements. 9. Prepare for bond closing: prepare Official Statement (public offering) or Private Placement Memorandum. 10. Execute mortgage loan closing documents and Regulatory Agreement and Land Use Agreement (recorded in county land records, typically 30-year term). 11. During construction/rehabilitation, submit monthly status reports and income certifications; upon completion, submit cost certification and occupancy documentation. 12. Ongoing annual audited financial statements and compliance reporting required.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for owners of agricultural land who participate in Maryland or County agricultural land preservation programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit equal to the full amount of County taxes owed on agricultural land enrolled in an agricultural land preservation program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of agricultural land participating in Maryland or County agricultural land preservation programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit against County taxes owed
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County
requirements_list: Property must be enrolled in Maryland agricultural land preservation program or County agricultural land preservation program
Annual application and proof of claim must be filed with the Director of Finance
Applicant must own the property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must file an annual application and proof of claim with the Director of Finance. The application must demonstrate that the property is enrolled in an approved agricultural land preservation program.

structured_extraction.program_description: An elective partnership program between Prince George's County and qualified tax-exempt faith-based organizations or other 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations designed to improve water quality by treating and reducing polluted stormwater runoff. Participating organizations may qualify for a reduction in a portion of their Clean Water Act Fee based on their participation in one or more stormwater management activities. Three options are available, each providing a different level of fee reduction in exchange for specific stormwater-related commitments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified organizations receive a reduction in their Clean Water Act Fee based on selected program options: Option 1 provides a 50% fee reduction for granting an easement to the County to install stormwater best management practices on the property; Option 2 provides a 25% fee reduction for participating in education and outreach campaigns; Option 3 provides a 25% fee reduction for using certified lawn care companies and implementing good housekeeping practices. Organizations may select one or all three options. An annual administrative fee of $20.58 per tax account still applies and cannot be waived.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tax-exempt faith-based organizations and 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations located in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fee reductions are applied toward reducing the organization's Clean Water Act Fee in exchange for implementing stormwater management practices to treat and reduce polluted stormwater runoff and improve water quality.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a tax-exempt faith-based organization or 501(c)(3) nonprofit
Must own property in Prince George's County
Must select and agree to implement one or more of three options: easement provision, outreach and education activities, or green care and good housekeeping practices
Organizations selecting Option 1 must sign a Maintenance Agreement and continuously maintain installed stormwater practices, subject to triennial inspection
Organizations selecting Option 3 must use lawn and landscaping companies certified by the Maryland Department of Agriculture
Organizations selecting Option 1 must grant the County an easement to install and maintain stormwater best management practices on the property
Organizations selecting Option 2 must participate in County education and outreach campaigns related to stormwater management
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Select program option(s) and complete the Alternative Compliance Application Form with digital signature, then mail to the Stormwater Management Division. Step 2: Meet with County agent to develop an alternative compliance plan and confirm feasibility of selected options. Step 3: Submit the written alternative compliance plan and CWAF Reduction Request Form to the Department of the Environment for review and decision on the amount of fee credit to be applied. Step 4: Upon approval, the fee reduction is applied to the organization's Clean Water Act Account.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for owners of residential structures that utilize solar energy or geothermal energy devices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit for residential structures utilizing solar energy or geothermal energy devices. The credit is applied against the property tax bill for homes that have installed qualified solar or geothermal energy systems. Specific credit amounts and calculation methods are determined by the county assessor based on the system specifications and installation date.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; applications accepted throughout the year
structured_extraction.contact_name: Director of Finance, Prince George's County Department of Finance
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential homeowners in Prince George's County with solar or geothermal energy systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit for homes utilizing solar energy or geothermal energy devices
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County
requirements_list: Must own residential property located in Prince George's County
Property must have installed and be utilizing solar energy or geothermal energy devices
Solar or geothermal system must meet county specifications and standards
Application and proof of claim (including documentation of system installation) must be filed with the Director of Finance
Property owner must be current on property tax payments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Homeowners must submit an application along with proof of installation of a qualified solar or geothermal energy system to the Director of Finance. Documentation should include details about the system type, installation date, and system specifications. The Director of Finance will review the claim and apply the appropriate tax credit to the property tax assessment.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free native trees and shrubs for schools to plant and maintain on school grounds. The program educates students about the importance of native trees, empowers them to enhance their community, and provides funds for tree planting projects in schoolyards. It supports both the planning and post-planting maintenance of native trees and shrubs on school campuses in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program is free to participating schools and provides free native trees and shrubs along with funds for planting projects on school grounds. DoE provides assistance with selecting tree planting locations on the school campus, developing a tree planting plan, and post-planting maintenance schedule. Trees must be planted during spring or fall to ensure survival, not during summer. Project organizers must commit to a two-year maintenance plan following tree planting, including watering trees every 7 days during dry periods, weeding and mulching up to two times per year, and pruning.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Schools and educational institutions in Prince George's County interested in planting native trees and shrubs on school grounds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting and maintaining native trees and shrubs on school grounds and schoolyards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County schools only.
requirements_list: Submit Intent to Apply Form
Schedule consultation with Program Coordinator
Submit Program Application
Develop tree planting plan for campus
Create post-planting maintenance plan for 2 years following planting
Trees must be planted during spring or fall, not summer
Projects must be located in school yards
Project must be approved by school principal and facility manager
Project organizer must commit to two-year maintenance plan
Request marking of utility lines by MISS Utility
Complete PGCPS Request for Building Alterations and Improvements form
Identify and avoid conflicts with other campus projects and Clean Water Partnership projects
Maintenance tasks include watering trees every 7 days during dry periods, weeding and mulching up to two times per year, and pruning
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools submit a completed Intent to Apply Form to the Department of the Environment, Sustainable Initiatives Division, 1801 McCormick Drive, Suite 500, Largo, Maryland 20774, ATTN: Carole Barth. The Program Coordinator will contact the school to schedule a required consultation. During the consultation, information is provided on completing the Program Application, developing a tree planting plan for the school campus, and creating a post-planting maintenance plan. Schools then submit the completed Program Application. Projects must be approved by both the school principal and facility manager.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps customers manage large past-due electric and gas bills by providing grants to retire outstanding balances. Eligible customers can receive up to $2,000 towards their past-due bill.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $2,000 towards past-due electric and gas bills. Customers must have a past-due bill of $300 or greater to be considered eligible. Customers may only receive an arrearage grant once every five years, with certain exceptions. Arrearage grants received between January 1, 2020, and December 31, 2021, will not count towards the five-year limitation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: You can apply at any time during the year, but you can only receive benefits once each year and must reapply each fiscal year (July-June).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households with large past-due electric and gas bills.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance can be used to pay past-due electric and gas bills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Income-based eligibility
Must have a past-due bill of $300 or greater
Can only receive an arrearage grant once every five years with certain exceptions
Arrearage grants received between January 1, 2020, and December 31, 2021, will not count towards the five-year limitation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply online at https://dhs.maryland.gov/office-of-home-energy-programs/ (available 24/7), by email to pgcdss.energy@maryland.gov with completed application and supporting documentation, by mail to Prince George's County Department of Social Services at 805 Brightseat Road Landover MD 20785, or by fax to 301-909-6331. In-person assistance is available at 425 Brightseat Road Landover MD 20785.

structured_extraction.program_name: BGE Electric Vehicle Charging Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A rebate and incentive program that helps residents and multifamily property owners offset the cost of adopting electric vehicles and installing electric vehicle charging stations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residential customers can receive rebates and incentives up to $300 for adopting an electric vehicle and installing a charger. Property managers, owners, and homeowners associations may be eligible to receive incentives up to $25,000 for installing Level 2 smart chargers or DC fast chargers on their properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: BGE customers who are interested in adopting electric vehicles or installing charging infrastructure at residential or multifamily properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of electric vehicles and Level 2 smart chargers or DC fast chargers for electric vehicle charging stations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service area of BGE, with focus on Prince George's County through the partnership with the County's Sustainable Energy program.
requirements_list: Must be a BGE customer
For residential: installing eligible charger or adopting an EV
For multifamily: property must qualify for installation of Level 2 smart chargers or DC fast chargers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the BGE resource page to receive information on rebates, incentives, general EV information, and guidance on finding and comparing available EVs and charger stations.

structured_extraction.program_description: The BRAC Zone program is a state program that provides financial assistance to local governments in areas designated for growth resulting from the Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) 2005 military base reorganization. The program focuses residential population growth in well-defined zones, aligns state resources to support local governments and businesses, and helps coordinate financing for public infrastructure improvements in these designated areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local jurisdictions in designated BRAC Zones receive payment of 100% of state real property tax increment on qualified properties and payment equal to 50% of the local jurisdiction's real property tax increment on qualified properties. These funds can be used to pay back bonds, including Tax Increment Financing bonds, issued for infrastructure improvements. Benefits are available for 10 years from the time the first project in the zone is designated as a qualified property. Projects can also receive priority consideration for financing assistance from various state agencies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and businesses located in designated BRAC Zones, as well as qualified properties within those zones.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure improvements and repayment of bonds, including Tax Increment Financing bonds, issued for infrastructure improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County areas designated as BRAC Zones following the 2005 Base Realignment and Closure process.
requirements_list: Located in a designated BRAC Zone
Property must be designated as a qualified BRAC Zone property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 to speak with a Business Development Specialist for more information about the application process and eligibility details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax exemption for real property owned by a Boys and Girls Club chartered by the Prince George's County Boys and Girls Club, Incorporated.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An annual property tax exemption is granted for real property owned by the Boys and Girls Club upon submission of an annual application and proof of claim. The property must be used for the organization's charitable or educational purposes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before October 1 of the tax year exemption is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Boys and Girls Club chartered by Prince George's County Boys and Girls Club, Incorporated.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The exemption applies to real property owned by the qualifying Boys and Girls Club that is used for charitable, educational, or recreational purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Real property must be owned by a Boys and Girls Club chartered by the Prince George's County Boys and Girls Club, Incorporated
Property must be used exclusively for the organization's exempt purposes
Annual application and proof of claim must be filed with the Director of Finance
Application must be filed on or before October 1 of the tax year for which the exemption is sought
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File an annual application and proof of claim with the Director of Finance on or before October 1 of the tax year for which the exemption is sought. Applications should include documentation demonstrating ownership of the property by the eligible Boys and Girls Club and evidence that the property is being used for exempt purposes.

structured_extraction.program_description: Call-A-Cab is a transportation assistance program that provides mobility at a reduced cost for County seniors age 60 and older and persons with disabilities. Eligible residents purchase coupon books that can be used to pay for rides with participating taxi companies when public transit options like Metrobus, Metrorail, and Call-A-Bus are not available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible residents can purchase up to fourteen $20 coupon books in a six-month period at $10 per book, providing a 50% discount on the face value of each coupon book. Coupons can be used in combination with cash to pay for rides with participating taxi companies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents age 60 and older and persons with disabilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for taxi rides with participating cab companies
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or older or a person with a disability
Must be a Prince George's County resident
Must provide proof of age and/or disability (acceptable forms include driver's license, Metro Senior Card, Metro Disability Card, or MetroAccess card)
May purchase up to fourteen $20 coupon books per six-month period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply online at the provided website or submit a printable application form by mail. To order coupon books, complete the application form, enclose a check or money order payable to Prince George's County ($10 per $20 coupon book), and mail to The Office of Transportation, 9400 Peppercorn Place, Suite 320, Largo, MD 20774. Include proof of age and/or disability with the application. Once received, use coupons by calling a participating taxi company, showing the coupon book to the driver, and paying with any combination of coupons and cash.
