Services include well and sick-child care visits, physical and eye exams, laboratory and X-ray services, immunizations, outpatient mental health and chemical dependency services, short-term physical therapy for children 10 years and older, and discounted eyeglasses at Kaiser Eye Care Centers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free healthcare services provided by Kaiser Permanente, including well and sick-child care visits, physical and eye exams, laboratory and X-ray services, immunizations, outpatient mental health and chemical dependency services, short-term physical therapy for children 10 years and older, and discounted eyeglasses at Kaiser Eye Care Centers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Uninsured children under age 21 who live in Prince George's County and meet income guidelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free healthcare services including preventive care, diagnostic services, immunizations, mental health services, physical therapy, and eyeglasses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Child must be under age 21
Child must live in Prince George's County
Child must not be eligible or enrolled in any other health insurance plan
Child must not be eligible for MCHP or MCHP Premium
Family income must be within 300% of the poverty level
Citizenship is not required

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Energy Program - Energy Efficiency Grant (Homeowners)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Clean Energy Program Energy Efficiency Grant for Homeowners is a Prince George's County program that provides supplemental grant funding to help Pepco and Washington Gas customers in nine designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs) implement energy efficiency improvements and retrofits on their residential properties. The program works in conjunction with EmPOWER Maryland energy incentives and takes a holistic approach to reducing energy barriers, supporting carbon reduction goals, and advancing renewable energy adoption. As of February 2024, the County has processed over 2,000 energy efficiency grant applications.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $7,500 to offset costs of energy efficiency measures and renewable energy adoption. The maximum grant award is $7,500, of which up to $5,000 can be allocated toward electric incentives and $2,500 toward natural gas incentives. Up to 50% of the total grant award ($3,750) can be allocated toward air sealing and insulation (excluding ancillary equipment like baffles and ventilation). The grant covers the $100 cost of the home energy assessment (amount included in total $7,500). Funds can also be used to address barriers preventing adoption of recommended efficiency measures. Grants are available in nine designated neighborhoods classified as Energy Resiliency Communities. Note: As of February 2024, the program is no longer funding electric incentives due to funding availability; all-electric homes do not qualify for the grant award.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pepco and Washington Gas customers living in nine designated Energy Resiliency Community (ERC) areas in Prince George's County who are willing to participate in applicable EmPOWER Maryland incentive programs. Single-family residents, townhouse residents, and condominium owners in individually metered properties (built before March 23, 2016).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency and retrofitting measures such as air sealing, insulation, appliance upgrades, HVAC equipment upgrades, water heater replacement, smart thermostats, duct sealing, windows and doors, attic insulation, and professional services needed to address barriers and facilitate higher efficiency and renewable energy adoption including solar photovoltaic and solar water heater systems. Funds can also be used to address barriers preventing adoption of recommended efficiency measures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to residents living within one of nine designated Energy Resiliency Community (ERC) areas in Prince George's County: Bladensburg - East Riverdale; Forestville; Hillcrest Heights - Marlow Heights; Kentland - Palmer Park; Oxon Hill - Glassmanor; Silver Hill; Suitland - Coral Hills; Langley Park; and Woodlawn - West Lanham. Residents must be utility customers of Pepco or Washington Gas and can verify ERC eligibility using the ERC Address Locator tool.
requirements_list: Must be a Prince George's County resident
Must be a Pepco and/or Washington Gas utility customer
Property must be located in a designated Energy Resiliency Community (ERC) verified using the ERC Address Locator tool
Live in a single-family, townhouse residence, or condominium that is individually metered and built before March 23, 2016

Apply to the applicable EmPOWER Maryland incentive program: Pepco's Home Performance with ENERGY STAR Program (HPwES) for market-rate applicants or Maryland DHCD's Low Income Energy Efficiency Program (LIEEP) for low-to-moderate-income applicants
Receive a comprehensive home energy assessment by a certified professional using a whole-house approach
Achieve minimum energy savings: 10% for electricity-only incentives or 15% for combined electricity and natural gas incentives

Submit an application with all required supporting documents including recent utility bills, home energy assessment report, proof of EmPOWER Maryland program application, W-9 form, Affidavit of Income, and Terms and Conditions Agreement
Selected contractor must be registered as a vendor with Prince George's County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Confirm eligibility by verifying you are a Prince George's County resident, Pepco and/or Washington Gas customer, and live in a designated ERC area using the ERC Address Locator tool. Step 2: Apply to the appropriate EmPOWER Maryland program (HPwES for market-rate or LIEEP for low-income applicants) and select a pre-approved contractor registered as a Prince George's County vendor to perform a comprehensive home energy assessment. Step 3: Submit prequalification documents to the Department of the Environment, Sustainable Energy including: recent utility bills (within 3 months), home energy assessment report, proof of EmPOWER Maryland program application, contract and itemized scope of work, W-9 form, signed Affidavit of Income, and signed Terms and Conditions Agreement. Prequalification letters are issued within 15 business days of receiving a complete application. Step 4: Upon prequalification approval, complete the energy efficiency work within 90 days (applicants may request one-time extension up to 6 months total). Step 5: Submit final required documents including HPwES Reservation of Funds email and test-out form, final itemized invoice with AHRI statements and equipment details, job completion date, and proof of any necessary permits. Final approval and site visit occur within 10 business days of invoice receipt. Step 6: Upon approval, the Office of Finance processes payment within 30 business days.

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Energy Program - Solar PV Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by Prince George's County that helps residents in nine designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs) install solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. The program requires that energy-efficiency measures be completed first, and works alongside state energy incentives to help recipients achieve at least 10% energy savings. The program supports Maryland and Prince George's County energy-efficiency and carbon reduction goals and is conducted as a research pilot with a limited number of awards available.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For homeowner-owned systems: grant awards up to $10,000 (income-qualified, household gross income less than 60% of median income for Prince George's County) or up to $5,000 (market-rate applicants) to cover eligible costs of installing a solar photovoltaic system, plus up to $2,000 for a solar power outlet in case of grid failure. For third-party owned/leased systems: grant awards up to $2,000 for installation costs plus up to $2,000 for a solar power outlet. Eligible costs include parts, components, and accessory equipment necessary to operate and install the system. Up to 15% of the grant award can be spent on reasonable installation facilitation measures such as tree trimming. The program aims to help recipients achieve at least 10% energy savings and is coupled with state energy incentives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Prince George's County within the Pepco and/or Washington Gas service territory who reside in one of nine designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs) and have successfully completed energy-efficiency improvements, and meet income or market-rate qualifications.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems and solar power outlets for grid failure backup on residential properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to residents within the Pepco and/or Washington Gas service territory who are located in one of nine designated Energy Resiliency Community (ERC) areas in Prince George's County.
requirements_list: Must be located within Pepco and/or Washington Gas service territory
Must reside in one of the nine designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs)
Must successfully implement energy-efficiency electricity and natural gas measures prior to applying

For income-qualified applicants (household gross income less than 60% of median income for Prince George's County): homeowner-owned systems eligible for up to $10,000 or leased/third-party owned systems up to $2,000
For market-rate applicants: homeowner-owned systems eligible for up to $5,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents must first complete energy-efficiency improvements, then contact Department of Sustainable Energy staff to confirm measures qualify and to begin the application process. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis from February 10 through August 15, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Energy Program - Solar Water Heater Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps residents access the benefits of solar water heating systems after successfully implementing energy-efficiency measures, while supporting Maryland and Prince George's County energy-efficiency and carbon reduction goals.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For homeowner-owned systems: grant awards up to $7,500 to cover eligible costs of installing a solar water heater. For third-party owned systems: grant awards up to $2,000 to cover eligible installation costs. Eligible costs include parts, components, and accessory equipment necessary to operate and install the system. Up to 15% of the grant award can be spent on reasonable installation facilitation measures.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents in Energy Resiliency Community areas who have successfully completed energy-efficiency improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of solar water heating systems on residential properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to residents in Energy Resiliency Community (ERC) designated areas in Prince George's County.
requirements_list: Successfully implement energy-efficiency electricity and natural gas measures prior to applying
System ownership status (homeowner-owned or third-party owned) determines eligible amount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents must first complete energy-efficiency improvements and then apply for the solar water heater grant. Contact Department of Sustainable Energy staff to confirm measures qualify and to begin the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Commercial Property Improvement Program (CPIP) provides grant incentives to retail shopping center owners and main street retail space owners to improve the appearance and enhance the retail experience at obsolete and underperforming retail centers and spaces in strong trade areas with high visibility in Prince George's County. The program assists with exterior façade enhancements, placemaking, lighting, and major building systems improvements to boost economic performance, marketability, competitiveness, and viability of retail centers. A 50% applicant match is required to ensure project commitment. The program is administered by the Prince George's County Redevelopment Authority.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to 50% of approved construction costs, with a minimum grant of $50,000 (requiring $100,000 total project costs) and a maximum grant of $350,000 (requiring $700,000 or more in total project costs). Grants reimburse up to 50% of approved construction costs as costs are incurred and documented. Architectural design and permit costs are reimbursed after construction is completed. Applicants must provide a 50% match of total project costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of retail shopping centers, retail centers, and main street retail spaces in Prince George's County, particularly those located in strong trade areas with high visibility.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior façade enhancements, placemaking, lighting, and major building systems improvements to retail centers and main street retail spaces to enhance marketability, competitiveness, viability, and overall appearance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. High-visibility retail areas and strong trade areas are prioritized.
requirements_list: Property must be a retail center or retail space
Location must be in a strong trade area with high visibility
Property must be obsolete or underperforming
50% applicant match required
Minimum grant $50,000 for $100,000 total project costs
Maximum grant $350,000 for $700,000 or more total project costs
Commercial space must be retail use only; places of worship and non-retail uses not funded
Shopping center owners who received CPIP funding in 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, or 2023 are not eligible
Construction must begin within 90 days after grant approval
Construction must be completed within 180 days after approval
Complete submissions required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a complete application with project details and proof of 50% match funding. Contact the program via email at CPIP@co.pg.md.us or by phone at 301-883-3623 with questions and inquiries. Construction must begin within 90 days of approval and be completed within 180 days of approval. Reimbursement occurs as costs are incurred and documented; architectural design and permit costs are reimbursed after construction completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program designed to assist local jurisdictions in implementing community development initiatives that develop viable urban communities by providing decent housing, creating a suitable living environment, and expanding economic opportunities for low and moderate-income persons. The program provides funding support to municipalities, local government agencies, and nonprofit organizations in Prince George's County to carry out housing, infrastructure, and public service activities benefiting low- and moderate-income communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development awards annual grants to Prince George's County on a competitive basis. The county then offers grants to municipalities and nonprofit organizations to carry out activities including affordable housing acquisition or preservation, neighborhood enhancement, and public services targeted at low- and moderate-income communities. Eligible uses include housing acquisition and rehabilitation, demolition, assistance to micro and small for-profit businesses, street improvements, health facilities, job development, youth services, senior programs, and health services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not currently accepting applications for Program Year 52
structured_extraction.program_audience: Municipalities, local government agencies, and nonprofit organizations located in Prince George's County seeking to fund community development projects that benefit low and moderate-income persons or address slums, blight, or urgent community needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable housing acquisition and rehabilitation, rental unit rehabilitation owned by nonprofits, demolition, direct assistance to for-profit micro and small businesses to create or retain jobs for low-to-moderate-income persons, public facilities and infrastructure improvements (streets, curbs, gutters, sidewalks, streetlights, sewers, storm drains, traffic signals, parks and recreation facilities, health facilities, and group home improvements), and public services (senior services, job development and training services, healthcare, youth services, and fair housing).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Applicant organizations or municipalities must be located in Prince George's County. Project beneficiaries must be low and moderate-income persons or must live in a low and moderate-income census tract or block group as determined by HUD, or the project must address slum or blighted conditions or urgent community needs.
requirements_list: At least 51 percent of the persons or households receiving the service must be low- and moderate-income, OR project beneficiaries must live in an area (census tract or block group) that is low- and moderate-income as determined by HUD, OR the project must address a slum or blighted condition or meet an urgent need.
Municipalities and local government agencies are eligible to apply.
Nonprofit organizations must provide a letter from the Internal Revenue Service certifying tax-exempt 501(c)(3) status.
Individual persons are not eligible to apply for CDBG funds.

Projects must meet one of three National Objectives: provide a benefit to low and moderate-income persons, prevent or eliminate slums and blight, or meet other urgent community development needs due to natural disasters or other emergencies.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Proposal application packets are available in October. Applicants submit proposals to a Proposal Advisory Group for review. The County Executive makes recommendations to the County Council. The County Council holds public hearings in April and adopts the Annual Action Plan by early May. The County submits the adopted Annual Action Plan to HUD by May of each year. Projects are implemented beginning July 1.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides small capital grants to civic and neighborhood associations and community-based organizations in Prince George's County to implement innovative projects within priority areas. The program funds capital projects in two categories: Neighborhood Beautification (streetscaping, street furniture, pedestrian enhancements, recreational improvements, signage, banners, way-finding systems, commercial façade improvements, public art installations) and Environment, Natural Resources and Sustainability (park restoration, stream restoration, open space restoration, urban agriculture, tree canopy replenishment, green roofs, low impact development, storm water management, preservation of historic landmarks and structures). The program aims to strengthen communities and build organizational capacity. The Redevelopment Authority of Prince George's County administers the program and awards up to $250,000 per fiscal year cycle, with $100,000 designated for projects in National Capital Strategic Economic Development Areas and $150,000 for county-wide projects, with individual grants up to $50,000 per organization.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Redevelopment Authority awards reimbursable capital grants up to $50,000 per organization, with $250,000 in total funding available per fiscal year cycle ($100,000 designated for National Capital Strategic Economic Development Areas within sustainable communities boundaries inside the Beltway, and $150,000 for county-wide projects). Grants are disbursed on a reimbursable basis, requiring payment up front for project expenses that will be reimbursed upon proof of payment. The grant performance period is one year from the date of execution of the CIG Grant Agreement. Grants must be used for capital purposes such as the purchase of equipment and materials for projects in one of two categories: Neighborhood Beautification or Environment, Natural Resources and Sustainability. Grants cannot be used for operating costs, program costs, salaries, stipends, or personnel expenses. Previously funded applicants can reapply only two years from the date of their originally approved application, and all prior CIG funds must be expended before submitting a new application. Organizations may only submit one CIG application per funding cycle.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Civic and neighborhood associations, community-based organizations, homeowners associations (HOAs), and houses of worship that are incorporated as 501(c)(3) non-profit entities and located within Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects including purchase of equipment and materials for: Neighborhood Beautification (streetscaping, street furniture, pedestrian enhancements, recreational improvements, signage, banners, way-finding systems, commercial façade improvements, internal and/or external improvements to commercial buildings used by the public, permanent public art installations); or Environment, Natural Resources and Sustainability (park restoration, stream restoration, open space restoration, urban agriculture, tree canopy replenishment, green roofs, low impact development, storm water management, preservation of historic landmarks, structures and sites). Funds cannot be used for operations, program costs, salaries, stipends, or personnel expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible applicants must be located within Prince George's County, Maryland, and projects must be carried out within the County. Projects located in the National Capital Strategic Economic Development Areas must be within previously designated sustainable communities' boundaries inside the Beltway, as approved by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. If the project is located in a municipality, municipal leadership approval is required. If located on private property, written agreement from the property owner is required. If located on government-owned or managed property, approval from the appropriate government agency is required.
requirements_list: Must be a civic/neighborhood association, community-based organization, HOA, or house of worship
Must be incorporated as a 501(c)(3) entity
Must be located within Prince George's County
Must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Must obtain a Certificate of Good Standing from the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Project must fall into one of two categories: Neighborhood Beautification or Environment, Natural Resources and Sustainability
Grant funds must be used for capital purposes only (equipment and materials); cannot be used for operations, program costs, salaries, stipends, or personnel
Project must have written approval from local municipal leadership (Mayor or Council) if located in a municipality
If located on private property, must provide letter of agreement or contract from property owner authorizing use of property
If located on government property, must provide written approval from appropriate government agency

Cannot fund projects previously funded through CIG
Can only submit one application per funding cycle
Grant is not final until CIG Grant Agreement is fully signed by RDA and Grantee AND Grantee provides certificate of insurance evidencing required coverage
Must provide evidence of community support through letters, petitions, resolutions or other documented public support
Must demonstrate project readiness through plans, bids, permits or other documentation
Should demonstrate leverage of additional funds and/or in-kind contributions from non-Prince George's County resources
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted in one original and three copies, mailed or hand-delivered (email applications will not be accepted). All applications and required supporting documentation must be received by May 18, 2026, by 5:00 PM EST. Post-marked date applies for mailed applications. Incomplete applications or those submitted after the deadline will not be accepted. Submit to: Andrea Anderson, Redevelopment Authority, 9200 Basil Court, Suite 504, Largo, MD 20774. Applications are evaluated by a Proposal Analysis Group (PAG) according to established criteria including physical impact and enhancement (30 points), track record of completed projects (20 points), demonstrated community/municipal support (20 points), project readiness and likelihood of implementation (20 points), and leverage of additional funds/in-kind contributions (10 points). Minimum 75 points required to qualify; up to 10 bonus points available for economic inclusion through subcontracting with eligible small/minority businesses (maximum 110 points possible). RDA staff will provide award recommendations to the Office of the County Executive for final approval. Selected applicants may be required to make formal project presentations and are subject to pre-award site visits. Upon approval, applicants enter into a CIG Grant Agreement with RDA. Questions must be submitted via email to Andrea Anderson (adanderson@co.pg.md.us) by May 8, 2026, at 5:00 PM EST; responses will be posted on the RDA website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A discretionary grant program offered by the Prince George's County Office of the County Executive to qualified nonprofit organizations. The program supports organizations' missions and goals through funding for projects that demonstrate need, sustainability, and community impact. Awards are based on criteria including community value, overall program costs, organizational stability, adequacy of other funding sources, evidence of partnerships and collaboration, and how dollars are invested within communities served.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Discretionary grants to qualified nonprofit organizations. Maximum award amounts do not exceed $100,000 in FY 2026. Previous awards have ranged from $1,000 to $125,000. Total award amount is disbursed in one lump sum payment via electronic deposit (ACH) within a minimum of 30 days of award notification. Funds are available based on funding availability and consideration of factors including organization mission and goals, statement of need, project description, sustainability relative to amount requested, evidence of partnerships and collaboration, and how dollars are invested within communities served. Grant recipients must submit a comprehensive final report documenting progress toward achieving stated results, organizational strengths and concerns, significant changes since award, plans for moving forward, financial challenges and mitigation strategies, and a budget versus actual variance analysis of CPG expenditures.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations incorporated in Maryland, the District of Columbia, or Virginia that provide services or activities in Prince George's County and are in good standing with their state of incorporation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects and programs that align with organization mission, address identified community need, demonstrate sustainability, and show evidence of partnerships and collaboration within communities served.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County; organization must provide services or activities in the county to be eligible.
requirements_list: Organization must be incorporated as a private 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization under the Internal Revenue Code
Organization must provide services or activities in Prince George's County
Organization must supply sufficient documentation proving current good standing status from the state where incorporated
Good standing documentation must be current year and dated within six months of application deadline
IRS Tax Determination Letter must be provided at time of application
Certificate of Status or equivalent proof of good standing is required
For organizations incorporated in Maryland: submit Maryland Certificate of Good Standing from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
For organizations incorporated in Washington, D.C.: submit D.C. Certificate of Good Standing or Clean Hands Certificate
For organizations incorporated in Virginia: submit Virginia Certificate of Good Standing from the State Corporation Commission
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application with required documentation to the Office of Management and Budget. Applications undergo eligibility verification review to determine if complete or incomplete. Only complete proposals are forwarded to the Executive Review Panel for review and funding consideration. The Executive Review Panel convenes to review proposals considering support of underserved populations, geographic diversity, administration's strategic priorities, and past performance. Award decisions are made by the Office of the County Executive. Award notification is sent via email. Payment is distributed via electronic deposit (ACH) within minimum 30 days of award notification. Grant recipients must submit final reports documenting program outcomes and financial performance.

Must not meet institutional level of care criteria.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit or exemption for land used to assist in the preservation of natural areas, for environmental education of the public, to promote conservation, or to maintain natural areas for public use or as wildlife sanctuaries.

Specific credit amounts are determined on a case-by-case basis based on the conservation value and use of the property. The exemption applies to the portion of the property that meets conservation land criteria.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Must be filed on or before October 1 of the tax year exemption is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in Prince George's County who own land used for conservation purposes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit or exemption for conservation land used for preservation of natural areas, environmental education, conservation promotion, or wildlife sanctuary purposes

Or land must be used to promote conservation

Owner must demonstrate qualified conservation use or purpose
Annual application and proof of claim must be filed with the Office of Law
Application must be filed on or before October 1 of the tax year exemption is sought

The Office of Law will review applications and determine eligibility based on the property's conservation value and qualifying use.

structured_extraction.program_name: Coordinated Specialty Care for First Episode Psychosis (FEP) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides specialized services and treatment coordination for individuals experiencing their first episode of psychosis, helping them access coordinated specialty care and rehabilitation services. The program is an evidence-based, multidisciplinary treatment team-based intervention that provides community-based, person-centered, recovery-oriented services and supports to youth and young adults ages 15-30 who are within one to two years of the initial onset of psychotic symptoms.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding is available through a Request for Application process for organizations and providers to establish Coordinated Specialty Care programs for First Episode Psychosis services. The award is anticipated to be up to $377,433 total, with the agreement duration from May 1, 2026, through June 30, 2031. The agreement is cost reimbursement-based. Funding for FY27 and FY28 shall be added by future amendments. Reimbursement is contingent upon program performance, submission of required reports, and submission of requests for payment. Monthly reimbursement requests must be submitted by the 10th day of each month using the Ariba System on the LBHA-provided invoice Form 437. The LBHA/County shall only authorize reimbursements of actual and reasonable expenditures in line with the applicant's approved budget.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed mental health services providers and behavioral health organizations in Prince George's County serving youth and young adults ages 15-30 experiencing their first episode of psychosis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To establish Coordinated Specialty Care programs for First Episode Psychosis services, including clinical evaluation, therapeutic services, medication management, supported employment/education services, recovery coaching, peer support services, crisis intervention, outreach and education, and family psychoeducation services.

Must provide three (3) attestation letters from community partners or organizations from the past 2 years attesting to experience providing services listed in Scope of Work

Must register with SAP Ariba system for submission of invoices
Must maintain a census of 25 youth and young adults, ages 15-30, per quarter
Must use the Core Assessment Battery (CAB) standardized assessment
Must use the Critical Time Intervention model (CTI) as step-down to lower level of care
Must ensure 24/7 crisis intervention availability

Must participate in monthly conference calls with BHA staff

structured_extraction.program_name: County Right of First Refusal Program: Multifamily Rental Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that gives Prince George's County the right to match offers and purchase multifamily rental properties with 20 or more dwelling units before they are sold to other buyers, with the goal of expanding the availability of affordable rental housing for low- to moderate-income households in the County. The County may exercise its right of first refusal or assign its purchase rights to a qualified third party, supporting the preservation and protection of the affordable housing stock throughout Prince George's County.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County exercises its right of first refusal to purchase multifamily rental properties (20+ units) or assign its purchase rights to a third party before the property owner sells to another buyer. The program preserves properties as affordable housing for low- to moderate-income households. Property owners must notify the Director of the Department of Housing and Community Development in writing after entering into a bona fide contract of sale. The County then has 60 days to exercise its right to purchase or assign those rights. For ROFR Preservation Fund loans, financing is available as subordinate loans up to $3,000,000 (exceptions may be approved) at 0% interest with up to 40-year terms. Loans are subordinated to senior financing, with no payment due prior to December 31, 2026, after which repayment is deferred until maturity. Prepayment allowed after 20 years with 10% penalty. Loan to value (LTV) up to 110% (up to 120% for high public purpose properties). Properties must establish affordability restrictions for at least 30 years. Borrower must submit annual compliance documentation and implement Resident Empowerment and Community Support Plan. Properties receive property tax reduction via PILOT (Payment In Lieu of Taxes). Prospective buyers seeking an exception to the ROFR must execute a Written Agreement with DHCD prior to entering into a contract of sale.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; 60-day evaluation period after ROFR offer received
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jonathan R. Butler, Director; Ashley P. Johnson-Hare, Deputy Director; Pamela A. Wilson, Chief, Housing Development Division; Karan Stewart; Kiara Jones, Administrative Aide
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners seeking to sell multifamily rental facilities with 20 or more dwelling units, prospective buyers interested in acquiring such properties, multifamily rental property stakeholders, and qualified non-profit and for-profit developers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and preservation of multifamily rental properties to maintain affordable housing for low- to moderate-income households. ROFR Preservation Fund loans can be used for acquisition, rehabilitation, and other typical transaction costs of properties acquired under the ROFR Program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program applies to all areas of Prince George's County, Maryland. For properties located within County municipalities, municipality approval is required prior to purchase. Municipalities have 180 days to approve or disapprove the County's ROFR actions. Properties receiving ROFR Preservation Fund loans funded with ARPA capital must be located within Qualified Census Tracts (QCTs). Properties receiving loans funded solely with Maryland DHCD funds may be located anywhere in Prince George's County.
requirements_list: Property must be a multifamily rental facility consisting of 20 or more dwelling rental units
Property owner must provide written notice to the Director of DHCD within 5 business days after entering into a bona fide contract of sale
Property owner must provide written notice to each tenant within 5 business days of contract execution
County must be given opportunity to exercise right of first refusal within 60 days of receiving complete ROFR offer and all required documentation
Prospective buyers seeking an exception must execute a Written Agreement with DHCD prior to entering into a bona fide contract of sale
ROFR offer must remain open for 60 days after all required documents have been submitted
Property inspection access must be provided within 45 days of notice of sale

For ROFR Preservation Fund loans: borrower must be approved by Department as eligible ROFR participant; property must establish affordability restrictions for at least 30 years; borrower must submit annual compliance documentation; borrower must implement approved Resident Empowerment and Community Support Plan including resident empowerment initiatives, 40% County-Certified County-Based Small Business participation requirement, 30% Minority Business Enterprise participation requirement, and local hiring goals for on-site staff

Owner must submit comprehensive ROFR documentation including: bona fide contract of sale, site plan, 3 years of income and expense statements, current rental schedule, current rent roll, rental license, use and occupancy permit, expected re-rent rates, mortgage holder information and existing loan balances, security deposit schedule, architectural/engineering plans, lead certification, Phase I Environmental Survey, capital needs assessment, underground storage tank information, service contracts, warranties, and notarized affidavit confirming tenant notice requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: (1) Property Owner enters into bona fide contract of sale with prospective buyer. (2) Within 5 business days, owner must provide written notice to each tenant (by hand or certified mail, return receipt requested) and written notice to the Director of DHCD (by certified mail, return receipt requested). (3) Within 5 business days of contract execution, owner submits written ROFR offer and all required ROFR Documents to Department. (4) Within 7 business days of receipt, Department makes initial evaluation and notifies owner of decision to accept, waive, or exempt the ROFR. (5) If Department exercises ROFR, owner's offer remains open for 60 days. Department may request property inspection within 45 days. (6) Department evaluates and decides whether to exercise ROFR, assign rights to qualified third party, or waive ROFR. (7) If Department exercises ROFR or assigns to third party, purchase must be completed within 180 days or as otherwise agreed. (8) If Department does not exercise ROFR, Certificate of Compliance is issued within 10 days. For exceptions to ROFR, prospective buyers must request approval from DHCD and execute Written Agreement prior to entering into contract. ROFR Preservation Fund loan application follows standard underwriting with Department approval of borrower's repayment strategy, Affordability Agreement terms, and Resident Empowerment and Community Support Plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for real property owned by Crescent Cities Charities, Inc. that is not exempt from taxation under Title 7 of the Tax-Property Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland.

The credit is granted annually upon submission of an application and proof of claim to the Director of Finance on or before October 1st of each taxable year. The credit is applicable to real property owned by Crescent Cities Charities, Incorporated that is not exempt from taxation under Title 7 of the Tax-Property Article.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Crescent Cities Charities, Inc.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real property owned by the organization that is not exempt from taxation under Title 7 of the Tax-Property Article.

requirements_list: Real property must be owned by Crescent Cities Charities, Incorporated
Real property must not be exempt from taxation under Title 7 of the Tax-Property Article
Annual application and proof of claim must be submitted to the Director of Finance on or before October 1st of each taxable year

structured_extraction.program_description: The Domestic Violence Community Assistance Fund provides grants to non-profit organizations to enhance services for individuals and families affected by domestic violence and human trafficking. The fund supports programs designed to prevent violence in the home and help people achieve independence. Services include legal assistance, counseling, support groups, employment training, and housing support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided to non-profit organizations to support programmatic services including support groups, perpetrator counseling, shelter and housing, legal services, counseling, case management, financial assistance, and emergency needs support for domestic violence victims and families.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations serving individuals and families affected by domestic violence or human trafficking in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support services for domestic violence and human trafficking survivors including legal services, counseling, support groups, employment training, housing assistance, shelter, case management, emergency financial assistance, and capacity building activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County
requirements_list: Applicant must be a non-profit organization
Organization must provide services to individuals and families affected by domestic violence and/or human trafficking
Services must support prevention of violence in the home and achievement of greater independence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit proposals describing how funds will be used to enhance services. Grantees receive funding and participate in capacity-building and technical assistance activities provided by the Greater Washington Community Foundation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Down Payment on Your Dream Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A down payment and closing cost assistance program for income-qualified first-time homebuyers or individuals who have not owned a home in the previous three years. The program provides assistance to purchase vacant foreclosed properties located in specified eligible zip codes within Prince George's County.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Down payment and closing cost assistance for purchasing vacant foreclosed properties. Applicants must contribute a minimum required cash contribution (up to $2,000 depending on income). Program funds are not given as cash back at settlement; excess funds are used to reduce or pay down the first mortgage.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-qualified first-time homebuyers or individuals who have not owned a home anywhere during the previous three years seeking to purchase vacant foreclosed properties in eligible zip codes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of vacant and foreclosed residential properties (single family homes, townhomes, or condominiums) located within one of 33 eligible zip codes and within 3 miles of applicant's place of employment.

structured_extraction.program_name: ENERGY STAR Certification and Green Leasing (ESGL) Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program providing funds to existing office and multifamily building owners who are Pepco and/or Washington Gas customers in Prince George's County to perform energy and water efficiency retrofits and obtain US EPA ENERGY STAR certification. The program aims to increase the number of ENERGY STAR certified buildings, encourage green leasing practices, support the county's greenhouse gas reduction goals, and attract and retain high-valued tenants. Building owners are encouraged to adopt green leasing best practices to promote energy-efficient behavior among tenants. The program targets a 20% or greater reduction in energy consumption for participating buildings.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maximum award available per application is $150,000. Incentives include: up to $50,000 to cover ASHRAE Level 2 Audit costs (if required); up to $100,000 for Electric and/or Natural Gas measures if an audit is required; up to $150,000 for Electric and/or Natural Gas measures if an ASHRAE Level 2 Audit is not required; and up to 100% of the cost of a Licensed Professional's sign-off to verify and stamp the ENERGY STAR certification application. Grants are intended to help recipients reduce energy consumption by 20% or greater for office buildings and multifamily dwellings.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy and water efficiency retrofits, ASHRAE Level 2 energy audit costs, electric and natural gas efficiency measures, and costs associated with a Licensed Professional's verification and stamping of the ENERGY STAR certification application for office and multifamily buildings.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit an application for ENERGY STAR certification and green leasing grant funding. The program provides funding to cover audit costs, energy and water efficiency retrofit measures, and professional verification of certification.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Economic Development Incentive (EDI) Fund is a multi-year economic development program administered by Prince George's County that provides loans and grants to eligible businesses and projects. The program focuses on expanding the County's commercial tax base, job retention and attraction, support for small and local businesses, promotion of development and redevelopment opportunities, transit-oriented development, and growth of key industry sectors. With a $50 million multi-year commitment, the EDI Fund offers financing at competitive market rates or slightly lower, with most awards structured as loans to small and medium-sized businesses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The EDI Fund has a $50 million multi-year commitment, with approximately $7 million to $11 million available each fiscal year. Most awards are made as loans to small and medium-sized businesses. Grants may be considered in particular and extraordinary circumstances involving large numbers of jobs. Interest rates are determined on a case-by-case basis depending on credit and personal history, generally set at competitive market rates or slightly lower in accordance with statutory goals. The Prince George's prime rate is 4%. An application fee of 1% of the loan amount is required, structured as follows: up to $1,000,000 requires $2,500 up front (with balance financed as part of total loan), and $1,000,000 and above requires $5,000 up front with remainder due at closing. A portion of the 1% fee may be financed as part of the total loan amount. All awardees must provide appropriate collateral or other security to protect the public investment. Businesses receiving aid are subject to audits and compliance reviews.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses and non-profit organizations located in or serving Prince George's County. Nonprofits are eligible for funding of projects resulting in growth to the county's commercial tax base and new jobs, but not for funding operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that grow the county's commercial tax base and add county jobs, including commercial tax base expansion, job retention and attraction, support for small and local businesses, development and redevelopment promotion, transit-oriented development, growth of key industry sectors, business financing for project development, business purchase, equipment acquisition, and working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses and projects located in Prince George's County, Maryland.

Projects must meet other specified economic development goals
All awardees must provide appropriate collateral or other security
Recipients subject to audits, compliance review, and oversight to assure accountability
Application fee (1% of loan amount)

Personal financial statements of owners holding 20% or more of the company

Current credit report (within last 6 months)
Business plan, executive summary, or capability statement

Disclosure of Interested Parties Form (K)
Business Indebtedness Form (N)

Resume of company owners and management team

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply by downloading an application from the website, filling out an online application, or picking up an application at the office. Once completed, submit the application by mail, online, or in person at the office. A business development specialist will review the application and contact the applicant. After initial review determines the application meets program requirements, additional documentation may be requested. Applications are processed through a step-by-step process designed for fair and efficient acceptance and processing. Applicants can check application progress online at the EDI Fund portal.

The program covers emergency expenses to help prevent homelessness and stabilize housing and essential services.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency expenses including eviction prevention, mortgage foreclosure prevention, utility shut-off prevention, delinquent water bill payment, and burial assistance.

Must have a minor child (0-21 years of age) or be pregnant

structured_extraction.program_name: Emergency Food Assistance Program / Food Pantry Services
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that expands access to nutritious food for households experiencing food insecurity in Prince George's County. It operates as a clearinghouse for distributing donated food through local community pantries and shelters, and maintains permanent food pantries at Prince George's County Department of Social Services (PGCDSS) service centers. The program provides free access to fresh produce, shelf-stable items, and essential groceries, helping reduce household hardship, support overall well-being, and contribute to housing stability by relieving the financial strain of food costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free food from community pantries, shelters, and permanent PGCDSS food pantry locations. Permanent food pantries are available Monday through Friday from 8:00 A.M. to 4:30 P.M. at three locations: Hyattsville (North County), Landover (Central County), and Temple Hills (South County). Services include fresh produce, shelf-stable items, and essential groceries. No registration required. Walk-ups welcome. Distribution also occurs through on-site pantries at DSS locations and community distribution partnerships.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All Prince George's County residents experiencing food insecurity, with emphasis on low-income individuals and families
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and distribution of fresh produce, shelf-stable items, and essential groceries
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Be a Prince George's County resident
Experience food insecurity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the food pantry locations Monday through Friday, 8:00 A.M. to 4:30 P.M. at Hyattsville (North County), Landover (Central County), or Temple Hills (South County). No registration required at PGCDSS food pantries — walk-ups welcome. You may also access the network at pgcfec.org/resources/find-food-food-pantry-listings/ to find local food pantries and community distribution partnerships.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Prince George's County program providing rental assistance to renters and landlords affected by financial hardship, including hardship arising from the COVID-19 pandemic. The program assists tenants with household income below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI) who are having difficulty paying rent. Tenants above 50% AMI must provide eviction documentation (court summons, court judgment, Warrant of Restitution, or Warrant for Possession), while tenants at or below 50% AMI do not require eviction paperwork. Landlords and property owners may also apply on behalf of qualifying tenants located in eligible census tracts or who previously applied without receiving assistance.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct financial assistance payments to help tenants pay delinquent or past-due rent. Payments can be made directly to landlords or to tenants for direct payment to landlords. The specific dollar amount is determined by the County Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) based on application review and funding availability. Priority is given to households at or below 50% of AMI. Maximum of 18 months of cumulative assistance payments. Tenants must have experienced unemployment, income reduction, significant costs, or other financial hardship directly or indirectly related to the COVID-19 pandemic. As of September 2023, approximately $11M in funding remains available for assistance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing (Portal access code required to apply)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Renters and landlords/property owners in Prince George's County. Tenants must have household income below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI) and be experiencing difficulty paying rent, including those facing eviction. Landlords may apply on behalf of eligible tenants in qualifying census tracts or who previously applied without receiving assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Delinquent and current rent payments. Financial hardship assistance for tenants related to or arising during the COVID-19 public health crisis.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rental property must be located in Prince George's County, Maryland. Applicants must be Prince George's County residents. For landlord applications, rental units must be located within census tracts in Prince George's County that meet risk factors such as housing stress, social factors, and pandemic effects, or in a Qualified Census Tract (QCT) as defined by HUD.
requirements_list: Household income below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI)
Difficulty paying rent (past due rent or utilities)
Rental property located in Prince George's County
Prince George's County residency
Financial hardship arising because of or during the COVID-19 public health crisis
Residency verification with current lease or approval letter

Income verification through W2s, tax filings, paystubs, or other income documentation for all household members over 18 years old who are not full-time students; self-certification letter accepted as last resort when income not verifiable due to COVID-19 impact
One or more household members qualified for unemployment or experienced income reduction, significant costs, or other financial hardship due directly or indirectly to COVID-19 pandemic
Signed lease or acceptable documentation such as utility payment evidence or landlord attestation (Landlord Attestation in Lieu of Current Lease acceptable for month-to-month leases or subleases)
For tenants at 30% AMI and below: eviction paperwork not required
For tenants at 31%-50% AMI: court summons required
For tenants at 51%-80% AMI: court judgment required
For landlord applicants: rental unit located in eligible census tract meeting risk factors or landlord previously applied in Fall 2020 without receiving assistance
For landlord applicants: property in a Qualified Census Tract (QCT) for income self-certification eligibility
Landlord must provide name, address, SSN or Tax Identification Number, property deed, W-9 form signed with company name matching ACH enrollment, and EFT/ACH enrollment form
Landlord must provide rent ledger showing past due amounts

Tenant must provide rent ledger, current valid lease with tenant names matching applicants, income verification documents for all household members 18 and older who are not full-time college students (Calendar Year 2020 income documentation plus current month 2021 documentation)
Detailed written attestation explaining financial hardship, reduced income, and significant costs incurred due to COVID-19, signed by all adult household members (18 and older)

Tenant applications prioritized based on income level and eviction status: at or below 30% AMI highest priority, followed by 31%-50% AMI with court summons, then 51%-80% AMI with court judgments; within income categories prioritized by scheduled evictions and utility shutoffs
Landlord applications prioritized for most vulnerable census tracts
Maximum 18 months cumulative assistance per tenant household
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Tenants and Landlords: 1. Call ERAP Hotline at (301) 883-6504, Press 9 to obtain an access code (portal currently closed, access code required). 2. Gather required documentation including income verification for all household members 18+ who are not full-time college students (Calendar Year 2020 documentation: 1040 tax form or W-2, 1099, bank statements, or last December paystub; plus current month 2021 documentation: paystubs or bank statements), signed lease or acceptable documentation of rental status (utility bills, bank statements, landlord attestation), written attestation of financial hardship due to COVID-19 signed by all adult household members, and evidence of housing instability (past due rent or utilities, notice of failure to pay). 3. For landlord applications: gather rent ledger, property deed, W-9 form (company name on Line 1 must match ACH enrollment company name), EFT/ACH enrollment form, management agreement if applicable, executed trust document if owned by trust. 4. Submit application through online portal with all required documents. 5. Applications screened for prioritization based on income level and housing instability indicators. 6. Assigned to reviewers for evaluation. 7. Quality control check conducted. 8. Finance and DHCD approval obtained. 9. Upon approval, receive notice of award with approved dollar amount. 10. Sign Rental Assistance Agreement and provide tenant affidavit certification to accept final assistance amount. 11. Receive payment following acceptance of assistance terms and approval through County Finance. 12. Additional information may be requested by DHCD to validate application information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Enterprise Zone Focus Area Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: A state and local incentive program that offers enhanced tax credits to businesses expanding or locating in designated Enterprise Zone Focus Areas. Businesses can receive higher state income tax credits for hiring disadvantaged or non-disadvantaged employees, and local property tax credits on both real and personal property expansion, renovation, or capital improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State Income Tax Credit: Disadvantaged employees receive $9,000 total per employee spread over 3 years ($4,500 in Year 1, $3,000 in Year 2, $1,500 in Year 3). Non-disadvantaged employees receive a one-time $1,500 credit per employee. Local Property Tax Credit: A 10-year credit against local real property taxes on a portion of real property expansion, renovation, or capital improvement equal to 80% of the eligible assessment in each year of the entire 10-year period. Additionally, a 10-year tax credit against local personal property taxes on new investments in personal property equal to 80% of the eligible assessments in each year of the entire 10-year period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses expanding or locating in designated Enterprise Zone Focus Areas in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits for state income taxes and local property and personal property taxes on business expansion, renovation, and capital improvements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated Enterprise Zone Focus Areas in Prince George's County
requirements_list: Business must be located in an Enterprise Zone Focus Area
For state income tax credit, must hire disadvantaged or non-disadvantaged employees
For local property tax credit, must have real property expansion, renovation, or capital improvement
For personal property tax credit, must make new investments in personal property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 and ask to speak with a Business Development Specialist for details on applying for Enterprise Zone Focus Area tax credits.

structured_extraction.program_name: Enterprise Zone Non-Focus Area Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: A state and local incentive program that offers tax credits to businesses expanding or locating in designated Enterprise Zone areas that are not Focus Areas. Businesses can receive state income tax credits for hiring disadvantaged or non-disadvantaged employees, and local property tax credits on real property expansion, renovation, or capital improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State Income Tax Credit: Disadvantaged employees receive $6,000 total per employee spread over 3 years ($3,000 in Year 1, $2,000 in Year 2, $1,000 in Year 3). Non-disadvantaged employees receive a one-time $1,000 credit per employee. Local Property Tax Credit: A 10-year credit on a portion of real property expansion, renovation, or capital improvement. The credit equals 80% of the eligible assessment in each of the first 5 years, then decreases by 10% annually for the second 5 years (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%).

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 2025 HUD Continuum of Care (CoC) Local Competition
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal funding competition administered locally by Prince George's County for organizations to apply for Continuum of Care Program grants to support homeless services and housing programs. This is the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development's primary funding source for homeless services. The FY 2025 competition NOFO was initially issued by HUD but was withdrawn on December 8, 2024 to allow for revisions, with a modified NOFO anticipated before the obligation deadline. Local competition materials including applications and scoring tools will be released once HUD provides further guidance. The competition includes funding for renewal projects, new permanent housing bonus projects, and domestic violence bonus projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funding through the HUD Continuum of Care Program to support homeless services and housing initiatives. FY 2024/2025 estimated funding includes $11,287,526 for renewal/reallocation/consolidation/transition projects, $564,376 for planning projects, $1,354,503 for new projects under permanent housing bonus, and $1,038,306 for new projects under DV housing bonus. Eligible project types include Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH), Rapid Re-Housing (RRH), Transitional Housing-Rapid Re-Housing (TH-RRH), and Joint Component Projects. Funds support leasing, operating, supportive services, rental assistance, HMIS, and project administration costs. Awards are made through a competitive local application and ranking process, with Tier 1 projects (approximately 90% of funds) receiving priority funding and Tier 2 projects (approximately 10% plus bonus funds) receiving funding based on available resources.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Letter of Intent Due Wednesday, December 10, 2025 at 5:00 PM (based on FY 2024 pattern; FY 2025 deadlines pending HUD guidance)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and government organizations providing homeless services and housing programs in Prince George's County. Eligible applicants must be non-profits or government agencies with active SAM registration, valid UEI number, nonprofit documentation, clean federal compliance status, sufficient financial capacity and management systems, and code of conduct on file with HUD.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support housing and services to address homelessness within the Prince George's County Continuum of Care area. Eligible uses include: (1) Permanent Supportive Housing with long-term rental assistance and supportive services for chronically homeless individuals and families; (2) Rapid Re-Housing providing short-term rental assistance and services to quickly move people into housing; (3) Transitional Housing-Rapid Re-Housing combining temporary housing with rapid transition to permanent solutions; (4) HMIS and planning activities; and (5) Project administration. Services must address identified needs including behavioral health, employment, income support, mainstream benefits access, community integration, and housing stability support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County Continuum of Care area (entire geographic area of Prince George's County, Maryland)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The FY 2025 CoC competition follows a multi-stage process: (1) HUD issues the NOFO (Notice of Funding Opportunity); (2) Prince George's County provides local notification to all CoC members and posts materials; (3) Organizations submit a Letter of Intent by the established deadline indicating funding type (regular/DV bonus), housing type, target population, and brief program description; (4) Interested applicants attend CoC Office Hours for technical assistance; (5) Applicants submit full applications through E-Snaps by the application deadline with required checklists and supplemental documents; (6) The CoC Project Review Committee (PRC) reviews and ranks applications based on established criteria; (7) The PRC presents recommendations to the full Homeless Services Partnership (HSP) for discussion and ratification by majority vote; (8) Applicants are notified of decisions; (9) The final CoC application is submitted to HUD by the federal deadline. Applicants may appeal placement in Tier 2, reduction of renewal amounts, or reallocation decisions within two business days of notification by contacting the CoC Planner in writing. Debriefings may be requested for non-selection decisions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development that helps Prince George's County expand the supply of decent, affordable housing for low and very low-income families. The program assists nonprofits and for-profit developers in producing and rehabilitating housing, helps first-time homebuyers purchase homes, supports group homes for special populations, and enables Community Housing Development Organizations to create housing opportunities for households of limited income. The program is operated under the requirements of Title 24 under the Code of Federal Regulations, Part 92.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance is provided to eligible projects and beneficiaries in the form of subordinate loans with a 2% simple interest rate during the permanent loan period and 0% interest during construction. For multifamily rental projects, HOME financing is made available as a Subordinate Loan. Loan amounts up to $2,500,000 are available, with exceptions approved at the discretion of the Department. Prince George's County receives approximately $3.5 million annually in HOME funds from HUD. HOME Loans are generally coterminous with Senior Loans, with a 40-year amortization from the beginning of the permanent loan period. Annual loan payments are due by April 30 unless an alternative date is agreed upon. A legal fee of $55,000 is due at closing. The HOME Loan may be prepaid in whole or in part without penalty provided the Borrower is in compliance with affordability and rental requirements. Loans are subordinate to Senior Loans approved by the Department and secured by a subordinate lien Deed of Trust recorded in the land records of Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis throughout the fiscal year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and for-profit developers, first-time homebuyers, Community Housing Development Organizations, and households of limited income in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Producing and rehabilitating housing, assisting first-time homebuyers to purchase homes, acquiring or improving group homes for special populations, creating housing opportunities for households of limited income, construction expenses, acquisition costs, and professional fees. HOME funds must be used for expenses allowable under 24 CFR Part 92.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Funding priorities include: Located within one mile of the Blue Line transit Corridor; Located within one mile of the Purple Line transit Corridor; New construction and/or preservation of affordable housing within one mile of existing and planned Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) Metro Stations throughout the County; Conformance with housing priorities and guidance in the Prince George's County's 2035 Adopted General Plan; Mixed-use, mixed-income affordable housing developments; and Affordable housing that includes sustainable design, energy efficiency and green design standards.
requirements_list: Projects must meet Federal lead-based paint regulations of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1992
Projects must comply with minimum affordability period requirements based on the type of eligible activity (minimum 15 years for rehabilitation and 20 years for new construction)
Beneficiaries must meet income limits as published by HUD on an annual basis
HOME units must be affordable to households with incomes at or below 60% of the Area Median Income (AMI)
At least 20% of all HOME units must be affordable to households with incomes at or below 50% of the AMI
At time of HOME loan closing, the Borrower and its managing entities must have business registrations that are in good standing

All members of the development team (Developer/Sponsor, Borrower, General Contractor and subcontractors, Managing Agent, Architect, and other professionals) may not be suspended, debarred, or deemed otherwise ineligible to receive federal funds
Development team must be approved by the Department and must have demonstrated experience in the immediate past five years with successful development and completion of affordable housing projects
Projects with 12 or more HOME units will be subject to the Davis-Bacon Act and must pay prevailing wage rates
An Affordability Agreement restricting the Property's rent and tenant income must be recorded in the Land Records for a period of at least 40 years

Developer must comply with the County's Diversity and Equity Policy for Publicly Subsidized Development Projects per Section 10-335 of the Prince George's County Code: At least 30% of Development Costs for Construction must be paid to County-Based Small Businesses (CBSB) and/or Locally-Owned and Operated Businesses (LOB), including at least 20% of design costs if applicable; at least 25% of Development Costs for Construction shall use Best Efforts to be paid to County-Based Minority Business Enterprises; General Contractor Team must include one or more CMBE and/or LOB; at least 25% of total work hours must be worked by County Residents, including at least 20% of specialty trade work hours
Section 3 of the Housing and Urban Development Act of 1968 requires 35% of total labor hours must be worked by qualifying Section 3 workers and 5% by Targeted Section 3 workers
Market assessment demonstrating current market demand required (no more than 6 months old from application submission)

All costs of due diligence are the sole responsibility of the Borrower; Department requires Reliance Letters for Environmental Report(s), Capital Needs Assessment (required for rehabilitation projects of 26+ units), and Property Appraisal
Property Manager must be approved by the Department
Borrower must submit annual documentation demonstrating compliance with Affordability Requirements and annual Financing Reporting

Projects must comply with Fair Housing Act, Executive Order 11063, accessibility requirements under Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, Americans with Disabilities Act, and the National Environmental Policy Act
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis throughout the fiscal year on a project-by-project basis. At the discretion of the Director, DHCD may accept program applications on a rolling basis or issue a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA). Financial assistance amounts are determined individually for each project through a comprehensive underwriting and subsidy layering analysis. DHCD conducts a preliminary underwriting analysis by independently evaluating the project budget, financing and development schedule. Underwriting includes examination of project sources and uses, cost and profit reasonableness, market demand, Developer experience and capacity, and financial commitments. DHCD updates project underwriting at initial closing or construction start and before additional HOME funds are awarded. The Department will not commit funds to a project until all necessary financing is secured and evidenced in writing, the underwriting and subsidy layering has been completed, and construction can be expected to begin within 12 months. Developers must submit: market assessment, Developer capacity documentation, sources and uses statement, operating pro forma, Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing Plan (HUD Form 935), Section 3 Business Plan, Supplier Diversity and Equity Plan, and all required due diligence reports. Written agreements must be executed before disbursing HOME funds, including Commitment and Program Agreement, Regulatory Agreement, Declaration of Covenants or Restrictive Covenants, Deed of Trust, Deed of Trust Note, Building Loan Agreement, and Payment in Lieu of Taxes Agreement (PILOT) as applicable.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded home rehabilitation assistance program administered by Prince George's County that provides financial assistance to homeowners of limited financial means for the rehabilitation and improvement of single-family owner-occupied homes. The program offers zero-percent interest loans with no monthly payment requirements, aimed at upgrading deteriorated dwellings to contemporary minimum property standards, eliminating housing code violations, and addressing health and safety concerns. Eligible repairs include lead, mold, and asbestos abatement; roof, electrical, plumbing, and flooring repairs; energy efficiency upgrades; and ADA-related improvements.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Home rehabilitation loans up to $60,000 at 0% interest with no monthly payment requirements. Eligible repairs include: health hazard remediation (lead, mold, asbestos abatement); safety and code compliance repairs (roof replacement, electrical systems, plumbing, flooring); energy efficiency upgrades (windows, insulation, air sealing, siding); ADA-related improvements (ramps, grab bars, railings); and other improvements considered on a case-by-case basis. The program also provides grant-based financial assistance for upgrading homes to contemporary minimum property standards and eliminating all housing code violations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners of limited financial means who own and occupy a single-family home in Prince George's County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation and improvement of single-family owner-occupied homes, including: health hazard remediation (lead, mold, asbestos abatement); safety and code compliance repairs (roof replacement, electrical systems, plumbing, flooring); energy efficiency upgrades (windows, insulation, air sealing, siding); ADA-related improvements (ramps, grab bars, railings); elimination of housing code violations; and upgrading homes to contemporary minimum property standards.

Must be of limited financial means; total household income cannot exceed program limits

Cannot have any current liens, judgments, or recent bankruptcy
