structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit is applied to the portion of leased property exclusively used by the municipal corporation, based on the amount of the credit that the property owner is contractually obligated to reduce from the tenant's tax liability. The credit is calculated on the assessed value of the property that is leased to and exclusively occupied by the municipal corporation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than April 1 prior to the tax year for which the credit is being requested
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners leasing real property to municipal corporations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit applies to the property tax imposed on the portion of the property leased to and exclusively used by the municipal corporation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in Prince George's County.
requirements_list: The portion of the property upon which the tax credit is based must be leased, occupied, and used exclusively by the municipal corporation
The credit does not apply when the municipal corporation subleases the property, uses the property for any profit-making purpose, or no longer occupies the property
The municipal corporation must be contractually liable to the owner for property taxes
The property owner must be contractually obligated to reduce, by the amount of the tax credit, the amount of taxes for which the municipal corporation is otherwise contractually liable
Application must be signed under oath by both the property owner and the municipal corporation
A copy of the executed lease must be submitted with the application
The lease must demonstrate that the property is used exclusively by the municipal corporation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application to the Supervisor of Assessments and Taxation no later than April 1 prior to the tax year for which the credit is being requested. The application must be signed under oath by both the property owner and the municipal corporation and must include a copy of the executed lease. Upon termination of the lease or cessation of possession by the tenant, the owner must notify the Supervisor of Assessments and Taxation within 30 days. Applications should be submitted to the Prince George's County Department of Finance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Annual funding program for owners and developers to support housing and community development projects, specifically multifamily rental housing, in Prince George's County. The county considers applications during the regular NOFA cycle and may also consider priority, time-sensitive projects outside the normal timeframe if they have secured financing. The 2026 NOFA seeks to support high-quality multifamily rental housing developments that leverage external financing, including Low Income Housing Tax Credits, and deliver durable affordability for low- and moderate-income households.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME) or County Housing Investment Trust Fund (HITF) loans up to $2,500,000 per project for acquisition/rehabilitation or new construction of affordable multifamily rental housing, in conjunction with applications to the State of Maryland for Low Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTC). DHCD prioritizes projects seeking 9% LIHTC but will consider 4% LIHTC awards based on funding priorities and available resources. Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) requests are reviewed on a project-by-project basis based on financial viability, with a maximum of $600 of tax relief per affordable unit per year. DHCD determines the appropriate source of County funding for each project based on resource availability and policy priorities.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Pamela Wilson, Chief Housing Development Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Experienced, mission-aligned development partners and owners seeking to develop affordable multifamily rental housing and community development projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, rehabilitation, or new construction of affordable multifamily rental housing. Projects must promote community stability, economic mobility, and equitable development, with emphasis on production of new affordable housing and preservation of existing affordable and naturally occurring affordable housing (NOAH).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, with priority given to projects within one-mile of any WMATA Metrorail Station. Any project awarded HOME funds must meet federal Neighborhood and Site Selection standards found at 24 CFR Part 92 Section 202 (A)(B).
requirements_list: Developers must comply with the County's Diversity and Equity Policy for Publicly Subsidized Development Projects (Section 10-335 of Prince George's County Code)
Priority projects outside the NOFA timeframe must have secured necessary financing and be in a position to progress towards closing
Projects must meet all applicable Federal, State of Maryland, and Prince George's County program regulations and requirements
Federal Section 3 compliance required: 25% of total labor hours by Section 3 workers; 5% by Targeted Section 3 workers
At least 30% of Development Costs for Construction paid to County-Based Small Businesses (CBSB) and/or Locally-Owned and Operated Businesses (LOB), including at least 20% of design costs
Use Best Efforts to achieve at least 25% of Development Costs for Construction paid to County-Based Minority Business Enterprises (CMBE)
General Contractor Team must include one or more businesses that are CMBE and/or LOB
At least 25% of total construction work hours by County Residents, including at least 20% of specialty trade work hours by County Residents
Projects must maintain compliance with federal anti-discrimination laws including Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
Payment to certified businesses must be made within 45 days after satisfactory completion of work
Developer must establish and maintain records and submit quarterly compliance reports during construction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit one complete electronic application by 5PM on April 30, 2026. 2. Request access to submit via email to Karan Stewart (kastewart@co.pg.md.us) to receive a OneDrive folder link for submission. 3. Submit required documentation: Form 202 (Excel), Maryland CDA Exhibits A-E (individual PDFs), Applicant Self Scoring Table (PDF), PGC DHCD Supplemental Application (PDF), and PILOT Analysis Workbook (Excel). 4. Attend optional pre-proposal conference on April 2, 2026 at 11am EST (email kkjones@co.pg.md.us to RSVP). 5. Submit questions by email to pawilson@co.pg.md.us through April 24, 2026. 6. Applicants notified of decisions on June 1, 2026. For priority, time-sensitive projects outside the regular NOFA window, request a pre-application meeting with DHCD to discuss project details, available resources, and schedule.

structured_extraction.program_name: Pathway to Purchase Home Buyer Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A homebuying assistance program administered by Prince George's County that helps first-time homebuyers achieve homeownership through down payment and closing cost assistance, favorable loan terms, and comprehensive support services. The program assists eligible buyers purchasing for-sale, foreclosed, or owner-occupied short-sale residential properties in Prince George's County. It provides financing support and connects borrowers with participating lenders and housing counseling agencies, along with required documentation and inspection processes.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides down payment and closing cost assistance to eligible first-time homebuyers through a 0% interest deferred payment loan secured by a second deed of trust. Maximum loan amount is $50,000 for households with income at or below 80% of Area Median Income. The loan has a 10-year affordability period with a recapture schedule based on how long the borrower maintains the property as primary residence: less than 1 year (100%), 1-2 years (90%), 2-3 years (80%), 3-4 years (70%), 4-5 years (60%), 5-6 years (50%), 6-7 years (40%), 7-8 years (30%), 8-9 years (20%), 9-10 years (10%), 10+ years (0% - loan forgiven). If the loan is in default, an annual interest rate of 5.75% applies. Housing or front-end debt-to-income ratio must not exceed 35% and back-end ratio must not exceed 47%. Assistance is delivered through participating lenders coordinated with approved housing counseling agencies. Loans can be used for down payment, closing costs, and mortgage principal reduction. No cash back to purchaser at settlement. Eligible properties must pass Housing Quality Standards (HQS) inspection conducted by American Property Consultants, Inc. (initial fee $139, follow-up $65). Sellers are encouraged to contribute at least 3% toward closing costs but this is not required. Maximum purchase price is $448,000 for resale properties and $485,000 for new construction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers in Prince George's County, Maryland who meet income and other eligibility requirements, including buyers of for-sale, foreclosed, or owner-occupied short-sale residential properties. Applicants must be 18 years or older, have not owned residential property in the past 3 years, intend to live in the home as primary residence, and have household income not exceeding 80% of Area Median Income (1 person: $91,800; 2 person: $104,900; 3 person: $118,000; 4 person: $131,100; 5 person: $141,600; 6 person: $152,100; 7 person: $162,600; 8 person: $173,100).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance, closing costs, and mortgage principal reduction for the purchase of residential properties (single family dwellings, townhouses, and condominiums) in Prince George's County. Funds cannot be used for realtor commissions, homeowners warranty, creditor collections, termite treatment, radon testing/treatment, mold testing/treatment, or bond fees. Borrower cannot receive any cash back at settlement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All zip codes within Prince George's County, Maryland are eligible.
requirements_list: First-time homebuyer status (no residential property ownership in past 3 years)
Age 18 or older
Household income at or below 80% of Area Median Income
Completion of minimum 8-hour housing counseling course through HUD-certified agency (online certificates accepted)
Creditworthiness and ability to qualify for first mortgage through Certified Participating Lender
Fully amortized, fixed-rate first mortgage (FHA or Conventional; no adjustable rate or balloon payment mortgages)
Maximum housing debt-to-income ratio of 35%, maximum back-end ratio of 47%
Ratified Contract of Sale with at least 21 business days remaining (excluding federal holidays)
Property must pass Housing Quality Standards (HQS) Inspection
Property must be for-sale, foreclosed, or owner-occupied short-sale residential property
Property cannot be currently tenant-occupied
Borrower and seller affidavits required
Lead disclosure required for properties built before 1978
EEOC form completion required
Borrower identification required
Property appraisal dated within 60 days of contract with appraiser's license copy
Termite inspection report required
No minimum cash contribution required from buyer
Agree to reside in property as primary residence for 10-year affordability period
For short sales: Bank approval with at least 21 business days remaining on contract extension required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact a Pathway to Purchase Program Participating Lender and obtain pre-approval for first mortgage. 2. Attend 8-hour HUD-certified housing counseling course (in-person or online; receive Certificate of Completion). 3. Familiarize yourself with HQS Move-in Inspection Checklist at www.hudpass.com/Pathwaytopurchase. 4. Work with real estate agent to identify eligible Prince George's County properties. 5. Place contract on residential property with at least 60 days for settlement and at least 21 business days remaining after application submittal. 6. Request HQS Inspection through American Property Consultants, Inc. via www.hudpass.com (click Pathway to Purchase) or email pathwayapc@gmail.com or fax 410-586-1963. Pay $139 inspection fee via APC website. All utilities must be on. 7. Schedule property inspection and ensure all deficiencies are corrected. 8. Obtain independent home inspection (except for newly constructed properties with use and occupancy certificate). 9. Contact Participating Lender and submit file to underwriting once contract is ratified. 10. Lender obtains conditional approval for first mortgage before submitting Pathway to Purchase application. 11. Lender submits complete application package to Sandy Dixon at SVDixon@co.pg.md.us or 301-883-7327. Application must include: completed Pathway to Purchase Application and Lender Certification Form, Certificate of Completion from housing counseling, ratified Contract of Sale with all addenda, Borrower Affidavit, Lead Disclosure, Seller Affidavit, EEOC Form, copy of lender's approved credit package with conditional approval letter and documentation, income verification for all household members 18+, HUD Part 5 Income Calculation Worksheet, property appraisal, termite inspection report, proof of passed HQS inspection, and any other documentation deemed necessary. 12. Program processes applications in 21 business days (not including federal holidays) after all documents received. Applications funded on first-come, first-ready basis. 13. Complete loan documents at closing: Promissory Note, Regulatory Agreement, Declaration of Covenants, and Deed of Trust. Final title policy and hazard insurance must list Prince George's County c/o Loan Servicing UDC as second mortgagee. 14. Contact K.K. Jones (kkjones@co.pg.md.us or 301-883-6511) for questions or more information.

For residential: must be a single-family home
For multifamily: property must qualify for installation
Residential: installation must occur after July 1, 2019
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Pepco EV Smart page to learn about electric vehicle charging station incentives and apply for rebates.

structured_extraction.program_description: A year-long structured lifestyle change program for people with prediabetes or at risk for type 2 diabetes. The program helps participants lose 5 to 7% of their body weight and make lasting lifestyle changes through healthy eating and increased physical activity to prevent or delay the onset of type 2 diabetes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A fee-for-service program available as a covered benefit through Medicare, Medicaid, and participating commercial health plans and managed care organizations, allowing participants to access the program at no or low cost. The program is delivered online and includes weekly Phase 1 classes (8 weeks), bi-weekly Phase 2 classes (16 weeks), and monthly Phase 3 classes (20 weeks) led by trained lifestyle coaches.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People 18 years or older who are overweight (Body Mass Index of 25 or higher; 23 or higher for Asian-Americans) and have prediabetes or are at risk for type 2 diabetes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in structured lifestyle coaching, classes focused on healthy eating, weight loss, physical activity, and stress management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available online to participants in Prince George's County.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years or older
Must be overweight with a Body Mass Index of 25 or higher (23 or higher for Asian-Americans)
Must not have a previous diagnosis of type 1 or type 2 diabetes
Must not be currently pregnant

Must have one of the following: a prediabetes blood test result within the past 12 months (Hemoglobin A1C of 5.7-6.4, Oral Glucose Tolerance Test of 140-199 mg/dl, or Fasting Glucose Test of 100-125 mg/dl), a previous diagnosis of gestational diabetes, or a high-risk result (score of 5 or higher) on the CDC prediabetes risk test
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call (301) 856-9645 or email wellnessinfo@co.pg.md.us to register. Once registration is completed, you will receive a follow-up confirmation call or email. The online program link will be emailed to registered participants prior to the program start date.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Climate-Smart Local Producers Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program that supports farmers and food producers, particularly those of color and historically underserved communities, to implement climate-smart farming practices. The program provides funding and technical support to reduce barriers to climate-smart practice implementation on existing and new farms, develop marketing strategies for locally-grown products, and measure greenhouse gas reductions from these practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A competitive $3,250,000 five-year grant from the USDA Partnerships for Climate-Smart Commodities program. Funding supports farmers and producers to implement climate-smart farming practices including reduced tillage, cover cropping, rotational grazing, nutrient management, and other practices. Priority emphasis on historically underserved producers including beginning farmers, socially disadvantaged farmers, veteran farmers, limited resource farmers, women farmers, and minority-owned producers growing specialty crops including fruits, vegetables, and other crops. Funding covers practice implementation costs, marketing strategy development for products grown using climate-smart practices, and monitoring and analysis of greenhouse gas reductions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and food producers in Prince George's County, with emphasis on beginning farmers, socially disadvantaged farmers, veteran farmers, limited resource farmers, women farmers, and producers of specialty crops including fruits and vegetables. Priority given to farmers and producers of color and historically underserved communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of climate-smart farming practices such as reduced tillage, cover cropping, rotational grazing, and nutrient management; development and implementation of marketing strategies for products grown using climate-smart practices that emphasize local food, climate-smart practices, and woman and minority-owned farms; monitoring and analysis of greenhouse gas reductions from farming practices and supply chain impacts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a farmer or food producer in Prince George's County
Preference for historically underserved producers including beginning farmers, socially disadvantaged farmers, veteran farmers, limited resource farmers, women farmers, and specialty crop producers
Eligible commodities include fruits, vegetables, specialty crops, and a variety of other crops
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This is a pilot program under development. The page indicates to monitor the website for more information on the pilot program as it becomes available. The program is being developed in partnership with Prince George's County Government Agencies and Entities, including the Department of the Environment (DoE), Prince George's Soil Conservation District (PGSCD), Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation (EDC), Prince George's County Food Equity Council (FEC), Low Impact Development Center, Inc. (LIDC), Bowie State University, and University of Maryland Extension.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Council Domestic Violence Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to support programs offering housing, workforce development, counseling and mental health services, and advocacy and legal services to individuals impacted by domestic violence and abuse in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Prince George's County Council appropriated $500,000 in FY 2025 to fund programs that provide housing, workforce development, counseling and mental health services, and advocacy and legal services to combat domestic violence and abuse.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Providers of domestic violence support services and programs serving individuals impacted by domestic violence and abuse.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding for programs that provide housing, workforce development, counseling and mental health services, and advocacy and legal services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for the grant through the Prince George's County Council website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Homeownership Preservation Program (PG HOPP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A home rehabilitation and repair assistance program that provides financial assistance to homeowners of limited financial means for health, safety, energy efficiency, and accessibility repairs in qualified owner-occupied single-family homes in Prince George's County. The program aims to upgrade deteriorated dwellings to contemporary minimum property standards, eliminate housing code violations, and address critical repair needs. Households earning under 50% of area median income are eligible for higher assistance amounts.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $30,000 for homeowners at or above 50% of area median income. Up to $50,000 for households under 50% of area median income. Services cover roofing and gutters, electrical repair, plumbing repair, tree removal, stairlift and accessibility equipment, HVAC replacement and repair, water heater replacement and repair, and rehabilitation to bring homes to contemporary minimum property standards including the elimination of housing code violations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners of limited financial means in Prince George's County who own and occupy a single-family home and meet income and eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health, safety, energy efficiency, and accessibility repairs to owner-occupied single-family homes, including roofing, gutters, electrical repair, plumbing repair, tree removal, stairlifts, accessibility equipment, HVAC replacement and repair, water heater replacement and repair, and general rehabilitation to meet contemporary minimum property standards and eliminate housing code violations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland only
requirements_list: Must own and occupy a single-family home in Prince George's County
Must be of limited financial means
Income and eligibility requirements apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: All interested parties must submit an inquiry either via Habitat for Humanity Montgomery Metro's website or by mail. Applicants must contact Habitat for Humanity at 301-990-0014 x 19 to be placed on the inquiry list. Applications can only be forwarded to those recorded on their inquiry list.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Stormwater Stewardship Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The program funds on-the-ground restoration and program activities that improve communities and water quality while engaging County residents in the restoration and protection of local waterways. Eligible activities include water quality improvement, citizen awareness and engagement, technical assistance to churches, tree planting, environmental education, and trash reduction in the Anacostia watershed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants fund on-the-ground restoration projects and program activities including water quality improvements, citizen awareness and engagement, technical assistance to churches, tree planting, environmental education programs, and trash reduction initiatives in the Anacostia watershed. Match funding is not required but is considered favorably in the review process. Historical funding ranges from approximately $585,429 to $2,051,010 annually, with individual grant awards varying based on project scope and competitiveness.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified tax-exempt or other 501(c) nonprofit organizations, municipalities, faith-based organizations, educational institutions, community associations, civic groups, homeowners, and businesses operating in Prince George's County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Water quality improvement projects, citizen awareness and engagement activities, technical assistance to churches, tree planting, environmental education programs, and trash reduction initiatives in the Anacostia watershed. Programs must be implemented in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must be implemented in Prince George's County, Maryland, with focus on the Anacostia watershed.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a qualified tax-exempt or 501(c) nonprofit organization, municipality, faith-based organization, educational institution, community association, civic group, homeowner, or business
Activities must be located in Prince George's County

Proposals are evaluated on likelihood of project success, cost-effectiveness and appropriate budget items, consistency with the request for proposals, sustainability, justification and need, appropriate partnership support, and demonstration value and transferability
Projects with matching funds or in-kind services are preferred
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process is competitive and managed by the Chesapeake Bay Trust, a state agency established by the Maryland General Assembly in 1985. Applicants submit a proposal and application package. Funding partners and an external Technical Review Committee evaluate all applications based on: likelihood of project success, cost-effectiveness and appropriate budget items, consistency with the request for proposals, sustainability, justification, partnerships, and demonstration value and transferability. For proposals over $5,000, external peer reviewers from the Technical Review Committee provide quantitative scoring and feedback. All applicants are offered the opportunity to receive reviewer feedback.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax exemption for privately owned landing strips that are certified by the Maryland State Aviation Administration, used by the public, licensed under state transportation law, and identified as essential to Maryland's air transportation system.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax exemption is granted for the real property that serves as a private landing strip. The exemption applies to the land and improvements used exclusively for landing strip operations. To qualify, the landing strip must be certified by the Maryland State Aviation Administration, operated for public use, properly licensed, and identified in the Maryland Aviation System Plan as essential to the state's air transportation system. The exemption removes the property from the tax rolls for the assessment year in which all requirements are met.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than October 1 of the tax year exemption is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of private landing strips that meet certification and operational requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The exemption applies to the real property used as a private landing strip, including the land and any improvements directly related to landing strip operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be certified by Maryland State Aviation Administration
Landing strip must be located on privately owned land
Must be used by the public
Must be licensed under Title V of the Transportation Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland
Must be identified in the Maryland Aviation System Plan as essential to the State's air transportation system
Application and proof of eligibility must be filed with the Director of Finance by October 1 of the tax year for which exemption is sought
Must demonstrate exclusive use for landing strip operations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File application and proof of eligibility with the Director of Finance no later than October 1 of the tax year for which the exemption is sought. Documentation of Maryland State Aviation Administration certification, licensing status, and identification in the Maryland Aviation System Plan must be provided. Contact the Prince George's County Finance Department at 301-952-4030 for application materials and instructions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The PBV Program provides affordable rental housing assistance at specific private properties throughout Prince George's County. Unlike tenant-based vouchers, PBV assistance is attached to designated units at approved properties and remains with the unit if a tenant moves out.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental assistance in the form of vouchers that reduce the rent burden for eligible low-income households. The assistance is tied to specific units at participating private properties. Eligibility is based on household income, family size, and the size of the available rental unit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The waitlist closed on Tuesday, March 17, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. EST. The program is currently not accepting applications.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households seeking affordable rental housing in Prince George's County. Households cannot participate in any other federally funded housing subsidy program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance for housing at approved properties. Households must qualify based on income, family size, and unit size availability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program serves Prince George's County, Maryland. PBV units are located at 11 specific properties throughout the county including Fort Washington, Capitol Heights, Upper Marlboro, Lanham, Glenarden, Bladensburg, Riverdale, Hyattsville, District Heights, and Clinton.
requirements_list: Household income must meet eligibility standards
Family size must match available unit size
Households cannot participate in any other federally funded housing subsidy program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online through the Rent Café portal during designated application periods. Applicants are randomly selected through a lottery process. Selected applicants are notified within 45 days and must complete eligibility verification and provide required documentation. Applications are then reviewed by the property landlord/development, and if approved, sent to HAPGC for final program eligibility review. Once approved, tenants begin occupying the PBV unit.

structured_extraction.program_name: Project Based Voucher Accessibility Waiting List
structured_extraction.program_description: A separate waiting list for persons who need accessible housing units that meet their accessibility needs related to a disability. The program provides accessible units through project-based vouchers to eligible current participants and residents of HAPGC housing programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides access to accessible housing units through project-based vouchers for persons with disabilities. Rental cost is typically 30% of household adjusted gross income. Eligible applicants can apply at any time and must submit a preliminary application to the 504 Coordinator. Applications are accepted in paper form only and are dated and time stamped to establish priority placement on the waiting list. Priority is given first to current residents and participants needing accessible units who use wheelchairs or scooters, second to other residents and participants with disability-related accessibility needs, third to applicants on waiting lists with wheelchairs or scooters, and fourth to other applicants with disability-related accessibility needs. Only the head of household is eligible to apply; other household members cannot apply separately. Applicants must be current participants, residents, or applicants of HAPGC programs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - applications accepted at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current participants of the Housing Choice Voucher Program, current residents of the Public Housing Program, current participants of the Project Based Voucher Program, current participants of the Moderate Rehabilitation Program, and current applicants on HAPGC waiting lists who have accessibility needs related to a disability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to accessible housing units that meet accessibility needs due to a disability. Rental units include single-family homes, townhomes, or apartments. The subsidy stays with the building; when you move out, you no longer have the rental assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be one of the following: current participant of HAPGC Housing Choice Voucher Program, current resident of HAPGC Public Housing Program, current participant of HAPGC Project Based Voucher Program, current participant of HAPGC Moderate Rehabilitation Program, or current applicant on an HAPGC waiting list
Must have accessibility needs related to a disability (including physical, developmental, intellectual, emotional, or mental health disability)
Only head of household is eligible to apply; other household members cannot apply separately
If on a waiting list, the application holder is the eligible household member to apply
Must submit preliminary application in paper form only
Must notify Central Intake Unit in writing of any changes in address, status, or family composition; failure to respond to mailings within the notice period will result in removal from waiting list
If you accept a Project Based Voucher, you will relinquish any tenant-based voucher, moderate rehabilitation unit, or public housing unit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit a Project Based Voucher Accessibility Waiting List (PBVAWL) preliminary application in paper form. Applications can be obtained at HAPGC's office at 9200 Basil Court, Suite 107, Largo, MD 20744 or downloaded online at ha.mypgc.us. All applications are dated and time stamped to establish priority placement. Submit completed applications to: The Housing Authority of Prince George's County, 504 Coordinator, 9200 Basil Court, Room 500, Largo, MD 20774. Applications can also be submitted by mail. Reasonable accommodations are available to complete the application, including auxiliary aids or services, materials in alternative formats, or help in completing paperwork.

structured_extraction.program_description: An apprenticeship program that provides individuals with developmental or intellectual disabilities ages 18-25 with meaningful paid job training experience through placement with a Prince George's County Government agency for up to one year. Participants enhance existing skills, learn new skills, and gain on-the-job work experience, working Monday through Friday for a maximum of 8 hours per day. The program is administered by Prince George's County's Aging and Disabilities Services Division.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive paid on-the-job training and work experience through placement with a Prince George's County Government agency for up to one year, working Monday through Friday for a maximum of 8 hours per day. Compensation is provided for hours worked during the apprenticeship period.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Valerie Berkeley, Project HIRE Program Manager; Adrian Dantzler, Sr., Community Development Assistant
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with intellectual or developmental disabilities ages 18-25 who are Prince George's County residents and associated with a supportive Employment Provider Agency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid job training and work experience in a County Government agency position.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County residents only.
requirements_list: Must have a developmental and/or intellectual disability
Must be between 18 and 25 years old
Must be a Prince George's County resident
Must be associated with a supportive Employment Provider Agency
Must be available to work Monday through Friday for a maximum of 8 hours per day
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested participants should contact their supportive Employment Provider Agency, which will assist them in completing the Project HIRE application and placement process. The provider agency will work with the program to facilitate job placement and apprenticeship coordination.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Authority manages approximately 400 rental units, including 5 public housing residential sites consisting of 376 units, funded by HUD operating subsidies. The program provides safe, decent, and affordable housing to Prince George's County residents with low to moderate incomes. The Housing Authority also provides participant families with programs that encourage self-sufficiency and may potentially lead to homeownership opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides 376 public housing units at 5 residential sites funded by HUD operating subsidies. Day-to-day operations are funded through a combination of HUD operating subsidies and tenant rental revenues.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents with low to moderate incomes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental housing at public housing residential sites
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Low to moderate income

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Safety Officer Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for full-time public safety officers employed by Prince George's County or bi-county agencies, and volunteer firefighters or emergency medical technicians who meet length of service award program eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to a $2,500 property tax credit (not to exceed County taxes due) against Prince George's County property taxes for qualified homeowners who are public safety officers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time firefighters, emergency medical technicians, correctional officers, police officers, public safety dispatchers, deputy sheriffs employed by Prince George's County or bi-county agencies, and volunteer firefighters or emergency medical technicians eligible under the length of service award program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit against County taxes owed
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County
requirements_list: Must be currently employed full-time as a public safety officer by Prince George's County Government, or employed full-time predominantly in Prince George's County by a bi-county agency including M-NCPPC
Alternatively, must be a volunteer firefighter or volunteer emergency medical technician for the Prince George's County Fire/EMS Department eligible under the length of service award program
Must own residential property (principal residence) in Prince George's County
Need property tax account number from tax bill or can look it up at taxinquiry.princegeorgescountymd.gov/
No reapplication required if already determined eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Public Safety Officers employed by Prince George's County apply through the credit application portal at propertytaxcredit.princegeorgescountymd.gov/. Volunteer firefighters or emergency medical technicians eligible under the length of service award program contact Vanessa Surles. Public safety officers employed by M-NCPPC contact Donna Truitt.

structured_extraction.program_description: The PSLF Program forgives the remaining balance on Direct Loans after borrowers have made the equivalent of 120 qualifying monthly payments under an accepted repayment plan while working full-time for an eligible government or not-for-profit employer.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Remaining balance on Direct Loans is forgiven after the borrower makes 120 qualifying monthly payments under an accepted repayment plan (Income-Driven Repayment plans including SAVE, PAYE, IBR, ICR, or the 10-year Standard Repayment Plan) while employed full-time by an eligible U.S. federal, state, local, or tribal government agency, military service, or qualifying 501(c)(3) not-for-profit organization, or serving in AmeriCorps or Peace Corps. The amount forgiven equals the principal and interest due on eligible Direct Loans when the final qualifying payment is made. Payments need not be consecutive.
structured_extraction.contact_name: OHRM HR Service Team / Federal Student Aid
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals employed full-time by U.S. federal, state, local, or tribal government agencies, military personnel, qualifying 501(c)(3) not-for-profit organizations, or serving in AmeriCorps or Peace Corps positions who have Direct Student Loans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Student loan forgiveness (forgives remaining balance on Direct Loans after 120 qualifying monthly payments).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to employees of qualifying government or not-for-profit organizations throughout the United States. Federal program administered by U.S. Department of Education.
requirements_list: Be employed by a U.S. federal, state, local, or tribal government organization, a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization, a non-profit organization providing non-governmental public services, or serving in AmeriCorps or Peace Corps
Work full-time (average of 30 or more hours per week) for that organization or in that position
Have Direct Loans or consolidate other federal student loans (FFEL or Perkins) into a Direct Consolidation Loan
Repay loans under an Income-Driven Repayment plan (SAVE, PAYE, IBR, ICR) or the 10-year Standard Repayment Plan
Make a total of 120 qualifying monthly payments on or after October 1, 2007 (payments need not be consecutive)
Payments must be made in full for the month or equivalent through eligible payment alternatives
Be employed full-time by a qualifying employer when applying for forgiveness
Certify employment by submitting the PSLF Certification and Application form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the PSLF Certification and Application form through the PSLF Help Tool at StudentAid.gov/pslf (recommended for electronic submission with digital signatures) or manually by printing and submitting to the U.S. Department of Education. The application requires certification by both the borrower and an authorized official from the qualifying employer verifying employment status and period. Borrowers should certify employment annually or when changing employers. Forms can be submitted online at StudentAid.gov (My Activity section), mailed to U.S. Department of Education P.O. Box 300010 Greenville, TX 75403, or faxed to 540-212-2415. For military employment, alternative documentation (Form DD-214 or SCRA Status Report) may substitute for employer certification. For closed employers or those unable to certify, alternative documentation such as W-2 forms or paystubs can be submitted.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Rain Check Rebate Program, established by the Prince George's County Council, provides financial incentives to property owners who install approved stormwater management practices on private property to reduce stormwater runoff, improve water quality in local streams and rivers, and build climate resilience. Eligible practices include cisterns, conservation landscaping, green roofs, pavement removal, permeable pavement, rain barrels, rain gardens, and urban tree canopy enhancements. The program is administered in partnership with the Chesapeake Bay Trust and awards rebates on a first-come, first-served basis. Residential properties have a lifetime rebate ceiling of $6,000, while commercial, multi-family, nonprofit, and association properties have a $20,000 ceiling.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis for eligible stormwater management projects. Rebate amounts vary by project type: cisterns at $2 per gallon stored (250 gallon minimum); conservation landscaping at $5 per square foot (250 square foot minimum); green roofs at $10 per square foot for less than 6 inches of planting material or $20 per square foot for more than 6 inches (commercial only, residential at $10); pavement removal at $6 per square foot; permeable pavement at $12 per square foot; rain barrels at $2 per gallon stored (50 gallon minimum for residential, 100 gallon for commercial); rain gardens at $10 per square foot (100 square foot minimum); and urban tree canopy at $150 per tree (5 foot minimum height). Residential properties have a lifetime rebate ceiling of $6,000, while commercial, multi-family, nonprofit, and association properties have a $20,000 ceiling. Rebates cannot exceed the project cost. For rain barrel projects, receipt or invoice must be within 12 months of applying. For all other projects, work must be completed within 12 months of receiving pre-approval from Chesapeake Bay Trust.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; rolling program with no defined application window
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-974-2941 (Prince George's County Department of the Environment); 301-883-5927 (Chesapeake Bay Trust for applications)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners (including housing cooperatives), commercial property owners, homeowner associations, condominium associations, civic associations, multi-family dwellings, nonprofit organizations, and not-for-profit organizations in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of approved stormwater management practices including cisterns, conservation landscaping, green roofs, pavement removal, permeable pavement, rain barrels, rain gardens, and urban tree canopy enhancements to reduce stormwater runoff, improve water quality, and mitigate flooding and climate change impacts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Properties within municipalities that have their own similar stormwater management rebate programs (City of Bowie, Town of Cheverly, Town of University Park, and City of College Park) are generally excluded; however, residents of these towns may participate in cistern, green roof, pavement removal, permeable pavement, rain barrel, and rain garden programs. Focused outreach also occurs in the Tantallon area of Fort Washington through the Community Stormwater Management Blitz pilot project. Properties must be privately owned and located within Prince George's County.
requirements_list: Applicant must own the property or be a nonprofit organization with an agreement to complete a project on private or public land
Property must be privately owned and located in Prince George's County
Projects must be completed within 12 months of receiving pre-approval from Chesapeake Bay Trust (or for rain barrels, receipt or invoice must be within 12 months of applying)
Chesapeake Bay Trust must inspect and confirm the completed project complies with the original approved application and follows County best practice guidelines
If property is part of a homeowner association, applicant must provide HOA approval documentation
Applicant cannot be eligible if the project involves permit requirements for new building construction, additions, or renovations
All applicants must sign a property owner agreement; commercial and public project applicants must also sign an operations and maintenance agreement
Property cannot be located within a municipality that has a similar stormwater management rebate program (unless participating in allowed practices for those municipalities)

Trees must be planted on residential or commercial properties and be native species, at least 5 feet tall, at least 1/2 inch caliper, planted in a 5-gallon or larger container or balled and burlapped, and planted between October 1 and May 1
Applicant must install eligible stormwater management practices that meet specifications outlined in fact sheets and guidelines for each practice type
Green roofs must replace existing roof area rather than expanding original roof footprint and require a structural load analysis report from a licensed structural engineer
Green roof retrofits must meet minimum size requirement (at least 1/4 of roof area)
Rain barrels must capture at least 50 gallons for residential properties or 100 gallons for commercial properties during a rain event
Rain gardens must have a minimum size of 100 square feet
Pavement removal for commercial properties must have a minimum size of 400 square feet
Permeable pavement for commercial properties must have a minimum size of 400 square feet and appropriate soil conditions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website or by contacting Chesapeake Bay Trust directly. The application process includes: 1) Applicants submit an application with project details; 2) Chesapeake Bay Trust staff pre-approve applications before implementation (except for rain barrel projects which do not require pre-approval); 3) Applicants complete the stormwater management project according to approved specifications; 4) After project completion, applicants submit invoices and receipts to Chesapeake Bay Trust for review and approval; 5) Chesapeake Bay Trust conducts pre- and post-inspections to verify project compliance with approved design and County best practice guidelines; 6) Upon verification, rebate is issued. Rebates are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. Projects must comply with County best practice guidelines as outlined in the specific fact sheets and guidelines for each stormwater management practice.

structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit program designed to encourage revitalization and property improvements in existing communities and designated Revitalization Tax Credit Districts in Prince George's County. The program provides relief from county property taxes on the incremental assessed value created by qualified real property improvements, including construction, reconstruction, or extension of non-residential and residential structures. Tax credits phase in gradually over multiple years for both non-residential and residential properties.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Non-residential properties receive a tax credit of 100% of the increased county property tax in year 1 after improvements are completed and assessed, then declining by 20 percentage points each year through year 5 (80%, 60%, 40%, 20%). Residential properties receive 100% credit in year 1, then 66% in year 2 and 33% in year 3, with a maximum of $200,000 in eligible improvements per dwelling unit. The credit applies to county property taxes on the increased assessed value only. Eligible improvements include construction, reconstruction, or extension of non-residential structures; reconstruction or extension of existing residential structures; construction or reconstruction of new single-family residential structures on lots where a residential structure has been razed or demolished within the prior 5 years or on vacant lots between adjacent single-family residential structures; and new construction in developments of fewer than 10 one-family dwellings.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than October 1 of the tax year the property becomes eligible
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers undertaking improvements or new construction in designated Revitalization Tax Credit Districts in Prince George's County, including non-residential developers and residential property owners. County Council approval is required for developments of ten or more single-family dwellings and multifamily residential units.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits apply to qualified non-residential or residential real property improvements that increase the assessed value of the property, including construction, reconstruction, or extension of non-residential structures; reconstruction or extension of existing residential structures; construction or reconstruction of new single-family residential structures on lots where a residential structure has been razed or demolished within the prior 5 years or on vacant lots between adjacent single-family residential structures; and new construction in developments of fewer than 10 one-family dwellings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within Prince George's County, Maryland, specifically within a designated Revitalization Tax Credit District established by County ordinance. County Council approval is required for residential developments of 10 or more single-family dwellings and for multifamily units.
requirements_list: The property must be located within a Revitalization Tax Credit District established by County ordinance
The improvements must require a County building permit
Property must undergo qualified real property improvements that result in increased assessed value
Improvements must be assessed and completed before tax credit begins
Application must be made under oath on an application provided by the Director of Finance
Application must provide a legal description of the property
Proof of a properly issued Use and Occupancy permit applicable to the eligible improvements must be submitted
Such other information or documentation as the Director may require must be provided
For residential developments of ten or more single-family dwellings or multifamily units, County Council approval is required
Maximum eligible residential improvements of $200,000 per dwelling unit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File an application under oath with the Director of Finance no later than October 1 of the tax year the property becomes eligible. The application must include a legal description of the property, proof of a properly issued Use and Occupancy permit, and any other information or documentation required by the Director to determine eligibility. Contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 to speak with a Business Development Specialist for additional information on the application process and eligibility requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Religious Organizations Leased Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit on the property tax imposed on real property leased to a religious group or organization that uses the property for public worship, educational purposes, or office space to support these uses.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit is applied to the portion of leased property used by the religious organization for qualifying purposes. The credit amount is based on the property tax that would be imposed on the leased portion of the property. The property owner must be contractually obligated to reduce the tenant's property tax liability by the amount of the credit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than September 1 of the tax year for which the credit is being requested
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners leasing real property to religious groups or organizations that use the property for public worship, education, or supporting office space.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit applies to the property tax imposed on the portion of the property leased to and used by the religious organization for public worship, educational purposes, or office space necessary to support or maintain these uses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in a commercial zone in Prince George's County.
requirements_list: The religious group or organization must have verifiable tax-exempt nonprofit status from the Internal Revenue Service
The religious group or organization must qualify for a property tax exemption under Section 7-204 of the Tax-Property Article

The portion of the property upon which the tax credit is based must be used exclusively for public religious worship, educational purposes, or office space necessary to support or maintain public religious worship or educational purposes
The property must not be leased, occupied, or used for the purpose of making a profit
The religious group or organization must be contractually liable to the owner for property taxes
The property owner must be contractually obligated to reduce, by the amount of the tax credit, the amount of taxes for which the religious group or organization is otherwise contractually liable
The property must be located in a commercial zone
Application must be signed under oath by both the property owner and the religious group or organization
A copy of the executed lease must be submitted with the application
The lease must be for the exclusive use of the religious organization in the leased space
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application to the Supervisor of Assessments and Taxation no later than September 1 of the tax year for which the credit is being requested. The application must be signed under oath by both the property owner and the religious organization and must include a copy of the executed lease agreement. Upon termination of the lease or cessation of possession by the tenant, the owner must notify the Supervisor of Assessments and Taxation within 30 days. Contact the Prince George's County Finance Department or Supervisor of Assessments and Taxation at 301-952-4030 for application forms and additional information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County applies a school facilities surcharge to new residential developments or redevelopments to cover anticipated increases in public educational services required to accommodate new residents. This program provides reductions and exemptions from that surcharge for eligible projects. A 50% reduction applies to multifamily properties located within one-quarter mile of a metro station, within the Bowie MARC Station Community Center Designation Area, or within an approved Transit District Overlay Zone. Full exemptions apply to studio and efficiency apartments located within one-quarter mile of a metro station or within an approved Transit District Overlay Zone.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The school facilities surcharge is reduced by 50% for multifamily properties within one-quarter mile of a metro station, within the Bowie MARC Station Community Center Designation Area, or within an approved Transit District Overlay Zone. Specifically, the surcharge is reduced from $15,489 per unit to $7,745 per unit outside the Capital Beltway, or from $9,035 per unit to $4,518 per unit inside the Capital Beltway or within a site plan that abuts an existing or planned WMATA mass transit rail station. Studio apartments and efficiency apartments located within one-quarter mile of a metro station or within an approved Transit District Overlay Zone receive a full exemption (100% waiver) from the school facilities surcharge.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers of new residential properties and redevelopments in Prince George's County, including multifamily housing developers and developers of studio or efficiency apartment units.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction or full exemption from school facilities surcharge fees owed on new residential developments or redevelopments, reducing the per-unit fee developers must pay toward public educational services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Specifically, properties within one-quarter mile of a metro station, within the Bowie MARC Station Community Center Designation Area, or within an approved Transit District Overlay Zone qualify for the 50% reduction. Studio and efficiency apartments within one-quarter mile of a metro station or within an approved Transit District Overlay Zone qualify for a full exemption.
requirements_list: Property must be a new residential development or redevelopment located in Prince George's County

For 50% surcharge reduction: property must be multifamily residential and located within one-quarter mile of a metro station, within the Bowie MARC Station Community Center Designation Area, or within an approved Transit District Overlay Zone

For full exemption: dwelling units must be studio apartments or efficiency apartments and the property must be located within one-quarter mile of a metro station or within an approved Transit District Overlay Zone

structured_extraction.program_name: Solarize Prince George's – Solar Energy Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A County-led campaign and grant program that makes going solar easier and more affordable for Prince George's County residents. The program connects residents with vetted solar installers and provides direct financial assistance on a first-come, first-served basis to help make rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) system installation affordable and accessible. Residents who are Pepco customers living in an Energy Resiliency Community (ERC) receive a higher grant amount ($10,000), while all other eligible homeowners receive a standard grant ($5,000).
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of $10,000 for Pepco customers living in an Energy Resiliency Community (ERC), or $5,000 for all other homeowners installing new rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. Funds are available on a first-come, first-served basis. Eligible costs include any parts, components, or accessory equipment necessary to operate and install solar systems. A maximum of 20% of the grant award can be spent on ancillary costs such as tree trimming, service panel upgrades, roof repairs, and mold remediation. The program connects residents with vetted solar installers through the Maryland Solar Access Program's Participating Contractor List. Grant payment is reimbursement-based; payment is only issued after all requested documents have been properly submitted.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis from November 10, 2025, to February 27, 2026. The deadline may be extended, but awards are limited, so early submission is strongly encouraged.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Prince George's County Government, Department of the Environment, Climate and Energy Division - Sustainable Energy
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents who own single-family residences and want to install new rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. Pepco customers residing in designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs) receive priority with higher grant amounts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financing to help make solar photovoltaic (PV) installation an affordable option for eligible homeowners. Funds cover costs associated with new rooftop solar PV system installation, including system components, equipment, and accessories. Up to 20% of the grant can be used for ancillary costs such as tree trimming, service panel upgrades, roof repairs, and mold remediation if approved by DoE staff.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Prince George's County residents. Pepco customers residing in the following Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs) are eligible for the higher $10,000 grant amount: Bladensburg - East Riverdale; Forestville; Hillcrest Heights - Marlow Heights; Kentland - Palmer Park; Oxon Hill – Glassmanor; Silver Hill; Suitland - Coral Hills; and Woodlawn– Lanham. Use the ERC Address Locator (http://bit.ly/ERClocator) to confirm eligibility.
requirements_list: Be a Prince George's County resident who has not previously received a Solar Energy Grant from Prince George's County
Live in a single-family residence as verified through MD SDAT Real Property Data Search (may include a dwelling unit within a townhouse where the applicant owns the roof)
Not already own a rooftop solar system; grant is exclusively for new solar PV system installation
Own the solar PV system through cash purchase, loan, or financing (third-party owned systems through lease or Power Purchase Agreement are ineligible)
Systems must be installed by contractors listed on the Maryland Solar Access Program's Participating Contractor List
Contractors must be properly licensed in Maryland (MHIC license, master electrician license, and NABCEP PVIP Certification required)
Contractors must be registered as vendors with Prince George's County
Solar PV systems must be at least 2 kW DC and designed to meet Minimum Benefit Requirements
All major system components must be new; equipment and hardware must meet current and applicable federal, state, and local regulations
Solar PV systems must produce at least 800 kWh per year per installed kW
Prequalification notice must be received before installation begins; systems installed prior to receiving prequalification do not qualify
Installation must be completed within 6 months of receiving prequalification approval
Final invoices must show job completion date
Proof of utility interconnection and Permission to Operate letter required
Proof of all necessary permits and third-party inspection sticker required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1 – Scan for Eligibility: Review eligibility requirements and determine if you qualify based on residency, property type, and lack of existing solar system. Step 2 – Obtain Financial Assistance: Determine your grant amount ($10,000 for Pepco customers in ERCs or $5,000 for others) and identify financing options. Step 3 – Look for an Eligible Solar Contractor: Select a contractor from the Maryland Solar Access Program Participating Contractor List. Ensure the contractor is a registered Prince George's County vendor, holds required Maryland licenses and certifications (MHIC, master electrician, NABCEP PVIP), and can meet all quality assurance requirements. Step 4 – Apply for Prequalification (before installation): Working with your contractor, gather and submit required prequalification documents via email to CleanE@co.pg.md.us or by mail/hand-delivery: completed grant application with signed Grant Award Terms and Conditions Agreement and Affidavit of Income, recent electricity bill (within 3 months, PDF format), final invoice using the County template, IRS Form W-9, contractor qualifications and certifications, detailed solar PV analysis showing projected energy savings and system specifications, pre-installation photos, signed contract between homeowner and contractor with itemized quote, and proof of financing if applicable. Alternatively, homeowners with MEA MSAP Reservation of Funds can submit MSAP application documents. Expected prequalification timeline: approximately 30 business days upon successful review of complete application. Note: Handwritten or digital signatures required on all documents; typed names not accepted. Step 5 – Receive Grant Funds (after installation): After installation completion, submit final documentation including updated final invoice if equipment changed, utility Permission to Operate letter and interconnection agreement, proof of all necessary permits and third-party inspection sticker, close-out documents (commissioning checklist, owner's manual, warranty proofs, as-built drawings), installation photos, proof of Maryland PSC system registration, proof of one month of solar generation, completed survey with feedback, and Authorization for Electronic Funds Disbursement form if applicable. Grant payment will only be issued upon receipt of all properly submitted documents. Final approval expected within 15 business days of invoice receipt, followed by County staff site visit verification. Payment processing expected within 30-60 business days after approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Summer Youth Enrichment Program (SYEP) provides enriching and constructive summer work experiences for youth and young adults ages 14 to 24 living in Prince George's County. Participants gain paid employment opportunities from July through August in community organizations, private sector companies, and government agencies, paired with developmental training and employment skills building. The program offers various tracks including job readiness training, industry-specific training (aviation, electrical, hospitality, digital marketing, help desk technology), and career exploration opportunities. Host employers hire youth directly or serve as designated worksites. The program also welcomes sponsorship partners who may contribute to Capstone Sponsorships (funding program curriculum, workforce training and transportation) or Student Sponsorships (funding individual students to be fully employed at nonprofit locations).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive paid summer employment from July through August with hourly wage rates: ages 14-15 receive training stipends of $300 (upon completing 75% of required course), ages 16-17 earn $13.00/hour (maximum 32 hours/week) or $400 stipend, and ages 18-24 earn $15.00/hour (maximum 40 hours/week) or $500 stipend. All hourly participants have FICA taxes withheld. Payments are made via direct deposit (or paper check mailed if no direct deposit provided). Program provides transportation subsidies, technology access to close the digital divide, job readiness training, professional development, career exposure, and employment skills building through various training programs offered by partner organizations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Host/Sponsor Partner Survey deadline: January 30, 2026; Youth participant applications: March 1-31, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth and young adults ages 14 to 24 living in Prince George's County seeking summer employment and career development; organizations (non-profit, for-profit, government) seeking to serve as host employers or sponsorship partners; community organizations seeking to contribute to youth employment funding through Capstone or Student Sponsorships.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Summer employment wages for youth participants (hourly or stipend-based); transportation subsidies; technology access to close the digital divide; work opportunities for additional youth participants; developmental training and employment skills building; job readiness training; professional development opportunities; career exploration; workforce training curriculum.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Youth must be Prince George's County residents. Organizations can be located anywhere but must employ or partner with Prince George's County youth.
requirements_list: Age 14 to 24 by July 1 (for youth participants)
Prince George's County resident (for youth participants)
Legally eligible to work in the United States (for youth participants)
Host employers must complete the 2026 SYEP Partner Participation Survey by January 30, 2026

Organizations must have Certificate of Insurance with Commercial General Liability Insurance ($1,000,000 per occurrence including sexual abuse and child molestation coverage), Commercial Auto Liability Insurance ($1,000,000 per occurrence), and Workers' Compensation and Employers' Liability Insurance (Maryland Statutory Benefits)
Nonprofit and government partners must execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU); corporate partners must execute a Referral Agreement
Organizations must provide IRS Form W-9
Organizations must have Personnel Policy addressing Sexual Harassment and Workplace Disturbances
For nonprofits, Prince George's County Government must be listed as additional insured on General Liability policy

For stipend programs: must complete 75% of required course to receive stipend; no partial stipends; all assignments and projects must be completed; must report to work and sign in with legal name; must make self visible during working hours, on-site or virtual meetings, or training; no credit given if not identifying with full first and last name on virtual platforms; all absences must be approved in advance by supervisor

For hourly participants: must not work over maximum weekly hours (32 hours for ages 16-17; 40 hours for ages 18-24); must sign in with supervisor; must make self visible during working hours and meetings; ages 14-17 cannot operate power tools or participate in certain forestry activities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Youth applicants should apply during the open application period from March 1 to March 31, 2026. Contact Human Resources Management at ohrm@co.pg.md.us or 301-883-6330 for youth application details. Applications are sorted by job interest and randomized; candidates are selected from randomized lists until all positions are filled. Selected candidates receive job offers and participate in onboarding April 21-June 30. Onboarding requires completion of W-4, MW507, I-9 Eligibility to Work Verification, Work Permit for Minors (ages 14-17), Workplace Harassment Avoidance Training video and acknowledgment, Code of Conduct Acknowledgement, and Direct Deposit or US Bank Card forms. In-person I-9 verification is conducted in advance. All required paperwork must be submitted by the due date or candidate forfeits job opportunity. Organizations interested in becoming host employers or sponsorship partners should email SYEPPartners@co.pg.md.us to make an inquiry and complete the 2026 SYEP Partner Participation Survey by January 30, 2026. Selected organizations will execute appropriate agreements (Referral Agreement for corporate partners, MOU for nonprofits and government entities) and provide required documentation including Certificate of Insurance, IRS Form W-9, and Personnel Policy. Sponsorship partners can choose Capstone Sponsorship levels ($100,000, $50,000, $25,000, $10,000, $5,000 or other amount) or Student Sponsorship levels (Fulfilling the Promise Partner $5,000 per youth age 16-22; Prince George's Pride Partner $3,500 per youth age 14-15; Transportation Partner $1,500 per youth for transportation support). Submit completed sponsorship form with check payable to 'SYEP Prince George's County' with 'Youth Jobs Fund' in memo line to: Community Foundation, 8181 Professional Place, Landover, MD 20785.

structured_extraction.program_description: A mechanism that helps fund public improvements related to economic development by issuing bonds to pay for infrastructure such as roads, parking, stormwater management, and other public improvements. The county delineates a project area and declares a base year; the base year's assessed valuation is taxed as before, while tax revenues from the incremental increase in assessed value above the base year attributable to new development are remitted to a special fund and used to pay debt service for identified public improvements. Projects within pre-designated TIF Districts have increased certainty of approval, though exact terms must be negotiated with the county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county delineates a project area and declares a base year. The base year's assessed valuation is taxed as before. Tax revenues from any incrementally higher assessed value above the base that is attributable to the new project are remitted to a special fund and used to pay debt service for identified improvements such as roads, parking, and stormwater management. The county issues bonds to finance these public infrastructure improvements, and projects within pre-designated TIF Districts have increased certainty of approval. Exact terms must be negotiated with the county.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and redevelopment projects within designated TIF Districts in Prince George's County that will create additional tax revenues for the county.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public improvements and infrastructure related to economic development, including parking facilities, roadways, stormwater management, and other public infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Pre-designated TIF Districts within Prince George's County that have been pre-qualified and designated as eligible for TIF financing.
requirements_list: Project must be located within a pre-designated TIF District
Development or redevelopment project must create additional tax revenues for the county
Project applicants must negotiate exact terms with the county
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 and ask to speak with a Business Development Specialist to discuss eligibility, confirm the project is within a designated TIF District, and negotiate the exact terms for the TIF bond.
