structured_extraction.program_description: Funds community groups, municipalities, libraries, and homeowner associations to plant native trees and shrubs in public or common areas to support reforestation and green space initiatives in Prince George's County. Provides landscape funding awarded to eligible organizations for tree planting projects that increase native tree canopy, improve air and water quality, enhance wildlife habitat, conserve energy, and reduce stormwater runoff.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided on a reimbursement basis with a 50 percent match requirement. Civic, neighborhood, community and homeowner associations and libraries may receive grants not to exceed $5,000 per year. Municipalities can apply for grants up to $10,000 per year. Eligible expenses include trees, shrubs, soil preparation, protective fencing, and mulch. Costs per plant including soil amendment, gator bags, and other expenditures cannot exceed $150 for a 5-foot tall/5-gallon tree. For larger stock, consult program manager for allowable cost. Trees must be at least 5 feet tall and planted in a 5-gallon or larger container or balled and burlapped. The 50 percent match can be provided as cash or in-kind contributions (goods, services, or volunteer time valued at $25/hour). Funds are disbursed after project completion upon submission of receipts and proof of payment, consistent with the approved grant agreement. Funds are available on a first-come basis, subject to availability of County funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a continuous basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Civic, neighborhood, community, and homeowner associations, local municipalities, and libraries in Prince George's County seeking to improve tree cover and green space through native tree planting projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Native tree and shrub plantings in public or private common areas, including parks, playgrounds, memorial and street tree plantings, and reforestation projects along streams. Eligible expenses include plant material, tree protectors and gator bags, site preparation costs (soil amendment and invasive plant removal), planting costs, protective fencing, and mulch. Volunteer time and in-kind donations of goods and services can be used toward the required 50 percent match.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County. Trees must be planted on community-owned land or property where the landowner has authorized the planting. Homeowner associations must provide proof of ownership.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a civic, neighborhood, community, or homeowner association, local municipality, or library located in Prince George's County
Projects must involve planting native trees and shrubs in public or common areas
Trees must be at least 5 feet tall and planted in a 5-gallon or larger container or balled and burlapped
Trees must be planted between October 1 and May 1
A 50 percent match (cash or in-kind) must be provided by the applicant for every grant dollar received
Written cost estimates signed by authorized representatives of landscape nurseries must be submitted; estimates should include a one-year guarantee on all trees
MISS UTILITY must be contacted prior to planting to locate underground utilities
A maintenance plan must be developed and implemented for a minimum of two years, including watering, pruning, tree wrap removal, and dead tree replacement
Landowner authorization/signature is required; homeowner associations must provide proof of ownership
Any permits necessary for the project are the responsibility of the applicant
Receipts and proof of payment must be provided for reimbursement
County staff must be allowed to inspect plantings and assess tree survivability within one year of planting and then every three years thereafter
Applicants are strongly encouraged to use the PGCTreeTRAK app to document tree locations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit the Intent to Apply form to initiate the process. 2. The Department of Environment program coordinator will contact the applicant to arrange a consultation to discuss the program and application process. 3. Complete the Tree ReLEAF Grant Application form with all required information including project summary, maintenance plan, cost estimates from landscape nurseries, itemized budget, volunteer hours (if applicable), and overall budget showing the 50 percent match. 4. Submit one copy of the completed grant application and all supporting materials (vicinity map, planting diagram, cost estimates, maintenance plan, volunteer documentation) to the Department of Environment, Sustainability Division, 1801 McCormick Drive, Suite 500, Largo, Maryland 20774, ATTN: Carole Barth, or email to cabarth@co.pg.md.us. 5. Prior to starting the project, enter into a grant award agreement with the Department of Environment. 6. Upon project completion, submit receipts and proof of payment to receive reimbursement up to the approved grant amount. Applications are evaluated for eligibility and allocation of funds on a continuous basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Truancy & Absenteeism Reduction Program (R.I.S.E. Truancy Initiative)
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive community-based program administered by Prince George's County that funds community-based partners to design and deliver services that reduce student truancy and chronic absenteeism for youth ages 12-18. The program addresses both immediate barriers to attendance and underlying causes of absenteeism through academic mentoring, family engagement, behavioral enrichment, wraparound services, culturally responsive interventions, technology solutions, and re-engagement strategies. It also aims to reduce juvenile delinquency by providing youth services, increasing parental engagement, and offering holistic family-centered supports. A $963,000 grant was secured to launch the initiative, with up to $730,000 distributed across three funding categories: Wraparound Services, Targeted Workshops, and Transportation & Outreach.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $730,000 in total funding distributed across three categories: Wraparound Services ($500,000), Targeted Workshops ($190,000), and Transportation & Outreach ($40,000). Additionally, a $963,000 grant was secured to launch the broader R.I.S.E. Truancy Initiative. The Office of the State's Attorney may fund multiple partners across categories based on need, capacity, and alignment with program goals.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sonja Welborne-Rice, Director of Community Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, community-based organizations, coalitions, and qualified service providers with relevant experience serving Prince George's County youth ages 12-18 and their families, particularly those experiencing truancy and chronic absenteeism, with a track record of delivering evidence-based and culturally responsive practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding can be used for academic mentoring and peer support, family engagement and outreach, behavioral enrichment for students and parents, wraparound services including workforce development and mental health support, culturally responsive interventions, technology solutions for attendance tracking and data analytics, re-engagement strategies for at-risk youth, youth services, parental engagement programming, and holistic family-centered supports to reduce juvenile delinquency and school truancy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County only.
requirements_list: Nonprofit organizations, community-based organizations, coalitions, or qualified service providers
Proven, evidence-based, and culturally responsive strategies
Demonstrated track record of working effectively with at-risk youth and their families
Experience collaborating with schools and community partners
Ability to deliver holistic, proactive approaches that measurably improve attendance
Ability to collect and report data on outcomes
Relevant experience and capacity to serve Prince George's County youth ages 12-18
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prepare a single PDF Expression of Interest (EOI) and supporting materials as separate files. Email the submission to communitysao@co.pg.md.us with the subject line 'SAO-PGC Truancy and Absenteeism Reduction Program – EOI Submission' by the deadline. The Office of the State's Attorney will review submissions post-deadline and notify selected partners.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free tax preparation and electronic filing services provided by IRS-certified volunteers for qualifying residents. The program helps eligible individuals prepare and file their federal income tax returns at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free tax preparation and electronic filing of federal income tax returns completed by IRS-certified volunteer tax preparers at no cost to eligible filers. Services include filing with both the IRS and Maryland. Returns are electronically filed. Services are provided in person at the Family Investment Division office (4235 28th Avenue, Temple Hills, MD 20748) on Wednesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays from 10 A.M. to 2 P.M. Tax refunds do not affect eligibility for benefits like SNAP and Temporary Cash Assistance.

Must be a Prince George's County resident
Appointment required
Must have all tax documents before scheduling appointment
Must bring Social Security card for everyone on the return
Must bring photo ID for taxpayer and spouse if filing jointly
Must bring bank account information for direct deposit to receive faster refund
Must bring W-2 forms and other income documents for 2024
Must bring applicable tax forms such as 1099-G, 1099-MISC, 1099-NEC, 1099-K, W-2G, 1099-INT/DIV
Must bring Form 1095-A if healthcare was purchased through marketplace
Must bring Forms 1098, 1098-E, 1098-T if issued

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 301-316-7900 to schedule a tax preparation appointment. You must have all of your tax documents before scheduling. Bring all required documents to your appointment for IRS-certified volunteers to prepare and electronically file your return with both the IRS and Maryland at no cost. For a complete list of tax situations covered by the program, visit https://bit.ly/VITAscope

structured_extraction.program_name: Disabled Emergency Worker Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Queen Anne's County program that provides property tax credit to emergency workers who are permanently and totally disabled in the line of duty.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit for permanently and totally disabled emergency workers (law enforcement officers, fire, rescue, or emergency medical service personnel) who became disabled in the line of duty. The credit applies to the assessed value of the primary residence of the disabled worker. For surviving spouses of fallen emergency workers, a similar property tax credit is available. The tax credit is applied annually to reduce the property tax bill for eligible applicants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Certificate of Service and Retirement Statement must be filed prior to June 15 of the taxable year for which the credit is requested to begin. Annual Eligibility Certification must be submitted each year to continue receiving the credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Permanently and totally disabled emergency workers (law enforcement, fire, rescue, emergency medical service personnel) and surviving spouses of fallen emergency workers in Queen Anne's County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax reduction on primary residence
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Queen Anne's County, Maryland only
requirements_list: For disabled workers: Must be permanently and totally disabled as a result of injury or occupational illness sustained in the line of duty prior to June 15 of the taxable year for which the credit is requested
For disabled workers: Must be or have been employed by a law enforcement agency, fire department, rescue squad, or emergency medical service provider in Queen Anne's County

For disabled workers: Must submit Certificate of Service from employer (police chief, fire chief, or HR representative) and Retirement Statement, Notice of Retirement Allowance, or Letter from State Retirement Agency prior to June 15
For surviving spouses: Must provide death certificate of emergency worker who died in the line of duty prior to June 15 of the taxable year for which the credit is requested
For surviving spouses: The emergency worker must have been employed by a law enforcement agency, fire department, rescue squad, or emergency medical service provider in Queen Anne's County
Must own and occupy the property as primary residence in Queen Anne's County
Must file initial application before June 15 of the taxable year to begin receiving the credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain Application form (for either disabled worker or surviving spouse of fallen emergency worker) from Queen Anne's County Tax Assessor or download from county website. 2. Complete the application form with personal and employment information. 3. Obtain Certificate of Service from your employer's chief or HR representative documenting your service and disability/death status. 4. Compile required documentation: For disabled workers - Retirement Statement, Notice of Retirement Allowance, or Letter from State Retirement Agency showing permanent and total disability. For surviving spouses - Death Certificate and proof of the worker's emergency service employment. 5. Submit completed application, Certificate of Service, and supporting documentation to Queen Anne's County Tax Assessor by June 15 of the taxable year for which you wish to receive the credit. 6. Submit Annual Eligibility Certification each subsequent year by June 15 to maintain the credit. Property tax assessment will reflect the credit on the tax bill.

Must submit Certificate of Service from the emergency worker's employer (chief or HR representative)
Surviving spouse must remain unmarried to continue receiving the credit
Must own property in Queen Anne's County, Maryland
Annual Eligibility Certification must be submitted each year to continue receiving the credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain Certificate of Service from the deceased emergency worker's employer (chief or HR representative). 2. Complete the Application for Surviving Spouse of Fallen Emergency Worker form. 3. Submit the application along with the original or certified copy of the death certificate and the Certificate of Service to Queen Anne's County prior to June 15 of the taxable year for which the credit is requested. 4. Submit Annual Eligibility Certification each subsequent year by June 15 to continue receiving the credit. Applications and forms are available from the Queen Anne's County Tax Assessor's office.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to local governments, non-profit animal welfare organizations, and individual pet owners to offer or access free or reduced-cost spay and neuter services for cats and dogs. Administered locally through Queen Anne's County Animal Services, the program aims to reduce the number of animals surrendered to and euthanized in shelters across Maryland by helping low-income residents afford these veterinary services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided to local governments and non-profit animal welfare organizations to deliver free or reduced-cost spay and neuter services to eligible residents. Individual pet owners can also apply for grants to help offset the cost of spay and neuter veterinary services for their cats or dogs. The program aims to make these essential veterinary services accessible to low-income households.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis - applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income residents of Queen Anne's County with household income under $60,000 annually who own cats or dogs, as well as local governments and non-profit animal welfare organizations serving Queen Anne's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free or reduced-cost spay and neuter services for cats and dogs owned by eligible residents. Funds support veterinary services to help reduce animal overpopulation in shelters.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live or operate within Queen Anne's County, Maryland. Services are administered through Queen Anne's County Animal Services, located at 201 Clay Drive, Queenstown, MD 21158.
requirements_list: Annual household income under $60,000
Resident of Queen Anne's County, Maryland
Own a cat or dog
Must complete the Maryland Spay/Neuter Grant Application with required documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Maryland Spay/Neuter Grant Application form available online through SeamlessDocs or the Queen Anne's County website. Submit the completed application along with required supporting documents to Queen Anne's County Animal Services. Applicants will be contacted to schedule their spay or neuter appointment. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and can be submitted at any time.

structured_extraction.program_description: Queen Anne's County provides grants to outside agencies through an annual grant application process managed by the Budget Section.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Queen Anne's County awards annual grants to eligible outside agencies. Grant amounts and specific funding levels are determined through the annual budget process. Grants must be used in accordance with the Outside Agency Grant Program Policies and Procedures. Eligible agencies may apply for funding to support their operations and programs that serve Queen Anne's County residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit outside agencies and organizations seeking funding from Queen Anne's County to support operations and community programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Agencies may use grant funds to support their operations and programs that serve Queen Anne's County residents, subject to compliance with the Outside Agency Grant Program Policies and Procedures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Queen Anne's County. Grants support agencies serving Queen Anne's County residents.
requirements_list: Agencies must be non-profit organizations
Agencies must submit the FY27 Outside Agency Grant Application with all required documentation
Agencies must comply with Queen Anne's County Outside Agency Grant Program Policies and Procedures
Agencies must demonstrate how their programs serve Queen Anne's County residents
Agencies must meet all eligibility criteria outlined in the program policies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested outside agencies must complete the FY27 Outside Agency Grant Application form according to the program's policies and procedures. Applications should include all required documentation and information demonstrating how the agency's programs serve Queen Anne's County. The County Budget Section manages the application review process, and grant awards are determined through the annual budget process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program established to support clean energy initiatives in Queen Anne's County, Maryland. The program provides financing for residential and commercial clean energy projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides loans to finance clean energy projects for residential and commercial properties. Eligible projects include solar photovoltaic systems, solar thermal systems, geothermal heat pump systems, wind energy systems, energy storage systems, and other renewable energy technologies. The specific loan terms, interest rates, maximum loan amounts, and repayment periods are determined by the county and may vary based on project type and applicant qualifications.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential and commercial property owners in Queen Anne's County seeking to finance clean energy projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Clean energy projects including solar photovoltaic systems, solar thermal systems, geothermal heat pump systems, wind energy systems, energy storage systems, and other renewable energy technologies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Queen Anne's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be located in Queen Anne's County
Applicant must own or have authority over the property
Project must involve eligible clean energy technology
Applicant must meet creditworthiness requirements established by the county
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should contact Queen Anne's County for specific application procedures, loan application forms, and current program details. The county reviews applications based on project eligibility, applicant creditworthiness, and available funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: A litter-reduction campaign that invites volunteer groups to adopt and maintain segments of county roadways by removing litter at least twice per year over a two-year period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides no financial cost to participate. Volunteers receive support from the Department of Public Works and work in partnership with the Roads Division to remove litter from adopted road segments. The county provides program coordination, materials for tracking cleanup efforts, recognition of volunteers, and technical assistance in identifying appropriate road segments for adoption.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, service organizations, businesses, families, non-profits, and homeowner associations interested in volunteering to reduce litter along Queen Anne's County roads.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Volunteer labor to remove litter and debris from adopted road segments. Participants commit to maintaining assigned road segments by removing litter at least twice per year.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Queen Anne's County local and neighborhood roads. Specific road segments available for adoption can be confirmed by contacting the Adopt-A-Road Coordinator at the Department of Public Works, Roads Division.
requirements_list: Must be an individual, service organization, business, family, non-profit, or homeowner association
Must commit to picking up litter from an adopted road segment at least twice per year
Must maintain the commitment for two consecutive years
Participation in countywide cleanup events counts towards the yearly requirement
Must complete the Adopt-A-Road Agreement Form
Must consult with the Adopt-A-Road Coordinator to identify available road segments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Queen Anne's County Department of Public Works at 410-758-0920, ext. 4125 to request an application or download the Adopt-A-Road Agreement Form. Complete the agreement form with your organization's information and commitment details. Mail the completed form to the Adopt-A-Road Coordinator at the Department of Public Works, Roads Division, 312 Safety Drive, Centreville, MD 21617. Consult with R. Shane Moore, P.E. to identify available road segments for adoption and receive assignment confirmation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Retired or Disabled Veterans' Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A Queen Anne's County program that provides a property tax credit to retired or disabled veterans and unmarried spouses of deceased retired or disabled veterans on their principal dwelling.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit equal to 20% of County Property Tax. The credit commences on July 1 following approval of the application. Credit continues for subsequent years by annual eligibility certification.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be received by June 15th to apply to the upcoming tax year
structured_extraction.contact_name: Queen Anne's County Department of Budget & Finance
structured_extraction.program_audience: Retired or disabled veterans and unmarried spouses of deceased retired or disabled veterans
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax reduction on principal dwelling
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Queen Anne's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be a retired or disabled veteran or unmarried spouse of a deceased retired or disabled veteran
Must own and occupy principal dwelling in Queen Anne's County
Must file evidence of eligibility with Queen Anne's County Department of Budget & Finance
Annual Eligibility Certification required to continue credit in subsequent years
Veteran must have served on active duty and been honorably discharged
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application for Retired or Disabled Veteran form and submit an Application Letter to Queen Anne's County Department of Budget & Finance by June 15. Submit required documentation including evidence of veteran status and ownership of principal dwelling. Submit Annual Eligibility Certification each year to continue receiving the credit in subsequent years. Applications are processed and approved applicants receive the tax credit commencing July 1.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Queen Anne's County program that allows people over 65 years old to defer county property tax increases for payment at a later date with interest.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Allows eligible seniors to defer county property tax increases. The deferred amount accrues interest and becomes due upon sale of the property, transfer of ownership, or death of the homeowner. This program provides relief for property owners over 65 who wish to defer payment of property tax increases while remaining in their homes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents over 65 years of age who own residential property in Queen Anne's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deferral of property tax increases on residential property
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Queen Anne's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be 65 years of age or older
Applicant must own and occupy the property as their principal residence
Must have lived in the dwelling for at least 5 years
Property must be residential in nature
Application must be submitted by June 1 annually
Applicant must meet income requirements as specified in program guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Tax Deferral Application form and submit it to Queen Anne's County by June 1 each year. The application must include proof of age, proof of residency, property ownership documentation, and income verification. Refer to the application form and program guidelines for complete details on required documentation and submission procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program for volunteer fire and EMS department members in Queen Anne's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit available to qualifying volunteer fire and EMS department members. The amount of the credit is based on a points system that evaluates factors such as years of service, hours volunteered, and certifications held. Points are calculated using the QAC Points System, and applicants must have a minimum qualifying score to receive the credit. The property tax credit is applied annually to the applicant's property tax bill for their primary residence in Queen Anne's County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Volunteer fire and EMS department members in Queen Anne's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit applied to county property taxes on primary residence
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Queen Anne's County, Maryland. Applicants must own property and reside in Queen Anne's County to be eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a current member of a volunteer fire or EMS department operating in Queen Anne's County
Must own property in Queen Anne's County
Primary residence must be located in Queen Anne's County
Must meet minimum points threshold established by QAC Points System based on years of service, hours volunteered, and certifications
Must submit completed 2026 QAC VFD Property Tax Credit Application form annually
Must provide documentation of volunteer service and certifications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the QAC Points System documentation to understand how points are calculated. 2. Gather required documentation including proof of service, volunteer hours, and certifications through SDAT and MdLandRec.net. 3. Complete the 2026 QAC VFD Property Tax Credit Application form. 4. Submit application to Fire and EMS Commission via the specified method. 5. Commission reviews application and verifies eligibility using points system. 6. Approved applicants receive property tax credit applied to their annual county property tax bill.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program providing subsidies to help low-income households afford Internet service by reducing their monthly broadband bills. Through providers such as Comcast Xfinity, eligible low-income households receive a monthly credit towards Internet and mobile services. Qualified households on Tribal lands receive an enhanced benefit amount.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-income households receive a monthly credit of up to $30 towards Internet and Xfinity mobile services. Qualified households within Tribal lands receive up to $75 per month. Internet Essentials service includes: Internet Essentials (50/10 Mbps at $9.95/month + tax, reduced to $0 with ACP credit) or Internet Essentials Plus (100/10 Mbps at $29.95/month + tax, reduced to $0 with ACP credit). Both tiers include free equipment (Gateway) rental. Xfinity Mobile service also available with unlimited plans starting at $45 per line per month or by-the-gig plans starting at $15/month. If a customer has both Internet and Xfinity Mobile service, the ACP benefit is first applied to Internet, with any balance applied to Xfinity Mobile.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households and individuals receiving qualifying benefits seeking affordable Internet service in Somerset County. Must be 18 years of age or older.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly broadband service costs, Internet service, or Xfinity mobile services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Somerset County, Maryland, and nationwide through the FCC program. Enhanced benefit available on Tribal lands. Service must be available in the applicant's Comcast service area.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years of age or older
Recipient of National School Lunch Program benefits
Recipient of SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) benefits
Recipient of Medicaid benefits
Recipient of Federal Public Housing Assistance
Recipient of Lifeline program benefits
Recipient of Federal Pell Grants
Recipient of WIC (Women, Infants, and Children) benefits
Recipient of SSI (Supplemental Security Income)
Or recipient of other qualifying benefit programs
Live in an area where Comcast Internet service is available
Have not had Comcast Internet within the last 90 days (waived for ACP enrollees)
Have no outstanding debt to Comcast that is less than one year old (waived for ACP enrollees)
Applicants can verify eligibility through the National Verifier by visiting acpbenefit.org or calling 833-511-0311
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Check ACP eligibility through the National Verifier. Visit acpbenefit.org or call 833-511-0311 to complete the National Verifier form and receive an Application ID. Step 2: Apply for Internet Essentials service. Visit InternetEssentials.com or call 855-8-INTERNET (1-855-846-8376) to apply. The application is available in English, Spanish, Chinese Traditional, Chinese Simplified, Russian, Somali, and Arabic. Applicants can verify identity using Social Security number, Alternate ID, or text message verification on mobile phone. Step 3: Receive your ACP credit. Visit Xfinity.com/acp and complete the Xfinity ACP enrollment form using your National Verifier Application ID. Sign into your Xfinity account, complete the ACP form, and submit. Expect status updates within 48 hours. Equipment will be dropped off at your door within 7-10 business days of approval. Current Xfinity or Internet Essentials customers can also apply for ACP by completing steps 1 and 3 only. Support available through USAC Affordable Connectivity Program Customer Support Center at (877) 384-2575, 7 days a week, 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. ET.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides grants for weatherization and related repairs for eligible members of Choptank Electric Cooperative.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided for weatherization and related home repairs for qualifying members of Choptank Electric Cooperative.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Members of Choptank Electric Cooperative who meet program eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Weatherization and related home repairs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to members of Choptank Electric Cooperative in the Choptank service area.
requirements_list: Must be a Choptank Electric Cooperative member

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for homeowners whose principal residence qualifies for homestead property tax exemption.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit for homeowners whose principal residence qualifies under the Homestead Tax Credit program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners seeking to have their principal residence approved for homestead tax credit eligibility.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit for principal residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Somerset County and statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can submit an online application through the Maryland One Stop portal or contact the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment (BEAD) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal funding program that expands high-speed internet access by supporting planning, infrastructure deployment, and adoption programs. The BEAD plan serves as Maryland's State Plan establishing commitments and strategy to support broadband projects over the next five years to close the digital divide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal funding to expand high-speed internet access through planning, infrastructure deployment, and adoption programs. Provides funding and technical assistance to improve broadband access to unserved and underserved Maryland communities. Funding supports capital projects for broadband infrastructure build-out, planning initiatives, and digital adoption programs to increase broadband utilization.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling applications; contact agency for specific deadlines
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland communities and jurisdictions seeking to improve broadband access, particularly unserved and underserved areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, infrastructure deployment, and adoption programs to expand high-speed internet access; capital projects for broadband network build-out; digital adoption and training programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland, with priority focus on unserved and underserved areas to close the digital divide. Eligible areas determined by broadband availability data and gap analysis.
requirements_list: Projects must address unserved or underserved broadband areas
Applicants must demonstrate commitment to broadband expansion goals
Projects should align with Maryland's broadband strategic priorities
Eligible applicants must be governmental, non-profit, or for-profit entities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For more information and to apply, visit the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Broadband website and State Plans webpage at https://dhcd.maryland.gov/Broadband/Pages/StatePlans.aspx. Prospective applicants should review the State Plan and contact the agency for application procedures, funding availability, and project requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Christmas In April, St. Mary's County
structured_extraction.program_description: A non-profit organization that assists low to moderate income homeowners with needed home repair projects at no charge to the homeowner.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Home repairs are made at no charge to eligible homeowners.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be submitted between May and October each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low to moderate income homeowners in St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Needed home repair projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a low to moderate income homeowner
Homes are selected by a committee based on varying factors
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must apply between May and October each year. Homes are selected by a committee based on varying factors. Repairs are made on the last Saturday in April.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Options Waiver and Community First Choice Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicaid waiver program designed for consumers who require nursing home level of care. It enables eligible consumers to live safely in the community and receive appropriate services instead of residing in a nursing facility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides or subsidizes a range of community-based services for eligible individuals who meet nursing home level of care requirements. Services include assisted living, case management, personal care services, accessibility adaptations, assistive devices, behavior consultation, personal emergency response systems, home-delivered meals, nutritional services, family and consumer training, medical adult day services, senior center services, medical equipment, and assistance with transitional costs. The program may also provide eligibility for other Medicaid services such as medical adult day care and prescription assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Consumers who require nursing home level of care and meet income and asset requirements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assisted living, case management, personal care services, accessibility adaptations, assistive devices, behavior consultation services, personal emergency response systems, home-delivered meals, nutritional services, family and consumer training, medical adult day services, senior center services, medical equipment, and assistance with transitional costs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must meet nursing home level of care
Must meet income requirements
Must meet asset requirements

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that provides federal funding to help homeowners reduce flood damage to their homes through eligible mitigation measures. The program covers 75% of project costs with homeowners providing 25% cost share.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants covering 75% of project costs for eligible flood mitigation measures. Homeowners must contribute 25% of the total project cost through an escrow account. The grant is offered on an annual basis with funding amounts determined by FEMA availability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application offered once per year; due dates communicated annually based on fund availability
structured_extraction.program_audience: St. Mary's County homeowners with homes at high risk for flood damage
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible flood mitigation measures that reduce disaster losses and flood damage to homes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, homes must be located within a flood zone
requirements_list: Home must be actively insured through the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP)
Home must be located within a flood zone
Homeowner must be willing and able to provide 25% of total project cost in escrow account upon approval
Elevation Certificate required
Copy of NFIP Declaration required
Documentation of previous flood losses if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Emergency Management staff at EMA@stmaryscountymd.gov with required documents and interest in applying. Staff will inform you of the next available application cycle and any additional requirements. Emergency Management staff will help obtain project proposals and required documentation, then submit the application on your behalf. The process may take several months from submission, approximately one year for project approval or denial, and potentially an additional year for funding release.

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Authority Home Repair Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides low-interest loans to homeowners for major home repairs such as roofing, wells, windows, and other significant home improvements.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans for major home repairs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in St. Mary's County needing major home repairs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Major home repairs including roofing, wells, windows, and similar projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner
Home must need major repairs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact The Housing Authority, St. Mary's County, Maryland for information on how to apply and determine eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides small one-time respite grants to families caring for an aging family member. The grant helps offset the cost of hiring a caregiver of the family's choice to provide a short break from caregiving responsibilities. Grants are also available for seniors caring for a grandchild under 18 years old and for parents caring for an adult child with a disability age 18 or older.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time respite grants to offset the cost of hiring a caregiver of the family's choice. The grant amount is contingent upon availability of funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families caring for aging family members, seniors caring for grandchildren under 18, and parents caring for adult children with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To hire a caregiver of the family's choice to provide respite care and a short break from caregiving responsibilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A free prescription discount card program that helps residents save money on prescription costs. Cardholders save an average of $21.41 per prescription or 30 percent off the retail price. The card can be used at participating pharmacies for prescriptions not covered by insurance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free discount cards offered through a partnership with the National Association of Counties and CVS Caremark. No enrollment forms, membership fees, or limitations on frequency of use. Cardholders present the card to participating pharmacies to receive discounts on prescriptions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: St. Mary's County residents seeking to reduce prescription medication costs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prescription medications not covered by insurance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County residents. Cards are available at all St. Mary's County libraries, Senior Activity Centers, and the Division of Human Services.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application process. Cards are free and available at all St. Mary's County libraries, Senior Activity Centers, and the Division of Human Services. Simply present the card to a participating pharmacy when filling a prescription.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides housing subsidies to individuals requiring assistance with rental costs through the US Department of Housing and Urban Development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Housing subsidies to help pay rental costs for individuals requiring assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals requiring assistance with rental costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact The Housing Authority, St. Mary's County, Maryland for more information and to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides older adults with door-to-door transportation to medical appointments, social engagements, shopping, and other destinations using volunteer drivers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Door-to-door transportation service provided by volunteer drivers using their personal vehicles. Riders make suggested donations based on distance: $10 for less than 15 miles, $15 for 15-30 miles, $20 for 31-50 miles, and $50 for out-of-county destinations (Annapolis, Baltimore, Washington D.C.). Transportation is limited to 4 trips per month per rider and is provided only when a driver is available. Riders are responsible for paying all tolls, parking, or other fees incurred during the trip.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults age 60 years or older who are St. Mary's County residents, unable to use other public transportation, and lack reliable transportation sources.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Door-to-door transportation to medical appointments, social engagements, shopping, and other destinations within St. Mary's County or out-of-county medical trips only.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County residents only. Out-of-county rides are limited to medical appointments only. Out-of-county transportation includes trips to Annapolis, Baltimore, and Washington D.C.
requirements_list: Be 60 years of age or older
Be a St. Mary's County resident
Have a low to moderate income not exceeding $5,216 per month for an individual or $7,050 for a couple
Have cognitive awareness and the ability to ambulate using a cane or walker (wheelchairs cannot be accommodated)
Lack access to reasonable, affordable transportation
Must use other forms of public transportation when available and appropriate
Complete the Senior Rides Application Form
Sign release/waiver form
Be ready at scheduled pickup time
Be prepared to pay all tolls, parking, or other fees incurred on the trip
Wear seatbelt
Be courteous
Transportation to procedures requiring anesthesia and/or excessive wait times will be considered at the time of request
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested older adults must complete the Senior Rides Application Form, which can be completed by phone, in person, or by mail. The application includes questions about income, medical assistance, mobility aids, disabilities, and transportation needs. Once accepted into the program, riders must request transportation at least 3 business days in advance for in-county destinations and 5 business days for out-of-county medical destinations, excluding the day of the request. Riders must sign a Ridership Release/Waiver form.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Shore Erosion Control Program provides technical and financial assistance to public and private property owners experiencing shore erosion problems. It supports projects that prevent sediment loss, reduce non-point source pollution, protect and restore tidal marshes, and protect structures. The program offers matching grants for both structural and vegetative erosion control projects, including establishment of Shore Erosion Control taxing districts.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants are available at 45/55 (County/private owner) for private landowners and 75/25 (State/public) for eligible public land protection projects covering design, construction, and project management for non-structural shorelines also known as Living Shorelines. Grants fund the construction of living shorelines using small stone structures, sand, and marsh grasses. The program provides funding, design, and construction assistance. Costs are recovered through annual special benefit assessments levied against properties in the taxing district.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners and property owners with shoreline erosion on their property in eligible areas; community or group of property owners
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding, design, and construction of non-structural shorelines and living shorelines including small stone structures, sand, and marsh grasses. Funds cover design, construction, and project management costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties along shorelines in St. Mary's County, including Chesapeake Bay and coastal bays
requirements_list: Property must be experiencing shoreline erosion
Submit a Letter of Interest (petition) indicating proposed district boundaries
DNR prepares a Need & Feasibility Report with proposed work and preliminary cost estimates
County conducts informational meeting to review the Need & Feasibility Report
75% of property owners in the proposed district must return signed Confirming Petitions in support
Public hearing held to establish district by ordinance
Final construction plans and cost estimates prepared by DNR or consultant
Board of County Commissioners holds public hearing to approve final plans and specifications
Construction advertised for bid and awarded
Annual special benefit assessment levied against properties in the district
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a Letter of Interest (petition) to St. Mary's County indicating proposed district boundaries. 2. Letter is forwarded to DNR Shore Erosion Control for consideration. 3. DNR prepares a Need & Feasibility Report including proposed work and preliminary cost estimates. 4. County conducts informational meeting with property owners to review the report. 5. County provides Confirming Petitions to each owner detailing estimated costs and project terms. If 75% of owners return signed petitions in support, the process continues. 6. Public hearing held to establish district by ordinance; County executes loan agreement with the State. 7. Complete construction plans and cost estimates are prepared. 8. Board of County Commissioners holds public hearing to present final plans and determine whether to proceed. 9. Construction is advertised for bid. 10. Escrow account established if owner cash contributions required. 11. Construction is awarded and completed. 12. Following construction, public hearing held to fix and levy annual assessment charge as special benefit assessment.

structured_extraction.program_description: Special Drainage Districts establish a mechanism by which property owners can correct and improve recurring drainage problems in their subdivisions and neighborhoods. The County may establish and maintain drainage systems with costs assessed to benefited properties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Drainage improvement costs including design, construction, and interest are made equitable by assessing costs to all benefited properties over a period not to exceed fifteen years. The County may maintain the system with perpetual annual maintenance assessments allocated to the district.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners experiencing recurring drainage problems in subdivisions and neighborhoods
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Correcting and improving drainage systems including design, construction, and ongoing maintenance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County subdivisions and neighborhoods
requirements_list: Petition with signatures from more than 50% of property owners within the proposed drainage district is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested parties must submit a petition signed by more than 50% of property owners within the proposed drainage district. Procedures for establishment and construction are available from the Department of Public Works.

structured_extraction.program_description: Special Road Taxing Districts allow property owners to establish a mechanism for upgrading substandard subdivision roads and making them suitable for acceptance into the County Highway Maintenance System. The County borrows funds for construction and benefited property owners repay the costs through the district.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County borrows funds for road construction and improvements. Benefited lot owners reimburse the costs of principal and interest over a period not to exceed twenty (20) years through special taxing assessments on their properties. Property owners bear the cost of design engineering, construction, and utility costs. The County covers administrative, preliminary engineering, and inspection costs. If construction to current standards requires additional costs beyond what was required at the time of subdivision approval, the County bears that difference. Assessment methods are determined individually per district based on benefit derived or lot width.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in subdivisions seeking to upgrade substandard roads
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Upgrading and improving substandard subdivision roads to make them suitable for County Highway Maintenance System acceptance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County subdivisions and neighborhoods. Only subdivision streets or roads constructed prior to January 1, 1977 are eligible for consideration.
requirements_list: Petition must be signed by two-thirds (2/3) of benefiting property owners
Subdivision streets must connect to an existing street or road in the County Highway Maintenance System or maintained by the State
Roads must meet acceptable standards that were in effect at the time the subdivision was approved
Property owners must submit a Letter of Interest with a map showing proposed district boundaries
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners submit a Letter of Interest with district map to the Board of County Commissioners. The County prepares a preliminary design and cost estimate and holds a public informational meeting. Property owners then submit a formal petition signed by two-thirds (2/3) of benefiting property owners. The Board approves the petition and draft ordinance, schedules a public hearing with a ten (10) day comment period, and adopts the establishment ordinance. Right-of-way deeds or plats are recorded. Plans and specifications are prepared, construction is scheduled based on Capital Improvement Program funding and departmental workload, and the road is accepted into the County Highway Maintenance System. Final assessment of costs and levy ordinance adoption follows.

structured_extraction.program_name: St. Mary's County FIRE/EMS Scholarship Program Year 2025-2026
structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program for active members of St. Mary's County Volunteer Fire Departments, Rescue Squads, or Advanced Life Support Units interested in pursuing fire and emergency medical services education and training through post-secondary institutions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship reimbursement for tuition and course materials for eligible fire and EMS personnel. The total funding available is spread amongst approved applicants based on the number of credit hours planned (maximum 36 credit hours per year), cost per credit hour, and course completion. Reimbursement is the lesser of the amount awarded or the total cost of tuition and course materials. Recipients must achieve a minimum grade of 2.0 or better on a 4.0 scale and provide registration receipts, bookstore receipts, grade reports, and LOSAP verification documentation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active members of St. Mary's County Volunteer Fire Departments, Rescue Squads, or Advanced Life Support Units seeking to pursue fire and EMS education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Scholarship funds to support tuition and course materials for fire and emergency medical services training and education leading to a certificate, diploma, or other evidence of qualification from a recognized post-secondary educational facility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland. Applicants must be active members of a St. Mary's County Volunteer Fire Department, Rescue Squad, or Advanced Life Support Unit.
requirements_list: Active member of a St. Mary's County Volunteer Fire Department, Rescue Squad, or Advanced Life Support Unit
Met minimum program requirements for the previous calendar year in the Length of Service Award Program (LOSAP)
Enrollment in courses at a recognized post-secondary educational facility leading to a certificate, diploma, or qualification
Courses must fall within the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026
Completed application form with all required information
Completed and signed Agreement (ESB26)
Completed IRS W-9 form
Copy of acceptance letter into post-secondary education institution (not required if follow-on applicant from previous year)
Copy of acceptance into clinical portion of studies if applicable
Must provide registration receipt and course material receipts within one month of enrollment
Must achieve minimum grade of 2.0 or better on 4.0 scale upon course completion
Must provide grade report within two weeks of course completion
Must meet LOSAP minimum program requirements for the enrollment year
Must provide copy of annual LOSAP form within one month of form generation
All documents must contain original signatures in blue ink or digitally encrypted date-stamped electronic signatures
No faxed copies accepted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain application materials from St. Mary's County Emergency Services. 2. Complete the Fire/EMS Scholarship Application form (2025-2026), ensuring all fields are answered completely. 3. Prepare required attachments: completed and signed Agreement (ESB26), confirmation of acceptance to post-secondary institution, school literature confirming cost per credit hour, and completed IRS W-9 form. 4. Obtain verification from your Fire Department Chief or President that you are an active member meeting LOSAP minimum program requirements. 5. Submit the complete application package to St. Mary's County Emergency Services, Attention: Angel Clem, P.O. Box 653, Leonardtown, MD 20650-0653 on or before 31 August 2025. 6. All documents must contain original signatures in blue ink or digitally encrypted date-stamped electronic signatures; no faxed copies are accepted. 7. The Emergency Services Board will review applications and make recommendations to the Commissioners of St. Mary's County for approval. 8. Notification of scholarship status is anticipated on or about 30 October 2025. 9. Upon award and registration, submit registration receipt and bookstore receipts to the Emergency Services Board. 10. Upon course completion, submit grade report showing satisfactory completion. 11. Upon completion of yearly LOSAP paperwork, submit proof of meeting LOSAP requirements. 12. Emergency Services will forward Scholarship Payment Request for processing.

structured_extraction.program_description: A transportation program for elderly and persons with disabilities in Maryland who do not have sufficient access to public transportation routes. The program provides general purpose transportation and encourages efficient coordination of transportation services and programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Door-to-door transportation service provided to seniors and persons with disabilities. Service operates Monday through Friday on scheduled zones with rides available between 10:00 a.m. and 1:00 p.m. (pick-up times between 9:30 and 10:00 a.m., return times between 12:00 and 2:00 p.m.). Fare is $3.00 per one-way trip or $6.00 for a round trip, with $3.00 charged for additional stops beyond one stop per round trip. Participants can schedule appointments up to 30 days in advance. The program provides over 17,000 rides annually, funded by state grant money ($130,000 to $175,000 per year) with required local match. Each passenger is allowed one designated stop per round trip; additional stops depend on allotted time. Weekly appointments such as therapy or dialysis can be scheduled with weekly confirmation. Drivers provide curb-to-curb or door-to-door service if requested in advance (drivers do not enter homes). All vehicles are wheelchair accessible with platform lifts (capacity 600 pounds, measuring 48.5" long by 31" wide) that can accommodate wheelchairs, walkers, and crutches. Riders may be accompanied by one attendant free of charge; additional attendants or companions must pay $3.00. Service animals performing specific functions are allowed. Passengers are responsible for paying exact fare at pickup (cash, checks, or SSTAP tickets only). No shows and failure to pay may result in suspension of service. Cancellations made the day before are accepted at no cost.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Mary Ann Coontz; Terry Kerns (Transportation Supervisor)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Elderly individuals (senior citizens) and persons with disabilities in St. Mary's County who lack sufficient access to public transportation routes. A paratransit application must be completed to qualify.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to medical appointments, social engagements, shopping, and other general purposes. Door-to-door service is provided to senior nutritional centers (Oakley, Northern, Loffler, and Garvey centers) daily. Medical appointments are given preference under a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland. Service is organized into five zones (Zone 1 through Zone 4 plus Thursday service) covering different areas on different days: Zone 1 (Monday) covers Charlotte Hall, Golden Beach, Helen, Chaptico, Budds Creek, Wicomico, and Clements; Zone 2 (Tuesday) covers Oakville, Loveville, Hollywood, Leonardtown, Avenue, Compton, and Mechanicsville; Zone 3 (Wednesday) covers California, Lexington Park, and Great Mills; Zone 4 (Friday) covers Piney Point, Ridge, Park Hall, Callaway, and St. Inigoes; Thursday provides service to all zones.
requirements_list: Must be an elderly senior citizen or person with a disability
Must not have sufficient access to public transportation routes or be unable to use public transportation
Must complete a paratransit application to qualify for eligibility
Must present proof of age to receive senior discount fares
Can schedule appointments up to 30 days in advance
Must be ready at scheduled pick-up time
Pickup locations must have wheelchair ramp or assistant for riders with mobility needs, with accessible driveways and safe turnaround space for buses
Must provide exact change at time of pickup (cash, checks, or SSTAP tickets only)
Riders allowed to transport only as many packages as physically carried
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Transportation Division at (301) 863-8400 ext. 1120 or (301) 475-4200 ext. 1120 or email SDispatchers@stmaryscountymd.gov to request a paratransit application. Once completed and evaluated, applicants will know results within 5 days. Eligible persons receive an identification card. To schedule appointments, call with your name, telephone number, location, destination, date and time of appointment. Riders can schedule rides up to 30 days in advance and schedule appointments between 10:00 a.m. and 1:00 p.m. Appointments must be scheduled with the Transportation Specialist; changes in designated stops with the driver are not acceptable. Call to confirm pick-up times on the morning of your appointment. The office is staffed Monday through Saturday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with voicemail available on Sunday. Senior identification cards are available through the STS Transit office at 44829 St. Andrews Church Road, California, Maryland 20619.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Waterway Improvement Program provides grants and loans for projects that mark channels and harbors, clear debris from waterways, dredge channels, and construct jetties and marine facilities beneficial to the boating public. The program is governed by Maryland Natural Resources Article, Section 8-707 and administered through Waterway Improvement Districts established in St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers three funding mechanisms through the Maryland Waterway Improvement Fund: (1) 100% grants if the project benefits the general boating public; (2) Interest-free long-term loans; or (3) 50/50 matching grants where the State reimburses 50% and the County/residents split remaining costs. The term of repayment for benefit assessments shall not exceed the lesser of 25 years or the estimated service life of the improvement. Maximum annual allocation per project is $25,000. County recovers costs through a special assessment levied against benefited property owners within the established Waterway Improvement District, paid annually with County taxes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private property owners seeking waterway improvements that benefit the boating public in St. Mary's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Marking channels and harbors, clearing debris from waterways, dredging channels, constructing jetties and marine facilities, and engineering and design services. For dredging projects, property owners must identify and provide an adequate spoil site for dredge materials.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Real property abutting a natural or artificial body of water in St. Mary's County, Maryland. The waterway improvement district must be defined and approved by affected property owners.
requirements_list: At least 75% of benefited property owners must sign a Letter of Interest defining district boundaries and indicating concurrence
At least 75% of benefited property owners must submit a formal petition that includes property identification, district boundary map, estimated costs, and chosen assessment method
Project must provide accessibility to sheltered water bodies, suitable anchorage conditions, relieve water access congestion, or provide water access for fueling, repair, storage, or berths
Project must be recommended by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources in a Need and Feasibility Report
The value of benefits must meet or exceed project costs to demonstrate no substantial, unreasonable, or unjust disproportionality between assessment and value accruing to the property
All co-owners of a property must sign petition documents; signatures of authorized officers required for corporate owners
Costs for advertising to establish, amend, modify, or dissolve a District are borne by current property owners in the District
Engineering and design service costs are the responsibility of property owners within the District if consulting engineers are needed
Future maintenance of the project is the responsibility of the District after completion
Maximum annual allocation per project is $25,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: (1) Affected property owners submit a Letter of Interest signed by at least 75% of proposed district properties, defining district boundaries and limits. (2) County submits Letter of Interest to Maryland Department of Natural Resources for a Need and Feasibility Report. (3) If DNR recommends the project, County holds a Public Informational Meeting to present findings, estimated costs, and funding options. (4) Property owners submit a formal Petition signed by at least 75% of benefited properties, identifying properties by tax map and parcel, selecting an assessment method (Cumulative Assessment Ratio or Equal Assessment), and providing an affidavit of ownership. (5) County staff approves the petition. (6) Board of County Commissioners holds a Public Hearing to establish the District by ordinance. (7) County obtains permits and prepares preliminary designs; community identifies dredge material placement sites. (8) Waterway Improvement Fund Grant Application submitted to DNR. (9) County designs project (in-house or by consultant contract) and prepares plans and specifications. (10) Project is advertised and construction bids solicited. (11) Public Informational Meeting held to discuss design and construction costs; if bids exceed ordinance amount, Public Hearing held to amend budget. (12) Construction contract awarded and executed. (13) After construction completion, County executes reimbursable Loan Agreement with DNR and requests reimbursement. (14) Public Hearing held to fix assessment via Levy Ordinance. (15) Board of County Commissioners levies benefit charges against each property in District, paid annually with County taxes.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 2025 Opioid Restitution Fund Community Micro Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program providing one-time funding allocations to non-profit organizations to support programs and services addressing the opioid crisis in Talbot County, including prevention, treatment, and recovery initiatives. Funding comes from the National Opioid Settlement Fund, Maryland state abatement grants, and settlements with pharmaceutical companies and distributors held accountable for their role in the opioid crisis. Eligible activities include school education campaigns, evidence-based overdose prevention, substance use treatment, crisis response systems, safe stations, intervention support, and stabilization centers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time funding allocations ranging from $1,000 to $20,000 per organization. Grant funds must be used by June 30, 2026. Funding supports opioid prevention and treatment initiatives including school education campaigns, evidence-based overdose prevention, substance use treatment, crisis response systems, safe stations, stabilization centers, and related community programs. Funding comes from the National Opioid Settlement Fund and Maryland state abatement grants.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Programs and services addressing the opioid crisis in Talbot County, including school education campaigns to prevent opioid use, evidence-based overdose prevention and substance use treatment, crisis response systems, safe stations, stabilization centers, intervention support, and drug awareness and treatment programming.

Assistance is limited to U.S. citizens and specified categories of non-citizens with eligible immigration status.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance to help households afford housing in the private rental market.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Preliminary applications must be submitted online at https://www.waitlistcheck.com/MD1645 between April 1, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. and April 30, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. All applications received during the open period have an equal chance of being selected through a computerized random selection process. Applicants selected for the waiting list will be contacted to complete a full eligibility application as housing vouchers become available. In-person assistance is available at multiple library locations throughout the region during designated dates and times in April.

structured_extraction.program_description: A public service program administered through Talbot County in partnership with the Maryland Department of Service and Civic Innovation. The program offers paid service opportunities combined with job training, skill development, and professional development for individuals ages 18 and older, including recent high school graduates. Participants are placed in service organizations aligned with their interests where they earn a minimum of $15 per hour working at least 30 hours per week. The program features partnerships with Maryland's Historically Black Colleges and Universities and community colleges to enhance collaboration and support. Upon successful completion of the service year, participants receive a $6,000 completion award. A Service Year Option track is tailored for high school graduates seeking structured service placements with coaching support, while the Maryland Corps track is open to individuals of all eligible ages seeking broader service and professional development opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants earn a minimum of $15 per hour while working at least 30 hours per week in service placements. Upon successful completion of their service year, participants receive a $6,000 completion award as either a direct payment or a deposit into a Maryland 529 Education Account.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants use wages and completion awards for living expenses, education, or career planning and advancement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, with partnerships through Historically Black Colleges and Universities and community colleges across the state.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide Medicaid grant program administered locally by the Talbot County Health Department that provides services and funds for seniors aged 65 and older who may be at risk of nursing home placement. The program aims to help seniors remain safely in the community as long as possible by offering four core services: screening for eligibility for supportive programs, comprehensive assessments of individual needs, case managers to secure and coordinate services, and a pool of gap funds to purchase services not covered by other programs. Talbot County is one of only two counties in the state in which the local Health Department directly administers the Senior Care program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides four core services: screening for eligibility for supportive programs, comprehensive assessments of individual needs, case managers to secure and coordinate services, and a pool of gap funds to purchase services not covered by other programs. Gap-filling funds provide chore services, personal care services, personal emergency response systems (emergency buttons), prescription co-pays, medical supplies, and transportation for eligible seniors aged 65 and older.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Talbot County residents aged 65 or older with moderate or severe functional disability who meet Maryland Department of Aging financial eligibility requirements and are at risk of nursing home placement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Gap funds can be used to purchase services not covered by other programs to help seniors remain safely in the community, including chore services, personal care services, personal emergency response systems, prescription co-pays, medical supplies, and transportation.

structured_extraction.program_description: An 8-week online entrepreneurial accelerator and training program sponsored by the Talbot County Department of Economic Development and Tourism in partnership with Will Holmes Consulting. The program helps small, minority-owned, and women-owned business owners in Talbot County succeed and grow by teaching business fundamentals including cash-flow projection, growth planning, financial management, sales and marketing, human resources, legal compliance, accounting, taxes, insurance, and capital preparation. Participants attend eight 3-hour sessions via Zoom on Tuesday evenings, complete weekly homework assignments, receive one-on-one mentoring from senior advisors in law, accounting, human resources, and marketing, and culminate in a final 15-minute PowerPoint presentation. Graduates receive a certificate of completion and a $2,000 grant funded by an anonymous donor to reinvest in their business.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 8-week online training program delivered via Zoom on Tuesday evenings from 6 to 9 p.m. Participants receive instruction in business infrastructure, leadership and growth planning, marketing and sales, accounting, human resources, legal matters, taxes, insurance, and capital preparation. The program includes weekly homework assignments, one-on-one meetings with senior advisors in law, accounting, human resources, and marketing, and culminates in a final 15-minute PowerPoint presentation. Each graduate receives a certificate of completion and a $2,000 grant (provided by an anonymous donor) to reinvest in their business. Graduates are required to report on business growth over subsequent years, including increased revenue and jobs added.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, minority-owned, and women-owned business owners in Talbot County who have operated their business for at least two years, have annual revenue of less than $1.5 million, and seek to increase revenue, add jobs, and make an impact on the local economy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and education in business management, financial planning, sales and marketing, human resources, legal compliance, accounting, and capital access strategies. The $2,000 graduation grant can be reinvested in the business to support growth and development initiatives.
