Have the ability to scale operations and hire employees
Desire to increase revenue, add jobs, and make an impact on the local economy
Commit to attending all 8 weekly Zoom sessions on Tuesday evenings from 6 to 9 p.m.
Complete and submit weekly homework assignments
Participate in one-on-one meetings with senior advisors in law, accounting, human resources, and marketing
Present cash flow projections
Give a final 15-minute PowerPoint presentation at graduation
Complete the 8-week entrepreneurship course to receive certificate and $2,000 grant
Report on business growth over coming years, including increased revenue and jobs added
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application at www.talbotworks.org by the deadline. Selected applicants will be invited to participate in a short Zoom interview. The program operates in cohorts facilitated through the Talbot County Department of Economic Development and Tourism. To graduate, participants must attend all classes, complete weekly homework assignments, meet with senior advisors, and deliver a final 15-minute PowerPoint presentation. Upon graduation, participants receive a certificate of completion and a $2,000 grant.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Tri-County Council for Western Maryland offers this revolving loan fund to help businesses in Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties. The program provides gap financing, partnering with banks and other lenders to fund the portion of a project that a primary lender cannot fully cover. The main goal is to create or retain jobs in the region by providing an ongoing financing tool — as borrowers repay loans, funds return to the pool to make additional loans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides loans from $10,000 to $400,000 as gap financing. A bank or other private lender must fund at least 50% of the project. Interest rates are tied to the prime interest rate. Loan terms are up to 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets such as real estate. A $250 non-refundable application fee is required, and approved borrowers are assessed a 1.5% loan origination fee at closing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses including corporations, partnerships, and sole proprietorships located in or seeking to locate or expand in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County that cannot obtain all needed funding from traditional lenders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business acquisition and expansion, land and building costs, machinery and equipment purchases, start-up costs, working capital, business relocation, and job creation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in or seeking to locate or expand in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County.
requirements_list: Must be a small business
Must be seeking to locate or expand in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County
A business plan is required
A private lender must fund at least 50% of the total project cost
Applicant must provide a denial letter from the primary lender for 100% of the project, along with their approval to finance a majority of the project
One job must be created or retained for every $30,000 borrowed within the first 36 months of the loan
A minimum equity injection of 10% is generally required for start-up businesses
Personal guaranties of the debt are required from all owners with 20% or greater interest
Applicants must provide a completed personal financial statement and 3 years of both business and personal tax returns
A $250 non-refundable application fee is required
Approved borrowers are assessed a 1.5% loan origination fee at closing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, create a business plan and determine your funding needs. Second, apply for a loan from a private bank to determine how much they will finance. Third, complete the program's application form and submit it with the required documents and application fee. Apply through Summit Financing Solutions, which participates with banks and other lenders.

structured_extraction.program_name: USDA Rural Energy for America Program (REAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides guaranteed loan financing and grant funding to agricultural producers and rural small businesses to purchase or install renewable energy systems or make energy efficiency improvements. The program supports energy efficiency improvements and renewable energy installations in rural businesses and agricultural operations across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Guaranteed loan financing and grant funding for agricultural producers and rural small businesses to purchase or install renewable energy systems or make energy efficiency improvements. Grants are available for energy efficiency and renewable energy projects in rural businesses and agricultural enterprises.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers and rural small businesses, including rural businesses and agricultural operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase or installation of renewable energy systems or energy efficiency improvements, including renewable energy installations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rural Maryland areas
requirements_list: Located in rural area
Primary business must be agriculture or rural enterprise
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Maryland Clean Energy Center or USDA for application information. Additional resources available through Garrett County Community Development Energy office.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program exclusively designed for agricultural businesses, farms, and farm owners in Washington County to support agricultural business growth and development through funding for innovation and equipment purchases. The Board of County Commissioners approved $300,000 from the Washington County Hotel Rental Tax Fund to support this program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Board of County Commissioners approved funding of $300,000 from the Washington County Hotel Rental Tax Fund for this agricultural grant program to support agricultural innovation and equipment purchases.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural businesses, farms, and farm owners in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Agricultural innovation and equipment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Not specified

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that encourages landowners to enter into an agreement to restrict their land from development for ten years. In return, landowners receive protection from nuisance complaints through the Right to Farm Ordinance, become eligible to sell Development Rights Easements through the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Program (MALPF), and receive a property tax credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners who voluntarily enter into a ten-year Agricultural Land Preservation District agreement receive county property tax credits for farmland, farm buildings, and a partial tax credit for the home. They also receive legal protection from nuisance complaints under the Right to Farm Ordinance and become eligible to apply to sell a permanent agricultural preservation easement to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF). The district agreement is notarized and recorded in the County land records, and runs with the land even if the property is sold or transferred during the ten-year period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County seeking to preserve their farmland while maintaining ownership, obtaining tax benefits, and protecting against nuisance complaints.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are not directly provided. Instead, landowners receive county property tax credits as compensation for voluntarily restricting development on their agricultural land for ten years, along with legal protections under the Right to Farm Ordinance and eligibility to sell a permanent easement to MALPF.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be agricultural land with a minimum of 50 acres as a stand-alone parcel or 20 acres if contiguous to other districts
Must have a minimum of 50% of soil classes I, II, and III
Must be outside water and sewer service areas
Must be outside of growth areas
Landowner must voluntarily enter into a ten-year restriction agreement
Land must be kept in agricultural use for a minimum of ten years
Land cannot be developed or subdivided for industrial, commercial, or residential use except as permitted by County regulations
Soil erosion and water quality practices contained within an approved soil conservation plan must be implemented within 10 years
Landowner must sign a notarized Agricultural Preservation District Agreement that is recorded in County land records
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners should contact the County's Department of Planning & Zoning to begin the process. Landowners complete the Agricultural District Intake Form providing information about the property, ownership, acreage, and farming operations. Once the property is determined to meet eligibility requirements, the landowner executes a notarized Agricultural Preservation District Agreement, which is then recorded in the Washington County land records. The agreement becomes effective upon recordation. Contact the Planning Department's Agricultural Land Preservation personnel at 240-313-2430 or askplanning@washco-md.net for guidance throughout the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive program providing incentives and financial assistance to support agricultural businesses and operations in Washington County, Maryland. The program offers multiple forms of financial support including loans, tax credits, subsidies, and grants to help farmers and agricultural businesses with operations, equipment, infrastructure, business development, farmland acquisition, and market access.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple incentives and financial programs coordinated through MARBIDCO and USDA agencies. Loan programs include: Maryland Resource-Based Industry Financing Fund (2.25% interest, up to $750,000), Rural Business Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund (5.25% interest, up to $100,000), Vineyard/Hops/Orchard Planting Loan Fund (4.50% interest, up to $100,000), Forestry Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund (4.75% interest, up to $150,000), and Rural Business Energy Efficiency Improvement Loan Fund (4.50% interest, $2,500-$30,000). Grant programs include: Maryland Urban Agriculture Commercial Lending Incentive Grant (up to $10,000), Maryland Value Added Producer Grant - Capital Assets Option ($2,500-$10,000), Maryland Value Added Producer Matching Grant (up to 15% of USDA match requirement), Next Generation Farmland Acquisition Program, Small Acreage Next Generation Program, Maryland Market Money Program (dollar-for-dollar match for federal nutrition benefits at farmers markets), USDA Farmers Market Promotion Program ($50,000-$500,000 with 25% match), USDA Local Food Promotion Program ($25,000-$500,000 with 25% match), USDA Rural Development Grants ($10,000-$500,000), USDA Value Added Producer Grants ($75,000-$250,000), Regional Food System Partnership Program ($100,000-$1,000,000 with 25% match), Community Food Projects ($35,000-$400,000 with 100% match), Rural Energy for America Program (loans and grants), Maryland Agriculture Water Quality Cost Share Program ($50,000-$300,000), and Maryland Agricultural Education and Rural Development Assistance Fund (up to $40,000).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by program; refer to individual program guidelines
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural businesses, farmers, forest products businesses, rural entrepreneurs, urban farmers, food system enterprises, and nonprofit organizations engaged in agricultural and rural development in Washington County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land acquisition, equipment purchases, working capital, facility construction and renovation, energy efficiency improvements, farmland conservation easements, market development, farmer training and technical assistance, water quality improvements, and business expansion or diversification related to agricultural and food system enterprises.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Some USDA programs define rural areas as territory not within the outer boundary of any city with population of 50,000 or more. Some programs may serve multi-county regions through partnerships.
requirements_list: Must be engaged in agricultural operations or related rural business
Must be located in or serving Washington County
For value-added programs: minimum 2 years in business (or June 30, 2020 for hemp fiber processors)
For USDA VAPG: must be eligible under USDA program guidelines
For farmland acquisition programs: must be beginning or young farmer
For MVAPG-CAO: product must be 'value added' with incremental value from physical state change, differentiated production/marketing, product segregation, or farm-based biomass energy
For USDA LFPP and FMPP: 25% match requirement
For Community Food Projects: 100% match requirement
For RFSP: 25% match requirement
For Next Generation Program: must demonstrate commitment to farmland conservation easement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Washington County Department of Business Development at 240-313-2280 or visit www.washco-md.net for information on available programs and application procedures. For MARBIDCO programs, contact MARBIDCO directly or the county agricultural land preservation program office. For USDA programs, visit respective USDA websites (USDA AMS, USDA Rural Development). Applications are accepted on a rolling basis for some programs; others have specific annual deadlines (e.g., Community Food Projects in June, MVAPG-CAO once per year, USDA VAPG annually). Refer to the Agriculture Incentives & Financial Programs document for detailed eligibility requirements and program specifics. Tri-County Council for Western Maryland (www.tccwmd.org) provides additional funding and grant resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program that provides grants to eligible entities for projects related to economic opportunities, workforce development, critical infrastructure, natural and cultural assets, and leadership and community capacity building in Appalachia.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided for projects in five goal areas: Economic Opportunities (entrepreneurial and business development), Ready Workforce (education, skills, and health), Critical Infrastructure (broadband, transportation, water/wastewater systems), Natural and Cultural Assets (community and economic development), and Leadership and Community Capacity (building leader and organizational capacity). Prioritized projects include Technology Development, Broadband, Education and Workforce Development, Tourism, Energy, Recovery Ecosystems, and Traditional Infrastructure. All ARC grants require a 50% match from other sources, and matching funds must be identified and committed at the time of application. Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact. The amount of ARC funding requested may be reduced to allow the maximum number of Washington County projects to be funded.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 3, 2026 for preliminary project submission; formal applications due November 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and government entities in Washington County, Maryland that have projects related to economic development, workforce, infrastructure, cultural assets, or community capacity in Appalachia.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects related to economic opportunities, workforce development, critical infrastructure including broadband and water/wastewater systems, natural and cultural assets, and leadership and community capacity building. Projects should be consistent with ARC 2024 Strategy Statement priorities including Technology Development, Broadband, Education and Workforce Development, Tourism, Energy, Recovery Ecosystems, and Traditional Infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. The county is part of the Appalachian Region served by the Appalachian Regional Commission.
requirements_list: 50% matching funds must be identified and committed at time of application
Matching funds must have commitment letters attached with committed status
Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact
All outputs and outcomes must be quantifiable with associated numeric values
Projects must align with one of the five ARC strategic goals
Projects must be consistent with State Strategic Goals and Objectives 2024-2028
Projects should reference any plan and/or economic documents showing the project is part of an overall plan for stimulating economic development
Organizational capacity to administer a federal grant must be demonstrated, including recent awards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Complete the Preliminary Project Description (PPD) form and ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources worksheet. Submit to the Office of Grant Management by April 3, 2026. Identify all matching funds with sources, amounts, and status (pending or committed). For pending funds, provide anticipated award dates. Provide commitment letters for all matching funds with committed status. Step 2: Washington County Commissioners review and rank projects, considering ARC 2024 Strategy Statement alignment and measurable outcomes. Step 3: County-ranked projects are submitted to Tri-County Council for Western Maryland for regional ranking. Step 4: Top-ranking projects receive a letter in early Fall inviting formal grant application submission to the Appalachian Regional Commission, due November 15. Note: The review committee may reduce the amount of ARC funding requested for each project to allow the maximum number of Washington County projects to be funded.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program providing financial support to charitable organizations within Washington County that offer services improving the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants awarded to recognized non-profit organizations on the Board of County Commissioners' Recognized Non-Profit List (1-108 List). Awards are based on priority service areas: Families and Children ($494,400), Domestic Violence ($386,400), Arts & Cultural ($135,600), Seniors ($136,800), Recreation ($33,600), and Other ($13,200). Total available funding for FY2027 is $1,200,000. Grant awards are disbursed in four quarterly installments (25% per quarter) beginning July 2026. Funds must be expended between July 1, 2026, and June 30, 2027. Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of the total request. Applicants must demonstrate efficient use of funds and results-based programmatic outcomes.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maria Kramer, Director; Carsten Ahrens, Senior Grant Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Recognized charitable non-profit organizations located in Washington County that are on the Board of County Commissioners' Recognized Non-Profit List (1-108 List).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports charitable organizations providing services that improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens. Organizations must demonstrate efficient use of funds and results-based programmatic outcomes. Funds can be used for operating expenses, capital expenses, or projects. All grant funds must be expended within one year. Requests to benefit individuals or fund endowments will be denied.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland only. Organization must have an office located within and provide services in Washington County.
requirements_list: Organization must be on the Board of County Commissioners' Recognized Non-Profit List (1-108 List)
Organization must be a charitable non-profit with IRS 501(c)(3) designation with Valid status
Organization must be incorporated with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and be In Good Standing at time of application submission
Organization must have an office in and provide services within Washington County
Organization must demonstrate at least one of the prioritized service areas: Families/Children, Domestic Violence, Arts & Cultural, Seniors, Recreation, or Other
Organization must not have unpaid liens or judgments against the corporation
Organization must not have unpaid or past due obligations to the Washington County Treasurer or any government entity
Application must be submitted during the published application window by the deadline
Application must be complete with all required signatures and attachments
Organization must provide most recent certified audit or detailed financial statement
Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of total request amount
Organization must be in good standing with State of Maryland at time of submission with proof required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations on the Recognized Non-Profit List receive a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) each year. Applicants complete the Community Organization Funding application packet which includes the application form, budget narrative worksheet, guidelines, checklist, and scoring rubric. Completed applications must be submitted in two formats: (1) six hard paper copies (unbound, secured with staples, binder clips, or rubber bands in a manila envelope) and (2) one electronic copy as a single PDF file. Paper copies may be mailed or dropped off at the Office of Grant Management, 100 West Washington Street, Room 1601, Hagerstown, MD 21740. Electronic copies must be emailed to cahrens@washco-md.net and cc jmackereth@washco-md.net. The Office of Grant Management reviews applications using a standardized rubric (Application Submission 10 points, Statement of Need 20 points, Past Performance 5 points, Organizational Capacity and Staffing 10 points, Program Plan 30 points, Collaborations and Partnerships 10 points, Budget and Narrative 15 points, for a maximum of 100 points). Organizations are urged to check applications thoroughly against the submittal checklist as OGM staff will not verify completeness or accuracy at submission. Applicants will be notified in writing when budget allocations are approved (typically May-June 2026). Technical assistance workshops are offered before the deadline. Two informational sessions were scheduled for Tuesday, December 2nd from 9:00-10:30 am or 3:00-4:30pm via Zoom.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commuter and Shuttle Bus COVID RELIEF Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to support Maryland commuter and shuttle bus companies facing continued financial impacts from the Coronavirus.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State grants totaling $8 million in Relief Act funding established in 2021 through bipartisan legislation to support commuter and shuttle bus companies facing continued financial impacts from COVID-19.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland commuter and shuttle bus companies facing continued financial impacts from COVID-19.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for commuter and shuttle bus companies facing continued financial impacts from COVID-19.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A state program that works in conjunction with the Federal Farm Service Agency's CREP Contract Program to make CREP contracts permanent through state-funded conservation easements. The program includes a matching component allowing landowners to add up to ten times the acreage of their existing CREP contract to their CREP easement to maximize land preservation and easement value. To date, $4,835,547 has been invested to permanently protect 1,926 acres in Washington County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program funds the purchase of permanent, state-funded conservation easements for properties with existing FSA CREP Contracts, making those federal contracts permanent. Landowners can add up to ten times the acreage of their CREP Contract to their CREP easement to maximize land preservation and easement value. Once the easement is sold, it remains effective in perpetuity. To date, $4,835,547 has been invested to permanently protect 1,926 acres in Washington County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County with existing Federal Farm Service Agency CREP contracts seeking to make those contracts permanent through state-funded conservation easements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to purchase permanent conservation easements that protect agricultural land and make existing federal CREP contracts permanent in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Applicants must have an existing FSA CREP Contract.
requirements_list: Must have an existing FSA CREP Contract
Property must be located in Washington County
Landowner must be willing to sell conservation easement
Easement becomes effective in perpetuity once sold
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners with existing FSA CREP Contracts apply for the easement program through the County's Land Preservation Office. Once the easement is applied for and sold, it remains effective in perpetuity.

structured_extraction.program_description: Reimbursement for eligible expenses associated with international marketing projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland companies that receive an ExportMD Award are eligible for up to $5,000 in reimbursement for expenses associated with an international marketing project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland companies pursuing international marketing projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expenses associated with international marketing projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that distributes funds from the Washington County Gaming Fund to eligible charitable organizations and non-profits in Washington County. Monies collected from tip jars are deposited into a dedicated Gaming Fund account. By statute, 50% of Gaming Funds are allocated to the Washington County Volunteer Fire & Rescue Association, with the remaining allocated to local charitable organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded from the Washington County Gaming Fund to support charitable organizations and community groups. Maximum distribution per application is $100,000. Organizations may apply for multiple projects by submitting separate applications for each project. The grant performance period is one year from award announcement (typically early August). Any funds not spent within the performance period must be returned to the fund. Specific grant amounts are determined by the Gaming Commission based on applications submitted and available funding.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Susan M. Buchanan, Director; M. Kramer; Jennifer Mackereth; Sara LaPole; Susan Buchanan
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) charitable organizations located in Washington County that provide support benefiting health and human services, emergency services, animal welfare, civic and community activities, athletic/recreational activities, educational and cultural activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: All funds must be used exclusively in Washington County and cannot be distributed outside of the County. Funds must be used for charitable purposes as approved in the grant application. Organizations must provide proof that funds were expended for approved purposes through invoices, proofs of purchase, or cancelled checks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland only. All funds must be used exclusively in Washington County and cannot be distributed outside of the County.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) charitable organization with valid status located in Washington County
Must provide services without discrimination based on race, creed, sex, age, color, national origin, marital status, familial status, sexual orientation, or disability
Must be a corporation, limited liability company, or unincorporated association
For corporations, articles of incorporation or organization must not be forfeited or in poor standing with the State Department of Taxation
Unincorporated associations must complete a Notice of Responsible Person form
Must complete Gaming Commission grant application signed by authorized official (President, Executive Director, CEO, Chairman, etc.)
Must submit required supporting documents including W-9 form, Notice of Responsible Person (if applicable), and most recent annual financial statement
Must provide 2019 Gaming Fund Grant Report or most recent year's report if organization received previous funding
Must provide evidence of how previously received Gaming Commission funds were expended (invoices, proofs of purchase, or cancelled checks required)
Must provide additional documentation to support request such as estimates, quotes, or partnership commitment letters
Churches and religious entities are not eligible
Organizations holding annual tip jar operator's licenses are not eligible
Political or governmental organizations are not eligible
Umbrella organizations are not eligible (except United Way of Washington County)

Booster organizations or entities supporting school-based programs cannot receive funding for property that becomes property of Washington County Public Schools unless they retain ownership and provide letter from School Superintendent confirming no ownership rights to the school system
Maximum distribution per application is $100,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted electronically via email only (no hard copies accepted). Submit application as PDF to jmackereth@washco-md.net copying slapole@washco-md.net by May 6, 2020 at 3:00 p.m. Applications must include: REQUEST form (signed by authorized official), FINANCIALS (most recent annual financial statement), GRPT (2019 Gaming Fund Grant Report or most recent report, with evidence of previous fund expenditure), DOC (supporting documentation such as estimates and quotes), NORP (Notice of Responsible Person form if unincorporated association), and W-9 form. A public funding hearing is held (June 23, 2020) where applicants may present and commissioners may ask clarifying questions. Applicants must schedule hearing time with Office of Grant Management. Gaming Commission reviews all applications and makes funding recommendations after the public hearing. Funding awards are announced during the Board of County Commissioners meeting in August, with award letters sent out and funds disbursed several weeks after announcement. The grant performance period is one year from award announcement.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to organizations operating within Washington County for one-time projects or events that were not budgeted or anticipated. The objective is to remedy or address current financial issues or situations requiring a prompt response and resolution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant awards are limited to a maximum of $2,000. The Board of County Commissioners may appropriate a portion of the General Fund Contingency annually to be awarded to targeted organizations meeting the funding goals. This portion of available funding may be adjusted annually at the discretion of the Board of County Commissioners. Grants are paid to the applicant, not to vendors for products or services. Unused funds must be returned to the Office of Grant Management within 30 days of the completion of the event or project.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Office of Grant Management
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations operating within Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: One-time projects or events that were not budgeted or anticipated and require prompt response and resolution. Cannot fund requests that benefit individuals (except individuals participating in group events), normal and routine operating and administrative expenses, organizations that support political candidates or whose primary purpose is to influence or attempt to initiate legislation, or for-profit ventures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Organizations must be operating within Washington County
Projects or events must be one-time projects
Projects must not otherwise qualify for general fund Community Organization Funding or Hotel Rental Tax Funding
Organizations must have an unexpected circumstance requiring prompt resolution
Organizations must provide evidence that the request meets a critical need in the community
Organizations must have no alternative source of funding
Organizations must have proven to be a valuable community resource
Maximum grant award is $2,000
All organizations receiving grant funding must complete a General Fund Contingency Grant Report and submit it with supporting documentation within 60 days of the completion of the event or project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding. Complete the General Fund Contingency Funding Grant Application form. The application packet includes guidelines and instructions, the grant application form, and the grant report form. Applications can be accessed and processed from the County's website (www.washco-md.net), or printed and mailed or emailed to the Office of Grant Management. Upon receipt, the OGM will: (1) Determine if the applicant is qualified to receive funding; (2) Determine if the event or project is qualified to receive funding; (3) Determine if the request meets the funding goals of the County Commissioners; (4) Approve or deny the request with the concurrence of the County Administrator; and (5) Notify the applicant in writing as to the approval or denial of their request. All organizations receiving grant funding must complete a General Fund Contingency Grant Report and submit it with supporting documentation to the Office of Grant Management within 60 days of the completion of the event or project.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides qualifying businesses with State income tax credits and local real property tax credits in return for job creation and capital investments made in designated Enterprise Zones within Washington County, Maryland. The program incentivizes business growth and investment in the Hagerstown/Washington County Enterprise Zone and its Focus Areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State income tax credits for job creation: $1,000 maximum one-time credit for most new jobs; $3,000 first year, $2,000 second year, and $1,000 third year for economically disadvantaged employees (certified by Maryland Department of Labor). Local real property tax credits for capital investments: 80% of property taxes on increased assessment for years 1-5, declining to 30% in year 10 over a 10-year period. Commercial building excise tax exemption for new construction within Enterprise Zones.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualifying businesses (proprietorships, partnerships, corporations) operating or investing in designated Hagerstown/Washington County Enterprise Zone or Hancock Enterprise Zone that create jobs and make capital investments in manufacturing, warehousing, research and development, corporate offices, service industries, or retail/mercantile businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits for businesses making capital investments (new construction, building additions, renovations) and creating jobs in designated Enterprise Zones. Credits support business expansion, job creation, and capital improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated Enterprise Zones in Washington County, Maryland: (1) Hagerstown/Washington County Enterprise Zone (~4,000 acres, includes Hopewell Valley Industrial Park, Washington County Business Park, CSX Valley Park, City of Hagerstown Business Park, and Central Business District); (2) Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (~1,500 acres). Personal property tax credits apply only to Focus Areas.
requirements_list: Business must be located within Zone boundaries on designation date, relocated to Zone after designation date, or started construction/expansion in Zone after designation date
For income tax credits: minimum of 1 new job in Central Business District or 5 new jobs outside CBD (Hagerstown zone); 1 new job in Hancock zone
For property tax credits: minimum capital investment of $5,000+ in Central Business District or Hancock zone; $50,000+ outside CBD
New jobs must be created after Zone designation date (Hagerstown: Dec 15, 1982; Hancock: Dec 15, 1995)
Employees must work minimum 35 hours per week, earn at least 150% of federal minimum wage, work at least 6 consecutive months, spend at least 50% of work time in Zone or Zone-related activities
Business must be in eligible category: manufacturing, warehousing, research and development, corporate offices, service industries (retail/mercantile only in CBD or Hancock)
Property tax credit property must be certified to Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation by December 31st of calendar year construction is completed
No replacement hires count toward new job requirements
Property must be real property only (not personal property, except in Focus Areas)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Determine if property is within Enterprise Zone by contacting Washington County Department of Business Development. 2) Verify minimum eligibility criteria for jobs or capital investment are met. 3) For property tax credits: Submit Request for Enterprise Zone Qualification form BEFORE project completion and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits. 4) For income tax credits: Submit Qualification form AFTER hiring new employees and submit 'New Jobs Created' form listing qualifying employees. 5) For income tax credits with disadvantaged employees: Contact Maryland Job Service Office (301-393-8200 or 301-393-8218) to identify and certify disadvantaged employees. 6) Washington County DBD reviews application and sends approval or denial letter; approval letters sent to state and local agencies. 7) Property tax credits automatically appear on tax bills in July or as credit vouchers (Hagerstown). 8) For income tax credits: Claim credits using Maryland Tax Form 500CR with approval letter from DBD on annual state return. No reapplication required for subsequent job credits after initial approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides financial incentives to property owners who undertake eligible historic preservation work on their properties located within historic districts or designated historic areas in Washington County, Maryland.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners can receive stackable tax credits for qualifying historic preservation expenses and improvements made to historic structures. The program offers a 25% County tax credit for rehabilitation, restoration, or preservation work that minimizes destruction of historic fabric and has thoughtful, sympathetic design. An additional 5% tax credit is available for new construction attached to existing historic structures. These credits can be combined with State (20%) and Federal (20%) credits for a possible total of 70% in combined credits. Unused credits can be carried over for up to 5 years or until expended. Qualified Rehabilitation Expenses (QREs) include roof repair/replacement, chimney repair/replacement, window restoration, new storm doors/windows, masonry re-pointing, structural repairs, architectural/engineering/consulting fees, and tool/equipment rental.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Department of Planning and Zoning, Historic District Commission
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential or commercial property owners with historic properties in Washington County historic districts or designated historic areas. Property must be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation, restoration, or renovation of historic structures including roof repair/replacement, chimney repair/replacement, window restoration, new storm doors/windows, masonry re-pointing, structural repairs, architectural/engineering/consulting fees, and tool/equipment rental.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland, specifically properties within: (1) Antietam Overlay (AO1 or AO2) districts; (2) Historic Rural Village contributing structures (Antietam, Cavetown, Fairplay, Highfield, Leitersburg, Pen Mar, Ringgold, Rohrersville, Sandy Hook, or Tilghmanton); (3) Properties with Historic Preservation (HP) Overlay zoning; or (4) Contributing structures in eligible municipalities listed on the National Register of Historic Places with appropriate zoning and design guidelines.
requirements_list: Property must be located within a designated historic district or qualifying historic area
Property must be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties
Work must qualify as historic preservation under program guidelines and Secretary of Interior Standards for Rehabilitation
Property must be within Antietam Overlay district, a Historic Rural Village, have HP Overlay zoning, or be in an eligible municipality on the National Register
Application must be submitted before work starts
Applicant must comply with all Federal, State and local laws including zoning, building, safety codes, and licensing requirements
For Part III, itemized expenses must be provided with invoices/receipts and proof of payment
Exterior work must be consistent with Washington County Design Guidelines for Historic Structures
Work must have thoughtful and sympathetic design that minimizes destruction of historic fabric
Property owners must maintain records with progress photos during project completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process consists of three parts submitted to Washington County Historic District Commission, c/o Department of Planning & Zoning, 747 Northern Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21742, or via email to askplanning@washco-md.net. Part I (Evaluation of Significance) determines if the structure qualifies and is required unless the property has HP Overlay zoning. Part II (Description of Rehabilitation) must be approved before work begins and evaluates whether proposed work meets Secretary of Interior Standards and County Design Guidelines; applicants must describe all exterior work with photos and estimates of Qualified Rehabilitation Expenditures. Part III (Request for Certification of Completed Work) is submitted at project completion with itemized expenses on the provided spreadsheet, invoices/receipts, proof of payment, and completion photos. The HDC reviews all documentation to determine eligible expenses and certifies qualified projects. All applications require signatures, and if the applicant is not the fee-simple owner, an Owner's Representative Affidavit must be included. Application materials are available at https://wcmd.info/3KSQwn1 and https://arcg.is/e5jCW.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides grants to help Washington County organizations, agencies, and businesses develop tourism attractions, enhance economic development, and support cultural and recreational projects. The program is designed to fund activities and events that would not otherwise happen without special funding support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded by a 6% County Hotel Rental Tax. Funds are invested back into the community through the Convention and Visitors Bureau, local municipalities, and designated local projects to support tourism attractions, economic development, and cultural and recreational initiatives. Grants are paid directly to the applicant (not to vendors). For requests of $25,000 or less, approval is made by the Office of Grant Management with concurrence of the County Administrator. For requests exceeding $25,000, final approval is made by the Board of County Commissioners. Any changes exceeding 10% of approved line items require approval by the Office of Grant Management. Unused funds must be returned to the County within 30 days of project completion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis throughout the fiscal year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Washington County local municipalities, businesses, organizations, residents, and visitors seeking to develop tourism attractions or cultural and recreational projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing tourism attractions (advertising, publicizing, distribution of tourism information, strategic planning, marketing special events and festivals, support of tourism-related facilities, conference centers, convention or visitor information centers), enhancing economic development (retaining and creating job opportunities, retaining business, assisting in expansion of local companies), supporting cultural and recreational projects that would not otherwise be funded.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a non-profit organization, government entity, or for-profit business (individuals are ineligible)
Cannot fund normal and routine operating and administrative expenses
Cannot support political candidates or organizations whose primary purpose is to influence or attempt to initiate legislation
Cannot fund endowments
Cannot fund organizations with budget deficits prior to application

Project must generate overnight stays in the County, encourage support of County business/restaurants/attractions, reach a broad segment of the community, seek multiple sources of support, yield benefits to the community, promote cooperation among organizers, and enhance or improve the community
Requests must qualify under Maryland Code, Article 24, 9-318
All grant recipients must submit a Hotel Rental Tax Grant Report with supporting documentation within 60 days of project completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete the Hotel Rental Tax Funding Application form available online through the County's website under the Office of Grant Management, or submit by email or mail. The application can be accessed from the County's internet site. Applications are received by the Office of Grant Management (OGM) throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding. The OGM will: (1) Determine if the applicant is qualified to receive funding; (2) Determine if the event or project is qualified to receive funding; (3) Determine if the request meets the funding goals of the County Commissioners and the purpose of the Hotel Rental Tax Funding; (4) For requests of $25,000 and below, approve or deny the request with concurrence of the County Administrator; (5) For requests of more than $25,000, forward the application to the County Administrator for review and then to the County Commissioners for final decision; (6) Notify the applicant in writing of approval or denial. Grant recipients must submit a Hotel Rental Tax Grant Report with budget itemizations and receipts within 60 days of project completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-regulated program that preserves high-ranking agricultural properties through the Purchase of Development Rights (PDR) easements. Applicant properties are ranked based on attributes such as soil quality, proximity to other easements, agricultural operation intensity, and proximity to growth areas and Priority Preservation Areas. The easement restrictions remain effective in perpetuity. To date, $49,855,542 has been invested to permanently protect 17,008 acres in Washington County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program purchases development rights easements from qualifying agricultural properties. The landowner receives compensation for the restricted development rights, and the property is permanently protected from development. Easement restrictions remain effective in perpetuity. To date, $49,855,542 has been invested to permanently protect 17,008 acres in Washington County.

Soil quality, proximity to other easements, agricultural operation intensity, and proximity to growth areas are evaluation criteria

structured_extraction.program_description: A program administered by the Maryland Agricultural Resource-Based Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) that provides down payment assistance to young and beginning farmers buying properties that qualify for the County's Agricultural Land Preservation District program. The program offers buyers 51 percent of a land-only fair market value appraisal for purchase assistance, capped at $500,000. After settlement, landowners must actively pursue a permanent easement through an approved program; if none is procured within seven years, the land becomes preserved through a MARBIDCO permanent easement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Buyers receive down payment assistance equal to 51 percent of a land-only fair market value appraisal of the property for purchase, capped at $500,000. After real estate settlement, the landowner must actively pursue a different permanent easement through an approved program and enroll in the County's Agricultural Land Preservation District. If after seven years no permanent easement is procured, the land becomes preserved through a MARBIDCO permanent easement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded program that focuses on preserving Maryland's best natural, agricultural, historical, and cultural areas and significant rural landscapes. The program encourages local governments and private land trusts to identify Rural Legacy Areas and competitively apply for funds to complement existing land preservation efforts or develop new ones. Funds are used to purchase permanent conservation easements from willing landowners to protect areas vulnerable to sprawl development, safeguarding the economic value of farming, forestry, recreation, and tourism.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program funds the purchase of permanent conservation easements from willing landowners to protect areas vulnerable to sprawl development. Easement restrictions remain effective in perpetuity and protect natural resources, safeguarding the economic value of farming, forestry, recreation, and tourism. To date, $28,499,083 has been invested to permanently protect 9,421 acres in Washington County.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax incentives and financial assistance programs designed to support business development, expansion, and workforce training in Washington County. The program includes multiple tax credit opportunities, workforce training grants, and other economic development incentives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides multiple forms of assistance including: (1) Tax credits and exemptions on real property, business personal property, and inventory for qualified businesses; (2) Job Creation & Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit Program offering 6-15 years of tax credits ranging from 26%-100% depending on investment level and job creation; (3) New Jobs Tax Credit providing 6-year credits (52% years 1-2, 39% years 3-4, 26% years 5-6) for businesses expanding by 10,000+ sq ft and creating 25+ new jobs; (4) Pad-Ready Site Commercial Stimulus Program offering 3-year tax credits at 0.4% of construction costs; (5) Brownfield Revitalization Incentive Program providing 5-10 year real property tax credits of 50%-70%; (6) C-PACE loans for energy efficiency and renewable energy projects with up to 100% financing and 20-year repayment; (7) Workforce training grants through Western Maryland Consortium offering up to $4,500 per worker for employee training; (8) Manufacturing machinery and equipment tax exemptions; (9) Research & development equipment tax exemptions; (10) Business inventory tax exemptions; (11) Utility incentives through Potomac Edison offering up to $1M for custom building projects; (12) Access to Foreign Trade Zone benefits including duty-free materials and imports.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit businesses located in or expanding to Washington County, particularly those in manufacturing, technology, and other priority industries; business owners seeking workforce training and development support; commercial property owners interested in energy efficiency improvements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business expansion and relocation; new facility construction; machinery and equipment purchases; working capital; employee recruitment, training and retention; building rehabilitation and code compliance; façade enhancements; energy efficiency and renewable energy projects; research and development activities; manufacturing operations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Specific programs target Enterprise Zones (Hagerstown-Washington County Enterprise Zone covering nearly 5,000 acres including Hopewell Valley Industrial Park and City of Hagerstown Business Park; Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone covering 1,500 acres). Foreign Trade Zone #255 encompasses approximately 1,700 acres including Hagerstown Regional Airport (387 acres), Williamsport (140 acres), Hopewell Valley (470 acres), Lakeside Corporate Center at Cascade (279 acres), and Hancock (128 acres). Priority Funding Areas as designated in Title 5, Subtitle 7B of the State Finance and Procurement Article also apply to certain programs.
requirements_list: Business must be located in Washington County or relocating to Washington County

structured_extraction.program_name: Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit

It helps attract new companies and supports existing companies that expand in the county, with credit amounts and duration depending on the project tier.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to a fifteen year tax credit on the County portion of real estate taxes for qualified businesses that expand or locate and meet specific investment and job creation thresholds. The credit amount and duration depend on the project tier: Tier 1 provides credits up to 52% for six years for existing businesses that expand by at least 1,500 sq. ft. and create at least 1 new full-time job; Tier 2 provides credits up to 30% for six years for new businesses obtaining at least 2,500 sq. ft. and creating at least 5 new full-time jobs; Tier 3 provides credits up to 100% for fifteen years for major investments of at least $10,000,000 in capital improvements and creation of at least 100 new full-time jobs.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real property tax credits for qualified capital investments and job creation in Washington County.

requirements_list: Must be located in a Priority Funding Area.
Cannot be located in an Enterprise Zone.
Submit an application before construction is complete.
Qualifying business must expand or locate in Washington County.
Must meet specific investment thresholds.
Must meet specific job creation thresholds.
Tier 1 (Existing Business): Expand by at least 1,500 sq. ft. and create at least 1 new full-time job paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage.
Tier 2 (New Business): Obtain at least 2,500 sq. ft. of space and create at least 5 new full-time jobs paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage.
Tier 3 (New or Existing Business): Invest at least $10,000,000 in capital improvements and create at least 100 new full-time jobs.
Must provide annual employment reports to maintain the credit.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, a business must notify the county of its intent to apply for the credit. Then, it submits an application packet to the Department of Business Development before finishing construction. The department will certify the business if it is eligible. After certification and project completion, the business must create the required number of new jobs. The business must submit yearly reports on employment to maintain the credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Federal Communications Commission program that helps families and households struggling to afford internet service during the COVID-19 pandemic. The program provides a monthly discount toward broadband service and a one-time discount to purchase a computer or tablet from participating providers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible households receive a discount of up to $50 per month toward broadband service. Households can also receive a one-time discount of up to $100 to purchase a laptop, desktop computer, or tablet from participating providers if they contribute more than $10 and less than $50 toward the purchase price.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Households with income at or below 135% of federal poverty guidelines, households participating in SNAP, Medicaid, or Lifeline, households approved for free and reduced-price school lunch or breakfast programs, households with a member who received a Federal Pell Grant during the current award year, households that experienced substantial loss of income due to job loss or furlough since February 29, 2020, or households that meet participating provider's low-income or COVID-19 program criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly broadband service discount or one-time computer or tablet purchase discount from participating providers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout the United States and territories where participating broadband providers offer service.
requirements_list: Household member income at or below 135% of Federal Poverty Guidelines or participation in assistance programs such as SNAP, Medicaid, or Lifeline
Approval to receive benefits under free and reduced-price school lunch or breakfast program including USDA Community Eligibility Provision in 2019-2020 or 2020-2021 school year
Household member received a Federal Pell Grant during current award year
Experienced substantial loss of income due to job loss or furlough since February 29, 2020 with 2020 household income at or below $99,000 for single filers and $198,000 for joint filers
Meets participating provider's eligibility criteria for existing low-income or COVID-19 program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible households can apply in three ways: contact a preferred participating broadband provider directly, apply online at GetEmergencyBroadband.org to find participating providers, or call 833-511-0311 to request a mail-in application. After submitting proof of eligibility documents to the support center address, households receive an eligibility determination and can then contact their preferred service provider to select an eligible service plan.

structured_extraction.program_name: USDA Rural Development Housing Rehabilitation Program (Section 504 Home Repair Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides loans to very-low-income homeowners to repair, improve, or modernize their homes, and grants to elderly very-low-income homeowners to remove health and safety hazards. This program helps homeowners in rural areas make necessary repairs to bring their homes up to safe and sanitary living standards.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Section 504 loans are available to very-low-income homeowners to repair, improve, or modernize their homes. Loans carry a fixed interest rate of 1% and can be amortized for up to 20 years. Grants are available to elderly homeowners age 62 or older who are unable to repay a repair loan. Grants can be up to $7,500 to remove health and safety hazards. Loans can be up to $20,000 depending on the scope of work needed. Both loans and grants require that the applicant's household income does not exceed the very low-income limit established by USDA for the applicable county.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Very-low-income homeowners in rural areas of Maryland who are unable to obtain affordable credit elsewhere and need to make repairs to bring their homes to safe and sanitary living standards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repair, improvement, and modernization of homes; removal of health and safety hazards including roof repairs, plumbing and electrical repairs, weatherization, accessibility modifications, and other work necessary to make the home safe and sanitary.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in rural areas served by USDA Rural Development Hagerstown Office, including Wicomico County and other eligible Maryland counties. Properties must be located in areas with populations of 10,000 or less.
requirements_list: Be the homeowner and occupy the home as primary residence
Be unable to obtain affordable credit elsewhere
Have household income that does not exceed the very low income limit for the applicable county
For loans: demonstrate ability to repay the loan
For grants: be age 62 or older and unable to repay a repair loan
Own a home that is unsafe or unsanitary
Property must be located in an eligible rural area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact the USDA Rural Development Hagerstown Office at (301) 797-0500 extension 4 or visit the Wicomico County Housing Department. 2. Provide documentation of household income, employment history, and assets. 3. Complete the Uniform Residential Loan Application (Form RD 410-4) and Authorization to Release Information (Form RD 3550-1). 4. Submit employment and asset certification (Form RD 3550-4). 5. Provide a checklist of items to accompany the application including proof of income, identification, and property information. 6. USDA staff will conduct a property inspection and appraisal. 7. Loan or grant approval and closing. 8. Work can begin once loan/grant is funded.
